لا يدري ولذلك قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه إذا ذكر العلماء فمالك النجم
الثاقب وما أحد أمن علي من مالك
وروي أن أبا جعفر المنصور منعه من رواية الحديث في طلاق المكره ثم دس
عليه من يسأله فروى على ملأ من الناس ليس على مستكره طلاق فضربه بالسياط
ولم يترك رواية الحديث
وقال مالك رحمه الله ما كان رجل صادقا في حديثه ولا يكذب إلا متع بعقله
ولم يصبه مع الهرم آفة ولا خرف
وأما زهده في الدنيا فيدل عليه ما روي أن المهدي أمير المؤمنين سأله فقال
له هل لك من دار فقال لا ولكن أحدثك سمعت ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن يقول نسب
المرء داره وسأله الرشيد هل لك دار فقال لا فأعطاه ثلاثة آلاف دينار وقال
اشتر بها دارا فأخذها ولم ينفقها فلما أراد الرشيد الشخوص قال لمالك رحمه
الله ينبغي أن تخرج معنا فإني عزمت على أن أحمل الناس على الموطأ كما حمل
عثمان رضي الله عنه الناس على القرآن فقال له أما حمل الناس على الموطأ
فليس إليه سبيل لأن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم افترقوا بعده في
الأمصار فحدثوا فعند كل أهل مصر علم وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اختلاف
أمتي رحمة (1) وأما الخروج معك فلا سبيل إليه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم المدينة خير لهم لو كانوا يعلمون (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة
تنفي خبثها كما ينفي الكير خبث الحديد (3) وهذه دنانيركم كما هي إن شئتم
فخذوها وإن شئتم فدعوها يعني أنك إنما تكلفني مفارقة المدينة لما اصطنعته
إلي فلا أوثر الدنيا على مدينة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهكذا كان زهد
مالك في الدنيا ولما حملت إليه الأموال الكثيرة من أطراف الدنيا لانتشار
علمه وأصحابه كان يفرقها في وجوه الخير ودل سخاؤه على زهده وقلة حبه للدنيا
وليس الزهد فقد المال وإنما الزهد فراغ القلب عنه ولقد كان سليمان عليه
السلام في ملكه من الزهاد
ويدل على احتقاره للدنيا ما روي عن الشافعي رحمه الله أنه قال رأيت على
باب مالك كراعا من أفراس خراسان ويقال مصر ما رأيت أحسن منه فقلت لمالك
رحمه الله ما أحسنه فقال هو هدية مني إليك يا أبا عبد الله فقلت دع لنفسك
منها دابة تركبها PageV01P027
فقال إني أستحي من الله تعالى أن أطأ تربة فيها نبي الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم بحافر دابة فانظر إلى سخائه إذ وهب جميع ذلك دفعة واحدة وإلى توقيره
لتربة المدينة
ويدل على إرادته بالعلم وجه الله تعالى واستحقار للدنيا ما روي أنه قال
دخلت على هارون الرشيد فقال لي يا أبا عبد الله ينبغي أن تختلف إلينا حتى
يسمع صبياننا منك الموطأ قال فقلت أعز الله مولانا الأمير إن هذا العلم
منكم خرج فإن أنتم أعزرتموه عز وإن أنتم أذللتموه ذل والعلم يؤتى ولا يأتي
فقال صدقت اخرجوا إلى المسجد حتى تسمعوا مع الناس
وأما أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى فلقد كان أيضا عابدا زاهدا بالله تعالى
خائفا منه مريدا وجه الله تعالى بعلمه فأما كونه عابدا فيعرف بما روي عن
ابن المبارك أنه قال كان أبو حنيفة رحمه الله له مروءة وكثرة صلاة
وروى حماد بن أبي سليمان أنه كان يحيي الليل كله
وروي أنه كان يحيي نصف الليل فمر يوما في طريق فأشار إليه إنسان وهو يمشي
فقال لآخر هذا هو الذي يحيي الليل كله فلم يزل بعد ذلك يحيي الليل كله وقال
أنا أستحي من الله سبحانهأن أوصف بما ليس في من عبادته
وأما زهده فقد روي عن الربيع بن عاصم قال أرسلني يزيد بن عمر بن هبيرة
فقدمت بأبي حنيفة عليه فأراده أن يكون حاكما على بيت المال فأبى فضربه
عشرين سوطا
فانظر كيف هرب من  الولاية واحتمل العذاب قال الحكم بن هشام الثقفي حدثت
بالشام حديثا في أبي حنيفة أنه كان من أعظم الناس أمانة وأراده السلطان على
أن يتولى مفاتيح خزائنه أو يضرب ظهره فاختار عذابهم له على عذاب الله تعالى
وروي أنه ذكر أبو حنيفة عند ابن المبارك فقال أتذكرون رجلا عرضت عليه
الدنيا بحذافيرها ففر منها
وروي عن محمد بن شجاع عن بعض أصحابه أنه قيل لأبي حنيفة قد أمر لك أمير
المؤمنين أبو جعفر المنصور بعشرة آلاف درهم قال فما رضي أبو حنيفة قال فلما
كان اليوم الذي توقع أن يؤتى بالمال فيه صلى الصبح ثم تغشى بثوبه فلم يتكلم
فجاء رسول الحسن بن قحطبة بالمال فدخل عليه فلم يكلمه فقال بعض من حضر ما
يكلمنا إلا بالكلمة بعد الكلمة أي هذه عادته فقال ضعوا المال في هذا الجراب
في زاوية البيت ثم أوصى أبو حنيفة بعد ذلك بمتاع بيته وقال لابنه إذا مت
ودفنتموني فخذ هذه البدرة واذهب بها إلى الحسن ابن قحطبة فقل له خذ وديعتك
التي أودعتها أبا حنيفة
قال ابنه ففعلت ذلك فقال الحسن رحمة الله على أبيك فلقد كان شحيحا على
دينه
وروي أنه دعي إلى ولاية القضاء فقال أنا لا أصلح لهذا فقيل له لم فقال إن
كنت صادقا فما أصلح لها وإن كنت كاذبا فالكاذب لا يصلح للقضاء
وأما علمه بطريق الآخرة وطريق أمور الدين ومعرفته بالله عز وجل فيدل عليه
شدة خوفه من الله تعالى وزهده في الدنيا وقد قال ابن جريج قد بلغني عن
كوفيكم هذا النعمان بن ثابت أنه شديد الخوف لله تعالى
وقال شريك النخعي كان أبو حنيفة طويل الصمت دائم الفكر قليل المحادثة
للناس فهذا من أوضح الأمارات على العلم الباطني والاشتغال بمهمات الدين فمن
أوتي الصمت والزهد فقد أوتي العلم كله فهذه نبذة من أحوال الأئمة الثلاثة
وأما الإمام أحمد بن حنبل وسفيان الثوري رحمهما الله تعالى فأتباعهما أقل
من أتباع هؤلاء وسفيان أقل أتباعا من أحمد ولكن  اشتهارهما بالورع والزهد
أظهر وجميع هذا الكتاب مشحون بحكايات أفعالهما وأقوالهما فلا حاجة إلى
التفصيل الآن فانظر الآن في غير هؤلاء الأئمة الثلاثة وتأمل أن هذه الأحوال
والأقوال والأفعال في الإعراض عن الدنيا والتجرد لله عز وجل هل يثمرها مجرد
العلم بفروع الفقه من معرفة السلم والإجارة والظهار والإيلاء واللعان أو
يثمرها علم آخر أعلى وأشرف منه وانظر إلى الذين ادعوا الاقتداء بهؤلاء
أصدقوا في دعواهم أم لا
PageV01P028
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make an incision, to determine, to render obligatory; a determined share or obligation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A religious duty (farḍ) as a determined divine command; farḍ kifāyah (collective obligation) vs. farḍ ʿayn (individual obligation).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of cutting/determining; metaphorically, a fixed religious duty.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, perception, cognition; the faculty of knowing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; ʿilm al-mukāshafah (science of unveiling) vs. ʿilm al-muʿāmalah (science of practical conduct).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: perception; metaphorical: the sciences as branches of divine and worldly knowledge.
- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To divide, to distribute; a division or category.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Division of knowledge into categories; the act of distinguishing types.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: partitioning; metaphorical: classification of sciences.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs complex conditional sentences (e.g., "if the land is devoid... then the people are in sin") and exceptive clauses ("no one is excused except...") requiring precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis to preserve the logical force of the argument.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the obligatory (al-farḍ) is not distinguished from other things except by mentioning the divisions of the sciences. The sciences, in relation to the purpose we are presently concerned with, divide into religious (sharʿiyyah) and non-religious. By "religious" I mean that which is derived from the prophets (peace and blessings of God upon them) and to which the intellect does not guide, such as arithmetic (al-ḥisāb), nor experience, such as medicine (al-ṭibb), nor audition, such as language (al-lughah). Thus, the sciences that are not religious divide into what is praiseworthy (maḥmūd), what is blameworthy (madhmūm), and what is permissible (mubāḥ). The praiseworthy is that which is connected to the interests of worldly affairs, such as medicine and arithmetic. This divides into what is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) and what is a virtue (faḍīlah) but not an obligation. As for the collective obligation, it is a science without which the establishment of worldly affairs cannot dispense, such as medicine, for it is necessary for the need of preserving bodies, and such as arithmetic, for it is necessary in transactions, the division of bequests, inheritances, and other matters. These are the sciences that, if a town were devoid of anyone to undertake them, the people of the town would be in sin (ḥaraj); and if one person undertakes them, it suffices, and the obligation falls from the others.

Do not be astonished at our saying that medicine and arithmetic are among the collective obligations, for the foundations of the crafts (uṣūl al-ṣināʿāt) are also among the collective obligations, such as agriculture, weaving, and statecraft—nay, even cupping (ḥijāmah) and tailoring. For if a town were devoid of a cupper, destruction would hasten upon its people, and they would be in sin by exposing themselves to ruin. For He who sent down the disease sent down the cure, guided to its use, and prepared the means for its pursuit; thus, it is not permissible to expose oneself to destruction by neglecting it.

As for what is counted a virtue, not an obligation, it is deep immersion in the subtleties of arithmetic, the realities of medicine, and other such things that can be dispensed with, but which yield an increase of strength in what is needed.

As for the blameworthy, it is the science of sorcery (siḥr), talismans (ṭilasmāt), the science of sleight-of-hand (shaʿbadhah), and deceptions (talbīsāt).

As for the permissible among them, it is the knowledge of poetry that contains no foolishness, historical reports, and what runs in their course.

As for the religious sciences—and they are the intended subject of this exposition—they are all praiseworthy, but what is imagined to be religious may be confused with them while being blameworthy. Thus, they divide into the praiseworthy and the blameworthy.

As for the praiseworthy, they have principles (uṣūl), branches (furūʿ), preliminaries (muqaddimāt), and completions (mutammimāt), and they are of four kinds.

The first kind is the principles, and they are four: the Book of God (mighty and majestic), the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), the consensus of the community (ijmāʿ al-ummah), and the reports of the Companions (āthār al-ṣaḥābah). Consensus is a principle insofar as it indicates the Sunnah, so it is a principle in the third degree. Likewise, the report (athar), for it also indicates the Sunnah, because the Companions (may God be pleased with them) witnessed the revelation and the descent (al-waḥy wa al-tanzīl) and perceived, through the circumstantial indications of the states (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl), what was hidden from others in their direct vision; and perhaps expressions do not encompass what was perceived through circumstantial indications. From this aspect, the scholars saw fit to follow them and adhere to their reports—this being under a specific condition, in a specific manner, according to those who hold it, and its exposition is not fitting for this art.

The second kind is the branches, which is what is understood from these principles not by the necessity of their wording but by meanings to which the intellects are alerted, and through which understanding expands until one understands from the uttered word something other than it, as was understood from his saying (peace be upon him): "The judge shall not judge while he is angry" (lā yaqḍī al-qāḍī wa-huwa ghaḍbān) — that he shall not judge if he is fearful, hungry, or pained by illness. This is of two kinds: one pertains to the interests of this world, encompassed by the books of jurisprudence (fiqh), and its guarantors are the jurists (fuqahāʾ), who are the scholars of this world. The second pertains to the interests of the Hereafter, and it is the science of the states of the heart, its praiseworthy and blameworthy traits, what is pleasing to God (exalted) and what is detested—this is encompassed by the latter half of this book, namely, the entirety of the Revival of the Religious Sciences (Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn). From it also derives the knowledge of what flows from the heart upon the bodily members in their acts of worship and customs, which is encompassed by the first half of this book.

The third kind is the preliminaries, which serve as instruments, such as the science of language (lughah) and grammar (naḥw), for they are instruments for the knowledge of the Book of God (exalted) and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him). Language and grammar are not, in themselves, among the religious sciences, but it becomes necessary to delve into them because of the religious law, since this sharīʿah came in the Arabic tongue, and no religious law appears except through a language; thus, learning that language becomes an instrument. Among the instruments is the science of writing script, except that it is not necessary, since the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was illiterate (ummī). If one could conceive of memory being self-sufficient for all that is heard, writing would be dispensed with, but it has become, by virtue of incapacity in most cases, necessary.

The fourth kind is the completions. This pertains to the science of the Qurʾān, for it divides into what relates to the wording, such as learning the variant readings (qirāʾāt) and the points of articulation of letters (makhārij al-ḥurūf); what relates to the meaning, such as exegesis (tafsīr), for its reliance is also upon transmission (naql), since language alone does not suffice for it; and what relates to its rulings, such as knowing the abrogating and abrogated (al-nāsikh wa al-mansūkh), the general and specific (al-ʿāmm wa al-khāṣṣ), the explicit and apparent (al-naṣṣ wa al-ẓāhir), and the manner of applying some of it with others—this is the science called the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl al-fiqh), and it also encompasses the Sunnah.

As for the completions in the reports and narrations (āthār wa akhbār), they are the knowledge of the transmitters (rijāl), their names, genealogies, the names of the Companions and their attributes, the knowledge of the probity (ʿadālah) of the narrators, the knowledge of their conditions to distinguish the weak from the strong, and the knowledge of their lifespans to distinguish the interrupted (mursal) from the connected (musnad), and likewise what pertains to this.

These, then, are the religious sciences, and all of them are praiseworthy—nay, all of them are among the collective obligations. If you say: "Why have you attached jurisprudence to the science of this world?"—know that God (mighty and majestic) brought forth Adam (peace be upon him) from dust, and brought forth his progeny from a lineage of clay and from gushing water; He brought them forth from the loins to the wombs, from there to this world, then to the grave, then to the standing (al-ʿarḍ), then to Paradise or to the Fire. This is their beginning, this is their end, and these are their stations. He created this world as provision (zād) for the Hereafter, so that they might take from it what is fit for provisioning. Had they taken it with justice, disputes would have ceased and the jurists would have been rendered idle. But they took it with lusts, and from this disputes were generated, and the need arose for a sovereign (sulṭān) to govern them; and the sovereign needed a law (qānūn) by which to govern them. Thus, the jurist (faqīh) is the one who knows the law of governance and the way of mediation among creatures when they contend by the rule of lusts. So the jurist is the teacher of the sovereign and his guide to the ways of governing creatures and restraining them, so that their affairs in this world may be ordered by their uprightness. By my life, it is also connected to religion, but not in itself; rather, through the mediation of this world, for this world is the tillage of the Hereafter (al-dunyā mazraʿat al-ākhirah), and religion is not completed except through this world.

Kingship and religion are twins: religion is the root, and the sovereign is its guardian. What has no root is demolished, and what has no guardian is lost. Kingship and restraint are not completed except through the sovereign, and the way of restraint in adjudicating disputes is through jurisprudence. Just as the governance of creatures by sovereignty is not, in the first degree, among the science of religion, but rather assists what religion is not completed without, so too is the knowledge of the way of governance. It is known that the pilgrimage (ḥajj) is not completed except with an armed escort (bādharqah) to guard against the Arabs on the road; but the pilgrimage is one thing, traversing the road to the pilgrimage is a second thing, undertaking the guard duty without which the pilgrimage is not completed is a third thing, and knowing the ways of guard duty, its stratagems, and its laws is a fourth thing. The sum of the art of jurisprudence is the knowledge of the ways of governance and guard duty. This is indicated by what is narrated as connected (musnad): "None gives legal opinion (yufīt) except three: a commander (amīr), one commanded (maʾmūr), or one who undertakes it gratuitously (mutakallif)." The commander is the imam, and they were the ones who gave legal opinions; the one commanded is his deputy; and the one who undertakes it gratuitously is other than them—he who assumes that burden without need.

The Companions (may God be pleased with them) used to be cautious about giving legal opinions (fatwā), to the point that each would refer the questioner to his companion; yet they were not cautious when asked about the science of the Qurʾān and the way of the Hereafter. In some narrations, "the one who undertakes it gratuitously" is replaced by "the ostentatious one" (murāʾī), for whoever assumes the peril of legal opinion without being designated by need seeks only status and wealth.

If you say: "This holds for you in the rulings of injuries (jirāḥāt), prescribed punishments (ḥudūd), fines (gharāmāt), and the adjudication of disputes, but it does not hold for what the quarter of acts of worship (rubʿ al-ʿibādāt) contains, such as fasting and prayer, nor for what the quarter of customs (rubʿ al-ʿādāt) contains, such as transactions, in clarifying the lawful and unlawful"—know that the closest of the acts that the jurist discusses, among the acts that are acts of the Hereafter, are three: Islam (al-islām), prayer (al-ṣalāh), and alms (al-zakāh), and the lawful and unlawful. If you contemplate the ultimate reach of the jurist's consideration in these, you will know that he does not pass beyond the bounds of this world to the Hereafter. And if you know this regarding these three, it is even more evident regarding others.

As for Islam, the jurist discusses what renders it valid and what invalidates it, and its conditions, and he looks only to the tongue. As for the heart, it is outside the jurisdiction of the jurist, because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) removed the masters of swords and sovereignty from it when he said to the one who killed a man who had uttered the word of Islam, excusing himself that he said it out of fear of the sword: "Why did you not split open his heart?" (halā shaqaqta ʿan qalbihi). Rather, the jurist rules on the validity of Islam under the shadows of swords, even though he knows that the sword did not uncover his intention for him, nor did it remove from his heart the veil of ignorance and confusion; but it is a deterrent against the sword-bearer, for the sword is extended to his neck and the hand is extended to his wealth, and this word upon the tongue protects his neck and his wealth as long as he has a neck and wealth—and that is in this world. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: "I was commanded to fight people until they say 'There is no god but God'; when they say it, they have protected from me their blood and their wealth" (umirtu an uqātila al-nās ḥattā yaqūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh, fa-idhā qālūhā fa-qad ʿaṣamū minnī dimāʾahum wa amwālahum). He made the effect of that upon blood and wealth. As for the Hereafter, wealth does not avail there; rather, the lights of the hearts, their secrets, and their sincerity avail—and that is not of jurisprudence. If the jurist delves into it, he is like one who delves into theology (kalām) and medicine, being outside his art.

As for prayer, the jurist gives the opinion of validity when one performs the form of the acts with the apparent conditions, even if he is heedless throughout his entire prayer, from its beginning to its end, occupied with thinking about the arithmetic of his transactions in the market, except at the takbīr. Such a prayer does not benefit in the Hereafter, just as the utterance of the tongue in Islam does not benefit; but the jurist rules its validity, meaning that by what he did, he fulfilled the compliance with the imperative form (imtithāl ṣīghat al-amr) and thereby warded off from himself killing and chastisement. As for humility (khushūʿ) and the presence of the heart, which is the act of the Hereafter and by which the outward act benefits, the jurist does not address it; and were he to address it, he would be outside his art.

As for alms, the jurist looks to what cuts off the sovereign's claim, to the point that if one refuses to pay it and the sovereign takes it by force, he rules that his liability is discharged. It is narrated that Abū Yūsuf the judge used to give his wealth to his wife at the end of the year (ḥawl) and take her wealth as a gift, to drop the alms obligation; this was mentioned to Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him), and he said: "That is from his jurisprudence." And he spoke truly, for that is from the jurisprudence of this world, but its harm in the Hereafter is greater than any offense; and such is the harmful science (al-ʿilm al-ḍārr).

As for the lawful and unlawful, scrupulousness (waraʿ) regarding the unlawful is from religion, but scrupulousness has four degrees. The first is the scrupulousness required for the probity of testimony (ʿadālat al-shahādah), by abandoning which a person exits from the qualification for testimony, judgeship, and authority—and it is the avoidance of the apparent unlawful. The second is the scrupulousness of the righteous (waraʿ al-ṣāliḥīn), which is the caution against ambiguities (shubuhāt) in which probabilities are balanced. He (peace be upon him) said: "Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt" (daʿ mā yurībuka ilā mā lā yurībuka), and he said: "Sin is the pricking of the hearts" (al-ithm ḥizāz al-qulūb). The third is the scrupulousness of the God-fearing (waraʿ al-muttaqīn), which is abandoning the purely lawful out of fear that it may lead to the unlawful. He (peace be upon him) said: "A man does not become among the God-fearing until he leaves what is harmless out of fear of what is harmful" (lā yakūn al-rajul min al-muttaqīn ḥattā yadaʿa mā lā baʾsa bihi makhāfatan mimmā bihi baʾs)—such as refraining from speaking about people's conditions out of fear of sliding into backbiting (ghībah), and refraining from eating lustful foods out of fear of the arousal of vigor and insolence (al-baṭar) that leads to committing forbidden acts. The fourth is the scrupulousness of the veracious (waraʿ al-ṣiddīqīn), which is turning away from all that is other than God (exalted), out of fear of spending an hour of one's life on what does not yield an increase of nearness to God (mighty and majestic), even if one knows and is certain that it does not lead to the unlawful. All these degrees are outside the jurist's consideration except the first degree, which is the scrupulousness of witnesses and judgeship, and what impugns probity; and undertaking that does not negate sin in the Hereafter. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to Wābiṣah: "Ask your heart for a legal opinion, even if they give you legal opinions, even if they give you legal opinions" (istafti qalbaka wa-in aftawka wa-in aftawka). The jurist does not speak of the prickings of the hearts and the manner of acting upon them, but only of what impugns probity. For the entire consideration of the jurist is tied to this world, by which the way of the Hereafter is set right. If he speaks of something of the attributes of the heart and the rulings of the Hereafter, that enters his speech by way of intrusion (tafafful), just as something of medicine, arithmetic, astronomy, and theology (ʿilm al-kalām) may enter his speech, and just as wisdom enters grammar and poetry.

Sufyān al-Thawrī—an imam in the outward science—used to say: "Seeking this is not from the provision of the Hereafter." How could it be, when they have agreed that honor in knowledge lies in acting upon it? So how could it be imagined that it is the science of ẓihār (injurious comparison), liʿān (mutual cursing), salam (advance payment), ijārah (hire), and ṣarf (currency exchange)? Whoever learns these things to draw near to God (exalted) is mad. Rather, the act is by the heart and the bodily members in acts of obedience, and the honor is those acts.

If you say: "Why have you equated jurisprudence with medicine, since medicine also pertains to this world—it is the health of the body—and by it the soundness of religion also pertains, and this equation contradicts the consensus of the Muslims?"—know that the equation is not necessary; rather, there is a difference between them, and jurisprudence is nobler than it in three respects. One: it is a religious science, being derived from prophecy, unlike medicine, which is not from the science of the religious law. Two: no one traversing the way of the Hereafter can dispense with it at all—neither the healthy nor the sick. As for medicine, only the sick need it, and they are the fewer. Three: the science of jurisprudence is adjacent to the science of the way of the Hereafter, because it considers the acts of the bodily members, and the source and origin of the acts of the bodily members are the attributes of the hearts; the praiseworthy acts issue from the praiseworthy traits that save in the Hereafter, and the blameworthy issue from the blameworthy. The connection of the bodily members to the heart is not hidden. As for health and sickness, their origin is the purity of the temperament (mizāj) and humors (akhlāṭ), and that is among the attributes of the body, not the attributes of the heart. Whenever jurisprudence is compared to medicine, its nobility appears; and when the science of the way of the Hereafter is compared to jurisprudence, the nobility of the science of the way of the Hereafter also appears.

If you say: "Explain to me the science of the way of the Hereafter in a detailed manner that points to its chapter headings, even if the enumeration of its details is not possible"—know that it is of two divisions: the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah) and the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). The first division is the science of unveiling, and it is the science of the inner (ʿilm al-bāṭin), and it is the ultimate of the sciences. Some of the knowers (ʿārifūn) have said: "Whoever has no share of this science, I fear for him an evil end." The least share of it is to affirm it as true and to submit to its people. Another said: "Whoever has two traits will not be opened to anything of this science: innovation (bidʿah) or pride (kibr)." It was said: "Whoever loves this world or persists in his whim will not be realized in it," though he may be realized in other sciences. The least punishment of one who denies it is that he tastes nothing of it. And it is recited in support of his saying:
"And be content with one whose absence is hidden from you... for that is a sin whose punishment is in it."

It is the science of the veracious and the near ones (al-ṣiddīqīn wa al-muqarrabīn)—I mean the science of unveiling. It is an expression for a light that appears in the heart upon its purification and sanctification from its blameworthy attributes; and from that light many things are unveiled that one had previously heard as names and imagined for them vague, unclear meanings, which then become clear, until true knowledge (maʿrifah) is attained of the essence of God (glorified), His enduring and perfect attributes, His acts, His wisdom in creating this world and the Hereafter, and the manner of His ordering the Hereafter upon this world; and the knowledge of the meaning of prophecy (nubuwwah) and the prophet, the meaning of revelation (waḥy), the meaning of Satan (shayṭān), the meaning of the words "angels" and "devils," the manner of the devils' enmity toward man, the manner of the angel's appearance to the prophets, the manner of revelation reaching them; and the knowledge of the dominion of the heavens and the earth (malakūt al-samāwāt wa al-arḍ), the knowledge of the heart and the manner of the clash of the hosts of angels and devils within it, the knowledge of the difference between the prompting of the angel (limmat al-malak) and the prompting of the devil (limmat al-shayṭān); and the knowledge of the Hereafter, Paradise and the Fire, the punishment of the grave, the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ), the Balance (al-mīzān), and the Reckoning (al-ḥisāb); and the meaning of His saying (exalted): {«اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا»} ("Read your book; sufficient is your own soul this day as a reckoner against you"), and the meaning of His saying (exalted): {«وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون»} ("And indeed the abode of the Hereafter—it is the life, if only they knew"), and the meaning of the meeting with God (mighty and majestic) and the vision of His noble face, the meaning of nearness to Him and descending into His vicinity, the meaning of attaining felicity by accompanying the most high assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā) and being in the company of the angels and prophets, and the meaning of the varying degrees of the people of Paradise until some see others as one sees the brilliant star (al-kawkab al-durrī) in the midst of the sky—and other things whose detail would be lengthy, for people have various stations regarding the meanings of these matters after affirming their principles. Some see that all of that is parables (amthilah) and that what God has prepared for His righteous servants is "what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart of any human," and that there is nothing with creation of Paradise except the attributes and names. Some see that some of it is parables and some corresponds to the realities understood from their wording. Likewise, some see that the ultimate of knowledge of God (mighty and majestic) is the acknowledgment of incapacity to know Him; some claim great things in knowledge of God (mighty and majestic); and some say the limit of knowledge of God (mighty and majestic) is what the belief of all the common folk reaches—that He is existent, knowing, powerful, hearing, seeing, speaking. By the science of unveiling, we mean that the veil is lifted so that the clarity of truth in these matters becomes evident to him with an evidentness that runs in the course of direct vision (ʿiyān) in which there is no doubt. This is possible in the substance of the human being, were it not that the mirror of the heart has accumulated rust and filth from the impurities of this world. By the science of the way of the Hereafter, we mean the knowledge of how to polish this mirror of those impurities that are the veil from God (glorified and exalted) and from knowledge of His attributes and acts. Its purification and cleansing are only through refraining from lusts and following the prophets (peace and blessings of God upon them) in all their states. To the extent that the heart is unveiled and aligned toward the direction of truth, its realities shine within it; and there is no way to it except through discipline (riyāḍah), whose detail will come in its place, and through knowledge and teaching. These are the sciences that are not inscribed in books, and one upon whom God has bestowed something of them does not speak of them except with their people—the one who shares in it by way of mutual reminder (mudhākarah) and by the path of secrets. This is the hidden science that he (peace be upon him) intended by his saying: "Indeed, there is a kind of knowledge like the hidden thing (al-maknūn); none knows it except the people of knowledge of God (exalted); when they speak of it, none denies it except those deluded by God (exalted)." So do not belittle a scholar to whom God (exalted) has given knowledge of it, for God (mighty and majestic) did not belittle him when He gave it to him.

As for the second division—the science of practical conduct—it is the science of the states of the heart. As for what is praiseworthy among them, such as patience (ṣabr), gratitude (shukr), fear (khawf), hope (rajāʾ), contentment (riḍā), renunciation (zuhd), piety (taqwā), sufficiency (qanāʿah), generosity (sakhāʾ), knowledge of the obligation of God (exalted) in all states, excellence (iḥsān), good opinion (ḥusn al-ẓann), good character (ḥusn al-khuluq), good companionship (ḥusn al-muʿāsharah), truthfulness (ṣidq), and sincerity (ikhlāṣ)—the knowledge of the realities of these states, their limits, their causes by which they are acquired, their fruits, their signs, and the treatment of what is weak among them until it strengthens, and what has departed until it returns—this is from the science of the Hereafter.

As for what is blameworthy among them: fear of poverty, displeasure with the decree (sukht al-maqdūr), rancor (ghill), malice (ḥiqd), envy (ḥasad), deceit (ghishsh), seeking elevation (ṭalab al-ʿulū), love of praise (ḥubb al-thanāʾ), love of long survival in this world for enjoyment, pride (kibr), ostentation (riyāʾ), anger (ghaḍab), haughtiness (anafah), enmity (ʿadāwah), hatred (baghḍāʾ), greed (ṭamaʿ), miserliness (bukhl), craving (raghbah), extravagance (badhakh), insolence (ashar), arrogance (baṭar), magnifying the rich, despising the poor, vainglory (fakhr), conceit (khuyalāʾ), rivalry (tanāfus), boasting (mubāhāh), disdain for the truth (istikbār ʿan al-ḥaqq), plunging into what does not concern one (khawḍ fīmā lā yaʿnī), love of much speech, self-praise (ṣalaf), self-adornment for creatures (tazayyun lil-khalq), flattery (madāhanah), self-amazement (ʿujb), preoccupation with the faults of others instead of one's own faults, the departure of sorrow from the heart, the exit of reverence (khashyah) from it, intense self-vindication when humiliated, weak vindication of the truth, taking friends in public while harboring enmity in secret, feeling secure from the stratagem of God (glorified and exalted) in stripping what He has given, reliance upon obedience, deceit (makr), treachery (khiyānah), fraud (mukhādaʿah), long hope (ṭūl al-amal), hardness (qaswah), roughness (faẓāẓah), rejoicing in this world, grief over its loss, intimacy with creatures (uns bil-makhlūqīn), desolation at their parting, harshness (jafāʾ), flightiness (ṭaysh), haste (ʿajalah), lack of modesty (qillat al-ḥayāʾ), and lack of mercy (qillat al-raḥmah). These and their like are among the attributes of the heart—the seedbeds of obscenities (maghāris al-fawāḥish) and the growth-places of forbidden acts. Their opposites—the praiseworthy traits—are the source of acts of obedience and acts of drawing near. The knowledge of the limits of these matters, their realities, their causes, their fruits, and their treatment is the science of the Hereafter, and it is an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) according to the legal opinions of the scholars of the Hereafter. The one who turns away from it perishes by the might of the King of Kings in the Hereafter, just as the one who turns away from the outward acts perishes by the sword of the sovereigns of this world, by the ruling of the legal opinions of the jurists of this world. The consideration of the jurists regarding individual obligations pertains to the soundness of this world, and this pertains to the soundness of the Hereafter. If a jurist were asked about the meaning of one of these meanings—even about sincerity (ikhlāṣ), for example, or about trust (tawakkul), or about the manner of guarding against ostentation—he would hesitate over it, even though it is his individual obligation whose neglect is his ruin in the Hereafter. Yet if you asked him about liʿān, ẓihār, racing (sabq), and archery (ramy), he would recite to you volumes of subtle subdivisions (tafrīʿāt) that ages pass without needing any of them; and if they were needed, the town would not lack someone to undertake them and suffice him the burden of toil in them. He continues to toil in them night and day, and in memorizing and studying them he neglects what is important in itself in religion. When he is reproached for this, he says: "I have occupied myself with it because it is the science of religion and a collective obligation"—thus deceiving himself and others in learning it. The astute one knows that if his purpose were to fulfill the right of the command regarding the collective obligation, he would have given precedence to the individual obligation; nay, he would have given precedence to many collective obligations. How many a town has no physician except from the people of the covenant (ahl al-dhimmah), and their testimony is not accepted in what pertains to physicians of the rulings of jurisprudence—yet we see no one occupying himself with it, while they vie with one another over the science of jurisprudence, especially the disputational (khilāfiyyāt) and dialectical (jadalīyāt) matters, and the town is crowded with jurists occupied with legal opinions and answering events. Would that I knew how the jurists of religion permit occupying oneself with a collective obligation that a group has already fulfilled, while neglecting what has no one to fulfill it! Is there any cause for this except that medicine does not provide a means to administering endowments (awqāf) and bequests (waṣāyā), seizing the wealth of orphans, assuming judgeship and governance, advancing over one's peers, and dominating one's enemies? Alas, alas! The science of religion has become effaced by the deception of evil scholars. God (exalted) is the one whose help

chapters.title_en: Section 13 — On What the Common People Count Among the Praiseworthy Sciences, Though It Is Not of Them
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| الباب الثالث فيما يعده العامة من العلوم المحمودة وليس منها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع د د (ʿ- d - d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Counting, reckoning, enumerating; also preparing or deeming something as belonging to a category.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for intellectual estimation and classification, often implying a subjective or erroneous judgment when applied to matters of religious merit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is numerical counting; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for "regarding" or "classifying" something as praiseworthy without objective basis.
- Root: ع م م (ʿ- m - m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Generality, commonality; the masses as opposed to the elite (al-khāṣṣah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, al-ʿāmmah refers to those who lack rigorous demonstrative reasoning (burhān) and rely on custom or authority (taqlīd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: covering all; metaphorical: the unlettered populace whose judgments are not grounded in verified knowledge.
- Root: ح م د (ḥ - m - d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Praise, commendation; that which is worthy of gratitude and acclaim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious sciences, maḥmūd (praiseworthy) is that which leads to salvation (najāh) and proximity to God, not merely what is socially esteemed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: verbal praise; here used in the technical sense of "approved by the Sacred Law" (sharʿ), not by popular opinion.
- Sībawayh Rule: **Al-ʿAṭf bi-lā Takrār** (Coordination without repetition) — The phrase "wa laysa minhā" (and it is not of them) functions as a restrictive clause, clarifying that the category named in the heading is only nominally included by the masses, not in reality. The particle "min" here is partitive, indicating exclusion from the true set.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the third section, concerning that which the common people (al-ʿāmmah) enumerate among the praiseworthy sciences (al-ʿulūm al-maḥmūdah), yet it is not truly of them. Know that the masses, being unacquainted with the realities of things and the ends of the religious law (al-sharīʿah), often mistake the outward forms of learning for its inner substance. They deem a science praiseworthy merely because it is widely practiced, or because it yields worldly benefit, or because it is associated with revered figures — not because it accords with the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ). Thus, they include in this category certain disciplines that are, in truth, either blameworthy (madhmūmah), or permissible but useless for the Hereafter, or even harmful to one's faith. It is incumbent upon the seeker of truth (ṭālib al-ḥaqq) to distinguish the genuine sciences — those that lead to knowledge of God and His attributes, and to the purification of the soul — from the counterfeit ones that merely parade in the garb of learning. For the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: {«مَنْ طَلَبَ الْعِلْمَ لِيُبَاهِيَ بِهِ الْعُلَمَاءَ أَوْ لِيُمَارِيَ بِهِ السُّفَهَاءَ أَوْ يَصْرِفَ بِهِ وُجُوهَ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ»} (Whoever seeks knowledge to vie with the scholars, or to dispute with the foolish, or to turn the faces of people toward him, he is in the Fire). So let the intelligent one not be deceived by the multitude of those who pursue such sciences, nor by their prestige among the masses; rather, let him weigh every science against the scale of the Law and the purpose of the Hereafter, and accept only that which brings him nearer to God, and reject all else, however adorned it may appear.

chapters.title_en: On the Explanation of the Aspects by Which Some Sciences Are Blameworthy, the Alteration of the Names of the Sciences, and the Praiseworthy vs. Blameworthy Measure of the Religious Sciences
chapters.arabic_text:
وفيه بيان الوجه الذي قد يكون به بعض العلوم مذموما وبيان تبديل أسامي
العلوم وهو الفقه والعلم والتوحيد والتذكير والحكمة وبيان القدر المحمود من
العلوم الشرعية والقدر المذموم منها
بيان علة ذم العلم المذموم لعلك تقول العلم هو معرفة الشيء على ما هو به
وهو من صفات الله تعالى فكيف يكون الشيء علما ويكون مع كونه علما مذموما
فاعلم أن العلم لا يذم لعينه وإنما يذم في حق العباد لأحد أسباب ثلاثة
الأول أن يكون مؤديا إلى ضرر ما إما لصاحبه أو لغيره كما يذم علم السحر
والطلسمات وهو حق إذ شهد القرآن له وأنه سبب يتوصل به إلى التفرقة بين
الزوجين وقد سحر (1) رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومرض بسببه حتى أخبره
جبريل عليه السلام بذلك وأخرج السحر من تحت حجر في قعر بئر وهو نوع يستفاد
من العلم بخواص الجواهر وبأمور حسابية في مطالع النجوم فيتخذ من تلك
الجواهر هيكل على صورة الشخص المسحور ويرصد به وقت مخصوص من المطالع وتقرن
به كلمات يتلفظ بها من الكفر والفحش المخالف للشرع ويتوصل بسببها إلى
الاستعانة بالشياطين ويحصل من مجموع ذلك بحكم إجراء الله تعالى العادة
أحوال غريبة في الشخص المسحور ومعرفة هذه الأسباب من حيث إنها معرفة ليست
بمذمومة ولكنها ليست تصلح إلا للإضرار بالخلق والوسيلة إلى الشر شر فكان
ذلك هو السبب في كونه علما مذموما بل من اتبع وليا من أولياء الله ليقتله
وقد اختفى منه في موضع  حريز إذا سأل الظالم عن محله لم يجز تنبيهه عليه بل
وجب الكذب فيه وذكر موضعه إرشاد وإفادة علم بالشيء على ما هو عليه ولكنه
مذموم لأدائه إلى الضرر
الثاني أن يكون مضرا بصاحبه في غالب الأمر كعلم النجوم فإنه في نفسه غير
مذموم لذاته إذ هو قسمان قسم حسابي وقد نطق القرآن بأن مسير الشمس والقمر
محسوب إذ قال عز وجل {الشمس والقمر بحسبان} وقال عز وجل {والقمر قدرناه
منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم} والثاني الأحكام وحاصله يرجع إلى الاستدلال
على الحوادث بالأسباب وهو يضاهي استدلال الطبيب بالنبض على ما سيحدث من
المرض وهو معرفة لمجاري سنة الله تعالى وعادته في خلقه ولكن قد ذمه الشرع
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا ذكر القدر فأمسكوا وإذا ذكرت النجوم فأمسكوا
وإذا ذكر أصحابي فأمسكوا (2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أخاف على أمتي بعدي ثلاثا حيف الأئمة والإيمان
بالنجوم والتكذيب بالقدر (3)
وقال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به في البر
والبحر ثم أمسكوا وإنما زجر عنه من ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه مضر بأكثر الخلق
فإنه إذا ألقي إليهم أن هذه الآثار تحدث عقيب سير الكواكب وقع في نفوسهم أن
الكواكب هي المؤثرة وأنها الآلهة المدبرة لأنها جواهر شريفة سماوية ويعظم
وقعها في القلوب فيبقى القلب ملتفتا إليها ويرى الخير والشر محذورا أو
مرجوا من جهتها PageV01P029
وينمحي ذكر الله سبحانه عن القلب فإنه الضعيف يقصر نظره على الوسائط
والعالم الراسخ هو الذي يطلع على أن الشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره
سبحانه وتعالى ومثال نظر الضعيف إلى حصول ضوء الشمس عقيب طلوع الشمس مثال
النملة لو خلق لها عقل وكانت على سطح قرطاس وهي تنظر إلى سواد الخط يتجدد
فتعتقد أنه فعل القلم ولا تترقى في نظرها إلى مشاهدة الأصابع ثم منها إلى
اليد ثم منها إلى الإرادة المحركة اليد ثم منها إلى الكاتب القادر المريد
ثم منه إلى خالق اليد والقدرة والإرادة فأكثر نظر الخلق مقصور  على الأسباب
القريبة السافلة مقطوع من الترقي إلى مسبب الأسباب فهذا أحد أسباب النهي عن
النجوم
وثانيها أن أحكام النجوم تخمين محض ليس يدرك في حق آحاد الأشخاص لا يقينا
ولا ظنا فالحكم به حكم يجهل فيكون ذمه على هذا من حيث أنه جهل لا من حيث
إنه علم فلقد كان ذلك معجزة لإدريس عليه السلام فيما يحكى وقد اندرس وانمحى
ذلك العلم وانمحق وما يتفق من إصابة المنجم على ندور فهو اتفاق لأنه قد
يطلع على بعض الأسباب ولا يحصل المسبب عقيبها إلا بعد شروط كثيرة ليس في
قدرة البشر الاطلاع على حقائقها فإن اتفق أن قدر الله تعالى بقية الأسباب
وقعت الإصابة وإن لم يقدر أخطأ ويكون ذلك كتخمين الإنسان في أن السماء تمطر
اليوم مهما رأى الغيم يجتمع وينبعث من الجبال فيتحرك ظنه بذلك وربما يحمى
النهار بالشمس ويذهب الغيم وربما يكون بخلافه ومجرد الغيم ليس كافيا في
مجيء المطر وبقية الأسباب لا تدرى وكذلك تخمين الملاح أن السفينة تسلم
اعتمادا على ما ألفه من العادة في الرياح ولتلك الرياح أسباب خفية هو لا
يطلع عليها فتارة يصيب في تخمينه وتارة يخطىء ولهذه العلة يمنع القول عن
النجوم أيضا
وثالثها أنه لا فائدة فيه فأقل أحواله أنه خوض في فضول لا يغني وتضييع
العمر الذي هو أنفس بضاعة الإنسان في غير فائدة وذلك غاية الخسران فقد مر
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم برجل والناس مجتمعون عليه فقال ما هذا فقالوا
رجل علامة فقال بماذا قالوا بالشعر وأنساب العرب فقال علم لا ينفع وجهل لا
يضر (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما العلم آية محكمة أو سنة قائمة أو
فريضة عادلة فإذن الخوض في النجوم وما يشبهه اقتحام خطر وخوض في جهالة من
غير فائدة فإن ما قدر كائن والاحتراز منه غير ممكن بخلاف الطب فإن الحاجة
ماسة إليه وأكثر أدلته بما يطلع عليه وبخلاف التعبير وإن كان تخمينا لأنه
جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءا من النبوة  ولا خطر فيه
السبب الثالث الخوض في علم لا يستفيد الخائض فيه فائدة علم فهو مذموم في
حقه كتعلم دقيق العلوم قبل جليلها وخفيها قبل جليها وكالبحث عن الأسرار
الإلهية إذ يطلع الفلاسفة والمتكلمون إليها ولم يستقلوا بها ولم يستقل بها
وبالوقوف على طرق بعضها إلا الأنبياء والأولياء فيجب كف الناس عن البحث
عنها وردهم إلى ما نطق به الشرع ففي ذلك مقنع للموفق فكم من شخص خاض في
العلوم واستضر بها ولو لم يخض فيها لكان حاله أحسن في الدين مما صار إليه
ولا ينكر كون العلم ضارا لبعض الناس كما يضر لحم الطير وأنواع الحلوى
اللطيفة بالصبي الرضيع بل رب شخص ينفعه الجهل ببعض الأمور فلقد حكي أن بعض
الناس شكا إلى طبيب عقم امرأته وأنها لا تلد فجس الطبيب نبضها وقال لا حاجة
لك إلى دواء الولادة فإنك ستموتين إلى PageV01P030
أربعين يوما وقد دل النبض عليه فاستشعرت المرأة الخوف العظيم وتنغص عليها
عيشها وأخرجت أموالها وفرقتها وأوصت وبقيت لا تأكل ولا تشرب حتى انقضت
المدة فلم تمت فجاء زوجها إلى الطبيب وقال له لم تمت فقال الطبيب قد علمت
ذلك فجامعها الآن فإنها تلد فقال كيف ذاك قال رأيتها سمينة وقد انعقد الشحم
على فم رحمها فعلمت أنها لا تهزل إلا بخوف الموت فخوفتها بذلك حتى هزلت
وزال المانع من الولادة فهذا ينبهك على استشعار خطر بعض العلوم ويفهمك معنى
قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعوذ بالله من علم لا ينفع (1) فاعتبر بهذه
الحكاية ولا تكن بحاثا عن علوم ذمها الشرع وزجر عنها ولازم الاقتداء
بالصحابة رضي الله عنهم واقتصر على اتباع السنة فالسلامة في الاتباع والخطر
في البحث عن الأشياء والاستقلال ولا تكثر اللجج برأيك ومعقولك ودليلك
وبرهانك وزعمك أني أبحث عن الأشياء لأعرفها على ما هي عليه فأي ضرر في
التفكر في العلم فإن ما يعود عليك من ضرره أكثر وكم من شيء تطلع عليه فيضرك
اطلاعك عليه ضررا يكاد يهلكك في الآخرة إن لم  يتداركك الله برحمته
واعلم أنه كما يطلع الطبيب الحاذق على أسرار في المعالجات يستبعدها من لا
يعرفها فكذلك الأنبياء أطباء القلوب والعلماء بأسباب الحياة الأخروية فلا
تتحكم على سننهم بمعقولك فتهلك فكم من شخص يصيبه عارض في أصبعه فيقتضي عقله
أن يطليه حتى ينبهه الطبيب الحاذق أن علاجه أن بطلى الكف من الجانب الآخر
من البدن فيستبعد ذلك غاية الاستبعاد من حيث لا يعلم كيفية انشعاب الأعصاب
ومنابتها ووجه التفافها على البدن فهكذا الأمر في طريق الآخرة وفي دقائق
سنن الشرع وآدابه وفي عقائده التي تعبد الناس بها أسرار ولطائف ليست في سعة
العقل وقوته الإحاطة بها كما أن في خواص الأحجار أمورا عجائب غاب عن أهل
الصنعة علمها حتى لم يقدر أحد على أن يعرف السبب الذي به يجذب المغناطيس
الحديد فالعجائب والغرائب في العقائد والأعمال وإفادتها لصفاء القلوب
ونقائها وطهارتها وتزكيتها وإصلاحها للترقي إلى جوار الله تعالى وتعرضها
لنفحات فضله أكثر وأعظم مما في الأدوية والعقاقير وكما أن العقول تقصر عن
إدراك منافع الأدوية مع أن التجربة سبيل إليها فالعقول تقصر عن إدراك ما
ينفع في حياة الآخرة مع أن التجربة غير متطرقة إليها وإنما كانت التجربة
تتطرق إليها لو رجع إلينا بعض الأموات فأخبرنا عن الأعمال المقبولة النافعة
المقربة إلى الله تعالى زلفى وعن الأعمال المبعدة عنه وكذا عن العقائد وذلك
مما لا يطمع فيه فيكفيك من منفعة العقل أن يهديك إلى صدق النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم ويفهمك موارد إشاراته فاعزل العقل بعد ذلك عن التصرف ولازم
الاتباع فلا تسلم إلا به والسلام ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من العلم
جهلا وإن من القول عيا (2) ومعلوم أن العلم لا يكون جهلا ولكنه يؤثر تأثير
الجهل في الإضرار وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم قليل من التوفيق خير من
كثير من العلم (3) وقال عيسى عليه السلام ما أكثر الشجر وليس كلها بمثمر
وليس كلها بطيب وما أكثر العلوم وليس كلها بنافع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ م م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, censure, dispraise — the opposite of praise (ḥamd); denotes a quality that invites reproach.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, blameworthiness (dhamm) attaches to acts or objects not for their essence but for their consequential harm or their status as means (wasā'il) to evil.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) blame is directed at the act itself; metaphorical (majāz) blame is directed at the means that lead to harm, even if the act in itself is permissible or true.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, perception, certainty; the faculty of apprehending a thing as it is.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Knowledge (ʿilm) as an attribute of God is absolute and unqualified; for creatures, it is blameworthy only when it becomes a veil from the divine or a source of injury.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal knowledge is neutral; metaphorical blame applies when knowledge is termed 'ignorance' (jahl) due to its harmful effect, as in the prophetic saying «إن من العلم جهلا».
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Causal Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jazā') — The sentence «فكيف يكون الشيء علما ويكون مع كونه علما مذموما» employs an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī) followed by a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), governing the logical impossibility of simultaneous essence and blame.
chapters.translation:
I say: In this section is an explanation of the aspect by which some sciences may be blameworthy, and an explanation of the alteration of the names of the sciences — namely jurisprudence (fiqh), knowledge (ʿilm), divine unity (tawḥīd), admonition (tadhkīr), and wisdom (ḥikmah) — and an explanation of the praiseworthy measure of the religious sciences and the blameworthy measure thereof.

**An Explanation of the Cause of Blaming the Blameworthy Science**

Perhaps you will say: Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing as it is, and it is an attribute of God, exalted be He. How then can a thing be knowledge and, while being knowledge, be blameworthy? Know that knowledge is not blamed for its own essence; rather, it is blamed with respect to servants for one of three reasons.

**The First Reason:** That it leads to some harm, either to its possessor or to another. Thus is blamed the science of sorcery (siḥr) and talismans (ṭilasmāt) — and this is true, for the Qur'an bears witness to it, and it is a means by which one seeks to cause separation between a married couple. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was bewitched and fell ill thereby, until Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed him of that, and he extracted the sorcery from beneath a stone at the bottom of a well. This is a type derived from knowledge of the properties of substances (khavāṣṣ al-jawāhir) and from astronomical calculations concerning the risings of the stars. From those substances a figure is fashioned in the form of the bewitched person, and a specific time is observed from the risings, and words are coupled with it — utterances of disbelief and obscenity contrary to the Sacred Law — and by these means one seeks the aid of devils. From the totality of that, by the decree of Allah's running custom (ʿādah), strange conditions occur in the bewitched person. The knowledge of these causes, insofar as it is knowledge, is not blameworthy; but it is not suited except for harming creatures, and the means to evil is evil. That, then, was the reason for its being a blameworthy science. Nay, if a person follows a saint (walī) of Allah's saints to kill him, and he has hidden in a fortified place, and a tyrant asks about his location, it is not permissible to point him out; rather, lying therein is obligatory. Mentioning his location would be guidance and the imparting of knowledge of a thing as it is, but it is blameworthy because it leads to harm.

**The Second Reason:** That it is harmful to its possessor in most cases, like the science of the stars (ʿilm al-nujūm). For it is not in itself blameworthy in its essence, since it is of two kinds. One kind is computational (ḥisābī), and the Qur'an has spoken that the course of the sun and moon is computed, for He, mighty and majestic, said: {«الشمس والقمر بحسبان»} ("The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation") and He, mighty and majestic, said: {«والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم»} ("And the moon — We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old palm-stalk"). The second kind is the judgments (aḥkām), and its sum total reverts to inferring future events from causes. This resembles the physician's inference from the pulse concerning what illness will occur — it is knowledge of the courses of Allah's sunnah and His custom in His creation. But the Sacred Law has censured it. He, peace be upon him, said: "When destiny (qadar) is mentioned, refrain; when the stars are mentioned, refrain; when my Companions are mentioned, refrain." And he, peace be upon him, said: "I fear for my community after me three things: the tyranny of the leaders, belief in the stars, and denial of destiny." And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Learn from the stars that by which you are guided in land and sea, then refrain."

It was prohibited only from three aspects. **One of them:** That it is harmful to most creatures. For when it is cast to them that these effects occur consequent upon the motion of the planets, it falls into their souls that the planets are the effective agents and that they are the directing deities, because they are noble celestial substances. Their weight in hearts becomes great, so the heart remains turned toward them, and good and evil are seen as feared or hoped from their direction — and the remembrance of Allah, glorified be He, is effaced from the heart. For the weak one confines his gaze to the intermediate causes, whereas the deeply rooted scholar is he who perceives that the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjugated by His command, exalted be He. The example of the weak one's gaze at the occurrence of sunlight consequent upon the rising of the sun is like the example of an ant — if intelligence were created for it, and it were on the surface of a page, and it looked at the blackness of the script renewing itself, it would believe that it is the act of the pen, and it would not ascend in its gaze to the sight of the fingers, then from them to the hand, then from it to the will moving the hand, then from it to the powerful, willing writer, then from him to the Creator of the hand, the power, and the will. Thus most of the gaze of creatures is confined to the near, lowly causes, cut off from ascending to the Causer of causes. This is one of the reasons for the prohibition of the stars.

**The Second of Them:** That the judgments of the stars are pure conjecture (takhmīn), not apprehended with respect to individual persons — neither with certainty nor with strong opinion. Thus to judge by them is to judge by ignorance, so its censure on this account is insofar as it is ignorance, not insofar as it is knowledge. Indeed, that was a miracle of Idrīs, peace be upon him, as is narrated — and that science has become effaced and obliterated. What happens of the astrologer's hitting the mark on rare occasions is by coincidence, for he may perceive some of the causes, but the effect does not occur consequent upon them except after many conditions whose realities are not within human power to perceive. If Allah, exalted be He, decrees the remainder of the causes, the hit occurs; if He does not decree, it misses. This is like a man's conjecture that it will rain today whenever he sees clouds gathering and rising from the mountains, so his opinion moves to that — and perhaps the day heats up with the sun and the clouds disperse, and perhaps it is otherwise. Mere clouds are not sufficient for the coming of rain, and the remainder of the causes are unknown. Likewise is the sailor's conjecture that the ship will be safe, relying on what he has habituated of the custom in winds — and those winds have hidden causes upon which he does not alight. Sometimes he hits in his conjecture and sometimes he misses. For this reason, speech about the stars is also prevented.

**The Third of Them:** That there is no benefit in it. The least of its states is that it is wading into superfluities that avail nothing, and the wasting of one's life — which is the most precious commodity of a human being — in that which has no benefit. That is the utmost loss. For the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, passed by a man with people gathered around him, and he said: "What is this?" They said: "A man of great learning (ʿallāmah)." He said: "In what?" They said: "In poetry and the genealogies of the Arabs." He said: "A knowledge that does not benefit, and an ignorance that does not harm." And he, peace be upon him, said: "Knowledge is only a confirmed verse (āyah muḥkamah), or an established sunnah (sunnah qā'imah), or an equitable obligation (farīḍah ʿādilah)." Thus wading into the stars and what resembles it is the plunging into danger and wading into ignorance without benefit. For what is decreed will be, and guarding against it is not possible — unlike medicine, for the need for it is pressing, and most of its evidences are by what one perceives; and unlike dream interpretation (taʿbīr), even though it is conjecture, for it is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy, and there is no danger in it.

**The Third Reason:** Wading into a science from which the wader derives no benefit of knowledge — it is blameworthy with respect to him, like learning the subtle parts of the sciences before their grand parts, and their hidden aspects before their manifest ones; and like the investigation of divine secrets (al-asrār al-ilāhiyyah), which the philosophers and the theologians (mutakallimūn) have sought to ascend to but have not been able to stand on their own therein, nor has anyone stood on some of their paths except the prophets and the saints. It is therefore obligatory to restrain people from investigating them and to return them to what the Sacred Law has spoken — in that is sufficiency for the one granted success. How many a person has waded into the sciences and been harmed by them, whereas had he not waded into them, his state in religion would have been better than what he came to! And it is not to be denied that knowledge is harmful to some people, just as the meat of birds and delicate kinds of sweets harm the suckling infant. Nay, perhaps a person is benefited by ignorance of some matters. For it is narrated that a certain man complained to a physician about his wife's barrenness and that she did not give birth. The physician felt her pulse and said: "You have no need of a medicine for childbirth, for you will die within forty days" — and the pulse had indicated that. The woman was seized by great fear, her life became bitter to her, she brought out her wealth and distributed it, made her will, and remained neither eating nor drinking until the period elapsed — and she did not die. Her husband came to the physician and said: "She did not die." The physician said: "I knew that. Now have intercourse with her, for she will give birth." He said: "How is that?" He said: "I saw that she was fat, and the fat had congealed over the mouth of her womb, and I knew that she would not become thin except by the fear of death. So I frightened her with that until she became thin, and the obstacle to childbirth was removed."

This alerts you to the apprehension of the danger of some sciences and makes you understand the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: "We seek refuge in Allah from knowledge that does not benefit." So take heed of this anecdote, and be not a researcher into sciences that the Sacred Law has censured and prohibited. Adhere to the emulation of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and confine yourself to following the Sunnah. For safety is in following, and danger is in investigating things and seeking to stand independently. Do not multiply arguments with your opinion, your intellect, your proof, and your demonstration, claiming: "I investigate things to know them as they are — what harm is there in reflecting upon knowledge?" For what returns upon you of its harm is greater. How many a thing you alight upon, and your alighting upon it harms you with a harm that almost destroys you in the Hereafter, unless Allah overtakes you with His mercy!

Know that just as the skilled physician alights upon secrets in treatments that those who do not know them find remote, so likewise the prophets are the physicians of hearts, and the scholars are the knowers of the causes of the life of the Hereafter. So do not impose your intellect upon their ways, lest you perish. How many a person is struck by an ailment in his finger, and his intellect dictates that he apply ointment to it — until the skilled physician alerts him that his treatment is to apply ointment to the palm of the hand from the other side of the body, and he finds that utterly remote, not knowing the manner of the branching of the nerves, their origins, and the aspect of their winding over the body. Thus is the matter in the path of the Hereafter, in the subtleties of the ways of the Sacred Law and its etiquettes, and in its beliefs by which people are bound to worship — there are secrets and subtleties not within the capacity and power of the intellect to encompass. Just as in the properties of stones there are wondrous matters whose knowledge is hidden from the people of the craft, so that no one is able to know the cause by which the magnet attracts iron — so the wonders and marvels in the beliefs and the works, and their imparting of purity to hearts, their cleansing, their sanctification, their purification, and their rectification for ascending to the vicinity of Allah, exalted be He, and their exposure to the breezes of His bounty — are more and greater than what is in medicines and drugs. And just as intellects fall short of apprehending the benefits of medicines, though experience is a path to them, so intellects fall short of apprehending what benefits in the life of the Hereafter, while experience does not extend to them. Experience would extend to them only if some of the dead returned to us and informed us of the accepted, beneficial works that draw near to Allah, exalted be He, in proximity, and of the works that distance from Him — and likewise of the beliefs. But that is something not to be hoped for. It suffices you of the benefit of the intellect that it guides you to the truthfulness of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and makes you understand the points of his allusions. Then, after that, remove the intellect from independent disposition and adhere to following — for you will not be saved except by it. And peace.

Therefore he, peace be upon him, said: "Verily, from knowledge there is ignorance, and from speech there is inability." And it is known that knowledge does not become ignorance, but it produces the effect of ignorance in causing harm. And he also said, peace be upon him: "A little of divine success (tawfīq) is better than much knowledge." And Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "How many are the trees, but not all of them bear fruit, and not all of them are good; and how many are the sciences, but not all of them are beneficial."

chapters.title_en: Exposition of What Has Been Altered from the Terminologies of the Sciences
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان ما بدل من  ألفاظ العلوم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Substitution, exchange, replacement of one thing for another; alteration of a word from its original form or meaning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes the corruption or displacement of revealed or technical terms from their intended significations, often leading to doctrinal confusion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical replacement of an object; metaphorical (majāz) = semantic shift in terminology, especially when later scholars alter the established nomenclature of earlier authorities.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, science, perception of a thing as it truly is; also the disciplines and bodies of knowledge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as the stable comprehension of reality; in technical usage, the systematic sciences (ʿulūm) with their fixed terminologies.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = knowledge as a mental act; metaphorical = the corpus of transmitted and rational sciences with their conventional vocabularies.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with an implied predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — the phrase «بيان ما بدل» functions as a heading (title), where the genitive construction (iḍāfah) governs the relative clause «ما بدل», indicating a specific exposition of that which has been altered.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us set forth an exposition of what has been altered from the terminologies of the sciences — that is, how the names and technical expressions used by the early scholars (al-salaf) have been displaced, either in their application or in their meanings, by later practitioners, such that the original intent has become obscured. Know that this alteration (tabdīl) is of two kinds: one pertains to the words themselves being transferred from their primary referents to other referents, and the other pertains to the meanings being narrowed or widened beyond their original scope. It is incumbent upon the seeker of truth to discern these changes, lest he be deceived by the outward agreement of terms while their inner significations have been corrupted.

chapters.title_en: The Origin of Confusion Between Blameworthy and Religious Sciences: The Five Corrupted Terms
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن منشأ التباس العلوم المذمومة بالعلوم الشرعية تحريف الأسامي
المحمودة وتبديلها ونقلها بالأغراض PageV01P031
الفاسدة إلى معان غير ما أراده السلف الصالح والقرن الأول وهي خمسة ألفاظ
الفقه والعلم والتوحيد والتذكير والحكمة فهذه أسام محمودة والمتصفون بها
أرباب المناصب في الدين ولكنها نقلت الآن إلى معان مذمومة فصارت القلوب
تنفر عن مذمة من يتصف بمعانيها لشيوع إطلاق هذه الأسامي عليهم
اللفظ الأول الفقه فقد تصرفوا فيه بالتخصيص لا بالنقل والتحويل إذا خصصوه
بمعرفة الفروع الغريبة في الفتاوي والوقوف على دقائق عللها واستكثار الكلام
فيها وحفظ المقالات المتعلقة بها فمن كان أشد تعمقا فيها وأكثر اشتغالا بها
يقال هو الأفقه ولقد كان اسم الفقه في العصر الأول مطلقا على علم طريق
الآخرة ومعرفة دقائق آفات النفوس ومفسدات الأعمال وقوة الإحاطة بحقارة
الدنيا وشدة التطلع إلى نعيم الآخرة واستيلاء الخوف على القلب ويدلك عليه
قوله عز وجل {ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم} وما يحصل
به الإنذار والتخويف هو هذا الفقه دون تفريعات الطلاق والعتاق واللعان
والسلم والإجارة فذلك لا يحصل به إنذار ولا تخويف بل التجرد له على الدوام
يقسي القلب وينزع الخشية منه كما نشاهد الآن من المتجردين له
وقال تعالى {لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها} وأراد به معاني الإيمان دون الفتاوى
ولعمري إن الفقه والفهم في اللغة اسمان بمعنى واحد وإنما يتكلم في عادة
الاستعمال به قديما وحديثا
قال تعالى {لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله} الآية فأحال قلة خوفهم من
الله واستعظامهم سطوة الخلق على قلة الفقه فانظر إن كان ذلك نتيجة عدم
الحفظ لتفريعات الفتاوى أو هو نتيجة عدم ما ذكرناه من العلوم
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم علماء فقهاء (1) للذين وفدوا عليه وسئل سعد بن
إبراهيم الزهري رحمه الله أي أهل المدينة أفقه فقال أتقاهم لله تعالى فكأنه
أشار إلى ثمرة الفقه والتقوى ثمرة العلم الباطني دون الفتاوى والأقضية
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا أنبئكم بالفقيه كل الفقيه قالوا بلى  قال من
لم يقنط الناس من رحمة الله ولم يؤمنهم من مكر الله ولم يؤيسهم من روح الله
ولم يدع القرآن رغبة عنه إلى ما سواه (2) ولما روى أنس بن مالك قوله صلى
الله عليه وسلم لأن أقعد مع قوم يذكرون الله تعالى من غدوة إلى طلوع الشمس
أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب (3) قال فالتفت إلى زيد الرقاشي وزياد
النميري وقال لم تكن مجالس الذكر مثل مجالسكم هذه يقص أحدكم وعظه على
أصحابه ويسرد الحديث سردا إنما كنا نقعد فنذكر الإيمان ونتدبر القرآن
ونتفقه في الدين ونعد نعم الله علينا تفقها فسمي تدبر القرآن وعد النعم
تفقها
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يفقه العبد كل الفقه حتى يمقت الناس في ذات
الله وحتى يرى القرآن وجوها كثيرة (4) وروى أيضا موقوفا على أبي الدرداء
رضي الله عنه مع قوله ثم يقبل على نفسه فيكون لها أشد مقتا وقد سأل فرقد
السبخي الحسن عن الشيء فأجابه فقال إن الفقهاء يخالفونك فقال الحسن رحمه
الله ثكلتك أمك فريقد وهل رأيت فقيها بعينك إنما الفقيه الزاهد في الدنيا
الراغب في الآخرة البصير بدينه المداوم على عبادة ربه الورع الكاف نفسه عن
أعراض المسلمين العفيف عن أموالهم الناصح لجماعتهم ولم يقل في جميع في ذلك
الحافظ لفروع الفتاوى ولست أقول إن اسم الفقه لم يكن متناولا للفتاوى في
الأحكام الظاهرة ولكن كان بطريق PageV01P032
العموم والشمول أو بطريق الاستتباع فكان إطلاقهم له على علم الآخرة أكثر
فبان من هذا التخصيص تلبيس بعث الناس على التجرد له والإعراض عن علم
الآخرة وأحكام القلوب ووجدوا على ذلك معينا من الطبع فإن علم الباطن غامض
والعمل به عسير والتوصل به إلى طلب الولاية والقضاء والجاه والمال متعذر
فوجد الشيطان مجالا لتحسين ذلك في القلوب بواسطة تخصيص اسم الفقه الذي هو
اسم محمود في الشرع
اللفظ الثاني العلم وقد كان يطلق ذلك على العلم بالله تعالى وبآياته
وبأفعاله في عباده وخلقه حتى أنه لما مات عمر رضي  الله عنه قال ابن مسعود
رحمه الله لقد مات تسعة أعشار العلم فعرفه بالألف واللام ثم فسره العلم
بالله سبحانه وتعالى وقد تصرفوا فيه أيضا بالتخصيص حتى شهروه في الأكثر بمن
يشتغل بالمناظرة مع الخصوم في المسائل الفقهية وغيرها فيقال هو العالم على
الحقيقة وهو الفحل في العلم ومن لا يمارس ذلك ولا يشتغل به يعد من جملة
الضعفاء ولا يعدونه في زمرة أهل العلم
وهذا أيضا تصرف بالتخصيص ولكن ما ورد من فضائل العلم والعلماء أكثره في
العلماء بالله تعالى وبأحكامه وبأفعاله وصفاته
وقد صار الآن مطلقا على من لا يحيط من علوم الشرع بشيء سوى رسوم جدلية في
مسائل خلافية فيعد بذلك من فحول العلماء مع جهله بالتفسير والأخبار وعلم
المذهب وغيره وصار ذلك سببا مهلكا لخلق كثير من أهل الطلب للعلم
اللفظ الثالث التوحيد وقد جعل الآن عبارة عن صناعة الكلام ومعرفة طريق
المجادلة والإحاطة بطرق مناقضات الخصوم والقدرة على التشدق فيها بتكثير
الأسئلة وإثارة الشبهات وتأليف الإلزامات حتى لقب طوائف منهم أنفسهم بأهل
العدل والتوحيد وسمى المتكلمون العلماء بالتوحيد مع أن جميع ما هو خاصة هذه
الصناعة لم يكن يعرف منها شيء في العصر الأول بل كان يشتد منهم النكير على
من كان يفتح بابا من الجدل والمماراة فأما ما يشتمل عليه القرآن من الأدلة
الظاهرة التي تسبق الأذهان إلى قبولها في أول السماع فلقد كان ذلك معلوما
للكل وكان العلم بالقرآن هو العلم كله وكان التوحيد عندهم عبارة عن أمر آخر
لا يفهمه أكثر المتكلمين وإن فهموه لم يتصفوا به وهو أن يرى الأمور كلها من
الله عز وجل رؤية تقطع التفاته عن الأسباب والوسائط فلا يرى الخير والشر
كله إلا منه جل جلاله فهذا مقام شريف إحدى ثمراته التوكل كما سيأتي بيانه
في كتاب التوكل
ومن ثمراته أيضا ترك شكاية الخلق وترك الغضب عليهم والرضا والتسليم لحكم
الله تعالى
وكانت إحدى ثمراته قول أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه لما قيل له في مرضه
أنطلب لك طبيبا فقال الطبيب أمرضني وقول آخر لما مرض فقيل له ماذا قال لك
الطبيب في مرضك فقال قال لي إني فعال لما أريد
وسيأتي في كتاب التوكل وكتاب التوحيد شواهد ذلك
والتوحيد جو هو نفيس وله قشران أحدهما أبعد عن اللب من الآخر فخصص الناس
الاسم بالقشر وبصنعة الحراسة للقشر وأهملوا اللب بالكلية فالقشر الأول هو
أن تقول بلسانك لا إله إلا الله وهذا يسمى توحيدا مناقضا للتثليث الذي صرح
به النصارى ولكنه قد يصدر من المنافق الذي يخالف سره جهره
والقشر الثاني أن لا يكون في القلب مخالفة وإنكار لمفهوم هذا القول بل
يشتمل ظاهر القلب على اعتقاده وكذلك التصديق به وهو توحيد عوام الخلق
والمتكلمون كما سبق حراس هذا القشر عن تشويش المبتدعة
والثالث وهو اللباب أن يرى الأمور كلها من الله تعالى رؤية تقطع التفاته
عن الوسائط وأن يعبده عبادة يفرده بها فلا يعبد غيره ويخرج عن هذا التوحيد
اتباع الهوى فكل متبع هواه فقد اتخذ هواه معبوده
قال الله تعالى {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبغض
إله عبد في الأرض
PageV01P033
عند الله تعالى هو الهوى (1) وعلى التحقيق من تأمل عرف أن عابد الصنم ليس
يعبد الصنم وإنما يعبد هواه إذ نفسه مائلة إلى دين آبائه فيتبع ذلك الميل
وميل النفس إلى المألوفات أحد المعاني التي يعبر عنها بالهوى ويخرج من هذا
التوحيد التسخط على الخلق والالتفات إليهم فإن من يرى الكل من الله عز وجل
كيف يتسخط على غيره فلقد كان التوحيد عبارة عن هذا المقام وهو مقام
الصديقين فانظر إلى ماذا حول وبأي قشر قنع منه وكيف اتخذوا هذا معتصما في
التمدح والتفاخر بما اسمه محمود مع الإفلاس عن المعنى الذي يستحق الحمد
الحقيقي وذلك كإفلاس من يصبح بكرة ويتوجه إلى القبلة ويقول وجهت وجهي للذي
فطر السموات والأرض حنيفا وهو أول كذب يفاتح الله به كل يوم إن لم يكن وجه
قلبه متوجها إلى الله تعالى على  الخصوص فإنه إن أراد بالوجه وجه الظاهر فما
وجهه إلا إلى الكعبة وما صرفه إلا عن سائر الجهات والكعبة ليست جهة للذي
فطر السموات والأرض حتى يكون المتوجه إليها متوجها إليه تعالى عن أن تحده
الجهات والأقطار
وإن أراد به وجه القلب وهو المطلوب المتعبد به فكيف يصدق في قوله وقلبه
متردد في أوطاره وحاجاته الدنيوية ومتصرف في طلب الحيل في جمع الأموال
والجاه واستكثار الأسباب ومتوجه بالكلية إليها فمتى وجه وجهه للذي فطر
السموات والأرض وهذه الكلمة خبر عن حقيقة التوحيد فالموحد هو الذي لا يرى
إلا الواحد ولا يوجه وجهه إلا إليه وهو امتثال قوله تعالى {قل الله ثم ذرهم
في خوضهم يلعبون} وليس المراد به القول باللسان فإنما اللسان ترجمان يصدق
مرة ويكذب أخرى
وإنما موقع نظر الله تعالى المترجم عنه هو القلب وهو معدن التوحيد ومنبعه
اللفظ الرابع الذكر والتذكير فقد قال الله تعالى {وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع
المؤمنين} وقد ورد في الثناء على مجالس الذكر أخبار كثيرة كقوله صلى الله
عليه وسلم إذا مررتم برياض الجنة فارتعوا قيل وما رياض الجنة قال مجالس
الذكر (2) وفي الحديث إن لله تعالى ملائكة سياحين في الدنيا سوى ملائكة
الخلق إذا رأوا مجالس الذكر ينادي بعضهم بعضا ألا هلموا إلى بغيتكم
فيأتونهم ويحفون بهم ويستمعون ألا فاذكروا الله وذكروا أنفسكم (3) فنقل ذلك
إلى ما ترى أكثر الوعاظ في هذا الزمان يواظبون عليه وهو القصص والأشعار
والشطح والطامات أما القصص فهي بدعة وقد ورد نهي السلف عن الجلوس إلى
القصاص وقالوا لم يكن ذلك في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (4) ولا في
زمن أبي بكر ولا عمر رضي الله عنهما حتى ظهرت الفتنة وظهر القصاص وروي أن
ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما خرج من المسجد فقال ما أخرجني إلا القاص ولولاه لما
خرجت
وقال ضمرة قلت لسفيان الثوري نستقبل القاص بوجوهنا فقال ولوا البدع
ظهوركم وقال ابن عون دخلت على ابن سيرين فقال ما كان اليوم من خبر  فقلت نهى
الأمير القصاص أن يقصوا فقال وفق للصواب
ودخل الأعمش جامع البصرة فرأى قاصا يقص ويقول حدثنا الأعمش فتوسط الحلقة
وجعل ينتف شعر إبطه فقال القاص يا شيخ ألا تستحي فقال لم أنا في سنة وأنت
في كذب أنا الأعمش وما حدثتك وقال أحمد أكثر الناس كذبا القصاص والسؤال
وأخرج علي رضي الله عنه القصاص من مسجد جامع البصرة PageV01P034
فلما سمع كلام الحسن البصري لم يخرجه إذا كان يتكلم في علم الآخرة
والتفكير بالموت والتنبيه على عيوب النفس وآفات الأعمال وخواطر الشيطان
ووجه الحذر منها ويذكر بآلاء الله ونعمائه وتقصير العبد في شكره ويعرف
حقارة الدنيا وعيوبها وتصرمها ونكث عهدها وخطر الآخرة وأهوالها فهذا هو
التذكير المحمود شرعا الذي روى الحث عليه في حديث أبي ذر رضي الله عنه حيث
قال حضور مجلس ذكر أفضل من صلاة ألف ركعة وحضور مجلس علم أفضل من عيادة ألف
مريض وحضور مجلس علم أفضل من شهود ألف جنازة فقيل يا رسول الله ومن قراءة
القرآن قال وهل تنفع قراءة القرآن إلا بالعلم (1) وقال عطاء رحمه الله مجلس
ذكر يكفر سبعين مجلسا من مجالس اللهو فقد اتخذ المزخرفون هذه الأحاديث حجة
على تزكية أنفسهم ونقلوا اسم التذكير إلى خرافاتهم وذهلوا عن طريق الذكر
المحمود واشتغلوا بالقصص التي تتطرق إليها الاختلافات والزيادة والنقص
وتخرج عن القصص الواردة في القرآن وتزيد عليها فإن من القصص ما ينفع سماعه
ومنها ما يضر وإن كان صدقا
ومن فتح ذلك الباب على نفسه اختلط عليه الصدق بالكذب والنافع بالضار فمن
هذا نهي عنه ولذلك قال أحمد بن حنبل رحمة الله ما أحوج الناس إلى قاص صادق
فإن كانت القصة من قصص الأنبياء عليهم السلام فيما يتعلق بأمور دينهم وكان
القاص صادقا صحيح الرواية فلست أرى بها بأسا فليحذر الكذب وحكايات أحوال
تومىء إلى هفوات أو مساهلات يقصر فهم العوام عن درك معانيها أو عن كونها
هفوة نادرة مردفة بتفكيرات متداركة بحسنات تغطي عليها فإن العامي يعتصم
بذلك في  مساهلاته وهفواته ويمهد لنفسه عذرا فيه ويحتج بأنه حكى كيت وكيت عن
بعض المشايخ وبعض الأكابر فكلنا بصدد المعاصي فلا غرو إن عصيت الله تعالى
فقد عصاه من هو أكبر مني ويفيده ذلك جراءة على الله تعالى من حيث لا يدري
فبعد الاحتراز عن هذين المحذورين فلا بأس به وعند ذلك يرجع إلى القصص
المحمودة وإلى ما يشتمل عليه القرآن ويصح في الكتب الصحيحة من الأخبار ومن
الناس من يستجيز وضع الحكايات المرغبة في الطاعات ويزعم أن قصده فيها دعوة
الخلق إلى الحق فهذه من نزعات الشيطان فإن في الصدق مندوحة عن الكذب وفيما
ذكر الله تعالى ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم غنية عن الاختراع في الوعظ كيف
وقد كره تكلف السجع وعد ذلك من التصنع
قال سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه لابنه عمر وقد سمعه يسجع هذا الذي
يبغضك إلي لا قضيت حاجتك أبدا حتى تتوب وقد كان جاءه في حاجة وقد قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم لعبد الله بن رواحة في سجع من ثلاث كلمات إياك والسجع يا
ابن رواحة (2) فكأن السجع المحذور المتكلف ما زاد على كلمتين ولذلك لما قال
الرجل في دية الجنين كيف ندى من لا شرب ولا أكل ولا صاح ولا استهل ومثل ذلك
يطل فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أسجع كسجع الأعراب (3)
وأما الأشعار فتكثيرها في المواعظ مذموم
قال الله تعالى {والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون}
وقال تعالى {وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له} وأكثر ما اعتاده الوعاظ من
الأشعار ما يتعلق بالتواصف في العشق وجمال المعشوق وروح الوصال وألم الفراق
والمجلس لا يحوي إلا أجلاف العوام وبواطنهم مشحونة بالشهوات وقلوبهم غير
منفكة عن الالتفات إلى الصور المليحة فلا تحرك الأشعار من قلوبهم إلا ما هو
مستكن PageV01P035
فيها فتشتعل فيها نيران الشهوات فيزعقون ويتواجدون وأكثر ذلك أو كله يرجع
إلى نوع فساد فلا ينبغي أن يستعمل من الشعر إلا ما فيه موعظة أو حكمة على
سبيل استشهاد واستئناس
وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من الشعر لحكمة (1) ولو حوى المجلس الخواص
الذين وقع الاطلاع على استغراق قلوبهم بحب الله تعالى ولم يكن معهم غيرهم
فإن أولئك لا يضر معهم الشعر الذي يشير ظاهره إلى الخلق فإن المستمع ينزل
كل ما يسمعه على ما يستولي على قلبه كما سيأتي تحقيق ذلك في كتاب السماع
ولذلك كان الجنيد رحمه الله يتكلم على بضعة عشر رجلا فإن كثروا لم يتكلم
وما تم أهل مجلسه قط عشرين
وحضر جماعة باب دار ابن سالم فقيل له تكلم فقد حضر أصحابك فقال لا ما
هؤلاء أصحابي إنما هم أصحاب المجلس إن أصحابي هم الخواص وأما الشطح فنعني
به صنفين من الكلام أحدثه بعض الصوفية
أحدهما الدعاوي الطويلة العريضة في العشق مع الله تعالى والوصال المغني
عن الأعمال الظاهرة حتى ينتهي قوم إلى دعوى الاتحاد وارتفاع الحجاب
والمشاهدة بالرؤية والمشافهة بالخطاب فيقولون قيل لنا كذا وقلنا كذا
ويتشبهون فيه بالحسين بن منصور الحلاج الذي صلب لأجل إطلاقه كلمات من هذا
الجنس ويستشهدون بقوله أنا الحق وبما حكي عن أبي يزيد البسطامي أنه قال
سبحاني سبحاني وهذا فن من الكلام عظيم ضرره في العوام حتى ترك جماعة من أهل
الفلاحة فلاحتهم وأظهروا مثل هذه الدعاوي فإن هذا الكلام يستلذه الطبع إذ
فيه البطالة من الأعمال مع تزكية النفس بدرك المقامات والأحوال فلا تعجز
الأغبياء عن دعوى ذلك لأنفسهم ولا عن تلقف كلمات مخبطة مزخرفة ومهما أنكر
عليهم ذلك لم يعجزوا عن أن يقولوا هذا إنكار مصدره العلم والجدال والعلم
حجاب والجدل عمل النفس وهذا الحديث لا يلوح إلا من الباطن بمكاشفة نور الحق
فهذا ومثله مما قد استطار في البلاد شرره وعظم في العوام ضرره حتى من نطق
بشيء منه فقتله أفضل في دين الله من إحياء عشرة وأما أبو يزيد البسطامي
رحمه الله فلا يصح عنه ما يحكى وإن سمع ذلك منه فلعله كان يحكيه عن الله عز
وجل في كلام  يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا
أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية
الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات
