That is: a Muslim relative of his dies at once, and thereafter he verifies with his heart, then seeks a legal opinion, saying: "I was not verifying with my heart at the moment of death, and the inheritance is now in my hand — is it lawful for me, between me and God Most High?" Or: he married a Muslim woman, then verified with his heart — is the renewal of the marriage incumbent upon him? This is a locus of consideration. It is possible to say: the rulings of this world are attached to the outward word, outwardly and inwardly. And it is possible to say: they are attached to the outward in respect of others, because his inward is not apparent to others, while his inward is apparent to himself, between him and God Most High. The more apparent — and God knows best — is that it is not lawful for him to take that inheritance, and the renewal of the marriage is incumbent upon him. For this reason, Ḥudhayfa, may God be pleased with him, would not attend the funeral of anyone who died among the hypocrites; and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, would defer to him in this, not attending if Ḥudhayfa, may God be pleased with him, did not attend. And prayer is an outward act in this world, even though it is among the acts of worship. And the avoidance of the unlawful is also among the things obligatory upon one for God, like prayer — for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The seeking of the lawful is an obligation after obligation." This is not contradictory to our saying that inheritance is a ruling of Islam, which is surrender. Rather, complete surrender is what encompasses the outward and the inward.

These are jurisprudential investigations, probabilistic (ẓanniyya), built upon the outward senses of the terms, the generalities, and the analogies. It should not be supposed by one deficient in the sciences that certainty is sought therein, merely because it is customary to adduce such matters in the art of theology (kalām), where certainty is sought. Never has one prospered who looked to customs and conventions in the sciences.

If you say: "What then is the doubt of the Muʿtazila and the Murjiʾa, and what is the proof of the nullity of their saying?" — I say: their doubt is the generalities of the Qurʾān.

As for the Murjiʾa: they said that the believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all the acts of disobedience — because of His saying, may He be exalted: {«فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا»} — "Whoever believes in his Lord shall not fear diminution nor injustice"; and His saying, glorified and exalted be He: {«والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون»} — "Those who believe in God and His messengers — those are the veracious ones"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها»} — up to His saying: {«فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء»} — "We denied and said: God has not sent down anything." His saying {«كلما ألقى فيها فوج»} — "Whenever a troop is cast into it" — is general, so whoever is cast into the Fire must be a denier. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى»} — "None shall burn in it except the most wretched, who denies and turns away" — and this is a restriction, an affirmation, and a negation. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون»} — "Whoever brings a good deed shall have better than it, and they shall be secure from terror that Day" — and faith is the head of good deeds. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«والله يحب المحسنين»} — "And God loves the doers of good"; and He said: {«إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا»} — "We do not waste the reward of one who does good work."

There is no proof for them in this. For wherever faith is mentioned in these verses, what is meant is faith together with action — since we have shown that faith may be employed, intending thereby Islam, which is compliance of heart, word, and deed. The proof of this interpretation is the many reports concerning the punishment of the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "There shall come forth from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of mustard-seed of faith" — for how shall he come forth if he did not enter? And from the Qurʾān, His saying, may He be exalted: {«إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء»} — "God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" — and the exception by will indicates division. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها»} — "Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger — for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally" — and its specification to unbelief is arbitrary. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم»} — "Truly, the wrongdoers are in enduring torment." And He said: {«ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار»} — "Whoever brings an evil deed — their faces shall be cast down into the Fire." These generalities stand in opposition to their generalities, and it is necessary to bring specification (al-takhṣīṣ) and interpretation (al-taʾwīl) to bear upon both sides — because the reports explicitly state that the disobedient are punished. Indeed, His saying, may He be exalted: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها»} — "There is none of you but shall come to it" — is almost explicit that this is unavoidable for all, for no believer is free of a sin he commits. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى»} — He intended thereby a specific group, or He intended by "the most wretched" a specific individual as well. And His saying, may He be exalted: {«كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها»} — "Whenever a troop is cast into it, its keepers ask them" — that is, a troop of the unbelievers. And the specification of generalities is readily admissible.

From this verse it occurred to al-Ashʿarī and a group of the theologians to deny the forms of generality (ṣiyagh al-ʿumūm), holding that these expressions are to be suspended until a contextual indicator appears showing their meaning.

As for the Muʿtazila: their doubt is His saying, may He be exalted: {«وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى»} — "And I am indeed forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does righteous work, then is guided"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات»} — "By the declining day, man is indeed in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا»} — "There is none of you but shall come to it — an inevitable decree upon your Lord" — then He said: {«ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا»} — "Then We shall save those who are God-fearing"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم»} — "Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger — for him is the Fire of Hell" — and every verse in which God, may He be exalted, mentions righteous action conjoined with faith; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها»} — "Whoever kills a believer deliberately — his recompense is Hell, abiding therein eternally."

These generalities also are specified by the evidence of His saying, may He be exalted: {«ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء»} — "And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" — so His will must remain operative in the forgiveness of all besides association (al-shirk). Likewise, his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "There shall come forth from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of mustard-seed of faith"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا»} — "We do not waste the reward of one who does good work"; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين»} — "God does not waste the reward of the doers of good" — so how should He waste the reward of the very root of faith and all acts of obedience by a single disobedience? And His saying, may He be exalted: {«ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا»} — "Whoever kills a believer deliberately" — that is, because of his faith; and it was revealed upon such an occasion.

If you say: "The choice has inclined to the view that faith is attained without action, yet it is well known from the Salaf their saying: 'Faith is conviction, utterance, and action.' What then is its meaning?" — We say: it is not far that action be counted as part of faith, because it completes and perfects it — just as it is said: "The head and the hands are part of the human being," and it is known that one ceases to be a human being by the absence of the head, but does not cease by being amputated of hand. Likewise, it is said: "The glorifications and the takbīrs are part of the prayer," even though the prayer is not nullified by their absence. So verification of the heart is to faith as the head is to the existence of the human being — for it ceases by its absence — and the rest of the acts of obedience are like the limbs, some higher than others. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The fornicator does not fornicate, at the time he fornicates, while he is a believer." And the Companions, may God be pleased with them, did not hold the Muʿtazilī doctrine of departure from faith by fornication. Rather, its meaning is: not a believer truly, with complete and perfect faith — just as it is said of one disabled, amputated of limbs: "This is not a human being" — that is, he does not have the perfection that lies beyond the reality of humanity.

chapters.title_en: The Question Concerning the Reality of Knowledge and Its Definition
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| مسألة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "a mark or trace by which a thing is known"; knowledge as an indelible impression left upon the soul.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿilm denotes the firm apprehension (iʿtiqād jāzim) of a thing as it truly is, distinguishing it from mere opinion (ẓann) and ignorance (jahl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the soul's grasp of the form of the known object; metaphorical (majāz) — any act of naming or signifying that points toward such grasp.
- Sībawayh Rule: Masʾalah as a verbal noun pattern (faʿalah) — denotes a "matter of inquiry" or "thesis" posed for resolution, carrying the syntactic force of a nominalized proposition.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the question (masʾalah) here concerns the reality of knowledge (ḥaqīqat al-ʿilm) and its definition (ḥadd). For the scholars of speculative theology (mutakallimūn) have differed concerning it, and their statements have multiplied, yet the truth in this matter is single and admits of no multiplicity. So let us set forth the well-known opinions, then follow them with the decisive verification (taḥqīq) that unveils the reality without excess or deficiency.

chapters.title_en: On the Increase and Decrease of Faith (Ziyādat al-Īmān wa Nuqṣānuhu)
chapters.arabic_text:
فإن قلت فقد اتفق السلف على أن الإيمان يزيد وينقص يزيد بالطاعة
وينقص بالمعصية فإذا كان التصديق هو الإيمان فلا يتصور فيه زيادة ولا نقصان
فأقول السلف هم الشهود العدول وما لأحد عن قولهم عدول فما ذكروه حق وإنما
الشأن في فهمه وفيه دليل على أن العمل ليس من أجزاء الإيمان وأركان وجوده
بل هو مزيد عليه يزيد به والزائد موجود والناقص موجود والشيء لا يزيد بذاته
فلا يجوز أن يقال الإنسان يزيد برأسه بل يقال يزيد بلحيته وسمنه ولا يجوز
أن يقال الصلاة تزيد بالركوع والسجود بل تزيد بالآداب والسنن فهذا تصريح
بأن الإيمان له وجود ثم بعد الوجود يختلف حاله بالزيادة والنقصان
فإن قلت فالإشكال قائم في أن التصديق كيف يزيد وينقص وهو خصلة واحدة
فأقول إذا تركنا المداهنة ولم نكترث بتشغيب من تشغب وكشفنا الغطاء ارتفع
الإشكال فنقول الإيمان اسم مشترك يطلق من ثلاثة أوجه الأول أنه أنه يطلق
للتصديق بالقلب على سبيل الاعتقاد والتقليد من غير كشف وانشراح صدر وهو
إيمان العوام بل إيمان الخلق كلهم إلا الخواص وهذا الاعتقاد عقدة عن القلب
تارة تشتد وتقوى وتارة تضعف وتسترخي كالعقدة على الخيط مثلا ولا تستبعد هذا
واعتبره باليهودي وصلابته في عقيدته التي لا يمكن  نزوعه عنها بتخويف وتحذير
ولا بتخييل ووعظ ولا تحقيق وبرهان وكذلك النصراني والمبتدعة وفيهم من يمكن
تشكيكه بأدنى كلام ويمكن استنزاله عن اعتقاده بأدنى استمالة أو تخويف مع
أنه غير شاك في عقده كالأول ولكنهما متفاوتان في شدة التصميم
وهذا موجود في الاعتقاد الحق أيضا والعمل يؤثر في نماء هذا التصميم
وزيادته كما يؤثر سقي الماء في نماء الأشجار ولذلك قال الله تعالى فزادتهم
إيمانا وقال تعالى ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
فيما يروى في بعض الأخبار الإيمان يزيد وينقص (2) وذلك بتأثير الطاعات في
القلب وهذا لا يدركه إلا من راقب أحوال نفسه في أوقات المواظبة على العبادة
والتجرد لها بحضور القلب مع أوقات الفتور وإدراك التفاوت في السكون إلى
عقائد الإيمان في هذه الأحوال حتى يزيد عقده استعصاء على من يريد حله
بالتشكيك بل من يعتقد في اليتيم معنى الرحمة إذا عمل بموجب اعتقاده فمسح
رأسه وتلطف به أدرك PageV01P120
من باطنه تأكيد الرحمة وتضاعفها بسبب العمل وكذلك معتقد التواضع إذا عمل
بموجبه عملا مقبلا أو ساجدا لغيره أحس من قلبه بالتواضع عند إقدامه على
الخدمة
وهكذا جميع صفات القلب تصدر منها أعمال الجوارح ثم يعود أثر الأعمال
عليها فيؤكدها ويزيدها وسيأتي هذا في ربع المنجيات والمهلكات عند بيان وجه
تعلق الباطن بالظاهر والأعمال بالعقائد والقلوب فإن ذلك من جنس تعلق الملك
بالملكوت وأعني بالملك عالم الشهادة المدرك بالحواس وبالملكوت عالم الغيب
المدرك بنور البصيرة والقلب من عالم الملكوت والأعضاء وأعمالها من عالم
الملك
ولطف الارتباط ودقته بين العالمين انتهى إلى حد ظن بعض الناس اتحاد
أحدهما بالآخر وظن آخرون أنه لا عالم إلا عالم الشهادة وهو هذه الأجسام
المحسوسة
ومن أدرك الأمرين وأدرك تعددهما ثم ارتباطهما عبر عنه فقال
رق الزجاج ورقت الخمر ... وتشابها فتشاكل الأمر
فكأنما خمر ولا قدح ... وكأنما قدح ولا خمر
ولنرجع إلى المقصود فإن هذا العلم خارج عن علم المعاملة ولكن بين العلمين
أيضا اتصال وارتباط فلذلك ترى علوم المكاشفة تتسلق  كل ساعة على علوم
المعاملة إلى أن تنكشف عنها بالتكليف فهذا وجه زيادة الإيمان بالطاعة بموجب
هذا الإطلاق ولهذا قال علي كرم الله وجهه إن الإيمان ليبدو لمعة بيضاء فإذا
عمل العبد الصالحات نمت فزادت حتى يبيض القلب كله وإن النفاق ليبدو نكتة
سوداء فإذا انتهك الحرمات نمت وزادت حتى يسود القلب كله فيطبع عليه فذلك هو
الختم وتلا قوله تعالى كلا بل ران على قلوبهم الآية
الإطلاق الثاني أن يراد به التصديق والعمل جميعا كما قال صلى الله عليه
وسلم الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يزني الزاني
حين يزني وهو مؤمن وإذا دخل العمل في مقتضى لفظ الإيمان لم تخف زيادته
ونقصانه وهل يؤثر ذلك في زيادة الإيمان الذي هو مجرد التصديق هذا فيه نظر
وقد أشرنا إلى أنه يؤثر فيه
الإطلاق الثالث أن يراد به التصديق اليقيني على سبيل الكشف وانشراح الصدر
والمشاهدة بنور البصيرة وهذا أبعد الأقسام عن قبول الزيادة ولكني أقول
الأمر اليقيني الذي لا شك فيه تختلف طمأنينة النفس إليه فليس طمأنينة النفس
إلى أن الاثنين أكثر من الواحد كطمأنينتها إلى أن العالم مصنوع حادث وإن
كان لا شك في واحد منهما فإن اليقينيات تختلف في درجات الإيضاح ودرجات
طمأنينة النفس إليها وقد تعرضنا لهذا في فصل اليقين من كتاب العلم في باب
علامات علماء الآخرة فلا حاجة إلى الإعادة
وقد ظهر في جميع الإطلاقات أن ما قالوه من زيادة الإيمان ونقصانه حق وكيف
وفي الأخبار أنه يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان وفي بعض
المواضع في خبر آخر مثقال دينار (2) فأي معنى لاختلاف مقاديره إن كان ما في
القلب لا يتفاوت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ي-د (Z-Y-D)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is excess, augmentation, or growth beyond a baseline; al-ziyādah implies an addition that accrues to an existing substrate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ziyādah in īmān denotes intensification of certitude (yaqīn) and tranquility (ṭuma'nīnah) in the heart, not quantitative accretion of a simple essence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to divisible bodies; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to qualities and states, where increase is by degree and firmness.
- Root: ن-ق-ص (N-Q-Ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Diminution, deficiency, or loss from a prior state of completeness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In faith, nuqṣān is the weakening of the heart's resolve and the loosening of conviction's knot, not the annihilation of its essence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used metaphorically for intensity of adherence, as a knot (ʿuqda) tightens or slackens.
- Root: ص-د-ق (Ṣ-D-Q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firmness and veracity in assent; taṣdīq is the heart's affirmation of truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taṣdīq is the cognitive act of assenting to prophetic reports; its degrees vary by clarity (inkishāf) and certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for verbal attestation; metaphorical for inner conviction that admits of strength and weakness.
- Root: ك-ش-ف (K-SH-F)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Unveiling, removal of a covering.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kashf is the illumination of the heart by which unseen realities are witnessed with the light of insight (nūr al-baṣīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical for intellectual disclosure, contrasted with taqlīd (blind acceptance).
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditioned Predication (al-Ḥaml al-Muqayyad) — When a predicate (e.g., "increases") is applied to a subject (e.g., "faith"), the syntactic form requires distinguishing the essence (dhāt) from its accidents (aʿrāḍ); the verb of increase takes an implicit prepositional complement (fī) indicating the locus of augmentation, as in "increases in firmness," not "increases in itself."
chapters.translation:
I say: If you say, "The Salaf (the righteous predecessors) have unanimously agreed that faith increases and decreases — it increases through obedience and decreases through disobedience. Now if taṣdīq (inner assent) is faith, then no increase or decrease is conceivable in it," — then I reply: The Salaf are the upright witnesses (al-shuhūd al-ʿudūl), and no one has any recourse to depart from their statement. What they mentioned is true; the real matter lies in understanding it. And in their statement there is evidence that action is not a part of faith nor a pillar of its existence, but rather something additional to it, by which it increases. The one who increases exists, and the one who decreases exists; and a thing does not increase in its own essence. Thus one may not say, "A man increases by his head," but rather one says, "He increases by his beard and his corpulence." Nor may one say, "The prayer increases by its bowing and prostration," but rather, "It increases by its etiquettes and its supererogatory practices (al-ādāb wa al-sunan)." This is an explicit declaration that faith has an existence, and after that existence its state varies by increase and decrease.

If you say, "The difficulty remains: how can taṣdīq, being a single trait, increase and decrease?" — then I reply: If we abandon flattery (al-mudāhanah), pay no heed to the clamor of the contentious, and lift the veil, the difficulty is resolved. We say: Faith (īmān) is a homonymous term (ism mushtarak) used in three senses.

The first sense: It is used for taṣdīq of the heart by way of belief (iʿtiqād) and emulation (taqlīd), without unveiling (kashf) and expansion of the breast (inshirāḥ al-ṣadr). This is the faith of the common folk — nay, the faith of all creatures except the elite (al-khawāṣṣ). This belief is a knot (ʿuqda) in the heart: at times it tightens and strengthens, and at times it weakens and slackens, like a knot on a thread, for example. Do not deem this remote. Consider the Jew and his rigidity in his creed, from which he cannot be drawn away by intimidation and warning, nor by fancy and exhortation, nor by verification and demonstration. Likewise the Christian and the innovator (al-mubtadiʿ). Among them there is one who can be thrown into doubt by the slightest speech, and can be dislodged from his belief by the least enticement or intimidation, even though he is not doubtful of his knot like the first. Yet the two differ in the intensity of resolve (shiddat al-taṣmīm). This exists also in true belief. And action influences the growth of this resolve and its increase, just as the watering of trees influences their growth. For this reason God—exalted is He—said: {«فَزَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا»} ("And it increased them in faith") and said: {«لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ»} ("That they may increase in faith upon their faith"). And the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—said, as narrated in some reports: "Faith increases and decreases." This is by the effect of acts of obedience upon the heart. None perceives this except one who observes the states of his own soul during times of persevering in worship and devoting himself to it with presence of heart, as against times of languor — and perceives the disparity in tranquility (sukūn) toward the tenets of faith in these various states, until his knot becomes more resistant to anyone who would undo it by skepticism. Nay, consider one who holds the meaning of mercy toward an orphan: when he acts upon the requirement of his belief — wiping the orphan's head and showing him kindness — he perceives from his inner self (bāṭin) the reinforcement of mercy and its multiplication by reason of the act. Likewise, one who holds the belief of humility: when he acts upon its requirement by advancing or prostrating to another, he feels in his heart humility when he undertakes the service.

And so it is with all the attributes of the heart: from them issue the works of the bodily members, then the effect of those works returns upon them, reinforcing and increasing them. This will come later in the Quarter of Deliverance and Destruction (Rubʿ al-Munjiyāt wa al-Muhlikāt), when explaining the manner of the attachment of the inner to the outer, and of works to beliefs and hearts. For that is of the same kind as the attachment of the Kingdom (al-Mulk) to the Dominion (al-Malakūt). By al-Mulk I mean the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah), perceived by the senses; and by al-Malakūt I mean the world of the unseen (ʿālam al-ghayb), perceived by the light of insight (nūr al-baṣīrah). The heart belongs to the world of al-Malakūt, while the members and their works belong to the world of al-Mulk. The subtlety and delicacy of the connection between the two worlds reached such a degree that some people imagined the union of one with the other, and others imagined that there is no world but the world of witness — namely, these sensed bodies. And one who perceived both matters — perceived their duality and then their connection — expressed it saying:

"The glass became fine and the wine became fine, and they resembled each other, so the matter became ambiguous:
As if there is wine and no cup, and as if there is a cup and no wine."

Let us return to the intended purpose. For this knowledge lies outside the science of practical dealing (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah), yet between the two sciences there is also connection and linkage. For this reason you see the sciences of unveiling (ʿulūm al-mukāshafah) climbing at every moment upon the sciences of practical dealing, until they are disclosed by them through the divine charge (al-taklīf). This, then, is the manner of faith's increase through obedience, according to this first usage. For this reason ʿAlī—may God honor his face—said: "Faith appears as a white gleam; when the servant performs righteous deeds, it grows and increases until the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy appears as a black spot; when sacred things are violated, it grows and increases until the whole heart becomes black, and then it is sealed over — and that is the sealing (al-khatm)." Then he recited the saying of God—exalted is He: {«كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ»} ("Nay, but that which they earned has rusted upon their hearts").

The second usage: That by faith is meant taṣdīq and action together, as the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Faith has seventy-odd branches," and said: "The fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer." When action enters into the import of the word faith, its increase and decrease are not obscure. And whether that affects the increase of faith which is mere taṣdīq — in this there is consideration (naẓar); and we have indicated that it does affect it.

The third usage: That by faith is meant certain assent (al-taṣdīq al-yaqīnī) by way of unveiling (kashf), expansion of the breast, and witnessing (mushāhadah) with the light of insight. This is the farthest of the divisions from admitting increase. But I say: The certain matter in which there is no doubt — the soul's tranquility (ṭuma'nīnah) toward it differs. For the soul's tranquility toward the fact that two is more than one is not like its tranquility toward the fact that the world is made and originated (maṣnūʿ ḥādith), even though there is no doubt in either of them. For certainties differ in their degrees of clarity and in the degrees of the soul's tranquility toward them. We have already touched upon this in the chapter on certainty (al-yaqīn) in the Book of Knowledge, in the section on the signs of the scholars of the Hereafter; there is no need to repeat it.

And it has become manifest in all the usages that what they said concerning the increase and decrease of faith is true. How could it be otherwise, when in the reports it is stated that there will come out of the Fire one in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of faith, and in some places in another report, the weight of a dīnār? What meaning could the difference in its measures have, if what is in the heart does not vary?

chapters.title_en: The Question (Al-Mas'alah)
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| مسألة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, inquire, request; the act of seeking knowledge or clarification through interrogation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, a "mas'alah" denotes a formal point of inquiry or doctrinal proposition requiring resolution, often tied to juridical or creedal disputation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "a question posed"; metaphorically, it extends to "a treatise or chapter" in scholarly works, where the inquiry itself becomes the structural unit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with implicit predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — the heading "mas'alah" stands as an absolute nominative, implying an elided verb or phrase such as "this is a question" (hādhihi mas'alah), marking a new discursive segment.
chapters.translation: ### |||| The Question

chapters.title_en: On the Wisdom of the Conditional Exception (Istithnāʾ) in Professing Faith — Concluding Section of the Book of the Foundations of Creed
chapters.arabic_text:
فإن قلت ما وجه قول السلف أنا مؤمن إن شاء الله والاستثناء شك
والشك في الإيمان كفر وقد كانوا كلهم يمتنعون عن جزم الجواب بالإيمان
ويحترزون عنه
فقال سفيان الثوري رحمه الله من قال أنا مؤمن عند الله فهو من الكذابين
ومن  قال أنا مؤمن حقا فهو بدعة فكيف يكون كاذبا وهو يعلم أنه مؤمن في نفسه
ومن كان مؤمنا في نفسه كان مؤمنا عند الله كما أن من كان طويلا وسخيا في
نفسه وعلم ذلك كان كذلك عند الله وكذا من PageV01P121
كان مسرورا أو حزينا أو سميعا أو بصيرا ولو قيل للإنسان هل أنت حيوان لم
يحسن أن يقول أنا حيوان إن شاء الله
ولما قال سفيان ذلك قيل له فماذا نقول قال قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل
إلينا وأي فرق بين أن يقول آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وبين أن يقول أنا
مؤمن وقيل للحسن أمؤمن أنت فقال إن شاء الله فقيل له لم تستثني يا أبا سعيد
في الإيمان فقال أخاف أن أقول نعم فيقول الله سبحانه كذبت يا حسن فتحق علي
الكلمة
وكان يقول ما يؤمنني أن يكون الله سبحانه قد اطلع علي في بعض ما يكره
فمقتني وقال اذهب لا قبلت لك عملا فأنا أعمل في غير معمل
وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم إذا قيل لك أمؤمن أنت فقل لا إله إلا الله وقال مرة
قل أنا لا أشك في الإيمان وسؤالك إياي بدعة
وقيل لعلقمة أمؤمن أنت قال أرجو إن شاء الله
وقال الثوري نحن مؤمنون بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله وما ندري ما نحن عند
الله تعالى فما معنى هذه الاستثناءات فالجواب أن هذا الاستثناء صحيح وله
أربعة أوجه وجهان مستندان إلى الشك لا في أصل الإيمان ولكن في خاتمته أو
كماله ووجهان لا يستندان إلى الشك
الوجه الأول الذي لا يستند إلى معارضة الشك الاحتراز من الجزم خيفة ما
فيه من تزكية النفس قال الله تعالى فلا تزكوا أنفسكم {وقال} ألم تر إلى
الذين يزكون أنفسهم وقال تعالى انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وقيل لحكيم
ما الصدق القبيح فقال ثناء المرء على نفسه
والإيمان من أعلى صفات المجد والجزم تزكية مطلقة وصيغة الاستثناء كأنها
ثقل من عرف التزكية كما يقال للإنسان أنت طبيب أو فقيه  أو مفسر فيقول نعم
إن شاء الله لا في معرض التشكيك ولكن لإخراج نفسه عن تزكية نفسه فالصيغة
صيغة الترديد والتضعيف لنفس الخبر ومعناه التضعيف اللازم من لوازم الخبر
وهو التزكية
وبهذا التأويل لو سئل عن وصف ذم لم يحسن الاستثناء
الوجه الثاني التأدب بذكر الله تعالى في كل حال وإحالة الأمور كلها إلى
مشيئة الله سبحانه فقد أدب الله سبحانه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال تعالى
ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك
فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين
محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه
شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما
كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل
المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1)
واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به
وهذه الصيغة دالة عليه حتى صار بعرف الاستعمال عبارة عن إظهار الرغبة
والتمني فإذا قيل لك إن فلانا يموت سريعا فتقول إن شاء الله فيفهم منه
رغبتك لا تشككك وإذا قيل لك فلان سيزول مرضه ويصح فتقول إن شاء الله بمعنى
الرغبة فقد صارت الكلمة معدولة عن معنى التشكيك إلى معنى الرغبة وكذلك
العدول إلى معنى التأدب لذكر الله تعالى كيف كان الأمر
الوجه الثالث مستنده الشك ومعناه أنا مؤمن حقا إن شاء الله إذ قال الله
تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا فانقسموا إلى قسمين
ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال
إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر
والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال
الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه
والثاني أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري  وجودها على الكمال أما العمل
فقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا
وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون {فيكون}
PageV01P122
الشك في هذا الصدق وكذلك قال الله تعالى ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم
الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين فشرط عشرين وصفا كالوفاء بالعهد والصبر
على الشدائد
ثم قال تعالى أولئك الذين صدقوا وقد قال تعالى يرفع الله الذين آمنوا
منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات وقال تعالى لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل
الفتح وقاتل الآية وقد قال تعالى هم درجات عند الله وقال صلى الله عليه
وسلم الإيمان عريان ولباسه التقوى (1) الحديث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا أدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق فهذا ما يدل على
ارتباط كمال الإيمان بالأعمال وأما ارتباطه بالبراءة عن النفاق والشرك
الخفي فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص وإن صام
وصلى وزعم أنه مؤمن من إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا اؤتمن خان وإذا خاصم
فجر (2) وفي بعض الروايات وإذا عاهد غدر وفي حديث أبي سعيد الخدري القلوب
أربعة قلب أجرد وفيه سراج يزهر فذلك قلب المؤمن وقلب مصفح فيه إيمان ونفاق
فمثل الإيمان فيه كمثل البقلة يمدها الماء العذب ومثل النفاق فيه كمثل
القرحة يمدها القيح والصديد فأي المادتين غلب عليه حكم له بها (3) وفي لفظ
آخر غلبت عليه ذهبت به وقال عليه السلام أكثر منافقي هذه الأمة قراؤها (4)
وفي حديث الشرك أخفى في أمتى من دبيب النمل على الصفا (5) وقال حذيفة رضي
الله عنه كان الرجل يتكلم بالكلمة على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
يصير بها منافقا إلى أن يموت وإني لأسمعها من أحدكم في اليوم عشر مرات (6)
وقال بعض العلماء أقرب الناس من النفاق من يرى أنه بريء من النفاق
وقال حذيفة المنافقون اليوم أكثر منهم على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
فكانوا إذ ذاك يخفونه وهم اليوم يظهرونه  وهذا النفاق يضاد صدق الإيمان
وكماله وهو خفي وأبعد الناس منه من يتخوفه وأقربهم منه من يرى أنه بريء منه
فقد قيل للحسن البصري يقولون أن لا نفاق اليوم فقال يا أخي لو هلك
المنافقون لاستوحشتم في الطريق
وقال هو أو غيره لو نبتت للمنافقين أذناب ما قدرنا أن نطأ على الأرض
بأقدامنا وسمع ابن عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا يتعرض للحجاج فقال أرأيت لو كان
حاضرا يسمع أكنت تتكلم فيه فقال لا فقال كنا نعد هذا نفاقا على عهد رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان ذا لسانين في
الدنيا جعله الله ذا لسانين في الآخرة وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم شر
الناس ذو الوجهين الذي يأتي هؤلاء بوجه ويأتي هؤلاء بوجه وقيل للحسن إن
قوما يقولون إنا لا نخاف النفاق فقال والله لأن أكون أعلم أني بريء من
النفاق أحب إلي من تلاع الأرض ذهبا
وقال الحسن إن من النفاق اختلاف اللسان والقلب والسر والعلانية والمدخل
والمخرج
وقال رجل لحذيفة رضي الله عنه إني أخاف أن أكون منافقا فقال لو كنت
منافقا ما خفت النفاق إن المنافق قد أمن النفاق
وقال ابن أبي مليكة أدركت PageV01P123
ثلاثين ومائة وفي رواية خمسين ومائة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
كلهم يخافون النفاق
وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان جالسا في جماعة من أصحابه
فذكروا رجلا وأكثروا الثناء عليه فبيناهم كذلك إذ طلع عليهم الرجل ووجهه
يقطر ماء من أثر الوضوء وقد علق نعله بيده وبين عينيه أثر السجود فقالوا يا
رسول الله هذا هو الرجل الذي وصفناه فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أرى على وجهه
سفعة من الشيطان فجاء الرجل حتى سلم وجلس مع القوم فقال النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم نشدتك الله هل حدثت نفسك حين أشرفت على القوم أنه ليس فيهم خير
منك فقال اللهم نعم (1) فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه اللهم إني
أستغفرك لما  علمت ولما لم أعلم فقيل له أتخاف يا رسول الله فقال وما يؤمنني
والقلوب بين إصبعين من أصابع الرحمن يقلبها كيف يشاء وقد قال سبحانه {وبدا
لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون} (2) قيل في التفسير عملوا أعمالا ظنوا
أنها حسنات فكانت في كفة السيئات
وقال سري السقطي لو أن إنسانا دخل بستانا فيه من جميع الأشجار عليها من
جميع الطيور فخاطبه كل طير منها بلغة فقال السلام عليك يا ولي الله فسكنت
نفسه إلى ذلك كان أسيرا في يديها فهذه الأخبار والآثار تعرفك خطر الأمر
بسبب دقائق النفاق والشرك الخفي وأنه لا يؤمن منه حتى كان عمر بن الخطاب
رضي الله عنه يسأل حذيفة عن نفسه وأنه هل ذكر في المنافقين وقال أبو سليمان
الداراني سمعت من بعض الأمراء شيئا فأردت أن أنكره فخفت أن يأمر بقتلي ولم
أخف من الموت ولكن خشيت أن يعرض لقلبي التزين للخلق عند خروج روحي فكففت
وهذا من النفاق الذي يضاد حقيقة الإيمان وصدقه وكماله وصفاءه لا أصله
فالنفاق نفاقان أحدهما يخرج من الدين ويلحق بالكافرين ويسلك في زمرة
المخلدين في النار
والثاني يفضي بصاحبه إلى النار مدة أو ينقص من درجات عليين ويحط من رتبة
الصديقين وذلك مشكوك فيه ولذلك حسن الاستثناء فيه
وأصل هذا النفاق تفاوت بين السر والعلانية والأمن من مكر الله والعجب
وأمور أخر لا يخلو عنها إلا الصديقون
الوجه الرابع وهو أيضا مستند إلى الشك وذلك من خوف الخاتمة فإنه لا يدري
أيسلم له الإيمان عند الموت أم لا فإن ختم له بالكفر حبط عمله السابق لأنه
موقوف على سلامة الآخر ولو سئل الصائم ضحوة النهار عن صحة صومه فقال أنا
صائم قطعا فلو أفطر في أثناء نهاره بعد ذلك لتبين كذبه إذ كانت الصحة
موقوفة على التمام إلى غروب الشمس من آخر النهار
وكما أن النهار ميقات تمام الصوم فالعمر ميقات تمام صحة الإيمان ووصفه
بالصحة قبل آخره بناء على الاستصحاب وهو مشكوك فيه والعاقبة مخوفة وللها
كان بكاء أكثر الخائفين لأجل أنها ثمرة القضية السابقة والمشيئة الأزلية
التي لا تظهر إلا بظهور المقضي به ولا مطلع عليه لأحد من البشر فخوف
الخاتمة كخوف السابقة وربما يظهر في الحال ما سبقت الكلمة بنقيضه فمن الذي
يدري أنه من الذين سبقت لهم من الله الحسنى وقيل في معنى قوله تعالى {وجاءت
سكرة الموت بالحق} أي بالسابقة يعني أظهرتها
وقال بعض السلف إنما يوزن من الأعمال خواتيمها
وكان أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه يحلف بالله ما من أحد يأمن أن يسلب إيمانه
إلا سلبه
وقيل من الذنوب ذنوب عقوبتها سوء الخاتمة نعوذ بالله من ذلك
وقيل هي عقوبات دعوى الولاية والكرامة بالافتراء
وقال بعض العارفين لو عرضت علي الشهادة عند باب الدار والموت على التوحيد
PageV01P124
عند باب الحجرة لاخترت الموت على التوحيد عند باب الحجرة لأني لا أدري ما
يعرض لقلبي من التغيير عن التوحيد إلى باب الدار وقال بعضهم لو عرفت واحدا
بالتوحيد خمسين سنة ثم حال بيني وبينه سارية ومات لم أحكم أنه مات على
التوحيد
وفي الحديث من قال أنا مؤمن فهو كافر ومن قال أنا عالم فهو جاهل (1) وقيل
في قوله تعالى وتمت كلمات ربك صدقا وعدلا صدقا لمن مات على الإيمان وعدلا
لمن مات على الشرك وقد قال تعالى {ولله عاقبة الأمور} فمهما كان الشك بهذه
المثابة كان الاستثناء واجبا لأن الإيمان عبارة عما يفيد الجنة كما أن
الصوم عبارة عما يبرىء الذمة
وما فسد قبل الغروب لا يبرىء الذمة فيخرج عن كونه صوما فكذلك الإيمان بل
لا يبعد أن يسأل عن الصوم الماضي الذي لا يشك فيه بعد الفراغ منه فيقال
أصمت بالأمس فيقول نعم إن شاء الله تعالى إذ الصوم الحقيقي هو المقبول
والمقبول غائب عنه لا يطلع عليه إلا الله تعالى فمن هذا حسن الاستثناء في
جميع أعمال البر ويكون ذلك شكا في القبول إذ يمنع من القبول بعد جريان ظاهر
شروط الصحة أسباب خفيفة لا يطلع عليها إلا رب الأرباب  جل جلاله فيحسن الشك
فيه
فهذه وجوه حسن الاستثناء في الجواب عن الإيمان وهي آخر ما نختم به كتاب
قواعد العقائد
تم الكتاب بحمد الله تعالى وصلى الله عليه وسلم على سيدنا محمد وعلى كل
عبد مصطفى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ث ن ي (th-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fold, double, repeat; secondary, second; the act of returning upon a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istithnāʾ as a grammatical-theological device of suspending absolute affirmation, linked to divine will (mashīʾah) and human epistemic limitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes exclusion of a part from a whole; metaphorical usage here shifts from doubt (shakk) to deference (taʾaddub) and aspiration (raghbah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Suspension (al-Taʿlīq bi-al-Sharṭ) — The particle "illā" with an implied future verb governs the apodosis, rendering the assertion contingent without negating its essential truth.
chapters.translation:
I say: If you say: "What is the purport of the predecessors' saying, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — for the exception implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from an unqualified answer affirming faith, and guarded against it. Sufyān al-Thawrī — God have mercy on him — said: 'Whoever says, "I am a believer before God," is among the liars; and whoever says, "I am a believer truly," has committed an innovation.' How then can one be a liar while he knows in himself that he is a believer? For whoever is a believer in himself is a believer before God, just as whoever is tall or generous in himself and knows that to be so is likewise before God. So too one who is joyful or sorrowful, or hearing or seeing. And were a man asked, 'Are you an animal?' it would not be fitting for him to say, 'I am an animal, if God wills.'"

And when Sufyān said that, it was said to him: "Then what shall we say?" He said: "Say: 'We believe in God and what has been sent down to us.'" And what difference is there between saying, 'We believe in God and what has been sent down to us,' and saying, 'I am a believer'? And it was said to al-Ḥasan: "Are you a believer?" He said: "If God wills." It was said to him: "Why do you make the exception, O Abū Saʿīd, in [matters of] faith?" He said: "I fear that if I say 'Yes,' God — glorified be He — will say: 'You have lied, O Ḥasan,' and the word will be realized against me." And he used to say: "What assures me that God — glorified be He — has not looked upon me in some [act] He dislikes, and abhorred me, and said: 'Go, I will not accept any deed from you'? So I labor in a place where there is no laboring."

And Ibrāhīm ibn Adham said: "When it is said to you, 'Are you a believer?' say: 'There is no god but God.'" And once he said: "Say: 'I do not doubt in faith, but your questioning me is an innovation.'" And it was said to ʿAlqamah: "Are you a believer?" He said: "I hope so, if God wills." And al-Thawrī said: "We are believers in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers — but we do not know what we are before God — exalted be He."

So what is the meaning of these exceptions? The answer is that this exception is sound, and it has four aspects: two aspects are grounded in doubt — not regarding the root of faith, but regarding its final end (khātima) or its perfection (kamāl) — and two aspects are not grounded in doubt.

The first aspect, which is not grounded in the opposition of doubt, is the guarding against unqualified affirmation out of fear of what it contains of self-justification (tazkiyat al-nafs). God — exalted be He — said: {«So do not justify yourselves»} and said: {«Have you not seen those who purify themselves?»} And He — exalted be He — said: {«See how they invent lies against God»}. And it was said to a sage: "What is ugly truthfulness?" He said: "A man's praise of himself." And faith is among the highest attributes of glory, and unqualified affirmation is an absolute self-justification. The formula of exception is as if a burden upon the one who recognizes self-justification — just as it is said to a man, "You are a physician, or a jurist, or an exegete," and he says, "Yes, if God wills" — not in the mode of doubting, but to remove himself from self-praise. So the formula is the formula of hesitation and weakening of the report itself, and its meaning is the weakening necessarily entailed by the report — namely, self-justification. By this interpretation, were he asked about a blameworthy attribute, the exception would not be fitting.

The second aspect is the observance of propriety (taʾaddub) by mentioning God — exalted be He — in every state, and referring all matters to the will of God — glorified be He. For God — exalted be He — taught His Prophet — peace be upon him — propriety, saying: {«And do not say of anything, "I will do that tomorrow," except if God wills»}. Then He did not restrict that to what is not doubted, but said — exalted be He: {«You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, heads shaved and hair cut short»} — and God — exalted be He — knew that they would enter without fail and that He had willed it. But the purpose was to teach them that. So the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — observed propriety in what he reported, whether known or doubted, until he said — peace be upon him — when he entered the graveyards: "Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people, and we, if God wills, shall join you." And joining them is not doubted, but the requirement of propriety is the mention of God — exalted be He — and the binding of matters to Him. And this formula indicates that, until by customary usage it became an expression of showing desire (raghbah) and aspiration (tamannī). So when it is said to you, "So-and-so will die soon," and you say, "If God wills," what is understood from you is your desire, not your doubt. And when it is said to you, "So-and-so's illness will leave him and he will recover," and you say, "If God wills," meaning desire — so the word has been diverted from the meaning of doubt to the meaning of desire. Likewise, it is diverted to the meaning of propriety by mentioning God — exalted be He — however the matter may be.

The third aspect is grounded in doubt, and its meaning is: "I am a believer truly, if God wills" — since God — exalted be He — said to a people specified by their very selves: {«Those are the believers truly»}. So they are divided into two categories. And this reverts to doubt regarding the perfection of faith, not its root. And every person is doubtful of the perfection of his faith, and that is not unbelief. Doubt regarding the perfection of faith is sound from two angles: one, that hypocrisy (nifāq) removes the perfection of faith, and it is hidden — one cannot ascertain one's innocence from it. The second, that faith is perfected by acts of obedience, and one does not know their existence in perfection. As for deeds, God — exalted be He — said: {«The believers are only those who believe in God and His Messenger, then do not doubt, and strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of God — those are the truthful»}. So doubt is regarding this truthfulness. Likewise, God — exalted be He — said: {«But righteousness is [in] one who believes in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets»} — and He stipulated twenty attributes, such as fulfillment of covenant and patience in hardship. Then He said — exalted be He: {«Those are the ones who are truthful»}. And He said — exalted be He: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»}. And He said — exalted be He: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} — the verse. And He said — exalted be He: {«They are degrees before God»}. And the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is piety" — the hadith. And the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." This indicates the linkage of the perfection of faith with deeds. As for its linkage with innocence from hypocrisy and hidden polytheism (al-shirk al-khafī), there is his saying — peace be upon him: "Four [traits], whoever has them, is a pure hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims to be a believer: whoever, when he speaks, lies; when he promises, breaks; when he is entrusted, betrays; and when he quarrels, transgresses." And in some narrations: "And when he makes a covenant, he treacherously breaks it." And in the hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: "Hearts are four: a bare heart in which a lamp shines — that is the heart of the believer; and a heart that is covered (muṣaffaḥ) in which there is faith and hypocrisy. The likeness of faith in it is like a green plant that sweet water nourishes, and the likeness of hypocrisy in it is like a sore that pus and matter nourish — whichever of the two nourishments prevails over it, it rules over him." And in another wording: "If it prevails over him, it carries him away." And he said — peace be upon him: "The most numerous of the hypocrites of this community are its reciters (qurrāʾ)." And in the hadith: "Hidden polytheism in my community is more concealed than the crawling of an ant upon a smooth rock." And Ḥudhayfa — God be pleased with him — said: "A man would speak a word in the time of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — by which he would become a hypocrite until he died, and I hear it from one of you ten times a day." And some scholars said: "The closest of people to hypocrisy is the one who sees himself as innocent of hypocrisy." And Ḥudhayfa said: "The hypocrites today are more numerous than they were in the time of the Prophet — peace be upon him. For then they concealed it, and today they display it." And this hypocrisy opposes the truthfulness of faith and its perfection, and it is hidden. And the farthest of people from it is the one who fears it, and the closest of them to it is the one who sees himself as innocent of it.

For it was said to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: "They say there is no hypocrisy today." He said: "O my brother, were the hypocrites to perish, you would feel lonely on the road." And he — or another — said: "Were the hypocrites to grow tails, we would not be able to tread the earth with our feet." And Ibn ʿUmar — God be pleased with him — heard a man speaking against al-Ḥajjāj, and said: "Do you think — were he present and hearing you, would you speak of him thus?" He said: "No." He said: "We used to count this as hypocrisy in the time of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him." And he said — peace be upon him: "Whoever has two tongues in this world, God will make him have two tongues in the Hereafter." And he also said — peace be upon him: "The worst of people is the double-faced one, who comes to these with one face and to those with another." And it was said to al-Ḥasan: "A people say, 'We do not fear hypocrisy.'" He said: "By God, that I should know that I am innocent of hypocrisy is dearer to me than the earth filled with gold." And al-Ḥasan said: "Part of hypocrisy is the discrepancy of tongue and heart, secret and public, entry and exit." And a man said to Ḥudhayfa — God be pleased with him: "I fear that I am a hypocrite." He said: "Were you a hypocrite, you would not fear hypocrisy — for the hypocrite feels secure from hypocrisy." And Ibn Abī Mulayka said: "I reached one hundred and thirty — and in another narration, one hundred and fifty — of the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — all of them fearing hypocrisy."

And it is narrated that the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — was sitting with a group of his Companions, and they mentioned a man and multiplied praise of him. While they were thus, the man appeared to them, his face dripping water from the trace of ablution, his sandal hung in his hand, and between his eyes the trace of prostration. They said: "O Messenger of God, this is the man we described." He said — peace be upon him: "I see on his face a black speck (sufʿah) from the devil." The man came until he greeted and sat with the people. The Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "I adjure you by God: did you say to yourself when you looked upon the people that there is none among them better than you?" He said: "O God, yes." He said — peace be upon him — in his supplication: "O God, I seek Your forgiveness for what I know and what I do not know." So it was said to him: "Do you fear, O Messenger of God?" He said: "And what assures me, while hearts are between two fingers of the fingers of the Merciful, turning them as He wills?" And He — glorified be He — said: {«And there will appear to them from God what they had never reckoned»}. It was said in the exegesis: "They did deeds they thought were good, and they were in the scale of evil deeds."

And Sarī al-Saqaṭī said: "Were a man to enter a garden containing all kinds of trees, upon which were all kinds of birds, and every bird addressed him in a tongue, saying, 'Peace be upon you, O friend of God,' and his soul were to rest in that — he would be a captive in their hands." These reports and traditions make known to you the gravity of the matter, due to the subtleties of hypocrisy and hidden polytheism, and that one is not secure from it — until ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — God be pleased with him — used to ask Ḥudhayfa about himself, whether he was mentioned among the hypocrites. And Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "I heard something from one of the commanders and wished to denounce it, but I feared he would order my execution. And I did not fear death, but I feared that my heart would be adorned for the creatures at the moment of my soul's departure, so I refrained." And this is of the hypocrisy that opposes the reality of faith, its truthfulness, its perfection, and its purity — not its root.

For hypocrisy is of two kinds: one that expels from religion and joins one to the disbelievers, and enters one into the ranks of those eternally in the Fire. The second leads its possessor to the Fire for a period, or diminishes his degrees in ʿIlliyyīn, and lowers his rank among the Ṣiddīqīn. And that is doubtful — therefore the exception is fitting in it. And the root of this hypocrisy is the discrepancy between secret and public, and security from God's deception (makr), and self-admiration (ʿujb), and other matters from which none are free except the Ṣiddīqīn.

The fourth aspect — also grounded in doubt — is from the fear of the final end (khātima). For one does not know whether faith will be secured for him at death or not. For if he is sealed with unbelief, his prior deeds are nullified, because they are contingent upon the soundness of the end. Were a fasting man asked in the forenoon about the soundness of his fast, and he said, "I am fasting, absolutely," then he broke his fast during the rest of the day, his lie would become evident — since soundness is contingent upon completion until sunset at the end of the day. And just as the day is the appointed term for the completion of the fast, so the lifespan is the appointed term for the completion of the soundness of faith. And describing it as sound before its end is based on presumption (istisḥāb), which is doubtful, and the end is feared. And for this reason, the weeping of most of the fearful was for the sake of the end — because it is the fruit of the prior decree (al-qaḍiyyah al-sābiqah) and the eternal will (al-mashīʾah al-azaliyyah), which does not appear except with the appearance of the decreed matter, and none of mankind has access to it. So the fear of the final end is like the fear of the prior decree. And perhaps what appears in the present moment is the opposite of what the word preceded with. So who knows that he is among those for whom the most beautiful [reward] has preceded from God? And it was said regarding the meaning of His saying — exalted be He: {«And the stupor of death has come with the truth»} — that is, with the prior decree, meaning it has made it manifest. And some of the predecessors said: "Only the final ends of deeds are weighed." And Abū al-Dardāʾ — God be pleased with him — used to swear by God: "No one is secure from his faith being stripped from him, except that it is stripped from him." And it was said: "Among sins are sins whose punishment is an evil final end — we seek refuge in God from that." And it was said: "They are punishments for the claim of sainthood (wilāyah) and miracle (karāmah) by fabrication." And some of the knowers (ʿārifūn) said: "Were martyrdom offered to me at the door of the house, and death upon monotheism at the door of the chamber, I would choose death upon monotheism at the door of the chamber — because I do not know what change from monotheism might occur to my heart by the time I reach the door of the house." And another said: "Were I to know a man upon monotheism for fifty years, then a pillar came between me and him and he died, I would not judge that he died upon monotheism." And in the hadith: "Whoever says, 'I am a believer,' is a disbeliever; and whoever says, 'I am a scholar,' is ignorant." And it was said regarding His saying — exalted be He: {«And the words of your Lord have been fulfilled, in truth and justice»} — "in truth" for whoever dies upon faith, and "in justice" for whoever dies upon polytheism. And He said — exalted be He: {«And to God belongs the final outcome of all matters»}. So whenever doubt is of this magnitude, the exception becomes obligatory — because faith is an expression of what benefits Paradise, just as the fast is an expression of what discharges the obligation (al-dhimmah). And what is corrupted before sunset does not discharge the obligation, and thus exits from being a fast. So too faith. Indeed, it is not far that one be asked about a past fast concerning which there is no doubt after its completion, and it be said: "Did you fast yesterday?" and he says: "Yes, if God — exalted be He — wills" — since the true fast is the accepted one, and the accepted is absent from him, known only to God — exalted be He. From this, the exception is fitting in all deeds of righteousness, and it is a doubt regarding acceptance (qabūl) — for hidden causes prevent acceptance after the apparent conditions of soundness have run their course, causes known only to the Lord of lords — majestic is His glory. So doubt therein is fitting.

These, then, are the aspects of the fittingness of the exception in answering regarding faith. And with this we conclude the Book of the Foundations of Creed.

The book is completed by the praise of God — exalted be He — and may He bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to every chosen servant.

chapters.title_en: The Book of the Mysteries of Purification — Being the Third Book of the Quarter of Acts of Worship
chapters.arabic_text: ### || كتاب أسرار الطهارة وهو الكتاب الثالث من ربع العبادات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core root meaning — cleanliness, purity, freedom from filth (both physical and moral); ṭahārah denotes the act of cleansing and the state of being pure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṭahārah signifies both external (ḥissī) purification from ritual impurities (ḥadath and khabath) and internal (maʿnawī) purification of the heart from vices — the latter being the ultimate goal of the former.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — washing with water; metaphorical (majāz) — cleansing the soul from sins and blameworthy traits, as in «طَهِّرْ قَلْبَكَ» (purify your heart).
- Sībawayh Rule: Idāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase «أسرار الطهارة» (mysteries of purification) employs a genitive annexation where the first term (muḍāf) is indefinite and the second (muḍāf ilayh) is definite, yielding a specific, restricted sense: not merely "secrets" but "the secrets pertaining to purification."
chapters.translation: ### The Book of the Mysteries of Purification — and it is the third book of the Quarter of Acts of Worship.

chapters.title_en: The Four Ranks of Purification and the True Meaning of Cleanliness in the Faith
chapters.arabic_text:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي تلطف بعباده فتعبدهم بالنظافة وأفاض على قلوبهم تزكية
لسرائرهم أنواره وألطافه وأعد لظواهرهم تطهيرا لها الماء المخصوص بالرقة
واللطافة وصلى الله على النبي محمد المستغرق بنور الهدى أطراف العالم
وأكنافه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين صلاة تنجينا بركاتها يوم المخافة وتنتصب
جنة بيننا وبين كل آفة
أما بعد
فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنى الدين على النظافة (2) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم مفتاح الصلاة الطهور (3) وقال الله تعالى {فيه رجال يحبون
أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين} وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الطهور نصف
الإيمان (4) وقال الله تعالى {ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد
ليطهركم} فتفطن ذوو البصائر بهذه الظواهر أن أهم الأمور تطهير السرائر إذ
يبعد أن يكون المراد بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الطهور نصف الإيمان عمارة
الظاهر بالتنظيف بإفاضة الماء وإلقائه وتخريب الباطن وإبقائه مشحونا
بالأخباث والأقذار هيهات PageV01P125
هيهات والطهارة لها أربع مراتب
المرتبة الأولى تطهير الظاهر عن الأحداث وعن الأخباث والفضلات
المرتبة الثانية تطهير الجوارح عن الجرائم والآثام
المرتبة الثالثة تطهير القلب عن الأخلاق المذمومة والرذائل الممقوتة
المرتبة الرابعة تطهير السر عما سوى الله تعالى وهي طهارة الأنبياء صلوات
الله عليهم والصديقين والطهارة في كل رتبة نصف العمل الذي فيها فإن الغاية
القصوى في عمل السر أن ينكشف له جلال الله تعالى وعظمته ولن تحل معرفة الله
تعالى بالحقيقة في السر ما لم يرتحل ما سوى الله تعالى عنه
ولذلك قال الله عز وجل {قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون} لأنهما لا
يجتمعان في قلب وما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه وأما عمل القلب فالغاية
القصوى  عمارته بالأخلاق المحمودة والعقائد المشروعة ولن يتصف بها ما لم
ينظف عن نقائضها من العقائد الفاسدة والرذائل الممقوتة فتطهيره أحد الشطرين
وهو الشطر الأول الذي هو شرط في الثاني فكان الطهور شطر الإيمان بهذا
المعنى وكذلك تطهير الجوارح عن المناهي أحد الشطرين وهو الشطر الأول الذي
هو شرط في الثاني فتطهيره أحد الشطرين وهو الشطر الأول وعمارتها بالطاعات
الشطر الثاني فهذه مقامات الإيمان ولكل مقام طبقة ولن ينال العبد الطبقة
العالية إلا أن يجاوز الطبقة السافلة فلا يصل إلى طهارة السر عن الصفات
المذمومة وعمارته بالمحمودة ما لم يفرغ من طهارة القلب عن الخلق المذموم
وعمارته بالخلق المحمود ولن يصل إلى ذلك من لم يفرغ عن طهارة الجوارح عن
المناهي وعمارتها بالطاعات وكلما عز المطلوب وشرف صعب مسلكه وطال طريقه
وكثرت عقباته فلا تظن أن هذا الأمر يدرك وينال بالهوينى نعم من عميت بصيرته
عن تفاوت هذه الطبقات لم يفهم من مراتب الطهارة إلا الدرجة الأخيرة التي هي
كالقشرة الأخيرة الظاهرة بالإضافة إلى اللب المطلوب فصار يمعن فيها ويستقصى
في مجاريها ويستوعب جميع أوقاته في الاستنجاء وغسل الثياب وتنظيف الظاهر
وطلب المياه الجارية الكثيرة ظنا منه بحكم الوسوسة وتخيل العقل أن الطهارة
المطلوبة الشريفة هي هذه فقط وجهالة بسيرة الأولين واستغراقهم جميع الهم
والفكر في تطهير القلب وتساهلهم في أمر الظاهر حتى إن عمر رضي الله عنه مع
علو منصبه توضأ من ماء في جرة نصرانية وحتى إنهم ما كانوا يغسلون اليد من
الدسومات والأطعمة بل كانوا يمسحون أصابعهم بأخمص أقدامهم وعدوا الأشنان من
البدع المحدثة ولقد كانوا يصلون على الأرض في المساجد ويمشون حفاة في
الطرقات ومن كان لا يجعل بينه وبين الأرض حاجزا في مضجعه كان من أكابرهم
وكانوا يقتصرون على الحجارة في الاستنجاء
وقال أبو هريرة وغيره من أهل الصفة كنا نأكل الشواء فتقام الصلاة فندخل
أصابعنا في الحصى ثم نفركها بالتراب ونكبر (1) وقال عمر رضي الله عنه ما
كنا نعرف الأشنان في عصر رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم وإنما كانت مناديلنا
بطون أرجلنا (2) كنا إذا أكلنا الغمر مسحنا بها ويقال أول ما ظهر من البدع
بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربع المناخل والأشنان والموائد والشبع
فكانت عنايتهم كلها بنظافة الباطن حتى قال بعضهم الصلاة في النعلين أفضل
لأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزع نعليه في صلاته بإخبار جبريل
عليه السلام له أن بهما نجاسة وخلع الناس نعالهم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لم
خلعتم نعالكم (3) وقال النخعي في الذين يخلعون نعالهم وددت لو أن محتاجا
جاء إليها فأخذها منكرا لخلع النعال
فهكذا كان تساهلهم في هذه الأمور بل كانوا يمشون في طين الشوارع حفاة
ويجلسون عليها ويصلون PageV01P126
في المساجد على الأرض ويأكلون من دقيق البر والشعير وهو يداس بالدواب
وتبول عليه ولا يحترزون من عرق الإبل والخيل مع كثرة تمرغها في النجاسات
ولم ينقل قط عن أحد منهم سؤال في دقائق النجاسات فهكذا كان تساهلهم فيها
وقد انتهت النوبة الآن إلى طائفة يسمون الرعونة نظافة فيقولون هي مبنى
الدين فأكثر أوقاتهم في تزيينهم الظواهر كفعل الماشطة بعروسها والباطن خراب
مشحون بخبائث الكبر والعجب والجهل والرياء والنفاق ولا يستنكرون ذلك ولا
يتعجبون منه ولو اقتصر مقتصر على الاستنجاء بالحجر أو مشى على الأرض حافيا
أو صلى على الأرض أو على بواري المسجد من غيرسجادة مفروشة أو مشى على الفرش
من غير غلاف للقدم من أدم أو توضأ من آنية عجوز أو رجل غير متقشف أقاموا
عليه القيامة وشدوا عليه النكير ولقيوه بالقذر وأخرجوه من زمرتهم واستنكفوا
عن مؤاكلته ومخالطته
فسموا البذاذة التي هي من الإيمان قذارة والرعونة نظافة فانظر كيف صار
المنكر معروفا والمعروف منكرا وكيف اندرس من الدين رسمه كما اندرس حقيقته
وعلمه
فإن قلت أفتقول إن هذه العادات التي أحدثها الصوفية في هيئاتهم ونظافتهم
من المحظورات أو المنكرات فأقول حاش لله أن أطلق القول فيه من غير تفصيل
ولكني أقول إن هذا التنظيف والتكلف وإعداد الأواني والآلات واستعمال غلاف
القدم والإزار المقنع به لدفع الغبار وغير ذلك من هذه الأسباب إن وقع النظر
إلى ذاتها على سبيل التجرد فهي من المباحات وقد يقترن بها أحوال ونيات
تلحقها تارة بالمعروفات وتارة بالمنكرات فأما كونها مباحة في نفسها فلا
يخفى أن صاحبها متصرف بها في ماله وبدنه وثيابه فيفعل بها ما يريد إذا لم
يكن فيه إضاعة وإسراف وأما مصيرها منكرا فبأن يجعل ذلك أصل الدين ويفسر به
قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنى الدين على النظافة حتى ينكر به على من يتساهل
فيه الأولين أو يكون القصد به تزيين الظاهر للخلق وتحسين موقع نظرهم فإن
ذلك هو الرياء المحظور فيصير منكرا بهذين الاعتبارين أما كونه معروفا فبأن
يكون القصد منه الخير دون التزين وأن لا ينكر على من ترك ذلك ولا يؤخر
بسببه الصلاة عن أوائل الأوقات ولا يشتغل به عن عمل هو أفضل منه أو عن علم
أو غيره فإذا لم يقترن به شيء من ذلك فهو مباح يمكن أن يجعل قربة بالنية
ولكن لا يتيسر ذلك إلا للبطالين الذين لو لم يشتغلوا بصرف الأوقات فيه
لاشتغلوا بنوم أو حديث فيما لا يعني فيصير شغلهم به أولى لأن الاشتغال
بالطهارات يجدد ذكر الله تعالى وذكر العبادات فلا بأس به إذا لم يخرج إلى
منكر أو إسراف
وأما أهل العلم والعمل فلا ينبغي أن يصرفوا من أوقاتهم إليه إلا قدر
الحاجة فالزيادة عليه منكر في حقهم وتضييع العمر الذي هو أنفس الجواهر
وأعزها في حق من قدر على الانتفاع به
ولا يتعجب من ذلك فإن حسنات الأبرار سيئات المقربين
ولا ينبغي للبطال أن يترك النظافة وينكر على المتصوفة ويزعم أنه يتشبه
بالصحابة إذ التشبه بهم في أن لا يتفرغ إلا لما هو أهم منه كما قيل لداود
الطائي لم لا تسرح لحيتك قال إني إذن لفارغ
فلهذا لا أرى للعالم ولا للمتعلم ولا للعامل أن يضيع وقته في غسل الثياب
إحترازا من أن يلبس الثياب المقصورة وتوهما بالقصار تقصيرا في  الغسل فقد
كانوا في العصر الأول يصلون في الفراء المدبوغة ولم يعلم منهم من فرق بين
المقصورة والمدبوغة في الطهارة والنجاسة بل كانوا يجتنبون النجاسة إذا
شاهدوها ولا يدققون نظرهم في استنباط الاحتمالات الدقيقة بل كانوا يتأملون
في دقائق الرياء والظلم حتى قال سفيان الثوري لرفيق له كان يمشي معه فنظر
إلى باب دار مرفوع معمور لا تفعل ذلك فإن الناس لو لم ينظروا إليه لكان
صاحبه لا يتعاطى هذا الإسراف
فالناظر إليه معين له على الإسراف
فكانوا يعدون جمام الذهن لاستنباط مثل هذه الدقائق لا في احتمالات
النجاسة
فلو وجد العالم عاميا
PageV01P127
يتعاطى له غسل الثياب محتاطا فهو أفضل فإنه بالإضافة إلى التساهل خير
وذلك العامي ينتفع بتعاطيه إذ يشغل نفسه الأمارة بالسوء بعمل المباح في
نفسه فيمتنع عليه المعاصي في تلك الحال
والنفس إن لم تشغل بشيء شغلت صاحبها وإذا قصد به التقرب إلى العالم صار
ذلك عنده من أفضل القربات
فوقت العالم أشرف من أن يصرفه إلى مثله فيبقى محفوظا عليه وأشرف وقت
العامي أن يشتغل بمثله فيتوفر الخير عليه من الجوانب كلها
وليتفطن بهذا المثل لنظائره من الأعمال وترتيب فضائلها ووجه تقديم البعض
منها على بعض فتدقيق الحساب في حفظ لحظات العمر بصرفها إلى الأفضل أهم من
التدقيق في أمور الدنيا بحذافيرها
وإذا عرفت هذه المقدمة واستبنت أن الطهارة لها أربع مراتب
فاعلم أنا في هذا الكتاب لسنا نتكلم إلا في المرتبة الرابعة وهي نظافة
الظاهر لأنا في الشطر الأول من الكتاب لا نتعرض قصدا إلا للظواهر
فنقول طهارة الظاهر ثلاثة أقسام طهارة عن الخبث وطهارة عن الحدث وطهارة
عن فضلات البدن وهي التي تحصل بالقلم والاستحداد واستعمال النورة والختان
وغيره
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is cleanliness and freedom from filth, whether physical or spiritual; the root denotes removal of impurity (najāsah) and defilement (khabath).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṭahārah signifies purification of the soul from moral vices and false beliefs, culminating in the heart's cleansing from all save God—the rank of the prophets and the veracious (ṣiddīqūn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, ṭahārah applies to physical washing with water; metaphorically (majāz), it extends to inner purification of the heart and secret (sirr), as in the prophetic saying "purification is half of faith" (al-ṭuhūr niṣf al-īmān).
- Root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The innermost secret, the hidden depth of the self; that which is concealed from others and even from oneself in its deepest recesses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The sirr is the innermost faculty of the soul where divine knowledge (maʿrifah) is unveiled; it is the locus of the highest spiritual rank, purified only by emptying it of all other than God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, a secret kept hidden; metaphorically, the spiritual core that must be emptied of creatures to be filled with the Creator.
- Root: خ-ب-ث (kh-b-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: That which is foul, corrupt, and impure—both physical filth and moral depravity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khabāʾith are the spiritual impurities of the heart—vices, false doctrines, and blameworthy traits—that must be expelled for faith to take root.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, physical impurity; metaphorically, the moral and spiritual corruptions that defile the inner self.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Gradation (al-tarattub) — The sentence structure employs a sequential ordering of ranks (marātib) where each level is a necessary condition (sharṭ) for the next, expressed through conditional and purposive clauses (law, ḥattā, fa-lā yaṣil), requiring careful parsing of the logical progression from outer to inner purification.
chapters.translation:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God, who is gracious to His servants, commanding them to cleanliness, and who pours upon their hearts the purification of their innermost secrets with His lights and graces, and who has prepared for their outward forms a cleansing through water, distinguished as it is by its gentleness and subtlety. And may God's blessings be upon the Prophet Muhammad, whose light of guidance has encompassed the extremities of the world and its regions, and upon his family, the good and the pure, a blessing whose blessings may save us on the Day of Fear and stand as a shield between us and every affliction.

To proceed:

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Religion is built upon cleanliness." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The key to prayer is purification." And God, exalted be He, said: {«فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين»} ("In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves"). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Purification is half of faith." And God, exalted be He, said: {«ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم»} ("God does not intend to place upon you any hardship, but He intends to purify you").

Thus, those of insight perceived through these outward texts that the most important of matters is the purification of the inner secrets (taṭhīr al-sarāʾir), for it is far-fetched that the intent of his saying, peace be upon him, "Purification is half of faith," should be the cultivation of the outward form through cleansing by pouring and casting water, while the inward is left ruined, remaining stuffed with filths and impurities. Far from it! Far from it!

And purification has four ranks:

The first rank: purifying the outward form from ritual impurities (aḥdāth) and from physical filths (akhbāth) and bodily waste.

The second rank: purifying the bodily members from crimes and sins.

The third rank: purifying the heart from blameworthy traits and abhorred vices.

The fourth rank: purifying the innermost secret (sirr) from all other than God, exalted be He—and this is the purification of the prophets, God's blessings be upon them, and of the veracious (ṣiddīqīn).

And purification in every rank is half of the work proper to that rank. For the ultimate goal in the work of the secret is that the majesty of God, exalted be He, and His greatness should be unveiled to it; and the knowledge of God (maʿrifah) in truth will never settle in the secret so long as anything other than God has not departed from it. For this reason God, mighty and majestic, said: {«قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون»} ("Say: God—then leave them in their vain discourse, playing"), because the two cannot coexist in one heart—and God has not made for any man two hearts in his breast.

As for the work of the heart, the ultimate goal is its cultivation with praiseworthy traits and lawful beliefs; and it will never be so characterized unless it is cleansed of their opposites—corrupt beliefs and abhorred vices. Thus, its purification is one of the two halves, being the first half which is a condition for the second. So "purification is half of faith" is true in this sense. Likewise, purifying the bodily members from forbidden things is one of the two halves, being the first half which is a condition for the second; its purification is one half, and their cultivation through acts of obedience is the second half.

These, then, are the stations of faith (maqāmāt al-īmān), and for every station there is a level. And a servant will never attain the higher level unless he passes beyond the lower level. Thus, one does not reach the purification of the secret from blameworthy attributes and its cultivation with praiseworthy ones unless he has completed the purification of the heart from blameworthy character and its cultivation with praiseworthy character. And one does not reach that unless he has completed the purification of the bodily members from forbidden things and their cultivation through acts of obedience.

And whenever the sought object is more precious and nobler, its path becomes harder, its road longer, and its obstacles more numerous. So do not think that this matter is attained and reached with ease and indolence. Indeed, whoever's insight is blind to the disparity of these levels understands from the ranks of purification only the last degree, which is like the outermost shell in relation to the sought kernel. So he becomes engrossed in it, exhausts himself in its channels, and spends all his time in cleansing after relieving oneself, washing garments, cleaning the outward form, and seeking abundant running waters—imagining, by the judgment of obsessive whisperings (waswasah) and the delusion of the intellect, that the sought and noble purification is only this. This is ignorance of the conduct of the early generations (salaf), and of their absorption of all concern and thought in purifying the heart, and their leniency in outward matters—so much so that ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, despite his lofty station, performed ablution from water in a Christian woman's jar. And they did not wash their hands from greases and foods, but rather wiped their fingers on the soles of their feet, and they counted soap-weed (ushnān) among the innovated novelties (bidaʿ). They used to pray on the ground in the mosques and walk barefoot in the streets; and whoever made no barrier between himself and the ground in his sleeping place was among their great ones. And they limited themselves to stones in cleansing after relieving oneself.

Abū Hurayrah and others of the People of the Bench (ahl al-ṣuffah) said: "We used to eat roasted meat, and when the prayer was established, we would thrust our fingers into the pebbles, then rub them with dust, and enter the prayer." And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "We did not know soap-weed (ushnān) in the era of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him; our handkerchiefs were the soles of our feet—when we ate greasy food, we wiped them with them." And it is said: The first novelties (bidaʿ) to appear after the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, were four: sieves, soap-weed, dining tables, and eating to satiety.

So their entire concern was with the cleanliness of the inward, until one of them said: "Prayer in sandals is superior," because the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, when he removed his sandals in his prayer upon the information of Gabriel, peace be upon him, that there was filth upon them, and the people removed their sandals, he said, peace be upon him: "Why did you remove your sandals?" And al-Nakhaʿī said regarding those who remove their sandals: "I wish that a needy person would come and take them," disapproving of the removal of sandals.

Thus was their leniency in these matters. Indeed, they walked barefoot in the mud of the streets, sat upon it, prayed in the mosques on the ground, and ate from the flour of wheat and barley which was trodden by beasts and urinated upon. And they did not guard against the sweat of camels and horses, despite their frequent rolling in impurities. And it has never been transmitted from any of them a question concerning the subtleties of impurities. Thus was their leniency in them.

And now the turn has come to a group who call foolish vanity (ruʿūnah) "cleanliness," saying it is the foundation of religion. So most of their time is spent in adorning their outward forms, like the act of a bridal beautician with her bride, while the inward is ruined, stuffed with the wickedness of pride, self-admiration, ignorance, ostentation (riyāʾ), and hypocrisy—and they do not disapprove of this nor marvel at it. And if one were to limit himself to cleansing with a stone, or walk on the ground barefoot, or pray on the ground or on the mosque's reed mats without a spread prayer rug, or walk on carpets without a leather foot-covering, or perform ablution from an old woman's vessel—a man not given to affected refinement—they would raise a great outcry against him, heap censure upon him, meet him with revulsion, expel him from their company, and disdain to eat with him or associate with him.

So they have named the shabbiness (badhādhah) which is part of faith "filth," and foolish vanity (ruʿūnah) "cleanliness." See how the disapproved has become approved and the approved disapproved, and how the mark of religion has been effaced from it, even as its reality and knowledge have been effaced.

If you say: "Do you then say that these customs which the Sufis have introduced in their appearances and their cleanliness are among the prohibited or disapproved things?" I say: God forbid that I should make an unqualified statement about this without detail. Rather, I say: This cleansing and affectation, the preparation of vessels and instruments, the use of foot-coverings and the veiled garment to repel dust, and other such causes—if one looks at them in themselves, in abstraction, they are among the permissible things (mubāḥāt). But there may attach to them states and intentions that sometimes render them among the approved things (maʿrūfāt) and sometimes among the disapproved things (munkarāt).

As for their being permissible in themselves, it is not hidden that their practitioner is thereby disposing of his own wealth, body, and garments, doing with them what he wills, so long as there is no wastefulness or extravagance in it.

As for their becoming disapproved (munkar), it is by making this a foundation of religion and interpreting by it his saying, peace be upon him, "Religion is built upon cleanliness," so that one thereby censures those who are lenient in it from among the early generations—or by intending thereby the adornment of the outward for creatures and the improvement of their view of him, for that is the prohibited ostentation (riyāʾ). Thus it becomes disapproved by these two considerations.

As for its being approved (maʿrūf), it is that the intention therein be goodness without adornment, and that one not censure those who abandon it, nor delay the prayer from its earliest times because of it, nor occupy himself with it to the exclusion of a work better than it, or of knowledge, or other things. When nothing of this attaches to it, it is permissible, and it can be made an act of devotion (qurbah) by intention. But this is not facilitated except for the idle (baṭṭālīn) who, if they did not occupy themselves with spending their time in it, would occupy themselves with sleep or idle talk about what does not concern them. Thus, their occupation with it is more fitting, because occupying oneself with purifications renews the remembrance of God and the remembrance of acts of worship. So there is no harm in it, so long as it does not lead to something disapproved or to extravagance.

As for the people of knowledge and practice, they should not divert from their time to it more than the measure of need; excess beyond that is disapproved in their case—a squandering of the lifespan, which is the most precious and dearest of jewels, for one who is able to benefit from it. And do not marvel at this, for "the good deeds of the righteous are the evil deeds of those brought near" (ḥasanāt al-abrār sayyiʾāt al-muqarrabīn).

Nor should the idle person abandon cleanliness and censure the Sufis, claiming that he is imitating the Companions—for imitating them consists in not being free except for what is more important than it, as was said to Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī: "Why do you not trim your beard?" He said: "Then I would indeed be idle."

For this reason, I do not deem it fitting for the scholar, nor for the student, nor for the practitioner to waste his time in washing garments, guarding against wearing improperly washed clothes, and imagining that the launderer has been negligent in the washing. For in the first age they used to pray in tanned furs, and none of them is known to have distinguished between improperly washed and tanned garments regarding purity and impurity. Rather, they avoided impurity when they witnessed it, and did not refine their gaze in deriving subtle probabilities. Rather, they reflected upon the subtleties of ostentation and injustice—so much so that Sufyān al-Thawrī said to a companion walking with him who looked at the raised, well-built door of a house: "Do not do that; for if people did not look at it, its owner would not engage in this extravagance. So the one who looks at it is his helper in extravagance."

Thus, they counted the freshness of the mind for deriving such subtleties as a duty, not for the probabilities of impurity.

So if a scholar finds a commoner (ʿāmmī) who occupies himself with washing his garments out of caution, that is better—for in comparison to leniency, it is good. And that commoner benefits from his occupation, for he occupies his soul, which commands to evil, with an act permissible in itself, and thereby refrains from sins in that state. For the soul, if not occupied with something, occupies its owner. And if he intends thereby drawing near to the scholar, it becomes with him among the most excellent of devotional acts.

So the scholar's time is too noble to divert it to such a matter; thus it remains preserved for him. And the most noble time of the commoner is to occupy himself with such a matter; thus goodness accrues to him from all sides.

And let one perceive by this example its parallels among works, the ordering of their excellences, and the manner of preferring some over others. For the precise reckoning in preserving the moments of the lifespan by directing them to what is best is more important than precision in all the affairs of this world, to their very entirety.
