And when you have understood this preamble and ascertained that purification has four ranks, know that in this book we speak only of the fourth rank—namely, the cleanliness of the outward—for in the first half of the book we do not intentionally address anything but the outward forms.

So we say: The purification of the outward is of three kinds: purification from physical filth (khabath), purification from ritual impurity (ḥadath), and purification from bodily waste—which is achieved by trimming the nails, shaving the pubic hair, using depilatory lime (nūrah), circumcision, and the like.

chapters.title_en: On the Purification from Filth (Ṭahārat al-Khabath): The Substance Removed, the Remover, and the Act of Removal
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| القسم الأول في طهارة الخبث والنظر فيه يتعلق بالمزال والمزال به والإزالة

### |||| الطرف الأول في المزال

وهي النجاسة
والأعيان ثلاثة جمادات وحيوانات وأجزاء حيوانات
أما الجمادات فطاهرة كلها إلا الخمر وكل منتبذ مسكر والحيوانات طاهرة
كلها إلا الكلب والخنزير وما تولد منهما أو من أحدهما
فإذا ماتت فكلها نجسة إلا خمسة الآدمي والسمك والجراد ودود التفاح وفي
معناه كل ما يستحيل من الأطعمة وكل ما ليس له نفس سائلة كالذباب والخنفساء
وغيرهما فلا ينجس الماء بوقوع شيء منها فيه
وأما أجزاء الحيوانات فقسمان أحدهما ما يقطع منه وحكمه حكم الميت
والشعر لا ينجس بالجز والموت والعظم ينجس
الثاني الرطوبات الخارجة من باطنه فكل ما ليس مستحيلا ولا له مقر فهو
طاهر كالدمع والعرق واللعاب والمخاط وما له مقر وهو مستحيل فنجس إلا ما هو
مادة الحيوان كالمني والبيض
والقيح والدم والروث والبول نجس من الحيوانات كلها
ولا يعفى عن شيء من هذه النجاسات قليلها وكثيرها إلا عن خمسة الأول أثر
النجو بعد الاستجمار بالأحجار يعفى عنه ما لم يعد المخرج
والثاني طين الشوارع وغبار الروث في الطريق يعفى عنه مع تيقن النجاسة
بقدر ما يتعذر الاحتراز عنه وهو الذي لا ينسب المتلطخ به إلى تفريط أو سقطة
الثالث ما على أسفل الخف من نجاسة لا يخلو الطريق عنها فيعفى عنه بعد
الدلك للحاجة
الرابع دم البراغيث ما قل منه أو كثر إلا إذا جاوز حد العادة سواء كان في
ثوبك أو في ثوب غيرك فلبسته
الخامس دم البثرات وما ينفصل منها من قيح وصديد
ودلك ابن عمر رضي الله عنه بثرة على وجهه فخرج منها الدم وصلى ولم يغتسل
وفي معناه ما يترشح من لطخات الدماميل التي تدوم غالبا وكذلك أثر الفصد
إلا ما يقع نادرا من خراج أو غيره فيلحق بدم الاستحاضة ولا يكون في معنى
البثرات التي لا يخلو الإنسان عنها في أحواله
ومسامحة الشرع في هذه النجاسات الخمس تعرفك أن أمر الطهارة على التساهل
وما ابتدع فيها وسوسة لا أصل لها

### |||| الطرف الثاني في المزال به
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of cleanliness, purity, and freedom from physical or ritual defilement; the opposite of najāsah (filth).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṭahārah signifies both sensory purity (naẓāfah) and spiritual purification (tazkiyah), yet here it is restricted to the legal category of removing physical impurities (khabath) as opposed to ritual impurity (ḥadath).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes actual cleansing with water or earth; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to exoneration from sin—but the present context is strictly literal.
- Root: ن-ج-س (n-j-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Filth, dirt, and that which is repugnant to the senses or to the Law.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Najāsah is a legal designation (ḥukm sharʿī) attached to specific substances, not a natural property; it renders prayer invalid if present beyond the pardoned limits.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical impurity; metaphorical for moral abomination—here, only the literal is intended.
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pardon, to excuse, to overlook; also to erase or obliterate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, ʿafw denotes the remission of a ruling (rafʿ al-ḥukm) regarding a small or unavoidable quantity of impurity, out of divine facilitation (taysīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for erasure; metaphorical for legal pardon—here, the legal sense of "excused" or "pardoned" is operative.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Exception (al-Istithnāʾ) — In the phrase "except five" (illā khamsah), the exception is muttaṣil (connected) and mufarragḥ (exhaustive), extracting the enumerated items from the general ruling of impurity, while the subsequent detailing (tafṣīl) follows the pattern of ʿaṭf al-bayān (explanatory apposition) to specify each pardoned case.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first section concerns the purification from filth (khabath). The inquiry into it pertains to three matters: the substance removed (al-muzāl), the remover (al-muzāl bihi), and the act of removal (al-izālah).

The first branch: the substance removed — and it is impurity (najāsah).

The [categories of] corporeal substances are three: inanimate solids (jamādāt), animals (ḥayawānāt), and parts of animals (ajzāʾ ḥayawānāt).

As for inanimate solids, all of them are pure (ṭāhir) except wine (khamr) and every intoxicating infusion (nabīdh muskir). As for animals, all of them are pure except the dog, the pig, and whatever is generated from both of them or from one of them.

When these [unclean animals] die, then all of them become impure (najis) — except five: the human being, the fish, the locust, and the worm of apples (dūd al-tuffāḥ). And in the same category [as the apple worm] is everything that transforms from foods [into worms], and everything that has no flowing blood (nafs sāʾilah) — such as the fly and the beetle and the like. Thus, water is not rendered impure by the falling of any of these into it.

As for the parts of animals, they are of two divisions. The first: whatever is cut off from a living animal — its ruling is the ruling of the dead [animal, i.e., impure]. However, hair is not rendered impure by shearing (jaz) or by death, whereas bone is rendered impure [by death].

The second division: the moistures (ruṭūbāt) that exit from its interior. So everything that is not transformed [from another substance] and has no receptacle (muqarr) is pure — such as tears, sweat, saliva, and nasal mucus. And whatever has a receptacle and is transformed [from another substance] is impure — except what is the generative substance (māddah) of the animal, such as semen (manī) and the egg.

Pus (qayḥ), blood, dung (rawth), and urine are impure from all animals.

And no remission (ʿafw) is granted for any of these impurities — whether little or much — except for five:

The first: the trace of excrement after cleansing with stones (istijmār); it is pardoned as long as the exit [of the anus] has not been re-soiled.

The second: the mud of the streets and the dust of dung upon the road; it is pardoned — even with certainty of the impurity — to the extent that avoidance is impossible, namely, that which does not attribute the one soiled with it to negligence (tafrīṭ) or a fall (saqṭah).

The third: whatever is upon the lower part of the leather sock (khuff) of impurity that the road does not lack; it is pardoned after rubbing (dalk) due to necessity.

The fourth: the blood of fleas — whether little or much — except when it exceeds the customary limit (ḥadd al-ʿādah), whether it be upon your garment or upon the garment of another which you then wear.

The fifth: the blood of pustules (buthrāt) and whatever separates from them of pus and serum (ṣadīd). And Ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — rubbed a pustule on his face, and blood came out of it, and he prayed without washing. And in the same category is what oozes from the smears of boils (damāmīl) that generally persist, and likewise the trace of bloodletting (faṣd) — except what occurs rarely from an abscess (kharāj) or otherwise, for that is annexed to the blood of prolonged uterine bleeding (istḥāḍah) and is not in the category of pustules from which a person is never free in his states.

And the Law’s leniency (musāmaḥah) regarding these five impurities informs you that the matter of purification is [built] upon facilitation (tasāhul). And what has been innovated in it of obsessive scruples (waswasah) has no foundation [in the Law].

chapters.title_en: On the Purification of Water and the Relaxation of Strictness in Matters of Filth (Fiqh al-Miyāh wa al-Tasāhu fī al-Najāsāt)
chapters.arabic_text:
وهو إما جامد وإما مائع أما الجامد فحجر الاستنجاء وهو مطهر تطهير تخفيف
بشرط أن يكون صلبا طاهرا منشفا غير محترم وأما المائعات فلا تزال النجاسات
بشيء منها إلا الماء ولا كل ماء بل الطاهر الذي  لم يتفاحش
PageV01P128
تغيره بمخالطة ما يستغنى عنه
ويخرج الماء عن الطهارة بأن يتغير بملاقاة النجاسة طعمه أو لونه أو ريحه
فإن لم يتغير وكان قريبا من مائتين وخمسين منا وهو خمسمائة رطل برطل
العراق لم ينجس لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بلغ الماء قلتين لم يحمل خبثا
(1) وإن كان دونه صار نجسا عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه هذا في الماء الراكد
وأما الماء الجاري إذا تغير بالنجاسة فالجرية المتغيرة نجسة دون ما فوقها
وما تحتها لأن جريات الماء متفاصلات
وكذا النجاسة الجارية إذا جرت بمجرى الماء فالنجس موقعها من الماء وما عن
يمينها وشمالها إذا تقاصر عن قلتين
وإن كان جري الماء أقوى من جري النجاسة فما فوق النجاسة طاهر وما سفل
عنها فنجس وإن تباعد وكثر إلا إذا اجتمع في حوض قدر قلتين
وإذا اجتمع قلتان من ماء نجس طهر ولا يعود نجسا بالتفريق
هذا هو مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه
وكنت أود أن يكون مذهبه كمذهب مالك رضي الله عنه في أن الماء وإن قل لا
ينجس إلا بالتغير إذ الحاجة ماسة إليه ومثار الوسواس اشترط القلتين ولأجله
شق على الناس ذلك وهو لعمري سبب المشقة ويعرفه من يجربه ويتأمله
ومما لا أشك فيه أن ذلك لو كان مشروطا لكان أولى المواضع بتعسر الطهارة
مكة والمدينة إذ لا يكثر فيهما المياه الجارية ولا الراكدة الكثيرة
ومن أول عصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى آخر عصر أصحابه لم تنقل
واقعة في الطهارة ولا سؤال عن كيفية حفظ الماء عن النجاسات
وكانت أواني مياههم يتعاطاها الصبيان والإماء الذين لا يحترزون عن
النجاسات
وقد توضأ عمر رضي الله عنه بماء في جرة نصرانية وهذا كالصريح في أنه لم
يعول إلا على عدم تغير الماء وإلا فنجاسة النصرانية وإنائها غالبة تعلم بظن
قريب فإذا عسر القيام بهذا المذهب
وعدم وقوع السؤال في تلك الأعصار دليل أول
وفعل عمر رضي الله عنه دليل ثان
والدليل الثالث إصغاء رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم الإناء للهرة (2)
وعدم تغطية الأواني منها بعد أن يرى أنها تأكل الفأرة ولم يكن في بلادهم
حياض تلغ السنانير فيها وكانت لا تنزل الآبار
والرابع أن الشافعي رضي الله عنه نص على أن غسالة النجاسة طاهرة إذا لم
تتغير ونجسة إن تغيرت وأي فرق بين أن يلاقي الماء النجاسة بالورود عليها أو
بورودها عليه وأي معنى لقول القائل إن قوة الورود تدفع النجاسة مع ان
الورود لم يمنع مخالطة النجاسة وإن أحيل ذلك على الحاجة فالحاجة أيضا ماسة
إلى هذا فلا فرق بين طرح الماء في إجانة فيها ثوب نجس أو طرح الثوب النجس
في الإجانة وفيها ماء وكل ذلك معتاد في غسل الثياب والأواني والخامس أنهم
كانوا يستنجون على أطراف المياه الجارية القليلة ولا خلاف في مذهب الشافعي
رضي الله عنه أنه إذا وقع بول في ماء جار ولم يتغير أنه يجوز التوضؤ به وإن
كان قليلا
وأي فرق بين الجاري والراكد وليت شعري هل الحوالة على عدم التغير أولى أو
على قوة الماء بسبب الجريان ثم ما حد تلك القوة أتجري في المياه الجارية في
أنابيب الحمامات أم لا فإن لم تجر فما الفرق وإن جرت فما الفرق بين ما يقع
فيها وبين ما يقع في مجرى الماء من الأواني على الأبدان وهي أيضا جارية ثم
البول أشد اختلاطا بالماء الجاري من نجاسة جامدة ثابتة إذا قضى بأن ما يجري
عليها وإن لم يتغير نجس أن يجتمع في مستنقع قلتان فأي فرق بين الجامد
والمائع والماء واحد والاختلاط أشد من المجاورة
والسادس أنه إذا وقع رطل من البول في قلتين ثم فرقتا فكل كوز يغترف منه
طاهر ومعلوم أن البول منتشر فيه وهو قليل وليت شعري هل تعليل طهارته بعدم
التغير أولى أو بقوة الماء بعد انقطاع الكثرة وزوالها مع PageV01P129
تحقق بقاء أجزاء النجاسة فيها
والسابع أن الحمامات لم تزل في الأعصار الخالية يتوضأ فيها المتقشفون
ويغمسون الأيدي والأواني في تلك الحياض مع قلة الماء  ومع العلم بأن الأيدي
النجسة والطاهرة كانت تتوارد عليها
فهذه الأمور مع الحاجة الشديدة تقوى في النفس أنهم كانوا ينظرون إلى عدم
التغير معولين على قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم خلق الماء طهورا لا ينجسه شيء
إلا ما غير طعمه أو لونه أو ريحه (1) وهذا فيه تحقيق وهو أن طبع كل مائع أن
يقلب إلى صفة نفسه كل ما يقع فيه وكان مغلوبا من جهته فكما ترى الكلب يقع
في المملحة فيستحيل ملحا ويحكم بطهارته بصيرورته ملحا وزوال صفة الكلبية
عنه فكذلك الخل يقع في الماء وكذا اللبن يقع فيه وهو قليل فتبطل صفته
ويتصور بصفة الماء وينطبع بطبعه إلا إذا كثر وغلب وتعرف غلبته بغلبة طعمه
أو لونه أو ريحه فهذا المعيار
وقد أشار الشرع إليه في الماء القوي على إزالة النجاسة وهو جدير بأن يعول
عليه فيندفع به الحرج ويظهر به معنى كونه طهورا إذ يغلب عليه فيطهره كما
صار كذلك فيما بعد القلتين وفي الغسالة وفي الماء الجاري وفي إصغاء الإناء
للهرة ولا تظن ذلك عفوا إذ لو كان كذلك لكان كأثر الاستنجاء ودم البراغيث
حتى يصير الماء الملاقي له نجسا ولا ينجس بالغسالة ولا بولوغ السنور في
الماء القليل
وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحمل خبثا فهو في نفسه مبهم فإنه يحمل
إذا تغير
فإن قيل أراد به إذا لم يتغير فيمكن أن يقال إنه أراد به أنه في الغالب
لا يتغير بالنجاسات المعتادة ثم هو تمسك بالمفهوم فيما إذا لم يبلغ قلتين
وترك المفهوم بأقل من ألأدلة التي ذكرناها ممكن وقوله لا يحمل خبثا ظاهره
نفي الحمل أي يقلبه إلى صفة نفسه كما يقال للمملحة لا تحمل كلبا ولا غيره
أي ينقلب وذلك لأن الناس قد يستنجون في المياه القليلة وفي الغدران ويغمسون
الأواني النجسة فيها ثم يترددون في أنها تغيرت تغيرا مؤثر أم لا فتبين أنه
إذا كان قلتين لا يتغير بهذه النجاسة المعتادة
فإن قلت فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه  وسلم لا يحمل خبثا ومهما كثرت حملها
فهذا ينقلب عليك فإنها مهما كثرت حملها حكما كما حملها حسا
فلا بد من التخصيص بالنجاسات المعتادة على المذهبين جميعا
وعلى الجملة فميلي في أمور النجاسات المعتادة إلى التساهل فهما من سيرة
الأولين وحسما لمادة الوسواس وبذلك أفتيت بالطهارة فيما وقع الخلاف فيه في
مثل هذه المسائل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-د (j-m-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Solid, congealed, that which is fixed and unmoving; opposed to liquid (mā'iʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, denotes the state of a substance retaining its form without flowing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical solidity; metaphorical (majāz) for firmness of resolve.
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cleanliness, purity, freedom from filth—both physical and spiritual.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purity (ṭahārah) as a legal category distinguishing permissible from impermissible.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical cleanliness; metaphorical for moral/spiritual purity.
- Root: غ-ل-ب (gh-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To overcome, dominate, prevail; the state of a thing's property superseding another's.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The principle of ghālib (predominance) in determining legal effect—when one substance overwhelms another, its ruling prevails.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical overpowering; metaphorical for legal predominance in juristic reasoning.
- Root: ن-ج-س (n-j-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Impurity, filth; that which is repugnant and forbidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal impurity (najāsah) as a status affecting permissibility of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical uncleanness; metaphorical for moral defilement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), as in "if it reaches two qullas, it does not carry impurity," where the legal ruling is suspended upon the fulfillment of the condition.
chapters.translation:
I say: And it [the purifying substance] is either solid or liquid. As for the solid, it is the stone of istinjā' (cleansing after relieving oneself), and it is a purifier with a purification of alleviation (takhfīf), on the condition that it be hard, pure, absorbent, and not venerated [i.e., not a substance held in respect, like food or inscribed material]. As for liquids, impurities are not removed by any of them except water—and not all water, but rather the pure [water] whose change has not become excessive (lam yatafāḥash) due to admixture with what is dispensable [i.e., foreign substances one can do without].

And water exits from the state of purity by becoming changed through contact with impurity—whether its taste, its color, or its odor [is altered]. If it is not changed, and it is near two hundred and fifty manns—which is five hundred ratls by the Iraqi ratl—it does not become impure, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إذا بلغ الماء قلتين لم يحمل خبثا»} ("When water reaches two qullas, it does not carry impurity"). But if it is less than that, it becomes impure according to al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him. This applies to still water (al-mā' al-rākid).

As for flowing water (al-mā' al-jārī), if it becomes changed by impurity, then the changed current (al-jaryah al-mutaghayyirah) is impure, but not what is above it or below it, because the currents of water are separate entities (mutafāṣilāt). Likewise, if a flowing impurity runs in the course of water, then the impure [portion] is its location in the water, and what is to its right and left—if it falls short of two qullas. And if the flow of the water is stronger than the flow of the impurity, then what is above the impurity is pure, and what is below it is impure—even if it is distant and abundant—except if it collects in a basin to the measure of two qullas. And if two qullas of impure water collect, it becomes pure, and it does not return to impurity by being divided [afterward].

This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him.

And I had wished that his school were like the school of Mālik, may God be pleased with him—namely, that water, however little, does not become impure except by change [of its properties]—for the need for it is pressing, and the source of obsessive scrupulosity (al-waswās) is the stipulation of two qullas, and for its sake this has become difficult for people. And by my life, it is the cause of hardship, and he who tries it and reflects upon it knows this.

And among what I do not doubt is that if this [stipulation of two qullas] were required, then the most fitting places for the difficulty of purification would be Mecca and Medina, for in them there are neither abundant flowing waters nor abundant still waters. And from the beginning of the era of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to the end of the era of his Companions, no incident concerning purification has been transmitted, nor any question about how to preserve water from impurities. And their water vessels were handled by boys and slave-girls who did not guard against impurities.

And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, performed ablution with water from a jar belonging to a Christian woman. This is almost explicit [proof] that he relied only upon the non-change of the water—for otherwise, the impurity of the Christian woman and her vessel is predominant, known by a near [degree of] conjecture. So when adhering to this school [of the two qullas] becomes difficult—

And the non-occurrence of questioning in those eras is the first proof.
And the act of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, is the second proof.
And the third proof is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, tilting the vessel for the cat {«إصغاء الإناء للهرة»} and not covering the vessels from it, after he saw that it eats the mouse—and in their lands there were no basins in which cats lapped, and they did not descend into wells.
And the fourth [proof] is that al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, explicitly ruled that the washing-water of impurity (ghusālah) is pure if it is not changed, and impure if it is changed. And what difference is there between water meeting impurity by flowing upon it, or impurity flowing upon it? And what meaning is there in one's saying, "The force of the flow repels impurity," given that the flow does not prevent the admixture of impurity? And if this is referred to necessity, then necessity also presses here—so there is no difference between throwing water into a basin containing an impure garment, or throwing the impure garment into the basin containing water. All of this is customary in washing clothes and vessels.
And the fifth [proof] is that they used to perform istinjā' at the edges of small flowing waters. And there is no disagreement in the school of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, that if urine falls into flowing water and it is not changed, it is permissible to perform ablution with it, even if it is little. And what difference is there between flowing and still [water]? Would that I knew—is reliance upon non-change more appropriate, or upon the strength of water due to its flowing? Then what is the limit of that strength? Does it flow in the waters of bathhouse pipes or not? If it does not flow, what is the difference? And if it flows, what is the difference between what falls into it and what falls into the course of water from vessels upon bodies—which are also flowing? Then urine is more thoroughly mixed with flowing water than a solid, fixed impurity. If it is ruled that what flows over it, even if unchanged, is impure—unless it collects in a pool to two qullas—then what difference is there between the solid and the liquid? Water is one, and mixing is more intense than mere adjacency.
And the sixth [proof] is that if a ratl of urine falls into two qullas, then they are divided, every jug scooped from it is pure—and it is known that the urine is dispersed in it, and it is little. Would that I knew—is the explanation of its purity by non-change more appropriate, or by the strength of water after the cessation of quantity and its removal, despite the confirmed persistence of impurity particles within it?
And the seventh [proof] is that bathhouses have never ceased, in bygone eras, to be places where the scrupulous (al-mutaqashshifūn) performed ablution, dipping hands and vessels into those basins—despite the scarcity of water and the knowledge that impure and pure hands would alternate upon them.

These matters, combined with the pressing necessity, strengthen in the soul that they were looking to non-change, relying upon his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«خلق الماء طهورا لا ينجسه شيء إلا ما غير طعمه أو لونه أو ريحه»} ("Water was created purifying; nothing makes it impure except what changes its taste, color, or odor"). And in this there is a realization (taḥqīq), namely: the nature (ṭabʿ) of every liquid is to convert to its own attribute everything that falls into it, being overcome from its direction. Just as you see a dog falling into a salt-mine, becoming salt, and it is ruled pure by its becoming salt and the removal of the attribute of dogginess from it—likewise vinegar falls into water, and likewise milk falls into it while little, so its attribute is nullified, and it is formed by the form of water and imprinted by its nature—except when it is abundant and predominant, and its predominance is known by the predominance of its taste, color, or odor. This is the criterion (al-miʿyār).

And the Law (al-sharʿ) has indicated this in the case of water strong enough to remove impurity, and it is worthy of reliance. For by it, hardship is repelled, and by it the meaning of its being purifying (ṭahūr) becomes manifest—for it [the impurity] is overcome by it, and it purifies it, just as it became so beyond two qullas, and in the washing-water, and in flowing water, and in the tilting of the vessel for the cat. And do not think this is gratuitous—for if it were so, it would be like the trace of istinjā' and the blood of fleas, such that the water touching it would become impure. Yet it does not become impure by the washing-water, nor by the lapping of a cat in little water.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, {«لا يحمل خبثا»} ("it does not carry impurity"), it is in itself ambiguous (mubham), for it does carry [impurity] when it is changed.

If it is said, "He meant 'when it is not changed,'" then it may be said: He meant that in the usual case, it is not changed by customary impurities. Then it is an appeal to the implied meaning (al-mafhūm) in the case of not reaching two qullas, and abandoning the implied meaning with lesser evidence than what we have mentioned is possible. And his saying, "it does not carry impurity," its apparent sense is the negation of carrying—i.e., it converts it to its own attribute, just as it is said of a salt-mine, "It does not carry a dog or anything else," i.e., it is converted. This is because people used to perform istinjā' in little waters and in pools, and dip impure vessels in them, then they would hesitate whether they had been changed with an effective change or not. So it was clarified that when it is two qullas, it is not changed by these customary impurities.

If you say, "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, 'It does not carry impurity,' and however much [impurity] increases, it carries it"—then this turns against you, for however much it increases, it carries it legally (ḥukman), just as it carries it sensibly (ḥissan). So specification (takhṣīṣ) to customary impurities is unavoidable on both schools alike.

And in sum, my inclination in matters of customary impurities is toward leniency (al-tasāhu), as an understanding of the practice of the early generations (al-awwalīn) and as a cutting off of the material of obsessive scrupulosity (al-waswās). And by this I have issued legal rulings (aftaytu) for purity in what has been disputed in such matters.

chapters.title_en: The Third Branch: On the Manner of Removing Impurity, and the Second Division: On the Purification from Events (Aḥdāth), Including the Chapter on the Etiquette of Relieving Oneself
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| الطرف الثالث في كيفية الإزالة

والنجاسة إن كانت حكمية وهي التي ليس لها جرم محسوس فيكفي إجراء الماء
على جميع مواردها وإن كانت عينية فلا بد من إزالة العين وبقاء الطعم يدل
على بقاء العين وكذا بقاء اللون إلا فيما يلتصق به فهو معفو عنه بعد الحت
والقرص
أما الرائحة فبقاؤها يدل على بقاء العين ولا يعفى عنها إلا إذا كان الشيء
له رائحة فائحة يعسر إزالتها فالدلك والعصر مرات متواليات يقوم مقام الحت
والقرص في اللون والمزيل للوسواس أن يعلم أن الأشياء خلقت طاهرة بيقين فما
لا يشاهد عليه نجاسة ولا يعلمها يقينا يصلي معه ولا ينبغي أن يتوصل
بالاستنباط إلى تقدير النجاسات

### ||| القسم الثاني طهارة الأحداث ومنها الوضوء والغسل والتيمم ويتقدمها الاستنجاء

فلنورد كيفيتها على الترتيب مع آدابها وسننها مبتدئين بسبب الوضوء وآداب
قضاء الحاجة إن شاء الله تعالى

### |||| باب آداب قضاء الحاجة

ينبغي أن يبعد عن أعين الناظرين في الصحراء وأن يستتر بشيء إن وجده وأن
لا يكشف عورته قبل الانتهاء PageV01P130
إلى موضع الجلوس وأن لا يستقبل الشمس والقمر وأن لا يستقبل القبلة ولا
يستدبرها إلا إذا كان في بناء والعدول أيضا عنها في البناء أحب وإن استتر
في الصحراء براحلته جاز وكذلك بذيله وأن يتقي الجلوس في متحدث الناس وأن لا
يبول في الماء الراكد ولا تحت الشجرة المثمرة ولا في الجحر وأن يتقي الموضع
الصلب ومهاب الرياح في البول استنزاها من رشاشه وأن يتكىء في جلوسه على
الرجل اليسرى وإن كان في بنيان يقدم الرجل اليسرى في الدخول واليمنى في
الخروج ولا يبول قائما
قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها من حدثكم  أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يبول
قائما فلا تصدقوه (1) وقال عمر رضي الله عنه رآني رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم وأنا أبول قائما فقال يا عمر لا تبل قائما (2) قال عمر فما بلت قائما
بعد وفيه رخصة إذ روى حذيفة رضي الله عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام بال
قائما فأتيته بوضوء فتوضأ ومسح على خفيه (3) ولا يبول في المغتسل قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم عامة الوسواس منه (4) وقال ابن المبارك قد وسع في البول في
المغتسل إذا جرى الماء عليه ذكره الترمذي وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام لا
يبولن أحدكم في مستحمه ثم يتوضأ فيه فإن عامة الوسواس منه وقال ابن المبارك
إن كان الماء جاريا فلا باس به ولا يستصحب شيئا عليه اسم الله تعالى أو
رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يدخل بيت الماء حاسر الرأس
وأن يقول عند الدخول بسم الله أعوذ بالله من الرجس النجس الخبيث المخبث
الشيطان الرجيم وعند الخروج الحمد لله الذي أذهب عني ما يؤذيني وأبقى علي
ما ينفعني ويكون ذلك خارجا عن بيت الماء وأن يعد النبل قبل الجلوس وأن لا
يستنجي بالماء في موضع الحاجة وأن يستبرىء من البول بالتنحنح والنثر ثلاثا
وإمرار اليد على أسفل القضيب ولا يكثر التفكر في الاستبراء فيتوسوس ويشق
عليه الأمر وما يحس به من بلل فليقدر أنه بقية الماء
فإن كان يؤذيه ذلك فليرش عليه الماء حتى يقوى في نفسه ذلك ولا يتسلط عليه
الشيطان بالوسواس
وفي الخبر أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم فعله أعني رش الماء (5) وقد كان أخفهم
استبراء أفقههم فتدل الوسوسة فيه على قلة الفقه
وفي حديث سلمان رضي الله عنه علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل شيء
حتى الخراءة فأمرنا أن لا نستنجي بعظم ولاروث ونهانا أن نستقبل القبلة
بغائط أو بول (6) وقال رجل لبعض الصحابة من الأعراب وقد خاصمه لا أحسبك
تحسن الخراء قال بلى وأبيك إني لأحسنها وإني بها لحاذق أبعد الأثر وأعد
المدر وأستقبل  الشيح وأستدبر الريح وأقعي إقعاء الظبي وأجفل إجفال النعام
الشيح نبت طيب الرائحة بالبادية والإقعاء ههنا أن يستوفز على صدور قدميه
والإجفال أن يرفع عجزه
ومن الرخصة أن يبول الإنسان قريبا من صاحبه مستترا عنه (7) فعل ذلك رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع شدة حيائه ليبين للناس ذلك PageV01P131
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ل (Z-W-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of removal, cessation, and departure of a thing from its place or state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, the elimination of a juridical impediment (ḥukmī) or physical substance (ʿaynī) that prevents the validity of prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical removal by scraping (ḥatt) and rubbing (qarṣ); metaphorical (majāz) for the flow of water as a symbolic purifier in non-corporeal cases.
- Root: ن-ج-س (N-J-S)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Filth, uncleanness, and that which is repugnant to sound nature.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A juridical category distinguishing ḥukmī (non-corporeal, e.g., the state of minor ritual impurity) from ʿaynī (corporeal, e.g., blood or urine).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tangible filth; metaphorical for the legal construct of impurity that water alone can efface.
- Root: و-س-و-س (W-S-W-S)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The faint, subtle whisper or suggestion that incites anxiety and doubt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The insinuation of Satan (waswās) that leads to obsessive scrupulosity (wasaṣ) in ritual practice, contrary to the certainty (yaqīn) of original purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the whisper; metaphorical for the psychological state of exaggerated doubt that the Law aims to repel.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if it is ḥukmī... then water suffices") and exceptions (e.g., "except for what adheres... it is pardoned") to delineate precise legal boundaries, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that impurity (najāsah), if it is juridical (ḥukmī)—that is, that which has no perceptible corporeal substance—then the flowing of water over all its loci is sufficient. But if it is corporeal (ʿaynī), then the removal of the very substance is obligatory. The persistence of taste indicates the persistence of the substance, and likewise the persistence of color, except for what adheres [to the garment] with difficulty—for that is pardoned after scraping (ḥatt) and rubbing (qarṣ). As for odor, its persistence indicates the persistence of the substance, and it is not pardoned unless the thing has a penetrating smell whose removal is difficult; then repeated rubbing and wringing, in successive rounds, stands in the place of scraping and rubbing for color. What removes obsessive scrupulosity (waswās) is the knowledge that things were created pure with certainty (yaqīn); thus, whatever one does not observe to bear impurity, nor know it with certainty, one may pray with it. One ought not to resort to speculative inference (istinbāṭ) to estimate [the presence of] impurities.

Then, the second division: the purification from events (ṭahārat al-aḥdāth), which includes ablution (wuḍūʾ), full washing (ghusl), and dry ablution (tayammum), preceded by the cleansing after relieving oneself (istinjāʾ). Let us present their modalities in order, along with their etiquettes and established practices (sunan), beginning with the cause of ablution and the etiquettes of answering the call of nature, if God Most High wills.

### Chapter: On the Etiquette of Answering the Call of Nature

One ought to distance oneself from the eyes of onlookers in the open desert, and to screen oneself with something if one finds it. One should not uncover one’s private parts before reaching the place of sitting. One should not face the sun or the moon, nor face the qiblah or turn one’s back to it—except if one is within a building; yet even in a building, turning away from it is more beloved. If one screens oneself in the desert with one’s riding beast, that is permissible, and likewise with the hem of one’s garment. One should avoid sitting in the frequented paths of people, and should not urinate in stagnant water, nor beneath a fruit-bearing tree, nor into a burrow. One should avoid a hard ground and the direction from which the wind blows, when urinating, as a precaution against its splash. One should lean, while sitting, upon the left leg. If one is in a building, one should put forward the left foot upon entering and the right foot upon exiting, and one should not urinate standing.

ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: “Whoever tells you that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, urinated standing, do not believe him.” And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, saw me urinating standing and said: ‘O ʿUmar, do not urinate standing.’” ʿUmar said: “So I never urinated standing after that.” Yet there is a concession (rukhaṣ) in it, for Ḥudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, urinated standing, and I brought him water for ablution, and he performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks (khuffayn). And one should not urinate in the bathing place (al-mughtasal). He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Most obsessive scrupulosity (waswās) comes from it.” Ibn al-Mubārak said: “It has been made wide in scope to urinate in the bathing place if water flows over it.” Al-Tirmidhī mentioned this. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Let none of you urinate in his bathing place, then perform ablution in it, for most obsessive scrupulosity comes from it.” Ibn al-Mubārak said: “If the water is flowing, there is no harm in it.” One should not carry with one anything upon which the name of God Most High or His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is inscribed, nor enter the place of water (bayt al-māʾ) with an uncovered head.

One should say upon entering: “In the name of God; I seek refuge in God from the filthy, the impure, the wicked, the corrupting, the accursed Satan.” And upon exiting: “Praise be to God who has removed from me what harms me and preserved for me what benefits me”—and this should be said outside the place of water. One should count the stones (al-nabl) before sitting, and should not cleanse oneself with water (istinjāʾ) in the very place of need. One should seek to be free of urine (istibrāʾ) by clearing the throat and sniffing three times, and by passing the hand along the underside of the penis. One should not dwell excessively in thought over istibrāʾ, lest one fall into obsessive scrupulosity (waswās) and the matter become burdensome upon him. Whatever moisture he perceives, let him deem it to be the remnant of water. If that harms him, let him sprinkle water upon it, so that this conviction is strengthened in his soul, and Satan does not overpower him through waswās. It is reported in the tradition that he, peace and blessings be upon him, did this—I mean, the sprinkling of water. And the one among them with the lightest istibrāʾ was the most learned in jurisprudence (afqahuhum); thus, obsessive scrupulosity in it indicates a deficiency of fiqh.

In the ḥadīth of Salmān, may God be pleased with him: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, taught us everything, even the manner of relieving oneself. He commanded us not to cleanse ourselves with bone or dung, and forbade us from facing the qiblah with excrement or urine.” And a man said to one of the desert Arabs (al-aʿrāb) who had disputed with him: “I do not think you know how to relieve yourself well.” He replied: “Yes, by your father, I do know it well, and I am skilled in it: I distance the trace, I count the clods, I face the wormwood (al-shīḥ), I turn my back to the wind, I squat like the squatting of the gazelle, and I leap like the leaping of the ostrich.” Al-shīḥ is a sweet-smelling plant of the desert; al-iqʿāʾ here means to rise up on the balls of one’s feet; al-ijfāl means to raise one’s buttocks.

And among the concessions is that a man may urinate near his companion while screened from him. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did this, despite his intense modesty, to make it permissible for the people.

chapters.title_en: The Manner of Istinjā' (Cleansing After Relieving Oneself)
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| كيفية الاستنجاء

ثم يستنجي لمقعدته بثلاثة أحجار فإن أنقى وإلا استعمل رابعا فإن أنقى
وإلا استعمل خامسا لأن الإنقاء واجب والإيتار مستحب
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من استجمر فليوتر (1) ويأخذ الحجر بيساره ويضعه
على مقدم المقعدة قبل موضع النجاسة ويمره بالمسح والإدارة إلى المؤخر ويأخذ
الثاني ويضعه على المؤخر كذلك ويمره إلى المقدمة ويأخذ الثالث فيديره حول
المسربة إدارة فإن عسرت الإدارة ومسح من المقدمة إلى المؤخرة أجزأه ثم يأخذ
حجرا كبيرا بيمينه والقضيب بيساره ويمسح الحجر بقضيبه ويحرك اليسار فيمسح
ثلاثا في ثلاثة مواضع أوفى ثلاثة أحجار أو في ثلاثة مواضع من جدار إلى أن
لا يرى الرطوبة في محل المسح فإن حصل ذلك بمرتين أتى بالثالثة ووجب ذلك إن
أراد الاقتصار على الحجر وإن حصل بالرابعة استحب الخامسة للإيتار
ثم ينتقل من ذلك الموضع إلى موضع آخر ويستنجي بالماء بأن يفيضه باليمنى
على محل النجو ويدلك باليسرى حتى لا يبقى أثر يدركه الكف بحس اللمس ويدرك
الاستقصاء فيه بالتعرض للباطن فإن ذلك منبع الوسواس وليعلم أن كل ما لا يصل
إليه الماء فهو باطن ولا يثبت حكم النجاسة للفضلات الباطنة ما لم تظهر وكل
ما هو ظاهر وثبت له حكم النجاسة فحد ظهوره أن يصل الماء إليه فيزيله ولا
معنى للوسواس
ويقول عند الفراغ من الاستنجاء اللهم طهر قلبي من النفاق وحصن فرجي من
الفواحش ويدلك يده بحائط أو بالأرض إزالة للرائحة إن بقيت
والجمع بين الماء والحجر مستحب فقد روي أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى {فيه رجال
يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
لأهل قباء ما هذه الطهارة التي أثنى  الله بها عليكم قالوا كنا نجمع بين
الماء والحجر (2)

### |||| كيفية الوضوء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ق-ي (n-q-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, cleanliness, removal of filth; "anqā" means to cleanse thoroughly until no trace remains.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purity (ṭahārah) as a prerequisite for prayer; "inqā'" denotes complete removal of impurity (najāsah) from the locus of excretion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical cleansing; metaphorical (majāz) — purification of the heart from hypocrisy (nifāq), as in the supplication cited.
- Root: و-ت-ر (w-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Odd number; "ītār" is making something odd (witr), as opposed to even (shafʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Commended (mustaḥabb) act of using an odd count of stones, following the Prophet's command; linked to divine love of odd numbers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — odd numerical count; metaphorical — perfection of an act through odd completion, as in prayer (witr).
- Root: س-ر-ب (s-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The channel or passage; "masrabah" refers to the anal canal or the inner recess of the posterior.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The internal cavity where impurity may linger; its "bāṭin" (inner part) is exempt from the ruling of najāsah until it emerges.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — anatomical passage; metaphorical — the hidden realm (bāṭin) versus the apparent (ẓāhir), a key distinction in jurisprudential rulings.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — "fa-in anqā wa-illā..." (if it cleanses, then...; otherwise...). The particle "fa" links the apodosis to the protasis, indicating sequential obligation; "illā" (else) introduces an alternative condition, parsed as "fa-in lam yunqi" (if it does not cleanse). This governs the escalating use of stones (third, fourth, fifth) based on the outcome.
chapters.translation:
Then he performs istinjā' (cleansing) for his posterior with three stones. If they cleanse thoroughly (anqā), then that suffices; otherwise, he uses a fourth. If it cleanses, then fine; otherwise, he uses a fifth — because thorough cleansing (inqā') is obligatory (wājib), while using an odd number (ītār) is commendable (mustaḥabb). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: {«من استجمر فليوتر»} — "Whoever uses stones for cleansing, let him use an odd number."

He takes the stone in his left hand and places it on the front part of the posterior, before the locus of impurity, and passes it with wiping and rotation toward the rear. He takes the second stone and places it on the rear similarly, passing it toward the front. He takes the third and rotates it around the anal passage (masrabah) in a circular motion. If rotation is difficult, wiping from front to rear suffices. Then he takes a large stone in his right hand and the penis in his left, wiping the stone over his penis and moving the left hand — wiping three times in three places, or with three stones, or in three spots on a wall — until no moisture is seen at the locus of wiping. If this is achieved with two wipes, he performs the third, and this is obligatory if he intends to limit himself to stones. If it is achieved with the fourth, he commends the fifth for the sake of oddness (ītār).

Then he moves from that place to another and performs istinjā' with water: he pours it with his right hand over the locus of excretion and rubs with his left until no trace remains that the palm can perceive by the sense of touch. He should not seek thoroughness by probing the inner part (bāṭin), for that is the source of obsessive doubt (waswās). Let him know that whatever water does not reach is "inner" (bāṭin), and the ruling of impurity (najāsah) does not apply to internal residues as long as they have not emerged. Whatever is apparent (ẓāhir) and subject to the ruling of impurity — the limit of its appearing is that water reaches it and removes it. There is no meaning to obsessive doubt (waswās).

Upon completing the istinjā', he says: "O Allah, purify my heart from hypocrisy (nifāq) and guard my private parts from lewd acts (fawāḥish)." Then he rubs his hand against a wall or the ground to remove any lingering odor.

Combining water and stones is commendable (mustaḥabb). It has been narrated that when the verse was revealed — {«فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين»} — "In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves" — the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to the people of Qubā': "What is this purification for which Allah has praised you?" They said: "We combine water with stones."

chapters.title_en: On the Etiquette of Ablution (Ādāb al-Wuḍūʾ) and Its Inner Significance
chapters.arabic_text:
إذا فرغ من الاستنجاء اشتغل بالوضوء فلم ير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
قط خارجا من الغائط إلا توضأ ويبتدىء بالسواك فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن أفواهكم طرق القرآن فطيبوها بالسواك (3) فينبغي أن ينوي عند
السواك تطهير فمه لقراءة القرآن وذكر الله تعالى في الصلاة وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم صلاة على أثر سواك أفضل من خمس وسبعين صلاة بغير سواك {حديث}
صلاة على أثر سواك أفضل من خمس وسبعين صلاة بغير سواك رواه أبو نعيم في
كتاب السواك من حديث ابن عمر بإسناد ضعيف ورواه أبو داود والحاكم وصححه
والبيهقي وضعفه من حديث عائشة وضعفه بلفظ من سبعين صلاة (4) حديث لولا أن
أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم بالسواك عند كل صلاة متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة (5)
حديث ما لي أراكم تدخلون علي قلحا استاكوا أخرجه البزار والبيهقي من حديث
العباس بن عبد المطلب وأبو داود والبغوي من حديث تمام بن العباس والبيهقي
من حديث عبد الله بن عباس وهو مضطرب (6) حديث كان يستاك من الليل مرارا
أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن عباس (7) حديث ابن عباس لم يزل يأمرنا رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم بالسواك حتى ظننا أنه سينزل عليه فيه شيء رواه أحمد //
وقال عليه السلام عليكم بالسواك فإنه PageV01P132
مطهرة للفم ومرضاة للرب (1) وقال علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه السواك
يزيد في الحفظ ويذهب البلغم (2) وكان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
يروحون والسواك على آذانهم
وكيفيته أن يستاك بخشب الأراك أو غيره من قضبان الأشجار مما يخشن ويزيل
القلح ويستاك عرضا وطولا وإن اقتصر فعرضا
ويستحب السواك عند كل صلاة وعند كل وضوء وإن لم يصل عقيبه وعند تغير
النكهة بالنوم أو طول الأزم أو كل ما تكره رائحته ثم عند الفراغ من السواك
يجلس للوضوء مستقبل القبلة ويقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال صلى الله عليه
وسلم لا  وضوء لمن لم يسم الله تعالى (3) أي لا وضوء كامل
ويقول عند ذلك أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون ثم يغسل
يديه ثلاثا قبل أن يدخلهما الإناء ويقول اللهم إني أسألك اليمن والبركة
وأعوذ بك من الشؤم والهلكة ثم ينوي رفع الحدث أو استباحة الصلاة ويستديم
النية إلى غسل الوجه فإن نسيها عند الوجه لم يجزه ثم يأخذ غرفة لفيه بيمينه
فيتمضمض بها ثلاثا ويغرغر بأن يرد الماء إلى الغلصمة إلا أن يكون صائما
فيرفق ويقول اللهم أعني على تلاوة كتابك وكثرة الذكر لك ثم يأخذ غرفة لأنفه
ويستنشق ثلاثا ويصعد الماء بالنفس إلى خياشيمه ويستنثر ما فيها ويقول في
الاستنشاق اللهم أوجد لي رائحة الجنة وأنت عني راض وفي الاستنثار اللهم إني
أعوذ بك من روائح النار ومن سوء الدار لأن الاستنشاق إيصال والاستنثار
إزالة ثم يغرف غرفة لوجهه فيغسله من مبدإ سطح الجبهة إلى منتهى ما يقبل من
الذقن في الطول ومن الأذن إلى الأذن في العرض ولا يدخل في حد الوجه
النزعتان اللتان على طرفي الجبينين فهما من الرأس ويوصل الماء إلى موضع
التحذيف وهو ما يعتاد النساء تنحية الشعر عنه وهو القدر الذي يقع في جانب
الوجه مهما وضع طرف الخيط على رأس الأذن والطرف الثاني على زاوية الجبين
ويوصل الماء إلى منابت الشعور الأربعة الحاجبان والشاربان والعذاران
والأهداب لأنها خفيفة في الغالب
والعذاران هما ما يوازيان الأذنين من مبدإ اللحية
ويجب إيصال الماء إلى منابت اللحية الخفيفة أعني ما يقبل من الوجه وأما
الكثيفة فلا وحكم العنفقة حكم اللحية في الكثافة والخفة ثم يفعل ذلك ثلاثا
ويفيض الماء على ظاهر ما استرسل من اللحية ويدخل الأصابع في محاجر العينين
وموضع الرمص ومجتمع الكحل وينقيهما
فقد روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل ذلك (4) ويأمل عند ذلك خروج الخطايا
من عينيه وكذلك عند كل عضو ويقول عنده اللهم بيض وجهي بنورك يوم تبيض وجوه
أوليائك ولا تسود وجهي بظلماتك يوم تسود وجوه  أعدائك ويخلل اللحية الكثيفة
عند غسل الوجه فإنه مستحب ثم يغسل يديه إلى مرفقيه ثلاثا ويحرك الخاتم
ويطيل الغرة ويرفع الماء إلى أعلى العضد فإنهم يحشرون يوم القيامة غرا
محجلين من آثار الوضوء كذلك ورد الخبر
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من استطاع أن PageV01P133
يطيل غرته فليفعل (1) وروي أن الحلية تبلغ مواضع الوضوء (2) ويبدأ
باليمنى ويقول اللهم أعطني كتابي بيميني وحاسبني حسابا يسيرا ويقول عند غسل
الشمال اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن تعطيني كتابي بشمالي أو من وراء ظهري ثم
يستوعب رأسه بالمسح بأن يبل يديه ويلصق رءوس أصابع يديه اليمنى باليسرى
ويضعهما على مقدمة الرأس ويمدهما إلى القفا ثم يردهما إلى المقدمة وهذه
مسحة واحدة يفعل ذلك ثلاثا ويقول اللهم اغشني برحمتك وأنزل علي من بركاتك
وأظلني تحت ظل عرشك يوم لا ظل إلا ظلك ثم يمسح أذنيه ظاهرهما وباطنهما بماء
جديد بأن يدخل مسبحتيه في صماخي أذنيه ويدير إبهاميه على ظاهر أذنيه ثم يضع
الكف على الأذنين استظهارا ويكرره ثلاثا ويقول اللهم اجعلني من الذين
يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه اللهم اسمعني منادي الجنة مع الأبرار ثم يمسح
رقبته بماء جديد لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم مسح الرقبة أمان من الغل يوم
القيامة (3) ويقول اللهم فك رقبتي من النار وأعوذ بك من السلاسل والأغلال
ثم يغسل رجله اليمنى ثلاثا ويخلل باليد اليسرى من أسفل أصابع الرجل اليمنى
ويبدأ بالخنصر من الرجل اليمنى ويختم بالخنصر من الرجل اليسرى ويقول اللهم
ثبت قدمي على الصراط المستقيم يوم تزل الأقدام في النار ويقول عند غسل
اليسرى أعوذ بك أن تزل قدمي عن الصراط يوم تزل فيه أقدام المنافقين ويرفع
الماء إلى أنصاف الساقين
فإذا فرغ رفع رأسه إلى السماء وقال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك
له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت
سوءا وظلمت نفسي أستغفرك اللهم وأتوب إليك فاغفر لي وتب على إنك أنت التواب
الرحيم اللهم اجعلني من التوابين  واجعلني من المتطهرين واجعلني من عبادك
الصالحين واجعلني عبدا صبورا شكورا واجعلني أذكرك كثيرا وأسبحك بكرة وأصيلا
يقال إن من قال هذا بعد الوضوء ختم على وضوئه بخاتم ورفع له تحت العرش فلم
يزل يسبح الله تعالى ويقدسه ويكتب له ثواب ذلك إلى يوم القيامة
ويكره في الوضوء أمور منها أن يزيد على الثلاث فمن زاد فقد ظلم وأن يسرف
في الماء توضأ عليه السلام ثلاثا وقال من زاد فقد ظلم وأساء (4) وقال سيكون
قوم من هذه الأمة يعتدون في الدعاء والطهور (5) ويقال من وهن علم الرجل
ولوعه بالماء في الطهور (6) وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم يقال إن أول ما يبتدىء
الوسواس من قبل الطهور وقال الحسن إن شيطانا يضحك بالناس في الوضوء يقال له
الولهان
ويكره أن ينفض اليد فيرش الماء وأن يتكلم في أثناء الوضوء وأن يلطم وجهه
بالماءلطما
وكره قوم التنشيف وقالوا الوضوء يوزن قاله سعيد بن المسيب والزهري لكن
روى معاذ رضي الله عنه أنه عليه السلام مسح وجهه بطرف ثوبه (7) وروت عائشة
رضي الله عنها أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت له منشفة (8) ولكن طعن في هذه
الرواية عن عائشة
ويكره أن يتوضأ من إناء صفر وأن يتوضأ بالماء المشمس وذلك من جهة الطب
وقد روي عن ابن عمر وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما كراهية إناء الصفر وقال
بعضهم أخرجت لشعبة ماء في إناء صفر فأبى أن يتوضأ منه
ونقل كراهية PageV01P134
ذلك عن ابن عمر وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما
ومهما فرغ من وضوئه وأقبل على الصلاة فينبغي أن يخطر بباله أنه طهر ظاهره
وهو موضع نظر الخلق أن يستحي من مناجاة الله تعالى من غير تطهير قلبه وهو
موضع نظر الرب سبحانه
وليحقق طهارة القلب بالتوبة
والخلو عن الأخلاق المذمومة والتخلق بالأخلاق الحميدة أولى
وأن من يقتصر على طهارة الظاهر كمن يدعو ملكا إلى بيته فتركه مشحونا
بالقاذورات واشتغل بتجصيص ظاهر الباب البراني من الدار
وما أجدر مثل هذا الرجل بالتعرض للمقت والبوار والله سبحانه  وتعالى أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, cleanliness, freedom from filth — both physical (naǧāsa) and ritual (ḥadath)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭahārah as the removal of both sensory impurities and spiritual defilement; the outward ablution mirrors inward purification of the heart (tazkiyah)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for washing with water; metaphorical extension to purification of the soul from sins — the outward act is a sign (ʿalāmah) of the inward reality
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (al-šarṭ wa-l-ǧawāb al-maḥḏūf) — "If one completes..." (idā faragha...) governs a sequence of habitual actions expressed in the imperfect tense, indicating recurring practice (istiḥbāb)
chapters.translation:
I say: When one has finished cleansing himself after relieving nature, he occupies himself with the ablution (wuḍūʾ). The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never seen coming out from the privy except that he performed ablution. He begins with the tooth-stick (siwāk), for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«إن أفواهكم طرق القرآن فطيبوها بالسواك»} "Your mouths are the pathways of the Qurʾān, so perfume them with the siwāk." It is fitting that one intend at the siwāk the purification of his mouth for the recitation of the Qurʾān and the remembrance of Allah the Exalted in prayer. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«صلاة على أثر سواك أفضل من خمس وسبعين صلاة بغير سواك»} "A prayer following a siwāk is better than seventy-five prayers without a siwāk." [This hadith was narrated by Abū Nuʿaym in his book on the siwāk from Ibn ʿUmar with a weak chain; Abū Dāwūd and al-Ḥākim narrated it and declared it sound (ṣaḥīḥ); al-Bayhaqī declared it weak from ʿĀʾishah with the wording "seventy prayers."] [Another hadith:] {«لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم بالسواك عند كل صلاة»} "Were it not that I would burden my community, I would have commanded them to use the siwāk at every prayer" — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh) from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah. [Another:] {«ما لي أراكم تدخلون علي قلحا استاكوا»} "Why do I see you entering upon me with yellowed teeth? Use the siwāk!" — narrated by al-Bazzār and al-Bayhaqī from the hadith of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and by Abū Dāwūd and al-Baghawī from the hadith of Tammām ibn al-ʿAbbās, and al-Bayhaqī from the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās — though its chain is disordered (muḍṭarib). [Another:] {«كان يستاك من الليل مرارا»} "He used to use the siwāk multiple times during the night" — narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās. [Another:] Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never ceased commanding us to use the siwāk until we thought that something was about to be revealed to him concerning it" — narrated by Aḥmad. And he, peace be upon him, said: {«عليكم بالسواك فإنه مطهرة للفم ومرضاة للرب»} "Upon you is the siwāk, for it purifies the mouth and pleases the Lord." ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah honor his face, said: "The siwāk increases memory and removes phlegm." The companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go to the evening prayer with the siwāk placed upon their ears.

Its manner is that one uses a stick of the arāk tree or other tree branches that are rough and remove the yellow film (qalaḥ). One rubs crosswise and lengthwise; if he limits himself, then crosswise suffices.

The siwāk is recommended at every prayer, at every ablution even if no prayer follows it, and upon change of breath due to sleep, prolonged silence, or anything whose odor is disliked. Then, upon completing the siwāk, he sits for the ablution facing the qiblah and says: "In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate" (bismillāh al-raḥmān al-raḥīm). The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«لا وضوء لمن لم يسم الله تعالى»} "There is no ablution for one who does not mention the name of Allah the Exalted" — that is, no complete ablution.

At that moment he says: "I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, O Lord, lest they attend me" (aʿūdhu bika min hamazāti al-shayāṭīn wa-aʿūdhu bika rabbi an yaḥḍurūn). Then he washes his hands three times before inserting them into the vessel, saying: "O Allah, I ask You for blessedness (yumn) and blessing (barakah), and I seek refuge in You from ill-omen (shuʾm) and destruction (halakah)." Then he intends the lifting of ritual impurity (rafʿ al-ḥadath) or the rendering permissible of prayer (istibāḥat al-ṣalāh), and he maintains this intention continuously until the washing of the face; if he forgets it at the face, it does not suffice him.

Then he takes a handful of water for his mouth with his right hand and rinses it (madmaḍah) three times, gargling (ghargarah) by returning the water to the glottis (ghalṣamah) — unless he is fasting, in which case he is gentle. He says: "O Allah, help me to recite Your Book and to remember You abundantly." Then he takes a handful for his nose and snuffs water (istinshāq) three times, drawing the water up by breath into his nostrils, and he expels what is within them (istinthār). He says during the snuffing: "O Allah, cause me to perceive the fragrance of Paradise while You are pleased with me," and during the expulsion: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the odors of the Fire and from the evil abode" — for the snuffing is a drawing in (īṣāl) and the expulsion is a removal (izālah).

Then he takes a handful for his face and washes it from the beginning of the surface of the forehead to the lowest part of what is included of the chin in length, and from ear to ear in width. The two temples (nazʿatān) at the two sides of the forehead do not enter into the limit of the face, for they belong to the head. He conveys water to the place of the forelock (tahḏīf) — which is what women habitually push the hair away from — being the portion that falls on the side of the face when one end of a thread is placed at the top of the ear and the other end at the corner of the forehead. He conveys water to the four growths of hair: the two eyebrows, the two moustaches, the two sideburns (ʿadhārān), and the eyelashes, for they are generally thin.

The two sideburns (ʿadhārān) are what run parallel to the ears from the beginning of the beard. It is obligatory to convey water to the roots of a thin beard — that is, what is included within the face — but as for a thick beard, no. The rule for the chin tuft (ʿanfaqah) follows that of the beard in thickness and thinness. Then he does this three times, pouring water over the exterior of what hangs down of the beard, inserting his fingers into the eye sockets (maḥājir al-ʿaynayn), the place of rheum (ramaṣ), and the gathering of kohl, and cleaning them — for it has been narrated that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did this. At that moment he hopes for the exit of sins from his eyes, and likewise at every limb. He says at that: "O Allah, whiten my face with Your light on the day when the faces of Your friends are whitened, and do not blacken my face with Your darknesses on the day when the faces of Your enemies are blackened." He also runs his fingers through a thick beard (takhlīl) during the washing of the face, for that is recommended.

Then he washes his hands up to the elbows three times, moving the ring, lengthening the blaze (ghurrah), and raising the water to the upper part of the upper arm — for they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with white blazes and white fetlocks (ghurr muḥajjalīn) from the traces of ablution; thus has the report come. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«من استطاع أن يطيل غرته فليفعل»} "Whoever can lengthen his blaze, let him do so." And it is narrated that the adornment (ḥilyah) reaches the places of ablution. He begins with the right hand, saying: "O Allah, give me my book in my right hand, and reckon with me an easy reckoning." And he says at the washing of the left: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from giving me my book in my left hand or from behind my back."

Then he wipes his entire head (masḥ) by wetting his hands, pressing the fingertips of his right hand against his left, placing them at the front of the head, drawing them to the nape (qafā), then returning them to the front — this being a single wipe. He does this three times, saying: "O Allah, cover me with Your mercy, send down upon me from Your blessings, and shade me under the shade of Your Throne on the day when there is no shade but Your shade." Then he wipes his ears, their exteriors and interiors, with fresh water, inserting his index fingers into the orifices of his ears and rotating his thumbs over the exteriors of his ears; then he places his palms over the ears as a precaution, repeating this three times, saying: "O Allah, make me among those who listen to the word and follow the best of it. O Allah, make me hear the caller of Paradise with the righteous." Then he wipes his neck with fresh water, due to his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«مسح الرقبة أمان من الغل يوم القيامة»} "Wiping the neck is security from fetters on the Day of Resurrection." He says: "O Allah, free my neck from the Fire, and I seek refuge in You from chains and yokes."

Then he washes his right foot three times, running his fingers with his left hand from beneath the toes of the right foot, beginning with the little toe of the right foot and ending with the little toe of the left foot. He says: "O Allah, make firm my foot upon the Straight Path on the day when feet slip in the Fire." And he says at the washing of the left: "I seek refuge in You from my foot slipping from the Path on the day when the feet of the hypocrites slip therein." He raises the water to the middle of the shanks.

When he finishes, he raises his head to the sky and says: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; there is no god but You. I have done evil and wronged myself; I seek Your forgiveness, O Allah, and I repent to You. So forgive me and accept my repentance, for You are the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful. O Allah, make me among the repentant, make me among the purified, make me among Your righteous servants, make me a patient and thankful servant, make me remember You abundantly and glorify You morning and evening." It is said that whoever says this after ablution has his ablution sealed with a seal, and it is raised for him beneath the Throne, and it continues to glorify Allah the Exalted and declare His holiness, and its reward is written for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Disliked matters in ablution include: exceeding three washes — for whoever exceeds has wronged; and extravagance in water. He, peace be upon him, performed ablution with three washes and said: {«من زاد فقد ظلم وأساء»} "Whoever exceeds has wronged and done ill." And he said: {«سيكون قوم من هذه الأمة يعتدون في الدعاء والطهور»} "There will be people from this community who transgress in supplication and in purification." And it is said: "From the weakness of a man's religion is his obsession with water in purification." Ibrāhīm ibn Adham said: "It is said that obsessive whispering (waswās) first begins from purification." And al-Ḥasan said: "There is a devil who laughs at people during ablution, called al-Walahān."

It is disliked to flick the hand and spray water, to speak during the ablution, and to slap the face with water. Some people disliked drying oneself, saying "the ablution is weighed" — this was said by Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhrī. However, Muʿādh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace be upon him, wiped his face with the edge of his garment; and ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, narrated that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had a towel — though this narration from ʿĀʾishah has been criticized.

It is disliked to perform ablution from a brass vessel (ināʾ ṣufr) and to perform ablution with sun-heated water (māʾ mushammas) — this from the standpoint of medicine. It has been narrated from Ibn ʿUmar and Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, the dislike of the brass vessel; and some said: "I brought water for Shuʿbah in a brass vessel, and he refused to perform ablution with it." The dislike of that has been transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar and Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Whenever one completes his ablution and turns to prayer, he should call to mind that he has purified his exterior — which is the place of the creatures' gaze — so that he may feel shame before Allah in intimate supplication (munājāh) without purifying his heart — which is the place of the Lord's, glory be to Him, gaze. Let him realize the purification of the heart through repentance (tawbah), and freedom from blameworthy traits, and the adornment with praiseworthy character — this being more fitting. And one who limits himself to the purification of the exterior is like one who invites a king to his house, then leaves it filled with filth while occupying himself with plastering the outer face of the door of the dwelling. How deserving is such a man of exposure to wrath and ruin! And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of Ablution (Faḍīlat al-Wuḍūʾ) and the Manner of Ritual Bathing (Kayfiyyat al-Ghusl)
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| فضيلة الوضوء

قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من توضأ فأحسن الوضوء وصلى ركعتين لم
يحدث نفسه فيهما بشيء من الدنيا خرج من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه (1) وفي لفظ
آخر ولم يسه فيهما غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا
ألا أنبئكم بما يكفر الله به الخطايا ويرفع به الدرجات إسباغ الوضوء على
المكاره ونقل الأقدام إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط
ثلاث مرات (2) وتوضأ صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة مرة وقال هذا وضوء لا يقبل
الله الصلاة إلا به وتوضأ مرتين مرتين وقال من توضأ مرتين مرتين أتاه الله
أجره مرتين وتوضأ ثلاثا ثلاثا وقال هذا وضوئي ووضوء الأنبياء من قبلي ووضوء
خليل الرحمن إبراهيم عليه السلام (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من ذكر الله
عند وضوئه طهر الله جسده كله ومن لم يذكر الله لم يطهر منه إلا ما أصاب
الماء (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من توضأ على طهر كتب الله له به عشر
حسنات (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الوضوء على الوضوء نور على نور (6) وهذا
كله حث على تجديد الوضوء وقال عليه السلام إذا توضأ العبد المسلم فتمضمض
خرجت الخطايا من فيه فإذا استنثر خرجت الخطايا من أنفه فإذا غسل وجهه خرجت
الخطايا من وجهه حتى تخرج من تحت أشفار عينيه فإذا غسل يديه خرجت الخطايا
من يديه حتى تخرج من تحت أظفاره فإذا مسح برأسه خرجت الخطايا من رأسه حتى
تخرج من تحت أذنيه وإذا غسل رجليه خرجت الخطايا من رجليه حتى تخرج من تحت
أظفار رجليه ثم كان مشيه إلى المسجد وصلاته نافلة له (7) ويروى إن الطاهر
كالصائم (8) قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من توضأ فأحسن الوضوء ثم رفع طرفه إلى
السماء فقال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده
ورسوله فتحت له أبواب الجنة الثمانية يدخل من أيها شاء (9) وقال عمر رضي
الله عنه PageV01P135
إن  الوضوء الصالح يطرد عنك الشيطان
وقال مجاهد من استطاع أن لا يبيت إلا طاهرا ذاكرا مستغفرا فليفعل فإن
الأرواح تبعث على ما قبضت عليه

### |||| كيفية الغسل

وهو أن يضع الإناء عن يمينه ثم يسمي الله تعالى ويغسل يديه ثلاثا ثم
يستنجي كما وصفت لك ويزيل ما على بدنه من نجاسة إن كانت ثم يتوضأ وضوءه
للصلاة كما وصفنا إلا غسل القدمين فإنه يؤخرهما فإن غسلهما ثم وضعهما على
الأرض كان إضاعة للماء ثم يصب الماء على رأسه ثلاثا ثم على شقه الأيمن
ثلاثا ثم على شقه الأيسر ثلاثا ثم يدلك ما أقبل من بدنه ويخلل شعر الرأس
واللحية ويوصل الماء إلى منابت ما كثف منه أو خف وليس على المرأة نقض
الضفائر إلا إذا علمت أن الماء لا يصل إلى خلال الشعر ويتعهد معاطف البدن
وليتق أن يمس ذكره في أثناء ذلك فإن فعل ذلك فليعد الوضوء وإن توضأ قبل
الغسل فلا يعيده بعد الغسل
فهذه سنن الوضوء والغسل ذكرنا منها ما لا بد لسالك طريق الآخرة من علمه
وعمله وما عداه من المسائل التي يحتاج إليها في عوارض الأحوال فليرجع فيها
إلى كتب الفقه
والواجب من جملة ما ذكرناه في الغسل أمران النية واستيعاب البدن بالغسل
وفروض الوضوء النية وغسل الوجه وغسل اليدين إلى المرفقين ومسح ما ينطلق
عليه الاسم من الرأس وغسل الرجلين إلى الكعبين والترتيب
وأما الموالاة فليست بواجبة
والغسل الواجب بأربعة بخروج المني والتقاء الختانين والحيض والنفاس وما
عداه من الأغسال سنة كغسل العيدين والجمعة والأعياد والإحرام والوقوف بعرفة
ومزدلفة ولدخول مكة وثلاثة أغسال أيام التشريق ولطواف الوداع على قول
والكافر إذا أسلم غير جنب والمجنون إذا أفاق ولمن غسل ميتا فكل ذلك مستحب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ض-أ (w-ḍ-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cleanliness and brightness; the act of washing specific bodily parts for purification; derived from waḍuʾa (to be pure, radiant).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ṭahārah) as a prerequisite for prayer—a physical symbol of inner spiritual cleansing from sins.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) washing of limbs; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "light upon light" (nūr ʿalā nūr) signifying cumulative spiritual elevation.
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing or bathing the entire body; removal of filth (najāsah) by water.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Full-body purification (ghusl) for major ritual impurity (janābah)—a comprehensive cleansing paralleling total spiritual renewal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal immersion/flow of water over the whole body; metaphorical completeness of devotion.
- Root: خ-ط-أ (kh-ṭ-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Error, sin, transgression; the act of missing the mark.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sins (khaṭāyā) as impurities expelled through ablution—moral defilement washed away by ritual purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal falling away of sins; metaphorical "exit from under the eyelids and nails" as a vivid image of thorough forgiveness.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "whoever performs ablution") governs the apodosis (e.g., "his sins depart"), with the conditional particle "man" requiring a verb in the past tense for both, as in the prophetic traditions cited.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the virtue of ablution (wuḍūʾ) is established by numerous authentic reports. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever performs ablution and perfects it, then prays two rakʿahs without letting his heart wander to anything of this world, emerges from his sins as on the day his mother bore him." In another wording: "And does not err in them, his past sins are forgiven." He, peace be upon him, also said: "Shall I not inform you of that by which Allah erases sins and raises degrees? Perfecting ablution despite hardships, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer—that is the ribāṭ (garrisoning the frontier)." He repeated this three times. He, peace be upon him, performed ablution once for each part and said: "This is an ablution without which Allah does not accept prayer." He performed it twice for each part and said: "Whoever performs ablution twice for each part, Allah gives him his reward twice." He performed it three times for each part and said: "This is my ablution and the ablution of the prophets before me, and the ablution of the Friend of the Merciful, Abraham, peace be upon him." He, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever mentions Allah during his ablution, Allah purifies his entire body; and whoever does not mention Allah, only the parts the water touches are purified." He, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever performs ablution while already in a state of purity, Allah writes for him ten good deeds." He, peace be upon him, said: "Ablution upon ablution is light upon light." All of this urges the renewal of ablution. He, peace be upon him, said: "When the Muslim servant performs ablution and rinses his mouth, sins exit from his mouth; when he snuffs water into his nose, sins exit from his nose; when he washes his face, sins exit from his face until they emerge from beneath his eyelashes; when he washes his hands, sins exit from his hands until they emerge from beneath his nails; when he wipes his head, sins exit from his head until they emerge from beneath his ears; and when he washes his feet, sins exit from his feet until they emerge from beneath his toenails. Then his walking to the mosque and his prayer are an additional supererogatory act for him." It is also narrated that "the pure one is like the fasting one." He, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever performs ablution and perfects it, then raises his gaze to the sky and says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger'—the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters through whichever he wishes." ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Sound ablution drives the devil away from you." Mujāhid said: "Whoever is able not to spend the night except in a state of purity, remembering Allah and seeking His forgiveness, let him do so, for souls are raised in the state in which they were seized."

As for the manner of ritual bathing (ghusl): One places the vessel to his right, then names Allah the Exalted, washes his hands three times, then cleanses his private parts as I described to you, and removes any filth on his body if present. Then he performs the ablution for prayer as we described, except for washing the feet—he delays them, for if he washes them and then places them on the ground, that is a waste of water. Then he pours water over his head three times, then over his right side three times, then over his left side three times. Then he rubs the front of his body and runs his fingers through the hair of his head and beard, ensuring water reaches the roots of thick or thin hair. It is not incumbent upon a woman to undo her braids unless she knows water will not reach the inner strands of her hair. He should attend to the folds of his body. Let him beware of touching his penis during this process, for if he does so, he must repeat the ablution. If he performed ablution before the bath, he does not repeat it after the bath.

These are the sunan (practices) of ablution and ritual bathing. We have mentioned from them what is indispensable for the wayfarer of the Hereafter to know and practice. As for other subsidiary questions needed in incidental circumstances, let him refer to the books of jurisprudence (fiqh).

The obligatory (wājib) elements of what we have mentioned in ritual bathing are two: the intention (niyyah) and covering the entire body with water. The obligatory elements of ablution are: the intention, washing the face, washing the hands up to the elbows, wiping what the name of "head" applies to, washing the feet up to the ankles, and the proper order (tartīb). As for continuity (muwālāh), it is not obligatory.

Ritual bathing becomes obligatory due to four causes: the emission of semen, the meeting of the two circumcisions (i.e., sexual intercourse), menstruation (ḥayḍ), and post-natal bleeding (nifās). All other baths are sunnah, such as the bath for the two ʿĪds, Friday, the festivals, entering the state of iḥrām, standing at ʿArafah and Muzdalifah, entering Mecca, three baths during the days of al-Tashrīq, and the farewell circumambulation (ṭawāf al-wadāʿ) according to one opinion. Likewise, the bath for a disbeliever who embraces Islam without being in a state of major impurity, for the insane person upon regaining consciousness, and for one who washes a deceased person—all of these are recommended (mustaḥabb).

chapters.title_en: On the Manner of Tayammum (Dry Ablution) and the Third Division of Cleanliness
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| كيفية التيمم

من تعذر عليه استعمال الماء لفقده بعد الطلب أو بمانع له عن الوصول إليه
من سبع أو حابس أو كان الماء الحاضر يحتاج إليه لعطشه أو لعطش رفيقه أو كان
ملكا لغيره ولم يبعه إلا بأكثر من ثمن المثل أو  كان به جراحة أو مرض وخاف
من استعماله فساد العضو أو شدة الضنا فينبغي أن يصبر حتى يدخل عليه وقت
الفريضة ثم يقصد صعيدا طيبا عليه تراب طاهر خالص لين بحيث يثور منه غبار
ويضرب عليه كفيه ضاما بين أصابعه ويمسح بهما جميع وجهه مرة واحدة وينوي عند
ذلك استباحة الصلاة ولا يكلف إيصال الغبار إلى ما تحت الشعور خفت أو كثفت
ويجتهد أن يستوعب بشرة وجهه بالغبار ويحصل ذلك بالضربة الواحدة فإن عرض
الوجه لا يزيد على عرض الكفين ويكفي في الاستيعاب غالب الظن ثم ينزع خاتمة
ويضرب ضربة ثانية يفرج فيها بين أصابعه ثم يلصق ظهور يده اليمنى ببطون
أصابع يده اليسرى بحيث لا يجاوز أطراف الأنامل من إحدى الجهتين عرض المسبحة
من الأخرى ثم يمر يده اليسرى من حيث وضعها على ظاهر ساعده الأيمن إلى
المرفق ثم يقلب بطن كفه اليسرى على باطن ساعده الأيمن ويمرها إلى الكوع
ويمر بطن إبهامه اليسرى على ظاهر إبهامه اليمنى ثم يفعل باليسرى كذلك
ثم يمسح كفيه ويخلل بين أصابعه وغرض هذا التكليف تحصيل الاستيعاب إلى
المرفقين بضربة واحدة فإن عسر عليه ذلك فلا بأس بأن يستوعب بضربتين وزيادة
وإذا صلى به الفرض فله أن يتنفل كيف شاء فإن جمع بين فريضتين فينبغي أن
يعيد التيمم للثانية
وهكذا يفرد كل فريضة بتيمم والله أعلم
PageV01P136

### ||| القسم الثالث من النظافة التنظيف عن الفضلات الظاهرة وهي نوعان أوساخ وأجزاء

### |||| النوع الأول الأوساخ والرطوبات المترشحة وهي ثمانية
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ي-م (t-y-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To intend, to aim at, to betake oneself to a thing; "al-ṣaʿīd" is the surface of the earth, whether soil or rock.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tayammum is a divinely ordained substitute (badal) for ablution, signifying intentional recourse to pure earth as an act of worship, not mere physical cleansing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "intending a thing"; metaphorically extended to the legal act of wiping the face and hands with earth, as the intention (niyyah) is its constitutive pillar.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The opening "من تعذر عليه" governs a series of apodoses (fa-yanbaghī...), requiring careful tracking of the protasis across multiple subordinate conditions.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the manner of tayammum (dry ablution): When a person finds the use of water impossible — either due to its absence after having sought it, or due to an obstacle preventing his access to it, such as a beast of prey or an imprisoning captor; or when the water present is needed by him for his own thirst or for the thirst of his companion; or when the water belongs to another and its owner will not sell it except at more than the fair price (thaman al-mithl); or when he has a wound or an illness and fears that using water would corrupt the limb or cause severe distress — then he should wait until the time of the obligatory prayer (farīḍah) enters upon him. Thereafter, he should betake himself to pure elevated ground (ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban) upon which there is pure, unmixed, soft dust, such that dust rises from it. He strikes it with both palms, drawing his fingers together, and wipes with them his entire face in a single stroke. At that moment he intends (yannī) the permissibility of the prayer (istibāḥat al-ṣalāh). He is not obligated to convey the dust to what lies beneath the hairs — whether they be sparse or thick — but he should strive to cover the entire skin of his face with dust. This is achieved by the single strike, for the surface area of the face does not exceed the breadth of the two palms. Sufficiency in covering is satisfied by predominant conjecture (ghālib al-ẓann). Then he removes his ring and strikes a second stroke, spreading his fingers apart. He then adheres the back of his right hand to the inner surface of the fingers of his left hand, such that the tips of the fingers do not exceed, from either side, the breadth of the index finger (al-musabbihah) of the other hand. He then passes his left hand from its place of placement over the outer forearm of his right arm up to the elbow. Then he turns the inner palm of his left hand onto the inner side of his right forearm and passes it down to the wrist (al-kūʿ). He passes the inner surface of his left thumb over the outer surface of his right thumb. He then does the same with the left arm likewise. Thereafter, he wipes his two palms and interlaces his fingers. The purpose of this obligation (taklīf) is to achieve complete coverage up to the two elbows with a single stroke. If that proves difficult for him, there is no harm in covering with two strokes or more. When he has prayed the obligatory prayer with this tayammum, he may perform supererogatory prayers (tanafful) as he wishes. But if he wishes to combine two obligatory prayers, he should renew the tayammum for the second one. Thus, each obligatory prayer is singled out with its own tayammum. And God knows best.

[Page V01P136]

### The Third Division of Cleanliness: Purification from Visible Filth — Two Types: Dirt and Particles

### The First Type: Dirt and Seeping Moistures — These Are Eight in Number

chapters.title_en: On the Purification of the Body from Filth and the Etiquettes of the Bathhouse (Section 62 of the Revival of the Religious Sciences)
chapters.arabic_text:
الأول ما يجتمع في شعر الرأس من الدرن والقمل فالتنظيف عنه مستحب بالغسل
والترجيل والتدهين إزالة للشعث عنه وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يدهن الشعر
ويرجله غبا ويأمر به (1) ويقول صلى الله عليه وسلم ادهنوا غبا (2) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم من كان له شعرة فليكرمها (3) أي ليصنها عن الأوساخ ودخل
عليه رجل ثائر الرأس أشعث اللحية فقال أما كان لهذا دهن يسكن به شعره ثم
قال يدخل أحدكم كأنه شيطان (4)
الثاني ما يجتمع من الوسخ في معاطف  الأذن والمسح يزيل ما يظهر منه وما
يجتمع في قعر الصماخ فينبغي أن ينظف برفق عند الخروج من الحمام فإن كثرة
ذلك ربما تضر بالسمع
الثالث ما يجتمع في داخل الأنف من الرطوبات المنعقدة الملتصقة بجوانبه
ويزيلها بالاستنشاق والاستنثار
الرابع ما يجتمع على الأسنان وطرف اللسان من القلح فيزيله السواك
والمضمضة وقد ذكرناهما
الخامس ما يجتمع في اللحية من الوسخ والقمل إذا لم يتعهد ويستحب إزالة
ذلك بالغسل والتسريح بالمشط
وفي الخبر المشهور أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لا يفارقه المشط والمدرى
والمرآة في سفر ولا حضر (5) وهي سنة العرب وفي خبر غريب أنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم كان يسرح لحيته في اليوم مرتين (6) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم كث اللحية
(7) وكذلك كان أبو بكر وكان عثمان طويل اللحية رقيقها وكان على عريض اللحية
قد ملأت ما بين منكبيه
وفي حديث أغرب منه قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها اجتمع قوم بباب رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم فخرج إليهم فرأيته يطلع في الحب يسوي من رأسه ولحيته
(8) فقلت أوتفعل ذلك يا رسول الله فقال نعم إن الله يحب من عبده أن يتجمل
لإخوانه إذا خرج إليهم والجاهل ربما يظن أن ذلك من حب التزين للناس قياسا
على أخلاق غيره وتشبيها للملائكة بالحدادين وهيهات فقد كان رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بالدعوة وكان من وظائفه أن يسعى في تعظيم أمر نفسه
في قلوبهم كيلا تزدريه نفوسهم ويحسن صورته في أعينهم كيلا تستصغره أعينهم
فينفرهم ذلك ويتعلق المنافقون بذلك في تنفيرهم
وهذا القصد واجب على كل عالم تصدي لدعوة الخلق إلى الله عز وجل وهو أن
يراعي من ظاهره ما لا يوجب نفرة الناس عنه
والاعتماد في مثل هذه الأمور على النية فإنها أعمال في أنفسها تكتسب
الأوصاف من المقصود فالتزين PageV01P137
على هذا القصد محبوب وترك الشعث في اللحية إظهارا للزهد وقلة المبالاة
