بالنفس محذور وتركه شغلا بما هو أهم منه محبوب
وهذه أحوال باطنة بين العبد وبين الله  عز وجل
والناقد بصير والتلبيس غير رائج عليه بحال وكم من جاهل يتعاطى هذه الأمور
التفاتا إلى الخلق وهو يلبس على نفسه وعلى غيره ويزعم أن قصده الخير فترى
جماعة من العلماء يلبسون الثياب الفاخرة ويزعمون أن قصدهم إرغام المبتدعة
والمجادلين والتقرب إلى الله تعالى به
وهذا أمر ينكشف يوم تبلى السرائر ويوم يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في
الصدور فعند ذلك تتميز السبيكة الخالصة من البهرجة فنعوذ بالله من الخزي
يوم العرض الأكبر
السادس وسخ البراجم وهي معاطف ظهور الأنامل كانت العرب لا تكثر غسل ذلك
لتركها غسل اليد عقيب الطعام فيجتمع في تلك الغضون وسخ فأمرهم رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم بغسل البراجم (1)
السابع تنظيف الرواجب (2) أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العرب
بتنظيفها وهي رءوس الأنامل وما تحت الأظفار من الوسخ لأنها كانت لا يحضرها
المقراض في كل وقت فتجتمع فيها أوساخ فوقت لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم قلم الأظفار ونتف الإبط وحلق العانة أربعين يوما (3) لكنه أمر رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتنظيف ما تحت الأظفار (4) وجاء في الأثر أن النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم استبطأ الوحي فلما هبط عليه جبريل عليه السلام قال له
كيف ننزل عليكم وأنتم لا تغسلون براجمكم ولا تنظفون رواجبكم (5) وقلحا لا
تستاكون مر أمتك بذلك والاف وسخ الظفر والتف وسخ الأذن وقوله عز وجل {فلا
تقل لهما أف} تعبهما أي بما تحت الظفر من الوسخ وقيل لا تتأذ بهما كما
تتأذى بما تحت الظفر
الثامن الدرن الذي يجتمع على جميع البدن برشح العرق وغبار الطريق وذلك
يزيله الحمام ولا بأس بدخول الحمام دخل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
حمامات الشام وقال بعضهم نعم البيت بيت الحمام يطهر البدن ويذكر النار روي
ذلك عن أبي الدرداء وأبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنهما
وقال بعضهم بئس البيت بيت الحمام يبدي العورة ويذهب الحياء فهذا تعرض
لآفته وذاك تعرض لفائدته ولا بأس بطلب فائدته عند  الاحتراز من آفته
ولكن على داخل الحمام وظائف من السنن والواجبات فعليه واجبان في عورته
وواجبان في عورة غيره
أما الواجبان في عورته فهو أن يصونها عن نظر الغير ويصونها عن مس الغير
فلا يتعاطى أمرها وإزالة وسخها إلا بيده ويمنع الدلاك من مس الفخذ وما بين
السرة إلى العانة وفي إباحة مس ما ليس بسوءة لإزالة الوسخ احتمال ولكن
الأقيس التحريم إذألحق مس السوأتين في التحريم بالنظر فكذلك ينبغي أن تكون
بقية العورة أعني الفخذين
والواجبان في عورة الغير أن يغض بصر نفسه عنها وأن ينهى عن كشفها لأن
النهي عن المنكر واجب وعليه ذكر ذلك وليس عليه القبول ولا يسقط عنه وجوب
الذكر إلا لخوف ضرب أو شتم أو ما يجري عليه مما هو حرام في نفسه فليس عليه
أن ينكر حراما يرهق المنكر عليه إلى مباشرة حرام آخر
فأما قوله أعلم أن ذلك لا يفيد ولا يعمل به فهذا PageV01P138
لا يكون عذرا بل لا بد من الذكر فلا يخلو قلب عن التأثر من سماع الإنكار
واستشعار الاحتراز عند التعبير بالمعاصي وذلك يؤثر في تقبيح الأمر في عينه
وتنفير نفسه فلا يجوز تركه ولمثل هذا صار الحزم ترك دخول الحمام في هذه
الأوقات إذ لا تخلو عن عورات مكشوفة لا سيما ما تحت السرة إلى ما فوق
العانة إذ الناس لا يعدونها عورة وقد ألحقها الشرع بالعورة وجعلها كالحريم
لها ولهذا يستحب تخلية الحمام
وقال بشر بن الحرث ما أعنف رجلا لا يملك إلا درهما دفعه ليخلي له الحمام
ورؤي ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما في الحمام ووجهه إلى الحائط وقد عصب عينيه
بعصابة وقال بعضهم لا بأس بدخول الحمام ولكن بإزارين إزار للعورة وإزار
للرأس يتقنع به ويحفظ عينيه وأما السنن فعشرة فالأول النية وهو أن لا يدخل
لعاجل دنيا ولا عابثا لأجل هوى بل يقصد به التنظف المحبوب تزينا للصلاة ثم
يعطي الحمامي الأجرة قبل الدخول فإن ما يستوفيه مجهول وكذا ما ينتظره
الحمامي فتسليم الأجرة  قبل الدخول دفع للجهالة من أحد العوضين وتطييب لنفسه
ثم يقدم رجله اليسرى عند الدخول ويقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أعوذ بالله
من الرجس النجس الخبيث المخبث الشيطان الرجيم ثم يدخل وقت الخلوة أو يتكلف
تخلية الحمام فإنه إن لم يكن في الحمام إلا أهل الدين والمحتاطين للعورات
فالنظر إلى الأبدان مكشوفة فيه شائبة من قلة الحياء وهو مذكر للنظر في
العورات ثم لا يخلو الإنسان في الحركات عن انكشاف العورات بانعطاف في أطراف
الإزار فيقع البصر على العورة من حيث لا يدري ولأجله عصب ابن عمر رضي الله
عنهما عينيه ويغسل الجناحين عند الدخول ولا يعجل بدخول البيت الحار حتى
يعرق في الأول وأن لا يكثر صب الماء بل يقتصر على قدر الحاجة فإنه المأذون
فيه بقرينة الحال والزيادة عليه لو علمه الحمامي لكرهه لا سيما الماء الحار
فله مئونة وفيه تعب وأن يتذكر حر النار بحرارة الحمام ويقدر نفسه محبوسا في
البيت الحار ساعة ويقيسه إلى جهنم فإنه أشبه بيت بجهنم النار من تحت
والظلام من فوق نعوذ بالله من ذلك بل العاقل لا يغفل عن ذكر الآخرة في لحظة
فإنها مصيره ومستقره فيكون له في كل ما يراه من ماء أو نار أو غيرهما عبرة
وموعظة فإن المرء ينظر بحسب همته
فإذا دخل بزاز ونجار وبناء وحائك دارا معمورة مفروشة فإذا تفقدتهم رأيت
البزاز ينظر إلى الفرش يتأمل قيمتها والحائك ينظر إلى الثياب يتأمل نسجها
والنجار ينظر إلى السقف يتأمل كيفية تركيبها والبناء ينظر إلى الحيطان
يتأمل كيفية إحكامها واستقامتها
فكذلك سالك طريق الآخرة لا يرى من الأشياء شيئا إلا ويكون له موعظة وذكرى
للآخرة بل لا ينظر إلى شيء إلا ويفتح الله عز وجل له طريق عبرة فإن نظر إلى
سواد تذكر ظلمة اللحد وإن نظر إلى حية تذكر أفاعي جهنم وإن نظر إلى صورة
قبيحة شنيعة تذكر منكرا ونكيرا والزبانية وإن سمع صوتا هائلا تذكر نفخة
الصور وإن رأى شيئا حسنا تذكر نعيم الجنة وإن  سمع كلمة رد أو قبول في سوق
أو دار تذكر ما ينكشف من آخر أمره بعد الحساب من الرد والقبول وما أجدر أن
يكون هذا هو الغالب على قلب العاقل إلا لا يصرفه عنه إلا مهمات الدنيا فإذا
نسب مدة المقام في الدنيا إلى مدة المقام في الآخرة استحقرها إن لم يكن ممن
أغفل قلبه وأعميت بصيرته
ومن السنن أن لا يسلم عند الدخول وإن سلم عليه لم يجب بلفظ السلام بل
يسكت إن أجاب غيره وإن أحب قال عافاك الله ولا بأس بأن يصافح الداخل ويقول
عافاك الله لابتداء الكلام
ثم لا يكثر الكلام في الحمام ولا يقرأ القرآن إلا سرا ولا بأس بإظهار
الاستعاذة من الشيطان ويكره دخول الحمام بين العشاءين وقريبا من الغروب فإن
ذلك وقت انتشار الشياطين ولا بأس أن يدلكه غيره فقد نقل ذلك عن يوسف بن
أسباط أوصى بأن يغسله إنسان لم يكن من أصحابه وقال إنه دلكني في الحمام مرة
فأردت أن أكافئه بما يفرح به وإنه
PageV01P139
ليفرح بذلك
ويدل على جوازه ما روى بعض الصحابة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نزل
منزلا في بعض أسفاره فنام على بطنه وعبد أسود يغمز ظهره فقلت ما هذا يا
رسول الله فقال إن الناقة تقحمت بي (1) ثم مهما فرغ من الحمام شكر الله عز
وجل على هذه النعمة
فقد قيل الماء الحار في الشتاء من النعيم الذي يسأل عنه
وقال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما الحمام من النعيم الذي أحدثوه
هذا من جهة الشرع
أما من جهة الطب فقد قيل الحمام بعد النورة أمان من الجذام وقيل النورة
في كل شهر مرة تطفىء المرة الصفراء وتنقي اللون وتزيد في الجماع
وقيل بولة في الحمام قائما في الشتاء أنفع من شربة دواء
وقيل نومة في الصيف بعد الحمام تعدل شربة دواء
وغسل القدمين بماء بارد بعد الخروج من الحمام أمان من النقرس
ويكره صب الماء البارد على الرأس عند الخروج وكذا شربه هذا حكم  الرجال
وأما النساء فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحل للرجل أن يدخل حليلته
الحمام (2) وفي البيت مستحم والمشهور أنه حرام على الرجال دخول الحمام إلا
بمئزر (3) وحرام على المرأة دخول الحمام إلا نفساء أو مريضة
ودخلت عائشة رضي الله عنها حماما من سقم بها
فإن دخلت لضرورة فلا تدخل إلا بمئزر سابغ ويكره للرجل أن يعطيها أجرة
الحمام فيكون معينا لها على المكروه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ف (na-ẓa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cleanliness, purity from physical dirt; removal of that which soils or defiles.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual and moral purification (taṭhīr) as a prerequisite for worship and spiritual refinement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical cleansing; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual purification from sin.
- Root: ح-م-م (ḥa-m-ma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Heat, the bathhouse (ḥammām); a place of hot water and steam.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The bathhouse as a site of bodily cleansing, yet fraught with dangers of exposing the ʿawrah (private parts).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical structure; metaphorical for the heat of Hellfire (nar) as a reminder.
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿa-wa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Defect, exposure; the private parts (ʿawrah) that must be concealed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal and moral obligation to guard one's own and others' ʿawrah from sight and touch.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bodily parts; metaphorical for vulnerability and shame before God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing clauses with "if" (in) and "except" (illā) to delineate legal obligations and exemptions, as in the conditions for entering the bathhouse and the exceptions for necessity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first [category of filth] is what accumulates in the hair of the head—dirt and lice. Cleaning it is recommended (mustaḥabb) through washing, combing, and oiling, to remove dishevelment (shaʿath). The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to oil his hair and comb it every other day (ghibban) and commanded others to do so. He said: "Oil your hair every other day." And he said: "Whoever has hair, let him honor it"—that is, protect it from filth. A man entered upon him with disheveled hair and a tousled beard, and he said: "Did this man not have oil to settle his hair with?" Then he said: "One of you enters as if he were a devil."

The second: What accumulates of grime in the folds of the ear. Wiping (al-masḥ) removes what appears of it, but what gathers in the depths of the ear canal should be cleaned gently upon leaving the bathhouse, for an excess of it may harm one's hearing.

The third: What gathers inside the nose of congealed moisture clinging to its sides. This is removed by snuffing water up (al-istinshāq) and blowing it out (al-istinthār).

The fourth: What accumulates on the teeth and the tip of the tongue of film (qalaḥ). This is removed by the toothstick (siwāk) and rinsing the mouth (maḍmaḍah), which we have already mentioned.

The fifth: What gathers in the beard of dirt and lice if it is not tended to. It is recommended to remove this by washing and combing with a comb. In the well-known report, the Prophet (peace be upon him) never parted with his comb, his hair-dresser (midrā), and his mirror, whether traveling or at home. This is the sunnah of the Arabs. In a rare report, the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to comb his beard twice a day. He had a thick beard, as did Abu Bakr. ʿUthmān had a long, thin beard, and ʿAlī had a broad beard that filled the space between his shoulders.

In a stranger report still, ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) said: "A group gathered at the door of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). He went out to them, and I saw him looking into a vessel, arranging his hair and beard." I said: "Do you do this, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Yes. Indeed, God loves that a servant beautify himself for his brothers when he goes out to them." The ignorant one might suppose this stems from a love of self-display before people, drawing an analogy from the character of others and likening the angels to blacksmiths. Far be it! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was commanded to call [people to God], and among his duties was to strive to magnify his own standing in their hearts, lest their souls disdain him, and to render his image fair in their eyes, lest their eyes belittle him—for that would drive them away, and the hypocrites would seize upon it to repel them.

This intent is obligatory upon every scholar who undertakes the call of creation to God (Exalted is He): to observe in his outward appearance that which does not cause people to recoil from him. Reliance in such matters is upon the intention (niyyah), for these are acts that in themselves acquire their qualities from their purpose. Thus, adornment with this intent is beloved; leaving the beard disheveled to display asceticism (zuhd) and disregard for oneself is perilous; while leaving it [unadorned] due to preoccupation with what is more important is beloved. These are inward states between the servant and God (Exalted is He). The discerning critic is perceptive, and deception (talbīs) does not pass with him at all. How many an ignorant one engages in these matters with an eye to creation, deceiving himself and others, claiming his intent is good! You see a group of scholars wearing fine garments, claiming their intent is to spite the innovators and disputants and to draw near to God thereby. This matter will be unveiled on the Day when secrets are tested, when what is in graves is scattered, and what is in breasts is brought forth. Then the pure ingot will be distinguished from the counterfeit. We seek refuge in God from disgrace on the Day of the Great Display.

The sixth: The filth of the knuckles (barājim)—the folds on the backs of the fingers. The Arabs did not often wash these, as they neglected washing the hands after food, so dirt gathered in those creases. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) commanded them to wash the knuckles.

The seventh: Cleaning the finger-joints (rawājib). The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) commanded the Arabs to clean them—these being the tips of the fingers and the dirt under the nails—because they did not have scissors at all times, so filth accumulated there. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) set a time limit for trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and shaving the pubic region: forty days. But he commanded cleaning under the nails. It is reported in the tradition that the Prophet (peace be upon him) awaited revelation, and when Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon him, he said: "How shall we descend upon you when you do not wash your knuckles, nor clean your finger-joints, nor remove the film from your teeth? Command your community to do this." And the filth of the nail and the filth of the ear [are mentioned]. God (Exalted is He) says: {«فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ»} ("So do not say to them 'Uff'")—meaning, do not weary them, even with the dirt under the nail. And it is said: do not harm them as you would be harmed by what is under the nail.

The eighth: The grime that accumulates over the entire body from the sweat's exudation and the dust of the road. The bathhouse removes this, and there is no harm in entering the bathhouse. The companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouses of Syria. Some of them said: "Excellent is the house, the house of the bathhouse! It purifies the body and reminds one of the Fire." This is reported from Abu al-Dardāʾ and Abu Ayyūb al-Anṣārī (may God be pleased with them). Others said: "Wretched is the house, the house of the bathhouse! It exposes the private parts and destroys modesty." This one addresses its harm, and that one addresses its benefit. There is no harm in seeking its benefit while guarding against its harm.

But upon the one entering the bathhouse are duties from the sunan and obligations (wājibāt). Upon him are two obligations concerning his own private parts (ʿawrah) and two concerning the private parts of others. As for the two concerning his own ʿawrah: he must shield it from the sight of others and shield it from the touch of others. Thus, he should not handle its affair or remove its filth except with his own hand, and he should prevent the attendant (dallāk) from touching the thigh and what is between the navel and the pubic region. Regarding the permissibility of touching what is not a shameful part (sawʾah) to remove filth, there is some probability, but the more sound analogy (al-qiyās) is prohibition, for the touch of the two shameful parts is linked to prohibition just as sight is. Likewise, the rest of the ʿawrah—namely, the thighs—should be treated the same.

As for the two obligations concerning the private parts of others: he must lower his own gaze from them and forbid their exposure, for commanding the good and forbidding the evil (al-nahy ʿan al-munkar) is obligatory. Upon him is the duty of verbal admonition (dhikr); acceptance is not upon him, nor does the obligation of admonition fall from him except out of fear of being struck, insulted, or subjected to something that is itself unlawful—for he is not obliged to forbid an evil if doing so would lead him into committing another evil. As for his saying, "I know it will not benefit nor be heeded"—this is no excuse. Rather, admonition is indispensable, for no heart is devoid of being affected by hearing disapproval and sensing caution when sins are mentioned. This influences the ugliness of the act in one's eyes and repels one's soul from it, so abandoning it is not permissible. For this reason, prudence dictates abandoning entry into the bathhouse at such times, for they are not free of exposed private parts—especially what is below the navel to above the pubic region, for people do not count it as ʿawrah, yet the Law has annexed it to the ʿawrah and made it like its sanctuary. Hence, it is recommended to reserve the bathhouse privately (takhliyat al-ḥammām).

Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith said: "How harsh is a man who owns but a single dirham and pays it to have the bathhouse emptied for himself!" Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both) was seen in the bathhouse with his face to the wall, having bound his eyes with a bandage. Some said: "There is no harm in entering the bathhouse, but with two wraps: one for the ʿawrah and one for the head, to cover oneself and protect one's eyes."

As for the sunan, they are ten. The first: the intention (niyyah)—that he does not enter for some immediate worldly gain, nor as a trifler following whim, but rather intends by it the beloved cleanliness, adorning himself for prayer. Then he gives the bathhouse attendant his fee before entering, for what he will receive is unknown, as is what the attendant anticipates; thus, paying the fee beforehand removes the uncertainty (jahālah) from one of the two exchange items and pleases his soul. Then he steps in with his left foot upon entering and says: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I seek refuge in God from the filth, the impurity, the wicked, the corrupting, the accursed Satan." Then he enters at a time of solitude or makes an effort to have the bathhouse emptied, for if there are none in the bathhouse but the religious and those cautious of private parts, still, looking at exposed bodies contains a taint of deficient modesty and reminds one of gazing at ʿawrahs. Moreover, a person is never free in his movements from the exposure of private parts due to a shift in the edges of his wrap, so the eye falls upon the ʿawrah unknowingly. For this reason, Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both) bound his eyes. He washes his sides upon entering and does not hasten into the hot chamber until he sweats in the first one. He should not pour water excessively but rather limit himself to what is needed, for that is what is permitted by the context of the situation; any excess, if the attendant knew of it, would displease him—especially hot water, for it has a cost and involves labor. He should recall the heat of the Fire by the heat of the bathhouse, imagining himself imprisoned in the hot chamber for an hour, and measure it against Hellfire—for it is the house most resembling Hell: fire from below and darkness from above. We seek refuge in God from that. Indeed, the intelligent man does not neglect the remembrance of the Hereafter for a single moment, for it is his destiny and his abode. Thus, in everything he sees—water, fire, or otherwise—he finds a lesson (ʿibrah) and an admonition, for a man looks according to his aspiration.

When a cloth-merchant, a carpenter, a builder, and a weaver enter a furnished, inhabited house, if you examine them, you see the cloth-merchant looking at the furnishings, pondering their value; the weaver looking at the garments, pondering their weave; the carpenter looking at the ceiling, pondering its construction; and the builder looking at the walls, pondering their solidity and straightness. Likewise, the traveler on the path of the Hereafter sees nothing of things but that it becomes for him an admonition and a reminder of the Hereafter. Nay, he looks at nothing but that God (Exalted is He) opens for him a path of reflection. If he sees darkness, he recalls the gloom of the grave; if he sees a serpent, he recalls the vipers of Hell; if he sees an ugly, hideous form, he recalls Munkar and Nakīr and the Zabāniyah; if he hears a terrifying sound, he recalls the Blast of the Trumpet (nafkhat al-ṣūr); if he sees something beautiful, he recalls the bliss of Paradise; if he hears a word of rejection or acceptance in a market or a house, he recalls what will be unveiled of his final affair after the Reckoning—of rejection and acceptance. How fitting it is that this should dominate the heart of the intelligent man, and nothing should divert him from it except the necessities of this world. For if he compares the duration of his stay in this world to the duration of his stay in the Hereafter, he will deem it insignificant—unless he is among those whose hearts are heedless and whose inner sight is blinded.

Among the sunan is that he should not greet (salām) upon entering, and if someone greets him, he should not respond with the words of salām but rather remain silent if another responds. If he wishes, he may say: "May God heal you" (ʿāfāka Allāh). There is no harm in shaking hands with the one entering and saying "May God heal you" as an opening of speech. Then he should not speak much in the bathhouse, nor recite the Qurʾān except silently. There is no harm in uttering the seek-refuge (istiʿādhah) from Satan. It is disliked (makrūh) to enter the bathhouse between the two evening prayers and near sunset, for that is a time when devils spread about. There is no harm in another rubbing him down, for this is transmitted from Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ, who bequeathed that a man who was not among his companions should wash him, saying: "He rubbed me down in the bathhouse once, and I wished to repay him with what would delight him—and he delights in that." Its permissibility is indicated by what some companions reported: that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) alighted at a waystation during one of his journeys, slept on his belly, and a black slave was massaging his back. I said: "What is this, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The she-camel threw me off." Then, when he finishes with the bathhouse, he thanks God (Exalted is He) for this blessing, for it has been said: "Hot water in winter is among the blessings about which one will be asked." Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both) said: "The bathhouse is among the blessings that people have newly introduced."

This is from the standpoint of the Law. As for the standpoint of medicine, it has been said: "The bathhouse after depilation (nūrah) is safety from leprosy." It is said: "Depilation once a month extinguishes the yellow bile, purifies the complexion, and increases sexual vigor." It is said: "A urination in the bathhouse while standing in winter is more beneficial than a draught of medicine." It is said: "A sleep in summer after the bathhouse equals a draught of medicine." Washing the feet with cold water after leaving the bathhouse is safety from gout. It is disliked to pour cold water on the head upon leaving, and likewise to drink it.

This is the ruling for men. As for women, he (peace be upon him) said: "It is not lawful for a man to let his wife enter the bathhouse," even if there is a bath in the house. The well-known ruling is that it is forbidden (ḥarām) for men to enter the bathhouse except with a waist-wrapper (miʾzar), and forbidden for women to enter the bathhouse except for one who is postpartum or ill. ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) entered a bathhouse due to an illness she suffered. If a woman enters out of necessity, she should not enter except with a full, ample wrap. It is disliked for a man to give her the bathhouse fee, for he would thereby be assisting her in the disliked act.

chapters.title_en: The Second Kind: On What Arises in the Body from Parts — Eight in Number
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| النوع الثاني فيما يحدث في البدن من الأجزاء  وهي ثمانية
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح د ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Origination, occurrence, coming-to-be after non-existence; a novel event (ḥādith) that was not previously.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, ḥudūth denotes temporal origination of contingent beings, contrasted with eternal pre-existence (qidam); here it signals the body’s generated states.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for what emerges in time; metaphorical (majāz) if applied to mental constructs — here literal, as bodily parts arise physically.
- Root: ج ز ء (j-z-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A part, portion, component; that which constitutes a whole (kull) when aggregated.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ontology, ajzāʾ are the constituent elements of composite bodies; in this context, the anatomical components of the human frame.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical division; not used metaphorically here — the text refers to actual bodily parts.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "وهي ثمانية" (and they are eight) functions as a parenthetical explicative clause (jumlah muʿtaridah) clarifying the enumeration, governed by the nominal sentence’s predicate structure.
chapters.translation: I say: The second kind [of created things] concerns what arises in the body from its parts — and these are eight in number.

chapters.title_en: On the Sunnahs of Fitrah: The Trimming of the Nail, the Moustache, and Other Practices of Personal Hygiene
chapters.arabic_text:
الأول شعر الرأس ولا بأس بحلقه لمن أراد التنظيف ولا بأس بتركه لمن يدهنه
ويرجله إلا إذا تركه قزعا أي قطعا وهو دأب أهل الشطارة أو أرسل الذوائب على
هيئة أهل الشرف حيث صار ذلك شعارا لهم فإنه إذا لم يكن شريفا كان ذلك
تلبيسا
الثاني شعر الشارب وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم قصوا الشارب وفي لفظ آخر
جزوا الشوارب وفي لفظ آخر حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى (4) أي اجعلوها حفاف
الشفة أي حولها وحفاف الشيء حوله ومنه {وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش}
وفي لفظ آخر احفوا وهذا يشعر بالاستئصال وقوله حفوا يدل على ما دون ذلك
وقال الله عز وجل أن يسئلكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا أي يستقصى عليكم وأما الحلق
فلم يرد
والإحفاء القريب من الحلق نقل عن الصحابة نظر بعض التابعين إلى رجل أحفى
شاربه فقال ذكرتني أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
وقال المغيرة بن شعبة نظر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد طال
شاربي فقال تعال فقصه لي على سواك (5) ولا بأس بترك سباليه وهما طرفا
الشارب فعل ذلك عمر وغيره لأن ذلك لا يستر الفم ولا يبقى فيه غمر الطعام إذ
لا يصل إليه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعفوا اللحى أي كثروها وفي الخبر إن
اليهود يعفون شواربهم PageV01P140
ويقصون لحاهم فخالفوهم (1) وكره بعض العلماء الحلق ورآه بدعة
الثالث شعر الإبط ويستحب نتفه في كل أربعين يوما مرة وذلك سهل على من
تعود نتفه في الابتداء فأما  من تعود الحلق فيكفيه الحلق إذ في النتف تعذيب
وإيلام والمقصود النظافة وأن لا يجتمع الوسخ في خللها ويحصل ذلك بالحلق
الرابع شعر العانة ويستحب إزالة ذلك إما بالحلق أو بالنورة ولا ينبغي أن
تتأخر عن أربعين يوما
الخامس الأظفار وتقليمها مستحب لشناعة صورتها إذا طالت ولما يجتمع فيها
من الوسخ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة أقلم أظفارك فإن
الشيطان يقعد على ما طال منها (2) ولو كان تحت الظفر وسخ فلا يمنع ذلك صحة
الوضوء لأنه لا يمنع وصول الماءولأنه يتساهل فيه للحاجة لا سيما في أظفار
الرجل وفي الأوساخ التي تجتمع على البراجم وظهور الأرجل والأيدي من العرب
وأهل السواد وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمرهم بالقلم وينكر عليهم
ما يرى تحت أظفارهم من الأوساخ ولم يأمرهم بإعادة الصلاة ولو أمر به لكان
فيه فائدة أخرى وهو التغليظ والزجر عن ذلك
ولم أر في الكتب خبرا مرويا في ترتيب قلم الأظفار ولكن سمعت أنه صلى الله
عليه وسلم بدأ بمسبحته اليمنى وختم بإبهامه اليمنى وابتدأ في اليسرى
بالخنصر إلى الإبهام (3) ولما تأملت في هذا خطر لي من المعنى ما يدل على أن
الرواية فيه صحيحة إذ مثل هذا المعنى لا ينكشف ابتداء إلا بنور النبوة وأما
العالم ذو البصيرة فغايته أن يستنبطه من العقل بعد نقل الفعل إليه
فالذي لاح لي فيه والعلم عند الله سبحانه أنه لا بد من قلم أظفار اليد
والرجل واليد أشرف من الرجل فيبدأ بها ثم اليمنى أشرف من اليسرى فيبدأ بها
ثم على اليمنى خمسة أصابع والمسبحة أشرفها إذ هي المشيرة في كلمتي الشهادة
من جملة الأصابع ثم بعدها ينبغي أن يبتدىء بما على يمينها إذ الشرع يستحب
إدارة الطهور وغيره على اليمين وإن وضعت ظهر الكف على الأرض فالإبهام هو
اليمين وإن وضعت بطن الكف فالوسطى هي اليمنى واليد إذا تركت بطبعها كان
الكف مائلا إلى جهة الأرض إذ جهة حركة اليمين إلى اليسار واستتمام  الحركة
إلى اليسار يجعل ظهر الكف عاليا فما يقتضيه الطبع أولى ثم إذا وضعت الكف
على الكف صارت الأصابع في حكم حلقة دائرة فيقتضي ترتيب الدور الذهاب عن
يمين المسبحة إلى أن يعود إلى المسبحة فتقع البداءة بخنصر اليسرى والختم
بإبهامها ويبقى إبهام اليمنى فيختم به التقليم
وإنما قدرت الكف موضوعة على الكف حتى تصير الأصابع كأشخاص في حلقة ليظهر
ترتيبها
وتقدير ذلك أولى من تقدير وضع الكف على ظهر الكف أو وضع ظهر الكف على ظهر
الكف فإن ذلك لا يقتضيه الطبع
وأما أصابع الرجل فالأولى عندي إن لم يثبت فيها نقل أن يبدأ بخنصر اليمنى
ويختم بخنصر اليسرى كما في التخليل فإن المعاني التي ذكرها في اليد لا تتجه
ههنا إذ لا مسبحة في الرجل
وهذه الأصابع في حكم صف واحد ثابت على الأرض فيبدأ من جانب اليمنى فإن
تقديرها حلقة بوضع الأخمص على الأخمص يأباه الطبع بخلاف اليدين
وهذه الدقائق في الترتيب تنكشف بنور النبوة في لحظة واحدة وإنما يطول
التعب علينا
ثم لو سئلنا ابتداء عن الترتيب في ذلك ربما لم يخطر لنا
وإذا ذكرنا فعله صلى الله عليه وسلم PageV01P141
وترتيبه ربما تيسر لنا مما عاينه صلى الله عليه وسلم بشهادة الحكم
وتنبيهه على المعنى استنباط المعنى ولا تظنن أن أفعاله صلى الله عليه وسلم
في جميع حركاته كانت خارجة عن وزن وقانون وترتيب بل جميع الأمور الاختيارية
التي ذكرناها يتردد فيها الفاعل بين قسمين أو أقسام كان لا يقدم على واحد
معين بالاتفاق بل بمعنى يقتضي الإقدام والتقديم فإن الاسترسال مهملا كما
يتفق سجية البهائم وضبط الحركات بموازين المعاني سجية أولياء الله تعالى
وكلما كانت حركات الإنسان وخطراته إلى الضبط أقرب وعن الإهمال وتركه سدى
أبعد كانت مرتبته إلى رتبة الأنبياء والأولياء أكثر وكان قربه من الله عز
وجل أظهر إذ القريب من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو القريب من الله عز وجل
والقريب من الله لا بد أن يكون قريبا فالقريب من القريب  قريب بالإضافة إلى
غيره فنعوذ بالله أن يكون زمام حركاتنا وسكناتنا في يد الشيطان بواسطة
الهوى
واعتبر في ضبط الحركات باكتحاله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنه كان يكتحل في
عينه اليمنى ثلاثا وفي اليسرى اثنين (1) فيبدأ باليمنى لشرفها
وتفاوته بين العينين لتكون الجملة وترا فإن للوتر فضلا عن الزوج فإن الله
سبحانه وتر يحب الوتر فلا ينبغي أن يخلو فعل العبد من مناسبة لوصف من أوصاف
الله تعالى
ولذلك استحب الإيتار في الاستجمار
وإنما لم يقتصر على الثلاث وهو وتر لأن اليسرى لا يخصها إلا واحدة
والغالب أن الواحدة لا تستوعب أصول الأجفان بالكحل وإنما خصص اليمين
بالثلاث لأن التفضيل لا بد منه للإيتار واليمين أفضل فهي بالزيادة أحق
فإن قلت فلم اقتصر على اثنين لليسرى وهي زوج فالجواب أن ذلك ضرورة إذ لو
جعل لكل واحدة وتر لكان المجموع زوجا إذ الوتر مع الوتر زوج ورعايته
الإيتار في مجموع الفعل وهو في حكم الخصلة الواحدة أحب من رعايته في الآحاد
ولذلك أيضا وجه وهو أن يكتحل في كل واحدة ثلاثا على قياس الوضوء (2) وقد
نقل ذلك في الصحيح وهو الأولى
ولو ذهبت أستقصي دقائق ما راعاه صلى الله عليه وسلم في حركاته لطال الأمر
فقس بما سمعته ما لم تسمعه
واعلم أن العالم لا يكون وارثا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا إذا اطلع
على جميع معاني الشريعة حتى لا يكون بينه وبين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
إلا درجة واحدة وهي درجة النبوة وهي الدرجة الفارقة بين الوارث والموروث إذ
الموروث هو الذي حصل المال له واشتغل بتحصيله واقتدر عليه والوارث هو الذي
لم يحصل ولم يقدر عليه ولكن انتقل إليه وتلقاه منه بعد حصوله له فأمثال هذه
المعاني مع سهولة أمرها بالإضافة إلى الأغوار والأسرار لا يستقل بدركها
ابتداء إلا الأنبياء ولا يستقل باستنباطها تلقيا بعد تنبيه الأنبياء عليها
إلا العلماء الذين هم ورثة الأنبياء عليهم السلام
السادس والسابع زيادة السرة وقلفة الحشفة أما السرة فتقطع في  أول الولادة
وأما التطهير بالختان فعادة اليهود في اليوم السابع من الولادة ومخالفتهم
بالتأخير إلى أن يثغر الولد أحب وأبعد عن الخطر قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
الختان سنة للرجال ومكرمة للنساء (3) وينبغي أن لا يبالغ في خفض المرأة قال
صلى الله عليه وسلم لأم عطية وكانت تخفض يا أم عطية أشمي ولا تنهكي فإنه
أسرى للوجه وأحظى عند الزوج (4) أي أكثر لماء الوجه ودمه وأحسن في جماعها
فانظر إلى جزالة لفظه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الكناية وإلى إشراق نور النبوة
من مصالح الآخرة التي هي أهم مقاصد النبوة إلى PageV01P142
مصالح الدنيا حتى انكشف له وهو أمي من هذا الأمر النازل قدره ما لو وقعت
الغفلة عنه خيف ضرره فسبحان من أرسله رحمة للعالمين ليجمع لهم بيمن بعثته
مصالح الدنيا والدين صلى الله عليه وسلم
الثامنة ما طال من اللحية وإنما أخرناها لنلحق بها ما في اللحية من السنن
والبدع إذ هذا أقرب موضع يليق به ذكرها وقد اختلفوا فيما طال منها فقيل إن
قبض الرجل على لحيته وأخذ ما فضل عن القبضة فلا بأس فقد فعله ابن عمر
وجماعة من التابعين واستحسنه الشعبي وابن سيرين وكرهه الحسن وقتادة وقالا
تركها عافية أحب لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعفوا اللحى والأمر في هذا قريب
إن لم ينته إلى تقصيص اللحية وتدويرها من الجوانب فإن الطول المفرط قد يشوه
الخلقة ويطلق ألسنة المغتابين بالنبذ إليه فلا بأس بالاحتراز عنه على هذه
النية
وقال النخعي عجبت لرجل عاقل طويل اللحية كيف لا يأخذ من لحيته ويجعلها
بين لحيتين فإن التوسط في كل شيء حسن ولذلك قيل كلما طالت اللحية تشمر
العقل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-م (q-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut, pare, or trim; the nail-paring (qalām) derives from the act of cutting and shaping, as the reed-pen (qalam) is shaped by cutting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the religious law, it signifies the removal of excess bodily growth as an act of purification (taṭhīr) and conformity to the primordial nature (fiṭrah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to the physical act of cutting; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the "paring" of the soul from worldly excess.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — The sequence of enumerated items (awwal, thānī, thālith...) is governed by the particle of coordination, linking each item as a coordinate member of a single grammatical series, each with its own governing verb or implied predicate.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first is the hair of the head. There is no harm in shaving it for one who desires cleanliness, and there is no harm in leaving it for one who oils it and combs it — except if he leaves it in patches (qazaʿ), that is, in cut-off pieces, which is the habit of rogues, or if he lets down long locks (al-dhawāʾib) in the manner of people of noble rank, when that has become their distinguishing emblem (shiʿār). For if he is not noble, then that is a deception (talbīs).

The second is the hair of the moustache. The Prophet ﷺ said: «قصوا الشارب» ("Trim the moustache"), and in another wording: «جزوا الشوارب» ("Clip the moustaches"), and in yet another: «حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى» ("Shave around the moustaches and let the beards grow thick") — that is, make them at the rim (ḥifāf) of the lip, meaning around it; and the rim (ḥifāf) of a thing is its surround. From this is the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic: {وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش} ("And you see the angels encircling (ḥāffīn) around the Throne"). In another wording: «أحفوا» ("Shave thoroughly"), and this suggests complete eradication (al-istiʾṣāl). His saying «حفوا» indicates something less than that. And God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {أن يسئلكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا} ("If He asks you for them and presses you (yuḥfikum), you would be niggardly") — that is, He would exact from you to the utmost. As for shaving (al-ḥalq) [of the moustache], nothing has been transmitted [to permit it].

And al-iḥfāʾ, which is close to shaving, has been transmitted from the Companions. Some of the Followers (al-tābiʿīn) looked at a man who had shaved his moustache thoroughly and said: "You have reminded me of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ."

Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ looked at me when my moustache had grown long and said: "Come, trim it for me on a tooth-stick (siwāk)." There is no harm in leaving the two ends (sibālāhu) — these being the two tips of the moustache — for ʿUmar and others did this, because that does not cover the mouth, nor does food residue (ghamar al-ṭaʿām) remain in it, since it does not reach it. And his saying ﷺ: «أعفوا اللحى» ("Let the beards grow thick") means: make them abundant. In the report: The Jews let their moustaches grow thick and trim their beards, so oppose them. Some scholars disliked shaving [the beard] and deemed it an innovation (bidʿah).

The third is the hair of the armpit. It is recommended (yustaḥabb) to pluck it once every forty days. This is easy for one who has accustomed himself to plucking from the beginning. As for one who has accustomed himself to shaving, shaving suffices him, for in plucking there is torment and pain. The intended purpose is cleanliness, and that filth not accumulate in its interstices — and this is achieved by shaving.

The fourth is the hair of the pubes. It is recommended to remove it, either by shaving or by depilatory lime (al-nūrah). It should not be delayed beyond forty days.

The fifth is the nails. Trimming them is recommended (mustaḥabb) because of the ugliness of their appearance when they grow long, and because of the filth that accumulates beneath them. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O Abū Hurayrah, trim your nails, for Satan sits upon whatever of them grows long." If there is filth beneath the nail, that does not prevent the validity of the ablution (wuḍūʾ), because it does not prevent the water from reaching [the skin], and because leniency is shown toward it out of necessity — especially regarding the nails of the foot, and the dirt that accumulates on the knuckles (al-barājim) and the backs of the feet and hands of the Arabs and the people of the countryside. The Messenger of God ﷺ used to command them to trim [their nails] and would disapprove of the filth he saw beneath their nails, yet he did not command them to repeat the prayer. Had he commanded that, there would have been another benefit in it — namely, severity and deterrence from that [practice].

I have not seen in the books any transmitted report (khabar) concerning the order of trimming the nails. But I have heard that he ﷺ began with his right index finger (musabbihah) and ended with his right thumb, and began on the left [hand] with the little finger, proceeding to the thumb. When I reflected upon this, there occurred to me a meaning that indicates the soundness of this report — for such a meaning is not unveiled at the outset except by the light of prophecy (nūr al-nubuwwah). As for the insightful scholar, his utmost is to derive it by reason after the action has been transmitted to him.

What became manifest to me in this — and knowledge is with God, the Glorified — is that the trimming of the nails of the hand and foot is inevitable. The hand is nobler than the foot, so one begins with it. Then the right is nobler than the left, so one begins with it. Then on the right there are five fingers, and the index finger (al-musabbihah) is the noblest of them, for it is the one pointed in the two words of the testimony of faith (shahādah) among the fingers. Then after it, one should begin with what is to its right — for the Sacred Law recommends the circulation of purification (al-ṭahūr) and other things toward the right. If the back of the hand is placed on the ground, then the thumb is the rightmost; but if the palm is placed, then the middle finger is the rightmost. When the hand is left to its natural disposition, the palm inclines toward the ground, for the direction of the right's movement is toward the left, and the completion of the movement toward the left makes the back of the hand uppermost. So what nature (al-ṭabʿ) dictates is more appropriate. Then, when the palm is placed upon the palm, the fingers come under the rule of a circular ring, and the order of the circle requires proceeding from the right of the index finger until one returns to the index finger. Thus the beginning falls upon the little finger of the left [hand] and the ending upon its thumb, and the right thumb remains, and with it the trimming is concluded.

I only estimated the palm as placed upon the palm so that the fingers become like persons in a circle, to make manifest their order. And this estimation is more appropriate than estimating the palm upon the back of the palm, or the back of the palm upon the back of the palm — for that is not dictated by nature.

As for the toes, the more appropriate in my view — if no transmission (naql) is established concerning them — is to begin with the little toe of the right foot and end with the little toe of the left, as in the case of the interdigital rubbing (takhīl) [in ablution]. For the meanings mentioned regarding the hand do not apply here, since there is no index finger (musabbihah) in the foot. These toes fall under the rule of a single row fixed upon the ground, so one begins from the right side. For estimating them as a circle by placing the soles upon the soles is repugnant to nature, unlike the two hands.

These subtleties (daqāʾiq) in ordering are unveiled by the light of prophecy in a single moment; it is only upon us that the toil is prolonged. Then, had we been asked at the outset about the order in this matter, perhaps it would not have occurred to us. But when his action ﷺ and his ordering are mentioned to us, perhaps the derivation of the meaning becomes facilitated for us — by what he ﷺ witnessed, through the testimony of wisdom (al-ḥikmah) and his indication of the meaning. And do not think that his actions ﷺ in all his movements were outside of measure, law, and order. Rather, all the voluntary matters we have mentioned — the agent wavers in them between two or several alternatives, and he does not advance upon one specific [alternative] by mere agreement, but by a meaning that necessitates the advance and the precedence. For letting oneself go, neglectfully, as happens, is the disposition of beasts; and governing movements by the balances of meanings is the disposition of the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh). The more a man's movements and thoughts are closer to governance and farther from neglect and being left to no purpose, the greater his rank in proximity to the ranks of the prophets and the friends of God, and the more manifest his nearness to God, the Mighty and Majestic. For the one near to the Prophet ﷺ is the one near to God, the Mighty and Majestic; and the one near to God must necessarily be near. So the one near to the near one is near in relation to others. We seek refuge in God from the reins of our movements and our stillness being in the hand of Satan by way of caprice (al-hawā).

Consider, regarding the governance of movements, his ﷺ use of kohl (iktiḥāl): he used to apply kohl to his right eye three times and to his left twice — beginning with the right due to its nobility. And his differentiation between the two eyes was so that the total would be odd (watr). For the odd has merit over the even, since God, the Glorified, is Odd (watr) and loves the odd. So it is fitting that the servant's action not be devoid of correspondence to one of the attributes of God, the Exalted. For this reason, the odd number (ītār) is recommended in the use of stones for cleansing (istijmār).

He did not confine himself to three [in the right eye] — which is odd — because the left would then receive only one, and generally one application does not cover the roots of the eyelids with kohl. Rather, he singled out the right for three because preference (tafḍīl) is inevitable for the odd, and the right is more excellent, so it is more deserving of the increase.

If you say: Why then did he confine himself to two for the left, which is even? The answer is that this is a necessity — for if each eye were given an odd number, the total would be even, since odd plus odd is even. And observing the odd in the total act — which is in the rule of a single trait — is more beloved than observing it in the individual parts. There is also another aspect to this: that he apply kohl to each eye three times, by analogy with the ablution (wuḍūʾ). This has been transmitted in the Ṣaḥīḥ, and it is more appropriate.

Were I to go on exhausting the subtleties of what he ﷺ observed in his movements, the matter would become long. So measure by what you have heard what you have not heard.

Know that the scholar is not an heir of the Prophet ﷺ unless he has attained to all the meanings of the Sacred Law, so that between him and the Prophet ﷺ there remains only a single degree — namely, the degree of prophecy (darajat al-nubuwwah). And it is the degree that differentiates between the heir and the one inherited from. For the one inherited from is he who acquired the wealth and busied himself with its acquisition and gained power over it; and the heir is he who did not acquire it nor gain power over it, but it was transferred to him and he received it from him after its acquisition. So such meanings — despite the ease of their matter in relation to the depths and secrets — none can grasp them at the outset except the prophets, and none can derive them by reception after the prophets' indication of them except the scholars, who are the heirs of the prophets, peace be upon them.

The sixth and seventh are the excess of the navel and the foreskin of the glans (qulfat al-ḥashafah). As for the navel, it is cut at the time of birth. As for purification by circumcision (al-khitān), it is the custom of the Jews on the seventh day after birth. Opposing them by delaying until the child's teeth appear (yuthghir) is more beloved and farther from danger. He ﷺ said: «الختان سنة للرجال ومكرمة للنساء» ("Circumcision is a Sunnah for men and an honor for women"). And one should not go to excess in the excision of the woman. He ﷺ said to Umm ʿAṭiyyah, who used to perform excision: "O Umm ʿAṭiyyah, trim but do not go deep (ashimmī wa lā tunhikī), for it is more radiant for the face and more favored with the husband" — that is, more abundant for the water and blood of the face, and better for her intercourse. So look at the consummate eloquence (jazālah) of his wording ﷺ in euphemism (kināyah), and at the shining of the light of prophecy from the interests of the Hereafter — which are the most important aims of prophecy — to the interests of this world, until there was unveiled to him, while he was unlettered (ummī), concerning this matter of lowly rank, that which, had negligence occurred regarding it, harm would be feared from it. Glory be to Him who sent him as a mercy to the worlds, to gather for them, by the blessing of his mission, the interests of this world and the religion. May God bless him and grant him peace.

The eighth is what grows long of the beard. We have delayed it only to append to it what pertains to the beard of Sunnahs and innovations (bidaʿ), for this is the nearest place befitting its mention. They have differed concerning what grows long of it. It was said: If a man grasps his beard and removes what exceeds the grip, there is no harm — for Ibn ʿUmar and a group of the Followers did this, and al-Shaʿbī and Ibn Sīrīn deemed it good. Al-Ḥasan and Qatādah disliked it, and they said: Leaving it is more beloved as well-being (ʿāfiyah), due to his saying ﷺ: «أعفوا اللحى» ("Let the beards grow thick"). The matter in this is near [to permissibility] as long as it does not reach the trimming of the beard and rounding it from the sides. For excessive length may disfigure the form and unleash the tongues of backbiters toward disparagement of it. So there is no harm in guarding against it with this intention.

Al-Nakhaʿī said: I marvel at an intelligent man with a long beard — how does he not take from his beard and make it between two beards? For moderation (al-tawassuṭ) in everything is good. For this reason it was said: The longer the beard, the more the intellect is tucked up (tashammara).

chapters.title_en: Section 65 — On the Discipline of the Soul and the Refinement of Character
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ض-ي (raḍiya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Contentment, satisfaction, approval; the state of being pleased with what is decreed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes the soul’s acquiescence to divine decree (riḍā bi’l-qaḍā’), a station of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — satisfaction of the heart; metaphorical (majāz) — acceptance of affliction as a form of worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with omitted copula (jumlah ismiyyah bi-ḥadhfi’l-khabar) — the heading implies a full predicate, e.g., “This is a section concerning…”
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the refinement of the soul (tahdhīb al-nafs) and the purification of the heart (taṣfiyat al-qalb) are the very essence of the religious sciences, and the goal of the path of the Hereafter. For the soul is a trust (amānah) from God, and its discipline is the key to felicity in both abodes. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: {«أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ»} — “Beware, in the body there is a lump of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Beware, it is the heart.” Thus, the heart is the sovereign, and the limbs are its subjects; the soul is the rider, and the body is its mount. Whoever disciplines his soul in this world, his journey to the Hereafter is eased; and whoever neglects it, his ruin is certain. So let the seeker of truth begin with self-knowledge (maʿrifat al-nafs), for he who knows his soul knows his Lord, as the wise have said: “He who knows himself, knows his Lord.” And the first step in this discipline is to sever the attachments of this world (qaṭʿ al-ʿalā’iq), and to empty the heart of all that is other than God, until it becomes a pure vessel for the light of divine knowledge (nūr al-maʿrifah). For the heart, when cleansed of blameworthy traits (akhlāq madhmūmah), is like a polished mirror that reflects the realities of the unseen (ḥaqā’iq al-ghayb). And this is the station of the prophets and the saints, and the ultimate goal of the sincere.

chapters.title_en: On the Ten Disapproved Practices Concerning the Beard and the Completion of the Book on the Secrets of Purification
chapters.arabic_text:
وفي اللحية عشر خصال مكروهة وبعضها أشد كراهة من بعض خضابها
بالسواد وتبييضها بالكبريت ونتفها ونتف الشيب منها والنقصان منها
والزيادة وتسريحها تصنعا لأجل الرياء وتركها شعثة إظهارا للزهد والنظر إلى
سوادها عجبا بالشباب وإلى بياضها تكبرا بعلو السن وخضابها بالحمرة والصفرة
من غير نية تشبها بالصالحين
أما الأول  وهو الخضاب بالسواد فهو منهي عنه لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير
شبابكم من تشبه بشيوخكم وشر شيوخكم من تشبه بشبابكم (1) والمراد بالتشبه
بالشيوخ في الوقار لا في تبييض الشعر ونهى عن الخضاب بالسواد (2) وقال هو
خضاب أهل النار (3) وفي لفظ آخر الخضاب بالسواد خضاب الكفار وتزوج رجل على
عهد عمر رضي الله عنه وكان يخضب بالسواد فنصل خضابه وظهرت شيبته فرفعه أهل
المرأة إلى عمر رضي الله عنه فرد نكاحه وأوجعه ضربا وقال غررت القوم
بالشباب ولبست عليهم شيبتك ويقال أول من خضب بالسواد فرعون لعنه الله وعن
ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يكون في آخر
الزمان قوم يخضبون بالسواد كحواصل الحمام لا يريحون رائحة الجنة (4)
الثاني الخضاب بالصفرة والحمرة وهو جائز تلبيسا للشيب على الكفار في
الغزو والجهاد فإن لم يكن على هذه النية بل للتشبه بأهل الدين فهو مذموم
وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفرة خضاب المسلمين والحمرة خضاب
المؤمنين (5) وكانوا يخضبون بالحناء للحمرة وبالخلوق والكتم للصفرة وخضب
بعض العلماء بالسواد لأجل الغزو وذلك لا بأس به إذا صحت النية ولم يكن فيه
هوى وشهوة
الثالث تبييضها بالكبريت استعجالا لإظهار علو السن توصلا إلى التوقير
وقبول الشهادة والتصديق بالرواية عن الشيوخ وترفعا عن الشباب وإظهارا لكثرة
العلم ظنا بأن كثرة الأيام تعطيه فضلا وهيهات فلا يزيد كبر السن للجاهل إلا
جهلا فالعلم ثمرة العقل وهي غريزة ولا يؤثر الشيب فيها ومن كانت غريزته
الحمق فطول المدة يؤكد حماقته وقد كان الشيوخ يقدمون الشباب PageV01P143
بالعلم
كان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقدم ابن عباس وهو حديث السن على أكابر
الصحابة ويسأله دونهم
وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما آتى الله عز وجل عبدا علما إلا شابا
والخير كله في الشباب ثم تلا قوله عز وجل {قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له
إبراهيم} وقوله تعالى {إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى} وقوله تعالى
{وآتيناه الحكم صبيا}  وكان أنس رضي الله عنه يقول قبض رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم وليس في رأسه ولحيته عشرون شعرة بيضاء فقيل له يا أبا حمزة فقد
أسن فقال لم يشنه الله بالشيب فقيل أهو شين فقال كلكم يكرهه (1) ويقال إن
يحيى بن أكثم ولي القضاء وهو ابن إحدى وعشرين سنة فقال له رجل في مجلسه
يريد أن يخجله بصغر سنه كم سن القاضي أيده الله فقال مثل سن عتاب بن أسيد
حين ولاه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إمارة مكة وقضاءها فأفحمه (2) وروي
عن مالك رحمه الله أنه قال قرأت في بعض الكتب لا تغرنكم اللحى فإن التيس له
لحية وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء إذا رأيت الرجل طويل القامة صغير الهامة عريض
اللحية فاقض عليه بالحمق ولو كان أمية بن عبد شمس وقال أيوب السختياني
أدركت الشيخ ابن ثمانين سنة يتبع الغلام يتعلم منه
وقال علي بن الحسين من سبق فيه العلم قبلك فهو إمامك فيه وإن كان أصغر
سنا منك وقيل لأبي عمرو بن العلاء أيحسن من الشيخ أن يتعلم من الصغير فقال
إن كان الجهل يقبح به فالتعلم يحسن به وقال يحيى بن معين لأحمد بن حنبل وقد
رآه يمشي خلف بغلة الشافعي يا أبا عبد الله تركت حديث سفيان بعلوه وتمشي
خلف بغلة هذا الفتى وتسمع منه فقال له أحمد لو عرفت لكنت تمشي من الجانب
الآخر إن علم سفيان إن فاتني بعلو أدركته بنزول وإن عقل هذا الشاب إن فاتني
لم أدركه بعلو ولا نزول
الرابع نتف بياضها استنكافا من الشيب وقد نهى عليه السلام عن نتف الشيب
وقال هو نور المؤمن (3) وهو في معنى الخضاب بالسواد وعلة الكراهية ما سبق
والشيب نور الله تعالى والرغبة عنه رغبة عن النور
الخامس نتفها أو نتف بعضها بحكم العبث والهوس وذلك مكروه ومشوه للخلقة
ونتف الفنيكين بدعة وهما جانبا العنفقة
شهد عند عمر بن عبد العزيز رجل كان ينتف فنيكيه فرد شهادته ورد عمر بن
الخطاب  رضي الله عنه وابن أبي ليلى قاضي المدينة شهادة من كان ينتف لحيته
وأما نتفها في أول النبات تشبها بالمرد فمن المنكرات الكبار فإن اللحية
زينة الرجال فإن لله سبحانه ملائكة يقسمون والذي زين بني آدم باللحى وهو من
تمام الخلق وبها يتميز الرجال عن النساء وقيل في غريب التأويل اللحية هي
المراد بقوله تعالى {يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء} قال أصحاب الأحنف بن قيس وددنا
أن نشتري للأحنف لحية ولو بعشرين ألفا وقال شريح القاضي وددت أن لي لحية
ولو بعشرة آلاف وكيف تكره اللحية وفيها تعظيم الرجل والنظر إليه بعين العلم
والوقار والرفع في المجالس وإقبال الوجوه إليه والتقديم على الجماعة ووقاية
العرض فإن من يشتم يعرض باللحية إن كان للمشتوم لحية وقد قيل إن أهل الجنة
مرد إلا هارون أخا موسى صلى الله عليهما وسلم فإن له لحية إلى سرته تخصيصا
له وتفضيلا
السادس تقصيصها كالتعبية طاقة على طاقة PageV01P144
للتزين للنساء والتصنع قال كعب يكون في آخر الزمان أقوام يقصون لحاهم
كذنب الحمامة ويعرقبون نعالهم كالمناجل أولئك لا خلاق لهم
السابع الزيادة فيها وهو أن يزيد في شعر العارضين من الصدغين وهو من شعر
الرأس حتى يجاوز عظم اللحى وينتهي إلى نصف الخد وذلك يباين هيئة أهل الصلاح
الثامن تسريحها لأجل الناس قال بشر في اللحية شركان تسريحها لأجل الناس
وتركها متفتلة لإظهار الزهد
التاسع والعاشر النظر في سوادها أو في بياضها بعين العجب وذلك مذموم في
جميع أجزاء البدن بل في جميع الأخلاق والأفعال على ما سيأتي بيانه فهذا ما
أردنا أن نذكره من أنواع التزين والنظافة وقد حصل من ثلاثة أحاديث من سنن
الجسد اثنتا عشرة خصلة خمس منها في الرأس وهي فرق شعر الرأس (1) والمضمضة
والاستنشاق (2) وقص الشارب والسواك وثلاثة في اليد والرجل وهي القلم وغسل
البراجم وتنظيف الرواجب (3) وأربعة في الجسد وهي نتف الإبط والاستحداد
والختان والاستنجاء بالماء فقد وردت الأخبار بمجموع ذلك وإذا كان غرض هذا
الكتاب التعرض للطهارة الظاهرة دون الباطنة  فلنتقصر على هذا وليتحقق أن
فضلات الباطن وأوساخه التي يجب التنظيف منها أكثر من أن تحصى وسيأتي
تفصيلها في ربع المهلكات مع تعريف الطرق في إزالتها وتطهير القلب منها إن
شاء الله عز وجل
تم كتاب أسرار الطهارة بحمد الله تعالى وعونه
ويتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب أسرار الصلاة والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله
على سيدنا محمد وعلى كل عبد مصطفى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ض-ب (kha-ḍa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dye, color, or stain; specifically the application of coloring agents to hair or cloth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The outward alteration of appearance; in the religious context, it pertains to the concealment or alteration of natural signs of age, carrying a moral weight regarding intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to the physical act of dyeing; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the "dyeing" of faith or character, as in "ṣibghat Allāh" (the dye of God).
- Root: ش-ي-ب (shī-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Whiteness of hair; the onset of old age; a sign of venerability but also of decline.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological lexicon, whiteness of hair is described as "nūr" (light) — a divine gift and mark of dignity, not a blemish.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical greying; metaphorical for the "whitening" of the soul through wisdom and piety.
- Root: ن-ت-ف (n-t-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pluck, pull out, or extract hair from the root.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): An act of altering the created form (taghyīr khalq Allāh); prohibited when done out of vanity or disdain for divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical act; metaphorical for the removal of dignity or the rejection of divine will.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditionality (al-Sharṭ) — The permissibility or prohibition of an act is often conditioned by the intention (niyyah) of the agent, as seen in the distinction between dyeing for jihad versus dyeing for vanity. This is parsed through the conditional particles (in/idhā) that govern the apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Concerning the beard, there are ten disapproved practices, and some are more severely disapproved than others: dyeing it black, whitening it with sulfur, plucking it, plucking the white hairs from it, reducing it, increasing it, combing it with affectation for the sake of ostentation, leaving it disheveled to display asceticism, gazing at its blackness with vanity over youth, and gazing at its whiteness with pride over advanced age, and dyeing it with red or yellow without the intention of resembling the righteous.

As for the first — namely, dyeing it black — it is prohibited, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «خير شبابكم من تشبه بشيوخكم وشر شيوخكم من تشبه بشبابكم» ("The best of your youth is he who resembles your elders, and the worst of your elders is he who resembles your youth.") The intended meaning of resembling the elders is in dignity (waqār), not in the whitening of hair. And he prohibited dyeing with black, saying: "It is the dye of the people of the Fire." In another wording: "Dyeing with black is the dye of the disbelievers." A man married during the era of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) while dyeing his hair black, but his dye faded and his grey hair appeared. The woman's family brought him to ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), who annulled his marriage, struck him painfully, and said: "You deceived the people with youth and concealed your greyness from them." It is said that the first to dye with black was Pharaoh — may Allah curse him. And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "There will come at the end of time a people who dye with black like the crops of pigeons; they will not smell the fragrance of Paradise."

The second is dyeing with yellow and red, which is permissible as a disguise of grey hair against the disbelievers during raids and jihad. But if it is not with this intention, rather for the sake of resembling the people of religion, then it is blameworthy. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Yellow is the dye of the Muslims, and red is the dye of the believers." They used to dye with henna for redness and with khilūq and katm for yellowness. Some scholars dyed with black for the sake of raids, and there is no harm in that if the intention is sound and there is no caprice or lust in it.

The third is whitening it with sulfur, hastening to display advanced age as a means to attain reverence, acceptance of testimony, and credence in narration from the elders, while elevating oneself above youth and displaying an abundance of knowledge, supposing that the multitude of days bestows virtue. How far from the truth! For old age increases the ignorant only in ignorance. Knowledge is the fruit of the intellect, which is an innate disposition (gharīzah), and grey hair has no effect upon it. Whoever's innate disposition is foolishness, the length of time only reinforces his foolishness. The elders used to give precedence to the youth in knowledge. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) used to give precedence to Ibn ʿAbbās, despite his young age, over the senior Companions, and would ask him rather than them. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not given any servant knowledge except while he is young, and all good is in youth." Then he recited the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم} ("They said: We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham") and His saying: {إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى} ("Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance") and His saying: {وآتيناه الحكم صبيا} ("And We gave him judgment while a child"). Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was taken, and there were not twenty white hairs on his head and beard." It was said to him: "O Abā Ḥamzah, he has aged." He said: "Allah did not disfigure him with grey hair." It was said: "Is it a disfigurement?" He said: "All of you dislike it." It is said that Yaḥyā ibn Aktham was appointed to the judiciary at the age of twenty-one. A man in his assembly said, intending to shame him for his young age: "How old is the judge, may Allah support him?" He replied: "The age of ʿAttāb ibn Asīd when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) appointed him to the governorship and judiciary of Mecca." Thus he silenced him. It is narrated from Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: "I read in some books: Let not the beards deceive you, for the he-goat has a beard." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "If you see a man tall of stature, small of head, and broad of beard, then judge him to be foolish, even if he were Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams." Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī said: "I reached an elder of eighty years who would follow a young boy to learn from him." ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: "Whoever precedes you in knowledge is your imam in it, even if he is younger in age than you." It was said to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "Is it proper for an elder to learn from a younger one?" He said: "If ignorance is disgraceful for him, then learning is honorable for him." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿīn said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, upon seeing him walking behind the mule of al-Shāfiʿī: "O Abā ʿAbdillāh, you have abandoned the elevated chain of Sufyān's hadith and walk behind the mule of this youth, listening to him?" Aḥmad said to him: "If you knew, you would walk on the other side. If the knowledge of Sufyān is lost to me in its elevation, I attain it in its descent; but if the intellect of this youth is lost to me, I could not attain it by elevation or descent."

The fourth is plucking the white hairs out of disdain for greyness. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prohibited the plucking of grey hair, saying: "It is the light of the believer." It is in the same category as dyeing with black, and the cause of disapproval is what has preceded. Grey hair is the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and aversion to it is aversion to the light.

The fifth is plucking it, or plucking part of it, out of frivolity and folly. This is disapproved and disfigures the natural form. Plucking the two side-tufts (al-finṭīkayn) — which are the two sides of the mustache — is an innovation (bidʿah). A man who plucked his two side-tufts testified before ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he rejected his testimony. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn Abī Laylā, the judge of Medina, rejected the testimony of one who plucked his beard. As for plucking it at the beginning of its growth to resemble beardless youths, that is among the grave abominations. For the beard is the adornment of men. Allah, Glorified be He, has angels who divide and distribute, and He who adorned the sons of Adam with beards — it is part of the perfection of creation, and by it men are distinguished from women. It was said in the interpretation of the unusual (gharīb al-taʾwīl): The beard is what is meant by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء} ("He increases in creation what He wills"). The companions of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said: "We wish we could buy a beard for al-Aḥnaf, even for twenty thousand." Shurayḥ the judge said: "I wish I had a beard, even for ten thousand." How could the beard be disliked, when in it lies the dignity of a man, the gazing upon him with the eye of knowledge and gravity, his elevation in assemblies, the turning of faces toward him, his precedence over the congregation, and the protection of his honor? For whoever is insulted, the insulter alludes to the beard if the insulted one has a beard. It has been said that the people of Paradise are beardless youths, except Hārūn, the brother of Moses (peace be upon them both), for he has a beard reaching to his navel, as a distinction and honor for him.

The sixth is trimming it in layers, one strand upon another, like the weaving of cloth, for the adornment of women and affectation. Kaʿb said: "There will be at the end of time a people who trim their beards like the tail of a pigeon and cut their sandals like sickles; those have no share (khalāq) in the Hereafter."

The seventh is increasing it, namely, adding to the hair of the cheeks from the temples — which is hair of the head — until it surpasses the jawbone and reaches the middle of the cheek. This deviates from the appearance of the people of righteousness.

The eighth is combing it for the sake of people. Bishr said: "In the beard there are two partners: combing it for the sake of people, and leaving it tangled to display asceticism."

The ninth and tenth are gazing at its blackness or its whiteness with the eye of vanity. This is blameworthy in all parts of the body, indeed in all character traits and actions, as will be explained later.

This, then, is what we intended to mention concerning the types of adornment and cleanliness. From three hadiths, there are twelve practices of the sunnah of the body: five pertain to the head — parting the hair of the head, rinsing the mouth, snuffing water into the nose, trimming the mustache, and using the toothstick (siwāk); three pertain to the hand and foot — trimming the nails, washing the knuckles, and cleaning the finger joints; and four pertain to the body — plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleansing with water after relieving oneself. The reports have come concerning all of this collectively. And since the purpose of this book is to address the outward purification (al-ṭahārah al-ẓāhirah) rather than the inward, let us confine ourselves to this. Let it be known that the inward impurities and filths from which one must cleanse are too numerous to count, and their detailed exposition will come in the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt), along with the definition of the ways to remove them and purify the heart from them, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

The Book of the Secrets of Purification is completed, by the praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His assistance. It will be followed, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, by the Book of the Secrets of Prayer. And praise be to Allah alone, and blessings upon our master Muḥammad and upon every chosen servant.

### || كتاب أسرار الصلاة ومهماتها

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي غمر العباد بلطائفه وعمر قلوبهم بأنوار الدين ووظائفه
التي تنزل عن عرش الجلال إلى السماء الدنيا من درجات الرحمة إحدى عواطفه
فارق الملوك مع التفرد بالجلال والكبرياء بترغيب الخلق في السؤال والدعاء
فقال هل من داع فأستجيب له وهل من مستغفر فأغفر له وباين السلاطين بفتح
الباب ورفع الحجاب فرخص للعباد في المناجاة بالصلوات كيفما تقلبت بهم
الحالات في الجماعات والخلوات ولم يقتصر على الرخصة بل تلطف بالترغيب
والدعوة وغيره من ضعفاء الملوك لا يسمح بالخلوة إلا بعد تقديم الهدية
والرشوة فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأقوى سلطانه وأتم لطفه وأعم إحسانه والصلاة
على محمد نبيه المصطفى ووليه المجتبى وعلى آله وأصحابه مفاتيح الهدى
ومصابيح الدجى وسلم تسليما
أما بعد فإن الصلاة عماد الدين وعصام اليقين ورأس القربات وغرة الطاعات
وقد استقصينا في فن الفقه في بسيط المذهب ووسيطه ووجيزه أصولها وفروعها
صارفين جمام العناية إلى تفاريعها النادرة
ووقائعها الشاذة لتكون خزانة للمفتي منها يستمد ومعولا له إليها يفزع
ويرجع
ونحن الآن PageV01P145
في هذا الكتاب نقتصر على ما لا بد للمريد منه من أعمالها الظاهرة
وأسرارها الباطنة وكاشفون من دقائق معانيها الخفية في معاني الخشوع
والإخلاص والنية ما لم تجر العادة بذكره في فن الفقه ومرتبون الكتاب على
سبعة أبواب
الباب الأول في فضائل الصلاة
الباب الثاني في تفضيل الأعمال الظاهرة من الصلاة
الباب الثالث في تفضيل الأعمال الباطنة منها
الباب الرابع في الإمامة والقدوة
الباب الخامس في صلاة الجمعة وأدابها
الباب السادس في مسائل متفرقة تعم بها  البلوى يحتاج المريد إلى معرفتها
الباب السابع في التطوعات وغيرها

### ||| الباب الأول في فضائل الصلاة السجود والجماعة والأذان وغيرها

### |||| فضيلة الأذان

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة يوم القيامة على كثيب من مسك أسود لا
يهولهم حساب ولا ينالهم فزع حتى يفرغ مما بين الناس رجل قرأ القرآن ابتغاء
وجه الله عز وجل وأم بقوم وهم به راضون ورجل أذن في مسجد ودعا إلى الله عز
وجل ابتغاء وجه الله ورجل ابتلي بالرزق في الدنيا فلم يشغله ذلك عن عمل
الآخرة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسمع نداء المؤذن جن ولا إنس ولا
شيء إلا شهد له يوم القيامة (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يد الرحمن على رأس
المؤذن حتى يفرغ من أذانه (3) وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل ومن أحسن قولا ممن
دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا نزلت في المؤذنين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا
سمعتم النداء فقولوا مثل ما يقول المؤذن (4) وذلك مستحب إلا في الحيعلتين
فإنه يقول فيهما لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله وفي قوله قد قامت الصلاة أقامها
الله وأدامها ما دامت السموات والأرض وفي التثويب صدقت وبررت ونصحت وعند
الفراغ يقول اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة والصلاة القائمة آت محمدا الوسيلة
والفضيلة والدرجة الرفيعة وابعثه المقام المحمود الذي وعدته إنك لا تخلف
الميعاد
وقال سعيد بن المسيب من صلى بأرض فلاة صلى عن يمينه ملك وعن شماله ملك
فإن أذن وأقام صلى وراءه أمثال الجبال من الملائكة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ذ-ن (Adh-Dhāl-Nūn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to listen, to hear, to announce" — the mu'adhdhin (caller) makes the announcement that summons ears to heed; also carries the sense of "permission" (idhn), as the call grants entry into divine service.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, adhān is the ritual proclamation that symbolizes the invitation (daʿwah) to God's presence, aligning with the Quranic verse {«وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ»} — the caller is the paradigm of one who invites to God with excellence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally (ḥaqīqah), adhān is the audible call; metaphorically (majāz), it is the spiritual summons that pierces the veil (ḥijāb) between the servant and the Lord, as the hadith "the Hand of the Merciful is over the head of the mu'adhdhin" indicates divine proximity, not corporeal extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In the phrase "رجل قرأ القرآن... ورجل أذن... ورجل ابتلي" the repetition of "رجل" (a man) functions as explanatory apposition, each clause specifying a distinct category of the saved, requiring the translator to preserve the tripartite structure without conflation.
chapters.translation:
I say: In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, who has inundated His servants with His subtle graces and has filled their hearts with the lights of religion and its obligations — lights that descend from the Throne of Majesty to the lowest heaven, one of the outpourings of His mercy being the degrees of His compassion. He has distinguished Himself from kings, despite His unique possession of majesty and grandeur, by encouraging His creatures to ask and to supplicate, saying: "Is there any caller that I may respond to him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him?" And He has set Himself apart from sovereigns by opening the door and raising the veil, granting His servants the license of intimate communion (munājāh) through the prayers, however their states may fluctuate, whether in congregations or in solitude. Nor did He stop at mere permission, but He gently urged and invited them — whereas the weak among earthly kings do not permit a private audience except after the presentation of gifts and bribes. Glory be to Him! How immense is His affair, how mighty His dominion, how complete His subtlety, how universal His beneficence! And blessings and peace be upon Muhammad, His chosen Prophet and elect Beloved, and upon his Family and Companions, the keys of guidance and the lamps of darkness.

To proceed: Know that the prayer (ṣalāh) is the pillar of religion, the bond of certainty, the foremost of acts of drawing near, and the brightest of acts of obedience. We have already exhausted, in the discipline of jurisprudence (fiqh), in the expansive, the intermediate, and the abridged treatments of the school, its principles and its branches, devoting the full vigor of our attention to its rare subdivisions and anomalous cases, so that it might serve as a treasury from which the mufti draws, and a support to which he repairs and returns. But now, in this present book, we confine ourselves to what is indispensable for the spiritual seeker (murīd) — namely, its outward acts and its inward secrets — and we shall unveil, from the subtle meanings hidden within the realities of humility (khushūʿ), sincerity (ikhlāṣ), and intention (niyyah), that which custom has not been wont to mention in the discipline of jurisprudence. We have arranged the book into seven chapters:

Chapter One: On the Virtues of the Prayer.
Chapter Two: On the Excellence of the Outward Acts of the Prayer.
Chapter Three: On the Excellence of the Inward Acts Thereof.
Chapter Four: On the Imamate and Following the Leader.
Chapter Five: On the Friday Prayer and Its Etiquettes.
Chapter Six: On Miscellaneous Questions of General Affliction (balwā) that the Seeker Needs to Know.
Chapter Seven: On Supererogatory Prayers and Other Matters.

### Chapter One: On the Virtues of the Prayer, the Prostration, the Congregation, the Call to Prayer, and Other Matters

### The Virtue of the Call to Prayer (Adhān)

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Three persons on the Day of Resurrection shall be upon a mound of black musk, neither will the reckoning terrify them nor will panic seize them until God finishes judging between mankind: a man who recited the Quran seeking the Face of God, Mighty and Majestic, and led a people who were well-pleased with him; a man who called the adhān in a mosque and invited to God, Mighty and Majestic, seeking the Face of God; and a man who was tried with provision in this world, yet it did not distract him from the work of the Hereafter." And he, peace be upon him, said: "No jinn, no human, and no thing hears the voice of the mu'adhdhin except that it bears witness for him on the Day of Resurrection." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The Hand of the Merciful is over the head of the mu'adhdhin until he finishes his call." And it was said concerning the interpretation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا»} ("And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and works righteousness") — that it was revealed concerning the mu'adhdhins. And he, peace be upon him, said: "When you hear the call, say the like of what the mu'adhdhin says." That is recommended (mustaḥabb), except in the two ḥayʿalahs (the phrases "Come to prayer, come to success"), for therein one says: "There is no might and no power except with God." And in his saying "The prayer has been established" (qad qāmat al-ṣalāh), one says: "May God establish it and perpetuate it as long as the heavens and the earth endure." And in the tathwīb (the second call in the dawn prayer: "Prayer is better than sleep"), one says: "You have spoken truly, and done well, and advised sincerely." And upon finishing, one says: "O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means (al-wasīlah), the excellence (al-faḍīlah), and the lofty rank, and raise him to the praiseworthy station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) which You have promised him — verily, You do not break the promise."

And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "Whoever prays in an open, desolate land, a king prays at his right and a king at his left; and if he calls the adhān and establishes the prayer, angels like mountains pray behind him."

### |||| فضيلة المكتوبة

قال الله تعالى إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على العباد فمن جاء بهن ولم يضيع منهن شيئا
استخفافا بحقهن كان له عند الله عهد أن يدخله الجنة ومن لم يأت بهن فليس له
عند الله عهد إن شاء عذبه وإن شاء أدخله الجنة (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
مثل الصلوات الخمس كمثل نهر عذب غمر بباب أحدكم يقتحم فيه كل يوم خمس  مرات
فما ترون ذلك يبقي من درنه قالوا لا شيء قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
PageV01P146
فإن الصلوات الخمس تذهب الذنوب كما يذهب الماء الدرن (1) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن الصلوات كفارة لما بينهن ما اجتنبت الكبائر (2) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم بيننا وبين المنافقين شهود العتمة والصبح لا يستطيعونهما (3)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لقي الله وهو مضيع للصلاة لم يعبأ الله بشيء من
حسناته (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عماد الدين فمن تركها فقد هدم
الدين (5) وسئل صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الأعمال أفضل فقال الصلاة لمواقيتها
(6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من حافظ على الخمس بإكمال طهورها ومواقيتها
كانت له نورا وبرهانا يوم القيامة ومن ضيعها حشر مع فرعون وهامان (7) وقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم مفتاح الجنة الصلاة (8) وقال ما افترض الله على خلقه
بعد التوحيد أحب إليه من الصلاة ولو كان شيء أحب إليه منها لتعبد به
ملائكته فمنهم راكع ومنهم ساجد ومنهم قائم وقاعد (9) وقال النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم من ترك صلاة متعمدا فقد كفر (10) أي قارب أن ينخلع عن الإيمان
بانحلال عروته وسقوط عماده كما يقال لمن قارب البلدة إنه بلغها ودخلها
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من ترك صلاة متعمدا فقد برىء من ذمة محمد عليه
السلام (11) وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه من توضأ فأحسن وضوءه ثم خرج عامدا
إلى الصلاة فإنه في صلاة ما كان يعمد إلى الصلاة وأنه يكتب له بإحدى خطوتيه
حسنة وتمحى عنه بالأخرى سيئة فإذا سمع أحدكم الإقامة فلا ينبغي له أن يتأخر
فإن أعظمكم أجرا أبعدكم دارا قالوا لم يا أبا هريرة قال من أجل كثرة الخطا
ويروى إن أول ما ينظر فيه من عمل العبد يوم القيامة الصلاة (12) فإن وجدت
تامة قبلت منه وسائر عمله وإن وجدت ناقصة ردت عليه وسائر عمله وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة مر أهلك بالصلاة فإن الله يأتيك بالرزق من حيث
لا تحتسب (13) وقال  بعض العلماء مثل المصلي مثل التاجر الذي لا يحصل له
الربح حتى يخلص له رأس المال وكذلك المصلي لا تقبل له نافلة حتى يؤدي
الفريضة
وكان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يقول إذا حضرت الصلاة قوموا إلى ناركم التي
أوقدتموها فأطفئوها

### |||| فضيلة إتمام الأركان

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الصلاة المكتوبة كمثل الميزان من أوفى استوفى
(14) وقال يزيد الرقاشي كانت PageV01P147
صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مستوية كأنها موزونة (1) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم إن الرجلين من أمتي ليقومان إلى الصلاة وركوعهما وسجودهما
واحد وإن ما بين صلاتيهما ما بين السماء والأرض (2) وأشار إلى الخشوع وقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينظر الله يوم القيامة إلى العبد لا يقيم صلبه بين
ركوعه وسجوده (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أما يخاف الذي يحول وجهه في
الصلاة أن يحول الله وجهه وجه حمار (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى
صلاة لوقتها وأسبغ وضوءها وأتم ركوعها وسجودها وخشوعها عرجت وهي بيضاء
مسفرة تقول حفظك الله كما حفظتني ومن صلى لغير وقتها ولم يسبغ وضوءها ولم
يتم ركوعها ولا سجودها ولا خشوعها عرجت وهي سوداء مظلمة تقول ضيعك الله كما
ضيعتني حتى إذا كانت حيث شاء الله لفت كما يلف الثوب الخلق فيضرب بها وجهه
(5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أسوأ الناس سرقة الذي يسرق من صلاته (6) وقال
ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه وسلمان رضي الله عنه الصلاة مكيال فمن أوفى استوفى
ومن طفف فقد علم ما قال الله في المطففين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ت-ب (kataba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To write, inscribe, ordain, or decree; a written obligation (kitāb) that is fixed and binding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine prescription (kitāb) as an eternal decree of obligation (farḍ) upon the believers, connoting determinacy and covenant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of writing; here metaphorical (majāz) for the fixed imposition of a duty with appointed times.
