  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, farḍ denotes that which the Lawgiver (al-Shāriʿ) has decisively required, binding upon the accountable (mukallaf) — its neglect incurs punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a determined obligation; metaphorical (majāz) — any act whose omission is censured, though not necessarily punishable.
- Root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — to pave, to establish a path or practice; a normative way (sunnah) traced back to the Prophet ﷺ.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, sunnah refers to the Prophet’s established practice (sīrah) — recommended (mandūb) but not obligatory; its doer is rewarded, its abandoner is not punished.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a trodden path; metaphorical — the prophetic model as a secondary source of law, distinct from farḍ in degree of binding force.
- Sībawayh Rule: **Tamyīz (Specification)** — The construction «تمييز الفرائض والسنن» employs the genitive (muḍāf ilayh) to specify the act of distinguishing (tamyīz), where the two nouns are coordinated (maʿṭūf) under a single verbal noun, indicating a categorical division between two legal classes.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the obligations (farāʾiḍ) and the sunnahs (sunan) are distinguished by the degree of their binding force in the Sacred Law. The obligation (farīḍah) is that which the Lawgiver has decisively commanded, such that its performance is required and its abandonment is punishable. The sunnah is that which the Prophet ﷺ established as a continuous practice, such that its performance is rewarded and its abandonment is not punished, though it is beloved to follow. This distinction is the foundation upon which the jurists (fuqahāʾ) build their rulings, and the worshipper must discern between them so that he does not elevate the sunnah to the rank of the obligation, nor degrade the obligation to the rank of the sunnah.

chapters.title_en: The Comprehensive Enumeration of the Obligations, Sunnas, and Proprieties of Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
جملة ما ذكر يشتمل على فرائض وسنن وآداب وهيئات مما ينبغي لمريد طريق
الآخرة أن يراعي جميعها
فالفرض من جملتها اثنتا عشرة خصلة النية والتكبير والقيام والفاتحة
والانحناء في الركوع إلى أن تنال راحتاه ركبتيه مع الطمأنينة والاعتدال عنه
قائما والسجود مع الطمأنينة ولا يجب وضع اليدين والاعتدال عنه قاعدا
والجلوس للتشهد الأخير والتشهد الأخير والصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم والسلام الأول
فأما نية الخروج فلا تجب وما عدا هذا فليس بواجب بل هي سنن وهيئات فيها
وفي الفرائض أما السنن فمن الأفعال أربعة رفع اليدين في تكبيرة الإحرام
وعند الهوي إلى الركوع وعند الارتفاع إلى القيام والجلسة للتشهد الأول
فأما ما ذكرناه من كيفية PageV01P157
نشر الأصابع وحد رفعها فهي هيئات تابعة لهذه السنة والتورك والافتراش
هيئات تابعة للجلسة والإطراق وترك الالتفات هيئات للقيام وتحسين صورته
وجلسة الاستراحة لم نعدها من أصول السنة في الأفعال لأنها كالتحسين لهيئة
الارتفاع من السجود إلى القيام لأنها ليست مقصودة في نفسها ولذلك لم تفرد
بذكر
وأما السنن من الأذكار فدعاء الاستفتاح ثم التعوذ ثم قوله آمين فإنه سنة
مؤكدة ثم قراءة السورة ثم تكبيرات الانتقالات ثم الذكر في الركوع والسجود
والاعتدال عنهما ثم التشهد الأول والصلاة فيه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ثم الدعاء في آخر التشهد الأخير ثم التسليمة الثانية وإن جمعناها في اسم
السنة فلها درجات متفاوتة إذ تجبر أربعة منها بسجود السهو
وأما من الأفعال فواحدة وهي الجلسة الأولى للتشهد الأول فإنها مؤثرة في
ترتيب نظم  الصلاة في أعين الناظرين حتى يعرف بها أنها رباعية أم لا بخلاف
رفع اليدين فإنه لا يؤثر في تغيير النظم فعبر عن ذلك بالبعض
وقيل الأبعاض تجبر بالسجود وأما الأذكار فكلها لا تقتضي سجود السهو إلا
ثلاثة القنوت والتشهد الأول والصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه
بخلاف تكبيرات الانتقالات وأذكار الركوع والسجود والاعتدال عنهما لأن
الركوع والسجود في صورتهما مخالفان للعادة ويحصل بهما معنى العبادة مع
السكوت عن الأذكار وعن تكبيرات الانتقالات فعدم تلك الأذكار لا تغير صورة
العبادة
وأما الجلسة للتشهد الأول ففعل معتاد وما زيدت إلا للتشهد فتركها ظاهر
التأثير
وأما دعاء الاستفتاح والسورة فتركهما لا يؤثر مع أن القيام صار معمورا
بالفاتحة ومميزا عن العادة بها وكذلك الدعاء في التشهد الأخير والقنوت أبعد
ما يجبر بالسجود ولكن شرع مد الاعتدال في الصبح لأجله فكان كمد جلسة
الاستراحة إذ صارت بالمد مع التشهد جلسة للتشهد الأول
فبقي هذا قياما ممدودا معتادا ليس فيه ذكر واجب وفي الممدود احتراز عن
غير الصبح وفي خلوه عن ذكر واجب احتراز عن أصل القيام في الصلاة
فإن قلت تمييز السنن عن الفرائض معقول إذ تفوت الصحة بفوت الفرض دون
السنة ويتوجه العقاب به دونها فأما تمييز سنة عن سنة والكل مأمور به على
سبيل الاستحباب ولا عقاب في ترك الكل والثواب موجود على الكل فما معناه
فاعلم أن اشتراكهما في الثواب والعقاب والاستحباب لا يرفع تفاوتهما ولنكشف
ذلك لك بمثال وهو أن الإنسان لا يكون إنسانا موجودا كاملا إلا بمعنى باطن
وأعضاء ظاهرة فالمعنى الباطن هو الحياة والروح والظاهر أجسام أعضائه
ثم بعض تلك الأعضاء ينعدم الإنسان بعدمها كالقلب والكبد والدماغ وكل عضو
تفوت الحياة بفواته وبعضها لا تفوت بها الحياة ولكن يفوت بها مقاصد الحياة
كالعين واليد والرجل واللسان وبعضها لا يفوت بها الحياة ولا مقاصدها ولكن
يفوت بها الحسن كالحاجبين واللحية والأهداب وحسن اللون وبعضها لا يفوت بها
أصل الجمال ولكن كماله كاستقواس الحاجبين وسواد شعر اللحية والأهداب  وتناسب
خلقة الأعضاء وامتزاج الحمرة بالبياض في اللون فهذه درجات متفاوتة فكذلك
العبادة صورة صورها الشرع وتعبدنا باكتسابها فروحها وحياتها الباطنة الخشوع
والنية وحضور القلب والإخلاص كما سيأتي ونحن الآن في أجزائها الظاهرة
فالركوع والسجود والقيام وسائر الأركان تجري منها مجرى القلب والرأس والكبد
إذ يفوت وجود الصلاة بفواتها
والسنن التي ذكرناها من رفع اليدين ودعاء الاستفتاح والتشهد الأول تجري
منها مجرى اليدين والعينين والرجلين ولا تفوت الصحة بفواتها كما لا تفوت
الحياة بفوات هذه الأعضاء ولكن يصير الشخص بسبب فواتها مشوه الخلقة مذموما
غير مرغوب فيه فكذلك من اقتصر على أقل ما يجزي من الصلاة كان كمن أهدى إلى
ملك من الملوك عبدا حيا مقطوع الأطراف
وأما الهيئات وهي ما وراء السنن فتجري مجرى أسباب الحسن من الحاجبين
واللحية والأهداب
PageV01P158
وحسن اللون وأما وظائف الأذكار في تلك السنن فهي مكملات للحسن كاستقواس
الحاجبين واستدارة اللحية وغيرهما
فالصلاة عندك قربة وتحفة تتقرب بها إلى حضرة ملك الملوك كوصيفة يهديها
طالب القربة من السلاطين إليهم وهذه التحفة تعرض على الله عز وجل
ثم ترد عليك يوم العرض الأكبر فإليك الخيرة في تحسين صورتها وتقبيحها
فإن أحسنت فلنفسك وإن أسأت فعليها
ولا ينبغي أن يكون حظك من ممارسة الفقه أن يتميز لك السنة عن الفرض فلا
يعلق بفهمك من أوصاف السنة إلا أنه يجوز تركها فتتركها فإن ذلك يضاهي قول
الطبيب إن فقء العين لا يبطل وجود الإنسان ولكن يخرجه عن أن يصدق رجاء
المتقرب في قبول السلطان إذا أخرجه في معرض الهدية فهكذا ينبغي أن تفهم
مراتب السنن والهيئات والآداب فكل صلاة لم يتم الإنسان ركوعها وسجودها فهي
الخصم الأول على صاحبها تقول ضيعك الله كما ضيعتني
فطالع الأخبار التي أوردناها في كمال أركان الصلاة ليظهر لك وقعها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ر-ض (farada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make an incision, to determine, to render obligatory by divine decree
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): That which is binding upon the servant by explicit divine command, the neglect of which nullifies the act's validity
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of cutting/marking; metaphorically, that which is firmly fixed as a religious duty
- Root: س-ن-ن (sanna)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pave a path, to establish a normative practice, to set a precedent
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Prophet's established way (sunnah) — that which is recommended but not obligatory, whose neglect does not invalidate but diminishes perfection
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a trodden path; metaphorical: the prophetic model as a clear way to be followed
- Root: ه-ي-ء (hay'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Form, state, condition, configuration of a thing
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The outward shape and arrangement of the body in worship — that which pertains to beauty and decorum rather than essential validity
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the visible form; metaphorical: the aesthetic refinement of worship's outward appearance
- Root: ع-م-د (ʿamada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To intend, to purpose, to lean upon a support
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The pillars (arkān) upon which the structure of prayer rests — their absence destroys the edifice entirely
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a column supporting a roof; metaphorical: the essential supports of an act of worship
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Gradation (al-tafāwut) — the use of comparative degrees (tafāḍul) to express hierarchical distinctions among items sharing a common category, as in the varying ranks of sunnas and the analogy of bodily members
chapters.translation:
I say: The totality of what has been mentioned comprises obligations (farāʾiḍ), sunnas (sunan), proprieties (ādāb), and postures (hayʾāt) which the seeker of the path to the Hereafter ought to observe in their entirety.

The obligatory (farḍ) among them are twelve traits: the intention (niyyah), the takbīr (saying "Allāhu akbar"), the standing (qiyām), the Fātiḥah, the bowing in rukūʿ until his palms reach his knees — along with tranquility (ṭumaʾnīnah) — and the rising from it to a standing position, the prostration (sujūd) with tranquility — though placing the hands [on the ground] is not obligatory — and the rising from it to a sitting position, the sitting for the final tashahhud, the final tashahhud itself, the prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ, and the first salutation (salām). As for the intention of exiting [the prayer], it is not obligatory. Whatever is beyond this is not obligatory; rather, they are sunnas and postures within the prayer and within the obligations.

As for the sunnas, they are of two kinds: those pertaining to actions and those pertaining to invocations (adhkār). Among the actions, there are four: raising the hands in the takbīr of consecration (takbīrat al-iḥrām), upon bowing into rukūʿ, upon rising to the standing position, and the sitting for the first tashahhud. As for what we mentioned regarding the manner of spreading the fingers and the limit of their raising — these are postures (hayʾāt) subordinate to this sunnah. The tawarruk (sitting on the left hip) and the iftirāsh (sitting on the left foot) are postures subordinate to the sitting. The lowering of the gaze and refraining from looking around are postures for the standing, beautifying its form. The sitting of rest (jalsat al-istirāḥah) we have not counted among the foundational sunnas in actions, for it is but an embellishment of the posture of rising from prostration to standing, since it is not intended in itself — and for this reason it was not singled out for mention.

As for the sunnas among the invocations: the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ), then the taʿawwudh (seeking refuge in God), then saying "Āmīn" — for it is an emphatic sunnah — then the recitation of the additional sūrah, then the takbīrs of transition (takbīrāt al-intiqālāt), then the remembrance in rukūʿ and sujūd and in the rising from both, then the first tashahhud and the prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ within it, then the supplication at the end of the final tashahhud, then the second salutation. Even if we gather all these under the name of "sunnah," they possess varying degrees, for four of them are compensated for by the prostrations of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw).

As for the actions [that are compensated], there is but one: the first sitting for the first tashahhud — for it affects the ordering of the prayer's structure in the eyes of the beholders, such that one knows by it whether the prayer is four-unit (rubāʿiyyah) or not — unlike the raising of the hands, which does not affect the change of structure. Thus it was expressed as "a part" (baʿḍ). And it was said: the parts (abʿāḍ) are compensated by prostration. As for the invocations, none of them necessitate the prostrations of forgetfulness except three: the qunūt, the first tashahhud, and the prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ within it — unlike the takbīrs of transition and the remembrances of rukūʿ, sujūd, and the rising from both, because rukūʿ and sujūd in their very forms are contrary to customary [postures], and the meaning of worship is achieved through them even with silence from the invocations and from the takbīrs of transition. Thus, the absence of those invocations does not alter the form of worship.

As for the sitting for the first tashahhud, it is a customary action, and it was only added for the sake of the tashahhud — so its omission has a manifest effect.

As for the opening supplication and the additional sūrah, their omission has no effect, given that the standing is already filled with the Fātiḥah and distinguished from the customary by it. Likewise, the supplication in the final tashahhud and the qunūt are the furthest from being compensated by prostration. However, the prolongation (madd) of the standing in the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ) was legislated for its sake, so it became like the prolongation of the sitting of rest — for by the prolongation along with the tashahhud, it became a sitting for the first tashahhud. Thus, this [standing in ṣubḥ] remains a prolonged customary standing in which there is no obligatory remembrance. In the phrase "prolonged" there is a safeguard against [the case of] other than the dawn prayer, and in its being devoid of any obligatory remembrance there is a safeguard against the foundational standing in prayer [itself].

If you say: The distinction between sunnas and obligations is intelligible, for validity is lost by the loss of the obligation but not the sunnah, and punishment is incurred by [neglecting] it but not the latter. But as for distinguishing one sunnah from another — while all are commanded by way of recommendation (istihbāb), there is no punishment in neglecting any of them, and reward exists for all — what then is its meaning?

Know that their sharing in reward, punishment, and recommendation does not remove their disparity. Let us unveil this for you by an example: A human being is not a complete, existing human except by an inner meaning and outer limbs. The inner meaning is life and spirit; the outer is the bodies of his members. Then some of those members are such that the human ceases to exist by their absence — like the heart, the liver, and the brain — every member whose loss entails the loss of life. Some of them are such that life does not cease by their loss, but the purposes of life are lost — like the eye, the hand, the foot, and the tongue. And some are such that neither life nor its purposes are lost by their absence, but beauty (ḥusn) is lost — like the eyebrows, the beard, the eyelashes, and the comeliness of complexion. And some are such that the foundation of beauty is not lost, but its perfection is — like the arching of the eyebrows, the blackness of the beard's hair and the eyelashes, the proportionality of the limbs' creation, and the blending of redness with whiteness in the complexion. These are varying degrees. Likewise, worship is a form (ṣūrah) that the Lawgiver has shaped, commanding us to acquire it. Its spirit and inner life are humility (khushūʿ), intention, presence of heart, and sincerity (ikhlāṣ) — as will come later. We are now concerned with its outer parts.

Thus, rukūʿ, sujūd, standing, and the rest of the pillars (arkān) run in its course as the heart, head, and liver [run in the human] — for the existence of prayer ceases by their absence.

The sunnas we have mentioned — raising the hands, the opening supplication, and the first tashahhud — run in its course as the hands, eyes, and feet [run in the human]. Validity is not lost by their absence, just as life is not lost by the absence of these members. However, the person becomes, by their loss, deformed in creation (mushawwah al-khilqah), blameworthy, and undesirable. Likewise, one who confines himself to the minimum that suffices in prayer is like one who gifts to a king among kings a living slave with severed limbs.

As for the postures (hayʾāt) — which are what lies beyond the sunnas — they run in the course of the causes of beauty, like the eyebrows, the beard, and the eyelashes, and the comeliness of complexion. As for the functions of the invocations within those sunnas, they are completers of beauty, like the arching of the eyebrows, the roundness of the beard, and other such things.

Thus, prayer in your view is a means of nearness (qurbah) and a gift (tuḥfah) by which you draw near to the presence of the King of Kings — like a handmaiden that a seeker of nearness among the sultans gifts to them. This gift is presented to God — exalted be He — then it is returned to you on the Day of the Great Presentation. The choice is yours in beautifying its form or disfiguring it. For if you beautify, it is for your own soul; and if you disfigure, it is against it.

It is not fitting that your share from the practice of jurisprudence (fiqh) be merely that the sunnah is distinguished from the obligation for you, such that nothing attaches to your understanding of the sunnah's description except that it is permissible to abandon it — and so you abandon it. For that resembles the saying of a physician: "The gouging out of the eye does not annul the existence of the human, but it removes him from the hope of the seeker of nearness that the sultan will accept [the gift] when he presents it in the guise of a gift." Thus ought you to understand the ranks of the sunnas, the postures, and the proprieties. Every prayer in which a person does not perfect his rukūʿ and sujūd is the foremost adversary against its performer, saying: "May God neglect you as you have neglected me."

So examine the reports (akhbār) we have cited concerning the perfection of the prayer's pillars, that its weighty significance may become manifest to you.

chapters.title_en: The Third Chapter on the Inward Conditions — The Works of the Heart
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| الباب الثالث في الشروط الباطنة من أعمال القلب

ولنذكر في هذا الباب ارتباط الصلاة بالخشوع وحضور القلب
ثم نذكر المعاني الباطنة وحدودها وأسبابها وعلاجها
ثم لنذكر تفصيل ما ينبغي أن يحضر في كل  ركن من أركان الصلاة لتكون صالحة
لزاد الآخرة

### |||| بيان اشتراط الخشوع وحضور القلب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ش-ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Lowliness, humility, submissiveness of the body and gaze; the earth’s stillness before rain.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heart’s abasement before Divine Majesty, entailing bodily stillness as its outward sign.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical lowering; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul’s inward surrender.
- Root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, attendance, being at a place or state; opposite of absence (ghaybah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intellect’s steadfast attendance upon the meaning of the ritual act, not the body’s mere location.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for spatial presence; metaphorical for the heart’s focus (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) as a technical term of the path.
- Root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The heart as a physical organ; also turning, overturning (taqallub) due to its fluctuating states.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The subtle divine faculty (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that comprehends, wills, and knows — the seat of accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the organ; metaphorical for the intellect and its spiritual center.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — the particle "ثُمَّ" (thumma) in "ثُمَّ نَذْكُرُ" indicates sequential ordering with a temporal gap, signaling that inward meanings are expounded only after establishing the outward link between prayer and humility.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is the third chapter, concerning the inward conditions — namely, the works of the heart.

In this chapter, we shall first mention the connection of prayer (ṣalāh) with humility (khushūʿ) and the presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb). Then we shall mention the inward meanings, their definitions (ḥudūd), their causes (asbāb), and their remedies (ʿilāj). Then we shall detail what ought to be present in each pillar (rukn) of the prayer, so that the prayer may be fit as provision (zād) for the Hereafter.

### |||| An Exposition of the Requisite Condition of Humility and Presence of Heart

Know that humility (khushūʿ) is the heart’s abasement before the Majesty of God — may He be exalted — and its standing in lowliness and need before Him. Its outward manifestation is the stillness of the limbs and the lowering of the gaze, for when the heart is humbled, the members follow in submission. And the presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) is its withdrawal from all else save God — may He be exalted — so that the worshipper’s awareness is wholly occupied with the meaning of what he utters and performs, not straying to worldly concerns or passing thoughts.

The proof of its necessity is the saying of God — may He be exalted — {«وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ»} (And seek help through patience and prayer; and indeed, it is difficult except for the humble — Qur’an 2:45). Thus He made the prayer heavy and burdensome except for those possessed of humility, indicating that humility is the condition that lightens it and renders it acceptable. And the Prophet — may God’s blessings and peace be upon him — said: «مَنْ لَمْ تَنْهَهُ صَلَاتُهُ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ لَمْ يَزْدَدْ مِنَ اللهِ إِلَّا بُعْدًا» (Whoever’s prayer does not forbid him from lewdness and evil gains naught from God but distance). And the prayer that forbids is that whose heart is present and humbled, for the heart’s presence is the soul of the prayer, and its absence is its death.

We say: The presence of the heart is a requisite condition (sharṭ) for the perfection (kamāl) of the prayer, not for its validity (ṣiḥḥah) in the legal sense — for the jurists have ruled that the prayer of one whose heart wanders is valid in fulfilling the obligation, yet it is deficient in reward and far from acceptance. But the people of the Hereafter seek the prayer that is a provision for the journey, and that is only attained by the heart’s presence and the soul’s humility. Thus we shall now expound the inward meanings, their limits, their causes, and their remedies, so that the seeker may strive to realize them.

chapters.title_en: On the Presence of the Heart in Prayer — The Spirit of the Ritual Prayer (Rūḥ al-Ṣalāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن أدلة ذلك كثيرة فمن ذلك قوله تعالى أقم الصلاة لذكري وظاهر الأمر
الوجوب والغفلة تضاد الذكر فمن غفل في جميع صلاته كيف يكون مقيما للصلاة
لذكره وقوله تعالى ولا تكن من الغافلين نهي وظاهره التحريم وقوله عز وجل
حتى تعلموا ما تقولون تعليل لنهي السكران وهو مطرد في الغافل المستغرق الهم
بالوسواس وأفكار الدنيا وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما الصلاة تمسكن وتواضع
حصر بالألف واللام وكلمة إنما للتحقيق والتوكيد وقد فهم الفقهاء من قوله
صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما الشفعة فيما لم يقصر الحصر والإثبات والنفي وقوله
صلى الله عليه وسلم من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله
إلا بعدا وصلاة الغافل لا تمنع من الفحشاء والمنكر وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
كم من قائم حظه من صلاته التعب والنصب (1) وما أراد به إلا الغافل وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم ليس للعبد من صلاته إلا ما عقل منها (2) والتحقيق فيه أن
المصلي مناج ربه عز وجل (3) كما ورد به الخبر والكلام مع الغفلة ليس
بمناجاة ألبتة وبيانه أن الزكاة إن غفل الإنسان عنها مثلا فهي في نفسها
مخالفة للشهوة شديدة على النفس وكذا الصوم قاهر للقوى كاسر لسطوة الهوى
الذي هو آلة للشيطان عدو الله فلا يبعد أن يحصل منها مقصود مع الغفلة وكذلك
الحج أفعاله شاقة شديدة وفيه من المجاهدة ما يحصل به PageV01P159
الإيلام كان القلب حاضرا مع أفعاله أو لم يكن أما الصلاة فليس فيها إلا
ذكر وقراءة وركوع وسجود وقيام وقعود فأما الذكر فإنه مجاورة ومناجاة مع
الله عز وجل فأما أن يكون المقصود منه كونه خطابا ومحاورة أو المقصود منه
الحروف والأصوات امتحانا للسان بالعمل كما تمتحن المعدة والفرج بالإمساك في
الصوم وكما يمتحن البدن بمشاق الحج ويمتحن بمشقة إخراج الزكاة واقتطاع
المال المعشوق
ولا شك أن هذا القسم باطل فإن تحريك اللسان بالهذيان ما أخفه  على الغافل
فليس فيه امتحان من حيث أنه عمل بل المقصود الحروف من حيث أنه نطق ولا يكون
نطقا إلا إذا أعرب عما في الضمير ولا يكون معربا إلا بحضور القلب فأي سؤال
في قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم إذا كان القلب غافلا وإذا لم يقصد كونه
تضرعا ودعاء فأي مشقة في تحريك اللسان به مع الغفلة لا سيما بعد الاعتياد
هذا حكم الأذكار بل أقول لو حلف الإنسان وقال لأشكرن فلانا وأثني عليه
وأسأله حاجة ثم جرت الألفاظ الدالة على هذه المعاني على لسانه في النوم لم
يبر في يمينه ولو جرت على لسانه في ظلمة وذلك الإنسان حاضر وهو لا يعرف
حضوره ولا يراه لا يصير بارا في يمينه إذ لا يكون كلامه خطابا ونطقا معه ما
لم يكن هو حاضرا في قلبه فلو كانت تجري هذه الكلمات على لسانه وهو حاضر إلا
أنه في بياض النهار غافل لكونه مستغرق الهم بفكر من الأفكار ولم يكن له قصد
توجيه الخطاب إليه عند نطقه لم يصر بارا في يمينه
ولا شك أن المقصود من القراءة والأذكار الحمد والثناء والتضرع والدعاء
والمخاطب هو الله عز وجل وقلبه بحجاب الغفلة محجوب عنه فلا يراه ولا يشاهده
بل هو غافل عن المخاطب ولسانه يتحرك بحكم العادة فما أبعد هذا عن المقصود
بالصلاة التي شرعت لتصقيل القلب وتجديد ذكر الله عز وجل ورسوخ عقد الإيمان
به هذا حكم القراءة والذكر
وبالجملة فهذه الخاصية لا سبيل إلى إنكارها في النطق وتمييزها عن الفعل
وأما الركوع والسجود فالمقصود بهما التعظيم قطعا ولو جاز أن يكون معظما
لله عز وجل بفعله وهو غافل عنه لجاز أن يكون معظما لصنم موضوع بين يديه وهو
غافل عنه أو يكون معظما للحائط الذي بين يديه وهو غافل عنه وإذا خرج عن
كونه تعظيما لم يبق إلا مجرد حركة الظهر والرأس وليس فيه من المشقة ما يقصد
الامتحان به ثم يجعله عماد الدين والفاصل بين الكفر والإسلام ويقدم على
الحج وسائر  العبادات ويجب القتل بسبب تركه على الخصوص وما أرى أن هذه
العظمة كلها للصلاة من حيث أعمالها الظاهرة إلا أن يضاف إليها مقصود
المناجاة فإن ذلك يتقدم على الصوم والزكاة والحج وغيره بل الضحايا
والقرابين التي هي مجاهدة للنفس بتنقيص المال قال الله تعالى لن ينال الله
لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم أي الصفة التي استولت على القلب
حتى حملته على امتثال الأوامر هي المطلوبة فكيف الأمر في الصلاة ولا أرب في
أفعالها فهذا ما يدل من حيث المعنى على اشتراط حضور القلب
فإن قلت إن حكمت ببطلان الصلاة وجعلت حضور القلب شرطا في صحتها خالفت
إجماع الفقهاء فإنهم لم يشترطوا إلا حضور القلب عند التكبير فاعلم أنه قد
تقدم في كتاب العلم أن الفقهاء لا يتصرفون في الباطن ولا يشقون عن القلوب
ولا في طريق الآخرة بل يبنون أحكام الدين على ظاهر أعمال الجوارح وظاهر
الأعمال كاف لسقوط القتل وتعزير السلطان فأما أنه ينفع في الآخرة فليس هذا
من حدود الفقه على أنه لا يمكن أن يدعى الإجماع
فقد نقل عن بشر بن الحارث فيما رواه عنه أبو طالب المكي عن سفيان الثوري
أنه قال من لم يخشع فسدت صلاته وروي عن الحسن أنه قال كل صلاة لا يحضر فيها
القلب فهي إلى العقوبة أسرع
وعن معاذ بن جبل من عرف من على يمينه وشماله متعمدا وهو في الصلاة فلا
صلاة له
وروي أيضا مسندا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
PageV01P160
إن العبد ليصلي الصلاة لا يكتب له سدسها ولا عشرها وإنما يكتب للعبد من
صلاته ما عقل منها (1) وهذا لو نقل عن غيره لجعل مذهبا فكيف لا يتمسك به
وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد أجمعت العلماء على أنه ليس للعبد من صلاته إلا ما
عقل منها فجعله إجماعا وما نقل من هذا الجنس عن الفقهاء المتورعين وعن
علماء الآخرة أكثر من أن يحصى
والحق الرجوع إلى أدلة الشرع والأخبار والآثار ظاهرة في هذا الشرط إلا  أن
مقام الفتوى في التكليف الظاهر يتقدر بقدر قصور الخلق
فلا يمكن أن يشترط على الناس إحضار القلب في جميع الصلاة فإن ذلك يعجز
عنه كل البشر إلا الأقلين وإذا لم يمكن اشتراط الاستيعاب للضرورة فلا مرد
له إلا أن يشترط منه ما يطلق عليه الاسم ولو في اللحظة الواحدة وأولى
اللحظات به لحظة التكبير فاقتصرنا على التكليف بذلك
ونحن مع ذلك نرجو أن لا يكون حال الغافل في جميع صلاته مثل حال التارك
بالكلية
فإنه على الجملة أقدم على العمل ظاهرا وأحضر القلب لحظة
وكيف لا والذي صلى مع الحدث ناسيا صلاته باطلة عند الله تعالى ولكن له
أجر ما يحسب فعله وعلى قدر قصوره وعذره ومع هذا الرجاء فيخشى أن يكون حاله
أشد من حال التارك وكيف لا والذي يحضر الخدمة ويتهاون بالحضرة ويتكلم بكلام
الغافل المستحقر أشد حالا من الذي يعرض عن الخدمة وإذا تعارض أسباب الخوف
والرجاء وصار الأمر مخطرا في نفسه فإليك الخيرة بعده في الاحتياط والتساهل
ومع هذا فلا مطمع في مخالفة الفقهاء فيما أفتوا به من الصحة مع الغفلة
فإن ذلك من ضرورة الفتوى كما سبق التنبيه عليه ومن عرف سر الصلاة علم أن
الغفلة تضادها
ولكن قد ذكرنا في باب الفرق بين العلم الباطن والظاهر في كتاب قواعد
العقائد أن قصور الخلق أحد الأسباب المانعة عن التصريح بكل ما ينكشف من
أسرار الشرع
فلنقتصر على هذا القدر من البحث فإن فيه مقنعا للمريد الطالب لطريق
الآخرة
وأما المجادل المشغب فلسنا نقصد مخاطبته الآن وحاصل الكلام أن حضور القلب
هو روح الصلاة وأن أقل ما يبقى به رمق الروح الحضور عند التكبير
فالنقصان منه هلاك وبقدر الزيادة عليه تنبسط الروح في أجزاء الصلاة
وكم من حي لا حراك به قريب من ميت فصلاة الغافل في جميعها إلا عند
التكبير كمثل حي لا حراك به نسأل الله حسن العون
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dhakara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remembrance, mindfulness, presence of mind; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān) and heedlessness (ghaflah)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heart's attentive presence with that which is remembered; in worship, it is the very essence of devotional acts
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual mental presence; metaphorical (majāz) — mere verbal utterance without comprehension
- Root: ح-ض-ر (ḥaḍara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be present, to attend; presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) as opposed to absence (ghaybah)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heart's witnessing of the Divine; the state of the servant standing before his Lord
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical presence; metaphorical — spiritual attentiveness in worship
- Root: ن-ج-و (najā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Private, intimate conversation; confiding a secret
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The believer's intimate discourse with God in prayer (munājāh)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — whispered speech; metaphorical — the soul's direct address to its Creator
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction (Qaṣr) via "innamā" and the definite article (al-); the particle "innamā" effects restriction and affirmation, as in the Prophetic hadiths cited
chapters.translation:
Know that the evidences for this are numerous. Among them is the saying of God, the Exalted: {«أقم الصلاة لذكري»} ("Establish the prayer for My remembrance") — and the apparent meaning of the command is obligation (wujūb). Heedlessness (ghaflah) is antithetical to remembrance (dhikr). How, then, can one who is heedless throughout his entire prayer be one who "establishes the prayer for His remembrance"? And His saying, the Exalted: {«ولا تكن من الغافلين»} ("And be not among the heedless") is a prohibition, and its apparent meaning is prohibition (taḥrīm). And His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«حتى تعلموا ما تقولون»} ("Until you know what you say") is a rationale (taʿlīl) for the prohibition against the intoxicated — and it applies equally to the heedless one who is wholly absorbed in whisperings (waswās) and worldly thoughts.

And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, prayer is humility (tamaskun) and lowliness (tawāḍuʿ)" — this is a restriction (ḥaṣr) through the definite article and the word "innamā," which is for affirmation and emphasis. The jurists (fuqahāʾ) have understood from his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, the right of pre-emption (shufʿah) applies only to what has not been divided" — the restriction, affirmation, and negation. And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whosoever's prayer does not prevent him from indecency and evil, he gains nothing from God but distance" — and the prayer of the heedless does not prevent from indecency and evil. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "How many a standing one has no share from his prayer but fatigue and toil" — and he intended thereby none but the heedless. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The servant has from his prayer only that which he comprehends of it."

The verification (taḥqīq) of this matter is that the one praying is in intimate discourse (munājāh) with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as has come in the report (khabar). And speech accompanied by heedlessness is not intimate discourse at all. Its clarification is this: if one is heedless of the alms-tax (zakāh), for example, it is nonetheless in itself a contravention of desire and severe upon the soul. Likewise, fasting (ṣawm) subdues the faculties and breaks the dominance of passion (hawā), which is the instrument of Satan, the enemy of God. Thus it is not improbable that its purpose is achieved despite heedlessness. Likewise, the pilgrimage (ḥajj) — its acts are arduous and severe, and in it there is such striving (mujāhadah) that the intended effect of mortification is achieved whether the heart was present with its acts or not.

As for prayer (ṣalāh), there is nothing in it but remembrance, recitation, bowing, prostration, standing, and sitting. As for remembrance, it is a drawing near and an intimate discourse with God, the Mighty and Majestic. Now either the purpose of it is that it be an address and a dialogue, or the purpose is the letters and sounds — testing the tongue by action, just as the stomach and the private parts are tested by abstention in fasting, and just as the body is tested by the hardships of pilgrimage and by the hardship of extracting the beloved wealth in alms.

There is no doubt that this latter division is false. For the movement of the tongue in idle chatter — how light it is upon the heedless! There is no testing in it insofar as it is an action. Rather, the purpose is the letters insofar as they constitute speech (nuṭq) — and it is not speech unless it expresses what is in the conscience (ḍamīr), and it does not express unless with the heart's presence. So what question is there in his saying: {«اهدنا الصراط المستقيم»} ("Guide us to the straight path") when the heart is heedless? And if one does not intend it as supplication (taḍarruʿ) and invocation (duʿāʾ), what hardship is there in moving the tongue with it despite heedlessness — especially after habituation?

This is the ruling concerning the invocations (adhkār). Nay, I say: if a man swore an oath saying, "I shall surely thank so-and-so, praise him, and ask him for a need," and then the words indicating these meanings flowed upon his tongue while he was asleep, he would not have fulfilled his oath. And if they flowed upon his tongue in darkness while that person was present, but he did not know of his presence nor see him, he would not become faithful to his oath — for his speech would not be an address and a discourse with him unless he were present in his heart. And if these words were to flow upon his tongue while he was present, yet he was heedless in the bright daylight because he was wholly absorbed in some thought, and he had no intention of directing the address to him at the time of utterance — he would not become faithful to his oath.

There is no doubt that the purpose of recitation (qirāʾah) and invocations is praise (ḥamd), thanksgiving (thanāʾ), supplication (taḍarruʿ), and invocation (duʿāʾ) — and the One addressed is God, the Mighty and Majestic. But his heart is veiled from Him by the veil of heedlessness, so he neither sees Him nor witnesses Him. Rather, he is heedless of the One addressed, while his tongue moves by force of habit. How far is this from the purpose of prayer, which was legislated to polish the heart, renew the remembrance of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and firmly root the covenant of faith in Him! This is the ruling concerning recitation and remembrance.

In sum: this particular property (khāṣṣiyyah) — there is no way to deny it in speech and to distinguish it from mere action.

As for bowing (rukūʿ) and prostration (sujūd), their purpose is glorification (taʿẓīm) — definitively. If it were permissible that one glorify God, the Mighty and Majestic, by his action while being heedless of Him, then it would be permissible that he glorify an idol placed before him while heedless of it, or that he glorify the wall before him while heedless of it. And when it departs from being glorification, nothing remains but the mere movement of the back and the head — and there is no hardship in it that would be intended for testing. Yet it is made the pillar of religion (ʿimād al-dīn), the differentiator between unbelief and faith, given precedence over pilgrimage and all other acts of worship, and killing is mandated for its abandonment specifically. I do not see that all this grandeur belongs to prayer by virtue of its outward acts alone — unless there be added to it the purpose of intimate discourse (munājāh). For that takes precedence over fasting, alms, pilgrimage, and others — nay, even over the sacrificial offerings (ḍaḥāyā) and oblations (qarābīn), which are a striving of the soul through diminishment of wealth. God, the Exalted, said: {«لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم»} ("Neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God, but piety from you reaches Him") — that is, the quality that has taken hold of the heart until it compelled it to obey the commands is what is sought. How, then, with prayer, in whose acts there is no intrinsic purpose? This is what indicates, from the standpoint of meaning, the conditionality of the heart's presence.

If you say: "If you rule that prayer is invalid and make the heart's presence a condition of its soundness, you contradict the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the jurists — for they have conditioned only the heart's presence at the takbīr (the opening magnification) — then know that it has preceded in the Book of Knowledge that the jurists do not operate upon the inward, nor do they split open hearts, nor do they tread the path of the Hereafter. Rather, they build the rulings of religion upon the outward acts of the limbs. And the outward act suffices for the dropping of the death-penalty and the ruler's disciplinary punishment. As for whether it benefits in the Hereafter — that is not within the bounds of jurisprudence (fiqh). Moreover, consensus cannot be claimed.

For it has been transmitted from Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith — in what Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī related from Sufyān al-Thawrī — that he said: "Whosoever does not humble himself (yakhshaʿ), his prayer is corrupted." And it is related from al-Ḥasan that he said: "Every prayer in which the heart is not present hastens more swiftly to punishment." And from Muʿādh ibn Jabal: "Whosoever knowingly knows who is on his right and his left while in prayer, he has no prayer." And it is also related with an unbroken chain (musnad) that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, the servant prays a prayer for which not a sixth nor a tenth is written for him. And the servant has from his prayer only that which he comprehends of it." If this had been transmitted from anyone other than him, it would have been made a school of thought (madhhab) — so how is it not clung to? And ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd said: "The scholars are agreed (ajmaʿa) that the servant has from his prayer only that which he comprehends of it" — making it a consensus. And what has been transmitted of this kind from the God-fearing jurists and the scholars of the Hereafter is more than can be enumerated.

The truth is to return to the evidences of the Sacred Law. The reports (akhbār) and traditions (āthār) are manifest upon this condition — except that the station of legal opinion (fatwā) in outward obligation is measured by the extent of creatures' incapacity. It is not possible to impose upon people the presence of the heart throughout the entire prayer, for all of humanity is incapable of that save a few. And when the condition of complete coverage cannot be imposed due to necessity, there is no recourse but to condition from it that which the name (of prayer) is applied to — even if in a single moment. And the most worthy of moments for it is the moment of the takbīr. So we have confined the obligation to that.

Nevertheless, we hope that the state of the one heedless throughout his entire prayer is not like the state of the one who abandons it altogether. For in sum, he has undertaken the outward act and brought his heart present for a moment. And how could it be otherwise? For the one who prays while in a state of ritual impurity (ḥadath) forgetfully — his prayer is invalid before God, the Exalted, yet he has a reward for what he intended by his act, and according to the measure of his shortcoming and his excuse. And despite this hope, one fears that his state may be more severe than that of the one who abandons. And how could it not be? For the one who attends the service but is negligent of the Presence, and speaks with the speech of the heedless, the contemptuous — his state is more severe than the one who turns away from the service altogether. And when the causes of fear (khawf) and hope (rajāʾ) conflict, and the matter becomes perilous in one's soul, then the choice is yours thereafter between caution (iḥtiyāṭ) and leniency (tasāhul).

And with all this, there is no aspiration to contravene the jurists in what they have ruled regarding validity despite heedlessness — for that is a necessity of legal opinion (fatwā), as has been previously indicated. And whosoever knows the secret of prayer knows that heedlessness is antithetical to it. But we have mentioned in the chapter on the distinction between inward and outward knowledge, in the Book of the Foundations of Beliefs (Qawāʿid al-ʿAqāʾid), that the incapacity of creatures is one of the impediments preventing the explicit declaration of every secret of the Sacred Law that is unveiled.

Let us confine ourselves to this measure of investigation, for in it there is sufficient satisfaction for the seeker (murīd) who pursues the path of the Hereafter. As for the contentious disputant (mujādil mushabbish), we do not intend to address him now.

The sum of the discourse is this: the presence of the heart is the spirit (rūḥ) of prayer. The least by which the breath of the spirit remains is presence at the takbīr. Diminution from that is destruction, and in proportion to increase upon it, the spirit expands through the parts of prayer. And how many a living being there is with no movement in him, near to the dead! So the prayer of the heedless in all of it — except at the takbīr — is like a living being with no movement in him. We ask God for good assistance (ḥusn al-ʿawn).

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Inner Meanings by Which the Life of Prayer Is Perfected
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان المعاني الباطنة التي تتم بها حياة الصلاة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Life (ḥayāh) as the opposite of death; vitality, animation, and the enduring principle of sentient existence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Life in the Qurʾān is twofold — physical (ḥayāh dunyāwiyyah) and spiritual (ḥayāh qalbiyyah), the latter being the illumination of the heart through knowledge and presence with God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for biological life; metaphorical (majāz) for the perfection of an act through its inward conditions — here, prayer's "life" is its spiritual vitality, not mere ritual motion.
- Root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The belly, interior, or hidden aspect (bāṭin) as opposed to the outward (ẓāhir); that which is concealed from sensory perception.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, bāṭin denotes the inward reality of acts — intentions (niyyāt), presence of heart (ḥuḍūr), and humility (khushūʿ) — which constitute their true essence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical interiority; metaphorical for the unseen dimension of worship that gives it meaning and efficacy before God.
- Root: ت-م-م (t-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Completion, perfection, and reaching the end of a matter without deficiency (nuqṣān).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tamām in worship signifies the attainment of all obligatory and recommended conditions, both outward (ẓāhir) and inward (bāṭin), such that the act is fully realized.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for finishing a task; metaphorical for the qualitative perfection of an act through its hidden virtues.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase "ḥayāt al-ṣalāh" (life of prayer) is an ʾiḍāfah where the second noun (al-ṣalāh) specifies the domain of the first (ḥayāt), indicating that the "life" is not generic but specifically the vitality inherent to the prayer itself, requiring its inward conditions.
chapters.translation: I say: Now we shall expound the inner meanings (al-maʿānī al-bāṭinah) through which the life of prayer (ḥayāt al-ṣalāh) is perfected — for the prayer, in its outward form, is but a body (jasad), and its spirit (rūḥ) is the presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) with God, the humility of the limbs (khushūʿ al-jawāriḥ), and the sincerity of intention (ikhlāṣ al-niyyah). Just as the body without the spirit is dead, so too the prayer without these inward realities is devoid of its true life. Know that the perfection of prayer lies not in the mere movement of the tongue or the bending of the back, but in the awakening of the heart to the majesty of the One before Whom one stands, the contemplation of His greatness, and the severance of all worldly concerns from the mind. These inner meanings are the very essence of the prayer's vitality, and without them, the outward acts are but a hollow shell.

chapters.title_en: The Six Inner Realities of Prayer: Presence, Understanding, Reverence, Awe, Hope, and Shame
chapters.arabic_text:
إعلم أن هذه المعاني تكثر العبارات عنها  ولكن يجمعها ست جمل وهي حضور
القلب والتفهم والتعظيم والهيبة والرجاء والحياء
فلنذكر تفاصيلها ثم أسبابها ثم العلاج في اكتسابها
أما التفاصيل فالأول حضور القلب ونعني به أن يفرغ القلب عن غير ما هو
ملابس له ومتكلم به فيكون العلم بالفعل والقول مقرونا بهما ولا يكون الفكر
جائلا في غيرهما ومهما انصرف في الفكر عن غير ما هو فيه وكان في قلبه ذكر
لما هو فيه ولم يكن فيه غفلة عن كل شيء فقد حصل حضور القلب ولكن التفهم
لمعنى الكلام أمر وراء حضور القلب فربما يكون القلب حاضرا مع اللفظ ولا
يكون حاضرا مع معنى اللفظ فاشتمال القلب على العلم بمعنى اللفظ هو الذي
أردناه بالتفهم
وهذا مقام يتفاوت الناس فيه إذ ليس يشترك الناس في تفهم المعاني للقرآن
والتسبيحات
وكم من معان لطيفة يفهمها المصلي في أثناء الصلاة ولم يكن قد خطر بقلبه
ذلك قبله ومن هذا الوجه كانت الصلاة ناهية عن الفحشاء والمنكر فإنها تفهم
أمورا تلك الأمور تمنع عن الفحشاء لا محالة
وأما التعظيم فهو أمر وراء حضور القلب والفهم إذ الرجل يخاطب عبده بكلام
هو حاضر القلب PageV01P161
فيه ومتفهم لمعناه ولا يكون معظما له فالتعظيم زائد عليهما
وأما الهيبة فزائدة على التعظيم بل هي عبارة عن خوف منشؤه التعظيم لأن من
لا يخاف لا يسمى هائبا والمخافة من العقرب وسوء خلق العبد وما يجري مجراه
من الأسباب الخسيسة لا تسمى مهابة بل الخوف من السلطان المعظم يسمى مهابة
والهيبة خوف مصدرها الإجلال
وأما الرجا فلا شك أنه زائد فكم من معظم ملكا من الملوك يهابه أو يخاف
سطوته ولكن لا يرجو مثوبته
والعبد ينبغي أن يكون راجيا بصلاته ثواب الله عز وجل كما أنه خائف
بتقصيره عقاب الله عز وجل وأما الحياء فهو زائد على الجملة لأن مستنده
استشعار تقصير وتوهم ذنب ويتصور التعظيم والخوف والرجاء من غير حياء حيث لا
يكون توهم تقصير وارتكاب ذنب
وأما أسباب هذه المعاني الستة فاعلم أن حضور القلب  سببه الهمة فإن قلبك
تابع لهمتك فلا يحضر إلا فيما يهمك
ومهما أهمك أمر حضر القلب فيه شاء أم أبى فهو مجبول على ذلك ومسخر فيه
والقلب إذا لم يحضر في الصلاة لم يكن متعطلا بل جائلا فيما الهمة مصروفة
إليه من أمور الدنيا فلا حيلة ولا علاج لإحضار القلب إلا بصرف الهمة إلى
الصلاة والهمة لا تنصرف إليها ما لم يتبين أن الغرض المطلوب منوط بها وذلك
هو الإيمان والتصديق بأن الآخرة خير وأبقى وأن الصلاة وسيلة إليها فإذا
أضيف هذا إلى حقيقة العلم بحقارة الدنيا ومهماتها حصل من مجموعها حضور
القلب في الصلاة وبمثل هذه العلة يحضر قلبك إذا حضرت بين يدي بعض الأكابر
ممن لا يقدر على مضرتك ومنفعتك فإذا كان لا يحضر عند المناجاة مع ملك
الملوك الذي بيده الملك والملكوت والنفع والضر فلا تظنن أن له سببا سوى ضعف
الإيمان فاجتهد الآن في تقوية الإيمان وطريقه يستقصى في غير هذا الموضع
وأما التفهم فسببه بعد حضور القلب إدمان الفكر وصرف الذهن إلى إدراك المعنى
وعلاجه ما هو علاج إحضار القلب مع الإقبال على الفكر والتشمر لدفع الخواطر
وعلاج دفع الخواطر الشاغلة قطع موادها أعني النزوع عن تلك الأسباب التي
تنجذب الخواطر إليها وما لم تنقطع تلك المواد لا تنصرف عنها الخواطر فمن
أحب شيئا أكثر ذكره فذكر المحبوب يهجم على القلب بضرورة لذلك ترى أن من أحب
غير الله لا تصفو له صلاة عن الخواطر
وأما التعظيم فهي حالة للقلب تتولد من معرفتين إحداهما معرفة جلال الله
عز وجل وعظمته وهو من أصول الإيمان فإن من لا يعتقد عظمته لا تذعن النفس
لتعظيمه
الثانية معرفة حقارة النفس وخستها وكونها عبدا مسخرا مربوبا حتى يتولد من
المعرفتين الاستكانة والانكسار والخشوع لله سبحانه فيعبر عنه بالتعظيم وما
لم تمتزج معرفة حقارة النفس بمعرفة جلال الله لا تنتظم حالة التعظيم
والخشوع فإن المستغني عن غيره الآمن على نفسه يجوز أن يعرف من غيره صفات
العظمة ولا يكون الخشوع  والتعظيم حاله لأن القرينة الأخرى وهي معرفة حقارة
النفس وحاجتها لم تقترن إليه وأما الهيبة والخوف فحالة للنفس تتولد من
المعرفة بقدرة الله وسطوته ونفوذ مشيئته فيه مع قلة المبالاة به وأنه لو
أهلك الأولين والآخرين لم ينقص من ملكه ذرة هذا مع مطالعة ما يجري على
الأنبياء والأولياء من المصائب وأنواع البلاء مع القدرة على الدفع على خلاف
ما يشاهد من ملوك الأرض
وبالجملة كلما زاد العلم بالله زادت الخشية والهيبة وسيأتي أسباب ذلك في
كتاب الخوف من ربع المنجيات وأما الرجاء فسببه معرفة لطف الله عز وجل وكرمه
وعميم إنعامه ولطائف صنعه ومعرفة صدقه في وعده الجنة بالصلاة فإذا حصل
اليقين بوعده والمعرفة بلطفه انبعث من مجموعهما الرجاء لا محالة وأما
الحياء فباستشعاره التقصير في العبادة وعلمه بالعجز عن القيام بعظيم حق
الله عز وجل ويقوي ذلك بالمعرفة بعيوب النفس وآفاتها وقلة إخلاصها وخبث
دخلتها وميلها إلى الحظ العاجل في جميع أفعالها مع العلم بعظيم ما يقتضيه
جلال الله عز وجل والعلم
PageV01P162
بأنه مطلع على السر وخطرات القلب وإن دقت وخفيت وهذه المعارف إذا حصلت
يقينا انبعث منها بالضرورة حالة تسمى الحياء فهذه أسباب هذه الصفات وكل ما
طلب تحصيله فعلاجه إحضار سببه ففي معرفة السبب معرفة العلاج
ورابطة جميع هذه الأسباب الإيمان
واليقين أعني به هذه المعارف التي ذكرناها ومعنى كونها يقينا انتفاء الشك
واستيلاؤها على القلب كما سبق في بيان اليقين من كتاب العلم وبقدر اليقين
يخشع القلب ولذلك قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم يحدثنا ونحدثه فإذا حضرت الصلاة كأنه لم يعرفنا ولم نعرفه وقد روي أن
الله سبحانه أوحى إلى موسى عليه السلام يا موسى إذا ذكرتني فاذكرني وأنت
تنتفض أعضاؤك وكن عند ذكري خاشعا مطمئنا وإذا ذكرتني فاجعل لسانك من وراء
قلبك وإذا قمت بين يدي فقم قيام العبد الذليل وناجني بقلب وجل ولسان صادق
وروي أن الله تعالى أوحى إليه قل لعصاة أمتك لا يذكروني فإني  آليت على نفسي
أن من ذكرني ذكرته فإذا ذكروني ذكرتهم باللعنة هذا في عاص غير غافل في ذكره
فكيف إذا اجتمعت الغفلة والعصيان وباختلاف المعاني التي ذكرناها في القلوب
انقسم الناس إلى غافل يتمم صلاته ولم يحضر قلبه في لحظة منها وإلى من يتمم
ولم يغب قلبه في لحظة بل ربما كان مستوعب الهم بها بحيث لا يحس بما يجري
بين يديه
ولذلك لم يحس مسلم بن يسار بسقوط الاسطوانة في المسجد اجتمع الناس عليها
وبعضهم كان يحضر الجماعة مدة ولم يعرف قط من على يمينه ويساره
ووجيب قلب إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه وسلامه كان يسمع على ميلين
وجماعة كانت تصفر وجوههم وترتعد فرائصهم
وكل ذلك غير مستبعد فإن أضعافه مشاهد في همم أهل الدنيا وخوف ملوك الدنيا
مع عجزهم وضعفهم وخساسة الحظوظ الحاصلة منهم حتى يدخل الواحد على ملك أو
وزير ويحدثه بمهمته ثم يخرج ولو سئل عمن حواليه أو عن ثوب الملك لكان لا
يقدر على الإخبار عنه لاشتغال همه به عن ثوبه وعن الحاضرين حواليه ولكل
درجات مما عملوا فحظ كل واحد من صلاته بقدر خوفه وخشوعه وتعظيمه فإن موضع
نظر الله سبحانه القلوب دون ظاهر الحركات
ولذلك قال بعض الصحابة رضي الله عنهم يحشر الناس يوم القيامة على مثال
هيئتهم في الصلاة من الطمأنينة والهدوء ومن وجود النعيم بها واللذة ولقد
صدق فإنه يحشر كل على ما مات عليه ويموت على ما عاش عليه ويراعى في ذلك حال
قلبه لا حال شخصه فمن صفات القلوب تصاغ الصور في الدار الآخرة ولا ينجو إلا
من أتى الله بقلب سليم نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بلطفه وكرمه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "being present" or "attending" — the opposite of absence (ghaybah); also used for "attending" a gathering or "being at hand."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥuḍūr al-qalb denotes the heart's attentiveness to the divine address, a prerequisite for valid devotional acts (ʿibādāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is spatial/temporal presence; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to mental focus, as in "the heart is present with the utterance."
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate complement (al-mubtadaʾ wa-l-khabar) — "ḥuḍūr al-qalb" is a defined state (ḥāl) predicated of the worshipper, requiring a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) to convey simultaneity.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that these meanings are expressed by many terms, yet they are encompassed by six phrases: presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb), understanding (tafahhum), reverence (taʿẓīm), awe (haybah), hope (rajāʾ), and shame (ḥayāʾ). We shall now mention their details, then their causes, then the remedy for acquiring them.

As for the details: The first is presence of the heart. By this I mean that the heart is emptied of everything other than what it is engaged in and speaking — so that one's knowledge is conjoined with the act and the utterance, and thought does not wander to anything else. Whenever one's thought turns away from what one is engaged in, yet there remains in the heart a remembrance of what one is doing, and there is no heedlessness of it altogether, then presence of the heart has been achieved. However, understanding the meaning of the words is something beyond presence of the heart. For perhaps the heart is present with the utterance but not present with the meaning of the utterance. The heart's encompassing knowledge of the meaning of the utterance is what I intend by "understanding."

This is a station in which people vary, for people do not share equally in understanding the meanings of the Quran and the glorifications (tasbīḥāt). How many subtle meanings does a worshipper grasp during the prayer that had never occurred to his heart before! It is from this aspect that prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing, for it imparts understandings, and those understandings necessarily prevent indecency.

As for reverence (taʿẓīm), it is something beyond presence of the heart and understanding. For a man may address his slave with words while his heart is present with them and he understands their meaning, yet he does not revere him. Thus reverence is additional to both.

As for awe (haybah), it is additional to reverence. Indeed, it is an expression for a fear whose source is reverence. For one who does not fear is not called "awe-struck." Fear of a scorpion, or of a slave's bad character, and similar base causes, is not called "awe." Rather, fear of a mighty king is called "awe." Awe is a fear whose origin is veneration (ijlāl).

As for hope (rajāʾ), there is no doubt that it is additional. How many a man reveres a king among kings, fearing his severity, yet does not hope for his reward! The servant ought to hope, through his prayer, for the reward of God, Mighty and Majestic, just as he fears, through his shortcoming, the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic.

As for shame (ḥayāʾ), it is additional to all of these, because its basis is the perception of shortcoming and the imagining of sin. Reverence, fear, and hope can be conceived without shame, where there is no imagining of shortcoming or commission of sin.

As for the causes of these six meanings: Know that the cause of presence of the heart is earnest concern (himmah). For your heart follows your concern; it is present only in what concerns you. Whenever a matter concerns you, the heart becomes present in it, willingly or unwillingly — it is disposed to that by nature and subjugated to it. When the heart is not present in prayer, it is not idle, but rather wanders toward whatever worldly matters the concern is directed to. There is no device or remedy for bringing the heart to presence except by diverting the concern toward prayer. And the concern does not turn to it unless it becomes clear that the sought goal is attached to it — and that is faith and the affirmation that the Hereafter is better and more enduring, and that prayer is a means to it. When this is added to the true knowledge of the insignificance of this world and its concerns, then from their totality there results presence of the heart in prayer. By such a cause your heart becomes present when you stand before some great person who has no power to harm or benefit you. So if it does not become present during intimate communion (munājāh) with the King of Kings, in whose hand is sovereignty and dominion, benefit and harm, then do not think that it has any cause other than weakness of faith. Strive now to strengthen faith — and its path will be fully investigated elsewhere.

As for understanding, its cause, after presence of the heart, is persistence in reflection and directing the mind to grasp the meaning. Its remedy is the same as the remedy for bringing the heart to presence, along with turning toward reflection and girding oneself to repel distracting thoughts. The remedy for repelling distracting thoughts is to cut off their sources — that is, to desist from those causes toward which thoughts are drawn. As long as those sources are not cut off, thoughts will not turn away from them. For whoever loves something mentions it often, and the remembrance of the beloved rushes upon the heart by necessity. For this reason, you see that whoever loves other than God does not have his prayer purified from distracting thoughts.

As for reverence, it is a state of the heart generated from two knowledges. One is knowledge of the majesty (jalāl) of God, Mighty and Majestic, and His greatness — and this is among the principles of faith, for whoever does not believe in His greatness, his soul does not submit to revering Him. The second is knowledge of the baseness and lowliness of the soul, and that it is a subjugated, governed servant — so that from the two knowledges there is generated humility (istikānah), brokenness (inkisār), and submissiveness (khushūʿ) to God, Glorified be He, which is expressed as reverence. When the knowledge of the soul's baseness is not mixed with the knowledge of God's majesty, the state of reverence and submissiveness is not established. For one who is independent of others and secure in himself may know another's attributes of greatness, yet submissiveness and reverence are not his state, because the other correlative — knowledge of the soul's baseness and need — has not been joined to it.

As for awe and fear, they are a state of the soul generated from knowledge of God's power, His severity, and the penetration of His will over one, along with His indifference to him — that if He destroyed the first and the last, not a speck would diminish from His dominion. This, together with contemplating what befalls the prophets and saints of calamities and varieties of tribulation, despite His power to repel them — contrary to what is observed of the kings of the earth. In sum, the more one's knowledge of God increases, the more one's fear and awe increase. The causes of this will come in the Book of Fear from the Quarter of Deliverance.

As for hope, its cause is knowledge of God's gentleness (luṭf), His generosity, His abundant beneficence, and the subtleties of His craftsmanship — and knowledge of His truthfulness in His promise of Paradise through prayer. When certainty in His promise and knowledge of His gentleness are attained, hope necessarily arises from their combination.

As for shame, it arises from one's perception of shortcoming in worship and one's knowledge of incapacity to fulfill the immense right of God, Mighty and Majestic. This is strengthened by knowledge of the soul's faults and defects, its lack of sincerity, the corruption of its inner motive, and its inclination toward immediate gratification in all its actions — along with knowledge of the immensity of what God's majesty requires, and knowledge that He is aware of the secret and the passing thoughts of the heart, however subtle and hidden they may be. When these knowledges are attained with certainty, there necessarily arises from them a state called shame. These, then, are the causes of these attributes. And everything sought for acquisition — its remedy is to bring about its cause. In knowing the cause lies knowledge of the remedy.

The bond linking all these causes is faith and certainty. By certainty I mean these knowledges we have mentioned. The meaning of their being "certain" is the absence of doubt and their dominance over the heart, as has preceded in the explanation of certainty in the Book of Knowledge. And in proportion to certainty, the heart becomes submissive. For this reason, ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, would converse with us and we with him — but when the time of prayer came, it was as though he did not know us, nor we him."

It has been narrated that God, Glorified be He, revealed to Moses, peace be upon him: "O Moses, when you remember Me, remember Me while your limbs tremble, and be at My remembrance submissive and tranquil. When you remember Me, place your tongue behind your heart. When you stand before Me, stand as a lowly servant stands, and commune with Me with a fearful heart and a truthful tongue."

It is also narrated that God, Exalted be He, revealed to him: "Say to the disobedient ones of your community: Let them not remember Me, for I have sworn upon Myself that whoever remembers Me, I remember him. So if they remember Me, I remember them with a curse." This concerns a disobedient one who is not heedless in his remembrance — so how would it be when heedlessness and disobedience are combined?

By the variation of the meanings we have mentioned in hearts, people are divided: into one who is heedless, completing his prayer while his heart is not present in a single moment of it; and into one who completes it while his heart is not absent for a single moment — indeed, perhaps he is so wholly occupied with it that he does not perceive what passes before him. For this reason, Muslim ibn Yasār did not notice the collapse of the pillar in the mosque, though the people gathered around it. And some used to attend the congregation for a long time and never knew who was on his right or left. The throbbing of Abraham's heart, God's prayers and peace be upon him, was heard for two miles. And a group would have their faces turn yellow and their flanks tremble.

All of this is not far-fetched, for its like is witnessed in the concerns of the people of this world and the fear of worldly kings — despite their incapacity, weakness, and the baseness of the gains obtained from them — so that a man enters upon a king or a vizier, relates his need to him, then exits; and if he were asked about those around him or about the king's garment, he could not report on it, because his concern for him distracted him from his garment and from those present around him. "For each are degrees according to what they have done" {«وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجَاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا»}. Each one's share of his prayer is in proportion to his fear, his submissiveness, and his reverence. For the place of God's, Glorified be He, regard is the hearts, not the outward movements.

For this reason, some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, said: "People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of their state in prayer — in tranquility and calm, and in the experience of bliss and delight therein." And indeed he spoke truly, for each is resurrected upon what he died, and dies upon what he lived. In that, the state of his heart is considered, not the state of his person. For from the attributes of hearts are the forms fashioned in the Hereafter. And none is saved except "one who comes to God with a sound heart" {«إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ»}. We ask God for good success through His gentleness and generosity.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Beneficial Remedy for the Presence of Heart (Ḥuḍūr al-Qalb)
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان الدواء النافع في حضور القلب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: دَوَاء (d-w-ā) — [Note: Root letters د، و، ء; per your constraint, I avoid previously used roots, but this root is mandated by the text itself; I shall anchor it via its semantic field without repeating the prohibited roots.]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — that which restores health (shifāʾ) and counteracts ailment; a curative agent, whether physical or spiritual.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the "remedy" (dawāʾ) for the heart is the removal of spiritual maladies (amrāḍ al-qulūb) through knowledge (ʿilm) and remembrance (dhikr), not mere physical medicine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — medicinal substance; metaphorical (majāz) — any means of rectifying a deficiency, here applied to the soul's distraction.
- Root: حُضُور (ḥ-ḍ-r) — [Root letters ح، ض، ر; again text-mandated, but I anchor via its semantic core without repeating prohibited roots.]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, attendance, being at hand; opposite of absence (ghaybah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In spiritual psychology, ḥuḍūr al-qalb is the heart's attentive engagement with the object of worship, free from heedlessness (ghaflah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical presence; metaphorical — the soul's focused awareness, as in "present with God" (ḥāḍir maʿa Allāh).
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — "dawāʾ al-nāfiʿ" (the beneficial remedy) is an attributive genitive where the adjective (nāfiʿ) qualifies the noun (dawāʾ), indicating a specific type of remedy, not a general one. The phrase "fī ḥuḍūr al-qalb" is a prepositional phrase (jār wa-majrūr) functioning as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) or adverbial specification, delimiting the scope of the remedy.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us set forth the exposition of the beneficial remedy for the presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) — that is, the means by which the heart may be brought to attend wholly upon the act of worship, and to be delivered from the wandering of thoughts and the intrusion of distracting concerns. Know that this remedy is compounded of two principles: the first is the earnest striving of the heart to draw itself away from all that is other than the object of worship; and the second is the firm restraint of the tongue from every utterance that does not pertain to the remembrance of God, until the heart, by repeated discipline, becomes habituated to presence and estranged from heedlessness. For the heart, like the limb, is trained by practice; and whosoever accustoms it to presence, it becomes present; and whosoever neglects it, it becomes scattered. This is the remedy whose efficacy is proven by the experience of the righteous, and whose benefit is witnessed by the soundness of the soul's state.

chapters.title_en: On the Means of Securing the Heart's Presence in Prayer and Repelling Distracting Thoughts
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن المؤمن لا بد أن يكون معظما لله عز وجل وخائفا منه وراجيا له
ومستحييا من تقصيره فلا ينفك عن هذه الأحوال بعد إيمانه وإن كانت قوتها
بقدر قوة يقينه فانفكاكه عنها في الصلاة لا سبب له إلا تفرق الفكر وتقسيم
الخاطر وغيبة القلب عن  المناجاة والغفلة عن الصلاة
ولا يلهي عن الصلاة إلا الخواطر الواردة الشاغلة فالدواء في إحضار القلب
هو دفع تلك الخواطر ولا يدفع الشيء إلا بدفع سببه فلتعلم سببه
وسبب موارد الخواطر إما أن يكون أمرا خارجا أو أمرا في ذاته باطنا
أما الخارج فما يقرع السمع أو يظهر للبصر فإن ذلك قد يختطف الهم حتى
يتبعه ويتصرف فيه ثم تنجر منه الفكرة إلى غيره ويتسلسل ويكون الإبصار سببا
للافتكار ثم تصير بعض تلك الأفكار سببا للبعض
ومن قويت نيته وعلت همته لم يلهه ما جرى على حواسه ولكن الضعيف لا بد وأن
يتفرق به فكره
وعلاجه قطع هذه الأسباب بأن يغض بصره أو يصلي في بيت مظلم أو لا يترك بين
يديه ما يشغل حسه ويقرب من حائط عند صلاته حتى لا تتسع مسافة بصره ويحترز
من الصلاة على الشوارع
PageV01P163
وفي المواضع المنقوشة المصنوعة وعلى الفرش المصبوغة
ولذلك كان المتعبدون يتعبدون في بيت صغير مظلم سعته قدر السجود ليكون ذلك
أجمع للهم
والأقوياء منهم كانوا يحضرون المساجد ويغضون البصر ولا يجاوزون به موضع
السجود ويرون كمال الصلاة في أن لا يعرفوا من على يمينهم وشمالهم
وكان ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما لا يدع في موضع الصلاة مصحفا ولا سيفا إلا
نزعه ولا كتابا إلا محاه
وأما الأسباب الباطنة فهي أشد فإن من تشعبت به الهموم في أودية الدنيا لا
ينحصر فكره في فن واحد بل لا يزال يطير من جانب إلى جانب وغض البصر لا
يغنيه فإن ما وقع في القلب من قبل كاف للشغل فهذا طريقه أن يرد النفس قهرا
إلى فهم ما يقرؤه في الصلاة ويشغلها به عن غيره ويعينه على ذلك أن يستعد له
قبل التحريم بأن يحدد على نفسه ذكر الآخرة وموقف المناجاة وخطر المقام بين
يدي الله سبحانه وهو المطلع ويفرغ قلبه قبل التحريم بالصلاة عما يهمه فلا
يترك لنفسه شغلا يلتفت إليه خاطره
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعثمان بن أبي شيبة  إني نسيت أن أقول
لك أن تخمر القدر الذي في البيت (1) فإنه لا ينبغي أن يكون في البيت شيء
يشغل الناس عن صلاتهم فهذا طريق تسكين الأفكار
فإن كان لا يسكن هوائج أفكاره بهذا الدواء المسكن فلا ينجيه إلا المسهل
الذي يقمع مادة الداء من أعماق العروق وهو أن ينظر في الأمور الصارفة
الشاغلة عن إحضار القلب ولا شك أنها تعود إلى مهماته وأنها إنما صارت مهمات
لشهواته فيعاقب نفسه بالنزوع عن تلك الشهوات وقطع تلك العلائق فكل ما يشغله
عن صلاته فهو ضد دينه وجند إبليس عدوه فإمساكه أضر عليه من إخراجه فيتخلص
منه بإخراجه كما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما لبس الخميصة التي أتاه بها
أبو جهم وعليها علم وصلى بها نزعها بعد صلاته وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
اذهبوا بها إلى أبي جهم فإنها ألهتني آنفا عن صلاتي وائتوني بأنبجانية أبي
جهم (2)
وأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتجديد شراك نعله ثم نظر إليه في
صلاته إذ كان جديدا فأمر أن ينزع منها ويرد الشراك الخلق (3)
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم قد احتذى نعلا فأعجبه حسنها فسجد وقال تواضعت
لربي عز وجل كي لا يمقتني ثم خرج بها فدفعها إلى أول سائل لقيه ثم أمر عليا
رضي الله عنه أن يشتري له نعلين سبتيتين جرداوين فلبسهما (4)
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم في يده خاتم من ذهب قبل التحريم وكان على المنبر
فرماه وقال شغلني هذا نظرة إليه ونظرة إليكم (5) وروي أن أبا طلحة صلى في
حائط وفيه شجر فأعجبه دبسي طار في الشجر يلتمس مخرجا فأتبعه بصره ساعة ثم
لم يدركم صلى فذكر لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أصابه من الفتنة ثم
قال يا رسول الله هو صدقة فضعه حيث شئت (6)
وعن رجل آخر أنه صلى في حائط له والنخل مطوقة بثمرها فنظر إليها فأعجبته
ولم يدر كم صلى فذكر ذلك لعثمان رضي الله عنه وقال هو صدقة فاجعله في سبيل
الله  عز وجل PageV01P164
فباعه عثمان بخمسين ألفا
فكانوا يفعلون ذلك قطعا لمادة الفكر وكفارة لما جرى من نقصان الصلاة وهذا
هو الدواء القاطع لمادة العلة ولا يغني غيره
فأما ما ذكرناه من التلطف بالتسكين والرد إلى فهم الذكر فذلك ينفع في
الشهوات الضعيفة والهمم التي لا تشغل إلا حواشي القلب
فأما الشهوة القوية المرهقة فلا ينفع فيها التسكين بل لا تزال تجاذبها
وتجاذبك ثم تغلبك وتنقضي جميع صلاتك في شغل المجاذبة
ومثاله رجل تحت شجرة أراد أن يصفو له فكره وكانت أصوات العصافير تشوش
عليه فلم يزل يطيرها بخشبة في يده ويعود إلى فكره فتعود العصافير فيعود إلى
التنفير بالخشبة فقيل له إن هذا أسير السواني ولا ينقطع فإن أردت الخلاص
فاقطع الشجرة
فكذلك شجرة الشهوات إذا تشعبت وتفرعت أغصانها انجذبت إليها الأفكار
انجذاب العصافير إلى الأشجار وانجذاب الذباب إلى الأقذار والشغل يطول في
دفعها فإن الذباب كلما ذب آب ولأجله سمي ذبابا
فكذلك الخواطر وهذه الشهوات كثيرة وقلما يخلو العبد عنها ويجمعها أصل
واحد وهو حب الدنيا وذلك رأس كل خطيئة وأساس كل نقصان ومنبع كل فساد
ومن انطوى باطنه على حب الدنيا حتى مال إلى شيء منها لا ليتزود منها ولا
ليستعين بها على الآخرة فلا يطمعن في أن تصفو له لذة المناجاة في الصلاة
فإن من فرح بالدنيا لا يفرح بالله سبحانه وبمناجاته
وهمة الرجل مع قرة عينه فإن كانت قرة عينه في الدنيا انصرف لا محالة
إليها همه ولكن مع هذا فلا ينبغي أن يترك المجاهدة ورد القلب إلى الصلاة
وتقليل الأسباب الشاغلة فهذا هو الدواء المر ولمرارته استبشعته الطباع
وبقيت العلة مزمنة وصار الداء عضالا حتى إن الأكابر اجتهدوا أن يصلوا
ركعتين لا يحدثوا أنفسهم فيها بأمور الدنيا فعجزوا عن ذلك فإذن لا مطمع فيه
لأمثالنا وليته سلم لنا من الصلاة شطرها أو ثلثها من الوسواس لنكون ممن خلط
عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا
وعلى الجملة فهمة الدنيا وهمة الآخرة في القلب مثل الماء الذي يصب في  قدح
مملوء بخل فبقدر ما ندخل فيه من الماء يخرج منه من الخل لا محالة ولا
يجتمعان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, attendance; the opposite of absence (ghaybah)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Presence of the heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) as the spiritual state requisite for valid devotional communion (munājāh)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical attendance; metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's attentiveness — the latter being the intended sense here
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — "If the cause is cut off, the effect ceases" (governing the logical structure of the therapeutic argument)
chapters.translation:
Know that the believer must necessarily hold Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in utmost veneration, fear Him, hope in Him, and feel shame before Him for his shortcomings. He is never free from these states after his faith, though their strength is proportionate to the strength of his certainty (yaqīn). His dissociation from them during prayer has no cause other than the scattering of thought, the division of the inner impulse, the heart's absence from the intimate communion (munājāh), and heedlessness of the prayer itself.

Nothing diverts one from prayer except the incoming thoughts that occupy the mind. The remedy, therefore, for summoning the heart lies in repelling those thoughts; and a thing is only repelled by repelling its cause. So let its cause be known.

The cause of incoming thoughts is either something external or something internal within the self itself. As for the external, it is whatever strikes the hearing or appears to the sight; for that may snatch away one's concern (himmah) until the heart follows it and becomes absorbed in it. Then from it, reflection drags on to something else, and so it chains onward: sight becomes the cause of thought, and then some of those thoughts become the cause of others.

Whoever's intention is strong and whose aspiration is lofty is not diverted by what passes over his senses; but the weak one's thought is inevitably scattered by it.

Its treatment is to cut off these causes — by lowering the gaze, or by praying in a dark room, or by not leaving before him anything that would occupy his sense, and by drawing near to a wall during his prayer so that the span of his vision does not widen. He should also be wary of praying on thoroughfares, and in places adorned with ornamentation and craftsmanship, and upon dyed carpets.

For this reason, the devoted worshippers used to worship in a small, dark room whose breadth was only the measure of prostration, so that this might be more concentrating for the concern (hamm). The strong among them, however, would attend the mosques and lower their gaze, not letting it pass beyond the place of prostration; and they deemed perfection of prayer to consist in not knowing who was on their right or their left.

Ibn ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — would not leave in his place of prayer any muṣḥaf or sword without removing it, nor any book without erasing it.

As for the internal causes, they are more severe. For whoever's concerns have branched out into the valleys of this world, his thought is not confined to a single channel; rather, it keeps flying from one side to another, and lowering the gaze does not avail him, for what has already settled in the heart from before is sufficient to occupy him. The way for such a one is to force the soul, by compulsion, to grasp the meaning of what he recites in prayer, and to occupy it with that to the exclusion of all else. He is aided in this by preparing beforehand, before the opening takbīr (taḥrīm), by impressing upon himself the remembrance of the Hereafter, the station of intimate communion, and the gravity of standing before Allah — Glorified be He — Who is the All-Seeing Watcher. And before the takbīr, he should empty his heart of whatever concerns him, leaving his soul no occupation to which his thought might turn.

The Messenger of Allah — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — said to ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah: "I forgot to tell you to cover the cooking-pot that is in the house, for it is not fitting that there be in the house anything that would distract people from their prayer." {«إني نسيت أن أقول لك أن تخمر القدر الذي في البيت فإنه لا ينبغي أن يكون في البيت شيء يشغل الناس عن صلاتهم»} This, then, is the way of calming thoughts.

But if his thoughts' agitations are not stilled by this calming remedy, then nothing saves him except the purgative that suppresses the very matter of the disease from the depths of the veins — namely, that he examine the matters that divert and occupy him away from summoning the heart. There is no doubt that they revert to his worldly concerns (muhimmāt), and that they became concerns only because of his appetites (shahawāt). So let him punish his soul by renouncing those appetites and cutting those attachments. For everything that occupies him away from his prayer is the antagonist of his religion and the soldier of Iblīs, his enemy; retaining it is more harmful to him than expelling it. So let him rid himself of it by expelling it — as it is related that when the Prophet — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — wore the cloak (khamīṣah) that Abū Jahm had brought him, which bore a decorative mark, and prayed in it, he removed it after his prayer and said: "Take it back to Abū Jahm, for it distracted me just now from my prayer; and bring me the plain woollen garment (anbijāniyyah) of Abū Jahm." {«اذهبوا بها إلى أبي جهم فإنها ألهتني آنفا عن صلاتي وائتوني بأنبجانية أبي جهم»}

And the Messenger of Allah — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — ordered the renewal of the strap of his sandal; then, when it was new, he looked at it during his prayer, so he ordered that it be removed and the old strap restored.

And it is related that he — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — had put on a pair of sandals, and their beauty pleased him; so he prostrated and said: "I humble myself to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, lest He abhor me." Then he went out with them and gave them to the first beggar he met. Then he commanded ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — to buy him two plain, unornamented sandals of tanned leather (sibtīyatayn jardāwayn), and he wore them.

And the Prophet — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — had in his hand a gold ring before the prohibition; and while he was on the pulpit, he cast it away and said: "This distracted me — a glance at it and a glance at you." {«شغلني هذا نظرة إليه ونظرة إليكم»} And it is related that Abū Ṭalḥah prayed in an enclosed garden in which there were trees, and a wild pigeon (dubsī) flying among the trees seeking an exit pleased him; he followed it with his gaze for a while, then he no longer knew how much he had prayed. He mentioned to the Messenger of Allah — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — what trial had befallen him, then said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is a charity; place it wherever you wish." {«يا رسول الله هو صدقة فضعه حيث شئت»}

And concerning another man, that he prayed in his garden while the palm-trees were girded with their fruit; he looked at them, and they pleased him, and he did not know how much he had prayed. He mentioned that to ʿUthmān — may Allah be pleased with him — and said: "It is a charity; place it in the path of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." So ʿUthmān sold it for fifty thousand [dirhams].

Thus they used to do this — cutting off the matter of thought, and as expiation for what had passed of the prayer's deficiency. And this is the remedy that severs the very matter of the malady; nothing else suffices.

As for what we mentioned of gentleness in calming and returning [the heart] to the understanding of the remembrance (dhikr), that avails only against weak appetites and concerns that occupy only the fringes of the heart. But as for the strong, overwhelming appetite, calming does not avail against it; rather, it keeps tugging at you and you at it, then it overcomes you, and your entire prayer passes away in the business of that tug-of-war.

Its parable: a man beneath a tree who wished his thought to be clear, but the voices of the sparrows disturbed him. He kept shooing them away with a stick in his hand, then returning to his thought; then the sparrows would return, and he would return to shooing them with the stick. It was said to him: "This one is a captive of the water-wheel (sawānī); it will never cease. If you want deliverance, cut down the tree."
