For this reason, when the reciter reads His saying—mighty and majestic is He: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ»} ("Have you considered what you sow"), {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ»} ("Have you considered what you emit"), {«أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ»} ("Have you considered the water you drink"), {«أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ»} ("Have you considered the fire you kindle")—he should not confine his gaze to water, fire, sowing, and semen. Rather, let him contemplate the semen—a drop of uniform parts—then look at how it divides into flesh, bone, veins, and nerves; how its organs are formed in diverse shapes of head, hand, foot, liver, heart, and others; then at what appears within it of noble attributes—hearing, sight, intellect, and others; then at what appears within it of blameworthy attributes—anger, lust, pride, ignorance, denial, and disputation—as He said—exalted is He: {«أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الْإِنسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُّبِينٌ»} ("Does man not see that We created him from a drop, and behold, he is a manifest adversary"). Let him contemplate these wonders to ascend from them to the wonder of wonders—the attribute from which these marvels issued. Thus he continues looking at the craftsmanship until he sees the Craftsman.

As for the states of the prophets (peace be upon them): when he hears how they were denied, struck, and some of them killed, let him understand from it the attribute of God's—mighty and majestic is He—self-sufficiency from the messengers and those to whom they were sent; that were He to destroy them all, it would not affect His dominion in the least. And when he hears of their victory in the end, let him understand God's power—mighty and majestic is He—and His will to support the truth.

As for the states of the deniers—like ʿĀd and Thamūd and what befell them—let his understanding from it be the sensing of fear of His severity and His retribution. And let his portion from it be taking heed in himself: that if he is heedless, ill-mannered, and deluded by the respite given him, perhaps retribution will overtake him and the decree will be executed upon him.

Likewise, when he hears the description of Paradise and the Fire and the rest of what is in the Qur'an—it is not possible to exhaust what is understood from it, for that has no end. Each servant has only according to his allotment. {«وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ»} ("Neither fresh nor dry but in a clear Book"). {«قُل لَّوْ كَانَ الْبَحْرُ مِدَادًا لِّكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ الْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَاتُ رَبِّي وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ مَدَدًا»} ("Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as replenishment"). For this reason ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) said: "Were I to wish, I would load seventy camels with the commentary of the Opening Sūrah."

The purpose of what we have mentioned is to point to the path of understanding, that its door may open. As for exhaustiveness, there is no aspiration for it. And whoever has no understanding of what is in the Qur'an—even at the lowest degree—enters into His saying—exalted is He: {«وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ ۖ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِندِكَ قَالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ مَاذَا قَالَ آنِفًا ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ»} ("And among them are those who listen to you, until when they depart from you they say to those who were given knowledge: 'What did he say just now?' Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed"). The seal is the obstacles we shall mention in the section on the obstacles to understanding. And it has been said: "The seeker is not a seeker until he finds in the Qur'an everything he desires, and knows from it the deficient from the abundant, and is rendered independent by the Master from the servants."

The sixth is self-emptying of the obstacles to understanding. For most people are prevented from understanding the meanings of the Qur'an by causes and veils that Satan has lowered over their hearts, so that the wonders of the Qur'an's secrets are blinded to them. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Were it not that the devils hover around the hearts of the children of Adam, they would look upon the Kingdom (malakūt)." And the meanings of the Qur'an are part of the malakūt. Everything that is hidden from the senses and is perceived only by the light of inner vision is of the malakūt.

The veils of understanding are four. The first is that one's concern be turned entirely to perfecting the letters by bringing them out from their points of articulation. A devil is appointed over this, charged with the reciters, to turn them away from understanding the meanings of the Word of God—mighty and majestic is He. He keeps driving them to repeat a letter, making them imagine that it has not come out from its point of articulation. Such a one's reflection is confined to the points of articulation of letters—how then can meanings be unveiled to him? The greatest laughter for Satan is the one who obeys such deception.

The second is that one be a blind follower (muqallid) of a school (madhhab) he has heard by imitation, frozen upon it, with partisanship for it fixed in his soul by mere following of what he has heard, without arriving at it through inner vision and direct witnessing. Such a person is shackled by his belief from going beyond it; he cannot conceive in his mind other than his belief. His gaze is arrested upon what he has heard. If a lightning-flash gleams from afar and a meaning appears to him that diverges from what he has heard, the devil of imitation attacks him saying: "How can this occur to your mind, when it contradicts the belief of your fathers?" So he sees that as a deception from Satan, and distances himself from it and guards against the like of it.

It was for the like of this that the Sufis said: "Knowledge is a veil." By "knowledge" they meant the beliefs upon which most people persist by mere imitation, or by mere dialectical phrases that the partisans of schools have polished and cast to them. As for true knowledge—which is unveiling and direct witnessing by the light of inner vision—how could it be a veil, when it is the ultimate object of seeking? This imitation may be false, and thus be an obstacle—like one who believes concerning "istiwā'" upon the Throne that it is physical settling and stability. If, for example, it occurs to him concerning "al-Quddūs" (the Holy) that He is sanctified above everything that is possible for His creatures, his imitation would not allow that to settle in his soul. Were it to settle in his soul, it would lead to a second and third unveiling, and would continue. But he hastens to repel that from his mind because it contradicts his false imitation. And it may be true, yet still be an obstacle to understanding and unveiling. For the truth that creation is charged to believe has ranks and degrees; it has an apparent beginning and a hidden depth. The freezing of one's nature upon the apparent prevents reaching the hidden depth—as we mentioned in the distinction between apparent and inner knowledge in the Book of the Foundations of Beliefs (Qawāʿid al-ʿAqā'id).

The third is that one be persistent upon a sin, or characterized by pride, or afflicted generally with an obeyed passion for this world. For that is a cause of the heart's darkness and rust. It is like filth upon a mirror, preventing the polish of truth from manifesting within it. It is the greatest veil of the heart, and by it most are veiled. The more the lusts accumulate, the more the meanings of the Word are concealed; and the lighter the burdens of this world upon the heart, the nearer the manifestation of meaning within it. The heart is like a mirror; lusts are like rust; and the meanings of the Qur'an are like the images that appear in the mirror. The discipline of the heart by removing lusts is like the polishing and cleansing of the mirror. For this reason he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When my community magnifies the dinar and the dirham, the awe of Islam is stripped from it; and when they abandon commanding the good and forbidding the evil, they are deprived of the blessing of revelation." Al-Fuḍayl said: "He means they are deprived of understanding the Qur'an."

God—mighty and majestic is He—has made turning in repentance (inābah) a condition for understanding and remembrance. He said—exalted is He: {«تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُّنِيبٍ»} ("An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance"), and He said—mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ إِلَّا مَن يُنِيبُ»} ("And none remembers except one who turns in repentance"), and He said—exalted is He: {«إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ»} ("Only those of understanding remember"). So the one who prefers the delusion of this world over the bliss of the Hereafter is not of those of understanding; therefore the secrets of the Book are not unveiled to him.

The fourth is that one has read an outward commentary (tafsīr ẓāhir) and believes that there is no meaning for the words of the Qur'an except what is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and others; that what lies beyond that is interpretation by opinion (tafsīr bi-l-ra'y); and that "whoever interprets the Qur'an by his opinion has taken his seat in the Fire." This too is among the great veils. We shall explain the meaning of interpretation by opinion in the fourth chapter, and that it does not contradict the saying of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him): "Except that God gives a servant understanding in the Qur'an"—and that were the meaning merely the apparent transmitted one, people would not have differed over it.

The seventh is particularization (takhṣīṣ)—that one deem himself the one intended by every address in the Qur'an. If he hears a command or prohibition, he deems himself the one commanded or forbidden. If he hears a promise or threat, likewise. If he hears the stories of the ancients and the prophets, he knows that mere storytelling is not intended; rather, the intent is that he take heed and extract from its folds what he needs. There is no story in the Qur'an except that its context is for a benefit regarding the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and his community. For this reason He said—exalted is He: {«مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ»} ("That by which We strengthen your heart"). So let the servant deem that God strengthened his heart by what He recounts to him of the states of the prophets and their patience under harm and their steadfastness in religion, awaiting God's victory.

How should he not deem this, when the Qur'an was not sent down to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) for the Messenger alone, but is a healing, a guidance, a mercy, and a light for the worlds? For this reason God—exalted is He—commanded all to give thanks for the blessing of the Book. He said—exalted is He: {«وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُم بِهِ»} ("And remember the favor of God upon you and what He sent down to you of the Book and the Wisdom, admonishing you thereby"), and He said—mighty and majestic is He: {«لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ»} ("We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance—will you not then reason?"), and {«وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ»} ("And We sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them"), and {«كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ»} ("Thus God strikes for the people their examples"), and {«وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم»} ("And follow the best of what was sent down to you from your Lord"), and {«هَٰذَا بَصَائِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ»} ("This is insights for the people and a guidance and a mercy for a people who are certain"), and {«هَٰذَا بَيَانٌ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ»} ("This is an explanation for the people and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing"). When the address intends all people, it intends each individual. So this single reciter is intended—what has he to do with other people? Let him deem himself the one intended. God—exalted is He—said: {«وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنُ لِأُنذِرَكُم بِهِ وَمَن بَلَغَ»} ("And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomsoever it reaches"). Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: "Whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is as though God spoke to him directly."

When he deems this, he will not make the study of the Qur'an his mere occupation; rather, he will read it as a servant reads the letter of his master, which he wrote to him to contemplate and act upon. For this reason one of the scholars said: "This Qur'an is letters that have come to us from our Lord—mighty and majestic is He—containing His covenants; we contemplate them in the prayers, pause upon them in seclusion, and execute them in acts of obedience and the followed Sunnahs."

Mālik ibn Dīnār used to say: "What has the Qur'an sown in your hearts, O people of the Qur'an? The Qur'an is the spring of the believer, just as rain is the spring of the earth."

And Qatādah said: "No one has sat with this Qur'an but that he rose with an increase or a decrease." God said—exalted is He: {«هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا»} ("It is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it increases the wrongdoers only in loss").

The eighth is being affected (ta'aththur)—that one's heart be affected by diverse impressions according to the diversity of the verses. Thus, according to each understanding, there is a state and a finding (wajd) with which the heart is characterized—of sorrow, fear, hope, and others. Whenever one's knowledge is complete, godly fear (khashyah) predominates over the states of his heart. For the constricting is predominant over the verses of the Qur'an: one does not see the mention of forgiveness and mercy except conjoined with conditions that the knower falls short of attaining—like His saying—mighty and majestic is He: {«وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ»} ("And indeed I am most forgiving"), then He followed it with four conditions: {«لِّمَن تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَىٰ»} ("for whoever repents, believes, does righteous work, and then is guided"); and His saying—exalted is He: {«وَالْعَصْرِ * إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ * إِلَّ

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Chapter on Understanding the Qur’an and Its Interpretation by Personal Opinion (tafsīr bi-l-ra’y) Without Transmission (naql)
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| الباب الرابع في فهم القرآن وتفسيره بالرأي من غير نقل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Comprehension, grasping the inner sense of speech; the mind’s apprehension of meaning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intellectual perception of the intended signification (dalālah) of divine discourse, distinct from mere hearing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual understanding; metaphorical (majāz) — superficial or conjectural grasping.
- Root: ر-أ-ي (r-’-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Opinion, personal judgment, or considered view; also vision and discernment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, ra’y denotes ungrounded subjective reasoning, opposed to transmitted authority (samʿ) and sound inference (naẓar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — sight/vision; metaphorical — intellectual opinion, often pejorative when detached from revelation.
- Root: ن-ق-ل (n-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Transmission, conveyance, or citation from an authoritative source.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The chain of narrated reports (riwāyah) from the Prophet and the Salaf, forming the basis of valid exegesis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical transfer; metaphorical — the unbroken transmission of knowledge.
- Sībawayh Rule: The construct phrase (al-bāb fī...) — a chapter heading governed by the preposition fī, indicating the scope of inquiry; the genitive construction (fahm al-Qur’ān) marks the object of the chapter’s subject matter.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the fourth chapter, concerning the understanding of the Qur’an and its interpretation by personal opinion (tafsīr bi-l-ra’y) without reliance on transmitted authority (naql).

chapters.title_en: On the Comprehension of the Qur'an's Inner Meanings and the Limits of Exoteric Interpretation
chapters.arabic_text:
لعلك تقول عظمت الأمر فيما سبق في فهم أسرار القرآن وما ينكشف لأرباب
القلوب الزكية من معانيه
PageV01P288
فكيف يستحب ذلك وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من فسر القرآن برأيه فليتبوأ
مقعده من النار (1) وعن هذا شنع أهل العلم بظاهر التفسير على أهل التصوف من
المقصرين المنسوبين إلى التصوف في تأويل كلمات في القرآن على خلاف ما نقل
عن ابن عباس وسائر المفسرين وذهبوا إلى أنه كفر فإن صح ما قاله أهل التفسير
فما معنى فهم القرآن سوى حفظ تفسيره وإن لم يصح ذلك فما معنى قوله صلى الله
عليه وسلم من فسر القرآن برأيه فليتبوأ مقعده  من النار فاعلم أن من زعم أن
لا معنى للقرآن إلا ما ترجمه ظاهر التفسير فهو مخبر عن حد نفسه وهو مصيب في
الإخبار عن نفسه ولكنه مخطئ في الحكم برد الخلق كافة إلى درجته التي هي حده
ومحطه بل الأخبار والآثار تدل على أن في معاني القرآن متسعا لأرباب الفهم
(2) قال علي رضي الله عنه إلا أن يؤتى الله عبدا فهما في القرآن فإن لم يكن
سوى الترجمة المنقولة فما ذلك الفهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن للقرآن
ظهرا وبطنا وحدا ومطلعا (3) ويروى أيضا عن ابن مسعود موقوفا عليه وهو من
علماء التفسير فما معنى الظهر والبطن والحد والمطلع وقال علي كرم الله وجهه
لو شئت لأوقرت سبعين بعيرا من تفسير فاتحة الكتاب فما معناه وتفسير ظاهرها
في غاية الاقتصار وقال أبو الدرداء لا يفقه الرجل حتى يجعل للقرآن وجوها
وقد قال بعض العلماء لكل آية ستون ألف فهم وما بقي من فهمها أكثر وقال
آخرون القرآن يحوي سبعة وسبعين ألف علم ومائتي علم إذ كل كلمة علم ثم
يتضاعف ذلك أربعة أضعاف إذ لكل كلمة ظاهر وباطن وحد ومطلع وترديد رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم عشرين مرة (4) لا يكون إلا
لتدبره باطن معانيها وإلا فترجمتها وتفسيرها ظاهر لا يحتاج مثله إلى تكرير
وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه من أراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليتدبر القرآن
وذلك لا يحصل بمجرد تفسير الظاهر وبالجملة فالعلوم كلها داخلة في أفعال
الله عز وجل وصفاته وفي القرآن شرح ذاته وأفعاله وصفاته وهذه العلوم لا
نهاية لها وفي القرآن إشارة إلى مجامعها والمقامات في التعمق في تفصيله
راجع إلى فهم القرآن ومجرد ظاهره التفسير لا يشير إلى ذلك بل كل ما أشكل
فيه على النظار واختلف فيه الخلائق في النظريات والمعقولات ففي القرآن إليه
رموز ودلالات عليه يختص أهل الفهم بدركها فيكف يفي بذلك ترجمة ظاهره
وتفسيره ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرءوا القرآن والتمسوا غرائبه  (5)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث علي كرم الله وجهه والذي بعثني بالحق نبيا
ليفترقن أمتي عن أصل دينها وجماعتها على اثنتين وسبعين فرقة كلها ضالة مضلة
يدعون إلى النار فإذا كان ذلك فعليكم بكتاب الله عز وجل فإن فيه نبأ من كان
قبلكم ونبأ ما يأتي بعدكم وحكم ما بينكم من خالفه من الجبابرة قصمه الله عز
وجل ومن ابتغى العلم في غيره أضله الله عز وجل وهو حبل الله المتين ونوره
المبين وشفاؤه النافع عصمة لمن تمسك به ونجاة لمن اتبعه لا يموج فيقوم ولا
يزيغ فيستقيم ولا تنقضي عجائبه ولا يخلقه كثرة الترديد (6) PageV01P289
الحديث وفي حديث حذيفة لما أخبره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالاختلاف
والفرقة بعده قال فقلت يا رسول الله فماذا تأمرني إن أدركت ذلك فقال تعلم
كتاب الله واعمل بما فيه فهو المخرج من ذلك قال فأعدت عليه ذلك ثلاثا فقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثا تعلم كتاب الله عز وجل واعمل بما فيه ففيه النجاة
(1) وقال علي كرم الله وجهه من فهم القرآن فسر به جمل العلم أشار به إلى أن
القرآن يشير إلى مجامع العلوم كلها وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله
تعالى ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا يعني الفهم في القرآن وقال عز
وجل ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما سمى ما آتاهما علما وحكما وخصص
ما انفرد به سليمان بالتفطن له باسم الفهم وجعله مقدما على الحكم والعلم
فهذه الأمور تدل على أن في فهم معاني القرآن مجالا رحبا ومتسعا بالغا وأن
المنقول من ظاهر التفسير ليس منتهى الإدراك فيه
فأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من فسر القرآن برأيه ونهيه عنه (2) صلى
الله عليه وسلم وقول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه أي أرض تقلني وأي سماء تظلني إذا
قلت في القرآن برأيي إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في الأخبار والآثار في النهي عن
تفسير القرآن بالرأي فلا يخلو إما أن يكون المراد به  الاقتصار على النقل
والمسموع وترك الاستنباط والاستقلال بالفهم أو المراد به أمرا آخر وباطل
قطعا أن يكون المراد به أن لا يتكلم أحد في القرآن إلا بما يسمعه لوجوه
أحدها أنه يشترط أن يكون ذلك مسموعا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ومسندا إليه وذلك مما لا يصادف إلا في بعض القرآن فأما ما يقوله ابن عباس
وابن مسعود من أنفسهم فينبغي أن لا يقبل ويقال هو تفسير بالرأي لأنهم لم
يسمعوه من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكذا غيرهم من الصحابة رضي الله
عنهم
والثاني أن الصحابة والمفسرين اختلفوا في تفسير بعض الآيات فقالوا فيها
أقاويل مختلفة لا يمكن الجمع بينها وسماع جميعها من رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم محال ولو كان الواحد مسموعا لرد الباقي فتبين على القطع أن كل
مفسر قال في المعنى بما ظهر له باستنباطه حتى قالوا في الحروف التي في
أوائل السور سبعة أقاويل مختلفة لا يمكن الجمع بينها فقيل إن الر هي حروف
من الرحمن وقيل إن الألف الله واللام لطيف والراء رحيم وقيل غير ذلك والجمع
بين الكل غير ممكن فكيف يكون الكل مسموعا
والثالث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا لابن عباس رضي الله عنه وقال اللهم
فقه في الدين وعلمه التأويل (3) فإن كان التأويل مسموعا كالتنزيل ومحفوظا
مثله فما معنى تخصيصه بذلك
والرابع أنه قال عز وجل لعلمه الذي يستنبطونه منهم فأثبت لأهل العلم
استنباطا ومعلوم أنه وراء السماع
وجملة ما نقلناه من الآثار في فهم القرآن يناقض هذا الخيال فبطل أن يشترط
السماع في التأويل وجاز لكل واحد أن يستنبط من القرآن بقدر فهمه وحد عقله
وأما النهي فإنه ينزل على أحد وجهين أحدهما أن يكون له في الشيء رأي وإليه
ميل من طبعه وهواه فيتأول القرآن على وفق رأيه وهواه وليحتج على تصحيح غرضه
ولو لم يكن له ذلك الرأي والهوى لكان لا يلوح له من القرآن ذلك المعنى وهذا
تارة يكون مع العلم كالذي  يحتج ببعض آيات القرآن على تصحيح بدعته وهو يعلم
أنه ليس المراد بالآية ذلك ولكن يلبس به على خصمه وتارة يكون مع الجهل ولكن
إذا كانت الآية محتملة فيميل فهمه إلى الوجه الذي PageV01P290
يوافق غرضه ويرجح ذلك الجانب برأيه وهواه فيكون قد فسر برأيه أي رأيه هو
الذي حمله على ذلك التفسير ولولا رأيه لما كان يترجح عنده ذلك الوجه وتارة
قد يكون له غرض صحيح فيطلب له دليلا من القرآن ويستدل عليه مما يعلم أنه ما
أريد به كمن يدعو إلى الاستغفار بالأسحار فيستدل بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
تسحروا فإن في السحور بركة (1) ويزعم أن المراد به التسحر بالذكر وهو يعلم
أن المراد به الأكل وكالذي يدعو إلى مجاهدة القلب القاسي فيقول قال الله عز
وجل اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى ويشير إلى قلبه ويومئ إلى أنه المراد بفرعون
وهذا الجنس قد يستعمله بعض الوعاظ في المقاصد الصحيحة تحسينا للكلام
وترغيبا للمستمع وهو ممنوع وقد تستعمله الباطنية في المقاصد الفاسدة لتغرير
الناس ودعوتهم إلى مذهبهم الباطل فينزلون القرآن على وفق رأيهم ومذهبهم على
أمور يعلمون قطعا أنها غير مرادة به فهذه الفنون أحد وجهي المنع من التفسير
بالرأي ويكون المراد بالرأي الرأي الفاسد الموافق للهوى دون الاجتهاد
الصحيح والرأي يتناول الصحيح والفاسد والموافق للهوى قد يخصص باسم الرأي
والوجه الثاني أن يتسارع إلى تفسير القرآن بظاهر العربية من غير استظهار
بالسماع والنقل فيما يتعلق بغرائب القرآن وما فيه من الألفاظ المبهمة
والمبدلة وما فيه من الاختصار والحذف والإضمار والتقديم والتأخير فمن لم
يحكم بظاهر التفسير وبادر إلى استنباط المعاني بمجرد فهم العربية كثر غلطه
ودخل في زمرة من يفسر بالرأي
فالنقل والسماع لا بد منه في ظاهر التفسير أولا ليتقي به مواضع الغلط ثم
بعد ذلك يتسع التفهم والاستنباط والغرائب التي لا تفهم إلا بالسماع كثيرة
ونحن نرمز إلى جمل منها ليستدل بها على أمثالها ويعلم أنه لا يجوز التهاون
بحفظ التفسير الظاهر أولا ولا مطمع في الوصول  إلى الباطن قبل إحكام الظاهر
ومن ادعى فهم أسرار القرآن ولم يحكم التفسير الظاهر فهو كمن يدعي البلوغ
إلى صدر البيت قبل مجاوزة الباب أو يدعي فهم مقاصد الأتراك من كلامهم وهو
لا يفهم لغة الترك فإن ظاهر التفسير يجري مجرى تعليم اللغة التي لا بد منها
للفهم وما لا بد فيه من السماع فنون كثيرة منها الإيجار بالحذف والإضمار
كقوله تعالى وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها معناه آية مبصرة فظلموا
أنفسهم بقتلها فالناظر إلى ظاهر العربية يظن أن المراد به أن الناقة كانت
مبصرة ولم تكن عمياء ولم يدر أنهم بماذا ظلموا غيرهم أو أنفسهم وقوله تعالى
وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم أي حب العجل فحذف الحب وقوله عز وجل إذا
لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات أي ضعف عذاب الأحياء وضعف عذاب الموتى فحذف
العذاب وأبدل الأحياء والموتى بذكر الحياة والموت وكل ذلك جائز في فصيح
اللغة
وقوله تعالى واسئل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها أي أهل
العير فالأهل فيهما محذوف مضمر وقوله عز وجل ثقلت في السموات والأرض معناه
خفيت على أهل السموات والأرض والشيء إذا خفي ثقل فأبدل اللفظ به وأقيم في
مقام على وأضمر الأهل وحذف
وقوله تعالى وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون أي شكر رزقكم وقوله عز وجل وآتنا
ما وعدتنا على رسلك أي على ألسنة رسلك فحذف ألسنة وقوله تعالى إنا أنزلناه
في ليلة القدر أراد القرآن وما سبق له ذكر
وقال عز وجل حتى توارت الحجاب أراد الشمس وما سبق لها ذكر وقوله تعالى
والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى أي
يقولون ما نعبدهم
وقوله عز وجل فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة
فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما
أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله قل كل من عند الله
وسبق إلى الفهم منه مذهب  القدرية ومنها المنقول المنقلب كقوله تعالى وطور
سينين أي طور PageV01P291
سيناء سلام على آل ياسين أي على الياس وقيل إدريس لأن في حرف ابن مسعود
سلام على إدراسين ومنها المكرر القاطع لوصل الكلام في الظاهر كقوله عز وجل
وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وقوله عز وجل
قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم معناه الذين
استكبروا لمن آمن من الذين استضعفوا ومنها المقدم والمؤخر وهو مظنة الغلط
كقوله عز وجل ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى معناه لولا
الكلمة وأجل مسمى لكان لزاما ولولاه لكان نصبا كاللزام وقوله تعالى يسألونك
كأنك حفي عنها أي يسألونك عنها كأنك حفي بها وقوله عز وجل لهم مغفرة ورزق
كريم كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى
قوله السابق قل الأنفال لله والرسول كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق أي فصارت
أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر
بالتقوى وغيره ومن هذا النوع قوله عز وجل حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول
إبراهيم لأبيه الآية ومنها المبهم وهو اللفظ المشترك بين معن من كلمة أو
حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ضرب
الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز
وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل
والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات
الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان
الاستحقاق
وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غير شي أم هم الخالقون أي من غير خالق فربما
يتوهم به أنه يدل على أنه لا يخلق شيء إلا من شيء
وأما القرين فكقوله عز وجل وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد ألقيا في جهنم  كل
كفار أراد به الملك الموكل به وقوله تعالى قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن
كان أراد به الشيطان
وأما الأمة فتطلق على ثمانية أوجه الأمة الجماعة كقوله تعالى وجد عليه
أمة من الناس يسقون وأتباع الأنبياء كقولك عن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
ورجل جامع للخير يقتدى به كقوله تعالى إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله والأمة
الدين كقوله عز وجل إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله
عز وجل إلى أمة معدودة وقوله عز وجل وادكر بعد أمة والأمة القامة يقال فلان
حسن الأمة أي القامة وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال صلى الله
عليه وسلم يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده (1) والأمة يقال هذه أمة زيد
أي أم زيد والروح أيضا ورد في القرآن على معان كثيرة فلا نطول بإيرادها
وكذلك قد يقع الإبهام في الحروف مثل قوله عز وجل قأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به
جمعا فالهاء الأولى كناية عن الحوافر وهي الموريات أي أثرن بالحوافر نقعا
والثانية كناية عن الإغارة وهي المغيرات صبحا فوسطن به جمعا جمع المشركون
فأغاروا بجمعهم وقوله تعالى فأنزلنا به الماء يعني السحاب فأخرجنا به من كل
الثمرات يعني الماء وأمثال هذا في القرآن لا ينحصر ومنها التدريج في البيان
كقوله عز وجل شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن إذ لم يظهر به أنه ليل أو
نهار وبان بقوله عز وجل إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ولم يظهر به أي ليلة
فظهر بقوله تعالى إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر وربما يظن في الظاهر الاختلاف
بين هذه الآيات فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يغني فيه إلا النقل والسماع فالقرآن من
أوله إلى آخره غير خال عن هذا الجنس لأنه أنزل بلغة العرب فكان مشتملا على
أصناف كلامهم من إيجاز وتطويل وإضمار وحذف وإبدال وتقديم وتأخير ليكون ذلك
مفحما لهم ومعجزا في حقهم فكل من اكتفى بفهم ظاهر العربية وبادر إلى تفسير
القرآن ولم يستظهر بالسماع والنقل  في هذه الأمور فهو داخل فيمن فسر القرآن
برأيه مثل أن يفهم من الأمة المعنى الأشهر منه فيميل طبعه ورأيه إليه فإذا
سمعه في موضع آخر مال برأيه إلى ما سمعه من مشهور PageV01P292
معناه وترك تتبع النقل في كثير معانيه فهذا ما يمكن أن يكون منهيا عنه
دون التفهم لأسرار المعاني كما سبق فإذا حصل السماع بأمثال هذه الأمور علم
ظاهر التفسير وهو ترجمة الألفاظ ولا يكفي ذلك في فهم حقائق المعاني ويدرك
الفرق بين حقائق المعاني وظاهر التفسير بمثال وهو إن الله عز وجل قال وما
رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى فظاهره تفسير واضح وحقيقة معناه غامض فإنه
إثبات للرمي ونفي له وهما متضادان في الظاهر ما لم يفهم أنه رمي من وجه ولم
يرم من وجه ومن الوجه الذي لم يرم رماه الله عز وجل
وكذلك قال تعالى قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم فإذا كانوا هم المقاتلين
كيف يكون الله سبحانه هو المعذب وإن كان الله تعالى هو المعذب بتحريك
أيديهم فما معنى أمرهم بالقتال فحقيقة هذا يستمد من بحر عظيم من علوم
المكاشفات لا يغني عنه ظاهر التفسير وهو أن يعلم وجه ارتباط الأفعال
بالقدرة الحادثة ويفهم وجه ارتباط القدرة بقدرة الله عز وجل حتى ينكشف بعد
إيضاح أمور كثيرة غامضة صدق قوله عز وجل وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى
ولعل العمر لو أنفق في استكشاف أسرار هذا المعنى وما يرتبط بمقدماته
ولواحقه لانقضى العمر قبل استيفاء جميع لواحقه وما من كلمة من القرآن إلا
وتحقيقها محوج إلى مثل ذلك وإنما ينكشف للراسخين في العلم من أسراره بقدر
غزارة علومهم وصفاء قلوبهم وتوفر دواعيهم على التدبر وتجردهم للطلب ويكون
لكل واحد حد في الترقي إلى درجة أعلى منه فأما الاستيفاء فلا مطمع فيه ولو
كان البحر مدادا والأشجار أقلاما فأسرار كلمات الله لا نهاية لها فتنفد
الأبحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات الله عز وجل
فمن هذا الوجه تتفاوت الخلق في الفهم بعد الاشتراك في معرفة  ظاهر التفسير
وظاهر التفسير لا يغني عنه ومثاله فهم بعض أرباب القلوب من قوله صلى الله
عليه وسلم في سجوده أعوذ برضاك من سخطك وأعوذ بمعافاتك من عقوبتك وأعوذ بك
منك لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (1) أنه قبل له اسجد واقترب
فوجد القرب في السجود فنظر إلى الصفات فاستعاذ ببعضها من بعض فإن الرضا
والسخط وصفان ثم زاد قربه فاندرج القرب الأول فيه فرقي إلى الذات فقال أعوذ
بك منك ثم زاد قربه بما استحيا به من الاستعاذة على بساط القرب فالتجأ إلى
الثناء فأثنى بقوله لا أحصي ثناء عليك ثم علم أن ذلك قصور فقال أنت كما
أثنيت على نفسك فهذه خواطر تفتح لأرباب القلوب ثم لها أغوار وراء هذا وهو
فهم معنى القرب واختصاصه بالسجود ومعنى الاستعاذة من صفة بصفة ومنه به
وأسرار ذلك كثيرة ولا يدل تفسير ظاهر عليه وليس اللفظ هو مناقضا لظاهر
التفسير بل هو استكمال له ووصول إلى لبابه عن ظاهره فهذا ما نورده لفهم
المعاني الباطنة لا ما يناقض الظاهر والله أعلم
تم كتاب آداب التلاوة والحمد لله رب العالمين والصلاة والسلام على محمد
خاتم النبيين وعلى كل عبد مصطفى من كل العالمين وعلى آل محمد وصحبه وسلم
يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب الأذكار والدعوات
والله المستعان لا رب سواه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Comprehension, understanding, intelligence; the faculty by which one grasps the reality of a thing
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Deep comprehension (tafahhum) as distinct from mere hearing (samāʿ); the intellectual apprehension of divine meanings
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal understanding (fahm al-ẓāhir) vs. penetrative insight (fahm al-bāṭin); the latter is a metaphorical extension of the root
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr (Ellipsis Restoration) — Many Qur'anic verses require restoring omitted elements (ḥadhf) to achieve correct syntactic parsing, as in "wa-as'al al-qaryah" (ask the town) where "ahl" (people) is implicit
chapters.translation:
You may say: "You have magnified the matter in what preceded regarding the comprehension of the secrets of the Qur'an and the meanings that unfold to possessors of pure hearts. How can this be deemed commendable, when he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion (ra'y), let him take his seat in the Fire'? And on this basis, the scholars of exoteric interpretation (ẓāhir al-tafsīr) have denounced the people of Sufism — specifically the deficient ones among those attributed to Sufism — for their allegorical interpretations (ta'wīl) of certain Qur'anic words contrary to what was transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and the rest of the commentators, declaring such to be unbelief (kufr). If what the exoteric commentators say is correct, then what is the meaning of 'comprehending the Qur'an' beyond memorizing its interpretation? And if it is not correct, then what is the meaning of his saying (peace be upon him): 'Whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion, let him take his seat in the Fire'?"

Know that whoever claims that there is no meaning to the Qur'an except what the exoteric interpretation (ẓāhir al-tafsīr) renders is reporting about the limit of his own self — and he is correct in reporting about himself — but he errs in judging that all of creation must be brought down to his own level, which is his limit and station. Rather, the reports (akhbār) and traditions (āthār) indicate that in the meanings of the Qur'an there is vast expanse for possessors of understanding (arbāb al-fahm). ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Except that Allah grants a servant understanding (fahm) in the Qur'an" — for if there were nothing beyond the transmitted rendering (tarjama), then what would that understanding be? And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed the Qur'an has an exterior (ẓahr) and an interior (baṭn), a limit (ḥadd) and an ascent (muṭṭalaʿ)." It is also related from Ibn Masʿūd as a stop (mawqūf) — and he was among the scholars of interpretation — so what is the meaning of "exterior," "interior," "limit," and "ascent"? And ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face) said: "If I wished, I would load seventy camels with the interpretation of the Opening Chapter (Fātiḥa)" — so what does this mean, given that the interpretation of its exterior is extremely brief? And Abū al-Dardā' said: "A man does not attain true jurisprudence (fiqh) until he makes for the Qur'an multiple faces (wujūh)." Some scholars have said: "For every verse there are sixty thousand comprehensions, and what remains of its comprehension is even more." Others said: "The Qur'an contains seventy-seven thousand and two hundred sciences, for every word is a science, then this multiplies fourfold, since every word has an exterior, an interior, a limit, and an ascent." And the repetition of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) of "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" twenty times could only be for his pondering (tadabbur) of the inner meanings thereof — otherwise, its rendering and exoteric interpretation do not require such repetition.

Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Whoever desires the knowledge of the ancients and the later ones, let him ponder the Qur'an" — and that is not attained by mere exoteric interpretation. In sum: all the sciences are included in the acts of Allah (mighty and majestic), His attributes, and in the Qur'an is the exposition of His essence (dhāt), His acts, and His attributes — and these sciences have no end. In the Qur'an there is an indication (ishāra) to their comprehensive principles (majāmiʿ), and the stations of deep penetration into their details revert to the comprehension of the Qur'an. Mere exoteric interpretation does not point to that. Rather, everything that has perplexed the speculative thinkers (nuẓẓār) and over which creatures have differed in theoretical and rational matters — in the Qur'an there are symbols (rumūz) and indications (dalālāt) thereof, which possessors of understanding are singled out to grasp. So how could the rendering of its exterior and its interpretation suffice for that? Therefore he (peace be upon him) said: "Recite the Qur'an and seek its wonders (gharā'ib)." And he (peace be upon him) said in the ḥadīth of ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face): "By Him who sent me with the truth as a prophet, my community will split from the root of its religion and its main body into seventy-two sects, all of them erring and leading astray, calling to the Fire. When that occurs, hold fast to the Book of Allah (mighty and majestic), for in it is the news of those before you, the news of what comes after you, and the judgment between you. Whoever opposes it among the tyrants, Allah (mighty and majestic) will crush him; whoever seeks knowledge in other than it, Allah (mighty and majestic) will lead him astray. It is the firm rope of Allah (ḥabl Allāh al-matīn), His clear light (nūruhu al-mubīn), and His healing that is beneficial — a protection for whoever clings to it, and a deliverance for whoever follows it. It does not waver so as to need straightening, nor does it deviate so as to need correction; its wonders do not come to an end, nor does it become worn out by much repetition."

And in the ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfa: when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed him of the disagreement and division after him, he said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me if I reach that?" He said: "Learn the Book of Allah and act by what is in it — it is the way out of that." He said: "I repeated that to him three times, and he said (peace be upon him) three times: 'Learn the Book of Allah (mighty and majestic) and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance.'"

And ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face) said: "Whoever comprehends the Qur'an, by it the comprehensive principles of knowledge are interpreted for him" — indicating that the Qur'an points to the comprehensive principles of all the sciences. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said regarding the saying of the Exalted: "And whoever is given wisdom (ḥikma) has been given abundant good" — meaning: understanding (fahm) in the Qur'an. And the Exalted said: "So We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment (ḥukm) and knowledge (ʿilm)" — He named what He gave them as knowledge and judgment, and singled out what was unique to Solomon — his acuteness of perception (tafaṭṭun) — by the name "understanding" (fahm), making it prior to judgment and knowledge. These matters indicate that in the comprehension of the Qur'an's meanings there is a spacious field and a far-reaching expanse, and that what is transmitted of exoteric interpretation is not the terminus of perception therein.

As for his saying (peace be upon him): "Whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion" and his prohibition thereof, and the saying of Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "What earth would carry me and what sky would shade me if I said about the Qur'an by my own opinion" — and other such reports and traditions prohibiting the interpretation of the Qur'an by opinion (ra'y) — this is either intended to mean restricting oneself to transmission (naql) and what is heard (masmūʿ), abandoning derivation (istinbāṭ) and independent comprehension, or it is intended to mean something else. It is absolutely false that it means no one should speak about the Qur'an except what he has heard, for several reasons:

**First**: That would require everything to be heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and attributed to him — but that is only found in part of the Qur'an. As for what Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd said from themselves, it would then have to be rejected, being called "interpretation by opinion," because they did not hear it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) — and likewise the rest of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them).

**Second**: The Companions and commentators differed in the interpretation of certain verses, offering divergent opinions that cannot be reconciled, and hearing all of them from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is impossible. If one were heard, the rest would be rejected. Thus it becomes certain that every commentator said about the meaning what appeared to him through his own derivation — until they said about the disjointed letters at the beginnings of the sūras seven divergent opinions that cannot be reconciled. It was said that "alif-lām-rā" are letters from "al-Raḥmān"; it was said that "alif" is Allāh, "lām" is Laṭīf (the Subtle), and "rā" is Raḥīm (the Merciful); and other opinions were given. Reconciliation of all of them is impossible — so how could all of them be heard?

**Third**: He (peace be upon him) supplicated for Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him): "O Allah, give him understanding in religion (faqqihhu fī al-dīn) and teach him the interpretation (ta'wīl)." If interpretation were heard like the revelation (tanzīl) and preserved like it, what would be the meaning of singling him out for that?

**Fourth**: The Exalted said: "for a knowledge that they derive (yastanbiṭūnahu) from them" — thus He affirmed for the people of knowledge a derivation (istinbāṭ), and it is known that this is beyond mere hearing.

The sum of what we have transmitted of the traditions on comprehending the Qur'an contradicts this fancy. Thus it is nullified that hearing (samāʿ) is required in interpretation (ta'wīl), and it is permissible for every person to derive from the Qur'an according to the measure of his understanding and the limit of his intellect.

As for the prohibition, it is to be applied to one of two aspects:

**The First Aspect**: That one has an opinion about a matter and an inclination toward it from his nature and passion (hawā), and he then interprets the Qur'an in accordance with his opinion and passion, seeking to argue for the correctness of his purpose — such that had he not had that opinion and passion, that meaning would not have occurred to him from the Qur'an. This is sometimes with knowledge — like one who argues with certain Qur'anic verses to support his innovation (bidʿa) while knowing that the verse does not mean that, but he obscures the matter against his opponent. Sometimes it is with ignorance — but when the verse is susceptible to multiple meanings, his understanding inclines to the aspect that agrees with his purpose, and he weights that side by his opinion and passion. Thus he has interpreted by his opinion, i.e., his opinion is what drove him to that interpretation, and had it not been for his opinion, that aspect would not have been weighted for him. Sometimes one may have a sound purpose and seek a proof for it from the Qur'an, adducing from it what he knows was not intended — like one who calls to seeking forgiveness in the last hours of the night and adduces his saying (peace be upon him): "Take the pre-dawn meal (saḥḥarū), for in the pre-dawn meal there is blessing," claiming that what is meant is the pre-dawn meal of remembrance (dhikr), while knowing that what is meant is eating. Or like one who calls to struggling against the hard heart and says: "Allah (mighty and majestic) said: 'Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed'" — pointing to his heart and indicating that "Pharaoh" means it. This kind is sometimes used by some preachers (wuʿʿāẓ) for sound purposes, to embellish speech and entice the listener — and it is prohibited. The Bāṭiniyya use it for corrupt purposes, to deceive people and call them to their false doctrine, applying the Qur'an in accordance with their opinion and doctrine to matters they know with certainty are not intended by it. These kinds are one of the two aspects of the prohibition of interpretation by opinion — and what is meant by "opinion" (ra'y) here is the corrupt opinion conforming to passion, not sound ijtihād. The word "opinion" encompasses both sound and corrupt; the one conforming to passion may be specifically designated by the name "opinion."

**The Second Aspect**: That one rushes to interpret the Qur'an by the exterior of Arabic (ẓāhir al-ʿarabiyya) without seeking support from hearing (samāʿ) and transmission (naql) regarding what pertains to the Qur'an's wonders (gharā'ib), its ambiguous expressions (alfāẓ mubhama), its altered forms (mubaddala), its abbreviations (ikhtiṣār), omissions (ḥadhf), implicit references (iḍmār), and its forward and backward arrangements (taqdīm wa ta'khīr). Whoever has not mastered exoteric interpretation and rushes to derive meanings by mere understanding of Arabic will err frequently and enter the ranks of those who interpret by opinion.

Thus transmission and hearing are indispensable in exoteric interpretation first, to guard against the places of error. Then after that, comprehension and derivation expand. The wonders that cannot be understood except by hearing are many, and we shall gesture to a summary of them so that one may infer their like from them and know that it is not permissible to be negligent in memorizing the exoteric interpretation first, nor is there any hope of reaching the interior (bāṭin) before mastering the exterior (ẓāhir). Whoever claims to comprehend the secrets of the Qur'an without mastering exoteric interpretation is like one who claims to reach the inner chamber of the house without passing through the door, or like one who claims to understand the purposes of the Turks from their speech while not knowing the Turkish language. For exoteric interpretation is like the teaching of the language that is indispensable for comprehension.

Among what requires hearing are many kinds:

**From them: abbreviation by omission and implicit reference (ījāz bi-al-ḥadhf wa al-iḍmār)** — like the saying of the Exalted: "And We gave to Thamūd the she-camel as a visible sign (mubṣira), but they wronged themselves by it" — meaning: a sign that makes visible (āya mubṣira), and they wronged themselves by killing it. The one who looks at the exterior of Arabic thinks that what is meant is that the she-camel was seeing and not blind, and he does not realize by what they wronged — others or themselves. And the saying of the Exalted: "And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf (al-ʿijl) by their unbelief" — i.e., the love of the calf, with "love" omitted. And the saying of the Exalted: "Then We would have made you taste double in life (ḍiʿf al-ḥayāt) and double in death (ḍiʿf al-mamāt)" — i.e., double the punishment of the living and double the punishment of the dead, with "punishment" omitted and "the living" and "the dead" substituted by the mention of "life" and "death." All of this is permissible in eloquent language.

And the saying of the Exalted: "And ask the town (al-qarya) in which we were, and the caravan (al-ʿīr) in which we approached" — i.e., the people of the caravan; "the people" (ahl) in both is omitted and implicit. And the saying of the Exalted: "It weighs heavy in the heavens and the earth (thaqulat fī al-samāwāt wa al-arḍ)" — meaning: it is hidden from the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth; and when a thing is hidden it becomes heavy, so the word was substituted for it and placed in the position of "upon" (ʿalā), with "the inhabitants" (ahl) made implicit and omitted.

And the saying of the Exalted: "And you make your provision (rizq) that you deny" — i.e., the gratitude for your provision. And the saying of the Exalted: "And grant us what You promised us upon Your messengers (ʿalā rusulik)" — i.e., upon the tongues of Your messengers, with "tongues" (alsina) omitted. And the saying of the Exalted: "Indeed We sent it down in the Night of Decree" — meaning the Qur'an, though no prior mention of it occurred. And the Exalted said: "until it concealed itself behind the veil (tawārat bi-al-ḥijāb)" — meaning the sun, though no prior mention of it occurred. And the saying of the Exalted: "And those who take protectors besides Him — we do not worship them except to bring us nearer to Allah in proximity (zulfā)" — i.e., they say: "We do not worship them..." And the saying of the Exalted: "What is the matter with these people that they scarcely understand any statement (ḥadīth)? Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself" — meaning: they scarcely understand a statement, saying: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself." For if this were not intended, it would contradict His saying: "Say: All is from Allah" — and from it the Qadariyya doctrine would be understood.

**From them: the transmitted altered (al-manqūl al-munqalib)** — like the saying of the Exalted: "And the Mount of Sīnīn (ṭūr sīnīn)" — i.e., the Mount of Sinai (ṭūr sīnā'). And "Peace upon the family of Yāsīn (āl yāsīn)" — i.e., upon Ilyās (Elijah); and it was said: Idrīs, because in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is "Peace upon Idrāsīn."

**From them: the repeated that severs the connection of speech in the exterior (al-mukarrar al-qāṭiʿ li-waṣl al-kalām fī al-ẓāhir)** — like the saying of the Exalted: "And those they invoke besides Allah do not follow partners (shurakā') — they follow nothing but conjecture." And the saying of the Exalted: "The chiefs who were arrogant among his people said to those who were weakened — to those who believed among them" — meaning: those who were arrogant said to those who believed among the weakened ones.

**From them: the advanced and delayed (al-muqaddam wa al-mu'akhkhar)**, which is a locus of error — like the saying of the Exalted: "And were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been a necessary attachment (lizām) and an appointed term (ajal musammā)" — meaning: were it not for the word and the appointed term, it would have been a necessary attachment; and without them it would be accusative (naṣb) like "lizām." And the saying of the Exalted: "They ask you as if you were wary of it (ka-annaka ḥafiyyun ʿanhā)" — i.e., they ask you about it as if you were well-informed of it. And the saying of the Exalted: "For them is forgiveness and a noble provision — as He brought you out from your house in truth (kamā akhrajaka rabbuka min baytika bi-al-ḥaqq)" — this speech is not connected; rather, it reverts to His prior saying: "Say: The spoils (anfāl) belong to Allah and the Messenger — as He brought you out from your house in truth," i.e., the spoils of war became yours since you were content with your departure while they were averse. Between the two speeches the command of piety and other matters intervened. And of this type is the saying of the Exalted: "until they believe in Allah alone — except the saying of Abraham to his father" — the verse.

**From them: the ambiguous (al-mubham)**, which is the word shared between meanings, whether of a noun or a particle. As for the noun — like "al-shay'" (thing), "al-qarīn" (companion), "al-umma" (community), "al-rūḥ" (spirit), and their like. Allah the Exalted said: "Allah strikes a parable: a slave owned, unable to do anything" — meaning: unable to spend from what he is given. And the saying of the Exalted: "And Allah strikes a parable: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything" — meaning: unable to command justice and uprightness. And the saying of the Exalted: "If you follow me, do not ask me about anything" — meaning: about the attributes of lordship, i.e., the sciences about which it is not lawful to ask until the knower initiates them at the time of their due.

And the saying of the Exalted: "Or were they created from nothing (min ghayr shay'), or are they the creators?" — i.e., from no creator. One might mistakenly think it indicates that nothing is created except from something.

As for "al-qarīn" — like the saying of the Exalted: "And his companion (qarīnuhu) said: 'This is what I have ready. Cast into Hell every obstinate disbeliever'" — meaning: the angel appointed over him. And the saying of the Exalted: "His companion said: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in deep error'" — meaning: the devil (shayṭān).

As for "al-umma," it is used in eight senses: (1) the community (jamāʿa) — like the saying of the Exalted: "And he found upon it a community of people watering"; (2) the followers of the prophets — like your saying "the umma of Muḥammad (peace be upon him)"; (3) a man who combines good and is followed as an exemplar — like the saying of the Exalted: "Indeed Abraham was an umma, devoutly obedient to Allah"; (4) the religion (dīn) — like the saying of the Exalted: "Indeed we found our fathers upon an umma (religion)"; (5) the time and period (ḥīn wa zamān) — like the saying of the Exalted: "until an umma (period) counted"; and the saying of the Exalted: "and he remembered after an umma (a long time)"; (6) the stature (qāma) — it is said: "So-and-so is handsome in umma," i.e., stature; (7) a man unique in a religion in which no one shares with him — he (peace be upon him) said: "Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl will be raised as an umma alone"; (8) it is said: "This is the umma of Zayd," i.e., the mother (umm) of Zayd. And "al-rūḥ" (spirit) also occurs in the Qur'an with many meanings, which we will not prolong by listing.

Likewise, ambiguity may occur in particles — like the saying of the Exalted: "So they raised thereby a dust cloud (fa-atharna bihi naqʿan), and penetrated thereby into the midst of the gathering (fa-wasaṭna bihi jamʿan)" — the first pronoun (hā') refers to the hooves, which are the "striking sparks" (al-mūriyāt), i.e., they raised by the hooves a dust cloud; the second refers to the raid (ighāra), which are the "charging at dawn" (al-mughīrāt ṣubḥan), i.e., they penetrated by the raid into the midst of the gathering of the polytheists, raiding with their host. And the saying of the Exalted: "And We sent down thereby (bihi) water" — meaning: by the cloud; "and We brought forth thereby (bihi) from all the fruits" — meaning: by the water. And examples of this in the Qur'an are beyond enumeration.

**From them: the gradation in clarification (al-tadrīj fī al-bayān)** — like the saying of the Exalted: "The month of Ramaḍān in which the Qur'an was sent down" — where it is not made clear whether it was night or day; then it became clear by His saying: "Indeed We sent it down in a blessed night" — but it was not made clear which night; then it became clear by His saying: "Indeed We sent it down in the Night of Decree." One might think in the exterior that there is contradiction between these verses. This and its like are matters in which nothing avails except transmission and hearing.

For the Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, is not free of this kind, because it was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and thus it comprises the varieties of their speech — abbreviation (ījāz), prolongation (iṭāla), implicit reference (iḍmār), omission (ḥadhf), substitution (ibdāl), advancement (taqdīm), and delay (ta'khīr) — so that it would be overwhelming to them and miraculous against them. Therefore, whoever is content with understanding the exterior of Arabic and rushes to interpret the Qur'an without seeking support from hearing and transmission in these matters is included among those who interpret the Qur'an by their opinion — like one who understands from "al-umma" its most famous meaning, and his nature and opinion incline to it; then when he hears it in another place, his opinion inclines to what he heard of its famous meaning, abandoning the pursuit of transmission in many of its meanings. This is what may be prohibited — not the deep comprehension of the secrets of meanings, as preceded.

When hearing is attained in such matters, the exoteric interpretation is known — which is the rendering of the words (tarjamat al-alfāẓ) — but that does not suffice for comprehending the realities of meanings (ḥaqā'iq al-maʿānī). The difference between the realities of meanings and exoteric interpretation can be grasped by an example: Allah (mighty and majestic) said: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw." Its exterior is a clear interpretation, but the reality of its meaning is obscure — for it affirms throwing and negates it, which are contradictory in the exterior, unless one understands that he threw in one respect and did not throw in another, and from the respect in which he did not throw, Allah (mighty and majestic) threw.

Likewise, the Exalted said: "Fight them — Allah will punish them by your hands." If they are the ones fighting, how is Allah (glorified) the punisher? And if Allah the Exalted is the punisher by moving their hands, then what is the meaning of commanding them to fight? The reality of this draws from a vast sea of the sciences of unveiling (mukāshafāt) that exoteric interpretation does not suffice for — namely, knowing the manner of the connection of acts to the originated power (al-qudra al-ḥāditha), and understanding the manner of the connection of that power to the power of Allah (mighty and majestic), until after the clarification of many obscure matters there unfolds the truth of His saying: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw." Perhaps if a lifetime were spent in uncovering the secrets of this meaning and what is connected to its premises and consequences, the lifetime would expire before exhausting all its consequences. And there is no word in the Qur'an whose verification does not require something like that. It unfolds only to those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm) from its secrets, according to the abundance of their sciences, the purity of their hearts, the fullness of their motivations for pondering, and their detachment for seeking. Each one has a limit in ascending to a degree higher than it. As for exhaustive attainment (istīfā'), there is no hope of it — even if the sea were ink and the trees were pens, the secrets of the words of Allah have no end: "The seas would be exhausted before the words of Allah (mighty and majestic) were exhausted."

From this aspect, creatures differ in comprehension after sharing in the knowledge of exoteric interpretation — and exoteric interpretation does not suffice. An example of this: some possessors of hearts understood from his saying (peace be upon him) in his prostration: "I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself" — that it was said to him: "Prostrate and draw near" (asjud wa iqtarib). He found nearness (qurb) in prostration, then looked to the attributes and sought refuge in some of them from others — for pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (sakhaṭ) are two attributes. Then his nearness increased, and the first nearness was subsumed in it, so he ascended to the Essence (dhāt) and said: "I seek refuge in You from You." Then his nearness increased further by what he felt of shame in seeking refuge on the carpet of nearness, so he resorted to praise and praised by saying: "I cannot enumerate praise of You." Then he knew that this was a shortcoming and said: "You are as You have praised Yourself." These are thoughts (khawāṭir) that open to possessors of hearts. Then beyond this they have depths — namely, comprehending the meaning of nearness and its specificity to prostration, the meaning of seeking refuge from one attribute by another, and from Him by Him — and the secrets of that are many, which exoteric interpretation does not indicate. This is not contradictory to exoteric interpretation; rather, it is a completion of it and an arrival at its core (lubāb) through its exterior (ẓāhir). This is what we present for comprehending inner meanings — not what contradicts the exterior. And Allah knows best.

The Book of the Etiquettes of Recitation is completed. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Peace and blessings be upon Muḥammad, the Seal of the Prophets, upon every chosen servant from all the worlds, and upon the family of Muḥammad and his Companions. It will be followed, Allah willing, by the Book of Remembrances and Supplications (Kitāb al-Adhkār wa al-Daʿawāt). And Allah is the one whose help is sought — there is no lord other than Him.

### || كتاب الأذكار والدعوات

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله الشاملة
رأفته العامة رحمته الذي جازى عباده عن ذكرهم بذكرهم فقال تعالى فاذكروني
أذكركم PageV01P293
ورغبهم في السؤال والدعاء بأمره فقال ادعوني أستجب لكم فأطمع المطيع
والعاصي والداني والقاصي في الانبساط إلى حضرة جلاله برفع الحاجات والأماني
بقوله فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان والصلاة على محمد سيد أنبيائه
وعلى آله وأصحابه خيرة أصفيائه وسلم تسليما كثيرا
أما بعد
فليس بعد تلاوة كتاب الله عز وجل عبادة تؤدى باللسان أفضل من ذكر الله
تعالى ورفع الحاجات بالأدعية الخالصة إلى الله تعالى فلا بد من شرح فضيلة
الذكر على الجملة  ثم على التفصيل في أعيان الأذكار
وشرح فضيلة الدعاء وشروطه وآدابه ونقل المأثور من الدعوات الجامعة لمقاصد
الدين والدنيا والدعوات الخاصة لسؤال المغفرة والاستعاذة وغيرها
ويتحرر المقصود من ذلك بذكر أبواب خمسة
الباب الأول في فضيلة الذكر وفائدته جملة وتفصيلا
الباب الثاني في فضيلة الدعاء وآدابه وفضيلة الاستغفار والصلاة على رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
الباب الثالث في أدعية مأثورة ومعزية إلى أصحابها وأسبابها
الباب الرابع في أدعية منتخبة محذوفة الإسناد من الأدعية الماثورة
الباب الخامس في الأدعية المأثورة عند حدوث الحوادث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "presence in the mind" or "uttering with the tongue"; also "honor" and "reminder" — the act of keeping something present after its absence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, dhikr is the heart's vigilance toward God, its highest form being verbal praise that both affirms and deepens that vigilance; it is the inverse of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — oral utterance of God's names; metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's persistent awareness of God even without speech.
- Root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, summon, or invoke; also "to claim" or "to name" — the act of directing one's need toward another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supplication (duʿāʾ) is the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftaqār) before the Creator, and the Creator's response is His mercy; it is an act of worship in itself, not merely a request.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — calling out with the tongue; metaphorical — the soul's humble turning to God through need, even without articulated words.
- Root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Nearness in place or rank; also kinship. The root implies removal of distance, whether physical or spiritual.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine nearness (qurb) is not spatial but relational — God's readiness to answer and His knowledge of the supplicant's state; it is a nearness of mercy, not of location.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — proximity in space; metaphorical — God's closeness to the one who calls, as in the verse cited, meaning His hearing and answering.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Inceptive Clauses (al-Ibtidāʾ) — The opening "الحمد لله" is a nominal sentence beginning with a definite predicate, establishing praise as a permanent attribute of God, not a contingent act; the subsequent relative clauses (الذي جازى...) are adjectival expansions (ṣilah) that specify the grounds of that praise.
chapters.translation:
### || The Book of Remembrances and Supplications

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, whose tenderness is all-encompassing, whose mercy is universal — He who recompensed His servants for their remembrance of Him with His remembrance of them, for He, exalted, said: {«So remember Me; I will remember you»} (Q. 2:152). And He encouraged them in asking and supplicating by His command, for He said: {«Call upon Me; I will answer you»} (Q. 40:60). Thus He gave hope to the obedient and the disobedient, the near and the far, that they might stretch forth toward the presence of His majesty by raising their needs and aspirations, through His saying: {«For I am near; I answer the call of the caller when he calls Me»} (Q. 2:186). And blessings upon Muhammad, the master of His prophets, and upon his family and companions, the choicest of His elect — and abundant peace.

To proceed:

After the recitation of the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, there is no act of worship performed by the tongue more excellent than the remembrance of God, exalted, and the raising of needs through supplications sincerely directed to God, exalted. Thus it is necessary to explain the virtue of remembrance (dhikr) in general, then in detail concerning the specific forms of remembrance; and to explain the virtue of supplication (duʿāʾ), its conditions, and its proprieties; and to transmit what is authentically reported of supplications that encompass the purposes of religion and this world, and the specific supplications for seeking forgiveness, seeking refuge, and other matters.

The intended aim of all this is set forth in five chapters:

Chapter One: On the virtue of remembrance and its benefit, in general and in detail.

Chapter Two: On the virtue of supplication and its proprieties, and the virtue of seeking forgiveness (istighfār) and invoking blessings upon the Messenger of God, peace be upon him.

Chapter Three: On supplications authentically reported, attributed to their transmitters, and the occasions for them.

Chapter Four: On selected supplications, with their chains of transmission omitted, drawn from the authentically reported supplications.

Chapter Five: On the supplications authentically reported for the occurrence of events and calamities.
