الرحيم عند الموت حسبي الله الرؤوف عند المسألة في القبر حسبي الله الكريم
عند الحساب حسبي الله اللطيف عند الميزان حسبي الله القدير عند الصراط حسبي
الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم وقد روي عن أبي الدرداء
أنه قال من قال في كل يوم سبع مرات فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو
عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم كفاه الله عز وجل ما أهمه من أمر آخرته
صادقا كان أو كاذبا

### |||| دعاء عتبة الغلام

وقد رؤي في المنام بعد موته فقال دخلت الجنة بهذه الكلمات اللهم يا هادي
المضلين ويا راحم المذنبين ويا مقيل عثرات العاثرين ارحم عبدك ذا الخطر
العظيم والمسلمين كلهم أجمعين واجعلنا مع الأخيار المرزوقين الذين أنعمت
عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين آمين يا رب العالمين

### |||| دعاء آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام

قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لما اراد الله عز وجل أن يتوب على آدم صلى الله
عليه وسلم طاف بالبيت سبعا PageV01P316
وهو يومئذ ليس بمبني ربوة حمراء ثم قام فصلى ركعتين ثم قال اللهم إنك
تعلم سري وعلانيتي فاقبل معذرتي وتعلم حاجتي فأعطني سؤلي وتعلم ما في نفسي
فاغفر لي ذنوبي اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا يباشر قلبي ويقينا صادقا حتى أعلم
أنه لن يصيبني إلا ما كتبته علي والرضا بما قسمته لي يا ذا الجلال والإكرام
فأوحى الله عز وجل إليه إني قد غفرت لك ولم يأتني أحد من ذريتك فيدعوني
بمثل الذي دعوتني به إلا غفرت له وكشفت غمومه وهمومه ونزعت الفقر من بين
عينيه واتجرت له من وراء كل تاجر وجاءته الدنيا وهي راغمة وإن كان لا
يريدها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Invocation, calling upon; the act of summoning or beseeching with earnestness
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supplication as the essence of worship (ʿibādah), the creature's acknowledgment of need before the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — direct address to God; metaphorical (majāz) — the state of humble entreaty itself
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ) — "man qāla... fa-innahu" (whoever says... then indeed), establishing causal nexus between utterance and divine response
chapters.translation:
**The Supplication of Qabīṣah ibn al-Mukhāriq**

When he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Teach me words by which God, Mighty and Majestic, will benefit me, for my age has advanced and I have become incapable of many things I used to do." He, peace be upon him, said: "As for your worldly life — when you pray the morning prayer, say three times: 'Glory be to God and with His praise; glory be to God the Magnificent; there is no might and no power except with God, the Most High, the Magnificent.' For if you say them, you will be secure from grief, leprosy, vitiligo, and paralysis. And as for your afterlife — say: 'O God, guide me from Your presence, and pour upon me from Your bounty, and spread upon me from Your mercy, and send down upon me from Your blessings.'" Then he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, if a servant meets God on the Day of Resurrection with these words, not abandoning them, four gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he shall enter through whichever of them he wishes."

**The Supplication of Abū al-Dardā', May God Be Pleased with Him**

It was said to Abū al-Dardā', may God be pleased with him: "Your house has burned down, and the fire had fallen upon your neighborhood." He said: "God would never do such a thing." This was said to him three times, and he kept saying: "God would never do such a thing." Then a visitor came to him and said: "O Abū al-Dardā', when the fire drew near your house, it was extinguished." He said: "I knew that." It was said to him: "We do not know which of your two statements is more wondrous." He said: "I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: 'Whoever says these words in a night or a day, nothing will harm him' — and I have said them. They are: 'O God, You are my Lord; there is no god but You; upon You I rely, and You are the Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no might and no power except with God, the Most High, the Magnificent. Whatever God wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. I know that God is powerful over all things, and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge, and has counted all things in number. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul, and from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.'"

**The Supplication of al-Khalīl Ibrāhīm, Peace Be Upon Him**

He used to say upon rising in the morning: "O God, this is a new creation — open it for me in obedience to You, and seal it for me with Your forgiveness and Your good pleasure, and provide me therein a good deed that You will accept from me, purify it for me, and multiply it for me. And whatever sin I commit therein, forgive me for it. Indeed, You are Forgiving, Merciful, Affectionate, Generous." He said: "Whoever supplicates with this supplication upon rising in the morning has rendered the thanks of his day."

**The Supplication of ʿĪsā, Peace Be Upon Him**

He used to say: "O God, I rise unable to repel what I dislike, nor do I possess the power to attain the benefit of what I hope for. The matter has come to rest in the hand of other than me, and I have become pledged for my deeds. So there is no poor one poorer than I. O God, do not let my enemy gloat over me, nor let my friend be grieved by me, and do not make my affliction in my religion, and do not make the world my greatest concern, and do not give dominion over me to one who will not have mercy on me. O Living One, O Self-Subsisting One."

**The Supplication of al-Khaḍir, Peace Be Upon Him**

It is said that al-Khaḍir and Ilyās, peace be upon them both, whenever they met in every season, did not part except upon these words: "In the name of God. Whatever God wills — there is no power except with God. Whatever God wills — every blessing is from God. Whatever God wills — all good is in the hand of God. Whatever God wills — none repels evil except God." Whoever says them three times upon rising in the morning will be secure from burning, drowning, and theft, God willing, the Exalted.

**The Supplication of Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, May God Be Pleased with Him**

Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān said: Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, may God have mercy on him, said to me: "Shall I not teach you ten words — five for the world and five for the hereafter? Whoever supplicates God, Mighty and Majestic, with them will find God, the Exalted, at their disposal." I said: "Write them down for me." He said: "No, but I will repeat them to you just as Bakr ibn Khunays, may God have mercy on him, repeated them to me: 'God suffices me for my religion. God suffices me for my worldly life. God, the Generous, suffices me for what concerns me. God, the Forbearing, the Strong, suffices me against whoever seeks to wrong me. God, the Severe, suffices me against whoever plots evil against me. God, the Merciful, suffices me at death. God, the Compassionate, suffices me at the questioning in the grave. God, the Generous, suffices me at the Reckoning. God, the Subtle, suffices me at the Balance. God, the Powerful, suffices me at the Bridge. God suffices me — there is no god but He; upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.'" And it has been related from Abū al-Dardā' that he said: "Whoever says every day seven times — 'But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He; upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne' — God, Mighty and Majestic, will suffice him for whatever concerns him of the matter of his afterlife, whether he be truthful or lying."

**The Supplication of ʿUtbah al-Ghulām**

He was seen in a dream after his death, and he said: "I entered Paradise by these words: 'O God, O Guide of the astray, O Merciful to the sinners, O Acceptor of the excuses of the stumbling — have mercy on Your servant of great worth, and on all the Muslims altogether, and place us among the righteous elect who are provided for — those upon whom You have bestowed favor, from the Prophets, the Truthful, the Martyrs, and the Righteous. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.'"

**The Supplication of Ādam, Peace Be Upon Him**

ʿĀ'ishah, may God be pleased with her, said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, wished to accept the repentance of Ādam, peace be upon him, he circumambulated the House seven times — and at that time it was not yet built, being a red hillock — then he stood and prayed two units, then said: "O God, You know my secret and my open — so accept my excuse. And You know my need — so grant me my request. And You know what is in my soul — so forgive me my sins. O God, I ask You for a faith that penetrates my heart, and a certain truthfulness until I know that nothing will befall me except what You have decreed upon me, and contentment with what You have apportioned for me. O Possessor of Majesty and Honor." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "I have indeed forgiven you, and no one from your progeny shall come to Me supplicating with the like of what you have supplicated to Me, except that I will forgive him, and remove his griefs and his sorrows, and pluck poverty from between his eyes, and cause him to profit from behind every merchant, and the world shall come to him despite itself — even if he does not desire it."

chapters.title_en: The Supplication of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him), the Supplication of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) with his Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham (may Allah be pleased with him)
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| دعاء علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

رواه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل
يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي
القيوم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العلي العظيم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا
أنا لم ألد ولم أولد إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العفو الغفور إني أنا
الله لا إله إلا أنا مبدىء كل شيء وإلي يعود العزيز الحكيم الرحمن الرحيم
مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد
الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك
القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر الخالق البارىء المصور
الكبير المتعال المقتدر القهار الحليم الكريم أهل الثناء والمجد أعلم السر
وأخفى القادر الرزاق فوق الخلق والخليقة (1) وذكر قبل كل كلمة إني أنا الله
لا إله إلا أنا كما أوردناه في الأول فمن دعا بهذه الأسماء فليقل إنك أنت
الله لا إله إلا أنت كذا وكذا فمن دعا بهن كتب من الساجدين المخبتين الذين
يجاورون محمدا وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى والنبيين صلوات  الله عليهم في دار
الجلال وله ثواب العابدين في السموات والأرضين وصلى الله على محمد وعلى كل
عبد مصطفى

### |||| دعاء ابن المعتمر وهو سليمان التيمي وتسبيحاته رضي الله عنه

روي أن يونس بن عبيد رأى رجلا في المنام ممن قتل شهيدا ببلاد الروم فقال
ما أفضل ما رأيت ثم من الأعمال قال رأيت تسبيحات ابن المعتمر من الله عز
وجل بمكان وهي هذه سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا
حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم عد ما خلق وعدد ما هو خالق وزنة ما خلق
وزنة ما هو خالق وملء ما خلق وملء ما هو خالق وملء سمواته وملء أرضه ومثل
ذلك وأضعاف ذلك وعدد خلقه وزنة عرشه ومنتهى رحمته ومداد كلماته ومبلغ رضاه
حتى يرضى وإذا رضي وعدد ما ذكره به خلقه في جميع ما مضى وعدد ما هم ذاكروه
فيما بقي في كل سنة وشهر وجمعة ويوم وليلة وساعة من الساعات وشم ونفس من
الأنفاس وأبد من الآباد من أبد إلى أبد أبد الدنيا وأبد الآخرة وأكثر من
ذلك لا ينقطع أوله ولاينفد آخره

### |||| دعاء إبراهيم بن أدهم رضي الله عنه

روى إبراهيم بن بشار خادمه أنه كان يقول هذا الدعاء في كل يوم جمعة إذا
أصبح وإذا أمسى مرحبا بيوم المزيد والصبح الجديد والكاتب والشهيد يومنا هذا
يوم عيد اكتب لنا فيه ما نقول بسم الله الحميد المجيد الرفيع الودود الفعال
في خلقه ما يريد أصبحت بالله مؤمنا وبلقائه مصدقا وبحجته معترفا ومن ذنبي
مستغفرا ولربوبية الله خاضعا PageV01P317
ولسوى الله في الآلهة جاحدا وإلى الله فقيرا وعلى الله متكلا وإلى الله
منيبا أشهد الله وأشهد ملائكته وأنبيائه ورسله وحملة عرشه ومن خلقه ومن هو
خالقه بأنه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وحده لا شريك له وأن محمدا عبده
ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة
حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك  حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب
فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن
شاء الله
اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما
استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل ذي شر
اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت واهدني
لأحسن الأخلاق فإنه لا يهدي لأحسنها إلا أنت واصرف عني سيئها فإنه لا يصرف
سيئها إلا أنت لبيك وسعديك والخير كله بيديك أنا لك وإليك أستغفرك وأتوب
إليك آمنت اللهم بما أرسلته من رسول وآمنت اللهم بما أنزلت من كتاب وصلى
الله على محمد النبي الأمي وعلى آله وسلم تسليما كثيرا خاتم كلامي ومفتاحه
وعلى أنبيائه ورسله أجمعين آمين يا رب العالمين
اللهم أوردنا حوض محمد واسقنا بكأسه مشربا رويا سائغا هنيا لا نظمأ بعده
أبدا واحشرنا في زمرته غير خزايا ولا ناكثين للعهد ولا مرتابين ولا مفتونين
ولا مغضوب علينا ولا ضالين
اللهم اعصمني من فتن الدنيا ووفقني لما تحب وترضى وأصلح لي شأني كله
وثبتني بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولا تضلني وإن كنت ظالما
سبحانك سبحانك يا علي يا عظيم يا بارىء يا رحيم يا عزيز يا جبار سبحان من
سبحت له السموات بأكنافها وسبحان من سبحت له البحار بأمواجها وسبحان من
سبحت له الجبال بأصدائها وسبحان من سبحت له الحيتان بلغاتها وسبحان من سبحت
له النجوم في السماء بأبراجها وسبحان من سبحت له الأشجار بأصولها وثمارها
وسبحان من سبحت له السموات السبع والأرضون السبع ومن فيهن ومن عليهن سبحان
من سبح له كل شيء من مخلوقاته تباركت وتعاليت سبحانك سبحانك يا حي يا قيوم
يا عليم يا حليم سبحانك لا إله إلا أنت وحدك لا شريك لك تحيي وتميت وأنت حي
لا تموت بيدك الخير وأنت على كل شيء قدير
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calling, invoking, supplication; the act of summoning or petitioning
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Duʿāʾ as the servant's humble petition to Allah, distinct from worship (ʿibādah) yet encompassing it
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal calling; metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's orientation toward Allah in need
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — governing the structure "fa-man daʿā... fa-l-yaqul" (whoever supplicates... let him say)
chapters.translation:
**Section on the Supplication of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him)**

It is narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "Verily, Allah the Exalted glorifies His own Self every day and says: 'Indeed, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds. Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me, the Most High, the Magnificent. Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me; I have not begotten, nor was I begotten. Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me, the Pardoner, the Forgiving. Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me, the Originator of everything, and to Me all things return — the Mighty, the Wise, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment, Creator of good and evil, Creator of Paradise and the Fire, the One, the Unique, the Single, the Self-Sufficient, He who has taken no companion nor any son, the Unique, the Odd, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Bestower of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Great, the Most Exalted, the Prevailing, the Subduer, the Forbearing, the Generous, Possessor of all praise and glory, Knower of the secret and what is more hidden, the Powerful, the Provider, above all creation and creatures.'" (1) And He mentions before every word: "Indeed, I am Allah — there is no deity except Me," just as we have recorded it at the beginning. So whoever supplicates with these Names, let him say: "Verily, You are Allah — there is no deity except You," and so forth. Whoever supplicates with them is recorded among the prostrating, humble devotees who will dwell alongside Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon them all) in the Abode of Majesty. And he shall have the reward of all worshippers in the heavens and the earths. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and upon every chosen servant.

**Section on the Supplication of Ibn al-Muʿtamir — namely Sulaymān al-Taymī — and his Glorifications (may Allah be pleased with him)**

It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw in a dream a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines. He asked him: "What is the most excellent deed you have seen?" He replied: "I saw the glorifications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station of great honor with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is Greater, and there is no might nor power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the count of what He has created, and to the count of what He is creating, and to the weight of what He has created, and to the weight of what He is creating, and to the fullness of what He has created, and to the fullness of what He is creating, and to the fullness of His heavens, and to the fullness of His earth, and to the like of that, and to multiples of that, and to the number of His creatures, and to the weight of His Throne, and to the limit of His mercy, and to the extent of His words (madād kalimātihi), and to the measure of His good pleasure until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, and to the number of what His creatures have remembered Him with throughout all that has passed, and to the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains — in every year, month, Friday, day, night, and hour of the hours, and every breath of the breaths, and every age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."

**Section on the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham (may Allah be pleased with him)**

Ibrāhīm ibn Bashshār, his servant, narrated that he used to say this supplication every Friday, in the morning and in the evening: "Welcome to the Day of Increase, and the new morning, and the recording scribe. This day of ours is a day of festival. Write down for us in it what we say: In the name of Allah, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious, the Exalted, the Loving, the Doer of whatever He wills in His creation. I have entered the morning believing in Allah, affirming the truth of meeting Him, acknowledging His proof, seeking forgiveness for my sin, humbling myself before the Lordship of Allah, denying any deity other than Allah, needy before Allah, relying upon Allah, and turning in repentance to Allah. I call Allah to witness, and I call His angels, His prophets, His messengers, the bearers of His Throne, and those of His creation whom He has created, to witness that He is Allah — there is no deity except Him, alone, without any partner — and that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), and that Paradise is true, and that the Fire is true, and that the Basin (al-ḥawḍ) is true, and that intercession is true, and that Munkar and Nakīr are true, and that Your promise is true, and that Your threat is true, and that meeting You is true, and that the Hour is coming — there is no doubt in it — and that Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves. Upon that I live, upon that I die, and upon that I shall be raised, if Allah wills.

O Allah, You are my Lord — there is no deity except You. You created me, and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You, O Allah, from the evil of what I have done, and from the evil of every possessor of evil.

O Allah, I have wronged my own soul, so forgive me my sins — for none forgives sins except You. And guide me to the best of moral characters, for none guides to the best of them except You. And turn away from me their evil, for none turns away their evil except You. Here I am at Your service, and here I am answering Your call. All good is in Your hands. I am Yours, and to You I return. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You. I believe, O Allah, in every messenger You have sent, and I believe, O Allah, in every book You have revealed. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them abundant peace — the seal of my speech and its key — and upon all his prophets and messengers. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

O Allah, bring us to the Basin of Muhammad, and give us to drink from his cup — a drink that is satisfying, wholesome, and pleasant, after which we shall never thirst again. And gather us in his company, neither disgraced, nor breakers of the covenant, nor doubters, nor seduced, nor objects of wrath, nor astray.

O Allah, protect me from the trials of this world, and grant me success in what You love and are pleased with, and set right for me all my affairs, and establish me firmly with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And do not lead me astray, even though I am a wrongdoer. Glory be to You, glory be to You, O Most High, O Magnificent, O Originator, O Merciful, O Mighty, O Compeller. Glory be to Him to Whom the heavens glorify with their regions, and glory be to Him to Whom the seas glorify with their waves, and glory be to Him to Whom the mountains glorify with their echoes, and glory be to Him to Whom the fish glorify in their languages, and glory be to Him to Whom the stars in the sky glorify within their constellations, and glory be to Him to Whom the trees glorify with their roots and their fruits, and glory be to Him to Whom the seven heavens and the seven earths glorify, and all who are within them and upon them. Glory be to Him to Whom every one of His creatures glorifies. Blessed are You and exalted. Glory be to You, glory be to You, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, O All-Knowing, O Forbearing. Glory be to You — there is no deity except You, alone, without partner. You give life and You cause death, and You are the Ever-Living who never dies. In Your hand is all good, and You have power over all things."

chapters.title_en: Chapter Four on Supplications Transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him) and His Companions (may God be pleased with them)
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| الباب الرابع في أدعية مأثورة عن النبي صلى  الله عليه وسلم وعن أصحابه رضي الله عنهم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د ع و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of calling, invoking, summoning; also supplication (duʿāʾ) as a verbal act of requesting aid or mercy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, duʿāʾ signifies the servant’s humble petition to God, an act of worship (ʿibādah) and acknowledgment of divine sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes direct vocal invocation; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any act of seeking nearness to God through prescribed words or deeds.
- Root: أ ث ر (a-tha-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To transmit, narrate, or leave a trace; maʾthūr refers to what is handed down from authoritative sources.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic tradition, maʾthūr designates supplications and practices established by revelation or prophetic example, carrying normative weight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical tracing; metaphorical sense is authoritative transmission of sayings or deeds.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أصحابه" uses the particle ʿan (from) twice to coordinate two distinct sources of transmission, each governed by the preceding noun "أدعية" (supplications), with the second ʿan repeating the preposition for clarity and emphasis.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the fourth chapter, concerning supplications (adʿiyah) transmitted (maʾthūrah) from the Prophet (peace be upon him) and from his Companions (may God be pleased with them).

chapters.title_en: On the Devotee's Supplications After the Prescribed Prayers — A Selection of Authentic Invocations
chapters.arabic_text:
محذوفة الأسانيد منتخبة من جملة ما جمعة أبو طالب المكي وابن خزيمة وابن
منذر رحمهم الله
يستحب للمريد إذا أصبح أن يكون أحب أوراده الدعاء كما سيأتي ذكره في كتاب
الأوراد فإن كنت من المريدين لحرث الآخرة المقتدين برسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم فيما دعا به فقل في مفتتح دعواتك (1) أعقاب صلواتك (2) سبحان ربي
العلي الأعلى الوهاب لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد
وهو على كل شيء قدير وقل رضيت بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا وبمحمد صلى الله
عليه وسلم نبيا (3) ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم فاطر السموات والأرض عالم الغيب
والشهادة رب كل شيء ومليكه أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أعوذ بك من شر نفسي وشر
الشيطان وشركه (4) وقل اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي
وأهلي ومالي اللهم استر عوراتي وآمن روعاتي وأقل PageV01P318
عثراتي واحفظني من بين يدي ومن خلفي وعن يميني وعن شمالي ومن فوقي وأعوذ
بك أن أغتال من تحتي (1) اللهم لا تؤمني مكرك ولا تولني غيرك ولا تنزع عني
سترك ولا تنسني ذكرك ولا تجعلني من الغافلين (2) وقل اللهم أنت ربي لا إله
إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك من شر ما
صنعت أبوء لك بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت
(3) ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم عافني في بدني وعافني في سمعي وعافني في بصري لا
إله إلا أنت (4) ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم إني أسألك الرضا بعد القضاء وبرد
العيش بعد الموت ولذة النظر إلى وجهك الكريم وشوقا إلى لقائك من غير ضراء
مضرة ولا فتنة مضلة وأعوذ بك أن أظلم أو أظلم أو أعتدي أو يعتدى علي أو
أكسب خطيئة أو ذنبا لا تغفره (5) اللهم إني أسألك الثبات في الأمر والعزيمة
في الرشد وأسألك شكر نعمتك وحسن عبادتك وأسألك قلبا خاشعا سليما وخلقا
مستقيما ولسانا صادقا وعملا  متقبلا وأسألك من خير ما تعلم وأعوذ بك من شر
ما تعلم وأستغفرك لما تعلم فإنك تعلم ولا أعلم وأنت علام الغيوب (6) اللهم
اغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت وما أسررت وما أعلنت وما أنت أعلم به مني فإنك
أنت المقدم وأنت المؤخر وأنت على كل شيء قدير وعلى كل غيب شهيد (7) اللهم
إني أسألك إيمانا لا يرتد ونعيما لا ينفد وقرة عين الأبد ومرافقة نبيك محمد
صلى الله عليه وسلم في أعلى جنة الخلد (8) اللهم إني أسألك الطيبات وفعل
الخيرات وترك المنكرات وحب المساكين أسألك حبك وحب من أحبك وحب كل عمل يقرب
إلي حبك وأن تتوب علي وتغفر لي وترحمني وإذا أردت بقوم فتنة فاقبضني إليك
غير مفتون (9) اللهم بعلمك الغيب وقدرتك على الخلق أحيني ما كانت الحياة
خيرا لي وتوفني ما كانت الوفاة خيرا لي أسألك خشيتك في الغيب والشهادة
وكلمة العدل في الرضا والغضب والقصد في الغنى والفقر ولذة النظر إلى وجهك
والشوق إلى لقائك وأعوذ بك من ضراء مضرة وفتنة مضلة واللهم زينا
PageV01P319
بزينة الإيمان واجعلنا هداة مهتدين (1) اللهم اقسم لنا من خشيتك ما تحول
به بيننا وبين معاصيك ومن طاعتك ما تبلغنا به جنتك ومن اليقين ما تهون به
علينا مصائب الدنيا والآخرة (2) اللهم املأ وجوهنا منك حياء وقلوبنا منك
فرقا واسكن في نفوسنا من عظمتك ما تذلل به جوارحنا لخدمتك واجعلك اللهم أحب
إلينا ممن سواك واجعلنا أخشى لك ممن سواك (3) اللهم اجعل أول يومنا هذا
صلاحا وأوسطه فلاحا وآخره نجاحا اللهم اجعل أوله رحمة وأسطه نعمة وآخره
تكرمة ومغفرة (4) الحمد لله الذي تواضع كل شيء لعظمته وذل كل شيء لعزته
وخضع كل شيء لملكه واستسلم كل شيء لقدرته والحمد لله الذي سكن كل شيء
لهيبته وأظهر كل شيء بحكمته وتصاغر كل شيء لكبريائه (5) اللهم صل على محمد
وعلى آل محمد وأزواج محمد وذريته وبارك على محمد وعلى آله وأزواجه وذريته
كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم في العالمين إنك حميد مجيد  (6)
اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي رسولك الأمين وأعطه
المقام المحمود الذي وعدته يوم الدين (7) اللهم اجعلنا من أوليائك المتقين
وحزبك المفلحين وعبادك الصالحين واستعملنا لمرضاتك عنا ووفقنا لمحابك منا
وصرفنا بحسن اختيارك لنا (8) نسألك جوامع الخير وفواتحه وخواتمه ونعوذ بك
من جوامع الشر وفواتحه وخواتمه (9) اللهم بقدرتك علي تب على إنك أنت التواب
الرحيم وبحلمك عني اعف عني إنك أنت الغفار الحليم وبعلمك بي ارفق بي إنك
أنت أرحم الراحمين وبملكك لي ملكني نفسي ولا تسلطها علي إنك أنت الملك
الجبار (10) سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي
فاغفر لي ذنبي إنك أنت ربي ولا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (11) اللهم ألهمني رشدي
وقني شر نفسي (12) اللهم ارزقني حلالا لا تعاقبني عليه وقنعني بما رزقتني
PageV01P320
واستعملني به صالحا تقبله مني (1) اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية وحسن
اليقين والمعافاة في الدنيا والآخرة (2) يا من لا تضره الذنوب ولا تنقصه
المغفرة هب لي ما لا يضرك وأعطني ما لا ينقصك ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا
مسلمين أنت ولي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين
أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا
حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير
ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر
لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا
وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين
سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم
ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة
وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى
قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا
إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا  واغفر
للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر
وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير
الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي
العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النبيين وآله
وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (5)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, summon, invoke; the core act of petitioning and supplication directed to God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological act of duʿā' as worship (ʿibādah) itself, acknowledging servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) and divine sovereignty (rubūbiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of vocal or inward calling upon God; metaphorical (majāz) when describing the "call" of one's state or need.
- Root: و-ر-د (wa-rā-dā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To arrive at water; a daily portion or litany of devotional recitation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The disciplined daily allotment of remembrance (dhikr) and supplication, structuring the seeker's time toward God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: approaching a watering-place; metaphorical: the soul's regular refreshment through prescribed invocations.
- Root: ح-ر-ث (ḥā-rā-thā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To till, cultivate, plow the earth for sowing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quranic metaphor for seeking the harvest of the Hereafter (ḥarth al-ākhirah) through deeds — the cultivation of one's eternal field.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Purely metaphorical (majāz) in this context; the world is the field, deeds are the seed, and the Hereafter is the harvest.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Omission (Ḥadhf al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "فإن كنت من المريدين" employs an implied conditional structure where the protasis is stated and the apodosis is understood from the imperative that follows, a common Qur'anic and classical pattern for exhortation.
chapters.translation:
I say: These supplications are transmitted with their chains of transmission omitted, being selected from the totality of what Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Mundhir — may God have mercy on them — collected.

Know that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the seeker (murīd), when he enters the morning, that the most beloved of his daily litanies (awrād) be supplication (duʿā'), as will be mentioned in the Book of Litanies. If you are among those who seek the cultivation of the Hereafter (ḥarth al-ākhirah), following the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — in what he supplicated with, then say at the opening of your supplications (1) and at the conclusion of your prescribed prayers (2):

"Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Bestower (al-Wahhāb). There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent."

And say: "I am well-pleased with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — as Prophet" — three times.

And say: "O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Lord of all things and their Sovereign, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul, and from the evil of Satan and his polytheism." (4)

And say: "O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family, and my wealth. O God, veil my faults, calm my fears, and forgive my stumbles. Protect me from before me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge in You from being treacherously destroyed from beneath me." (1)

"O God, do not leave me to Your cunning, do not entrust me to other than You, do not strip away from me Your covering, do not make me forget Your remembrance, and do not make me among the heedless." (2)

And say: "O God, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin; so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You." (3) — three times.

And say: "O God, grant me well-being in my body, grant me well-being in my hearing, grant me well-being in my sight. There is no god but You." (4) — three times.

And say: "O God, I ask You for contentment after decree, and the coolness of life after death, and the delight of gazing upon Your Noble Face, and longing for Your meeting — without harmful adversity or misleading trial. And I seek refuge in You from committing injustice or suffering injustice, from transgression or suffering transgression, or from earning an error or a sin that You will not forgive." (5)

"O God, I ask You for steadfastness in the affair and resolve upon right guidance. I ask You for gratitude for Your favor and excellence of worship of You. I ask You for a humble, sound heart; an upright character; a truthful tongue; and accepted deeds. I ask You for the good of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know — for You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen." (6)

"O God, forgive me what I have advanced and what I have deferred, what I have concealed and what I have declared, and what You know better than I. For You are the Advancer and You are the Deferrer, and You are over all things omnipotent, and over every unseen thing a Witness." (7)

"O God, I ask You for faith that does not regress, bounty that does not expire, the eternal delight of the eye, and the companionship of Your Prophet Muḥammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — in the highest of the everlasting Paradise." (8)

"O God, I ask You for the good things, the doing of good deeds, the abandonment of evil deeds, and love of the poor. I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of every deed that draws me near to Your love; and that You turn to me in repentance, forgive me, and have mercy upon me. And if You intend a trial for a people, then take me to You untried." (9)

"O God, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive so long as life is good for me, and cause me to die when death is good for me. I ask You for fear of You in the unseen and the witnessed, the word of justice in contentment and anger, moderation in wealth and poverty, the delight of gazing upon Your Face, and longing for Your meeting. And I seek refuge in You from harmful adversity and misleading trial. O God, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guided guides." (1)

"O God, apportion to us from Your fear that which will interpose between us and Your acts of disobedience; from Your obedience that which will convey us to Your Paradise; and from certainty that which will make the calamities of this world and the Hereafter light upon us." (2)

"O God, fill our faces with modesty before You, and our hearts with awe of You, and settle within our souls from Your majesty that which will subdue our limbs to Your service. Make You, O God, more beloved to us than anyone other than You, and make us more fearful of You than of anyone other than You." (3)

"O God, make the beginning of this our day righteousness, its middle success, and its end triumph. O God, make its beginning mercy, its middle blessing, and its end honor and forgiveness." (4)

"Praise be to God, before Whose majesty everything humbles itself, before Whose might everything is subdued, before Whose sovereignty everything yields, and before Whose power everything surrenders. And praise be to God, before Whose awe everything is stilled, by Whose wisdom everything is manifested, and before Whose grandeur everything becomes small." (5)

"O God, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, the wives of Muḥammad and his progeny; and bless Muḥammad and his family, his wives and his progeny, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham among the worlds. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." (6)

"O God, send blessings upon Muḥammad, Your servant, Your Prophet, and Your Messenger — the unlettered Prophet, Your trustworthy Messenger — and grant him the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) which You promised him on the Day of Judgment." (7)

"O God, make us among Your righteous friends (awliyā'), Your successful party (ḥizb), and Your righteous servants. Employ us in that which pleases You from us, grant us success in that which You love from us, and divert us by Your good choice for us." (8)

"We ask You for the comprehensive goods, their openings and their endings; and we seek refuge in You from the comprehensive evils, their openings and their endings." (9)

"O God, by Your power over me, turn to me in repentance — indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful. By Your forbearance toward me, pardon me — indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Forbearing. By Your knowledge of me, be gentle with me — indeed, You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. By Your sovereignty over me, take possession of my soul for me and do not let it dominate me — indeed, You are the Sovereign, the Compeller." (10)

"Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise. There is no god but You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me my sin — indeed, You are my Lord, and none forgives sins but You." (11)

"O God, inspire me with my right guidance and protect me from the evil of my soul." (12)

"O God, provide me with lawful sustenance for which You will not call me to account, and make me content with what You have provided me, and employ me in it righteously that You may accept it from me." (1)

"O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, excellence of certainty, and preservation of well-being in this world and the Hereafter." (2)

"O You Whom sins do not harm and Whom forgiveness does not diminish — bestow upon me what does not harm You, and give me what does not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the Hereafter; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, for You are the best of forgivers. And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith — up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ»} (Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise). Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord — to the end of the Surah." (3)

"My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small. And forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women — the living among them and the dead." (4)

"My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. Indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return. There is no might and no power except through God, the Most High, the Magnificent. God suffices us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muḥammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace." (5)

chapters.title_en: The Types of Divinely-Transmitted Seeking of Refuge (Istiʿādhah) from the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| أنواع الاستعاذة المأثورة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

اللهم إني أعوذ بك من البخل وأعوذ بك من الجبن وأعوذ بك من أن أرد إلى
ارذل العمر وأعوذ بك من فتنة الدنيا وأعوذ بك من عذاب القبر (6) اللهم إني
أعوذ بك من طبع يهدي إلى طمع ومن طمع في غير مطمع ومن PageV01P321
طمع حيث لا مطمع (1) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من علم لا ينفع وقلب لا يخشع
ودعاء لا يسمع ونفس لا تشبع وأعوذ بك من الجوع فإنه بئس الضجيع ومن الخيانة
فإنها بئست البطانة ومن الكسل والبخل والجبن والهرم ومن أن أرد إلى ارذل
العمر ومن فتنة الدجال وعذاب القبر ومن فتنة المحيا والممات اللهم إنا
نسألك قلوبا أواهة مخبتة منيبة في سبيلك اللهم إني أسألك عزائم مغفرتك
وموجبات رحمتك والسلامة من كل إثم والغنيمة من كل بر والفوز بالجنة والنجاة
من النار (2) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من التردي وأعوذ بك من الغم والغرق والهدم
وأعوذ بك من أن أموت في سبيلك مدبرا وأعوذ بك من أن أموت في تطلب الدنيا
(3) اللهم إني أعوذ بك شر ما علمت ومن شر ما لم أعلم (4) اللهم جنبني
منكرات الأخلاق والأعمال والأدواء والأهواء (5) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من جهد
البلاء ودرك الشقاء وسوء القضاء وشماتة الأعداء (6) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من
الكفر والدين والفقر وأعوذ بك من عذاب جهنم وأعوذ بك من فتنة الدجال (7)
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر سمعي وبصري وشر لساني وقلبي وشر منيي (8) اللهم
إني أعوذ بك من جار السوء في دار المقامة فإن جار البادية يتحول (9) اللهم
إني أعوذ بك من القسوة والغفلة والعيلة والذلة والمسكنة  وأعوذ بك من الكفر
والفقر والفسوق والشقاق والنفاق وسوء الأخلاق وضيق الأرزاق والسمعة والرياء
وأعوذ بك من الصمم والبكم والعمى والجنون والجذام والبرص وسيىء الأسقام
(10) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من زوال نعمتك ومن تحول عافيتك ومن فجأة نقمتك ومن
جميع سخطك (11) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب النار وفتنة النار وعذاب القبر
وشر فتنة الغنى وشر فتنة الفقر وشر فتنة PageV01P322
المسيح الدجال وأعوذ بك من المغرم والمأثم (1) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من نفس
لا تشبع وقلب لا يخشع وصلاة لا تنفع ودعوة لا تستجاب وأعوذ بك من شر الغم
وفتنة الصدر (2) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من غلبة الدين وغلبة العدو وشماتة
الأعداء (3) وصلى الله على محمد وعلى كل عبد مصطفى من كل العالمين آمين

### ||| الباب الخامس في الأدعية المأثورة عند حدوث كل حادث من الحوادث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is clinging, seeking protection, and taking shelter with one who can repel harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes the soul's attachment to God as the sole Defender against spiritual and physical evils, both known and hidden.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for physical refuge; metaphorically (majāz) for seeking divine preservation from moral and eschatological calamities.
- Root: ب-خ-ل (b-kh-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Restraint of what should be given; withholding due right.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A vice of the soul opposing generosity (sakhāʾ), rooted in excessive love of accumulation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for withholding wealth; metaphorical for withholding knowledge or praise.
- Root: ج-ب-ن (j-b-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cowardice, weakness of heart in facing danger.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A moral failing that impedes the soul from righteous action and steadfastness in faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical fear; metaphorical for spiritual timidity before truth.
- Root: خ-ز-ل (kh-z-l) [as in ارذل]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The lowest, most contemptible state of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Refers to decrepitude of old age when intellect and strength decline.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical decline; metaphorical for the degradation of one's spiritual state.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The repeated "wa-aʿūdhu bika" (and I seek refuge in You) functions as coordinated clauses (jumal maʿṭūfah) linked by wāw, each carrying independent supplicatory force, requiring the verb to be re-stated for emphasis and rhythmic invocation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the transmitted forms of seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) from the Prophet ﷺ are numerous, each addressing a distinct peril of this world and the next. Among them:

(1) "O God, I seek refuge in You from miserliness (al-bukhl), and I seek refuge in You from cowardice (al-jubn), and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit age (aradhal al-ʿumur), and I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world (fitnat al-dunyā), and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr)."

(2) "O God, I seek refuge in You from a nature that leads to covetousness (ṭamaʿ), and from covetousness in that which is not a place of hope, and from covetousness where there is no object of hope."

(3) "O God, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that does not humble itself (lā yakhshaʿ), from a supplication that is not heard, and from a soul that is not satisfied. And I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is an evil bedfellow; and from treachery (al-khiyānah), for it is an evil companion; and from laziness (al-kasal), miserliness, cowardice, and senility (al-haram); and from being returned to the most decrepit age; and from the trial of the Dajjāl and the punishment of the grave; and from the trial of life and the trial of death."

(4) "O God, we ask You for hearts that are penitent (awwāhah), humble (mukhbitah), and returning to You (munībah) in Your path."

(5) "O God, I ask You for the firm resolutions of Your forgiveness (ʿazāʾim maghfiratika), the causes of Your mercy (mūjibāt raḥmatika), safety from every sin, the gain of every righteousness, victory with Paradise, and deliverance from the Fire."

(6) "O God, I seek refuge in You from falling (al-taraddī), and I seek refuge in You from grief (al-ghamm), drowning (al-gharaq), and collapse (al-hadm); and I seek refuge in You from dying while fleeing in Your path; and I seek refuge in You from dying while pursuing this world."

(7) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I know and from the evil of what I do not know."

(8) "O God, keep me away from the abominable acts of character (makārim al-akhlāq), deeds, ailments, and passions (al-ahwāʾ)."

(9) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of affliction (juhd al-balāʾ), the overtaking of misery (darak al-shaqāʾ), the evil of decree (sūʾ al-qaḍāʾ), and the gloating of enemies (shamātat al-aʿdāʾ)."

(10) "O God, I seek refuge in You from disbelief (al-kufr), debt (al-dayn), and poverty (al-faqr); and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell; and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Dajjāl."

(11) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing and my sight, the evil of my tongue and my heart, and the evil of my seminal fluid (mannī)."

(12) "O God, I seek refuge in You from an evil neighbor in the abode of permanent residence (dār al-maqāmah), for the neighbor of the desert may move away."

(13) "O God, I seek refuge in You from hardness of heart (al-qaswah), heedlessness (al-ghaflah), destitution (al-ʿaylah), humiliation (al-dhillah), and abasement (al-maskanah); and I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, immorality (al-fusūq), discord (al-shiqāq), hypocrisy (al-nifāq), evil character, straitened provision, seeking reputation (al-sumʿah), and ostentation (al-riyāʾ); and I seek refuge in You from deafness (al-ṣamam), muteness (al-bakam), blindness (al-ʿamā), madness (al-junūn), leprosy (al-judhām), vitiligo (al-baraṣ), and evil ailments."

(14) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your favor (zawāl niʿmatika), the transition of Your well-being (taḥawwul ʿāfiyatika), the suddenness of Your retribution (fajʾat niqmatika), and from all of Your wrath (sakhaṭika)."

(15) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire and the trial of the Fire, the punishment of the grave, the evil of the trial of wealth, the evil of the trial of poverty, and the evil of the trial of the Messiah the Dajjāl; and I seek refuge in You from debt (al-maghram) and sin (al-maʾtham)."

(16) "O God, I seek refuge in You from a soul that is not satisfied, a heart that does not humble itself, a prayer that does not benefit, and a supplication that is not answered; and I seek refuge in You from the evil of grief and the trial of the breast (fitnat al-ṣadr)."

(17) "O God, I seek refuge in You from the dominance of debt (ghalabat al-dayn), the dominance of the enemy (ghalabat al-ʿadū), and the gloating of enemies (shamātat al-aʿdāʾ)."

And may God bless Muhammad and every chosen servant from all the worlds. Amen.

chapters.arabic_text:
إذا أصبحت وسمعت الأذان فيستحب لك جواب المؤذن وقد ذكرناه وذكرنا أدعية
دخول الخلاء والخروج منه وأدعية الوضوء في كتاب الطهارة فإذا خرجت إلى
المسجد فقل اللهم اجعل في قلبي نورا وفي لساني نورا واجعل في سمعي نورا
واجعل في بصري نورا واجعل خلفي نورا وأمامي نورا واجعل من فوقي نورا اللهم
أعطني (4) نورا وقل أيضا اللهم إني أسألك بحق السائلين عليك وبحق ممشاي هذا
إليك (5) فإني لم أخرج أشرا ولا بطرا ولا رياء ولا سمعة خرجت اتقاء سخطك
وابتغاء مرضاتك فأسألك أن تنقذني من النار وأن تغفر لي ذنوبي إنه لا يغفر
الذنوب إلا أنت
فإن خرجت من المنزل لحاجة فقل بسم الله رب أعوذ بك أن أظلم أو أظلم أو
أجهل أو يجهل علي (6) بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
العلي العظيم بسم الله التكلان على الله (7)
فإذا انتهيت إلى المسجد تريد دخوله فقل اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد
وسلم اللهم اغفر لي جميع ذنوبي وافتح لي أبواب رحمتك (8) وقدم رجلك اليمنى
في الدخول فإذا رأيت في المسجد من يبيع أو يبتاع فقل لا أربح الله تجارتك
(9) وإذا رأيت من ينشد ضالة في المسجد فقل لا ردها الله عليك أمر به رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (10) فإذا صليت ركعتي الصبح فقل بسم الله اللهم
إني أسألك رحمة من عندك تهدي بها قلبي الدعاء إلى آخره (11) PageV01P323
كما أوردناه عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
فإذا ركعت فقل في ركوعك اللهم لك ركعت ولك خشعت وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت وعليك
توكلت أنت ربي خشع سمعي وبصري ومخي وعظمي وعصبي وما استقلت به قدمي لله رب
العالمين (1) وإن أحببت فقل سبحان ربي العظيم ثلاث مرات (2) أو سبوح قدوس
رب الملائكة والروح (3) فإذا رفعت رأسك من الركوع فقل سمع الله لمن حمده
ربنا لك الحمد ملء السموات وملء الأرض وملء ما شئت من شيء بعد أهل الثناء
والمجد أحق ما قال العبد وكلنا لك عبد لا مانع لما أعطيت ولا معطي لما منعت
ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد (4) وإذا سجدت فقل اللهم لك سجدت وبك آمنت ولك
أسلمت سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق سمعه وبصره فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين
اللهم سجد لك سوادي وخيالي وآمن بك فؤادي أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي وهذا
ما جنيت على نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (5) أو تقول سبحان
ربي الأعلى ثلاث مرات (6) فإذا فرغت من الصلاة فقل اللهم أنت السلام ومنك
السلام تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام (7) وتدعو بسائر الأدعية التي ذكرناها
فإذا قمت من المجلس وأردت دعاء يكفر لغو المجلس فقل سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك
أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أستغفرك وأتوب إليك عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي
فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (8)
فإذا دخلت السوق فقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد
يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير (9) بسم الله
اللهم إني أسألك خير هذه السوق وخير ما فيها اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شرها  وشر
ما فيها اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أصيب فيها يمينا فاجرة أو صفقة خاسرة (10)
فإن كان عليك دين فقل اللهم اكفني بحلالك عن حرامك وأغنني بفضلك عمن سواك
(11)
فإذا لبست ثوبا جديدا فقل اللهم كسوتني هذا الثوب فلك الحمد أسألك من
خيره وخير ما صنع له وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما صنع له (12)
وإذا PageV01P324
رأيت شيئا من الطيرة تكرهه فقل اللهم لا يأتي بالحسنات إلا أنت ولا يذهب
بالسيئات إلا أنت ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله (1)
وإذا رأيت الهلال فقل اللهم أهله علينا بالأمن والإيمان والبر والسلامة
والإسلام والتوفيق لما تحب وترضى والحفظ عمن تسخط ربي وربك الله (2) ويقول
هلال رشد وخير آمنت بخالقك (3) اللهم إني أسألك خير هذا الشهر وخير القدر
وأعوذ بك من شر يوم الحشر (4) وتكبر قبله أولا ثلاثا
وإذا هبت الريح فقل اللهم إني أسألك خير هذه الريح وخير ما فيها وخير ما
أرسلت به ونعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما فيها ومن شر ما أرسلت به (5)
وإذا بلغك وفاة أحد فقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون
اللهم اكتبه في المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين
اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله (6)
وتقول عند التصدق {ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم}
وتقول عند الخسران {عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون}
وتقول عند ابتداء الأمور ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيىء لنا من أمرنا رشدا
رب اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري
وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب
النار تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا
وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته
(7)
فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا
قبل ذلك (8) قاله كعب
فإذا أمطرت السماء فقل اللهم سقيا هنيئا وصيبا نافعا (9) اللهم اجعله  صيب
رحمة ولا تجعله صيب عذاب (10)
فإذا غضبت فقل اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي PageV01P325
وأجرني من الشيطان الرجيم (1)
فإذا خفت قوما فقل اللهم إنا نجعلك في نحورهم ونعوذ بك من شرورهم (2)
فإذا غزوت فقل اللهم أنت عضدي ونصيري وبك أقاتل (3)
وإذا طنت أذنك فصل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقل ذكر الله من ذكرني
بخير (4)
فإذا رأيت استجابة دعائك فقل الحمد لله الذي بعزته وجلاله تتم الصالحات
وإذا أبطأت فقل الحمد لله على كل حال (5)
وإذا سمعت أذان المغرب فقل اللهم هذا إقبال ليلك وإدبار نهارك وأصوات
دعاتك وحضور صلواتك أسألك أن تغفر لي (6)
وإذا أصابك هم فقل اللهم إني عبدك وابن عبدك وابن أمتك ناصيتي بيدك ماض
في حكمك عدل في قضاؤك أسالك بكل اسم هو لك سميت به نفسك أو أنزلته في كتابك
أو علمته أحدا من خلقك أو استأثرت به في علم الغيب عندك أن تجعل القرآن
ربيع قلبي ونور صدري وجلاء غمي وذهاب حزني وهمي (7) قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
ما أصاب أحدا حزن فقال ذلك إلا أذهب الله همه وأبدله مكانه فرحا فقيل له يا
رسول الله أفلا نتعلمها فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بلى ينبغي لمن سمعها أن
يتعلمها
وإذا وجدت وجعا في جسدك أو جسد غيرك فارقة برقية رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم كان إذا اشتكى الإنسان قرحة أو جرحا وضع سبابته على الأرض ثم رفعها
وقال بسم الله تربة أرضنا بريقة بعضنا يشفى سقيمنا بإذن ربنا (8)
وإذا وجدت وجعا في جسدك فضع يدك على الذي يتألم من جسدك وقل بسم الله
ثلاثا وقل سبع مرات أعوذ بعزة الله وقدرته من شر ما أجد وأحاذر (9)
فإذا أصابك كرب فقل لا إله إلا الله العلي الحليم لا إله إلا الله رب
العرش العظيم لا إله إلا الله رب السموات السبع ورب العرش الكريم (10)
فإن أردت النوم فتوضأ أولا ثم توسد على يمينك مستقبل القبلة ثم كبر الله
تعالى أربعا وثلاثين  وسبحه ثلاثا وثلاثين واحمده ثلاثا وثلاثين (11) ثم قل
اللهم إني أعوذ برضاك من سخطك وبمعافاتك من عقوبتك وأعوذ بك منك اللهم إني
لا أستطيع أن أبلغ ثناء عليك ولو حرصت ولكن أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (12)
اللهم باسمك أحيا وأموت (13) اللهم رب السموات ورب الأرض ورب كل شيء ومليكه
فالق الحب والنوى ومنزل التوراة والإنجيل PageV01P326
والقرآن أعوذ بك من شر كل ذي شر ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها أنت
الأول فليس قبلك شيء وأنت الآخر فليس بعدك شيء وأنت الظاهر فليس فوقك شيء
وأنت الباطن فليس دونك شيء اقض عني الدين وأغنني من الفقر (1) اللهم إنك
خلقت نفسي وأنت تتوفاها لك مماتها ومحياها اللهم إن أمتها فاغفر لها وإن
أحييتها فاحفظها اللهم إني أسألك العافية في الدنيا والآخرة (2) باسمك ربي
وضعت جنبي فاغفر لي ذنبي (3) اللهم قني عذابك يوم تجمع عبادك (4) اللهم
أسلمت لك نفسي إليك ووجهت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري إليك والجأت ظهري إليك رغبة
ورهبة إليك لا ملجأ ولا منجا منك إلا إليك آمنت بكتابك الذي أنزلت ونبيك
الذي أرسلت (5)
ويكون هذا آخر دعائك فقد أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك وليقل
قبل ذلك اللهم أيقظني في أحب الساعات إليك واستعملني بأحب الأعمال إليك
تقربني إليك زلفى وتبعدني من سخطك بعدا أسألك فتعطيني وأستغفرك فتغفر لي
وأدعوك فتستجيب لي (6)
فإذا استيقظت من نومك عند الصباح فقل الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعدما أماتنا
وإليه النشور (7) أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله والعظمة والسلطان لله والعزة
والقدرة لله (8) أصبحنا على فطرة الإسلام وكلمة الإخلاص وعلى دين نبينا
محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وملة أبينا إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين (9)
اللهم بك أصبحنا وبك أمسينا وبك نحيا وبك نموت وإليك المصير (10) اللهم إني
أسألك أن تبعثنا في هذا اليوم إلى كل خير ونعوذ بك أن نجترح فيه سوءا أو
نجره إلى مسلم فإنك قلت {وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار
ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى}  (11) اللهم فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا
والشمس والقمر حسبانا أسألك خير هذا اليوم وخير ما فيه وأعوذ بك من شره وشر
ما فيه (12) بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ما شاء الله
PageV01P327
كل نعمة من الله ما شاء الله الخير كله بيد الله ما شاء الله لا يصرف
السوء إلا الله (1) رضيت بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا وبمحمد صلى الله عليه
وسلم نبيا ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير (2) وإذا أمسى قال
ذلك إلا أنه يقول أمسينا ويقول مع ذلك أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات وأسمائه
كلها من شر ما ذرأ وبرأ ومن شر كل ذي شر ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها
إن ربي على صراط مستقيم (3) وإسناده جيد ولمسلم من حديث أبي هريرة في
الدعاء عند النوم أعوذ بك من شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها وللطبراني في
الدعاء من حديث أبي الدرداء (4) وإذا نظر في المرآة قال الحمد لله الذي سوى
خلقي فعدله وكرم صورة وجهي وحسنها وجعلني من المسلمين (5) وإذا اشتريت
خادما أو غلاما أو دابة فخذ بناصيته وقل اللهم إني أسألك خيره وخير ما جبل
عليه وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما جبل عليه (6) وإذا هنأت بالنكاح فقل بارك الله
فيك وبارك عليك وجمع بينكما في خير (7) وإذا قضيت الدين فقل للمقضي له بارك
الله لك في أهلك ومالك إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنما جزاء السلف الحمد
والأداء (8)
فهذه أدعية لا يستغني المريد عن حفظها وما سوى ذلك من أدعية السفر
والصلاة والوضوء ذكرناها في كتاب الحج والصلاة والطهارة فإن قلت فما فائدة
الدعاء والقضاء لا مرد له فاعلم أن من القضاء رد البلاء بالدعاء فالدعاء
سبب PageV01P328
لرد البلاء واستجلاب الرحمة كما أن الترس سبب لرد السهم والماء سبب لخروج
النبات من الأرض فكما أن الترس يدفع السهم فيتدافعان فكذلك الدعاء والبلاء
يتعالجان وليس من شرط الاعتراف بقضاء الله تعالى أن لا يحمل السلاح وقد قال
تعالى {خذوا حذركم} وأن  لا يسقي الأرض بعد بث البذر فيقال إن سبق القضاء
بالنبات نبت البذر وإن لم يسبق لم ينبت بل ربط الأسباب بالمسببات هو القضاء
الأول الذي هو كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب وترتيب تفصيل المسببات على تفاصيل
الأسباب على التدريج والتقدير هو القدر والذي قدر الخير قدره بسبب والذي
قدر الشر قدر لدفعه سببا فلا تناقض بين هذه الأمور عند من انفتحت بصيرته ثم
في الدعاء من الفائدة ما ذكرناه في الذكر فإنه يستدعي حضور القلب مع الله
وهو منتهى العبادات ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الدعاء مخ العبادة (1)
والغالب على الخلق أنه لا تنصرف قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله عز وجل إلا عند إلمام
حاجة وإرهاق ملمة فإن الإنسان إذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض فالحاجة تحوج إلى
الدعاء والدعاء يرد القلب إلى الله عز وجل بالتضرع والاستكانة فيحصل به
الذكر الذي هو أشرف العبادات ولذلك صار البلاء موكلا بالأنبياء عليهم
السلام ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل لأنه يرد القلب بالافتقار والتضرع
إلى الله عز وجل ويمنع من نسيانه وأما الغنى فسبب للبطر في غالب الأمور فإن
الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى فهذا ما أردنا أن نورده من جملة الأذكار
والدعوات والله الموفق للخير وأما بقية الدعوات في الأكل والسفر وعيادة
المريض وغيرها فستأتي في مواضعها إن شاء الله تعالى وعلى الله التكلان نجز
كتاب الأذكار والدعوات بكماله يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب الأوراد والحمد
لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-ب (jawaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To answer, respond, reply; the response of one who is called.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The response of the servant to the caller (mu'adhdhin) as an act of worship mirroring the divine response to supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the exchange of speech; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to God's answering of prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Answer Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The protasis "if you do X" governs the apodosis "then say Y," with the imperative as the standard answer to a conditional when the action is commanded.
chapters.translation:
I say: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is commendable (mustaḥabb) for you to answer the mu'adhdhin, and we have already mentioned this along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy and the supplications of ablution in the Book of Purification. When you set out for the mosque, say: "O Allah, place in my heart a light, and in my tongue a light, and place in my hearing a light, and place in my sight a light, and place behind me a light, and before me a light, and place above me a light. O Allah, grant me a light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking to You — for I have not come out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have come out seeking to avoid Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to save me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins but You."

If you leave the house for some need, say: "In the name of Allah. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or being treated with ignorance. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. There is no might and no power except with Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. In the name of Allah, upon Allah do I rely."

When you arrive at the mosque intending to enter it, say: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and grant him peace. O Allah, forgive me all my sins and open for me the gates of Your mercy." And put forward your right foot when entering. If you see in the mosque someone buying or selling, say: "May Allah not profit your trade." And if you see someone announcing a lost object in the mosque, say: "May Allah not return it to you" — this was commanded by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When you have prayed the two units of the dawn (ṣubḥ), say: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You for mercy from Your presence by which You may guide my heart..." — the supplication to its end, as we have transmitted it from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

When you bow (rukūʿ), say in your bowing: "O Allah, to You I bow, and to You I humble myself, and in You I believe, and to You I submit, and upon You I rely. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my brain, my bones, my sinews, and whatever my feet carry have humbled themselves to Allah, the Lord of the worlds." And if you wish, say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent" three times, or "Most Holy, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit." When you raise your head from bowing, say: "Allah hears him who praises Him. Our Lord, to You is all praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth and filling whatever You will after that. O Possessor of praise and glory, most worthy of what the servant says — and all of us are Your servants — there is no preventer of what You give, nor giver of what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You." When you prostrate (sujūd), say: "O Allah, to You I prostrate, and in You I believe, and to You I submit. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and formed it and opened its hearing and sight. Blessed be Allah, the Best of creators. O Allah, my dark form and my shadow have prostrated to You, and my heart has believed in You. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin. This is what I have wrought against myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You." Or you may say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" three times. When you finish the prayer, say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor." And supplicate with the rest of the supplications we have mentioned. When you rise from the gathering and wish a supplication that expiates the idle talk of the gathering, say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You."

When you enter the marketplace, say: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not. In His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this market and the good of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from striking in it a false oath or a losing bargain." If you have a debt upon you, say: "O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful provision against Your forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty from all besides You."

When you put on a new garment, say: "O Allah, You have clothed me with this garment, so to You be praise. I ask You for its good and the good of that for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of that for which it was made."

When you see something of ill omen (ṭiyarah) that you dislike, say: "O Allah, none brings good things but You, and none removes evil things but You. There is no might and no power except with Allah."

When you see the new crescent moon, say: "O Allah, bring it upon us with security and faith, with well-being and safety, with Islam and success in what You love and are pleased with, and with protection from what You abhor. My Lord and your Lord is Allah." And he says: "A crescent of guidance and good. I believe in your Creator." "O Allah, I ask You for the good of this month and the good of the decree, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of the Day of Gathering." And he says the takbīr (Allāhu akbar) three times before it.

When the wind blows, say: "O Allah, I ask You for the good of this wind and the good of what is in it and the good of what it has been sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it and the evil of what it has been sent with."

When news of someone's death reaches you, say: "Verily we belong to Allah and verily to Him we return, and verily to our Lord we are turning. O Allah, write him among the doers of good, and place his record in ʿIlliyyīn, and appoint for his posterity a successor among those who remain. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward, and do not try us after him, and forgive us and him."

And you say at the time of giving charity: {«رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ»} ("Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing").

And you say at the time of loss: {«عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ»} ("Perhaps our Lord will give us better than it in exchange; indeed we are desirous of our Lord").

And you say at the commencement of affairs: "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. My Lord, expand for me my breast and ease for me my task."

And you say when looking at the sky: {«رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ»} ("Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire"). "Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon."

When you hear the sound of thunder, say: "Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels from His awe."

If you see lightning bolts, say: "O Allah, do not kill us with Your wrath and do not destroy us with Your punishment, but grant us well-being before that." This was said by Kaʿb.

When the sky rains, say: "O Allah, a wholesome watering and a beneficial downpour. O Allah, make it a downpour of mercy and do not make it a downpour of punishment."

When you become angry, say: "O Allah, forgive me my sin and remove the rage of my heart, and save me from the accursed Satan."

When you fear a people, say: "O Allah, we place You against their throats, and we seek refuge in You from their evils."

When you go on a raid (ghazw), say: "O Allah, You are my support and my helper, and by You I fight."

When your ear rings, send blessings upon Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and say: "May Allah mention with good the one who mentioned me with good."

When you see the answer to your supplication, say: "Praise be to Allah, by whose might and majesty good deeds are accomplished." And when it is delayed, say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."

When you hear the adhān of sunset (maghrib), say: "O Allah, this is the coming of Your night and the departure of Your day, and the voices of Your callers and the presence of Your prayers. I ask You to forgive me."

When distress befalls you, say: "O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your handmaid. My forelock is in Your hand, Your decree is executed upon me, and Your judgment upon me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours — by which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creatures, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen with You — that You make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my breast, the dispeller of my grief, and the remover of my sorrow and distress." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "No one is afflicted with sorrow and says this except that Allah removes his sorrow and gives him joy in its place." It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not learn it?" He said: "Yes, it behooves whoever hears it to learn it."

When you feel pain in your body or in the body of another, treat it with the ruqyah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When a person complained of a sore or a wound, he would place his index finger on the ground, then raise it and say: "In the name of Allah. The dust of our earth, with the saliva of some of us, heals our sick by the permission of our Lord."

When you feel pain in your body, place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say "In the name of Allah" three times, and say seven times: "I seek refuge in the might of Allah and His power from the evil of what I find and fear."

When distress (karb) befalls you, say: "There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Noble Throne."

If you intend to sleep, perform ablution first, then recline on your right side facing the qiblah, then say the takbīr (Allāhu akbar) thirty-four times, the tasbīḥ (subḥān Allāh) thirty-three times, and the taḥmīd (al-ḥamdu lillāh) thirty-three times. Then say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. O Allah, I cannot attain full praise of You, though I strive, but You are as You have praised Yourself." "O Allah, in Your name I live and I die." "O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of everything and its Sovereign, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every possessor of evil and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. You are the First, so nothing is before You; You are the Last, so nothing is after You; You are the Manifest, so nothing is above You; You are the Hidden, so nothing is below You. Settle my debt and enrich me against poverty." "O Allah, You created my soul and You take it. To You belong its death and its life. O Allah, if You cause it to die, forgive it, and if You give it life, protect it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter." "In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, so forgive me my sin." "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You gather Your servants." "O Allah, I have submitted my soul to You, and I have turned my face to You, and I have entrusted my affair to You, and I have leaned my back upon You, in desire and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no deliverance from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed and in Your Prophet whom You have sent."

And let this be the last of your supplication, for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. And let him say before that: "O Allah, awaken me in the hours most beloved to You, and employ me in the deeds most beloved to You, that they may bring me near to You in closeness and distance me from Your wrath in distance. I ask You and You give me; I seek Your forgiveness and You forgive me; I call upon You and You answer me."

When you wake from your sleep in the morning, say: "Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection." "We have entered the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah. Greatness and sovereignty belong to Allah. Might and power belong to Allah." "We have entered the morning upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah) of Islam, upon the word of sincerity, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and upon the creed of our father Abraham, a ḥanīf, and he was not of the polytheists." "O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return." "O Allah, I ask You to raise us in this day to every good, and I seek refuge in You from committing in it any evil or bringing it upon a Muslim, for You have said: {«وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُم بِاللَّيْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بِالنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ لِيُقْضَىٰ أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى»} ("And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He raises you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled")." "O Allah, Splitter of the dawn and Maker of the night a stillness and the sun and moon a reckoning, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it." "In the name of Allah. Whatever Allah wills — there is no power except with Allah. Whatever Allah wills — every blessing is from Allah. Whatever Allah wills — all good is in the hand of Allah. Whatever Allah wills — none repels evil but Allah." "I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as Prophet. Our Lord, upon You we rely, and to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return." And when he enters the evening, he says the same, except that he says "We have entered the evening," and he adds: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah and all His names from the evil of what He has created and brought forth, and from the evil of every possessor of evil, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path." Its chain of transmission (isnād) is sound (jayyid). Muslim has from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah concerning the supplication at sleep: "I seek refuge in You from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold." And al-Ṭabarānī has it in the supplication from the ḥadīth of Abū al-Dardā'.

When he looks in the mirror, he says: "Praise be to Allah who shaped my creation and made it balanced, honored the form of my face and beautified it, and made me among the Muslims."

When you purchase a servant, a boy, or an animal, take hold of its forelock and say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good and the good of what it was created upon, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what it was created upon."

When you are congratulated upon marriage, say: "May Allah bless you and bless upon you, and may He unite you both in good."

When you repay a debt, say to the one repaid: "May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth" — for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The recompense of a loan is praise and repayment."

These are supplications that the seeker (murīd) cannot do without memorizing. As for the rest of the supplications — of travel, prayer, and ablution — we have mentioned them in the Book of Pilgrimage, the Book of Prayer, and the Book of Purification.

If you say: "What is the benefit of supplication, when the decree (qaḍā') cannot be repelled?" — Know that part of the decree is the repelling of affliction by supplication. Supplication is a cause for repelling affliction and drawing down mercy, just as the shield is a cause for repelling the arrow and water is a cause for bringing forth vegetation from the earth. Just as the shield repels the arrow and the two contend, so too supplication and affliction contend with one another. It is not a condition of acknowledging the decree of Allah, the Most High, that one should not bear arms — for He, the Most High, has said: {«خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ»} ("Take your precaution") — nor that one should not water the earth after sowing the seed, such that it might be said: "If the decree of vegetation preceded, the seed would grow; and if it did not precede, it would not grow." Rather, the linking of causes to their effects is itself the first decree, which is like the blink of an eye or even nearer. And the arrangement of the details of effects upon the details of causes, gradually and by measure, is the divine ordainment (qadar). He who ordained good ordained it through a cause, and He who ordained evil ordained for its repulsion a cause. There is no contradiction among these matters for one whose inner sight has been opened.

Then in supplication there is the benefit we mentioned concerning remembrance (dhikr), for it calls for the presence of the heart with Allah, and that is the ultimate goal of acts of worship. For this reason the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship." The prevailing condition of people is that their hearts do not turn to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except at the onset of a need or the pressing of a calamity — for "when evil touches man, he is full of extensive supplication." Need compels one to supplication, and supplication returns the heart to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through humility and submissiveness, thereby attaining the remembrance that is the noblest of acts of worship. For this reason, affliction is entrusted to the prophets, peace be upon them, then to the saints, then to the most excellent and then the most excellent — because it returns the heart through neediness and supplication to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and prevents forgetfulness of Him. As for wealth, it is a cause of insolence in most matters, for "man does indeed transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient."

This is what we intended to present from the totality of remembrances (adhkār) and supplications (daʿawāt). Allah is the Grantor of success to good. As for the remaining supplications — concerning eating, travel, visiting the sick, and others — they will come in their proper places, Allah willing. Upon Allah is reliance. The Book of Remembrances and Supplications is completed in its entirety. It will be followed, Allah willing, by the Book of Liturgies (al-Awrād). Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and grant them peace.
