From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Thawbān — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever confines himself (ʿakafa nafsahu) between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ in a congregational mosque, speaking nothing but prayer or Quran, it is incumbent upon Allah to build for him two palaces in Paradise, each palace spanning a journey of one hundred years, and to plant for him between them vegetation that, if all the people of the world were to traverse it, would encompass them."

He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever bows ten rakʿahs between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise." ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Then our palaces will be many, O Messenger of Allah!" He replied: "Allah's (gift) is more abundant and more excellent" — or he said "more pure."

From Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever prays Maghrib in congregation, then prays two rakʿahs after it without speaking anything of worldly matters in between, and recites in the first rakʿah the Opening of the Book (Fātiḥat al-Kitāb) and ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and two verses from its middle — {«وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ ۖ لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ الرَّحِيمُ»} and {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ»} to the end of the verse — and recites Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad fifteen times, then bows and prostrates. When he stands for the second rakʿah, he recites the Opening of the Book, the Throne Verse (Āyat al-Kursī), and the two verses after it up to His saying {«أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ»}, and three verses from the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah, from His saying {«لِّلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} to its end, and Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad fifteen times." The description of its reward in the ḥadīth exceeds all enumeration.

Karz ibn Wabarah — who was among the abdāl (substitutes, saintly figures) — said: I said to al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him: "Teach me something that I may do every night." He said: "When you pray Maghrib, stand up until the time of the ʿIshāʾ prayer, praying, without speaking to anyone, and devote yourself to your prayer in which you are engaged. Conclude the prayer (salām) after every two rakʿahs, and recite in every rakʿah the Opening of the Book once and Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad three times. When you finish your prayer, return to your dwelling without speaking to anyone, and pray two rakʿahs, reciting the Opening of the Book and Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad seven times in each rakʿah. Then prostrate after your salām and seek forgiveness of Allah, the Exalted, seven times, and say: 'Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greater, and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent' seven times. Then raise your head from prostration, sit upright, raise your hands, and say: 'O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O God of the first and the last, O Most Merciful of this world and the Hereafter and of both, O Lord, O Lord, O Lord, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah.' Then stand while raising your hands and supplicate with this invocation. Then sleep wherever you wish, facing the qiblah on your right side, and send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and persist in sending blessings upon him until sleep overcomes you."

I (Karz) said to him: "I would love for you to tell me from whom you heard this." He said: "I was present with Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he taught this invocation and it was revealed to him, and I was with him, and that was in my presence. So I learned it from the one who taught it to him."

It is said that whoever persists in this invocation and this prayer with sound certainty (ḥusn yaqīn) and sincere intention (ṣidq niyyah) will see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in his dream before departing this world. Indeed, some people did this and saw that they were admitted into Paradise, saw the prophets therein, and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, therein, spoke with him, and he taught them.

In sum, what has been reported concerning the virtue of reviving the time between the two evening prayers is abundant, to the extent that it was said to ʿUbayd Allāh, the freed slave (mawlā) of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, command any prayer other than the obligatory ones?" He said: "What is between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ."

He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever prays between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ — that is the prayer of the penitent (ṣalāt al-awwābīn)."

Al-Aswad said: "I never came to Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, at this time except that I saw him praying." I asked him about it, and he said: "Yes, it is the hour of heedlessness (sāʿat al-ghaflah)."

Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, used to persist in it and say: "It is the night-rising (nāshiʾat al-layl)," and he would say: "In it was revealed the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} (Their sides forsake their beds)."

Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: I said to Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī: "I fast during the day and break my fast between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ — do you prefer this, or that I break my fast during the day and revive the time between them?" He said: "Combine both." I said: "If that is not feasible?" He said: "Break your fast and pray between them."

### |||| The Virtue of the Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl)
