chapters.arabic_text:
أما من الآيات فقوله تعالى {إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل}
الآية وقوله تعالى {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقوله سبحانه
وتعالى {تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع} وقوله تعالى أمن هو قانت آناء الليل
الآية وقوله عز وجل {والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما} وقوله تعالى
{واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قيل هي قيام الليل يستعان بالصبر عليه على
مجاهدة النفس ومن الأخبار قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعقد الشيطان على قافية
رأس أحدكم إذا هو نام ثلاث عقد يضرب مكان كل عقدة عليك ليل طويل فارقد فإن
استيقظ وذكر الله تعالى انحلت عقدة فإن توضأ انحلت عقدة فإن صلى انحلت عقدة
فأصبح نشيطا طيب النفس وإلا أصبح خبيث النفس كسلان (2) وفي الخبر أنه ذكر
عنده رجل ينام كل الليل حتى يصبح فقال ذاك رجل بال الشيطان في ادنه (3) وفي
الخبر إن للشيطان سعوطا ولعوقا وذرورا فإذا أسعط العبد ساء خلقه وإذا ألعقه
ذرب لسانه بالشر وإذا ذره نام الليل حتى يصبح (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
ركعتان يركعهما العبد  في جوف الليل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها ولولا أن أشق
على أمتي لفرضتهما عليهم (5) وفي الصحيح عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم قال إن من الليل ساعة لا يوافقها عبد مسلم يسأل الله تعالى خيرا إلا
أعطاه إياه وفي رواية يسأل الله تعالى خيرا من الدنيا والآخرة وذلك في كل
ليلة وقال المغيرة بن شعبة قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى تفطرت
قدماه فقيل له أما قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فقال أفلا أكون
عبدا شكورا (6) ويظهر من معناه أن ذلك كناية عن زيادة الرتبة فإن الشكر سبب
المزيد قال تعالى {لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا
هريرة أتريد أن تكون رحمة الله عليك حيا وميتا ومقبورا ومبعوثا قم من الليل
فصل وأنت تريد رضا ربك يا أبا هريرة صل في زوايا بيتك يكن نور بيتك في
السماء كنور الكواكب والنجم عند أهل الدنيا (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
عليكم بقيام الليل فإنه دأب الصالحين قبلكم فإن قيام الليل قربة إلى الله
عز وجل وتكفير للذنوب PageV01P353
ومطردة للداء عن الجسد ومنهاة عن الإثم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما
من امرئ تكون له صلاة بالليل فغلبه عليها النوم إلا كتب له أجر صلاته وكان
نومه صدقة عليه (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر لو أردت سفرا أعددت له
عدة قال نعم قال فكيف سفر طريق القيامة ألا أنبئك يا أبا ذر بما ينفعك ذلك
اليوم قال بلى بأبي أنت وأمي قال صم يوما شديد الحر ليوم النشور وصل ركعتين
في ظلمة الليل لوحشة القبور وحج حجة لعظائم الأمور وتصدق بصدقة على مسكين
أو كلمة حق تقولها أو كلمة شر تسكت عنها (3) وروي أنه كان على عهد النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل إذا أخذ الناس مضاجعهم وهدأت العيون قام يصلي ويقرأ
القرآن ويقول يا رب النار أجرني منها فذكر ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه  وسلم
فقال إذا كان ذلك فآذنوني فأتاه فاستمع فلما أصبح قال يا فلان هلا سألت
الله الجنة قال يا رسول الله إني لست هناك ولا يبلغ عملي ذاك فلم يلبث إلا
يسيرا حتى نزل جبرائيل عليه السلام وقال أخبر فلانا أن الله قد أجاره من
النار وأدخله الجنة (4) ويروى أن جبرائيل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم نعم الرجل ابن عمر لو كان يصلي بالليل فأخبره النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم بذلك فكان يداوم بعده على قيام الليل (5) قال نافع كان يصلي
بالليل ثم يقول يا نافع أسحرنا فأقول لا فيقوم لصلاته ثم يقول يا نافع
أسحرنا فأقول نعم فيقعد فيستغفر الله تعالى حتى يطلع الفجر وقال علي بن أبي
طالب شبع يحيى بن زكريا عليهما السلام من خبز شعير فنام عن ورده حتى أصبح
فأوحى الله تعالى إليه يا يحيى أوجدت دارا خيرا لك من داري أم وجدت جوارا
خيرا لك من جواري فوعزتي وجلالي يا يحيى لو اطلعت إلى الفردوس اطلاعه لذاب
شحمك ولزهقت نفسك اشتياقا ولو اطلعت إلى جهنم اطلاعة لذاب شحمك ولبكيت
الصديد بعد الدموع ولبست الجلد بعد المسوح وقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم إن فلانا يصلي بالليل فإذا أصبح سرق فقال سينهاه ما يعمل (6) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم رحم الله رجلا قام من الليل فصلى ثم أيقظ امرأته فصلت فإن
أبت نضح في وجهها الماء (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم رحم الله امرأة قامت
من الليل فصلت ثم أيقظت زوجها فصلى فإن أبى نضحت في وجهه الماء وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم من استيقظ من الليل وأيقظ امرأته فصليا ركعتين كتبا من
الذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل الصلاة
بعد المكتوبة قيام الليل (9) وقال PageV01P354
عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من نام عن حزبه أو عن
شيء منه بالليل فقرأه بين صلاة الفجر والظهر كتب له كأنما قرأه من الليل
(1) الآثار  روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يمر بالآية من ورده بالليل فيسقط
حتى يعاد منها أياما كثيرة كما يعاد المريض وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
إذا هدأت العيون قام فيسمع له دوي كدوي النحل حتى يصبح ويقال إن سفيان
الثوري رحمه الله شبع ليلة فقال إن الحمار إذا زيد في علفه زيد في عمله
فقام تلك الليلة حتى أصبح وكان طاوس رحمه الله إذا اضطجع على فراشه يتقلى
عليه كما تتقلى الحبة على المقلاة ثم يثب ويصلي إلى الصباح ثم يقول طير ذكر
جهنم نوم العابدين وقال الحسن رحمه الله ما نعلم عملا أشد من مكابدة الليل
ونفقة هذا المال فقيل له ما بال المتهجدين من أحسن الناس وجوها قال لأنهم
خلوا بالرحمن بالرحمن فألبسهم نورا من نوره وقدم بعض الصالحين من سفره فمهد
له فراش فنام عليه حتى فاته ورده فحلف أن لا ينام بعدها على فراش أبدا وكان
عبد العزيز بن رواد إذا جن عليه الليل يأتي فراشه فيمو يده عليه ويقول إنك
للين ووالله إن في الجنة لألين منك ولا يزال يصلي الليل كله وقال الفضيل
إني لأستقبل الليل من أوله فيهولني طوله فأفتتح القرآن فأصبح وما قضيت
نهمتي وقال الحسن إن الرجل ليذنب الذنب فيحرم به قيام الليل وقال الفضيل
إذا لم تقدر على قيام الليل وصيام النهار فاعلم أنك محروم وقد كثرت خطيئتك
وكان صلة بن أشيم رحمه الله يصلي الليل كله فإذا كان في السحر قال إلهي ليس
مثلي يطلب الجنة ولكن أجرني برحمتك من النار وقال رجل لبعض الحكماء إني
لأضعف عن قيام الليل فقال له يا أخي لا تعص الله تعالى ولا تقم بالليل وكان
للحسن بن صالح جارية فباعها من قوم فلما كان في جوف الليل قامت الجارية
فقالت يا أهل الدار الصلاة الصلاة فقالوا أصبحنا أطلع الفجر فقالت وما
تصلون إلا المكتوبة قالوا نعم فرجعت إلى الحسن فقالت يا مولاي بعتني من قوم
لا يصلون إلا المكتوبة ردني  فردها وقال الربيع بت في منزل الشافعي رضي الله
عنه ليالي كثيرة فلم يكن ينام من الليل إلا يسيرا وقال أبو الجويرية لقد
صحبت أبا حنيفة رضي الله عنه ستة أشهر فما فيها ليلة وضع جنبه على الأرض
وكان أبو حنيفة يحيي نصف الليل فمر بقوم فقالوا إن هذا يحيي الليل كله فقال
إني أستحي أن أوصف بما لا أفعل فكان بعد ذلك يحيى الليل كله ويروى أنه ما
كان له فراش بالليل ويقال إن مالك بن دينار رضي الله عنه بات يردد هذه
الآية ليلة حتى أصبح أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا
وعملوا الصالحات الآية وقال المغيرة بن حبيب رمقت مالك بن دينار فتوضأ بعد
العشاء ثم قام إلى مصلاه فقبض على لحيته فخنقته العبرة فجعل يقول حرم شيبة
مالك على النار إلهي قد علمت ساكن الجنة من ساكن النار فأي الرجلين مالك
وأي الدارين دار مالك فلم يزل ذلك قوله حتى طلع الفجر وقال مالك بن دينار
شهوت ليلة عن وردي ونمت فإذا أنا في المنام بجارية كأحسن ما يكون وفي يدها
رقعة فقالت لي أتحسن تقرأ فقلت نعم فدفعت إلي الرقعة فإذا فيها
أألهتك اللذائذ والأماني ... عن البيض الأوانس في الجنان
تعيش مخلدا لا موت فيها ... وتلهو في الجنان مع الحسان
تنبه من منامك إن خيرا ... من النوم التهجد بالقران
وقيل حج مسروق فما بات ليلة إلا ساجدا ويروى عن أزهر بن مغيث وكان من
القوامين أنه قال رأيت في PageV01P355
المنام امرأة لا تشبه نساء أهل الدنيا فقلت لها من أنت قالت حوراء فقلت
زوجيني نفسك فقالت اخطبني إلى سيدي وأمهرني فقلت وما مهرك قالت طول التهجد
وقال يوسف بن مهران بلغني أن تحت العرش ملكا في صورة ديك براثنه من لؤلؤ
وصئصئه من زبرجد أخضر فإذا مضى ثلث الليل الأول ضرب بجناحيه وزقا وقال ليقم
القائمون فإذا مضى نصف الليل ضرب بجناحيه وزقا وقال ليقم المتهجدون فإذا
مضى ثلثا الليل ضرب بجناحيه  وزقا وقال ليقم المصلون فإذا طلع الفجر ضرب
بجناحيه وزقا وقال ليقم الغافلون وعليهم أوزارهم وقبل أن وهب بن منبه
اليماني ما وضع جنبه إلى الأرض ثلاثين سنة وكان يقول لأن أرى في بيتي
شيطانا أحب إلي من أن أرى في بيتي وسادة لأنها تدعو إلى النوم وكانت له
مسورة من أدم إذا غلبه النوم وضع صدره عليها وخفق خفقات ثم يفزع إلى الصلاة
وقال بعضهم رأيت رب العزة في النوم فسمعته يقول وعزتي وجلالي لأكرمن مثوى
سليمان التيمي فإنه صلى لي الغداة بوضوء العشاء أربعين سنة ويقال كان مذهبه
أن النوم إذا خامر القلب بطل الوضوء وروي في بعض الكتب القديمة عن الله
تعالى أنه قال إن عبدي الذي هو عبدي حقا الذي لا ينتظر بقيامه صياح الديكة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand upright, to rise, to establish; the core sense of physical standing in prayer
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām al-layl as the standing of the servant before his Lord in devotional vigilance, contrasted with the sleep of heedlessness
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal standing (ḥaqīqah) vs. the metaphorical sense of "persevering" in obedience
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clauses with fa-jawāb (response particle) — the apodosis following "if" clauses (e.g., "if he wakes... then one knot is loosed") demonstrates the causal efficacy of each act
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the Quranic verses, there is the saying of the Exalted: {«Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night»} — the verse. And His saying, the Exalted: {«Indeed, the rising of the night is most firm in tread and most upright in speech»}. And His saying, Glorified and Exalted: {«Their sides forsake their beds»}. And His saying, the Exalted: {«Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night»} — the verse. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«And those who pass the night prostrating and standing before their Lord»}. And His saying, the Exalted: {«And seek help through patience and prayer»} — it is said this means the night prayer, by which one seeks help through patience upon it, in struggling against the soul.

As for the reports, there is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The devil ties three knots at the nape of the head of any one of you when he sleeps, striking at each knot: 'You have a long night ahead, so sleep.' If he wakes and remembers Allah, the Exalted, one knot is loosed; if he performs ablution, a knot is loosed; if he prays, a knot is loosed — and he rises in the morning vigorous and good of spirit. Otherwise, he rises evil of spirit and sluggish." (2) And in the report, a man was mentioned before him who slept the entire night until morning, and he said: "That is a man into whose ear the devil has urinated." (3) And in the report: "The devil has a snuff, a lozenge, and a powder. If he snuffs a servant, his character becomes evil; if he lozenges him, his tongue becomes sharp with evil; if he powders him, he sleeps the night until morning." (4) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Two rakʿahs that a servant prays in the depths of the night are better for him than the world and all that is in it. Were it not that I would burden my community, I would have made them obligatory upon them." (5) And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, on the authority of Jābir, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, there is an hour of the night during which no Muslim servant asks Allah, the Exalted, for anything good but that He grants it to him." And in another narration: "He asks Allah, the Exalted, for good of this world and the Hereafter — and that is every night." And al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood in prayer until his feet became swollen. It was said to him: "Has not Allah forgiven you your former and latter sins?" He said: "Shall I not then be a grateful servant?" (6) And it appears from its meaning that this is an allusion to the increase of rank, for gratitude is the cause of increase. The Exalted said: {«If you are grateful, I will surely increase you»}. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "O Abū Hurayrah, do you wish that the mercy of Allah be upon you living, dead, buried, and resurrected? Rise from the night and pray, intending the pleasure of your Lord. O Abū Hurayrah, pray in the corners of your house, and the light of your house will be in the heaven like the light of the stars and planets to the people of the world." (7) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Upon you is the night prayer, for it is the practice of the righteous before you. Indeed, the night prayer is a means of nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, an expiation for sins, a repeller of illness from the body, and a preventer from sin." (1) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "There is no man who has a night prayer and sleep overcomes him regarding it, but that the reward of his prayer is written for him, and his sleep is a charity upon him." (2) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, to Abū Dharr: "If you intended a journey, would you prepare provisions for it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what of the journey of the Day of Resurrection? Shall I not inform you, O Abū Dharr, of what will benefit you on that day?" He said: "Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom." He said: "Fast a severely hot day for the Day of Resurrection, pray two rakʿahs in the darkness of the night for the loneliness of the graves, perform a pilgrimage for the great matters, and give charity to a poor person — or a word of truth you speak, or a word of evil you remain silent from." (3) And it is narrated that in the era of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, there was a man who, when people took to their beds and eyes grew still, would rise to pray and recite the Quran, saying: "O Lord, the Fire — protect me from it." This was mentioned to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: "If that is so, then inform me." So he came to him and listened. When morning came, he said: "O so-and-so, why did you not ask Allah for Paradise?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am not of that station, nor does my deed reach that." Not long passed until Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and said: "Inform so-and-so that Allah has protected him from the Fire and admitted him to Paradise." (4) And it is narrated that Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "What an excellent man is Ibn ʿUmar — were he but to pray at night." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed him of that, and thereafter he persisted in the night prayer. (5) Nāfiʿ said: He would pray at night, then say: "O Nāfiʿ, have we reached dawn?" I would say: "No," and he would rise to pray. Then he would say: "O Nāfiʿ, have we reached dawn?" I would say: "Yes," and he would sit and seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted, until dawn broke. And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, peace be upon them both, was satiated with barley bread, and slept past his litany until morning. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "O Yaḥyā, have you found a dwelling better for you than My dwelling, or a neighborhood better for you than My neighborhood? By My might and My majesty, O Yaḥyā, if you were to gaze upon Paradise with a single gaze, your fat would melt and your soul would expire in longing; and if you were to gaze upon Hell with a single gaze, your fat would melt, you would weep blood after tears, and you would wear coarse garments after soft ones." And it was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "So-and-so prays at night, but when morning comes, he steals." He said: "What he does will prevent him from that." (6) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "May Allah have mercy on a man who rises from the night and prays, then wakes his wife and she prays; if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face." (7) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "May Allah have mercy on a woman who rises from the night and prays, then wakes her husband and he prays; if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever wakes from the night and wakes his wife, and they pray two rakʿahs, they are written among those who remember Allah much, the men and the women." (8) And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The best prayer after the obligatory one is the night prayer." (9) And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever sleeps past his litany, or part of it, at night, and then recites it between the dawn prayer and the noon prayer, it is written for him as though he had recited it at night." (1)

THE NARRATIONS OF THE COMPANIONS AND FOLLOWERS: It is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, would pass by a verse from his litany at night and fall down, and would be nursed back from it for many days as a sick man is nursed. And Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, when eyes grew still, would rise, and a humming like the humming of bees would be heard from him until morning. And it is said that Sufyān al-Thawrī, may Allah have mercy on him, was satiated one night and said: "When a donkey is given extra fodder, its work increases." So he stood that night until morning. And Ṭāwūs, may Allah have mercy on him, when he lay on his bed, would toss upon it as a grain of corn tosses on a frying pan, then would leap up and pray until morning, then say: "The mention of Hell has put to flight the sleep of the worshippers." And al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "We know of no deed more severe than struggling through the night and spending this wealth." It was said to him: "How is it that those who pray at night are among the most beautiful of people in face?" He said: "Because they have secluded themselves with the Most Merciful, so He has clothed them with light from His light." And one of the righteous returned from a journey, and a bed was spread for him, and he slept upon it until his litany passed him by. So he swore that he would never sleep on a bed again. And ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rawwād, when night fell upon him, would come to his bed, run his hand over it, and say: "You are soft indeed — and by Allah, in Paradise there is softer than you." And he would continue praying the entire night. And al-Fuḍayl said: "I face the night from its beginning, and its length terrifies me. So I open the Quran, and morning comes while I have not yet satisfied my desire." And al-Ḥasan said: "A man commits a sin, and is thereby deprived of the night prayer." And al-Fuḍayl said: "If you are unable to pray at night and fast by day, then know that you are deprived, and your sins have multiplied." And Ṣilah ibn Ashyam, may Allah have mercy on him, would pray the entire night, and when it was the time of dawn, he would say: "O my God, one like me does not ask for Paradise, but protect me by Your mercy from the Fire." And a man said to one of the sages: "I am too weak for the night prayer." He said to him: "O my brother, do not disobey Allah, the Exalted, and do not stand at night." (i.e., if you cannot pray, at least do not sin). And al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ had a slave-girl, and he sold her to some people. When it was the depths of the night, the slave-girl rose and said: "O people of the house, the prayer, the prayer!" They said: "Have we reached morning? Has dawn appeared?" She said: "Do you pray nothing but the obligatory?" They said: "Yes." So she returned to al-Ḥasan and said: "O my master, you sold me to people who pray nothing but the obligatory — take me back." So he took her back. And al-Rabīʿ said: I stayed in the house of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, for many nights, and he would not sleep from the night except a little. And Abū al-Juwayriyyah said: I accompanied Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him, for six months, and in all that time there was not a single night in which he placed his side upon the ground. And Abū Ḥanīfah used to revive half the night. He passed by some people who said: "This man revives the entire night." He said: "I am ashamed to be described with what I do not do." So thereafter he revived the entire night. And it is narrated that he had no bed at night. And it is said that Mālik ibn Dīnār, may Allah be pleased with him, spent a night repeating this verse until morning: {«Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds»} — the verse. And al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥabīb said: I watched Mālik ibn Dīnār — he performed ablution after the evening prayer, then stood at his prayer place, grasped his beard, and weeping choked him. He began saying: "The whiteness of Mālik's beard is forbidden to the Fire. O my God, You know the inhabitant of Paradise from the inhabitant of the Fire — so which of the two men is Mālik, and which of the two abodes is Mālik's abode?" His words continued thus until dawn broke. And Mālik ibn Dīnār said: One night I desired my litany but slept. Then I saw in a dream a maiden of the most beautiful form, and in her hand was a scroll. She said to me: "Do you know how to read?" I said: "Yes." So she handed me the scroll, and in it was written:

"Have the pleasures and hopes distracted you / From the white-skinned maidens in the Gardens?
You shall live immortal, no death therein / And delight in the Gardens with the beautiful.
Awaken from your slumber — for better / Than sleep is the night vigil with the Quran."

And it is said that Masrūq performed the pilgrimage and did not spend a single night except prostrating. And it is narrated from Azhar ibn Mughīth, who was among those who stood much in prayer, that he said: I saw in a dream a woman unlike the women of this world. I said to her: "Who are you?" She said: "A ḥūrī." I said: "Marry me to yourself." She said: "Propose to me to my Master, and give me my dowry." I said: "What is your dowry?" She said: "The length of the night vigil." And Yūsuf ibn Mahrān said: It has reached me that beneath the Throne there is an angel in the form of a rooster, its claws of pearl and its comb of green chrysolite. When the first third of the night passes, it beats its wings and crows, saying: "Let the standers rise." When half the night passes, it beats its wings and crows, saying: "Let the night-vigilants rise." When two-thirds of the night pass, it beats its wings and crows, saying: "Let the pray-ers rise." When dawn breaks, it beats its wings and crows, saying: "Let the heedless rise, with their burdens upon them." And it is said that Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamānī did not place his side upon the ground for thirty years, and he would say: "That I should see a devil in my house is dearer to me than that I should see a pillow in my house, for it calls to sleep." And he had a leather cushion — when sleep overcame him, he would place his chest upon it, doze a few moments, then hasten back to prayer. And one of them said: I saw the Lord of Might in a dream, and I heard Him say: "By My might and My majesty, I shall honor the abode of Sulaymān al-Taymī, for he prayed the dawn prayer to me with the ablution of the evening prayer for forty years." And it is said his view was that when sleep overcomes the heart, the ablution is nullified. And it is narrated in some ancient books, from Allah, the Exalted, that He said: "Indeed, My servant who is truly My servant is the one who does not wait for the crowing of the roosters to rise for prayer."

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Means by Which Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl) Is Facilitated
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان الأسباب التي بها يتيسر قيام الليل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ي س ر (y-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease, facility, readiness; opposite of difficulty (ʿusr). Connotes natural aptitude and smoothness of action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, refers to divine facilitation (taysīr) — God's granting of capacity and spiritual openness for acts of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical ease; metaphorical (majāz) — inner spiritual preparedness and removal of obstacles from the heart.
- Root: ق و م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, rise, establish; qiyām al-layl specifically denotes the voluntary night prayer, standing in devotion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām in worship implies steadfastness of the soul in obedience, not merely bodily posture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical standing; metaphorical — persistence in devotion and vigilance of the heart.
- Root: ب ي ن (b-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Clarification, separation, exposition; bayān as making something distinct and manifest.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In scholarly discourse, bayān is the elucidation of causes and means — here, the practical and spiritual prerequisites.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — clear speech; metaphorical — systematic disclosure of hidden causes.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — "bayān al-asbāb" (exposition of the causes) forms an annexation where the first term (bayān) is semantically incomplete without the second (al-asbāb), indicating that the exposition is intrinsically tied to its object.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us set forth the exposition of the means by which the night vigil (qiyām al-layl) is rendered easy and facilitated — for the heart, when it is sound and its intention sincere, still requires certain outward and inward aids that prepare the soul for this station of worship. Know that these means are of two kinds: those pertaining to the outward habits of the body, and those pertaining to the inward states of the heart. The outward means include moderating one's food and drink, avoiding excess that induces heaviness and slumber, and accustoming oneself to wakefulness at the hour of the latter part of the night. The inward means include purifying the heart from worldly preoccupations, severing attachment to that which distracts the mind, and filling the breast with the remembrance of the Hereafter — for the soul, when it is unburdened of worldly cares, rises readily to the service of its Lord, and the night vigil becomes for it a delight rather than a burden. And God is the Granter of success.

chapters.title_en: On the Facilitating Conditions for Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl) — Outward and Inward Aids
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن قيام الليل عسير على الخلق إلا على من وفق للقيام بشروطه الميسرة
له ظاهرا وباطنا فأما الظاهرة فأربعة أمور الأول أن لا يكثر الأكل فيكثر
الشرب فيغلبه النوم ويثقل عليه القيام كان بعض الشيوخ يقف على المائدة كل
ليلة ويقول معاشر المريدين لا تأكلوا كثيرا فتشربوا كثيرا فترقدوا كثيرا
فتتحسروا عند الموت كثيرا وهذا هو الأصل الكبير وهو تخفيف المعدة عن ثقل
الطعام الثاني أن لا يتعب نفسه بالنهار في الأعمال التي تعيا بها الجوارح
وتضعف بها الأعصاب فإن ذلك أيضا مجلبة للنوم الثالث أن لا يترك القيلولة
بالنهار فإنها سنة للاستعانة على قيام الليل (1) الرابع أن لا يحتقب
الأوزار بالنهار فإن ذلك مما يقسي القلب ويحول بينه وبين أسباب الرحمة قال
رجل للحسن يا أبا سعيد إني أبيت معافى وأحب قيام الليل وأعد طهوري فما بالي
لا أقوم فقال ذنوبك قيدتك وكان الحسن رحمة الله إذا دخل السوق فسمع لغطهم
ولغوهم يقول أظن أن ليل هؤلاء ليل سوء فإنهم لا يقيلون وقال الثوري حرمت
قيام الليل خمسة أشهر بذنب أذنبته قيل وما ذاك الذنب قال رأيت رجلا يبكي
فقلت في نفسي  هذا مراء وقال بعضهم دخلت على كرز بن وبرة وهو يبكي فقلت أتاك
نعي بعض أهلك فقال اشد فقلت وجع يؤلمك قال أشد قلت فما ذاك قال بابي مغلق
وستري مسبل ولم أقرأ حزبي البارحة وما ذاك إلا بذنب أحدثته وهذا لأن الخير
يدعو إلى الخير والشر يدعو إلى الشر والقليل من كل واحد منهما يجر إلى
الكثير ولذلك قال أبو سليمان الداراني لا تفوت أحدا صلاة الجماعة إلا بذنب
وكان يقول الاحتلام بالليل عقوبة والجنابة بعد وقال بعض العلماء إذا صمت يا
مسكين فانظر عند من تفطر وعلى أي شيء تفطر فإن العبد ليأكل أكلة فينقلب
قلبه عما كان عليه ولا يعود إلى حالته الأولى فالذنوب كلها تورث قساوة
القلب وتمنع من قيام الليل وأخصها بالتأثير تناول الحرام وتؤثر اللقمة
الحلال في تصفية القلب وتحريكه إلى الخير ما لا يؤثر غيرها ويعرف ذلك أهل
المراقبة للقلوب بالتجربة بعد شهادة الشرع له ولذلك قال بعضهم كم من أكلة
منعت قيام ليلة وكم من نظرة منعت قراءة سورة وإن العبد ليأكل أكلة أو يفعل
فعلة فيحرم بها قيام سنة وكما إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر فكذلك
الفحشاء تنهى عن الصلاة وسائر الخيرات وقال بعض السجانين PageV01P356
كنت سجانا نيفا وثلاثين سنة أسأل كل مأخوذ بالليل أنه هل صلى العشاء في
جماعة فكانوا يقولون لا وهذا تنبيه على أن بركة الجماعة تنهى عن تعاطي
الفحشاء والمنكر
وأما الميسرات الباطنة فأربعة أمور الأول سلامة القلب عن الحقد على
المسلمين وعن البدع وعن فضول هموم الدنيا فالمستغرق الهم بتدبير الدنيا لا
يتيسر له القيام وإن قام فلا يتفكر في صلاته إلا في مهماته ولا يجول إلا في
وساوسه وفي مثل ذلك يقال
يخبرني البواب أنك نائم ... وأنت إذا استيقظت أيضا فنائم
الثاني خوف غالب يلزم القلب مع قصر الأمل فإنه إذا تفكر في أهوال الآخرة
ودركات جهنم طار نومه وعظم حذره كما قال طاوس إن ذكر جهنم طير نوم العابدين
وكما حكي أن غلاما  بالبصرة اسمه صهيب كان يقوم الليل كله فقالت له سيدته إن
قيامك بالليل يضر بعملك بالنهار فقال إن صهيبا إذا ذكر النار لا يأتيه
النوم وقيل لغلام آخر وهو يقوم كل الليل فقال إذا ذكرت النار اشتد خوفي
وإذا ذكرت الجنة اشتد شوقي فلا أقدر أن أنام وقال ذو النون المصري رحمه
الله
منع القرآن بوعده ووعيده ... مقل العيون بليلها أن تهجعا
فهموا عن الملك الجليل كلامه ... فرقابهم ذلت إليه تخضعا
وأنشدوا أيضا
يا طويل الرقاد والغفلات ... كثرة النوم تورث الحسرات
إن في القبر إن نزلت إليه ... لرقادا يطول بعد الممات
ومهادا ممهدا لك فيه ... بذنوب عملت أو حسنات
أأمنت البيات من ملك المو ... ت وكم نال آمنا ببيات
وقال ابن المبارك
إذا ما الليل أظلم كابدوه ... فيسفر عنهم وهم ركوع
أطار الخوف نومهم فقاموا ... وأهل الأمن في الدنيا هجوع
الثالث أن يعرف فضل قيام الليل بسماع الآيات والأخبار والآثار حتى يستحكم
به رجاؤه وشوقه إلى ثوابه فيهيجه الشوق لطلب المزيد والرغبة في درجات
الجنان كما حكي أن بعض الصالحين رجع من غزوته فمهدت امرأته فراشها وجلست
تنتظره فدخل المسجد ولم يزل يصلي حتى أصبح فقالت له زوجته كنا ننتظرك مدة
فلما قدمت صليت إلى الصبح قال والله إني كنت أتفكر في حوراء من حور الجنة
طول الليل فنسيت الزوجة والمنزل فقمت طول ليلتي شوقا إليها
الرابع وهو أشرف البواعث الحب لله وقوة الإيمان بأنه في قيامه لا يتكلم
بحرف إلا وهو مناج ربه وهو مطلع عليه مع مشاهدة ما يخطر بقلبه وأن تلك
الخطرات من الله تعالى خطاب معه فإذا أحب الله تعالى أحب لا محالة الخلوة
به وتلذذ بالمناجاة فتحمله لذة المناجاة بالحبيب على طول القيام ولا ينبغي
أن يستبعد هذه اللذة إذ يشهد لها العقل والنقل فأما العقل فليعتبر حال
المحب لشخص بسبب جماله أو لملك بسبب إنعامه وأمواله أنه كيف يتلذذ به في
الخلوة ومناجاته حتى لا يأتيه النوم طول ليله فإن قلت إن الجميل يتلذذ
بالنظر إليه وإن الله تعالى لا يرى فاعلم
PageV01P357
أنه لو كان الجميل المحبوب وراء ستر أو كان في بيت مظلم لكان المحب يتلذذ
بمجاورته المجردة دون النظر ودون الطمع في أمر آخر سواه وكان يتنعم بإظهار
حبه عليه وذكره بلسانه بمسمع منه وإن كان ذلك أيضا معلوما عنده فإن قلت إنه
ينتظر جوابه فليتلذذ بسماع جوابه وليس يسمع كلام الله تعالى فاعلم أنه إن
كان يعلم أنه لا يجيبه ويسكت عنه فقد بقيت له أيضا لذة في عرض أحواله عليه
ورفع سريرته إليه كيف والموقن يسمع من الله تعالى كل ما يرد على خاطره في
أثناء مناجاته فيتلذذ به وكذا الذي يخلو بالملك ويعرض عليه حاجاته في جنح
الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله
خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات
وأما النقل فيشهد له أحوال قوام الليل في تلذذهم بقيام الليل واستقصارهم له
كما يستقصر المحب ليلة وصال الحبيب حتى قيل لبعضهم كيف أنت والليل قال ما
راعيته قط يريني وجهه ثم ينصرف وما تأملته بعد وقال آخر أنا والليل فرسا
رهان مرة يسبقني إلى الفجر ومرة يقطعني عن الفكر وقيل لبعضهم كيف الليل
عليك فقال ساعة أنا فيها بين حالتين أفرح بظلمته إذا جاء وأغتم بفجره إذا
طلع ما تم فرحي به قط وقال علي بن بكار منذ أربعين سنة ما أحزنني شيء سوى
طلوع الفجر وقال الفضيل بن عياض إذا غربت الشمس فرحت بالظلام لخلوتي بربي
وإذا طلعت حزنت لدخول الناس علي وقال أبو سليمان أهل الليل في ليلهم ألذ من
أهل اللهو في لهوهم ولولا الليل ما أحببت البقاء في الدنيا وقال أيضا لو
عوض الله أهل الليل من ثواب أعمالهم ما يجدونه من اللذة لكان ذلك أكثر من
ثواب أعمالهم وقال بعض العلماء ليس في الدنيا وقت يشبه نعيم أهل الجنة إلا
ما يجده أهل التملق في قلوبهم بالليل  من حلاوة المناجاة وقال بعضهم لذة
المناجاة ليست من الدنيا إنما هي من الجنة أظهرها الله تعالى لأوليائه لا
يجدها سواهم وقال ابن المنكدر ما بقي من لذات الدنيا إلا ثلاث قيام الليل
ولقاء الإخوان والصلاة في الجماعة وقال بعض العارفين إن الله تعالى ينظر
بالأسحار إلى قلوب المتيقظين فيملؤها أنوارا فترد الفوائد على قلوبهم
فتستنير ثم تنتشر من قلوبهم العوافي إلى قلوب الغافلين وقال بعض العلماء من
القدماء أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى بعض الصديقين إن لي عبادا من عبادي أحبهم
ويحبونني ويشتاقون إلي وأشتاق إليهم ويذكرونني وأذكرهم وينظرون إلي وأنظر
إليهم فإن حذوت طريقهم أحببتك وإن عدلت عنهم مقتك قال يا رب وما علامتهم
قال يراعون الظلال بالنهار كما يراعي الراعي غنمه ويحنون إلى غروب الشمس
كما تحن الطير إلى أوكارها فإذا جنهم الليل واختلط الظلام وخلا كل حبيب
بحبيبه نصبوا إلى أقدامهم وافترشوا إلى وجوههم وناجوني بكلامي وتملقوا إلي
بإنعامي فبين صارخ وباكي وبين متأوه وشاكي بعيني ما يتحملون من أجلي وبسمعي
ما يشتكون من حبي أول ما أعطيهم أقذف من نوري في قلوبهم فيخبرون عني كما
أخبر عنهم والثانية لو كانت السموات السبع والأرضون السبع وما فيهما من
موازينهم لاستقللتها لهم والثالثة أقبل بوجهي عليهم أفترى من أقبلت بوجهي
عليه أيعلم أحد ما أريد أن أعطيه وقال مالك بن دينار رحمه الله إذا قام
العبد يتهجد من الليل قرب منه الجبار عز وجل وكانوا يرون ما يجدون من الرقة
والحلاوة في قلوبهم والأنوار من قرب الرب تعالى من القلب وهذا له سر وتحقيق
ستأتي الإشارة إليه في كتاب المحبة وفي الأخبار عن الله عز وجل أي عبدي أنا
الله الذي اقتربت من قلبك وبالغيب رأيت نوري وشكا بعض المريدين إلى أستاذه
طول سهر الليل وطلب حيلة يجلب بها النوم فقال أستاذه يا بني إن لله نفحات
في الليل والنهار تصيب القلوب المتيقظة تحظىء القلوب النائمة فتعرض لتلك
النفحات فقال يا سيدي تركتني لا أنام بالليل ولا  بالنهار
PageV01P358
واعلم أن هذه النفحات بالليل أرجى لما في قيام الليل من صفاء القلب
واندفاع الشواغل وفي الخبر الصحيح عن جابر بن عبد الله عن رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن من الليل ساعة لا يوافقها عبد مسلم يسأل الله
تعالى خيرا إلا أعطاه إياه (1) وفي رواية أخرى يسأل الله خيرا من أمر
الدنيا والآخرة إلا أعطاه وذلك كل ليلة ومطلوب القائمين تلك الساعة وهي
مهمة في جملة الليل كليلة القدر في شهر رمضان وكساعة يوم الجمعة وهي ساعة
النفحات المذكورة والله أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-ل (qalla)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be few, little, scanty; diminution of quantity or intensity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for the reduction of worldly attachments and bodily appetites that impede worship; the "little" (qalīl) of good or evil draws to the "much" (kathīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for scarcity; metaphorical for spiritual lightness and freedom from the heaviness of satiety.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — "If you say... know that" (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) structures dialectical objections and responses, requiring the apodosis to be introduced by fa-.
chapters.translation:
Know that night vigil is difficult for creatures, except for the one who is granted success in performing it according to its facilitating conditions, outwardly and inwardly.

As for the outward conditions, they are four matters:

**The first:** That one not eat much, for then one drinks much, and sleep overcomes him, and rising for prayer becomes heavy upon him. Some of the elders (shuyūkh) used to stand at the dining table every night and say: "O company of seekers (murīdīn)! Do not eat much, so that you drink much, so that you sleep much, so that you grieve much at death." This is the great principle — lightening the stomach from the heaviness of food.

**The second:** That one not exhaust himself by day in labors that weary the limbs and weaken the nerves, for that too invites sleep.

**The third:** That one not abandon the midday nap (qaylūlah) by day, for it is a sunnah as an aid for night vigil.

**The fourth:** That one not accumulate sins (awzār) by day, for that hardens the heart and interposes between it and the means of mercy. A man said to al-Hasan [al-Baṣrī]: "O Abū Saʿīd, I go to bed healthy, and I love night vigil, and I prepare my purification — what is the matter that I do not rise?" He said: "Your sins have bound you." And al-Hasan — may God have mercy on him — when he entered the market and heard their clamor and idle talk, would say: "I think the night of these people is an evil night, for they do not take the midday nap." And al-Thawrī said: "I was deprived of night vigil for five months due to a sin I committed." It was asked: "And what was that sin?" He said: "I saw a man weeping, and I said to myself: 'This is ostentation (riyā').'"

And some of them said: "I entered upon Karz ibn Wabarah while he was weeping, and I said: 'Has news of the death of one of your family come to you?' He said: 'More severe.' I said: 'A pain afflicting you?' He said: 'More severe.' I said: 'Then what is it?' He said: 'My door is closed, my veil is lowered, and I did not recite my portion (ḥizb) last night — and that is only due to a sin I newly committed.'" This is because good calls to good, and evil calls to evil, and the little of each draws to the much. For this reason, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "No one misses the congregational prayer except due to a sin." And he used to say: "Nocturnal emission (iḥtilām) by night is a punishment, and defilement (janābah) after it [is likewise]."

And some scholars said: "O poor man, if you fast, then consider with whom you break your fast, and upon what you break it. For the servant may eat a single morsel, and his heart is overturned from what it was upon, and he does not return to his former state." All sins bequeath hardness of heart and prevent night vigil, and the most specific of them in effect is the consumption of the unlawful (ḥarām). And the lawful morsel (al-luqmah al-ḥalāl) affects the purification of the heart and its movement toward good in a way that nothing else does. Those who watch over hearts (ahl al-murāqabah) know this by experience, after the testimony of the Sacred Law to it. For this reason, some of them said: "How many a morsel has prevented a night's vigil, and how many a glance has prevented the recitation of a sūrah! Indeed, the servant may eat a morsel or commit an act, and is thereby deprived of a year's vigil." And just as prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing, so too indecency forbids prayer and all other good deeds.

And one of the prison wardens said: "I was a warden for thirty-odd years, asking every person seized at night whether he had prayed the ʿishā' in congregation — and they would all say no." This is an indication that the blessing of the congregation forbids the commission of indecency and wrongdoing.

---

As for the inward facilitating conditions, they are four matters:

**The first:** Soundness of the heart from rancor against the Muslims, from innovations (bidaʿ), and from superfluous worldly concerns. For the one engrossed in managing the world, vigil is not facilitated; and if he rises, he does not reflect in his prayer except upon his pressing affairs, and his mind does not wander except among his whisperings (wasāwis). Regarding such a one it is said:

*"The doorkeeper tells me you are asleep — and you, when you awaken, are also asleep."*

**The second:** A prevailing fear that clings to the heart, along with the shortening of hope (qasr al-amal). For when one reflects upon the terrors of the Hereafter and the depths of Hell, his sleep flies away and his caution becomes great. As Ṭāwūs said: "The mention of Hell puts to flight the sleep of the worshippers." And as it is related that a youth in Baṣrah named Ṣuhayb used to stand the whole night, and his mistress said to him: "Your standing at night harms your work by day." He said: "Ṣuhayb, when he mentions the Fire, sleep does not come to him." And it was said to another youth who stood the whole night: [He replied:] "When I mention the Fire, my fear intensifies; and when I mention Paradise, my longing intensifies — so I cannot sleep."

And Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī — may God have mercy on him — said:

*"The Qur'an, by its promise and its threat, has prevented the eyes of the abstinent from slumbering at night. They understood from the Majestic King His speech, so their necks bowed to Him in submission."*

And they also recited:

*"O you of prolonged sleep and heedlessness — much sleep bequeaths regrets. Indeed, in the grave, when you descend into it, there is a long slumber after death — a bed prepared for you therein, of sins you committed or good deeds. Are you secure from the night assault of the Angel of Death? How many a secure one has been seized by night assault!"*

And Ibn al-Mubārak said:

*"When the night darkens, they endure it — and dawn breaks upon them while they are bowing. Fear put their sleep to flight, so they rose — while the people of security in this world are slumbering."*

**The third:** That one know the merit of night vigil by hearing the verses, the reports (akhbār), and the traditions (āthār), so that his hope and longing for its reward become firmly established, and longing stirs him to seek more and to desire the ranks of the Gardens. As it is related that one of the righteous returned from his raid, and his wife spread his bed and sat waiting for him. He entered the mosque and did not cease praying until morning. His wife said to him: "We were waiting for you for a while, and when you arrived, you prayed until dawn." He said: "By God, I was reflecting upon a ḥūrī from the ḥūr of Paradise the whole night, and I forgot the wife and the home — so I stood my entire night longing for her."

**The fourth — and it is the noblest of the motives:** Love for God (al-ḥubb li-Allāh) and the strength of faith that in his vigil, he does not utter a single letter except that he is privately conversing with his Lord (munājāt), Who is overseeing him, along with the witnessing that what passes through his heart — those passing thoughts (khaṭarāt) — are a discourse from God most high addressed to him. So when one loves God, he inevitably loves seclusion with Him and takes delight in the private conversation (al-munājāh). The delight of intimate converse with the Beloved carries him to prolonged standing.

One should not deem this delight remote, for reason and revelation both testify to it.

As for reason: Let one consider the state of a lover of a person for the sake of his beauty, or of a king for the sake of his beneficence and wealth — how he delights in seclusion with him and in conversing with him, so that sleep does not come to him the whole night. If you say: "The beautiful one is delighted by looking at him, whereas God most high is not seen" — know that if the beautiful beloved were behind a curtain, or in a dark house, the lover would still delight in his mere proximity, without sight and without coveting anything else besides him. He would take pleasure in displaying his love to him and in mentioning him with his tongue within his hearing, even if that too were known to him. If you say: "He awaits his reply, so let him delight in hearing his answer — and he does not hear the speech of God most high" — know that even if he knew that he would not answer him and would remain silent toward him, there would still remain for him a delight in presenting his states to him and raising his secret to him. How much more so, when the one of certainty (al-mūqin) hears from God most high everything that occurs to his mind during his intimate converse, and delights in it! Likewise, the one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depths of the night delights in the hope of his beneficence. And hope with respect to God most high is truer, and what is with God is better, more enduring, and more beneficial than what is with others. So how could one not delight in presenting his needs to Him in seclusions?

As for revelation: It is attested by the states of those who stand the night, in their delight in night vigil and their finding it short — just as the lover finds short the night of union with the beloved. It was said to one of them: "How are you with the night?" He said: "I never observed it showing me its face and then departing, nor did I ever contemplate it afterwards." Another said: "The night and I are two racehorses — sometimes it outruns me to dawn, and sometimes it cuts me off from reflection." It was said to another: "How is the night upon you?" He said: "An hour in which I am between two states: I rejoice at its darkness when it comes, and I grieve at its dawn when it rises — my joy in it is never completed." And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār said: "For forty years, nothing has grieved me except the rising of dawn." And al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: "When the sun sets, I rejoice at the darkness for my seclusion with my Lord; and when it rises, I grieve at the entry of people upon me." And Abū Sulaymān said: "The people of the night are, in their night, more delighted than the people of amusement in their amusement. Were it not for the night, I would not love remaining in this world." And he also said: "If God were to give the people of the night, in exchange for the reward of their deeds, what they find of delight, that would be greater than the reward of their deeds."

And one of the scholars said: "There is nothing in this world resembling the bliss of the people of Paradise except what the people of supplication (ahl al-tamalluq) find in their hearts at night, of the sweetness of intimate converse (ḥalāwah al-munājāh)." And another said: "The delight of intimate converse is not of this world; it is of Paradise, which God most high has manifested to His friends (awliyā') — none find it besides them." And Ibn al-Munkadir said: "Nothing remains of the delights of this world except three: night vigil, meeting the brethren, and prayer in congregation."

And one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: "God most high looks, in the last hours of the night (asḥār), upon the hearts of the wakeful, and fills them with lights. The benefits then return upon their hearts, and they become illumined; then well-being (al-ʿawāfī) spreads from their hearts to the hearts of the heedless."

And one of the ancient scholars said: "God most high revealed to one of the sincerely truthful (ṣiddīqīn): 'I have servants among My servants whom I love and who love Me; they long for Me and I long for them; they remember Me and I remember them; they look upon Me and I look upon them. If you tread their path, I will love you; and if you turn away from them, I will detest you.' He said: 'O Lord, and what is their sign?' He said: 'They tend the shade by day as the shepherd tends his flock, and they yearn for the setting of the sun as birds yearn for their nests. When the night envelops them, and the darkness mingles, and every lover is alone with his beloved, they set up their feet and spread their faces [in prostration], and they converse intimately with Me through My speech, and they flatter Me through My beneficence. Among them is one crying out, one weeping, one sighing, one complaining. With My eye do I see what they endure for My sake, and with My ear do I hear what they complain of for My love. The first thing I give them is that I cast from My light into their hearts, so that they inform of Me as I inform of them. The second is that were the seven heavens and the seven earths and all that is in them placed in their scales, I would deem it too little for them. The third is that I turn My face toward them — do you think that anyone knows what I intend to give the one toward whom I have turned My face?'"

And Mālik ibn Dīnār — may God have mercy on him — said: "When the servant rises to pray the night prayer (tahajjud), the Omnipotent (al-Jabbār), mighty and majestic, draws near to him." And they used to hold that what they found of tenderness (al-riqqah) and sweetness in their hearts, and the lights, [arise] from the proximity of the Lord most high to the heart. This has a secret and a realization to which reference will come in the Book of Love (Kitāb al-Maḥabbah). And in the reports from God, mighty and majestic: "O My servant, I am God, Who has drawn near to your heart, and in the unseen you have seen My light."

And one of the seekers (murīdīn) complained to his master of the length of wakefulness at night, and sought a stratagem to bring sleep. His master said: "O my son, God has breaths (nafaḥāt) in the night and the day that strike the wakeful hearts and pass by the sleeping hearts — so expose yourself to those breaths." He said: "O my master, you have left me sleeping neither by night nor by day!"

---

Know that these breaths are more to be hoped for at night, because of what night vigil contains of purity of heart and the repulsion of distractions. And in the sound report (al-khabar al-ṣaḥīḥ) from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: {«"Indeed, there is an hour of the night in which no Muslim servant coincides with it, asking God most high for good, except that He gives it to him"»} — and in another narration: {«"asking God for good of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, except that He gives it to him"»} — and that is every night. And that hour is what the vigil-keepers seek; it is in the totality of the night like the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) in Ramaḍān, and like the hour of Friday. It is the hour of the aforementioned breaths. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Methods of Dividing the Parts of the Night
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان طرق القسمة لأجزاء الليل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, or distribution into parts; a portion (qism) or share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, division (qisma) pertains to the rational partitioning of time or entities into discrete categories, often for devotional or legal purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual partitioning of a physical or temporal whole; metaphorical (majāz) — conceptual or methodological division, as here, where "methods" (ṭuruq) are the means of such partitioning.
- Root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Clarity, separation, or elucidation; making something distinct and manifest.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Bayān as the act of clarifying a matter, often used for divine or prophetic exposition of religious obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — separation of things; metaphorical — explanation or demonstration, as in "exposition" of a method.
- Root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Night, from sunset to dawn; the period of darkness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional context, the night is a time for supererogatory worship (qiyām al-layl), and its division relates to vigil and prayer timings.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the astronomical night; metaphorical — a period of spiritual darkness or trial, though here used literally.
- Sībawayh Rule: Idāfah (Construct State) — The phrase "ṭuruq al-qisma" (methods of division) is an annexation where the first term (ṭuruq) is indefinite and the second (al-qisma) is definite, yielding a specific, defined meaning: "the methods of the division." The preposition "li-" (for) introduces a purpose or object, governing "ajzāʾ al-layl" (parts of the night), indicating the intended scope of the exposition.
chapters.translation: I say: Now I shall set forth the methods of dividing the parts of the night, so that the seeker may apportion his vigil according to the hours thereof, and thereby order his worship in due measure.

chapters.title_en: The Seven Ranks of Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl) by Duration
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن إحياء الليل من حيث المقدار له سبع مراتب الأولى إحياء كل الليل
وهذا شأن الأقوياء الذين تجردوا لعبادة الليل وتلذذوا بمناجاته وصار ذلك
غذاء لهم وحياة لقلوبهم فلم يتعبوا بطول القيام وردوا المنام إلى النهار
وفي وقت اشتغال الناس وقد كان ذلك طريق جماعة من السلف كانوا يصلون الصبح
بوضوء العشاء حكى أبو طالب المكي أن ذلك حكي على سبيل التواتر والاشتهار عن
أربعين من التابعين وكان فيهم من واظب عليه أربعين سنة قال منهم سعيد بن
المسيب وصفوان بن سليم المدنيان وفضيل بن عياض ووهيب بن الورد المكيان
وطاوس ووهب بن منبه اليمانيان والربيع بن خيثم والحكم الكوفيان وأبو سليمان
الداراني وعلي بن بكار الشاميان وأبو عبد الله الخواص وأبو عاصم العباديان
وحبيب أبو محمد وأبو جابر السلماني الفارسيان ومالك بن دينار سليمان التيمي
ويزيد الرقاشي وحبيب بن أبي ثابت ويحيى البكاء البصريون وكهمس بن المنهال
وكان يختم في الشهر تسعين ختمة وما لم يفهمه رجع وقرأه مرة أخرى وأيضا من
أهل المدينة أبو حازم ومحمد بن المنكدر في جماعة يكثر عددهم المرتبة
الثانية أن يقوم نصف الليل وهذا لا ينحصر عدد المواظبين عليه من السلف
وأحسن فيه أن ينام الثلث الأول من الليل والسدس الأخير منه حتى يقع قيامه
في جوف الليل ووسطه فهو الأفضل المرتبة الثالثة أن يقوم ثلث الليل فينبغي
أن ينام النصف  الأول والسدس الأخير وبالجملة نوم آخر الليل محبوب لأنه يذهب
النعاس بالغداة وكانوا يكرهون ذلك ويقلل صفرة الوجه والشهرة به فلو قام
أكثر الليل ونام سحرا قلت صفرة وجهه وقل نعاسه وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أوتر من آخر الليل فإن كانت له حاجة
إلى أهله دنا منهن وإلا اضطجع في مصلاه حتى يأتيه بلال فيؤذنه للصلاة (2)
وقالت أيضا رضي الله عنها ما ألفيته بعد السحر إلا نائما (3) حتى قال بعض
السلف هذه الضجعة قبل الصبح سنة منهم أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وكان نوم هذا
الوقت سببا للمكاشفة والمشاهدة من وراء حجب الغيب وذلك لأرباب القلوب وفيه
استراحة PageV01P359
تعين على الورد الأول من أوراد النهار وقيام ثلث الليل من النصف الأخير
ونوم السدس الأخير قيام داود صلى الله عليه وسلم المرتبة الرابعة أن يقوم
سدس الليل أو خمسه وأفضله أن يكون في النصف الأخير وقبل السدس الأخير منه
المرتبة الخامسة أن لا يراعي التقدير فإن ذلك إنما يتيسر لنبي يوحى إليه أو
لمن يعرف منازل القمر ويوكل به من يراقبه ويواظبه ويوقظه ثم ربما يضطرب في
ليالي الغيم ولكنه يقوم من أول الليل إلى أن يغلبه النوم فإذا انتبه قام
فإذا غلبه النوم عاد إلى النوم فيكون له في الليل نومتان وقومتان وهو من
مكابدة الليل وأشد الأعمال وأفضلها وقد كان هذا من أخلاق رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم (1) وهو طريقة ابن عمر وأولي العزم من الصحابة وجماعة من
التابعين رضي الله عنهم وكان بعض السلف يقول هي أول نومة فإذا انتبهت ثم
عدت إلى النوم فلا أنام الله لي عينا فأما قيام رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم من حيث المقدار فلم يكن على ترتيب واحد بل ربما كان يقوم نصف الليل أو
ثلثه أو سدسه (2) يختلف ذلك في الليالي ودل عليه قوله تعالى في الموضعين من
سورة المزمل إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه  وثلثه فأدنى من
ثلثي الليل كأنه بصفه ونصف سدسه فإن كسر قوله ونصفه وثلثه كان نصف الثلثين
فيقرب من الثلث والربع وإن نصب كان نصف الليل وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقوم إذا سمع الصارخ (3) يعني الديك وهذا يكون
السدس فما دونه وروى غير واحد أنه قال راعيت صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم في السفر ليلا فنام بعد العشاء زمانا ثم استيقظ فنظر في الأفق فقال
ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا حتى بلغ إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ثم استل من فراشه
سواكا فاستاك به وتوضأ وصلى حتى قلت صلى مثل الذي نام ثم اضطجع حتى قلت نام
مثل ما صلى ثم استيقظ فقال ما قال أول مرة وفعل ما فعل أول مرة (4) المرتبة
السادسة وهي الأقل أن يقوم مقدار أربع ركعات أو ركعتين أو تتعذر عليه
الطهارة فيجلس مستقبل القبلة ساعة مشتغلا بالذكر والدعاء فيكتب في جملة
قوام الليل برحمة الله وفضله وقد جاء في الأثر صل من الليل ولو قدر حلب شاة
(5) فهذه طرق القسمة فليختر المريد لنفسه ما يراه أيسر عليه وحيث يتعذر
عليه القيام في وسط الليل فلا ينبغي أن يهمل إحياء ما بين العشاءين والورد
الذي بعد العشاء ثم يقوم قبل الصبح وقت السحر فلا يدركه الصبح PageV01P360
نائما ويقوم بطرفي الليل وهذه هي المرتبة السابعة ومهما كان النظر إلى
المقدار فترتيب هذه المراتب بحسب طول الوقت وقصره وأما في الرتبة الخامسة
والسابعة لم ينظر فيهما إلى القدر فليس يجري أمرهما في التقدم والتأخر على
الترتيب المذكور إذ السابعة ليست دون ما ذكرناه في السادسة ولا الخامسة دون
الرابعة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥayya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To live, to revive, to bring to life; the opposite of death (mawt). Reviving the night means filling it with acts of worship that give it spiritual life.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, iḥyāʾ denotes the enlivening of the heart through remembrance and obedience, paralleling God's reviving of the dead. The night's "revival" is a metaphor for the soul's wakefulness in devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = restoring life to a corpse; metaphorical (majāz) = spending the night in worship, as if giving it life. Here it is majāz, since the night itself is not literally alive.
- Root: ق-و-م (qāma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand upright, to rise; qiyām al-layl is the standing in prayer at night.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām in worship signifies the soul's uprightness before God, a posture of servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) and vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical standing; metaphorical = persistence in devotion. The term qiyām al-layl is a metonymy for the entire night vigil, including sitting and recitation.
- Root: ر-ت-ب (rataba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To arrange, to set in order; marātib (ranks) are degrees of precedence and excellence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Marātib imply a hierarchy of spiritual stations, where higher ranks correspond to greater effort and proximity to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = ordered steps; metaphorical = graded levels of religious merit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text uses "fa-law qāma" (if he were to stand) and "fa-idhā" (when) to structure hypothetical and temporal sequences, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis to preserve the logical flow of the author's argument.
chapters.translation:
Know that the revival of the night, with respect to its duration, has seven ranks. The first is the revival of the entire night. This is the way of the strong ones who have devoted themselves exclusively to the worship of the night, delighting in intimate converse with Him (munājāt), and it has become nourishment for them and life for their hearts. They are not wearied by the length of standing, and they relegate sleep to the daytime, at the time when people are occupied [with worldly affairs]. This was the path of a group of the Salaf (pious predecessors) who used to pray the dawn prayer with the ablution of the night prayer. Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī narrated that this was reported on the basis of tawātur (mass transmission) and widespread fame from forty of the Tābiʿūn (successors). Among them were those who persisted in this for forty years. He mentioned from them: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, the two Medinese; Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ and Wahīb ibn al-Ward, the two Meccans; Ṭāwūs and Wahb ibn Munabbih, the two Yemenis; al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham and al-Ḥakam, the two Kufans; Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī and ʿAlī ibn Bakkār, the two Syrians; Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawwāṣ and Abū ʿĀṣim, the two ʿAbbādians; Ḥabīb Abū Muḥammad and Abū Jābir al-Sulamānī, the two Persians; Mālik ibn Dīnār, Sulaymān al-Taymī, Yazīd al-Raqāshī, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, and Yaḥyā al-Bakkāʾ, the Basrans; and Kahmas ibn al-Minhāl, who would complete ninety recitations of the Qurʾān in a month, and whatever he did not understand, he would return to and recite it again. Also from the people of Medina were Abū Ḥāzim and Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, along with a group whose number is great.

The second rank is to stand for half the night. The number of those from the Salaf who persisted in this is not limited. The best manner in this is to sleep the first third of the night and the last sixth of it, so that his standing falls in the middle of the night and its center — this is the most virtuous.

The third rank is to stand for a third of the night. In this, one should sleep the first half and the last sixth. In sum, sleeping at the end of the night is beloved, because it removes drowsiness in the morning, and they (the Salaf) used to dislike that [drowsiness], and it diminishes the yellowness of the face and the fame [of excessive devotion]. For if one stood for most of the night and slept at the pre-dawn hour (saḥar), his face's yellowness would diminish and his drowsiness would lessen. ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, when he performed the witr prayer at the end of the night, if he had a need for his family, he would draw near to them, and otherwise he would lie down in his prayer place until Bilāl came to him and called him to prayer." She also said, may God be pleased with her: "I never found him after the saḥar except sleeping." Until some of the Salaf said: "This lying down before the dawn prayer is a Sunnah," among them Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. And sleeping at this time was a cause for unveiling (mukāshafah) and witnessing (mushāhadah) from behind the veils of the unseen — this is for the masters of hearts. In it there is also rest that aids one in the first litany (wird) of the day's litanies. And standing a third of the night from the latter half, with sleep in the last sixth, is the standing of Dāwūd, peace be upon him.

The fourth rank is to stand a sixth of the night or a fifth. The best of this is that it be in the latter half, before the last sixth of it.

The fifth rank is not to observe a fixed measure. For this is only facilitated for a prophet to whom revelation comes, or for one who knows the stations of the moon and appoints someone to watch over him, observe him, and wake him. Then perhaps he may be disturbed on cloudy nights. Rather, he stands from the beginning of the night until sleep overcomes him; when he wakes, he stands; when sleep overcomes him, he returns to sleep. Thus he has two sleeps and two standings in the night. This is among the most strenuous struggles of the night (mukābadah al-layl) and the most severe and most virtuous of deeds. This was among the character traits of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is the way of Ibn ʿUmar and the resolute ones (ulū al-ʿazm) among the Companions, and a group of the Tābiʿūn, may God be pleased with them. Some of the Salaf used to say: "This is the first sleep; if I wake and then return to sleep, may God not give sleep to my eyes." As for the standing of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, with respect to duration, it was not upon a single fixed order. Rather, sometimes he would stand half the night, or a third, or a sixth — this varied across the nights. This is indicated by His saying, the Exalted, in the two places of Sūrat al-Muzzammil: {«إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ»} (Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it). So "less than two-thirds" is as if He described half and a sixth; for if His word "and half of it" and "and a third of it" is read in the genitive (kasr), then "half" is half of the two-thirds, which approximates a third and a quarter; and if read in the accusative (naṣb), it is half of the night. ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, would stand when he heard the crower" — meaning the rooster — and this would be a sixth or less. More than one person narrated that he said: "I observed the prayer of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, during a journey at night. He slept after the night prayer for a while, then woke and looked at the horizon and said: {«رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا»} (Our Lord, You did not create this in vain) until he reached {«إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ»} (Indeed, You do not fail the promise). Then he drew out from his bedding a toothstick (siwāk), cleaned his teeth with it, performed ablution, and prayed until I said: 'He prayed as long as he slept.' Then he lay down until I said: 'He slept as long as he prayed.' Then he woke and said what he said the first time, and did what he did the first time."

The sixth rank, which is the least, is to stand for the measure of four rakʿahs, or two rakʿahs, or if ablution is difficult for him, he sits facing the qiblah for an hour, occupied with remembrance and supplication, and he is written among the number of those who stand the night, by God's mercy and bounty. It has come in the athar (tradition): "Pray at night, even if [only] the measure of the milking of a sheep." These are the ways of division. So let the seeker (murīd) choose for himself what he finds easiest, and wherever standing in the middle of the night is difficult for him, he should not neglect reviving [the time] between the two evening prayers (al-ʿishāʾayn) and the litany (wird) after the night prayer. Then he stands before the dawn prayer at the time of saḥar, so that the dawn does not overtake him sleeping, and he stands at both ends of the night. This is the seventh rank.

Whenever the consideration is of duration, the ordering of these ranks is according to the length or shortness of time. As for the fifth and seventh ranks, since no fixed measure is considered in them, their matter of precedence and posteriority does not follow the aforementioned order — for the seventh is not below what we mentioned in the sixth, nor is the fifth below the fourth.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Virtuous Nights and Days
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| بيان الليالي والأيام الفاضلة

اعلم أن الليالي المخصوصة بمزيد الفضل التي يتأكد فيها استحباب الإحياء
في السنة خمس عشرة ليلة لا ينبغي أن يغفل المريد عنها فإنها مواسم الخيرات
ومظان التجارات ومتى غفل التاجر عن المواسم لم يربح ومتى غفل المريد عن
فضائل الأوقات لم ينجح فستة من هذه الليالي في  شهر رمضان خمس في أوتار
العشر الأخير إذ فيها يطلب ليلة القدر وليلة سبع عشرة من رمضان فهي ليلة
صبيحتها يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان فيه كانت وقعة بدر وقال ابن الزبير
رحمه الله هي ليلة القدر وأما التسع الأخر فأول ليلة من المحرم وليلة
عاشوراء وأول ليلة من رجب وليلة النصف منه وليلة سبع وعشرين منه وهي ليلة
المعراج وفيها صلاة مأثورة فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للعامل في هذه
الليلة حسنات مائة سنة (1) فمن صلى في هذه الليلة اثنتي عشرة ركعة يقرأ في
كل ركعة فاتحة الكتاب وسورة من القرآن ويتشهد في كل ركعتين ويسلم في آخرهن
ثم يقول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر مائة مرة ثم
يستغفر الله مائة مرة ويصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مائة مرة ويدعو
لنفسه بما شاء من أمر دنياه وآخرته ويصبح صائما فإن الله يستجيب دعاءه كله
إلا أن يدعو في معصية وليلة النصف من شعبان ففيها مائة ركعة يقرأ في كل
ركعة بعد الفاتحة سورة الإخلاص عشر مرات كانوا لا يتركونها كما أوردناه في
صلاة التطوع وليلة عرفة وليلتا العيدين قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أحيا
ليلتي العيدين لم يمت قلبه يوم تموت القلوب (2) وأما الأيام الفاضلة فتسعة
عشر يستحب مواصلة الأوراد فيها يوم عرفة ويوم عاشوراء ويوم سبعة وعشرين من
رجب له شرف عظيم روى أبو هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من صام
يوم سبع وعشرين من رجب كتب الله له صيام ستين شهرا (3) وهو اليوم الذي أهبط
الله فيه جبرائيل عليه السلام على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالرسالة ويوم
سبعة عشر من رمضان وهو يوم وقعة بدر ويوم النصف من شعبان ويوم الجمعة ويوما
العيدين والأيام المعلومات وهي عشر من ذي الحجة والأيام المعدودات وهي أيام
التشريق وقد روى أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا سلم يوم
الجمعة سلمت الأيام  وإذا سلم شهر رمضان سلمت السنة (4) وقال بعض العلماء من
أخذه مهناة في الأيام الخمسة في الدنيا لم ينل مهناة في الآخرة وأراد به
العيدين والجمعة وعرفة وعاشوراء ومن فواضل الأيام في الأسبوع يوم الخميس
والاثنين ترفع فيهما الأعمال إلى الله تعالى وقد ذكرنا فضائل الأشهر
والأيام للصيام في كتاب الصوم فلا حاجة إلى الإعادة والله أعلم وصلى الله
على كل عبد مصطفى من كل العالمين PageV01P361

### |

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

### || كتاب آداب الأكل وهو الكتاب الأول من ربع العادات من كتاب إحياء العلوم

الحمد لله الذي أحسن تدبير الكائنات فخلق الأرض والسماوات
وأنزل الماء الفرات من المعصرات فأخرج به الحب والنبات
وقدر الأرزاق والأفوات
وحفظ بالمأكولات قوى الحيوانات وأعان على الطاعات والأعمال الصالحات بأكل
الطيبات والصلاة على محمد ذي المعجزات الباهرات وعلى آله وأصحابه صلاة
تتوالى على ممر الأوقات وتتضاعف بتعاقب الساعات وسلم تسليما كثيرا
أما بعد فإن مقصد ذوي الألباب لقاء الله تعالى في دار الثواب ولا طريق
إلى الوصول للقاء الله إلى بالعلم والعمل ولا تمكن المواظبة عليهما إلا
بسلامة البدن ولا تصفو سلامة البدن إلا بالأطعمة والأقوات والتناول منها
بقدر الحاجة على تكرر الأوقات فمن هذا الوجه قال بعض السلف الصالحين إن
الأكل من الدين وعليه نبه رب العالمين بقوله وهو أصدق القائلين كلوا من
الطيبات واعملوا صالحا فمن يقدم على الأكل ليستعين به على العلم والعمل
ويقوي به على التقوى فلا ينبغي أن يترك نفسه مهملا سدى يسترسل في الأكل
استرسال البهائم في المرعى فإن ما هو ذريعة إلى الدين ووسيلة إليه ينبغي أن
تظهر أنوار الدين عليه
وإنما أنوار الدين آدابه وسننه التي يزم العبد بزمامها ويلجم المتقي
بلجامها حتى يتزن بميزان الشرع شهوة الطعام في إقدامها وإحجامها فيصير
بسببها مدفعة للوزر ومجلبة للأجر وإن كان فيها أوفى حظ للنفس
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل ليؤجر حتى في اللقمة يرفعها إلى فيه
والى في امعليه السلام رأته (1)
وإنما ذلك إذا رفعها بالدين وللدين  مراعيا فيه آدابه ووظائفه
وها نحن نرشد إلى وظائف الدين في الأكل فرائضها وسننها وآدابها ومروءاتها
وهيئاتها في أربعة أبواب وفصل في آخرها
الباب الأول فيما لا بد للآكل من مراعاته وإن انفرد بالأكل
الباب الثاني فيما يزيد من الآداب بسبب الاجتماع على الأكل
الباب الثالث فيما يخص تقديم الطعام إلى الإخوان الزائرين
الباب الرابع فيما يخص الدعوة والضيافة وأشباهها PageV02P002
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superabundance, excellence, and superiority in rank or merit
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, that which elevates an act or time above its ordinary measure in divine reward
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of surplus; metaphorically applied to times as "virtuous" (fāḍilah) by attribution of divine favor
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥayyā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To live; to quicken; to keep awake in vigil
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual vigilance (iḥyāʾ) as the antithesis of heedlessness (ghaflah), a mode of worship
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "giving life"; metaphorically, "reviving the night" (iḥyāʾ al-layl) through prayer and remembrance
- Root: غ-ف-ل (ghafla)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neglect, inattention, absence of mind from a matter
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The moral failing of the seeker (murīd) who misses divinely appointed seasons of grace
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "forgetfulness"; metaphorically, the trader's loss of profit when absent from the market
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (in) and apodosis (lam yarbaḥ) structure in "متى غفل التاجر عن المواسم لم يربح" demonstrates the classical pairing of temporal-condition with jussive response, indicating a necessary causal consequence.
chapters.translation:
Know that the nights singled out for surpassing merit, in which the commendability of vigil (iḥyāʾ) is emphatically affirmed, are fifteen nights in the year. The seeker (murīd) ought not to be heedless of them, for they are the seasons of good things and the markets of trade. Whenever the trader is heedless of the seasons, he does not profit; and whenever the seeker is heedless of the virtues of times, he does not succeed.

Six of these nights fall in the month of Ramadan: five in the odd nights of the final ten [nights], for therein the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) is sought; and the night of the seventeenth of Ramadan — for its morning is the Day of Discrimination (yawm al-furqān), the day the two hosts met, wherein occurred the Battle of Badr. Ibn al-Zubayr (may God have mercy on him) said it is the Night of Power.

As for the remaining nine: the first night of Muḥarram; the night of ʿĀshūrāʾ; the first night of Rajab; the night of the middle of it; and the night of the twenty-seventh of it — which is the Night of the Ascension (laylat al-miʿrāj). In it there is a transmitted prayer (ṣalāh maʾthūrah), for he (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the one who acts in this night: "the merits of a hundred years." Whoever prays in this night twelve rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Opening of the Book and a chapter from the Qurʾān, and makes the tashahhud in every two rakʿahs and gives the salutation at their end, then says "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greater" one hundred times, then seeks God's forgiveness one hundred times, and sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) one hundred times, and supplicates for himself as he wishes concerning the matters of his world and his hereafter, and wakes up fasting — then God answers all his supplication, unless he supplicates for something in disobedience.

And the night of the middle of Shaʿbān: in it there are one hundred rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah after the Opening the Chapter of Sincerity (al-Ikhlāṣ) ten times. They would not abandon it, as we have related in the book of supererogatory prayer (ṣalāt al-tatawwuʿ). And the night of ʿArafah, and the two nights of the two Festivals (al-ʿīdayn). He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever revives the two nights of the two Festivals, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die."

As for the virtuous days, they are nineteen. It is commendable to maintain the regular litanies (awrād) therein: the Day of ʿArafah; the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ; and the twenty-seventh of Rajab — it has great honor. Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever fasts the twenty-seventh day of Rajab, God writes for him the fast of sixty months." It is the day on which God descended Gabriel (peace be upon him) upon Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) with the message (al-risālah). And the seventeenth of Ramadan — it is the day of the Battle of Badr. And the middle day of Shaʿbān. And the day of Friday. And the two days of the two Festivals. And the "known days" (al-ayyām al-maʿlūmāt) — they are the ten of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. And the "numbered days" (al-ayyām al-maʿdūdāt) — they are the days of Tashrīq.

Anas narrated from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "When Friday is sound, the days are sound; and when the month of Ramadan is sound, the year is sound." Some scholars said: "Whoever takes his ease (muhannāʾ) in the five days in this world will not attain ease in the hereafter" — meaning thereby the two Festivals, Friday, ʿArafah, and ʿĀshūrāʾ.

Among the supererogatory merits of the days of the week are Thursday and Monday, for in them deeds are raised up to God Most High. We have already mentioned the merits of the months and the days for fasting in the Book of Fasting (Kitāb al-Ṣawm), so there is no need for repetition. And God knows best. And may God bless every chosen servant from among all the worlds.

---

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

### The Book of the Etiquettes of Eating — It is the First Book of the Quarter of Customs (rubʿ al-ʿādāt) from the Revival of the Religious Sciences

Praise be to God, who perfected the governance of created things, and created the earth and the heavens, and sent down the sweet water from the rain-clouds, bringing forth thereby grain and vegetation, and apportioned provisions and sustenance, and preserved by means of foods the powers of living beings, and aided obedience and righteous deeds through the eating of good things. And blessings upon Muḥammad, possessor of dazzling miracles, and upon his family and companions — blessings that follow one another across the passage of times and multiply with the succession of hours — and abundant peace.

To proceed: The aim of those possessed of intellects (ulū al-albāb) is the meeting of God Most High in the Abode of Recompense. There is no path to reaching the meeting of God except through knowledge and action; and perseverance in both is not possible except through soundness of the body; and soundness of the body is not purified except through foods and provisions, partaking of them in the measure of need, repeated over the succession of times. From this aspect, some of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn) said that eating is part of religion. Upon this the Lord of the Worlds alerted us by His saying — and He is the most truthful of speakers: {«كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا»} ("Eat of the good things and work righteousness").

Whoever undertakes eating in order to seek aid thereby for knowledge and action, and to strengthen himself for piety, ought not to leave his soul neglected and untended, letting himself loose in eating as beasts loose themselves in pasture. For that which is a means to religion and a pathway to it — the lights of religion ought to appear upon it.

And the lights of religion are its etiquettes (ādāb) and its normative practices (sunan), by which the servant is bridled with their reins and the God-fearing is muzzled with their bit, until the appetite for food is balanced by the scale of the Sacred Law in its advance and its retreat. By means of them, one becomes a repeller of burden (wizr) and an attractor of reward (ajr), even if therein lies the fullest share for the soul.

He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, a man is rewarded even for the morsel he raises to his mouth" — and in another narration: "and to his wife." That is only so when he raises it with religion and for religion, observing therein its etiquettes and its functions.

And here we now guide to the functions of religion in eating: its obligations (farāʾiḍ), its normative practices (sunān), its etiquettes (ādāb), its manly virtues (murūʾāt), and its forms (hayʾāt) — in four chapters, with a concluding section at their end.

Chapter One: What the eater must observe even if he eats alone.
Chapter Two: What additional etiquettes arise from gathering together for eating.
Chapter Three: What pertains specifically to presenting food to visiting brethren.
Chapter Four: What pertains specifically to invitation (daʿwah), hospitality (ḍiyāfah), and their like.

chapters.title_en: The First Chapter on What Is Necessary for the One Who Eats Alone, Comprising Three Divisions: Before Eating, During Eating, and After Finishing

### ||| الباب الأول فيما لابد للمنفرد منه وهو ثلاثة أقسام قسم قبل الأكل وقسم مع الأكل وقسم بعد الفراغ منه

### |||| القسم الأول في الآداب التي تتقدم على الأكل وهي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ر د (f-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Solitude, uniqueness, being alone; al-fard is the single one, and tafarrud denotes isolation from others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Individuality as a state of ontological and practical separation; here, it refers to the eater’s physical and social isolation, not spiritual uniqueness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of being alone; no metaphorical extension intended—it denotes the actual condition of dining without company.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, partition, apportioning; qism is a portion or category.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Logical division of a whole into exhaustive parts; here, the three temporal phases of the meal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally as a classificatory term, not metaphorically.
- Root: أ ك ل (a-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Eating, consuming food; the act of ingestion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical nourishment as a lawful human need, subject to ethical regulation in religious praxis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of eating; no figurative sense here.
- Root: ف ر غ (f-r-gh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness, completion, cessation; farāgh means finishing and vacating.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Completion of an action, marking the boundary of the ritualized meal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of concluding; not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "وهو ثلاثة أقسام" (and it is three divisions) is an explanatory appositive clarifying the preceding "ما لابد للمنفرد منه" (what is necessary for the one alone), while the subsequent "قسم قبل الأكل..." enumerates via explicit division (taqsīm), each governed by the same syntactic frame.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first chapter concerns what is indispensable for the one who eats alone, and it comprises three divisions: a division before eating, a division during eating, and a division after finishing the meal.

The first division concerns the etiquettes (ādāb) that precede eating, and they are as follows.

chapters.title_en: On the Etiquette of Eating: The First to Seventh Proprieties (Ādāb al-Akl)
