He said: "No." He said: "Were you his companion in travel, by which noble character is discerned?" He said: "No." He said: "Did you deal with him in dīnār and dirham, by which a man's scrupulousness is made evident?" He said: "No." He said: "I think you saw him standing in the mosque, murmuring the Qurʾān, lowering his head at times and raising it at others." He said: "Yes." He said: "Go — you do not know him." And he said to the man: "Go, and bring me one who knows you."

chapters.title_en: Chapter Five — On the Merchant’s Compassion for His Religion in What Concerns His Own Self and What Pertains to His Hereafter
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| الباب الخامس في شفقة التاجر على دينه فيما يخصه ويعم آخرته
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش ف ق (shafaqah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — tenderness, solicitude, and protective concern; the trembling of the heart out of care for another’s welfare.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, shafaqah denotes a virtue of the soul that impels one to avert harm and secure benefit for the object of concern — here, the merchant’s own religion (dīn) as the ultimate object of protective care.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the physical trembling of compassion; metaphorical (majāz) — the earnest vigilance of the heart over one’s spiritual state, akin to a shepherd’s watchfulness over his flock.
- Root: ت ج ر (tijārah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trade, commerce, exchange of goods for profit; derived from tajara — to engage in buying and selling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and ethical context, tijārah is often contrasted with the “trade that never perishes” (tijāratan lan tabūr) — the exchange of worldly goods for spiritual gain; here, the merchant’s worldly trade is the arena where his religious vigilance must operate.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — commercial transaction; metaphorical — the soul’s bartering of fleeting worldly profit against enduring hereafter (ākhirah) reward.
- Root: خ ص ص (khaṣṣa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To single out, to be particular to; khuṣūṣ — specificity, exclusivity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes what is particular to an individual as opposed to the general (ʿāmm); here, the merchant’s personal religious obligations (farḍ al-ʿayn) versus communal ones.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — private ownership or concern; metaphorical — the inward, personal dimension of faith that cannot be delegated.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase “فيما يخصه ويعم آخرته” employs a conjunctive (wa) linking two prepositional phrases, where the second (yaʿummu ākhiratahu) extends the scope of the first (yakhuṣṣuhu), creating a comprehensive binary: the particular (personal religious duties) and the general (all that encompasses the hereafter). The construction requires the reader to parse both as coordinate objects of the same governing preposition (fī), indicating that the merchant’s compassion must cover both spheres simultaneously.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the fifth chapter, concerning the merchant’s compassion (shafaqah) for his religion — both in what is particular to his own self (mā yakhuṣṣuhu) and in what encompasses his hereafter (mā yaʿummu ākhiratahu).

chapters.title_en: On the Merchant's Vigilance Over His Religion and the Seven Principles of Mercantile Piety
chapters.arabic_text:
ولا ينبغي للتاجر أن يشغله معاشه عن معاده فيكون عمره ضائعا وصفقته خاسرة
وما يفوته من الربح في الآخرة لا يفي به ما ينال في الدنيا فيكون اشترى
الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة بل العاقل ينبغي أن يشفق على نفسه وشفقته على نفسه
يحفظ رأس ماله ورأس ماله دينه وتجارته فيه
قال بعض السلف أولي الأشياء بالعاقل أحوجه إليه في العاجل وأحوج شيء إليه
في العاجل أحمده عاقبة في الآجل
وقال معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه في وصيته إنه لا بد لك من نصيبك في الدنيا
وأنت إلى نصيبك من الآخرة أحوج فابدأ بنصيبك من الآخرة فخذه فإنك ستمر على
نصيبك من الدنيا فتنظمه
قال الله تعالى ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا أي لا تنس في الدنيا نصيبك منها
للآخرة فإنها مزرعة الآخرة وفيها تكتسب الحسنات
وإنما تتم شفقة التاجر على دينه بمراعاة سبعة أمور
الأول حسن النية والعقيدة في ابتداء  التجارة فلينو بها الاستعفاف عن
السؤال وكف الطمع عن الناس استغناء بالحلال عنهم واستعانة بما يكسبه على
الدين وقياما بكفاية العيال ليكون من جملة المجاهدين به ولينو النصح
للمسلمين وأن يحب لسائر الخلق ما يحب لنفسه ولينو اتباع طريق العدل
والإحسان في معاملته كما ذكرناه ولينو الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر في
كل ما يراه في السوق فإذا أضمر هذه العقائد والنيات كان عاملا في طريق
الآخرة فإن استفاد مالا فهو مزيد وإن خسر في الدنيا ربح في الآخرة
الثاني أن يقصد القيام في صنعته أو تجارته بفرض من فروض الكفايات فإن
الصناعات والتجارات لو تركت بطلت المعايش وهلك أكثر الخلق
فانتظام أمر الكل بتعاون الكل وتكفل كل فريق بعمل ولو أقبل كلهم على صنعة
واحدة لتعطلت البواقي وهلكوا وعلى هذا حمل بعض الناس قوله صلى الله عليه
وسلم اختلاف أمتي رحمة (1)
أي اختلاف همهم في الصناعات والحرف
ومن الصناعات ما هي مهمة ومنها ما يستغنى عنها لرجوعها إلى طلب النعم
والتزين في الدنيا فليشتغل بصناعة مهمة ليكون في قيامه بها كافيا عن
المسلمين مهما في الدين وليجتنب صناعة النقش والصياغة وتشييد البنيان بالجص
وجميع ما تزخرف به الدنيا فكل ذلك كرهه ذوو الدين فأما عمل الملاهي والآلات
التي يحرم استعمالها فاجتناب ذلك من قبيل ترك الظلم ومن جملة ذلك خياطة
الخياط القباء من الإبر يسم للرجال وصياغة الصائغ مراكب الذهب أو خواتيم
الذهب للرجال فكل ذلك من المعاصي والأجرة المأخوذة عليه حرام ولذلك أوجبنا
الزكاة فيها وإن كنا لا نوجب الزكاة في الحلي لأنها إذا قصدت للرجال فهي
محرمة وكونها مهيأة للنساء لا يلحقها بالحلي المباح ما لم يقصد ذلك بها
فيكتسب حكمها من القصد
وقد ذكرنا أن بيع الطعام وبيع الأكفان مكروه لأنه يوجب انتظار موت الناس
وحاجتهم بغلاء السعر PageV02P083
ويكره أن يكون جزارا لما فيه من قساوة القلب وأن يكون حجاما أو كناسا لما
فيه من مخامرة النجاسة وكذا الدباغ وما في معناه وكره ابن سيرين الدلالة
وكره قتادة أجرة الدلال ولعل السبب فيه قلة استغناء الدلال عن الكذب
والإفراط في الثناء على السلعة لترويجها ولأن العمل فيه لا يتقدر فقد يقل
وقد يكثر ولا ينظر في مقدار الأجرة إلى عمله بل إلى قدر قيمة الثوب هذا هو
العادة وهو ظلم بل ينبغي أن ينظر إلى قدر التعب وكرهوا شراء الحيوان
للتجارة لأن المشتري يكره قضاء الله فيه وهو الموت الذي بصدده لا محالة
وحلوله
وقيل بع الحيوان واشتر الموتان وكرهوا الصرف لأن الاحتراز فيه عن دقائق
الربا عسير ولأنه طلب لدقائق الصفات فيما لا يقصد أعيانها وإنما يقصد
رواجها وقلما يتم للصيرفي ربح إلا باعتماد جهالة معامله بدقائق النقد فقلما
يسلم الصيرفي وإن احتاط ويكره للصيرفي وغيره كسر الصحيح والدنانير إلا عند
الشك في جودته أو عند ضرورة
قال أحمد بن حنبل رحمة الله ورد نهي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (1)
وعن أصحابه في الصياغة من الصحاح وأنا أكره الكسر وقال يشتري بالدنانير
دراهم ثم يشتري بالدرهم ذهبا ويصوغه واستحبوا تجارة البز
قال سعيد بن المسيب ما من تجارة أحب إلي من البز ما لم يكن فيها أيمان
وقد روي خير تجارتكم البز وخير صنائعكم الخرز (2)
وفي حديث آخر لو اتجر أهل الجنة لاتجروا في البز ولو اتجر أهل النار
لاتجروا في الصرف (3)
وقد كان غالب أعمال الأخيار من السلف عشر صنائع الخرز والتجارة والحمل
والخياطة والحذو والقصارة وعمل الخفاف وعمل الحديد وعمل المغازل ومعالجة
صيد البر والبحر والوراقة قال عبد الوهاب الوراق
قال لي أحمد بن حنبل ما صنعتك قلت الوراقة قال كسب طيب ولو كنت صانعا
بيدي لصنعت صنعتك ثم قال لي لا تكتب إلا مواسطة واستبق الحواشي وظهور
الأجزاء
وأربعة من الصناع موسومون عند الناس بضعف الرأي الحاكة والقطانون
والمغازليون والمعلمون
ولعل ذلك لأن أكثر مخالطتهم مع النساء والصبيان ومخالطة ضعفاء العقول
تضعف العقل كما أن مخالطة العقلاء تزيد في العقل
وعن مجاهد أن مريم عليها السلام مرت في طلبها لعيسى  عليه السلام بحاكة
فطلبت الطريق فأرشدوها غير الطريق فقالت اللهم انزع البركة من كسبهم وأمتهم
فقراء وحقرهم في أعين الناس فاستجيب دعاؤها
وكره السلف أخذ الأجرة على كل ما هو من قبيل العبادات وفروض الكفايات
كغسل الموتى ودفنهم وكذا الأذان وصلاة التراويح وإن حكم بصحة الاستئجار
عليه وكذا تعليم القرآن وتعليم علم الشرع فإن هذه أعمال حقها أن يتجر فيها
للآخرة وأخذ الأجرة عليها استبدال بالدنيا عن الآخرة ولا يستحب ذلك
الثالث أن يمنعه سوق الدنيا عن سوق الآخرة وأسواق الآخرة المساجد
قال الله تعالى رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة
وإيتاء الزكاة وقال الله تعالى في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه
فينبغي أن يجعل أول النهار إلى وقت دخول السوق لآخرته فيلازم المسجد ويواظب
على الأوراد
كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول للتجار اجعلوا أول نهاركم لآخرتكم وما بعده
لدنياكم
وكان صالحو السلف يجعلون أول PageV02P084
النهار وآخره للآخرة والوسط للتجارة ولم يكن يبيع الهريسة والرءوس بكرة
إلا الصبيان وأهل الذمة لأنهم كانوا في المساجد بعد
وفي الخبر إن الملائكة إذا صعدت بصحيفة العبد وفيها في أول النهار وفي
آخره ذكر الله وخير كفر الله عنهما ما بينهما من سيئ الأعمال (1)
وفي الخبر تلتقي ملائكة الليل والنهار عند طلوع الفجر وعند صلاة العصر
فيقول الله تعالى وهو أعلم بهم كيف تركتم عبادي فيقولون تركناهم وهو يصلون
وجئناهم وهم يصلون فيقول الله سبحانه وتعالى أشهدكم أني قد غفرت لهم (2)
ثم مهما سمع الأذان في وسط النهار للأولى والعصر فينبغي أن لا يعرج على
شغل وينزعج عن مكانه ويدع كل ما كان فيه فما يفوته من فضيلة التكبيرة
الأولى مع الإمام في أول الوقت لا توازيها الدنيا بما فيها ومهما لم يحضر
الجماعة عصى عند بعض العلماء
وقد كان السلف يبتدرون عند الأذان ويخلون الأسواق للصبيان وأهل الذمة
وكانوا يستأجرون بالقراريط لحفظ الحوانيت في أوقات الصلوات وكان ذلك معيشة
لهم
وقد جاء في تفسير  قوله تعالى {لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} أنهم
كانوا حدادين وخرازين فكان أحدهم إذا رفع المطرقة أو غرز الإشفى فسمع
الأذان لم يخرج الإشفى من المغرز ولم يوقع المطرقة ورمى بها وقام إلى
الصلاة
الرابع أن لا يقتصر على هذا بل يلازم ذكر الله سبحانه في السوق ويشتغل
بالتهليل والتسبيح فذكر الله في السوق بين الغافلين أفضل
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذاكر الله في الغافلين كالمقاتل خلف الفارين
وكالحي بين الأموات وفي لفظ آخر كالشجرة الخضراء بين الهشيم وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم من دخل السوق فقال لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له الملك وله
الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير كتب الله
له ألف ألف حسنة (3)
وكان ابن عمر وسالم بن عبد الله ومحمد بن واسع وغيرهم يدخلون السوق
قاصدين لنيل فضيلة هذا الذكر
وقال الحسن ذاكر الله في السوق يجيء يوم القيامة له ضوء كضوء القمر
وبرهان كبرهان الشمس ومن استغفر الله في السوق غفر الله له بعدد أهلها
وكان عمر رضي الله عنه إذا دخل السوق قال اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الكفر
والفسوق ومن شر ما أحاطت به السوق اللهم إني أعوذ بك من يمين فاجرة وصفقة
خاسرة
وقال أبو جعفر الفرغاني كنا يوما عند الجنيد فجرى ذكر ناس يجلسون في
المساجد ويتشبهون بالصوفية ويقصرون عما يجب عليهم من حق الجلوس ويعيبون من
يدخل السوق فقال الجنيد كم ممن هو في السوق حكمه أن يدخل المسجد ويأخذ بإذن
بعض من فيه فيخرجه ويجلس مكانه وإني لأعرف رجلا يدخل السوق ورده كل يوم
ثلثمائة ركعة وثلاثون ألف تسبيحة
قال فسبق إلى وهمي أنه يعني نفسه فهكذا كانت تجارة من يتجر لطلب الكفاية
لا للتنعم في الدنيا فإن من يطلب الدنيا للاستعانة بها على الآخرة كيف يدع
ربح الآخرة والسوق والمسجد والبيت له حكم واحد وإنما النجاة بالتقوى
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتق  الله حيثما كنت (4)
فوظيفة التقوى لا تنقطع عن المتجردين للدين كيفما تقلبت بهم الأحوال وبه
تكون حياتهم وعيشتهم إذ فيه يرون تجارتهم وربحهم وقد قيل من أحب الآخرة عاش
ومن أحب الدنيا طاش والأحمق يغدو ويروح في لاش والعاقل عن عيوب نفسه فتاش
PageV02P085
الخامس أن لا يكون شديد الحرص على السوق والتجارة وذلك بأن يكون أول داخل
وآخر خارج وبأن يركب البحر في التجارة فهما مكروهان يقال إن من ركب البحر
فقد استقصى في طلب الرزق
وفي الخبر لا يركب البحر إلا لحج أو عمرة أو غزو (1)
وكان عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما يقول لا تكن أول داخل في
السوق ولا آخر خارج منها فإن بها باض الشيطان وفرخ
روي عن معاذ بن جبل وعبد الله بن عمر إن إبليس يقول لولده زلنبور سر
بكتائبك فأت أصحاب الأسواق زين لهم الكذب والحلف والخديعة والمكر والخيانة
وكن مع أول داخل وآخر خارج منها
وفي الخبر شر البقاع الأسواق وشر أهلها أولهم دخولا وآخرهم خروجا (2)
وتمام هذا الاحتراز أن يراقب وقت كفايته فإذا حصل كفاية وقته انصرف
واشتغل بتجارة الآخرة هكذا كان صالحو السلف فقد كان منهم من إذا ربح دانقا
انصرف قناعة به
وكان حماد بن سلمة يبيع الخز في سفط بين يديه فكان إذا ربح حبتين رفع
سفطه وانصرف
وقال إبراهيم بن بشار قلت لإبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله أمر اليوم أعمل في
الطين فقال يا ابن بشار إنك طالب ومطلوب يطلبك من لا تفوته وتطلب ما قد
كفيته أما رأيت حريصا محروما وضعيفا مرزوقا فقلت إن لي دانقا عند البقال
فقال عز علي بك تملك دانقا وتطلب العمل وقد كان فيهم من ينصرف بعد الظهر
ومنهم بعد العصر ومنهم من لا يعمل في الأسبوع إلا يوما أو يومين وكانوا
يكتفون به
السادس أن لا يقتصر على اجتناب الحرام بل يتقي مواقع الشبهات ومظان الريب
ولا ينظر إلى الفتاوى بل يستفتي قلبه فإذا وجد فيه حزازة  اجتنبه وإذا حمل
إليه سلعة رابه أمرها سأل عنها حتى يعرف وإلا أكل الشبهة وقد حمل إلى رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لبن فقال من أين لكم هذا فقالوا من الشاة فقال ومن
أين لكم هذه الشاة فقيل من موضع كذا فشرب منه ثم قال إنا معاشر الأنبياء
أمرنا أن لا نأكل إلا طيبا ولا نعمل إلا صالحا (3)
وقال إن الله تعالى أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين فقال {يا أيها
الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم} (4) أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة
(5) حديث كان لا يسأل عن كل ما يحمل إليه رواه أحمد من حديث جابر أن رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه مروا بامرأة فذبحت لهم شاة الحديث فأخذ
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقمة فلم يستطع أن يسيغها فقال هذه شاة ذبحت
بغير إذن أهلهاالحديث وله من حديث أبي هريرة كان إذا أتى بطعام من غير أهله
سأل عنهالحديث وإسنادهما جيد وفي هذا أنه كان لا يسأل عما أتي به من عند
أهله والله أعلم //
وإنما الواجب أن ينظر التاجر إلى من يعامله فكل منسوب إلى ظلم أو خيانة
أو سرقة أو ربا فلا يعامله وكذا الأجناد والظلمة لا يعاملهم البتة ولا
يعامل أصحابهم وأعوانهم لأنه معين بذلك على الظلم
وحكي عن رجل أنه تولى عمارة سور لثغر من الثغور
قال فوقع في نفسي من ذلك شيء وإن كان ذلك العمل من الخيرات بل من فرائض
الإسلام ولكن كان الأمير الذي تولى في محلته من الظلمة
قال فسألت سفيان رضي الله PageV02P086
عنه فقال لا تكن عونا لهم على قليل ولا كثير فقلت هذا سور في سبيل الله
للمسلمين فقال نعم ولكن أقل ما يدخل عليك أن تحب بقاءهم ليوفوك أجرك فتكون
قد أحببت بقاء من يعصي الله
وقد جاء في الخبر من دعا لظالم بالبقاء فقد أحب أن يعصي الله في أرضه (1)
وفي الحديث إن الله ليغضب إذا مدح الفاسق (2)
وفي حديث آخر  من أكرم فاسقا فقد أعان على هدم الإسلام (3)
ودخل سفيان على المهدي وبيده درج أبيض فقال يا سفيان أعطني الدواة حتى
أكتب فقال أخبرني أي شيء تكتب فإن كان حقا أعطيتك
وطلب بعض الأمراء من بعض العلماء المحبوسين عنده أن يناوله طينا ليختم به
الكتاب فقال ناولني الكتاب أولا حتى أنظر ما فيه فهكذا كانوا يحترزون عن
معاونة الظلمة ومعاملتهم أشد أنواع الإعانة فينبغي أن يجتنبها ذوو الدين ما
وجدوا إليه سبيلا
وبالجملة فينبغي أن ينقسم الناس عنده إلى من يعامل ومن لا يعامل وليكن من
يعامله أقل ممن لا يعامله في هذا الزمان قال بعضهم أتى على الناس زمان كان
الرجل يدخل السوق ويقول من ترون لي أن أعامل من الناس فيقال له عامل من شئت
ثم أتى زمان آخر كانوا يقولون عامل من شئت إلا فلانا وفلانا ثم أتى زمان
آخر فكان يقال لا تعامل أحدا إلا فلانا وفلانا وأخشى أن يأتي زمان يذهب هذا
أيضا
وكأنه قد كان الذي كان يحذر أن يكون إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون
السابع ينبغي أن يراقب جميع مجاري معاملته مع واحد من معامليه فإنه مراقب
ومحاسب فليعد الجواب ليوم الحساب والعقاب في كل فعلة وقولة إنه لم أقدم
عليها ولأجل ماذا فإنه يقال إنه يوقف التاجر يوم القيامة مع كل رجل كان
باعه شيئا وقفة ويحاسب عن كل واحد فهو محاسب على عدد من عامله
قال بعضهم رأيت بعض التجار في النوم فقلت ماذا فعل الله بك فقال نشر علي
خمسين ألف صحيفة فقلت هذه كلها ذنوب فقال هذه معاملات الناس بعدد كل إنسان
عاملته في الدنيا لكل إنسان صحيفة مفردة فيما بيني وبينه من أول معاملته
إلى آخرها فهذا ما على المكتسب في عمله من العدل والإحسان والشفقة على
الدين فإن اقتصر على العدل كان من الصالحين وإن أضاف إليه الإحسان كان من
المقربين وإن راعى مع ذلك وظائف الدين كما ذكر في الباب الخامس كان من
الصديقين والله أعلم  بالصواب
تم كتاب الكسب والمعيشة بحمد الله ومنه PageV02P087

- Root: ش-ف-ق (shafaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of tenderness, compassion, and solicitous care; the trembling of the heart out of concern for another's welfare.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological context, it denotes the soul's protective concern for its own ultimate salvation—a form of self-compassion that guards the capital of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here as the merchant's vigilant care for his religion, not metaphorically; it is the operative virtue of the entire section.
- Root: ر-ب-ح (rabiḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Profit, gain, and success in trade; the opposite of loss (khusr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Transposed to the eschatological register—true profit is the gain of the Hereafter; worldly loss is insignificant beside it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in commercial contexts, but here extended metaphorically (majāz) to the spiritual economy of salvation.
- Root: خ-س-ر (khasira)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lose, to perish, to suffer diminution; the antithesis of profit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic idiom, the ultimate loss (khusrān) is the squandering of one's eternal portion for the ephemeral world.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for a failed transaction, but the deeper referent is the eschatological bankruptcy of the heedless.
- Root: ن-ص-ح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sincerity, good counsel, and the desire for another's genuine welfare.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A cardinal virtue in the religious life—sincere goodwill toward all Muslims, as the Prophet said: "Religion is sincerity."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in intent; the merchant must intend sincere counsel to his fellow Muslims in all his transactions.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause with In (إن الشرطية) — The frequent use of "in" (if) constructions (e.g., "fa-in ʿaṣama hādhihi al-ʿaqāʾid") establishes a causal nexus between the merchant's inward intentions and his outward spiritual outcomes, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis to preserve the logical sequence of Ghazali's argument.
chapters.translation:
I say: It behooves not the merchant that his livelihood (maʿāsh) distract him from his ultimate return (maʿād), lest his life be wasted and his transaction be a losing one. Whatever profit he forfeits in the Hereafter cannot be compensated by what he attains in this world; for then he would have purchased the present life at the price of the Hereafter. Rather, the intelligent man ought to be compassionate toward his own soul (yushfiq ʿalā nafsihi), and his compassion for his soul preserves his capital—and his capital is his religion (dīn), and his trade is therein.

One of the Salaf (predecessors) said: "The thing most befitting the intelligent man is that which he most needs in the immediate term; and the thing he most needs in the immediate term is that whose consequence is most praiseworthy in the eventual term."

Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may God be pleased with him) said in his testament: "You inevitably have your portion in this world, yet you are more in need of your portion in the Hereafter. So begin with your portion of the Hereafter and take it; for you will pass by your portion of this world and will set it in order."

God Most High said: {«And do not forget your portion of this world»} (al-Qaṣaṣ 28:77)—that is, do not, in this world, forget your portion of it [that is destined] for the Hereafter; for this world is the tillage of the Hereafter, and in it are good deeds acquired.

The merchant's compassion for his religion is only perfected by observing seven matters:

**The First:** Good intention (ḥusn al-niyyah) and sound creed at the commencement of trade. Let him intend thereby: abstinence from begging (al-istiʿfāf ʿan al-suʾāl), the restraint of covetousness from people, sufficiency through the lawful (ḥalāl) instead of them, assistance upon his religion through what he earns, and the fulfillment of his family's maintenance—so that he may be among the strivers (mujāhidīn) thereby. Let him intend sincere counsel (al-nuṣḥ) to the Muslims, and that he love for all creatures what he loves for himself. Let him intend the pursuit of the path of justice (al-ʿadl) and beneficence (al-iḥsān) in his dealings, as we have mentioned. And let him intend commanding the good and forbidding the evil in everything he witnesses in the market. When he conceals these creeds and intentions, he is a worker upon the path of the Hereafter: if he gains wealth, it is an increase; and if he loses in this world, he profits in the Hereafter.

**The Second:** That he intend, in his craft or trade, the fulfillment of a communal obligation (farḍ min furūḍ al-kifāyāt). For if crafts and trades were abandoned, livelihoods would be ruined and most of creation would perish. The order of the whole is only established by the mutual cooperation of all, with each group undertaking a work. Were they all to devote themselves to a single craft, the rest would be disrupted and they would perish. Upon this some people interpreted the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "The divergence of my community is a mercy" (1)—that is, the divergence of their concerns in crafts and professions.

Among crafts, some are essential (muhimmah) and some are dispensable, because they revert to the pursuit of luxuries and adornment in this world. Let him occupy himself with an essential craft, so that in his pursuit of it he suffices the Muslims in what pertains to religion. Let him avoid the craft of engraving, goldsmithing, the construction of buildings with plaster, and all that adorns this world—for all such things were disapproved by people of religion. As for the making of instruments of amusement and the apparatus whose use is forbidden, avoiding that falls under the category of abandoning wrongdoing. Included therein is the tailor's sewing of a man's garment (qabāʾ) with silk brocade (ibrīsam) for men, and the goldsmith's fashioning of gold vessels or gold rings for men—all of these are acts of disobedience, and the wage taken for them is unlawful (ḥarām). For this reason we have made the zakāt obligatory upon them, although we do not make zakāt obligatory upon [lawful] ornaments—because when they are intended for men, they are forbidden; and their being prepared for women does not attach them to permissible ornaments unless that is intended thereby; their ruling is acquired from the intention.

We have already mentioned that selling food and selling shrouds is disapproved (makrūh), because it entails awaiting people's death and their need through the inflation of prices. (Page V02P083) It is disapproved to be a butcher, because of the hardness of heart it entails; and to be a cupper (ḥajjām) or a sweeper (kannās), because of the contamination with filth; likewise tanning and what is analogous to it. Ibn Sīrīn disapproved of brokerage (dilālah), and Qatādah disapproved of the broker's wage. Perhaps the reason is the broker's scant freedom from lying and from excessive praise of the commodity to promote it; and because the work therein is not measurable—it may be little or much, and the amount of the wage is not considered by his labor but by the value of the garment; this is the custom, and it is an injustice. Rather, one ought to consider the amount of exertion. They disapproved of buying animals for trade, because the buyer dislikes God's decree therein—namely, death, which inevitably approaches and befalls. It was said: "Sell the animal and buy the dead [merchandise]." They disapproved of money-changing (ṣarf), because guarding against the subtleties of usury (ribā) therein is difficult, and because it is a pursuit of subtle qualities in things whose essences are not intended but only their circulation; and rarely does a money-changer profit except by relying on his counterpart's ignorance of the subtleties of coinage. Thus the money-changer rarely remains safe, even if he is cautious. It is disapproved for the money-changer and others to break sound [coins] and dīnārs, except when doubting their quality or in cases of necessity.

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal (may God have mercy on him) said: "A prohibition was reported from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) (1) and from his Companions regarding the fashioning of sound [coins], and I disapprove of breaking them." He said: "One buys with dīnārs dirhams, then buys with the dirham gold and fashions it." They deemed commendable the trade in fine cloth (bazz). Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "No trade is more beloved to me than fine cloth, so long as there are no oaths therein." It has been related: "The best of your trades is fine cloth, and the best of your crafts is needlework (kharz)" (2). In another ḥadīth: "If the people of Paradise traded, they would trade in fine cloth; and if the people of the Fire traded, they would trade in money-changing" (3).

The predominant occupations of the righteous among the Salaf were ten crafts: needlework, trade, porterage, tailoring, shoemaking, fulling (qiṣārah), making sandals, ironwork, spindle-making, and the pursuit of hunting on land and sea, and book-copying (wirāqah). ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Warrāq said: "Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said to me: 'What is your craft?' I said: 'Book-copying.' He said: 'A good earning. Were I a craftsman with my hands, I would practice your craft.' Then he said to me: 'Do not write except the middle [of the page], and reserve the margins and the backs of the fascicles.'"

Four of the craftsmen are marked among people with weakness of intellect: weavers, cotton-carders, spinners, and teachers. Perhaps that is because most of their association is with women and boys, and associating with the weak-minded weakens the intellect, just as associating with the intelligent increases the intellect.

It is related from Mujāhid that Mary (peace be upon her), while seeking Jesus (peace be upon him), passed by weavers and asked for the road, but they directed her away from it. She said: "O God, remove the blessing from their earnings, make them die poor, and render them contemptible in people's eyes." Her supplication was answered.

The Salaf disapproved of taking wages for everything that falls under the category of acts of worship and communal obligations—such as washing the dead and burying them; likewise the call to prayer (adhān) and the tarāwīḥ prayer, even if the validity of hiring for them is ruled; likewise teaching the Qur'an and teaching the science of the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ). For these are works whose due is that one trade in them for the Hereafter; taking wages for them is an exchange of this world for the Hereafter, and that is not commendable.

**The Third:** That the market of this world not prevent him from the market of the Hereafter—and the markets of the Hereafter are the mosques. God Most High said: {«Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakāt»} (al-Nūr 24:37). And God Most High said: {«In houses God has permitted to be raised, and His name is mentioned therein»} (al-Nūr 24:36). He ought to make the beginning of the day, up to the time of entering the market, for his Hereafter—frequenting the mosque and persevering in his litanies (awrād).

ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) used to say to the merchants: "Make the beginning of your day for your Hereafter, and what follows it for your worldly affairs." The righteous among the Salaf made the beginning (Page V02P084) and the end of the day for the Hereafter, and the middle for trade. None sold porridge (harīsah) and heads early in the morning except boys and the people of the dhimmah, because they [the Salaf] were in the mosques at that time.

In the report: "When the angels ascend with the scroll of the servant, and in it, at the beginning of the day and its end, is the remembrance of God and goodness, God forgives, for the sake of these two, the evil deeds between them" (1). In the report: "The angels of night and day meet at the break of dawn and at the ʿaṣr prayer. God Most High says—and He knows best about them—'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We left them praying, and we came to them while they were praying.' God Most High says: 'I call you to witness that I have forgiven them'" (2).

Then, whenever he hears the call to prayer in the middle of the day for the noon (ẓuhr) and the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayers, he ought not to turn aside to any occupation; he should be stirred from his place and abandon whatever he was engaged in. For what he forfeits of the virtue of the first takbīrah with the imam at the beginning of the time is not equaled by this world and all that is in it. And if he does not attend the congregational prayer, he has disobeyed, according to some scholars.

The Salaf used to hasten at the call to prayer and leave the markets to the boys and the people of the dhimmah. They used to hire, for small coins (qarārīṭ), people to guard the shops at the times of prayers, and that was a livelihood for them.

It has come in the interpretation of God's saying {«Neither commerce nor sale distracts them from the remembrance of God»} that they were blacksmiths and needle-workers. One of them, when he raised his hammer or inserted his awl (ishfā) and heard the call to prayer, would not withdraw the awl from its hole nor bring down the hammer—he would throw it down and rise to prayer.

**The Fourth:** That he not be content with this, but rather persevere in the remembrance of God Most High in the market, occupying himself with the tahlīl (saying lā ilāha illā Allāh) and the tasbīḥ (glorification). For the remembrance of God in the market, among the heedless, is more excellent.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The one who remembers God among the heedless is like the fighter behind the fleeing, and like the living among the dead." In another wording: "Like the green tree among dry brushwood." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever enters the market and says: 'There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not; in His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things'—God writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds" (3).

Ibn ʿUmar, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ, and others used to enter the market intending to attain the virtue of this remembrance. Al-Ḥasan said: "The one who remembers God in the market will come on the Day of Resurrection with a light like the light of the moon and a proof like the proof of the sun. Whoever seeks God's forgiveness in the market, God forgives him to the number of its inhabitants."

ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him), when he entered the market, said: "O God, I seek refuge in You from disbelief (kufr) and wickedness (fusūq), and from the evil of what surrounds the market. O God, I seek refuge in You from a false oath and a losing transaction."

Abū Jaʿfar al-Farghānī said: "One day we were with al-Junayd, and mention was made of people who sit in the mosques, imitating the Sufis, falling short of what is incumbent upon them regarding the right of sitting [there], and censuring those who enter the market. Al-Junayd said: 'How many are those in the market whose due it is to enter the mosque, take permission from one of those therein, remove him, and sit in his place! And I know a man who enters the market with his daily litany of three hundred rakʿahs and thirty thousand glorifications.'"

He said: "It occurred to my mind that he meant himself." Such was the trade of those who trade seeking sufficiency (kifāyah), not for luxury in this world. For whoever seeks this world as an aid upon the Hereafter—how could he abandon the profit of the Hereafter? The market, the mosque, and the house have for him one single ruling; salvation is only through piety (taqwā). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Fear God wherever you are" (4). The function of piety is not cut off from those who devote themselves to religion, however their circumstances turn; and in it is their life and their livelihood, for therein they see their trade and their profit. It has been said: "Whoever loves the Hereafter lives; whoever loves this world is scattered (ṭāsha); the fool goes to and fro in nothing, and the intelligent one searches out his own faults." (Page V02P085)

**The Fifth:** That he not be excessively eager for the market and trade—namely, by being the first to enter and the last to leave, and by taking to the sea in trade; both are disapproved. It is said: "Whoever takes to the sea has been extreme in seeking provision." In the report: "None takes to the sea except for pilgrimage (ḥajj), ʿumrah, or warfare" (1). ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may God be pleased with them both) used to say: "Do not be the first to enter the market nor the last to leave it, for therein the devil has laid his eggs and hatched his young."

It is related from Muʿādh ibn Jabal and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that Iblīs says to his offspring, Zalanbūr: "Go with your battalions and come to the people of the markets; embellish for them lying, swearing, deception, trickery, and treachery; and be with the first to enter and the last to leave them." In the report: "The worst of places are the markets, and the worst of their people are the first to enter and the last to leave them" (2).

The completion of this caution is that he watch over the time of his sufficiency: when he has obtained the sufficiency of his time, he departs and occupies himself with the trade of the Hereafter. Thus were the righteous among the Salaf. Among them was one who, when he profited a small coin (dāniq), departed, content with it. Ḥammād ibn Salamah used to sell silk (khazz) in a basket before him; when he profited two grains, he would lift his basket and depart.

Ibrāhīm ibn Bashshār said: "I said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham (may God have mercy on him): 'Today I am commanded to work in clay.' He said: 'O son of Bashshār, you are a seeker and one sought. He who seeks you cannot be escaped, and you seek what has already been sufficed for you. Have you not seen the eager one deprived, and the weak one provided for?' I said: 'I have a dāniq with the grocer.' He said: 'It is grievous to me that you possess a dāniq and yet seek work.'" Among them was one who departed after the noon prayer, and among them one who departed after the afternoon prayer; and among them one who worked only one or two days a week, and they were content with that.

**The Sixth:** That he not be content with avoiding the unlawful (ḥarām), but rather guard against the loci of ambiguities (shubuhāt) and the places of suspicion (mawāḍiʿ al-rayb). Let him not look to legal opinions (fatāwā), but rather consult his heart: if he finds in it a prickling unease (ḥazāzah), let him avoid it. If a commodity is brought to him and its matter troubles him, let him ask about it until he knows it; otherwise he consumes the ambiguous. A milk was brought to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and he said: "Where did you get this?" They said: "From the sheep." He said: "And where did you get this sheep?" It was said: "From such-and-such a place." Then he drank from it, and said: "We, the company of prophets, have been commanded not to eat except what is good (ṭayyib), and not to act except righteously" (3). And he said: "God Most High commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: {«O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you»} (al-Baqarah 2:172)" (4). Muslim related it from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah (5). The ḥadīth that he would not ask about everything brought to him was related by Aḥmad from the ḥadīth of Jābir: that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his Companions passed by a woman who slaughtered a sheep for them—the ḥadīth. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) took a morsel but could not swallow it, and said: "This is a sheep slaughtered without the permission of its owners"—the ḥadīth. And from him, from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah: "When food was brought to him from other than his own family, he would ask about it"—the ḥadīth. Their chains are sound. In this [we learn] that he would not ask about what was brought from his own family. And God knows best.

The obligatory matter is that the merchant look to whom he deals with: anyone attributed to injustice (ẓulm), treachery (khiyānah), theft, or usury—he should not deal with him. Likewise, the soldiers and the tyrants (ẓalamah)—he should not deal with them at all, nor with their companions and helpers, because he thereby aids them in injustice.

It is related of a man that he undertook the construction of a wall for one of the frontier outposts (thughūr). He said: "Something of that fell into my heart, even though that work was among the good deeds—nay, among the obligations of Islam—but the commander who undertook it in his district was among the tyrants." He said: "I asked Sufyān (may God be pleased with him) (Page V02P086) about it, and he said: 'Do not be a helper to them in little or much.' I said: 'This is a wall in the path of God for the Muslims.' He said: 'Yes, but the least that enters upon you is that you love their survival so that they pay you your wage—and thus you have loved the survival of one who disobeys God.'"

It has come in the report: "Whoever prays for the survival of a tyrant has loved that God be disobeyed in His earth" (1). In the ḥadīth: "God is angered when a wicked person (fāsiq) is praised" (2). In another ḥadīth: "Whoever honors a wicked person has aided in the demolition of Islam" (3).

Sufyān entered upon al-Mahdī, who had in his hand a white scroll, and he said: "O Sufyān, give me the inkwell so that I may write." He said: "Tell me what you will write; if it is the truth, I will give it to you." Some commander sought from one of the scholars imprisoned with him that he hand him clay to seal a letter with. He said: "Hand me the letter first, so that I may see what is in it." Thus were they cautious about aiding the tyrants. And dealing with them is the most severe kind of aid; the people of religion ought to avoid it as long as they find a way to do so.

In sum, people ought to be divided for him into those he deals with and those he does not. Let those he deals with be fewer than those he does not, in this age. Some of them said: "There came upon people a time when a man would enter the market and say: 'Whom do you see for me to deal with among the people?' It would be said to him: 'Deal with whomever you wish.' Then came another time when they would say: 'Deal with whomever you wish, except so-and-so and so-and-so.' Then came another time when it was said: 'Do not deal with anyone except so-and-so and so-and-so.' And I fear that a time will come when this too will pass away." It is as though what he feared had already come to be—"Truly we belong to God, and to Him we return."

**The Seventh:** He ought to watch over all the channels of his dealings with each one of those he deals with, for he is watched and reckoned. Let him prepare the answer for the Day of Reckoning and Punishment for every deed and every word: "Why did I do this, and for what reason?" For it is said that the merchant will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection with every man to whom he sold something—a stop—and he will be reckoned for each one. Thus he is reckoned according to the number of those he dealt with.

Some of them said: "I saw one of the merchants in a dream and said: 'What has God done with you?' He said: 'Fifty thousand scrolls were spread out for me.' I said: 'Are all these sins?' He said: 'These are the dealings with people, according to the number of every person I dealt with in this world—for every person a separate scroll, concerning what was between me and him from the beginning of the dealing to its end.'"

This, then, is what is incumbent upon the earner in his work of justice (al-ʿadl), beneficence (al-iḥsān), and compassion for religion. If he confines himself to justice, he is among the righteous (al-ṣāliḥīn); if he adds beneficence thereto, he is among the near ones (al-muqarrabīn); and if he observes, along with that, the functions of religion as mentioned in the fifth chapter, he is among the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn). And God knows best what is correct.

The Book of Earning and Livelihood is completed, by the praise of God and His grace. (Page V02P087)

chapters.title_en: The Book of the Lawful and the Unlawful — Section 216: Opening Discourse on the Virtue of the Lawful and the Blame of the Unlawful
chapters.arabic_text:
### || كتاب الحلال والحرام وهو الكتاب الرابع من ربع العادات من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي خلق الإنسان من طين لازب وصلصال ثم ركب صورته في أحسن
تقويم وأتم اعتدال ثم غذاه في أول نشوه بلبن استصفاه من بين فرث ودم سائغا
كالماء الزلال ثم حماه بما آتاه من طيبات الرزق عن دواعي الضعف والانحلال
ثم قيد شهوته المعادية له عن السطوة والصيال وقهرها بما افترضه عليه من طلب
القوت الحلال وهزم بكسرها جند الشيطان المتشمر للإضلال ولقد كان يجري من
ابن آدم مجرى الدم السيال فضيق عليه عزة الحلال المجرى والمجال إذ كان لا
يبذرقه إلى أعماق العروق إلا الشهوة الماثلة إلى الغلبة والاسترسال فبقي
لما زمت بزمام الحلال خائبا خاسرا ما له من ناصر ولا وال

### |||| فضيلة الحلال ومذمة الحرام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ل-ب (ṭ-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Seeking, pursuing, demanding with earnestness and intent
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The quest for sustenance as an act of obedience when directed toward the lawful (ḥalāl)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of pursuit; metaphorical sense of spiritual striving (ṭalab al-ḥalāl as jihād of the soul)
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate emphasis (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — "the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear" establishes a permanent, unalterable state.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to Allah, who created man from clinging clay and molded pottery, then fashioned his form in the most excellent proportion and most complete balance. Then He nourished him in his earliest growth with milk which He extracted from between excrement and blood — palatable and pure, like fresh flowing water. Then He protected him, through what He granted him of the goodly provisions, from the incitements of weakness and dissolution. Then He restrained his appetite — which is his enemy — from assault and aggression, and subdued it by what He made obligatory upon him: the pursuit of lawful sustenance. By breaking this appetite, He routed the hosts of Satan who girds himself for misguidance. Indeed, Satan used to course through the son of Adam like flowing blood; so the might of the lawful narrowed his passage and his domain — for nothing could inject him into the depths of the veins except the desire that inclines toward dominance and unchecked release. Thus, when this desire was bridled with the rein of the lawful, Satan remained disappointed and lost, having neither helper nor protector.

And blessings be upon Muhammad, the guide from misguidance, and upon his family — the best of families — with abundant peace.

To proceed: The Prophet ﷺ said: «طلب الحلال فريضة على كل مسلم» — "The pursuit of the lawful is an obligation upon every Muslim" — narrated by Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him. This obligation, among all other obligations, is the most resistant to comprehension by the intellects, and the heaviest upon the bodily members in actual practice. For this reason, it has become utterly effaced — both as knowledge and as practice. The obscurity of its knowledge became the cause of the effacement of its practice, for the ignorant assumed that the lawful is nonexistent, that the path to reaching it is blocked, and that nothing remains of the goodly things except fresh water and grass growing in dead lands. As for everything else, they claimed, transgressing hands have corrupted it and corrupt transactions have spoiled it. And when contentment with grass and vegetation became impossible, they saw no course except to plunge broadly into the unlawful. So they abandoned this pivot of the religion entirely, and did not perceive any distinction or separation between different kinds of wealth. Far from it! Far from it! For the lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are ambiguous matters. And these three remain perpetually conjoined, however circumstances may shift and turn.

And since this was an innovation (bidʿah) whose harm pervaded the religion and whose sparks spread among creation, it became incumbent to unveil its corruption by guiding toward the apprehension of the distinction between the lawful, the unlawful, and the ambiguous — in a manner of verification and clarification. Nor does the constriction [of circumstances] remove it from the realm of possibility.

We shall now elucidate this in seven chapters:

Chapter One: On the virtue of seeking the lawful, the blame of the unlawful, the degrees of the lawful and the unlawful.

Chapter Two: On the ranks of ambiguities (shubuhāt), their sources, and distinguishing them from the lawful and the unlawful.

Chapter Three: On inquiry, questioning, rushing in, and negligence — and their loci of occurrence regarding the lawful and the unlawful.

Chapter Four: On how the penitent exits from financial injustices.

Chapter Five: On the stipends of rulers and their gifts — what is permissible thereof and what is forbidden.

Chapter Six: On entering upon rulers and mixing with them.

Chapter Seven: On miscellaneous questions. [Page V02P088]

### ||| Chapter One: On the Virtue of the Lawful, the Blame of the Unlawful, and the Exposition of the Categories of the Lawful and Its Degrees, and the Categories of the Unlawful and the Degrees of Scrupulousness (waraʿ) Therein

### |||| The Virtue of the Lawful and the Blame of the Unlawful

chapters.title_en: On the Virtue of Lawful Sustenance (Ṭalab al-Ḥalāl) and the Severity of the Unlawful (Ḥarām)
chapters.arabic_text:
قال الله تعالى كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا أمر بالأكل من الطيبات قبل
العمل
وقيل إن المراد به الحلال
وقال تعالى ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون
أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية
وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن
كنتم مؤمنين {ثم قال} فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله {ثم قال}
وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم {ثم قال} ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها
خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار
والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
وروى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال طلب
الحلال فريضة على كل مسلم ولما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب العلم فريضة على
كل مسلم (1)
قال بعض العلماء أراد به طلب علم الحلال والحرام وجعل المراد بالحديثين
واحدا
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من سعى على عياله من حله فهو كالمجاهد في سبيل
الله ومن طلب الدنيا حلالا في عفاف كان في درجة الشهداء (2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أكل الحلال أربعين يوما نور الله قلبه وأجرى
ينابيع الحكمة من قلبه على لسانه (3)
وفي رواية زهده الله في الدنيا وروي أن سعدا سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم أن يسأل الله تعالى أن يجعله مجاب  الدعوة فقال له أطب طعمتك تستجب
دعوتك (4)
ولما ذكر صلى الله عليه وسلم الحريص على الدنيا قال رب أشعث أغبر مشرد في
الأسفار مطعمه حرام وملبسه حرام وغذي بالحرام يرفع يديه فيقول يا رب يا رب
فأنى يستجاب لذلك (5)
وفي حديث ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله ملكا على بيت
المقدس ينادي كل ليلة من أكل حراما لم يقبل منه صرف ولا عدل (6)
فقيل الصرف النافلة والعدل الفريضة
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من اشترى ثوبا PageV02P089
بعشرة دراهم وفي ثمنه درهم حرام لم يقبل الله صلاته ما دام عليه منه شيء
(1)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كل لحم نبت من حرام فالنار أولى به (2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لم يبال من أين اكتسب المال لم يبال الله من
أين أدخله النار (3)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم العبادة عشرة أجزاء تسعة منها في طلب الحلال (4)
روي هذا مرفوعا وموقوفا على بعض الصحابة أيضا
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أمسى وانيا من طلب الحلال بات مغفورا له
وأصبح والله عنه راض (5)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أصاب مالا من مأثم فوصل به رحما أو تصدق به
أو أنفقه في سبيل الله جمع الله ذلك جميعا ثم قذفه في النار (6)
وقال عليه السلام خير دينكم الورع (7)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لقي الله ورعا أعطاه الله ثواب الإسلام كله
(8)
ويروى أن الله تعالى قال في بعض كتبه وأما الورعون فأنا أستحي أن أحاسبهم
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم درهم من ربا أشد عند الله من ثلاثين زنية في
الإسلام (9)
وفي حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه المعدة حوض البدن والعروق إليها واردة
فإذا صحت المعدة صدرت العروق بالصحة وإذا سقمت صدرت بالسقم (10)
ومثل الطعمة من الدين مثل الأساس من البنيان فإذا ثبت الأساس وقوي استقام
البنيان وارتفع وإذا ضعف الأساس واعوج انهار البنيان ووقع
وقال الله عز وجل أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من  الله الآية
وفي الحديث من اكتسب مالا من حرام فإن تصدق به لم يقبل منه وإن تركه
وراءه كان زاده إلى النار (11)
وقد ذكرنا جملة من الأخبار في كتاب آداب الكسب تكشف عن فضيلة الكسب
الحلال
وأما الآثار فقد ورد أن الصديق رضي الله عنه شرب لبنا من كسب عبده ثم سأل
عبده فقال تكهنت لقوم فأعطوني فأدخل أصابعه في فيه وجعل يقيء حتى ظننت أن
نفسه ستخرج ثم قال اللهم إني أعتذر إليك مما حملت العروق وخالط الأمعاء
(12)
وفي بعض الأخبار أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبر بذلك فقال أو علمتم
أن الصديق PageV02P090
لا يدخل جوفه إلا طيبا وكذلك شرب عمر رضي الله عنه من لبن إبل الصدقة
غلطا فأدخل إصبعه وتقيأ وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها إنكم لتغفلون عن أفضل
العبادة هو الورع وقال عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنه لو صليتم حتى تكونوا
كالحنايا وصمتم حتى تكونوا كالأوتار لم يقبل ذلك منكم إلا بورع حاجز
وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله ما أدرك من أدرك إلا من كان يعقل ما يدخل
جوفه
وقال الفضيل من عرف ما يدخل جوفه كتبه الله صديقا فانظر عند من تفطر يا
مسكين وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله لم لا تشرب من ماء زمزم فقال لو كان
لي دلو شربت منه
وقال سفيان الثوري رضي الله عنه من أنفق من الحرام في طاعة الله كان كمن
طهر الثوب النجس بالبول والثوب النجس لا يطهره إلا الماء والذنب لا يكفره
إلا الحلال
وقال يحيى بن معاذ الطاعة خزانة من خزائن الله إلا أن مفتاحها الدعاء
وأسنانه لقم الحلال
وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يقبل الله صلاة امرىء في جوفه حرام وقال
سهل التستري لا يبلغ العبد حقيقة الإيمان حتى يكون فيه أربع خصال أداء
الفرائض بالسنة وأكل الحلال بالورع واجتناب النهي من الظاهر والباطن والصبر
على ذلك إلى الموت
وقال من أحب أن يكاشف بآيات الصديقين فلا يأكل إلا  حلالا ولا يعمل إلا في
سنة أو ضرورة
ويقال من أكل الشبهة أربعين يوما أظلم قلبه وهو تأويل قوله تعالى {كلا بل
ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون} وقال ابن المبارك رد درهم من شبهة أحب إلي
من أن أتصدق بمائة ألف درهم ومائة ألف ومائة ألف حتى بلغ إلى ستمائة ألف
وقال بعض السلف إن العبد يأكل أكله فيتقلب قلبه فينغل كما ينغل الأديم
ولا يعود إلى حاله أبدا
وقال سهل رضي الله عنه من أكل الحرام عصت جوارحه شاء أم أبى علم أو لم
يعلم
ومن كانت طعمته حلالا أطاعته جوارحه ووفقت للخيرات وقال بعض السلف إن أول
لقمة يأكلها العبد من حلال يغفر له ما سلف من ذنوبه ومن أقام نفسه مقام ذل
في طلب الحلال تساقطت عنه ذنوبه كتساقط ورق الشجر
وروي في آثار السلف أن الواعظ كان إذا جلس للناس قال العلماء تفقدوا منه
ثلاثا فإن كان معتقدا لبدعة فلا تجالسوه فإنه عن لسان الشيطان ينطق وإن كان
سيء الطعمة فعن الهوى ينطق فإن لم يكن مكين العقل فإنه يفسد بكلامه أكثر
مما يصلح فلا تجالسوه
وفي الأخبار المشهورة عن على عليه السلام وغيره إن الدنيا حلالها حساب
وحرامها عذاب
وزاد آخرون وشبهتها عتاب
وروي أن بعض الصالحين دفع طعاما إلى بعض الأبدال فلم يأكل فسأله عن ذلك
فقال نحن لا نأكل إلا حلالا فلذلك تستقيم قلوبنا ويدوم حالنا ونكاشف
الملكوت ونشاهد الآخرة ولو أكلنا مما تأكلون ثلاثة أيام لما رجعنا إلى شيء
من علم اليقين ولذهب الخوف والمشاهدة من قلوبنا فقال له الرجل فإني أصوم
الدهر وأختم القرآن في كل شهر ثلاثين مرة فقال له البدل هذه الشربة التي
رأيتني شربتها من الليل أحب إلى من ثلاثين ختمة في ثلثمائة ركعة من أعمالك
وكانت شربته من لبن ظبية وحشية
وقد كان بين أحمد بن حنبل ويحيى بن معين صحبة طويلة فهجره أحمد إذ سمعه
يقول إني لا أسأل أحدا شيئا ولو أعطاني الشيطان شيئا  لأكلته حتى اعتذر يحيى
وقال كنت أمزح فقال تمزح بالدين أما علمت أن الأكل من الدين قدمه الله
تعالى على العمل الصالح فقال {كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا} وفي الخبر
أنه مكتوب في التوراة من لم يبال من أين مطعمه لم يبال الله من أي أبواب
النيران أدخله وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه لم يأكل بعد قد قتل عثمان ونهب
الدار طعاما إلا مختوما حذرا من الشبهة
واجتمع الفضيل بن عياض وابن عيينة وابن المبارك عند وهيب بن الورد بمكة
فذكروا الرطب فقال وهيب هو من أحب الطعام إلي إلا أني لا آكله لاختلاط رطب
مكة ببساتين زبيدة وغيرها فقال له
PageV02P091
ابن المبارك إن نظرت في مثل هذا ضاق عليك الخبز
قال وما سببه قال إن أصول الضياع قد اختلط بالصوافي فغشي على وهيب فقال
سفيان قتلت الرجل فقال ابن المبارك ما أردت إلا أن أهون عليه فلما أفاق قال
لله على أن لا آكل خبزا أبدا حتى ألقاه
قال فكان يشرب اللبن قال فأتته أمه بلبن فسألها فقالت هو من شاة بني فلان
فسأل عن ثمنها وأنه من أين كان لهم فذكرت فلما أدناه من فيه قال بقي أنها
من أين كانت ترعى فسكتت فلم يشرب لأنها كانت ترعى من موضع فيه حق للمسلمين
فقالت أمه اشرب فإن الله يغفر لك فقال ما أحب أن يغفر لي وقد شربته فأنال
مغفرته بمعصيته
وكان بشر الحافي رحمه الله من الورعين فقيل له من أين تأكل فقال من حيث
تأكلون ولكن ليس من يأكل وهو يبكي كمن يأكل وهو يضحك
وقال يد أقصر من يد ولقمة أصغر من لقمة وهكذا كانوا يحترزون من الشبهات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Food, sustenance, that which is ingested; the act of eating and its substance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The physical intake that directly nourishes the body, which in turn determines the spiritual state of the heart; the Quranic command «كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ» links bodily nourishment to righteous action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical eating; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual nourishment and the state of the soul, as the heart is said to be "fed" by what enters the belly.
- Root: و-ر-ع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be cautious, to abstain, to hold back from what is doubtful or forbidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The highest degree of piety (taqwā) in action—scrupulous avoidance of the unlawful (ḥarām) and the ambiguous (shubhah), which is the foundation of accepted deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical restraint; metaphorical for the heart's vigilance, as the "wariness" (waraʿ) is the internal guard against spiritual corruption.
- Root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To earn, to acquire, to seek provision through effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The acquisition of wealth and sustenance, which is either praiseworthy (ḥalāl) or blameworthy (ḥarām), and which directly impacts the validity of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for economic activity; metaphorical for the earning of spiritual reward or punishment.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Emphasis (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In the verse «فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا فَأْذَنُوا بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ», the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are structured to emphasize the severity of the consequence, showing that the unlawful eater is in a state of war with God.
chapters.translation:
I say: God Most High said: «Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds» {«كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا»} — He commanded eating from the good things before [mentioning] the deed. And it is said that what is meant by this is the lawful (al-ḥalāl). And He said Most High: «And do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood» {«وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ»}. And He said Most High: «Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly...» — the verse. And He said Most High: «O you who believe, fear God and give up what remains of usury (ribā), if you are believers» {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَذَرُوا مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ»}. Then He said: «And if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger» {«فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا فَأْذَنُوا بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ»}. Then He said: «And if you repent, then you shall have your principal sums» {«وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ»}. Then He said: «And whoever returns [to usury], then those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever» {«وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ»}. He made the consumer of usury, at the beginning of the matter, one who is notified of waging war against God, and at its end, one who is exposed to the Fire. And the verses concerning the lawful and the unlawful are beyond counting.

And Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he said: "Seeking the lawful is an obligation upon every Muslim." And when he, peace be upon him, said: "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim," some scholars said: He meant by it seeking the knowledge of the lawful and the unlawful, and they made the meaning of the two hadiths one.

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever strives for his family from what is lawful, he is like a warrior (mujāhid) in the path of God. And whoever seeks the world lawfully, in chastity, he will be in the rank of the martyrs."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever eats lawful food for forty days, God illuminates his heart and causes springs of wisdom to flow from his heart upon his tongue." And in another narration: "God makes him abstinent (zāhid) in the world."

And it is narrated that Saʿd asked the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, to ask God Most High to make him one whose supplication is answered. He said to him: "Make your food lawful, and your supplication will be answered."

And when he, peace be upon him, mentioned the one eager for the world, he said: "Perhaps a disheveled, dusty man, driven away in journeys, whose food is unlawful and whose clothing is unlawful, and who is nourished with the unlawful, raises his hands and says: 'O Lord, O Lord!' — so how can that be answered for him?"

And in the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Indeed, God has an angel at the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis) who calls out every night: 'Whoever eats the unlawful, neither supererogatory (ṣarf) nor obligatory (ʿadl) deed will be accepted from him.'" And it was said: al-ṣarf is the supererogatory act, and al-ʿadl is the obligatory act.

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever buys a garment for ten dirhams, and in its price there is one unlawful dirham, God will not accept his prayer as long as any of it remains upon him."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Every flesh that grows from the unlawful, the Fire is more deserving of it."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever does not care from where he earns wealth, God will not care from which gate of the Fire He enters him."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Worship is ten parts; nine of them are in seeking the lawful." This is narrated as raised (marfūʿ) and also as stopped (mawqūf) on some of the Companions.

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever reaches the evening weary from seeking the lawful, he spends the night forgiven, and wakes in the morning with God pleased with him."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever obtains wealth from a sinful source, and then joins family ties with it, or gives charity from it, or spends it in the path of God, God will gather all of that together and then cast it into the Fire."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "The best of your religion is scrupulous wariness (al-waraʿ)."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever meets God with wariness, God will give him the reward of all of Islam."

And it is narrated that God Most High said in some of His books: "As for the wary (al-waraʿūn), I am ashamed to call them to account."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "A dirham from usury is more severe with God than thirty acts of fornication in Islam."

And in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him: "The stomach is the basin of the body, and the veins flow into it. When the stomach is sound, the veins issue forth with soundness; and when it is sick, they issue forth with sickness."

And the likeness of food in religion is like the foundation in a building: when the foundation is firm and strong, the building stands upright and rises; and when the foundation is weak and crooked, the building collapses and falls. And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: «Is he who founds his building upon piety from God...» — the verse {«أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَى تَقْوَى مِنَ اللَّهِ»}.

And in the hadith: "Whoever earns wealth from the unlawful, and then gives charity from it, it will not be accepted from him; and if he leaves it behind him, it will be his provision to the Fire."

We have already mentioned a number of reports in the Book of the Etiquettes of Earning (Kitāb Ādāb al-Kasb) that reveal the virtue of lawful earning.

As for the sayings of the Companions and Successors (al-āthār), it is narrated that al-Ṣiddīq (Abū Bakr), may God be pleased with him, drank milk from the earning of his slave, then asked his slave, who said: "I practiced divination for a people, and they gave me [this]." So he put his fingers into his mouth and began to vomit until I thought his soul would come out. Then he said: "O God, I seek Your excuse for what the veins have carried and what has mixed with the intestines."

And in some reports, he, peace be upon him, was informed of that and said: "Did you not know that al-Ṣiddīq does not let anything enter his belly except what is pure?"

Likewise, ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, drank from the milk of the charity camels by mistake, so he put his finger in and vomited.

And ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "You are indeed heedless of the best of worship — it is wariness (al-waraʿ)."

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "If you prayed until you became like bows [bent in prayer], and fasted until you became like arrows [thin], none of that would be accepted from you except with a wariness that restrains [you from the unlawful]."

And Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, may God have mercy on him, said: "Those who attained [the truth] only attained it by being mindful of what enters their bellies."

And al-Fuḍayl said: "Whoever knows what enters his belly, God writes him as a ṣiddīq (truthful one). So consider, O poor one, with whom you break your fast."

And it was said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, may God have mercy on him: "Why do you not drink from the water of Zamzam?" He said: "If I had a bucket, I would drink from it."

And Sufyān al-Thawrī, may God be pleased with him, said: "Whoever spends from the unlawful in obedience to God is like one who cleanses a filthy garment with urine — and a filthy garment is only cleansed with water, and a sin is only expiated with the lawful."

And Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "Obedience is a treasure from the treasures of God, except that its key is supplication, and its teeth are lawful morsels."

And Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: "God does not accept the prayer of a man in whose belly there is the unlawful."

And Sahl al-Tustarī said: "A servant does not reach the reality of faith until he possesses four qualities: performing the obligatory acts according to the Sunnah, eating the lawful with wariness, avoiding what is forbidden outwardly and inwardly, and being patient upon that until death."

And he said: "Whoever loves to be unveiled with the signs of the ṣiddīqīn, let him eat nothing but the lawful, and do nothing but in accordance with the Sunnah or necessity."

And it is said: "Whoever eats the ambiguous (shubhah) for forty days, his heart is darkened." And this is the interpretation of His saying Most High: «No! Rather, the stain has covered their hearts from what they earned» {«كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ»}.

And Ibn al-Mubārak said: "Returning one dirham of the ambiguous is more beloved to me than giving in charity one hundred thousand dirhams, and one hundred thousand, and one hundred thousand" — until he reached six hundred thousand.

And some of the Salaf said: "A servant eats a morsel, and his heart turns over and becomes tainted just as leather becomes tainted, and it never returns to its former state."

And Sahl, may God be pleased with him, said: "Whoever eats the unlawful, his limbs disobey him, whether he wills or not, whether he knows or does not know. And whoever's food is lawful, his limbs obey him and are guided to good deeds."

And some of the Salaf said: "Indeed, the first lawful morsel a servant eats, his past sins are forgiven him. And whoever places himself in a position of humility in seeking the lawful, his sins fall away from him like the falling of leaves from a tree."

And it is narrated in the reports of the Salaf that the preacher, when he sat before the people, would say: "The scholars — examine three things in him: if he holds a heretical belief (bidʿah), do not sit with him, for he speaks with the tongue of Satan; and if his food is bad, he speaks from caprice (hawā); and if he is not firm in intellect, he corrupts with his speech more than he rectifies, so do not sit with him."

And in the well-known reports from ʿAlī, peace be upon him, and others: "The world — its lawful is [subject to] accounting, and its unlawful is [subject to] punishment." And others added: "And its ambiguous is [subject to] reproach."

And it is narrated that some of the righteous gave food to one of the Abdāl (substitutes), and he did not eat. So he asked him about that, and he said: "We eat nothing but the lawful, and therefore our hearts remain upright, our state endures, we are unveiled to the Kingdom (al-Malakūt), and we witness the Hereafter. If we ate what you eat for three days, we would not return to any of the knowledge of certainty, and fear and witnessing would depart from our hearts." The man said to him: "But I fast perpetually and complete the Quran thirty times each month." The Badal said to him: "This drink that you saw me drink at night is more beloved to me than thirty completions of the Quran in three hundred units of prayer from your deeds." And his drink was from the milk of a wild gazelle.

And there was a long companionship between Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Yaḥyā ibn Muʿīn, and Aḥmad abandoned him when he heard him say: "I do not ask anyone for anything, and even if Satan gave me something, I would eat it." Until Yaḥyā apologized and said: "I was joking." He said: "Do you joke about religion? Do you not know that eating is part of religion, which God Most High placed before righteous deeds, saying: «Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds» {«كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا»}?"

And in the report, it is written in the Torah: "Whoever does not care from where his food comes, God will not care from which of the gates of the Fire He enters him."

And it is narrated from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, that after ʿUthmān was killed and the house was plundered, he did not eat any food except what was sealed, out of caution against the ambiguous (shubhah).

And al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, Ibn ʿUyaynah, and Ibn al-Mubārak gathered at Wahīb ibn al-Ward in Mecca, and they mentioned fresh dates (ruṭab). Wahīb said: "It is the most beloved food to me, except that I do not eat it because of the mixing of Mecca's dates with the orchards of Zubaydah and others." Ibn al-Mubārak said to him: "If you look into such matters, bread will become too narrow for you." He said: "And what is its cause?" He said: "The origins of the estates have become mixed with the conquered lands (al-ṣawāfī)." So Wahīb fainted. Sufyān said: "You have killed the man." Ibn al-Mubārak said: "I only intended to make it easier for him." When he regained consciousness, he said: "God has upon me that I will never eat bread again until I meet Him." He said: "So he used to drink milk." He said: "His mother brought him milk, and he asked her about it. She said: 'It is from the sheep of so-and-so's family.' He asked about its price and from where they had it, and she mentioned [the source]. When he brought it near his mouth, he said: 'It remains that from where did it graze?' She was silent, so he did not drink, because it had grazed from a place in which there was a right of the Muslims. His mother said: 'Drink, for God will forgive you.' He said: 'I would not love that He forgive me while I have drunk it, attaining His forgiveness through His disobedience.'"

And Bishr al-Ḥāfī, may God have mercy on him, was among the wary. It was said to him: "From where do you eat?" He said: "From where you eat. But the one who eats while weeping is not like the one who eats while laughing." And he said: "A hand shorter than a hand, and a morsel smaller than a morsel." And thus they were cautious against the ambiguous (shubhāt).

chapters.title_en: The Categories of the Lawful and Its Entrances
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| أصناف الحلال ومداخله

اعلم أن تفصيل الحلال والحرام إنما يتولى بيانه كتب الفقه ويستغني المريد
عن تطويله بأن يكون له طعمة معينة يعرف بالفتوى حلها لا يأكل من غيرها فأما
من يتوسع في الأكل من وجوه متفرقة فيفتقر إلى علم الحلال والحرام كله كما
فصلناه في  كتب الفقه
ونحن الآن نشير إلى مجامعه في سياق تقسيم وهو أن المال إنما يحرم إما
لمعنى في عينه أو لخلل في جهة اكتسابه

### ||||| القسم الأول الحرام لصفة في عينه كالخمر والخنزير وغيرهما

وتفصيله أن الأعيان المأكولة على وجه الأرض لا تعدو ثلاثة أقسام فإنها
إما أن تكون من المعادن كالملح والطين وغيرهما أو من النبات أو من
الحيوانات
أما المعادن فهي أجزاء الأرض وجميع ما يخرج منها فلا يحرم أكله إلا من
حيث أنه يضر بالآكل وفي بعضها ما يجري مجرى السم والخبز لو كان مضرا لحرم
أكله والطين الذي يعتاد أكله لا يحرم إلا من حيث الضرر
وفائدة قولنا إنه لا يحرم مع أنه لا يؤكل أنه لو وقع شيء منها في مرقة أو
طعام مائع لم يصر به محرما
وأما النبات فلا يحرم منه إلا ما يزيل العقل أو يزيل الحياة أو الصحة
فمزيل العقل البنج والخمر وسائر المسكرات ومزيل الحياة السموم ومزيل الصحة
الأدوية في غير وقتها وكأن مجموع هذا يرجع إلى الضرر إلا الخمر والمسكرات
فإن الذي لا يسكر منها أيضا حرام مع قلته لعينه ولصفته وهي الشدة المطربة
وأما السم فإذا خرج عن كونه مضرا لقلته أو لعجنه بغيره فلا يحرم
وأما الحيوانات فتنقسم إلى ما يؤكل وإلى ما لا يؤكل وتفصيله في كتاب
الأطعمة والنظر يطول في تفصيله لا سيما في الطيور الغريبة وحيوانات البر
والبحر وما يحل أكله منها فإنما يحل إذا ذبح ذبحا شرعيا روعي فيه شروط
الذابح والآلة والذبح وذلك مذكور في
كتاب الصيد والذبائح وما لم يذبح ذبحا شرعيا أو مات فهو حرام ولا يحل
إلا ميتتان السمك والجراد وفي معناهما ما يستحيل من الأطعمة كدود التفاح
والخل والجبن فإن الاحتراز منهما غير ممكن فأما إذا أفردت وأكلت فحكمها حكم
الذباب والخنفساء والعقرب وكل ما ليس له نفس سائلة لا سبب في تحريمها إلا
الاستقذار ولو لم يكن لكان لا يكره فإن وجد شخص لا يستقذره لم يلتفت إلى
خصوص طبعه فإنه التحق بالخبائث لعموم الاستقذار فيكره أكله كما لو جمع
المخاط وشربه كره
PageV02P092
ذلك وليست الكراهة لنجاستها فإن الصحيح أنها لا تنجس بالموت إذ أمر رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يمقل الذباب في الطعام إذا وقع فيه (1)
وربما يكون حارا ويكون ذلك سبب موته ولم تهرت نملة أو ذبابة في قدر لم
يجب إراقتها إذ المستقذر هو جرمه إذا بقي له جرم ولم ينجس حتى يحرم
بالنجاسة وهذا يدل على أن تحريمه للاستقذار ولذلك نقول لو وقع جزء من آدمي
ميت في قدر ولو وزن دانق حرم الكل لا لنجاسته فإن الصحيح أن الآدمي لا ينجس
بالموت ولكن لأن أكله محرم احتراما لا استقذارا
وأما الحيوانات المأكولة إذا ذبحت بشرط الشرع فلا تحل جميع أجزائها بل
يحرم منها الدم والفرث وكل ما يقضى بنجاسته منها بل تناول النجاسة مطلقا
محرم ولكن ليس في الأعيان شيء محرم نجس إلا من الحيوانات
وأما من النبات فالمسكرات فقط دون ما يزيل العقل ولا يسكر كالبنج فإن
نجاسة المسكر تغليظ للذجر عنه لكونه في مظنة التشوف ومهما وقعت قطرة من
النجاسة أو جزء من نجاسة جامدة في مرقة أو طعام أو دهن حرم أكل جميعه ولا
يحرم الانتفاع به لغير الأكل فيجوز الاستصباح بالدهن النجس وكذا طلاء السفن
والحيوانات وغيرها فهذه مجامع ما يحرم لصفة في ذاته
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط ع م (ṭaʿima)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sustenance, food, that which is eaten; a means of livelihood
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Provision (rizq) as that by which one sustains the body's constitution
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for edible substance; metaphorical for any acquired benefit
- Root: ك س ب (kasaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Acquisition, earning, gaining by effort
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The voluntary act of obtaining something permissible or forbidden
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for manual gain; metaphorical for any mode of procurement
- Root: ض ر ر (ḍarra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Harm, injury, detriment to body or state
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): That which corrupts the soul or body, opposed to benefit (nafʿ)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical injury; metaphorical for spiritual ruin
- Root: ق ذ ر (qadhara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Filth, abomination, that which repels the sound nature
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The impure (khabīth) as that which the Law deems repugnant universally
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical uncleanness; metaphorical for moral repulsiveness
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Partitioning (taqsīm) — The division of the lawful and unlawful into exhaustive categories (ḥaṣr) governed by the particle "innamā" (only), requiring the predicate to be restricted to the enumerated branches.
chapters.translation:
I say: The detailed exposition of the lawful and the unlawful is undertaken solely by the books of jurisprudence (fiqh), and the seeker (murīd) is spared its prolixity by having a fixed sustenance (ṭuʿmah) whose lawfulness he knows through legal opinion (fatwā), eating from nothing other than it. As for one who expands his eating across manifold sources, he stands in need of the entire knowledge of the lawful and the unlawful, as we have detailed in the books of jurisprudence.

Now we shall indicate its comprehensive principles in the course of a division (taqsīm), namely: wealth is rendered unlawful either by a meaning in its very essence (ʿayn) or by a defect in the mode of its acquisition (kasb).

### The First Division: The Unlawful by Virtue of an Attribute in Its Essence, Such as Wine, Swine, and Others

Its detail is that the edible substances (aʿyān) upon the face of the earth do not exceed three categories: they are either from minerals (maʿādin), such as salt, clay, and the like; or from plants (nabāt); or from animals (ḥayawānāt).

As for minerals, they are parts of the earth and all that issues from it. Nothing of them is unlawful to eat except by virtue of its harming the eater. Among them are things that run the course of poison. Even bread, were it harmful, would be unlawful to eat. The clay that is customarily eaten is not unlawful except by virtue of harm.

The benefit of our saying that it is not unlawful, even though it is not eaten, is that if something of it falls into a broth or a liquid food, it does not thereby become unlawful.

As for plants, nothing is unlawful from them except that which removes the intellect, or removes life, or removes health. That which removes the intellect is henbane (banj), wine, and all intoxicants (muskirāt). That which removes life is poisons (sumūm). That which removes health is medicines taken outside their proper time. It is as though the totality of this reverts to harm, except wine and intoxicants—for even that which does not intoxicate from them is also unlawful, however little it be, by virtue of its essence and its attribute, namely, the exhilarating potency (al-shiddah al-muṭribah). As for poison, when it departs from being harmful—due to its scantiness or its admixture with something else—it is not unlawful.

As for animals, they divide into what is eaten and what is not eaten. Its detail is in the Book of Foods (Kitāb al-Aṭʿimah). The inquiry into its detail would be prolonged, especially regarding strange birds and the beasts of land and sea. What is lawful to eat from them is lawful only when slaughtered with a legal slaughter (dhakāh sharʿiyyah) in which the conditions of the slaughterer, the instrument, and the act of slaughter are observed—this is mentioned in the Book of Hunting and Slaughtered Animals (Kitāb al-Ṣayd wa al-Dhabāʾiḥ). What is not slaughtered legally, or dies [of itself], is unlawful. Nothing is lawful from carrion (maytah) except two: fish and locust. In their meaning are included foods that transform, such as the worms of apples, vinegar, and cheese—for guarding against them is not possible. But if they are isolated and eaten, their ruling is the ruling of the fly, the beetle, and the scorpion. Everything that has no flowing blood (nafs sāʾilah) has no cause for its unlawfulness except repugnance (istiqdhār). Were it not for that, it would not be disliked. If a person is found who does not find it repugnant, no heed is paid to his particular temperament, for it has joined the abominations (khabāʾith) by virtue of universal repugnance; thus its eating is disliked, just as if one gathered mucus and drank it—that would be disliked.

PageV02P092

That [dislike] is not due to its impurity (najāsah), for the correct view is that it does not become impure by death, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the fly be dipped into the food when it falls into it. It may be hot, and that may be the cause of its death. Nor has an ant or a fly that fell into a cooking pot necessitated the throwing away of its contents. For the repugnant thing is its body (jirm) when its body remains; it does not become impure so as to be unlawful by impurity. This indicates that its unlawfulness is for repugnance. Therefore we say: if a part of a dead human being fell into a pot—even weighing a dāniq—the whole becomes unlawful, not due to its impurity, for the correct view is that the human being does not become impure by death, but because eating him is unlawful out of reverence (iḥtirām), not repugnance.

As for edible animals, when slaughtered according to the condition of the Law, not all their parts are lawful. Rather, unlawful from them are the blood, the excrement (farth), and everything judged to be impure from them. Indeed, ingesting impurity absolutely is unlawful. But among the substances (aʿyān), there is nothing impure and unlawful except from animals.

As for plants, only intoxicants are [unlawful and impure], not that which removes the intellect without intoxicating, such as henbane. For the impurity of the intoxicant is an intensification of deterrence against it, because it stands in the position of being coveted. Whenever a drop of impurity, or a part of solid impurity, falls into a broth, food, or oil, eating all of it becomes unlawful. But using it for other than eating is not unlawful, so it is permissible to burn impure oil in lamps, and likewise to coat ships and animals with it. These, then, are the comprehensive principles of what is unlawful by virtue of an attribute in its essence.

chapters.title_en: The Second Division: What is Forbidden Due to a Defect in the Means of Establishing Possession
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||||| القسم الثاني ما يحرم لخلل في جهة إثبات اليد عليه

وفيه يتسع النظر فنقول أخذ المال إما أن يكون باختيار المالك أو بغير
اختياره فالذي يكون بغير اختياره كالإرث والذي يكون باختياره إما أن لا
يكون من مالك كنيل المعادن أو يكون من مالك والذي أخذ من مالك فإما أن يؤخذ
قهرا أو يؤخذ تراضيا والمأخوذ قهرا إما أن يكون لسقوط عصمة المالك كالغنائم
أو لاستحقاق الأخذ كزكاة الممتنعين والنفقات الواجبة عليهم والمأخوذ تراضيا
إما أن يؤخذ بعوض كالبيع والصداق والأجرة وإما أن يؤخذ بغير عوض كالهبة
والوصية فيحصل من هذا السياق ستة  أقسام
الأول ما يؤخذ من غير مالك كنيل المعادن وإحياء الموات والاصطياد
والاحتطاب والاستقاء من الأنهار والاحتشاش فهذا حلال بشرط أن لا يكون
المأخوذ مختصا بذي حرمة من الآدميين فإذا انفك من الاختصاصات ملكها آخذها
وتفصيل ذلك في كتاب إحياء الموات
الثاني المأخوذة قهرا ممن لا حرمة له وهو الفيء والغنيمة وسائر أموال
الكفار والمحاربين وذلك حلال للمسلمين إذا أخرجوا منها الخمس وقسموها بين
المستحقين بالعدل ولم يأخذوها من كافر له حرمة وأمان وعهد
وتفصيل هذه الشروط في كتاب السير من كتاب الفيء والغنيمة وكتاب الجزية
الثالث ما يؤخذ قهرا باستحقاق عند امتناع من وجب عليه فيؤخذ دون رضاه
وذلك حلال إذا تم سبب الاستحقاق وتم وصف المستحق الذي به استحقاقه واقتصر
على القدر المستحق واستوفاه ممن يملك الاستيفاء من قاض أو سلطان أو مستحق
وتفصيل ذلك في
كتاب تفريق الصدقات وكتاب الوقف وكتاب النفقات إذ فيها النظر في صفة
المستحقين للزكاة والوقف والنفقة وغيرها من الحقوق فإذا استوفيت شرائطها
كان المأخوذ حلالا
الرابع ما يؤخذ تراضيا بمعاوضة وذلك حلال إذا روعي شرط العوضين وشرط
العاقدين وشرط اللفظين أعني الإيجاب والقبول مع ما تعبد الشرع به من اجتناب
الشروط المفسدة
وبيان ذلك في كتاب البيع والسلم والإجارة والحوالة والضمان والقراض
والشركة والمساقاة والشفعة والصلح والخلع والكتابة والصداق PageV02P093
وسائر المعاوضات
الخامس ما يؤخذ عن رضا من غير عوض وهو حلال إذا روعي فيه شرط المعقود
عليه وشرط العاقدين وشرط العقد ولم يؤد إلى ضرر بوارث أو غيره وذلك مذكور
في كتاب الهبات والوصايا والصدقات
السادس
ما يحصل بغير اختيار كالميراث وهو حلال إذا كان الموروث قد اكتسب المال
من بعض الجهات الخمس على وجه حلال ثم كان ذلك بعد قضاء الدين وتنفيذ
الوصايا وتعديل القسمة بين الورثة وإخراج الزكاة والحج والكفارة إن كان
واجبا وذلك مذكور في كتاب الوصايا والفرائض فهذه مجامع مداخل الحلال
والحرام أومأنا إلى جملتها ليعلم المريد أنه إن كانت طعمته متفرقة لا من
