### ||| الباب الثاني فيما لا بد للمسافر من تعلمه من رخص السفر وأدلة القبلة والأوقات

اعلم أن المسافر يحتاج في أول سفره الى أن يتزود لدنياه ولآخرته
أما زاد الدنيا فالطعام والشراب وما يحتاج إليه من نفقة
فإن خرج متوكلا من غير زاد فلا بأس به إذا كان سفره في قافلة أو بين قرى
متصلة
وإن ركب البادية وحده أو مع قوم لا طعام معهم ولا شراب فإن كان ممن يصبر
على الجوع أسبوعا أو عشرا مثلا أو يقدر على أن يكتفي بالحشيش فله ذلك
وإن لم يكن له قوة الصبر على الجوع ولا القدرة على الاجتزاء بالحشيش
فخروجه منغير زاد معصية فإنه ألقى نفسه بيده إلى التهلكة ولهذا سر سيأتي في
كتاب التوكل PageV02P257
وليس معنى التوكل التباعد عن الأسباب بالكلية ولو كان كذلك لبطل التوكل
بطلب الدلو والحبل ونزع الماء من البئر ولوجب أن يصبر حتى يسخر الله له
ملكا أو شخصا آخر حتى يصب الماء في فيه
فإن كان حفظ الدلو والحبل لا يقدح في التوكل وهو آلة الوصول إلى المشروب
فحمل عين المطعوم والمشروب حيث لا ينتظر له وجود أولى بأن لا يقدح فيه
وستأتي حقيقة التوكل في موضعها فإنه يلتبس إلا على المحققين من علماء
الدين
وأما زاد الآخرة فهو العلم الذي يحتاج إليه في طهارته وصومه وصلاته
وعبادته فلا بد وأن يتزود منه إذ السفر تارة يخفف عنه أمورا فيحتاج الى
معرفة القدر الذي يخففه السفر كالقصر والجمع والفطر وتارة يشدد عليه أمورا
كان مستغنيا عنها في الحضر كالعلم بالقبلة وأوقات الصلوات فإنه في البلد
يكتفي بغيره من محاريب المساجد وأذان المؤذنين وفي السفر قد يحتاج الى أن
يتعرف بنفسه
فإذن ما يفتقر الى تعلمه ينقسم الى قسمين

### |||| القسم الأول العلم برخص السفر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-د (z-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Provision, sustenance stored for a journey; both literal food and metaphorical spiritual preparation
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Earthly provision (zād al-dunyā) vs. otherworldly provision (zād al-ākhirah) — the latter being knowledge (ʿilm) that secures salvation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for food/water; metaphorical extension to spiritual preparedness
- Root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To entrust, delegate, rely upon another
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawakkul — complete reliance on God while employing permissible means (asbāb); not abandonment of causality
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes ḥaqīqah (trusting God) from majāz (misinterpretation as fatalistic inaction)
- Root: ر-خ-ص (r-kh-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Leniency, concession, easing of a ruling
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal dispensations (rukhaṣ) granted by God for travelers — shortening prayer (qaṣr), combining prayers (jamʿ), breaking fast (fiṭr)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: softness/pliability; technical: jurisprudential easing of obligations
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — "If he goes out relying on God without provision, there is no harm" — the protasis sets a hypothetical condition, the apodosis delivers the legal verdict, requiring precise parsing of the particle "in" (if) as conditional, not temporal.
chapters.translation:
Know that the traveler, at the outset of his journey, stands in need of provisioning himself for both his worldly life and his afterlife.

As for the provision of this world — it is food, drink, and whatever expenditure he requires. If he sets out relying on God (mutawakkil) without provision, there is no blame upon him, provided his journey is within a caravan or amidst contiguous villages. But if he ventures into the open desert alone, or with a company having neither food nor drink with them — then if he is one who can endure hunger for a week or ten days, for instance, or is able to content himself with grazing herbs, then that is permissible for him. However, if he possesses neither the strength to endure hunger nor the capacity to subsist on herbs, then his setting out without provision is an act of disobedience — for he has cast himself with his own hand into destruction (tahlukah). Concerning this, there is a secret that will come in the Book of Reliance on God (Kitāb al-Tawakkul). [Page V02P257]

And the meaning of reliance on God (tawakkul) is not the utter abandonment of means (asbāb) altogether. Were it so, then reliance would be nullified by the very seeking of the bucket and the rope, and the drawing of water from the well — and it would become obligatory upon one to wait until God subjugated to him an angel or another person to pour water into his mouth. Now, if the preservation of the bucket and rope does not impugn reliance on God — being merely the instrument (ālah) for reaching the drinkable water — then the carrying of the very substance of food and drink, where no prospect of their availability is anticipated, is all the more fitting not to impugn it. The reality of reliance on God will come in its proper place, for it is obscure except to the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) among the scholars of religion.

As for the provision of the afterlife — it is the knowledge (ʿilm) he requires for his purification, his fasting, his prayer, and his worship. He must therefore provision himself with it, for travel sometimes lightens certain matters for him, and he then needs to know the extent to which travel lightens them — such as shortening the prayer (qaṣr), combining prayers (jamʿ), and breaking the fast (fiṭr). And sometimes travel intensifies matters that were unnecessary for him in settled residence — such as knowledge of the qibla direction and the times of the prayers. For in the city, he suffices with what others provide — the prayer niches (maḥārīb) of the mosques and the calls of the muezzins — whereas in travel, he may need to ascertain these matters by himself.

Thus, what he stands in need of learning divides into two divisions:

### The First Division: Knowledge of the Travel Concessions (rukhaṣ al-safar)
