chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| بيان آدابه وأخلاقه  في اللباس

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يلبس من الثياب ما وجد من إزار أو رداء أو قميص
أو جبة أو غير ذلك (1) وكان يعجبه الثياب الخضر (2) وكان أكثر لباسه البياض
ويقول ألبسوها أحياءكم وكفنوا فيها موتاكم وكان يلبس القباء المحشو للحرب
وغير الحرب (3) وكان له قباء سندس فيلبسه فتحسن خضرته على بياض لونه (4)
وكانت ثيابه كلها مشمرة فوق الكعبين ويكون الأزار فوق ذلك إلى نصف الساق
(5) وكان قميصه مشدود الأزرار وربما حل الأزرار في الصلاة وغيرها (6) وكانت
له ملحفة مصبوغه بالزعفران وربما صلى بالناس فيها وحدها (7) وربما ليس
الكساء وحده ما عليه غيره (8) وكان له كساء ملبد يلبسه ويقول إنما أنا عبد
ألبس كما يلبس العبد (9) وكان له ثوبان PageV02P374
لجمعته خاصة سوى ثيابه في غير الجمعة (1) وربما لبس الإزار الواحد ليس
عليه غيره ويعقد طرفيه بين كتفيه (2) وربما أم به الناس على الجنائز (3)
وربما صلى في بيته في الإزار الواحد ملتحفا به مخالفا بين طرفيه ويكون ذلك
الإزار الذي جامع فيه يومئذ (4) وكان ربما صلى بالليل بالإزار ويرتدي ببعض
الثوب مما يلي هدبه ويلقى البقية على بعض نسائه فيصلي كذلك (5) ولقد كان له
كساء فوهبه فقالت له أم سلمة بأبي أنت وأمي ما فعل ذلك الكساء الأسود فقال
كسوته فقالت ما رأيت شيئا قط كان أحسن من بياضك على سواده (6) وقال أنس
وربما رأيته يصلي بنا الظهر في شملة عاقدا بين طرفيه (7) وكان  يتختم (8)
وربما خرج وفي خاتمه الخيط المربوط يتذكر به الشيء (9) وكان يختم به على
الكتب ويقول الخاتم على الكتاب خير من التهمة (10) وكان يلبس القلانس تحت
العمائم وبغير عمامة وربما نزع قلنسوته من رأسه فجعلها سترة بين يديه ثم
يصلى إليها (11) وربما لم تكن العمامة فيشد العصابة PageV02P375
على رأسه وعلى جبهته (1) وكانت له عمامة تسمى السحاب فوهبها من علي فربما
طلع على فيها فيقول صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاكم علي في السحاب (2) وكان إذا
لبس ثوبا لبسه من قبل ميامنه (3) ويقول الحمد لله الذي كساني ما أواري به
عورتي وأتجمل به في الناس (4) وإذا نزع ثوبه أخرجه من مياسره (5) وكان إذا
لبس جديدا أعطى خلق ثيابه مسكينا ثم يقول ما من مسلم يكسو مسلما من سمل
ثيابه لا يكسوه إلا الله إلا كان في ضمان الله وحرزه وخيره ما واراه حيا
وميتا (6) وكان له فراش من أدم حشوه ليف طوله ذراعان أو نحوه وعرضه ذراع
وشبر أو نحوه (7) وكانت له عباءة تفرش له حيثما تنقل تثنى طاقين تحته (8)
وكان ينام على الحصير ليس تحته شيء غيره (9) وكان من خلقه تسمية دوابه
وسلاحه ومتاعه وكان اسم رايته العقاب
واسم سيفه الذي يشهد به الحروب ذو الفقار
وكان له سيف يقال له المخذم
وآخر يقال له الرسوب وآخر يقال له القضيب
وكانت قبضة سيفه محلاة بالفضة (10) PageV02P376
وكان يلبس المنطقة من الآدم فيها ثلاث حلق من فضة (1) وكان اسم قوسه
الكتوم وجعبته الكافور (2) وكان اسم ناقته القصواء وهي التي يقال لها
العضبا واسم بغلته الدلدل وكان اسم حماره يعفور واسم شاته التي يشرب لبنها
عينة (3) وكان له مطهرة من فخار يتوضأ فيها ويشرب منها (4) فيرسل الناس
أولادهم الصغار الذين قد عقلوا فيدخلوه على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
فلا يدفعون عنه فإذا وجدوا في المطهرة ماء شربوا منه ومسحوا على وجوههم
وأجسادهم ويبتغون بذلك البركة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, clothe, don; the act of enveloping the body with a garment; also used for concealment and veiling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, لباس denotes the outward covering of the body, while metaphorically it extends to the covering of the soul with virtue or vice (e.g., {«لِبَاسُ التَّقْوَىٰ»} — "the raiment of righteousness").
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical garments; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to states of piety or sin, as in "clothing oneself in patience."
- Root: ز-ع-ف-ر-ا-ن (z-ʿ-f-r-ā-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Saffron; a yellow dye derived from the crocus flower, used for coloring garments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a technical theological term; denotes a permissible dye, though its use on clothing was a matter of prophetic practice and personal preference.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal reference to the dye; no metaphorical extension in this context.
- Root: ع-م-م (ʿ-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wrap or wind around the head; the turban (ʿimāmah) as a distinctive head covering.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbolizes honor and dignity in social and religious life; the turban was a mark of distinction among the Arabs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical turban; metaphorically, "the crown of the Arabs" in rhetorical usage.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Āmilah (Governing Agent) — In the phrase "كان يلبس من الثياب ما وجد" (he used to wear from garments whatever he found), the verb كان governs the nominal sentence, and the relative clause ما وجد functions as the object, with the preposition من indicating partitive extraction (tabʿīḍ), showing selection from a category.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now I shall expound upon his etiquette and character regarding clothing.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to wear from garments whatever he found — whether an izār (waist-wrapper), a ridāʾ (cloak), a qamīṣ (shirt), a jubbah (long coat), or other than that. (1) He was pleased by green garments. (2) Yet the most of his clothing was white, and he would say: "Clothe your living in it and shroud your dead in it." He would wear the padded quilted coat (qabāʾ) for war and for other than war. (3) He had a qabāʾ of sundus (fine silk) which he would wear, and its greenness would appear beautiful against the whiteness of his complexion. (4) All his garments were hitched up above the ankles, and the izār would be above that up to the middle of the shin. (5) His shirt was buttoned up, and sometimes he would unbutton the buttons in prayer and other situations. (6) He had a wrap (milḥafah) dyed with saffron, and sometimes he would lead the people in prayer wearing it alone. (7) Sometimes he would wear the cloak (kisāʾ) alone with nothing else upon him. (8) He had a felted cloak (kisāʾ mulabbad) which he would wear, saying: "I am but a servant; I wear as the servant wears." (9) He had two garments specifically for his Friday (Jumuʿah) prayer, apart from his other garments on other days. (1) Sometimes he would wear a single izār with nothing else upon him, tying its two ends between his shoulders. (2) Sometimes he would lead the people in prayer over the funerals (janāʾiz) in this state. (3) Sometimes he would pray in his house in a single izār, wrapping himself in it, crossing its two ends, and that would be the very izār in which he had had marital intercourse that day. (4) Sometimes he would pray at night in the izār, donning a portion of the cloth near its fringe, and casting the remainder over one of his wives, and he would pray in this manner. (5) He had a cloak which he gifted away, and Umm Salamah said to him: "May my father and mother be your ransom — what became of that black cloak?" He said: "I clothed someone with it." She said: "I have never seen anything more beautiful than your whiteness against its blackness." (6) Anas said: "And sometimes I would see him leading us in the noon prayer (ẓuhr) in a single wrap (shamlah), tying its two ends together." (7) He used to wear a signet ring (khatam). (8) Sometimes he would go out with a thread tied to his ring, by which he would remind himself of a matter. (9) He would seal letters with it, saying: "A seal on a letter is better than suspicion." (10) He would wear caps (qalānis) under his turbans, and also without a turban; and sometimes he would remove his cap from his head and place it as a sutrah (screen) before him, then pray toward it. (11) Sometimes he had no turban, so he would bind a headband (ʿiṣābah) upon his head and forehead. (1) He had a turban called al-Saḥāb (the Cloud), which he gifted to ʿAlī; and sometimes he would appear wearing it, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say: "ʿAlī has come to you in the Cloud." (2) When he put on a garment, he would put it on starting from his right side. (3) And he would say: "Praise be to God who has clothed me with that by which I cover my nakedness and adorn myself among the people." (4) When he removed his garment, he would take it off from his left side. (5) When he wore something new, he would give his old worn garments to a poor person, then say: "No Muslim clothes another Muslim with the worn-out garments of his clothing — clothing him only for God's sake — except that he is under God's protection and safeguard, and God's goodness is what covers him, living and dead." (6) He had a mattress of leather (adim) stuffed with palm fiber (līf), its length being two cubits (dhirāʿ) or thereabouts, and its width one cubit and a span (shibr) or thereabouts. (7) He had an ʿabāʾah (woolen cloak) which was spread for him wherever he moved, folded double beneath him. (8) He used to sleep on a straw mat (ḥaṣīr) with nothing else beneath him. (9) It was among his habits to name his mounts, his weapons, and his belongings. The name of his banner was al-ʿUqāb (the Eagle). The name of his sword with which he witnessed battles was Dhū al-Faqār. He had a sword called al-Mikhdham, another called al-Rasūb, and another called al-Qaḍīb. The hilt of his sword was adorned with silver. (10) He used to wear a belt (minṭaqah) of leather (adim) with three rings of silver upon it. (1) The name of his bow was al-Katūm, and his quiver was al-Kāfūr. (2) The name of his she-camel was al-Qaṣwāʾ — she who is also called al-ʿAḍbāʾ — and the name of his mule was al-Duldul, and the name of his donkey was Yaʿfūr, and the name of his ewe from whose milk he drank was ʿAynah. (3) He had a water vessel (muṭahharah) of clay (fakhkhār) from which he would perform ablution (wuḍūʾ) and from which he would drink. (4) The people would send their young children who had reached the age of discernment, and they would enter upon the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and they would not be turned away. When they found water in the vessel, they would drink from it and wipe their faces and bodies with it, seeking thereby blessing (barakah).

chapters.title_en: The Explanation of His Pardon (ʿAfw) — Peace Be Upon Him — Despite His Capability, and His Overlooking What He Disliked
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| بيان عفوه صلى الله عليه وسلم مع قدرته

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أحلم الناس (5) وأرغبهم في  العفو مع القدرة حتى
أتى بقلائد من ذهب وفضة فقسمها بين أصحابه فقام رجل من أهل البادية فقال يا
محمد والله لئن أمرك الله أن تعدل فما أراك تعدل فقال ويحك فمن يعدل عليه
بعدي فلما ولي قال ردوه على رويدا (6) روى جابر أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان
يقبض للناس يوم خيبر من فضة في ثوب بلال فقال له رجل يا رسول الله أعدل
فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحك فمن يعدل إذا لم أعدل فقد خبت
إذن وخسرت إن كنت لا أعدل فقام عمر فقال ألا أضرب عنقه فإنه منافق فقال
معاذ الله أن يتحدث الناس أني أقتل أصحابي (7) وكان رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم في حرب فرأوا من المسلمين غرة فجاء رجل حتى قام على رأس رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالسيف فقال من يمنعك مني فقال الله فقال فسقط
السيف من يده فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم السيف وقال من يمنعك مني
فقال كن خير آخذ قال قل أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله فقال لا
غير أني لا أقاتلك ولا أكون معك PageV02P377
ولا أكون مع قوم يقاتلونك فخلى سبيله فجاء أصحابه فقال جئتكم من عند خير
الناس (1) وروى أنس أن يهودية أتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بشاة مسمومة
ليأكل منها فجيء بها إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألها عن ذلك فقالت
أردت قتلك فقال ما كان الله ليسلطك على ذلك قالوا أفلا تقتلها فقال لا
(2) وسحره رجل من اليهود فأخبره جبريل عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام بذلك حتى
استخرجه وحل العقد فوجد لذلك خفة وما ذكر ذلك لليهودي ولا أظهره عليه قط
(3) وقال علي رضي الله عنه بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنا الزبير
والمقداد فقال انطلقوا حتى تأتوا روضة خاخ فإن بها ظعينة معها كتاب فخذوه
منها فانطلقنا حتى أتينا روضة خاخ فقلنا أخرجي الكتاب فقالت ما معي من كتاب
فقلنا  لتخرجن الكتاب أو لننزعن الثياب فأخرجته من عقاصها فأتينا به النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم فإذا فيه من حاطب بن أبي بلتعة إلى أناس من المشركين
بمكة يخبرهم أمرا من أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا حاطب ما هذا
قال يا رسول الله لا تعجل علي أني كنت امرأ ملصقا في قومي وكان من معك من
المهاجرين لهم قرابات بمكة يحمون أهلهم فأحببت إذ فاتني ذلك من النسب منهم
أن أتخذ فيهم يدا يحمون بها قرابتي ولم أفعل ذلك كفرا ولا رضا بالكفر بعد
الإسلام ولا ارتدادا عن ديني فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه صدقكم
فقال عمر رضي الله عنه دعني أضرب عنق هذا المنافق فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
إنه شهد بدرا وما يدريك لعل الله عز وجل قد اطلع على أهل بدر فقال اعملوا
ما شئتم فقد غفرت لكم (4) وقسم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسمة فقال رجل
من الأنصار هذه قسمة ما أريد بها وجه الله فذكر ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم فاحمر وجهه وقال رحم الله أخي موسى قد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر (5)
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لا يبلغني أحد منكم عن أحد من أصحابي شيئا
فإني أحب أن أخرج إليكم وأنا سليم الصدر (6)

### ||| بيان إغضائه صلى الله عليه وسلم عما كان يكرهه

كان رسول الله رقيق البشرة لطيف الظاهر والباطن يعرف في وجهه غضبه ورضاه
(7) وكان إذا اشتد وجده أكثر من مس لحيته الكريمة (8) وكان لا يشافه أحد
بما يكرهه دخل عليه رجل وعليه صفرة فكرهها فلم يقل له شيئا حتى خرج فقال
لبعض القوم لو قلتم لهذا أن يدع هذه (9) يعني الصفرة وبال أعرابي في المسجد
بحضرته فهم به PageV02P378
الصحابة فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تزرموه أي لا تقطعوا عليه البول ثم
قال له إن هذه المساجد لا تصلح لشيء من القذر والبول والخلاء (1) وفي رواية
قربوا ولا تنفروا
وجاءه أعرابي يوما  يطلب منه شيئا فأعطاه صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قال له
أحسنت إليك قال الأعرابي لا ولا أجملت قال فغضب المسلمون وقاموا إليه فأشار
إليهم أن كفوا ثم قام ودخل منزله وأرسل إلى الأعرابي وزاده شيئا ثم قال
أحسنت إليك قال نعم فجزاك الله من أهل وعشيرة خيرا فقال له النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم إنك قلت ما قلت وفي نفس أصحابي شيء من ذلك فإن أحببت فقل بين
أيديهم ما قلت بين يدي حتى يذهب من صدورهم ما فيها عليك قال نعم فلما كان
الغد أو العشى جاء فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن هذا الأعرابي قال ما
قال فزدناه فزعم أنه رضي أكذلك فقال الأعرابي نعم فجزاك الله من أهل وعشيرة
خيرا فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن مثلي ومثل هذا الأعرابي كمثل رجل كانت له
ناقة شردت عليه فاتبعها الناس فلم يزيدوها إلا نفورا فناداهم صاحب الناقة
خلوا بيني وبين ناقتي فإني أرفق بها وأعلم فتوجه لها صاحب الناقة بين يديه
فأخذ لها من قمام الأرض فردها هونا حتى جاءت واستناخت وشد عليها رحلها
واستوى عليها وإني لو تركتكم حيث قال الرجل ما قال فقتلتموه دخل النار (2)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-F-W)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pardon, to efface, to leave something unpunished; the root denotes "excess" and "remission" — the act of forgoing what is due to one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Pardon (ʿafw) is the deliberate relinquishment of retribution (intiqām) by one who possesses full power (qudrah) over the offender — a mark of divine attribute (al-ʿAfuww) mirrored in prophetic character.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of "erasing the trace of the offense"; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the heart's state — the absence of rancor (ghill) alongside the absence of punishment.
- Root: غ-ض-ي (Gh-D-Y) [for Ighḍāʾ]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To close the eye partially, to wink; extended to "overlooking" a fault with deliberate inattention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ighḍāʾ is the volitional act of not perceiving what one sees — a virtue of forbearance (ḥilm) that preserves social harmony.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the eye's action; metaphorical: the soul's refusal to dwell on another's offense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In "أحلم الناس وأرغبهم في العفو مع القدرة," the second epithet is coordinated to specify the first, with "مع القدرة" (despite capability) functioning as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) that intensifies the praise by negating any excuse for vengeance.
chapters.translation:
### ||| The Explanation of His Pardon — Peace Be Upon Him — Despite His Capability

He — Peace Be Upon Him — was the most forbearing of people and the most desirous of pardon despite capability, until [the following occurred]: Gold and silver necklaces were brought to him, and he divided them among his companions. A man of the Bedouin stood up and said: "O Muhammad, by God, if God has commanded you to be just, then I do not see you being just." He said: "Woe to you — who then would be just over you after me?" When the man turned away, he said: "Bring him back to me, gently." (6) Jābir narrated that he — Peace Be Upon Him — was taking for the people, on the Day of Khaybar, some silver in the garment of Bilāl, when a man said to him: "O Messenger of God, be just." The Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — said: "Woe to you — who would be just if I am not just? Then I would have failed and lost if I were not just." Then ʿUmar stood up and said: "Shall I not strike his neck? For he is a hypocrite." He said: "God forbid that people should say that I kill my companions." (7) And the Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — was in a war, and they perceived a moment of negligence among the Muslims, so a man came until he stood over the head of the Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — with a sword, and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "God." He said: "Then the sword fell from his hand, and the Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — took the sword and said: 'Who will protect you from me?' He said: 'Be the best taker.' He said: 'Say: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that I am the Messenger of God.' He said: 'No, but [I pledge] that I will not fight you, nor will I be with you — nor will I be with a people who fight you.' So he released him. Then his companions came to him, and he said: 'I have come to you from the presence of the best of people.'" (1) And Anas narrated that a Jewish woman came to the Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — with a poisoned sheep so that he might eat from it. It was brought to the Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — and he asked her about that, and she said: "I intended to kill you." He said: "God would not have given you power over that." They said: "Shall we not kill her?" He said: "No." (2) And a man of the Jews cast a spell on him, and Gabriel — upon him the most excellent prayer and peace — informed him of that, until he extracted it and untied the knots, and he felt a lightness from that. And he never mentioned that to the Jew, nor did he ever expose him for it. (3) And ʿAlī — may God be pleased with him — said: "The Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — sent me, al-Zubayr, and al-Miqdād, and said: 'Go until you reach the meadow of Khākh, for there is a woman traveler there with a letter — take it from her.' So we went until we reached the meadow of Khākh, and we said: 'Bring out the letter.' She said: 'I have no letter with me.' We said: 'You will bring out the letter, or we will strip off your garments.' So she brought it out from her hair-braids, and we brought it to the Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — and behold, in it was [a message] from Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to some of the polytheists of Mecca, informing them of some matter concerning the Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him. He said: 'O Ḥāṭib, what is this?' He said: 'O Messenger of God, do not hasten against me. I was a man attached [by alliance] among my people, and those of the emigrants who were with you had kinsfolk in Mecca who protected their families. So I loved — since I lacked that share of lineage among them — to take a favor with them by which they might protect my kin. And I did not do this out of unbelief, nor out of satisfaction with unbelief after Islam, nor out of apostasy from my religion.' The Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — said: 'He has spoken truthfully to you.' Then ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — said: 'Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite.' He — Peace Be Upon Him — said: 'He witnessed Badr. And what do you know — perhaps God — Mighty and Majestic — has looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" (4) And the Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — made a distribution, and a man of the Anṣār said: "This is a distribution by which the Face of God was not intended." That was mentioned to the Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — and his face reddened, and he said: "May God have mercy on my brother Moses — he was harmed by more than this, and he was patient." (5) And he — Peace Be Upon Him — used to say: "Let none of you convey to me anything about any of my companions, for I love to go out to you with a sound breast."

### ||| The Explanation of His Overlooking (Ighḍāʾ) What He Disliked

The Messenger of God — Peace Be Upon Him — was delicate of skin, gentle in outward and inward [disposition]; his anger and his pleasure were known in his face. (7) And when his distress intensified, he would increase his touching of his noble beard. (8) And he never addressed anyone with what he disliked. A man entered upon him with yellowness [of dye] upon him, and he disliked it, but he said nothing to him until he left, then he said to some of the people: "Would that you had said to this man: 'Let him leave this.'" (9) — meaning the yellowness. And a Bedouin urinated in the mosque in his presence, and the companions rushed at him, but he — Peace Be Upon Him — said: "Do not interrupt him" — that is, do not cut off his urination. Then he said to him: "These mosques are not fit for any of the filth, urine, or excrement." (1) And in another narration: "Draw near, and do not repel." And a Bedouin came to him one day seeking something from him, and he — Peace Be Upon Him — gave him, then said to him: "I have done well by you." The Bedouin said: "No, and you have not done beautifully." The Muslims became angry and rose against him, and he gestured to them to hold back. Then he stood, entered his home, and sent to the Bedouin, adding something more for him, then said: "I have done well by you." He said: "Yes — may God reward you with good from a people and kin." The Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — said to him: "You said what you said, and in the breasts of my companions there is something of that. If you wish, say before them what you said before me, so that what is in their breasts against you may depart." He said: "Yes." Then when the next day or the evening came, he arrived, and the Prophet — Peace Be Upon Him — said: "This Bedouin said what he said, and we increased him, and he claims that he is satisfied — is it so?" The Bedouin said: "Yes — may God reward you with good from a people and kin." He — Peace Be Upon Him — said: "My example and the example of this Bedouin is like the example of a man who had a she-camel that bolted from him. The people followed her, but that only increased her in flight. So the owner of the she-camel called out to them: 'Leave me and my she-camel, for I am gentler with her and know her better.' Then the owner of the she-camel turned to her, took for her some of the earth's litter, and returned her gently until she came and knelt, and he saddled her and mounted her. And had I left you where the man said what he said, and you had killed him, he would have entered the Fire." (2)

chapters.title_en: Exposition of His Generosity and Munificence, and His Courage and Humility (Peace Be Upon Him)
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| بيان سخاوته وجوده صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود الناس وأسخاهم وكان في شهر رمضان كالريح
المرسلة لا يمسك شيئا (3) وكان علي رضي الله عنه إذا وصف النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم قال كان أجود الناس كفا وأوسع الناس صدرا وأصدق الناس لهدة
وأوفاهم ذمة وألينهم عريكة وأكرمهم عشيرة من رآه بديهة هابه ومن خالطه
معرفة أحبه يقول ناعته لم أر قبله ولا بعده مثله (4) وما سئل عن شيء قط على
الإسلام إلا أعطاه (5) وإن رجلا أتاه فسأله فأعطاه غنما سدت ما بين جبلين
فرجع إلى قومه وقال أسلموا فإن محمدا يعطي عطاء من لا يخشى الفاقة
وما سئل شيئا قط فقال لا (6) وحمل إليه تسعون ألف درهم فوضعها على حصير
ثم قام إليها فقسمها  فما رد سائلا حتى فرغ منها (7) وجاء رجل فسأله فقال ما
عندي شيء ولكن ابتع علي فإذا جاءنا شيء قضيناه فقال عمر يا رسول الله ما
كلفك الله مالا تقدر عليه فكره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك فقال الرجل
أنفق ولا تخش من ذلك العرش إقلالا فتبسم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
PageV02P379
وعرف السرور في وجهه (1) ولما قفل من حنين جاءت الأعراب يسألونه حتى
اضطروه إلى شجرة فخطفت رداءه فوقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال
أعطوني ردائي لو كان لي عدد هذه العضاة نعما لقسمتها بينكم ثلا لا تجدوني
بخيلا ولا كذابا ولا جبانا (2)

### ||| بيان شجاعته صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أنجد الناس وأشجعهم (3) قال علي رضي الله عنه لقد
رأيتني يوم بدر ونحن نلوذ بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو أقربنا إلى العدو
وكان من أشد الناس يومئذ بأسا (4) وقال أيضا كنا إذا احمر البأس ولقي القوم
القوم اتقينا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فما يكون أحد أقرب إلى العدو
منه (5) قيل وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم قليل الكلام قليل الحديث فإذا أمر
الناس بالقتال تشمر وكان من أشد الناس بأسا (6) وكان الشجاع هو الذي يقرب
منه في الحرب لقربه من العدو (7) وقال عمران بن حصين ما لقى رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم كتيبة إلا كان أول من يضرب (8) وقالوا كان قوي البطش (9)
ولما غشيه المشركون نزل عن بغلته فجعل يقول
أنا النبي لا كذب أنا ابن عبد المطلب
فما رؤي يومئذ أحد كان أشد منه (10)

### ||| بيان تواضعه صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أشد الناس تواضعا في علو منصبه (11) قال ابن عامر
رأيته يرمي الجمرة على ناقة شهباء لا ضرب ولا طرد ولا إليك إليك (12) وكان
يركب الحمار موكفا عليه قطيفة وكان مع ذلك يستردف (13) وكان يعود
PageV02P380
المريض ويتبع الجنازة ويجيب دعوة المملوك (1) ويخصف النعل ويرقع الثوب
وكان يصنع في بيته مع أهله في حاجتهم (2) وكان  أصحابه لا يقومون له لما
عرفوا من كراهته لذلك (3) وكان يمر على الصبيان فيسلم عليهم (4) وأتى صلى
الله عليه وسلم برجل فأرعد من هيبته فقال له هون عليك فلست بملك إنما أنا
ابن امرأة من قريش تأكل القديد (5) وكان يجلس بين أصحابه مختلطا بهم كأنه
أحدهم فيأتي الغريب فلا يدري أيهم هو حتى يسأل عنه حتى طلبوا إليه أن يجلس
مجلسا يعرفه الغريب فبنوا له دكانا من طين فكان يجلس عليه (6) وقالت له
عائشة رضي الله عنها كل جعلني الله فداك متكئا فإنه أهون عليك قال فأصغى
رأسه حتى كاد أن تصيب جبهته الأرض ثم قال بل آكل كما يأكل العبد وأجلس كما
يجلس العبد (7) وكان لا يأكل على خوان ولا في سكرجة حتى لحق بالله تعالى
(8) وكان لا يدعوه أحد من أصحابه وغيرهم إلا قال لبيك (9) وكان إذا جلس مع
الناس إن تكلموا في معنى الآخرة أخذ معهم وإن تحدثوا في طعام أو شراب تحدث
معهم وإن تكلموا في الدنيا تحدث معهم رفقا بهم وتواضعا لهم (10) وكانوا
يتناشدون الشعر بين يديه أحيانا ويذكرون أشياء من أمر الجاهلية ويضحكون
فتبسم هو إذا ضحكوا ولا يزجرهم إلا عن حرام (11)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-د (j-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of goodness, excellence, and the act of giving freely without constraint; al-jūd is the quality of one whose hand is open in beneficence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, jūd is the praiseworthy disposition of the soul that impels one to bestow what is needed without expectation of return, mirroring divine generosity (al-karam al-ilāhī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its literal sense (ḥaqīqah) of open-handed giving, not metaphorical; the comparison to the "released wind" is a rhetorical simile (tashbīh) indicating unrestrained swiftness and abundance.
- Root: ش-ج-ع (sh-j-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes strength of heart and firmness in the face of danger; shajāʿah is courage as a settled trait of boldness in battle.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ethical Kalām, shajāʿah is the median virtue between recklessness (tahawwur) and cowardice (jubn), perfected in the prophetic character.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage in martial contexts; the phrase "when battle grew hot" (iḥmarra al-ba's) is a metaphorical expression for the intensity of combat.
- Root: ت-و-ض-ع (t-w-ḍ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: From waḍaʿa, to lower or place down; tawāḍuʿ is self-abasement in rank, the opposite of pride (kibr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A cardinal virtue in the prophetic model—humility before God and creation, not as degradation but as exalted modesty rooted in awareness of one's servitude (ʿubūdiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of lowering oneself; the Prophet's statement "I am but the son of a woman of Quraysh who eats dried meat" is a literal self-description used to dispel awe, not a metaphor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — In "كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود الناس" the predicate (khabar) is a comparative adjective (afʿal al-tafḍīl) functioning as a perpetual state (ḥāl muqaddarah), indicating a continuous attribute, not a transient condition.
chapters.translation:
### ||| Exposition of His Generosity and Munificence (Peace Be Upon Him)

He (Peace Be Upon Him) was the most generous of people and the most munificent of them, and during the month of Ramadan he was like the released wind, withholding nothing. {«...»} ʿAlī (May Allah Be Pleased With Him) said, when describing the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him): "He was the most generous of people in hand, the most expansive of people in breast, the most truthful of people in speech, the most faithful of people in covenant, the gentlest of people in temperament, and the most honorable of people in company. Whoever saw him at first glance was awed by him, and whoever mixed with him in acquaintance loved him. His describer would say: 'I have not seen before him nor after him his like.'" He was never asked for anything at all upon Islam except that he gave it. A man came to him and asked him, and he gave him a flock of sheep that filled the space between two mountains. The man returned to his people and said: "Embrace Islam, for Muhammad gives the gift of one who does not fear poverty." And he was never asked for anything at all but that he said "No." Ninety thousand dirhams were carried to him, and he placed them on a mat, then stood over them and distributed them—he did not turn away a single beggar until he had finished them. A man came and asked him, and he said: "I have nothing with me, but buy on my account, and when something comes to us we will repay it." ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has not burdened you with what you cannot afford." The Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) disliked that remark. Then the man said: "Spend, and do not fear from the Owner of the Throne any diminishment." The Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) smiled, and the joy was recognized in his face. When he returned from Ḥunayn, the Bedouins came asking him until they pressed him against a tree, and his cloak was snatched from him. The Messenger of Allah (Peace Be Upon Him) stopped and said: "Give me back my cloak. If I had as many camels as these thorn-trees, I would divide them among you. You will not find me miserly, nor a liar, nor a coward."

### ||| Exposition of His Courage (Peace Be Upon Him)

He (Peace Be Upon Him) was the most valiant of people and the most courageous of them. ʿAlī (May Allah Be Pleased With Him) said: "I saw myself on the Day of Badr, and we were seeking refuge with the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him), and he was the closest of us to the enemy, and he was that day the most severe of people in might." He also said: "When battle grew hot and the ranks met the ranks, we shielded ourselves with the Messenger of Allah (Peace Be Upon Him), and no one was closer to the enemy than he." It was said: He (Peace Be Upon Him) was sparing in speech and brief in conversation, but when he commanded the people to fight, he girded himself, and he was the most severe of people in might. The brave man was the one who drew near to him in war, because of his proximity to the enemy. ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: "The Messenger of Allah (Peace Be Upon Him) never encountered a battalion except that he was the first to strike." And they said: He was mighty in assault. When the polytheists overwhelmed him, he dismounted from his mule and began to say: "I am the Prophet, no lie—I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib." And no one was seen that day who was more severe than he.

### ||| Exposition of His Humility (Peace Be Upon Him)

He (Peace Be Upon Him) was the most intense of people in humility, despite the loftiness of his station. Ibn ʿĀmir said: "I saw him casting the pebbles at the Jamrah upon a she-camel, with no striking, no driving away, and no 'Move! Move!'" He would ride a donkey with a saddle-cloth thrown over it, and despite that he would take a companion behind him. He would visit the sick, follow the funeral procession, and accept the invitation of a slave. He would mend his sandals and patch his garment, and he would work in his house with his family in their needs. His companions would not stand up for him, knowing his dislike of that. He would pass by children and greet them. A man was brought to him (Peace Be Upon Him) and trembled with awe of him, so he said to him: "Take it easy, for I am not a king. I am but the son of a woman of Quraysh who eats dried meat." He would sit among his companions, mingling with them as if he were one of them, so a stranger would come and not know which of them he was until he asked about him. They even requested him to sit in a place where the stranger could recognize him, so they built him a bench of clay, and he would sit upon it. ʿĀʾishah (May Allah Be Pleased With Her) said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, eat reclining, for it is easier for you." So he inclined his head until his forehead nearly touched the ground, then said: "Rather, I eat as the slave eats, and I sit as the slave sits." He did not eat upon a table, nor upon a small dish, until he met Allah (Exalted Is He). No one among his companions or others would call him except that he said: "At your service." When he sat with people—if they spoke of the matter of the Hereafter, he joined them; if they conversed about food or drink, he conversed with them; if they spoke of worldly matters, he spoke with them—out of gentleness toward them and humility before them. They would recite poetry in his presence at times, and mention things of the age of ignorance, and laugh, and he would smile when they laughed, and he would not forbid them except from what was unlawful.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of His Appearance and Physical Form (Peace and Blessings Be Upon Him)
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| بيان صورته وخلقته صلى الله عليه وسلم

وكان من صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لم يكن بالطويل البائن ولا
بالقصير المتردد بل كان ينسب إلى الربعة إذا مشى وحده ومع ذلك فلم يكن
يماشيه أحد من الناس ينسب إلى الطول إلا طاله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ولربما اكتنفه الرجلان الطويلان فيطولهما فإذا فارقاه نسبا إلى الطول ونسب
هو صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الربعة ويقول صلى الله عليه وسلم جعل الخير كله
في الربعة (12) PageV02P381
وأما لونه فقد كان أزهر اللون ولم يكن بالآدم ولا بالشديد البياض والأزهر
هو الأبيض الناصع الذي لا تشوبه صفرة ولا حمرة ولا شيء من الألوان ونعته
عمه أبو طالب فقال
وأبيض يستسقى الغمام بوجهه ... ثمال اليتامى عصمة للأرامل (1)
ونعته بعضهم بأنه مشرب  بحمرة فقالوا إنما كان المشرب منه بالحمرة ما ظهر
للشمس والرياح كالوجه والرقبة والأزهر الصافي عن الحمرة ما تحت الثياب منه
وكان عرقه صلى الله عليه وسلم في وجهه كاللؤلؤ أطيب من المسك الأذفر
وأما شعره فقد كان رجل الشعر حسنه ليس بالسبط ولا الجعد القطط وكان إذا
مشطه بالمشط يأتى كأنه حبك الرمل
وقيل كان شعره يضرب منكبيه وأكثر الرواية أنه كان إلى شحمة أذنيه ربما
جعله غدائر أربعا تخرج كل أذن من بين غديرتين
وربما جعل شعره على أذنيه فتبدوا سوالفه تتلألأ
وكان شيبه في الرأس واللحية سبع عشرة شعرة ما زاد على ذلك
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن الناس وجها وأنورهم لم يصفه واصف إلا شبهه
بالقمر ليلة البدر وكان يرى رضاه وغضبه في وجهه لصفاء بشرته وكانوا يقولون
هو كما وصفه صاحبه أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه حيث يقول
أمين مصطفى للخير يدعو ... كضوء البدر زايله الظلام
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم واسع الجبهة أزج الحاجبين سابغهما وكان أبلج ما
بين الحاجبين كأن ما بينهما الفضة المخلصة وكانت عيناه نجلاوين أدعجهما
وكان في عينيه تمزج من حمرة وكان أهدب الأشفار حتى تكاد تلتبس من كثرتها
وكان أقنى العرنين أي مستوى الأنف وكان مفلج الأسنان أي متفرقها وكان إذا
افتر ضاحكا افتر عن مثل سنا البرق إذا تلألأ وكان من أحسن عباد الله شفتين
وألطفهم ختم فم وكان سهل الخدين صلبهما ليس بالطويل الوجه ولا المكلثم كث
اللحية وكان يعفي لحيته ويأخذ من شاربه وكان أحسن عباد الله عنقا لا ينسب
إلى الطول ولا إلى القصر ما ظهر من عنقه للشمس والرياح فكأنه إبريق فضة
مشرب ذهبا يتلألأ في بياض الفضة وفي حمرة الذهب وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم
عريض الصدر لا يعدو لحم بعض بدنه بعضا كالمرآة في استوائها وكالقمر في
بياضه موصول ما بين لبته وسرته بشعر منقاد كالقضيب لم يكن في صدره ولا بطنه
شعر غيره وكانت له عكن ثلاث يغطي الإزار  منها واحدة ويظهر اثنتان وكان عظيم
المنكبين أشعرهما ضخم الكراديس أي رءوس العظام من المنكبين والمرفقين
والوركين وكان واسع الظهر ما بين كتفيه خاتم النبوة وهو مما يلي منكبه
الأيمن فيه شامة سوداء تضرب إلى الصفرة حولها شعرات متواليات كأنها من عرف
فرس وكان عبل العضدين والذراعين طويل PageV02P382
الزندين رحب الراحتين سائل الأطراف كأن أصابعه قضبان الفضة كفه ألين من
الخز كأن كفه كف عطار طيبا مسها بطيب أو لم يمسها يصافحه المصافح فيظل يومه
يجد ريحها ويضع يده على رأس الصبي فيعرف من بين الصبيان بريحها على رأسه
وكان عبل ما تحت الإزار من الفخذين والساق وكان معتدل الخلق في السمن بدن
في آخر زمانه وكان لحمه متماسكا يكاد يكون على الخلق الأول لم يضره السمن
وأما مشيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فكان يمشي كأنما يتقلع من صخر وينحدر من
صبب يخطو تكفيا ويمشي الهوينى بغير تبختر والهوينى تقارب الخطا وكان صلى
الله عليه وسلم يقول أنا أشبه الناس بآدم صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان أبي
إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم أشبه الناس بي خلقا وخلقا وكان يقول إن لي عند
ربي عشرة أسماء أنا محمد وأنا أحمد وأنا الماحي الذي يمحو الله بي الكفر
وأنا العاقب الذي ليس بعده أحد وأنا الحاشر يحشر الله العباد على قدمى وأنا
رسول الرحمة ورسول التوبة ورسول الملاحم والمقفى قفيت الناس جميعا وأنا قثم
(1) قال أبو البحتري والقثم الكامل الجامع والله أعلم

### ||| بيان معجزاته وآياته الدالة على صدقه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر ب ع (r-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Medium stature; the fourth part of a thing; dwelling in a place (rubʿah denotes a balanced, moderate build).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Proportionality as a sign of prophetic perfection—neither excess nor deficiency in creation (khalq), mirroring the divine wisdom of the middle path.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) reference to bodily measure; metaphorically (majāz) extended to moral excellence, as the Prophet's saying "all good is placed in the rubʿah" elevates physical moderation to a spiritual principle.
- Root: ز ه ر (z-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Radiant whiteness; blossoming brightness (azhar = luminous white, free from blemish).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The luminous complexion (azhar al-lawn) as a visible trace of prophetic light (nūr), connecting physical description to the inner illumination of prophethood.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal color description; majāz in the poetic simile of rain-seeking clouds, where the face's radiance becomes a cause of divine blessing.
- Root: ق ط ط (q-ṭ-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Curly, tightly coiled hair (jaʿd qaṭaṭ); the opposite of straight (sabṭ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hair texture as part of the prophetic physiognomy (shamāʾil), each trait confirming the perfection of his human form.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of hair; the simile "like the ridges of sand" (ḥabak al-raml) is a visual majāz conveying orderly waves.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl and Tamyīz (Circumstantial Clause and Specification) — In sentences like "kāna azhar al-lawn" (he was radiant of complexion), the noun after the adjective functions as a tamyīz specifying the domain of the attribute, a construction the translator must preserve to avoid ambiguity between physical and metaphorical readings.
chapters.translation:
### ||| Exposition of His Appearance and Physical Form (Peace and Blessings Be Upon Him)

Among the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was that he was neither conspicuously tall nor excessively short, but rather was attributed to medium stature (al-rubʿah) when he walked alone. Yet despite this, no one who walked alongside him and was attributed to tallness but that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) towered over him. And at times two tall men would flank him, and he would surpass them in height; but when they parted from him, they were attributed to tallness, while he (peace and blessings be upon him) was attributed to medium stature. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) would say: "All good is placed in the rubʿah." (12) PageV02P381

As for his complexion, it was azhar (radiant white) — neither tawny (ādam) nor intensely white. Azhar is the pure, brilliant white that is not tinged with yellowness, redness, or any other color. His uncle Abū Ṭālib described him, saying:

"And a white one by whose face the clouds are sought for rain — a refuge for orphans, a safeguard for widows." (1)

Some described him as tinged with redness (mushrab bi-ḥumrah), and they said: only that part of him exposed to the sun and winds — such as the face and neck — was tinged with redness; while the azhar, pure of redness, was what lay beneath his garments. And his sweat (peace and blessings be upon him) upon his face was like pearls, more fragrant than the strongest musk (al-misk al-adhfar).

As for his hair, it was wavy (rajl), beautiful — neither straight (sabṭ) nor tightly curled (jaʿd qaṭaṭ). When he combed it with a comb, it appeared like the ridges of sand (ḥabak al-raml).

It was said his hair reached his shoulders, but the more frequent narration is that it reached his earlobes. Sometimes he would arrange it in four plaits (ghadāʾir), each ear emerging from between two plaits. And sometimes he would let his hair fall over his ears, so that his forelocks (sawālif) appeared glistening.

His gray hairs on the head and beard numbered seventeen, no more than that.

He (peace and blessings be upon him) was the most beautiful of people in face and the most luminous of them. No describer described him but likened him to the full moon on the night of the badr (full moon). His pleasure and his anger could be seen in his face due to the clarity of his skin. And they would say: he is as his companion Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) described him, saying:

"A trusted one, chosen, calling to goodness — like the light of the full moon from which darkness has departed."

He (peace and blessings be upon him) had a broad forehead (wāsiʿ al-jabhah), arched, full eyebrows (azajj al-ḥājibayn sābighahumā), and there was a space between his eyebrows (ablaJ) as if what lay between them was pure silver. His eyes were wide (najlāwān) and intensely black (adʿajahumā), and there was in his eyes a tinge of redness. His eyelashes were so long and dense (ahdab al-ashfār) that they almost intertwined from their abundance. His nose was aquiline (aqnā al-ʿarnayn), that is, level in the bridge. His teeth were spaced (mufallaj al-asnān), that is, separated one from another. When he smiled broadly, he revealed teeth like a flash of lightning when it glistens. He was among the most beautiful of Allah's servants in lips and the most delicate in the seal of his mouth. His cheeks were smooth yet firm — his face neither long nor round and full (mukaltham). His beard was thick (kathth al-liḥyah), and he would let his beard grow full and trim his mustache. He had the most beautiful neck among Allah's servants — neither attributed to length nor shortness. What appeared of his neck to the sun and winds was like a silver ewer (ibrīq fiḍḍah) tinged with gold, glistening in the whiteness of silver and the redness of gold.

He (peace and blessings be upon him) was broad-chested, with flesh that did not overrun one part of his body over another — like a mirror in its evenness and like the moon in its whiteness. Between his chest (labbah) and navel ran a line of hair, straight like a rod; there was no other hair on his chest or belly. He had three folds of flesh (ʿakan) — the waistcloth covered one of them and two were visible. His shoulders were massive (ʿaẓīm al-mankibayn) and hairy, with large joints (ḍikhām al-karādīs), that is, the heads of the bones of the shoulders, elbows, and hips. His back was broad, and between his shoulder blades was the Seal of Prophethood (khātam al-nubuwwah), located near his right shoulder — a black mole tinged with yellowness, around which were continuous hairs as if from the mane of a horse. His upper arms and forearms were thick (ʿabil), his forearms (zandayn) long, his palms wide (raḥb al-rāḥatayn), and his fingers tapering (sāʾil al-aṭrāf), as if his fingers were rods of silver. His palm was softer than silk (khazz); it was as if his hand was the hand of a perfumer — whether it had touched perfume or not, whoever shook his hand would smell its fragrance for the rest of the day. And he would place his hand on a child's head, and the child would be known among the other children by the fragrance on his head.

His thighs and shanks beneath the waistcloth were thick (ʿabil). His build was moderate in fleshiness — he became somewhat fleshy (badan) in his later time, yet his flesh remained firm, almost as it was in his original state; the fleshiness did him no harm.

As for his walk (peace and blessings be upon him), he walked as if he were being detached from a rock and descending from a slope (ṣabab). He stepped with a slight sway (takaffuʾ) and walked with a gentle pace (al-huwaynā), without strutting — al-huwaynā being the shortening of steps. He (peace and blessings be upon him) would say: "I am the most similar of people to Adam (peace be upon him), and my father Abraham (peace be upon him) was the most similar of people to me in form (khalqan) and character (khuluqan)." And he would say: "Indeed, I have ten names with my Lord: I am Muḥammad, and I am Aḥmad, and I am al-Māḥī (the Eraser) by whom Allah erases disbelief, and I am al-ʿĀqib (the Last) after whom there is no one, and I am al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer) — the people will be gathered at my footsteps, and I am the Messenger of Mercy, the Messenger of Repentance, the Messenger of Battles (al-Malāḥim), and al-Muqaffā (the Final One) — I was sent last after all people, and I am Qutham." (1) Abū al-Bakhtarī said: "Qutham is the complete, the comprehensive one." And Allah knows best.

### ||| Exposition of His Miracles and Signs Indicating His Truthfulness

chapters.title_en: The Evidences of Prophethood and the Certainty of His Truthfulness (Shawāhid al-Nubuwwa wa al-Ṣidq)
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن من شاهد أحواله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصغى إلى سماع أخباره
المشتملة على أخلاقه وأفعاله وأحواله وعاداته وسجاياه وسياسته لأصناف الخلق
وهدايته إلى ضبطهم وتألفه أصناف الخلق وقوده إياهم إلى طاعته مع ما يحكى من
عجائب أجوبته في مضايق الأسئلة وبدائع تدبيراته في مصالح الخلق ومحاسن
إشاراته في تفصيل ظاهر الشرع الذي يعجز الفقهاء والعقلاء عن إدراك أوائل
دقائقها في طول أعمارهم لم يبق له ريب ولا شك في أن ذلك لم  يكن مكتسبا
بحيلة تقوم بها القوة البشرية بل لا يتصور ذلك إلا بالاستمداد من تأييد
سماوي وقوة إلهية وأن ذلك كله لا يتصور لكذاب ولا ملبس بل كانت شمائله
وأحواله شواهد قاطعة بصدقه حتى إن العربي القح كان يراه فيقول والله ما هذا
وجه كذاب فكان يشهد له بالصدق بمجرد شمائله فكيف من شاهد أخلاقه ومارس
أحواله في جميع مصادره وموارده وإنما أوردنا بعض أخلافه لتعرف محاسن
الأخلاق وليتنبه لصدقه صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلو منصبه ومكانته العظيمة عند
الله إذ آتاه الله جميع ذلك وهو رجل أمي لم يمارس العلم ولم يطالع الكتب
ولم يسافر قط في طلب علم ولم يزل بين أظهر الجهال من الأعراب يتيما ضعيفا
مستضعفا فمن أين حصل له محاسن الأخلاق والآداب ومعرفة مصالح الفقه مثلا فقط
دون غيرهم من العلوم فضلا عن معرفة الله تعالى وملائكته وكتبه وغير ذلك من
خواص النبوة لولا صريح الوحي ومن أين لقوة البشر الاستقلال بذلك فلو لم يكن
له إلا هذه الأمور الظاهرة لكان فيه كفاية
وقد ظهر من آياته ومعجزاته مالا يستريب فيه محصل فلنذكر من جملتها ما
استفاضت به الأخبار واشتملت عليه الكتب الصحيحة إشارة إلى مجامعها من غير
تطويل بحكاية التفصيل
فقد خرق الله العادة على يده غير مرة إذ شق له القمر بمكة لما سألته قريش
آية (2) وأطعم النفر الكثير في PageV02P383
منزل جابر (1) وفي منزل أبي طلحة ويوم الخندق (2) ومرة أطعم ثمانين من
أربعة أمداد شعير وعناق (3) وهو من أولاد المعز فوق العتود ومرة أكثر من
ثمانين رجلا من أقراص شعير حملها أنس في يده (4) ومرة أهل الجيش من تمر
يسير ساقته بنت بشير في يدها فأكلوا كلهم حتى شبعوا من ذلك وفضل لهم (5)
ونبع الماء من بين أصابعه عليه السلام فشرب أهل العسكر كلهم وهم عطاش
وتوضئوا من قدح صغير ضاق عن أن يبسط عليه السلام يده فيه (6) وأهراق صلى
الله عليه وسلم وضوءه في عين تبوك ولا ماء فيها ومرة أخرى في  بئر الحديبية
فجاشتا بالماء فشرب من عين تبوك أهل الجيش وهم ألوف حتى رووا وشرب من بئر
الحديبية ألف وخمسمائة ولم يكن فيها قبل ذلك ماء (7) وأمر صلى الله عليه
وسلم عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أن يزود أربعمائة راكب من تمر كان في
اجتماعه كربضة البعير وهو موضع بروكه فزودهم كلهم منه وبقي منه فحبسه (8)
ورمى الجيش بقبضة من تراب فعميت عيونهم ونزل بذلك القرآن في قوله تعالى وما
رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى (9) وأبطل الله تعالى الكهانة بمبعثه صلى الله
عليه وسلم فعدمت وكان ظاهرة موجودة (10) وحن الجذع الذي كان يخطب إليه لما
عمل له المنبر حتى سمع منه جميع أصحابه مثل صوت الإبل فضمه إليه فسكن (11)
ودعا اليهود إلى تمني الموت وأخبرهم بأنهم لا يتمنونه فحيل بينهم وبين
النطق بذلك وعجزوا عنه (12) وهذا مذكور في سورة يقرأ بها في جميع جوامع
الإسلام من شرق الأرض إلى غربها يوم الجمعة PageV02P384
جهرا تعظيما للآية التي فيها
وأخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم بالغيوب وأنذر عثمان بأن تصيبه بلوى بعدها
الجنة (1) وبأن عمارا تقتله الفئة الباغية (2) وأن الحسن يصلح الله به
فئتين من المسلمين عظيمتين (3) وأخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم عن رجل قاتل في
سبيل الله أنه من أهل النار (4) فظهر ذلك بأن ذلك الرجل قتل نفسه وهذه كلها
أشياء إلهية لا تعرف البتة بشيء من وجوه تقدمت المعرفة بها لا بنجوم ولا
بكشف ولا بخط ولا بزجر لكن بإعلام الله تعالى له ووحيه إليه
واتبعه سراقة بن مالك فساخت قدما فرسه في الأرض وأتبعه دخان حتى استغاثه
فدعا له فانطلق الفرس وأنذره بأن سيوضع في ذراعيه سوارا كسرى (5) فكان كذلك
وأخبر بمقتل الأسود العنسي الكذاب ليلة قتله وهو بصنعاء اليمن وأخبر بمن
قتله (6) وخرج على مائة من قريش ينتظرونه فوضع التراب على رءوسهم ولم يروه
(7) وشكا إليه البعير بحضرة أصحابه وتذلل له (8) وقال لنفر من أصحابه
مجتمعين أحدكم في النار ضرسه مثل أحد فماتوا كلهم على استقامة وارتد  منهم
واحد فقتل مرتدا (9) وقال لآخرين منهم آخركم موتا في النار فسقط آخرهم موتا
في النار فاحترق فيها فمات (10) ودعا شجرتين فأتتاه واجتمعتا ثم أمرهما
فافترقتا
وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو الربعة فإذا مشى مع الطوال طالهم (11) ودعا
صلى الله عليه وسلم النصارى إلى المباهلة فامتنعوا فعرفهم صلى الله عليه
وسلم أنهم إن فعلوا ذلك هلكوا فعلموا صحة قوله فامتنعوا (12) وأتاه عامر بن
الطفيل بن مالك وأربد بن قيس وهما فارسا العرب وفاتكاهم عازمين على قتله
صلى الله عليه وسلم فحيل بينهما وبين ذلك ودعا عليهما فهلك عامر بغدة وهلك
أربد بصاعقة أحرقته (13) وأخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يقتل PageV02P385
أبي بن خلف الجمحي فخدشه يوم أحد خدشا لطيفا فكانت منيته فيه (1)
وأطعم صلى الله عليه وسلم السم فمات الذي أكله معه وعاش هو صلى الله عليه
وسلم بعده أربع سنين وكلمه الذراع المسموم (2)
وأخبر عليه السلام يوم بدر بمصارع صناديد قريش ووقفهم على مصارعهم رجلا
رجلا فلم يتعد واحد منهم ذلك الموضع (3) وأنذر صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن
طوائف من أمته يغزون في البحر فكان كذلك (4) وزويت له الأرض فأري مشارقها
ومغاربها وأخبر بأن ملك أمته سيبلغ ما زوي له منها فكان كذلك فقد بلغ ملكهم
من أول المشرق من بلاد الترك إلى آخر المغرب من بحر الأندلس وبلاد البربر
ولم يتسعوا في الجنوب ولا في الشمال كما أخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم سواء
بسواء (5) وأخبر فاطمة ابنته رضي الله عنها بأنها أول أهله لحاقا به (6)
فكان كذلك
وأخبر نساءه بأن أطولهن يدا أسرعهن لحاقا به فكانت زينب بنت جحش الأسدية
أطولهن يدا بالصدقة أولهن لحوقا به رضي الله عنها (7)
ومسح ضرع شاة حائل لا لبن لها فدرت (8) وكان ذلك سبب إسلام ابن مسعود رضي
الله عنه
وفعل ذلك مرة أخرى في خيمة أم معبد الخزاعية
وندرت عين بعض أصحابه فسقطت فردها صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده فكانت أصح
عينيه وأحسنهما (9) وتفل في عين علي رضي الله عنه  وهو أرمد يوم خيبر فصح من
وقته وبعثه بالراية (10) وكانوا يسمعون تسبيح الطعام بين يديه صلى الله
عليه وسلم (11) وأصيبت رجل بعض أصحابه صلى الله عليه وسلم فمسحها بيده
فبرأت من حينها (12) وقل زاد جيش كان معه صلى الله عليه وسلم فدعا بجميع ما
بقي فاجتمع شيء يسير جدا فدعا فيه بالبركة ثم أمرهم فأخذوا فلم يبق وعاء في
العسكر إلا ملىء من ذلك (13) وحكى الحكم بن العاص بن وائل قوله الحكم بن
العاص بن وائل هكذا في النسخ وصوابه كما في الشارح الحكم بن العاص بن أمية
بن عبد شمس اه مصححه مشيته PageV02P386
صلى الله عليه وسلم مستهزئا فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كذلك فكن فلم يزل
يرتعس حتى مات (1) وخطب صلى الله عليه وسلم امرأة فقال له أبوها إن بها
برصا امتناعا من خطبته واعتذارا ولم يكن بها برص فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
فلتكن كذلك (2) فبرصت وهي أم شبيب بن البرصاء الشاعر
إلى غير ذلك من آياته ومعجزاته صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنما اقتصرنا على
المستفيض
ومن يستريب في انخراق العادة على يده ويزعم أن آحاد هذه الوقائع لم تنقل
تواترا بل المتواتر هو القرآن فقط كمن يستريب في شجاعة علي رضي الله عنه
وسخاوة حاتم الطائي ومعلوم أن آحاد وقائعهم غير متواترة ولكن مجموع الوقائع
يورث علما ضروريا ثم لا يتمارى في تواتر القرآن وهي المعجزة الكبرى الباقية
بين الخلق وليس لنبي معجزة باقية سواه صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ تحدى بها رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلغاء الخلق وفصحاء العرب وجزيرة العرب حينئذ
مملوءة بآلاف منهم والفصاحة صنعتهم وبها منافستهم ومباهاتهم
وكان ينادي بين أظهرهم أن يأتوا بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا وقال ذلك
تعجيزا لهم فعجزوا عن ذلك وصرفوا عنه حتى عرضوا أنفسهم للقتل ونساءهم
وذراريهم للسبي وما استطاعوا أن يعارضوا ولا أن يقدحوا في جزالته وحسنه ثم
انتشر ذلك بعده في أقطار العالم شرقا وغربا قرنا بعد قرن وعصرا بعد عصر  وقد
انقرض اليوم قريب من خمسمائة سنة فلم يقدر أحد على معارضته
فأعظم بغباوة من ينظر في أحواله ثم في أقواله ثم في أفعاله ثم في أخلاقه
ثم في معجزاته ثم في استمرار شرعه إلى الآن ثم في انتشاره في أقطار العالم
ثم في إذعان ملوك الأرض له في عصره وبعد عصره مع ضعفه ويتمه ثم يتمارى في
ذلك في صدقه
وما أعظم توفيق من آمن به وصدقه واتبعه في كل ما ورد وصدر فنسأل الله
تعالى أن يوفقنا للإقتداء به في الأخلاق والأفعال والأحوال والأقوال بمنه
وسعة جوده تم الجزء الثاني من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين ويليه الجزء الثالث
ويشتمل على ربع المهلكات PageV02P387
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify, be present; presence of ocular or direct evidence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony that yields necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī) — the highest epistemic grade in Kalām.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal witnessing (shuhūd) vs. metaphorical attestation (shahāda) of character as proof.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl Clause (Jumla Ḥāliyya) — circumstantial clauses describing simultaneous states, used to layer evidence cumulatively.
chapters.translation:
Know that whoever observes his states, peace be upon him, and lends ear to the hearing of his reports — which encompass his moral traits, his deeds, his conditions, his customs, his innate dispositions, and his governance of the various classes of creation, his guidance in disciplining them, his drawing together of the diverse kinds of people, his leading them to his obedience — along with what is related of the wonders of his answers in the straits of questions, the novelties of his stratagems in the welfare of creation, and the excellences of his indications in the detailing of the outward aspects of the Sacred Law, which the jurists and the intelligent are incapable of grasping the beginnings of its subtleties throughout the whole of their lives — no doubt or uncertainty remains for him that all of this was not acquired by any device that human power could accomplish. Rather, it cannot be conceived except through drawing upon a heavenly reinforcement and a divine power. And that all of this cannot be conceived from a liar nor from one who confuses. Indeed, his noble traits and his states were decisive witnesses to his truthfulness — so much so that a pure, unlettered Arab would see him and say: "By God, this is not the face of a liar!" Thus he would testify to his truthfulness merely by his outward appearance. How then for one who witnessed his moral character and practiced his states in all his comings and goings?

We have only mentioned some of his traits so that the excellences of character might be known, and so that one might be alerted to his truthfulness, peace be upon him, the loftiness of his station, and his great rank with God — since God gave him all of that while he was an unlettered man who had not practiced learning, nor studied books, nor ever traveled in search of knowledge, and who remained continually among the ignorant Bedouins, an orphan, weak, and deemed weak. From where then did he acquire the excellences of character and etiquette, and the knowledge of the welfare of jurisprudence, for example alone, apart from other sciences — let alone knowledge of God Most High, His angels, His books, and other special properties of prophethood — were it not for the plain revelation? And from where could human power independently accomplish that? If he had nothing but these outward matters, it would be sufficient.

And there have appeared from his signs and miracles that which no discerning person can doubt. So let us mention from among them what the reports have widely transmitted and what the sound books have comprised, as an indication of their collective import, without prolonging the narration of detail.

For God broke the custom (khāriq al-ʿāda) at his hand more than once: the moon was split for him in Mecca when Quraysh asked him for a sign. He fed a great multitude in the house of Jābir, and in the house of Abū Ṭalḥa, and on the Day of the Trench. Once he fed eighty men from four measures of barley and a young she-goat — one of the kids of goats above the yearling. Another time he fed more than eighty men from barley loaves that Anas carried in his hand. And once he fed the people of the army from a small amount of dates that the daughter of Bashīr carried in her hand — they all ate until they were satiated, and there remained a surplus for them. Water gushed forth from between his fingers, peace be upon him, and all the people of the army drank, though they were thirsty, and they performed ablution from a small cup too small for him to spread his hand in it. He poured out his ablution water into the spring of Tabūk, which had no water in it, and another time into the well of al-Ḥudaybiyya — and both gushed forth with water. The people of the army, numbering thousands, drank from the spring of Tabūk until quenched, and from the well of al-Ḥudaybiyya drank fifteen hundred, though before that there was no water in it. He commanded ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, to supply four hundred riders from dates that were in his gathering like the resting place of a camel — its kneeling spot — and he supplied them all from it, and a remainder stayed with him, so he kept it. He threw a handful of dust at the army and their eyes were blinded, and the Qurʾān descended regarding that in His saying, Most High: {«وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ»} ("And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw"). God Most High nullified soothsaying by his mission, peace be upon him, so it ceased to exist, though it had been a manifest phenomenon. The palm-trunk against which he used to lean while delivering the sermon moaned when the pulpit was made for him, until all his companions heard from it a sound like the moaning of a camel; he drew it to him and it became still. He called the Jews to wish for death and informed them that they would not wish for it — so they were prevented from uttering that and were incapacitated from it. This is mentioned in a chapter recited in all the congregational mosques of Islam, from the east of the earth to its west, on Friday, aloud, as a magnification of the sign contained therein.

And he informed, peace be upon him, of unseen things: he warned ʿUthmān that a trial would befall him followed by Paradise; that ʿAmmār would be killed by the transgressing faction; that al-Ḥasan would reconcile through him two great factions of the Muslims. He informed, peace be upon him, of a man who fought in the path of God that he was of the people of the Fire — and that became manifest, for that man killed himself. These are all divine matters that can never be known by any of the means by which knowledge was previously acquired — neither by stars, nor by unveiling, nor by geomancy, nor by augury — but only by God's informing him of them and His revelation to him.

Surāqa ibn Mālik followed him, and the hooves of his horse sank into the earth, and smoke pursued him until he sought his intercession; he prayed for him, and the horse was released. And he warned him that the bracelets of Khusraw would be placed upon his forearms — and so it was. He informed of the killing of al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, the liar, on the very night he was killed, while he was in Ṣanʿāʾ of Yemen, and he informed of the one who killed him. He went out against a hundred of Quraysh who were waiting for him, and he placed dust upon their heads while they did not see him. A camel complained to him in the presence of his companions and humbled itself before him. He said to a group of his companions gathered together: "One of you is in the Fire, his molar like Mount Uḥud" — and they all died upon uprightness, and one of them apostatized and was killed as an apostate. He said to others of them: "The last of you to die will be in the Fire" — and the last of them to die fell into the Fire, burned in it, and died. He called two trees, and they came to him and joined together; then he commanded them and they separated.

He was, peace be upon him, of medium stature — when he walked with tall people, he towered over them. He called the Christians to mutual cursing (mubāhala), and they refrained; he informed them, peace be upon him, that if they did so they would perish — so they knew the truth of his statement and refrained. ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl ibn Mālik and Arbad ibn Qays came to him — both the horsemen of the Arabs and their warriors — resolved upon killing him, peace be upon him; but they were prevented from that, and he prayed against them: ʿĀmir perished by a glandular swelling, and Arbad perished by a thunderbolt that burned him. He informed, peace be upon him, that he would kill Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī — and he scratched him on the Day of Uḥud with a slight scratch, and his death was in it.

He ate, peace be upon him, poisoned food, and the one who ate it with him died, while he himself, peace be upon him, lived after it four years — and the poisoned foreleg of lamb spoke to him. He informed, peace be upon him, on the Day of Badr of the places of death of the chiefs of Quraysh, and he pointed them out to their death-sites, man by man — and not one of them exceeded that spot. He warned, peace be upon him, that groups from his community would raid by sea — and so it was. The earth was folded for him, and he was shown its easts and its wests, and he informed that the dominion of his community would reach what was folded for him of it — and so it was, for their dominion reached from the beginning of the east of the lands of the Turks to the end of the west of the sea of al-Andalus and the lands of the Berbers, and they did not expand in the south nor in the north, exactly as he informed, peace be upon him, precisely. He informed his daughter Fāṭima, may God be pleased with her, that she would be the first of his family to join him — and so it was.

He informed his wives that the one with the longest hand among them would be the swiftest to join him — and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh al-Asadiyya was the longest of them in hand through charity, and the first of them to join him, may God be pleased with her.

He wiped the udder of a she-goat that had no milk, and it flowed with milk — and that was the cause of the Islam of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him. He did that another time in the tent of Umm Maʿbad al-Khuzāʿiyya.

The eye of one of his companions protruded and fell out; he, peace be upon him, returned it with his hand, and it became the soundest of his two eyes and the most beautiful of them. He spat into the eye of ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, when he was afflicted with ophthalmia on the Day of Khaybar, and he was cured from that very moment, and he sent him with the banner. They used to hear the glorification of food before him, peace be upon him. The leg of one of his companions, peace be upon him, was afflicted, and he wiped it with his hand, and it was healed instantly. The provisions of an army with him, peace be upon him, ran low; he called for all that remained, and a very small amount gathered; he invoked blessing upon it, then commanded them, and they took — and there remained no vessel in the camp except it was filled from that.

Al-Ḥakam ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil — thus in the copies, and the correct form as in the commentator is al-Ḥakam ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams — imitated his gait, peace be upon him, mockingly. He, peace be upon him, said: "Thus be!" — and he continued trembling until he died. He proposed to a woman, and her father said to her: "She has leprosy," as a refusal of his proposal and an excuse — though she had no leprosy. He, peace be upon him, said: "Let it be so!" — and she became leprous. She is the mother of Shabīb ibn al-Barṣāʾ, the poet.

And so on, beyond this, of his signs and miracles, peace be upon him. We have confined ourselves to what is widely transmitted (mustafīḍ).

And whoever doubts the breaking of custom at his hand, and claims that the individual instances of these events were not transmitted by tawātur, but rather the mutawātir is only the Qurʾān — he is like one who doubts the bravery of ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, or the generosity of Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī. It is known that the individual instances of their deeds are not mutawātir, but the totality of the deeds engenders necessary knowledge. Then one does not dispute the tawātur of the Qurʾān — and it is the greatest miracle, the enduring one among creation. No prophet has an enduring miracle besides him, peace be upon him — for the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, challenged with it the eloquent of creation and the fluent of the Arabs, and the Arabian Peninsula at that time was filled with thousands of them, eloquence being their craft, their rivalry, and their boast.

He called out among them to bring its like, even if some of them were to be helpers to others. He said that as a challenge to incapacitate them — and they were incapacitated from it and turned away from it, until they exposed themselves to killing and their women and children to captivity, and they could not oppose it nor find fault in its grandeur and beauty. Then it spread after him throughout the regions of the world, east and west, century after century and age after age — and nearly five hundred years have now passed, and no one has been able to oppose it.

How great is the stupidity of one who looks at his states, then his sayings, then his deeds, then his moral traits, then his miracles, then the continuance of his Law until now, then its spread throughout the regions of the world, then the submission of the kings of the earth to him in his time and after his time — despite his weakness and orphanhood — and then still disputes his truthfulness!

And how great is the divine success of one who believed in him, affirmed him, and followed him in all that came and went forth. So we ask God Most High to grant us success in following him in moral traits, deeds, states, and sayings — by His grace and the abundance of His bounty.

Here ends the second part of the Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences. It is followed by the third part, which comprises the Quarter of the Destructive Matters.

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

### || كتاب شرح عجائب القلب وهو الكتاب الأول من ربع المهلكات

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي تتحير دون إدراك جلاله القلوب والخواطر وتدهش في مبادي
إشراق أنواره الأحداق والنواظر المطلع على خفيات السرائر العالم بمكنونات
الضمائر المستغني في تدبير مملكته عن المشاور والموازر مقلب القلوب وغفار
الذنوب وستار العيوب ومفرج الكروب
والصلاة على سيد المرسلين وجامع شمل الدين وقاطع دابر الملحدين
وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وسلم كثيرا
أما بعد فشرف الإنسان وفضيلته التي فاق بها جملة من أصناف الخلق
باستعداده لمعرفة الله سبحانه التي هي في الدنيا جماله وكماله وفخره وفي
الآخرة عدته وذخره وإنما استعد للمعرفة بقلبه لا بجارحة من جوارحه فالقلب
هو العالم بالله
وهو المتقرب إلى الله وهو العامل لله وهو الساعي إلى الله وهو المكاشف
بما عند الله ولديه وإنما الجوارح أتباع وخدم وآلات يستخدمها القلب
ويستعملها استعمال المالك للعبد واستخدام الراعي للرعية والصانع للآلة
فالقلب هو المقبول عند الله إذا سلم من غير الله وهو المحجوب عن الله إذا
صار مستغرقا بغير الله وهو المطالب وهو المخاطب وهو المعاتب وهو الذي يسعد
بالقرب من الله فيفلح إذا زكاه وهو الذي يخيب ويشقى إذا دنسه ودساه وهو
المطيع بالحقيقة لله تعالى وإنما الذي ينتشر على الجوارح من  العبادات
أنواره وهو العاصي المتمرد على الله تعالى وإنما الساري إلى الأعضاء من
الفواحش آثاره وبإظلامه واستنارته تظهر محاسن الظاهر ومساويه إذ كل إناء
ينضح بما فيه وهو الذي إذا عرفه الإنسان فقد عرف نفسه وإذا عرف نفسه فقد
عرف ربه وهو الذي إذا جهله الإنسان فقد جهل نفسه وإذا جهل نفسه فقد جهل ربه
ومن جهل قلبه فهو بغيره أجهل إذ أكثر الخلق جاهلون بقلوبهم وأنفسهم وقد حيل
بينهم وبين أنفسهم فإن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
وحيلولته بأن يمنعه عن مشاهدته ومراقبته ومعرفة صفاته وكيفية تقلبه بين
إصبعين مع أصابع الرحمن وأنه كيف يهوى مرة إلى أسفل السافلين وينخفض إلى
أفق الشياطين وكيف يرتفع أخرى إلى أعلى عليين ويرتقي إلى عالم الملائكة
المقربين
ومن لم يعرف قلبه ليراقبه ويراعيه ويترصد لما يلوح من خزائن الملكوت عليه
وفيه فهو ممن قال الله تعالى فيه نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم
الفاسقون فمعرفة القلب وحقيقة أوصافه
PageV03P002
أصل الدين وأساس طريق السالكين
وإذ فرغنا من الشطر الأول من هذا الكتاب من النظر فيما يجري على الجوارح
من العبادات والعادات وهو العلم الظاهر ووعدنا أن نشرح في الشطر الثاني ما
يجري على القلب من الصفات المهلكات والمنجيات وهو العلم الباطن فلا بد أن
نقدم عليه كتابين كتابا في شرح عجائب صفات القلب وأخلاقه وكتابا في كيفية
رياضة القلب وتهذيب أخلاقه ثم نندفع بعد ذلك في تفصيل المهلكات والمنجيات
فلنذكر الآن من شرح عجائب القلب بطريق ضرب الأمثال ما يقرب من الأفهام
فإن التصريح بعجائبه وأسراره الداخلة في جملة عالم الملكوت مما يكل عن دركه
أكثر الأفهام

### ||| بيان معنى النفس والروح والقلب والعقل وما هو المراد بهذه الأسامي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and fluctuation; the physical organ (the heart) as the seat of constant transformation between states.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heart as the spiritual center (al-lubb) — the locus of cognition (maʿrifah), volition, and divine address; distinct from the corporeal organ.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the pine-shaped organ; metaphorical (majāz) usage denotes the subtle spiritual faculty (al-lāṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that perceives and knows.
- Sībawayh Rule: Predicate-Initial Nominal Sentences (al-ibtidāʾ bi-l-khabar) — The repeated pattern "القلب هو..." (the heart is the one who...) employs fronted predicates for emphatic exclusivity (ḥaṣr), establishing the heart's unique epistemic and spiritual agency.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.

Praise be to Allah, before Whose majesty's comprehension hearts and thoughts are bewildered, and at the first dawning of His lights, pupils and glances are dazzled — He who is aware of the hidden secrets of consciences, who knows what is concealed within breasts, who in the governance of His dominion is independent of any counselor or supporter, who overturns hearts, who forgives sins, who veils faults, and who relieves distresses.

And blessings upon the master of the messengers, the unifier of the scattered threads of religion, the cutter-off of the root of the heretics, and upon his pure and immaculate family — abundant peace.

To proceed: The honor of man and his excellence, by which he surpasses the multitude of created kinds, lies in his preparedness for the knowledge of Allah, Glorified be He — which in this world is his beauty, his perfection, and his pride, and in the Hereafter is his provision and his treasure. And he is prepared for that knowledge only through his heart (qalb), not through any limb of his limbs. For the heart is the one that knows Allah, the one that draws near to Allah, the one that acts for Allah, the one that strives toward Allah, and the one that is unveiled to what is with Allah and before Him. The limbs are but followers, servants, and instruments which the heart employs and uses — the use of a master for his slave, the employment of a shepherd for his flock, and the use of a craftsman for his tool.

Thus the heart is that which is accepted by Allah when it is sound from other-than-Allah; it is that which is veiled from Allah when it becomes engrossed in other-than-Allah; it is the one that is called to account, the one that is addressed, the one that is rebuked; it is the one that attains felicity through nearness to Allah and thus prospers when it is purified; and it is the one that fails and is wretched when it is defiled and buried. It is the one that is truly obedient to Allah, Exalted be He — for what spreads over the limbs of acts of worship are but its lights — and it is the one that is disobedient and rebellious against Allah, Exalted be He — for what courses through the organs of indecencies are but its traces. Through its darkness and its illumination, the beauties and defects of the outward appear, for every vessel exudes what it contains.

It is the one which, when a man knows it, he has known his own self (nafs); and when he knows his self, he has known his Lord. It is the one which, when a man is ignorant of it, he has been ignorant of his self; and when he is ignorant of his self, he has been ignorant of his Lord. And whoever is ignorant of his heart is even more ignorant of other things, for most of creation are ignorant of their hearts and their selves — a barrier has been set between them and their selves, for Allah sets a barrier between a man and his heart {«وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ»} (Know that Allah comes between a man and his heart — Qur'an 8:24).

And His interposition is that He prevents him from witnessing it, from watching over it, from knowing its attributes, and from understanding how it turns between two fingers among the fingers of the All-Merciful — how it descends at one moment to the lowest of the low and sinks to the horizon of the devils, and how it rises at another moment to the highest of the high and ascends to the world of the angels brought near.

And whoever does not know his heart so as to watch over it, to tend to it, and to lie in wait for what flashes upon it and within it from the treasuries of the Dominion (malakūt) — he is among those of whom Allah, Exalted be He, said: {«نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأَنْسَاهُمْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ»} (They forgot Allah, so He made them forget their own selves — those are the wicked — Qur'an 59:19). Thus the knowledge of the heart and the reality of its attributes is the root of religion and the foundation of the path of the wayfarers.

And since we have completed the first half of this book concerning what occurs upon the limbs of acts of worship and customs — which is the outward knowledge (al-ʿilm al-ẓāhir) — and we have promised to explain in the second half what occurs upon the heart of the destructive and saving attributes — which is the inward knowledge (al-ʿilm al-bāṭin) — it is necessary that we preface it with two books: a book on the explanation of the marvels of the heart's attributes and its moral qualities, and a book on the manner of disciplining the heart and refining its character. Then after that we shall proceed to the detailed exposition of the destroyers and the saviors.

Let us now mention, from the explanation of the marvels of the heart, by way of striking parables, that which brings it near to understanding — for the explicit disclosure of its marvels and its inner secrets, which fall within the totality of the world of the Dominion (malakūt), is something that most intellects are too weak to grasp.

### The Clarification of the Meaning of the Self (nafs), the Spirit (rūḥ), the Heart (qalb), and the Intellect (ʿaql), and What Is Intended by These Names

اعلم أن هذه الأسماء الأربعة تستعمل في هذه الأبواب ويقل في فحول العلماء
من يحيط بهذه الأسامي واختلاف معانيها وحدودها ومسمياتها وأكثر الأغاليط
منشؤها الجهل بمعنى هذه الأسامي واشتراكها بين مسميات مختلفة ونحن نشرح في
معنى هذه الأسامي ما يتعلق بغرضنا
اللفظ الأول لفظ القلب  وهو يطلق لمعنيين
أحدهما اللحم الصنوبري الشكل المودع في الجانب الأيسر من الصدر وهو لحم
مخصوص وفي باطنه تجويف وفي ذلك التجويف دم أسود هو منبع الروح ومعدنه ولسنا
نقصد الآن شرح شكله وكيفيته إذ يتعلق به غرض الأطباء ولا يتعلق به الأغراض
الدينية وهذا القلب موجود للبهائم بل هو موجود للميت ونحن إذا أطلقنا لفظ
القلب في هذا الكتاب لم نعن به ذلك فإنه قطعة لحم لا قدر له وهو من عالم
الملك والشهادة إذ تدركه البهائم بحاسة البصر فضلا عن الآدميين
والمعنى الثاني هو لطيفة ربانية روحانية لها بهذا القلب الجسماني تعلق
وتلك اللطيفة هي حقيقة الإنسان وهو المدرك العالم العارف من الإنسان وهو
المخاطب والمعاقب والمعاتب والمطالب ولها علاقة مع القلب الجسماني وقد
تحيرت عقول أكثر الخلق في إدراك وجه علاقته فإن تعلقه به يضاهي تعلق
الأعراض بالأجسام والأوصاف بالموصوفات أو تعلق المستعمل للآلة بالآلة أو
تعلق المتمكن بالمكان وشرح ذلك مما نتوقاه لمعنيين
أحدهما أنه متعلق بعلوم المكاشفة وليس غرضنا من هذا الكتاب إلا علوم
المعاملة
والثاني أن تحقيقه يستدعي إفشاء سر الروح وذلك مما لم يتكلم فيه رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (1) فليس لغيره أن يتكلم فيه والمقصود أنا إذا
أطلقنا لفظ القلب في هذا الكتاب أردنا به هذه اللطيفة وغرضنا ذكر أوصافها
وأحوالها لا ذكر حقيقتها في ذاتها وعلم المعاملة يفتقر إلى معرفة صفاتها
وأحوالها ولا يفتقر إلى ذكر حقيقتها
اللفظ الثاني الروح وهو أيضا يطلق فيما يتعلق بجنس غرضنا لمعنيين
أحدهما جسم لطيف منبعه تجويف القلب الجمساني فينشر بواسطة العروق الضوارب
إلى سائر أجزاء البدن وجريانه في البدن وفيضان أنوار الحياة والحس والبصر
والسمع والشم منها على أعضائها يضاهي فيضان النور من السراج الذي يدار في
زوايا البيت فإنه لا ينتهي إلى جزء من البيت إلا ويستنير به والحياة مثالها
النور الحاصل في الحيطان والروح مثالها السراج وسريان الروح وحركته في
الباطن مثال حركة السراج في جوانب البيت بتحريك محركه والأطباء إذا  أطلقوا
