يسركم فوالله ما الفقر أخشى عليكم ولكني أخشى عليكم أن تبسط عليكم الدنيا
كما بسطت على من كان قبلكم فتنافسوها كما تنافسوها فتهلككم كما أهلكتهم (1)
وقال أبو سعيد الخدري قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أكثر ما أخاف
عليكم ما يخرج الله لكم من بركات الأرض فقيل ما بركات الأرض قال زهرة
الدنيا (2)
وقال صلى  الله عليه وسلم لا تشغلوا قلوبكم بذكر الدنيا (3)
فنهى عن ذكرها فضلا عن إصابة عينها وقال عمار بن سعيد مر عيسى عليه
السلام بقرية فإذا أهلها موتى في الأفنية والطرق فقال يا معشر الحواريين إن
هؤلاء ماتوا عن سخطة ولو ماتوا عن غير ذلك لتدافنوا فقالوا يا روح الله
وددنا أن لو علمنا خبرهم فسأل الله تعالى فأوحى إليه إذا كان الليل فنادهم
يجيبوك فلما كان الليل أشرف على نشز ثم نادى يا أهل القرية فأجابه مجيب
لبيك يا روح الله فقال ما حالكم وما قصتكم قال بتنا في عافية وأصبحنا في
الهاوية قال وكيف ذاك قال بحبنا الدنيا وطاعتنا أهل المعاصي قال وكيف كان
حبكم للدنيا قال حب الصبي لأمه إذا أقبلت فرحنا بها وإذا أدبرت حزنا وبكينا
عليها قال فما بال أصحابك لم يجيبوني قال لأنهم ملجمون بلجم من نار بأيدي
ملائكة غلاظ شداد قال فكيف أجبتني أنت من بينهم قال لأني كنت فيهم ولم أكن
منهم فلما نزل بهم العذاب أصابني معهم فأنا معلق على شفير جهنم لا أدري
أأنجوا منها أم أكبكب فيها فقال المسيح للحواريين لأكل خبز الشعير بالملح
الجريش ولبس المسوح والنوم على المزابل كثير مع عافية الدنيا والآخرة وقال
أنس كانت ناقة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العضباء لا تسبق فجاء أعرابي
بناقة له فسبقها فشق ذلك على المسلمين فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه حق على
الله أن لا يرفع شيئا من الدنيا إلا وضعه (4) وقال عيسى عليه السلام من
الذي يبني على موج البحر دارا تلكم الدنيا فلا PageV03P205
تتخذوها قرارا وقيل لعيسى عليه السلام علمنا علما واحدا يحبنا الله عليه
قال ابغضوا الدنيا يحبكم الله تعالى وقال أبو الدرداء قال رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم لو تعلمون ما أعلم لضحكتم قليلا ولبكيتم كثيرا ولهانت عليكم
الدنيا ولآثرتم الآخرة (1) ثم قال أبو الدرداء من قبل نفسه لو تعلمون ما
أعلم لخرجتم إلى الصعدات تجأرون وتبكون على أنفسكم ولتركتم أموالكم لا  حارس
لها ولا راجع إليها إلا ما لابد لكم منه ولكن يغيب عن قلوبكم ذكر الآخرة
وحضرها الأمل فصارت الدنيا أملك بأعمالكم وصرتم كالذين لا يعلمون فبعضكم شر
من البهائم التي لا تدع هواها مخافة مما في عاقبته ما لكم لا تحابون ولا
تناصحون وأنتم إخوان على دين الله ما فرق بين أهوائكم إلا خبث سرائركم ولو
اجتمعتم على البر لتحاببتم ما لكم تناصحون في أمر الدنيا ولا تناصحون في
أمر الآخرة ولا يملك أحدكم النصيحة لمن يحبه ويعينه على أمر آخرته ما هذا
إلا من قلة الإيمان في قلوبكم لو كنتم توقنون بخير الآخرة وشرها كما توقنون
بالدنيا لآثرتم طلب الآخرة لأنها أملك لأموركم فإن قلتم حب العاجلة غالب
فإنا نراكم تدعون العاجلة من الدنيا للآجل منها تكدون أنفسكم بالمشقة
والاحتراف في طلب أمر لعلكم لا تدركونه فبئس القوم أنتم ما حققتم إيمانكم
بما يعرف به الإيمان البالغ فيكم فإن كنتم في شك مما جاء به محمد صلى الله
عليه وسلم فائتونا لنبين لكم ولنريكم من النور ما تطمئن إليه قلوبكم والله
ما أنتم بالمنقوصة عقولكم فنعذركم إنكم تستبينون صواب الرأي في دنياكم
وتأخذون بالحزم في أموركم ما لكم تفرحون باليسير من الدنيا تصيبونه وتحزنون
على اليسير منها يفوتكم حتى يتبين ذلك في وجوهكم ويظهر على ألسنتكم
وتسمونها المصائب وتقيمون فيها المآتم وعامتكم قد تركوا كثيرا من دينهم ثم
لا يتبين ذلك في وجوهكم ولا يتغير حالكم إني لأرى الله قد تبرأ منكم يلقى
بعضكم بعضا بالسرور وكلكم يكره أن يستقبل صاحبه بما يكره مخافة أن يستقبله
صاحبه بمثله فاصطحبتم على الغل ونبتت مراعيكم على الدمن وتصافيتم على رفض
الأجل ولوددت أن الله تعالى أراحني منكم وألحقني بمن أحب رؤيته ولو كان حيا
لم يصابركم فإن كان فيكم خير فقد أسمعتكم وإن تطلبوا ما عند الله تجدوه
يسيرا وبالله أستعين على نفسي وعليكم وقال عيسى عليه السلام يا معشر
الحواريين ارضوا بدنيء الدنيا مع سلامة الدين كما رضى أهل  الدنيا بدنيء
الدين مع سلامة الدنيا وفي معناه قيل
أرى رجالا بأدنى الدين قد قنعوا ... وما أراهم رضوا في العيش بالدون
فاستغن بالدين عن دنيا الملوك كما استغنى ... الملوك بدنياهم عن الدين
وقال عيسى عليه السلام يا طالب الدنيا لتبر تركك الدنيا أبر
وقال نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم لتأتينكم بعدي دنيا تأكل إيمانكم كما تأكل
النار الحطب (2)
وأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى عليه السلام يا موسى لا تركنن إلى حب الدنيا
فلن تأتيني بكبيرة هي أشذ منها
ومر موسى عليه السلام برجل وهو يبكي ورجع وهو يبكي فقال موسى يا رب عبدك
يبكي من مخافتك فقال يا ابن عمران لو سال دماغه مع دموع عينيه ورفع يديه
حتى يسقطا لم أغفر له وهو يحب الدنيا
الآثار قال علي رضي الله عنه من جمع فيه ست خصال لم يدع للجنة مطلبا ولا
عن النار مهربا أولها من PageV03P206
عرف الله وأطاعه وعرف الشيطان فعصاه وعرف الحق فاتبعه وعرف الباطل فاتقاه
وعرف الدنيا فرفضها وعرف الآخرة فطلبها
وقال الحسن رحم الله أقواما كانت الدنيا عندهم وديعة فأدوها إلى من
ائتمنهم عليها ثم راحوا خفافا وقال أيضا رحمه الله من نافسك في دينك فنافسه
ومن نافسك في دنياك فألقها في نحره وقال لقمان عليه السلام لابنه يا بني إن
الدنيا بحر عميق وقد غرق فيه ناس كثير فلتكن سفينتك فيه تقوى الله عز وجل
وحشوها الإيمان بالله تعالى وشراعها التوكل على الله عز وجل لعلك تنجو وما
أراك ناجيا وقال الفضيل طالت فكرتي في هذه الآية {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض
زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} وقال
بعض الحكماء إنك لن تصبح في شيء من الدنيا إلا وقد كان له أهل قبلك وسيكون
له أهل بعدك وليس لك من الدنيا إلا عشاء ليلة وغداء يوم فلا تهلك في أكله
وصم عن الدنيا وأفطر على الآخرة وإن رأس مال الدنيا الهوى وربحها النار
وقيل لبعض الرهبان كيف  ترى الدهر قال يخلق الأبدان ويجدد الآمال ويقرب
المنية ويبعد الأمنية قيل فما حال أهله قال من ظفر به تعب ومن فاته نصب وفي
ذلك قيل
ومن يحمد الدنيا لعيش يسره ... فسوف لعمري عن قليل يلومها
إذا أدبرت كانت على المرء حسرة ... وإن أقبلت كانت كثيرا همومها وقال بعض
الحكماء كانت الدنيا ولم أكن فيها وتذهب الدنيا ولا أكون فيها فلا أسكن
إليها فإن عيشها نكد وصفوها كدر وأهلها منها على وجل إما بنعمة زائلة أو
بلية نازلة أو منية قاضية وقال بعضهم من عيب الدنيا أنها لا تعطي أحدا ما
يستحق لكنها إما أن تزيد وإما أن تنقص وقال سفيان أما ترى النعم كأنها
مغضوب عليها قد وضعت في غير أهلها وقال أبو سليمان الداراني من طلب الدنيا
على المحبة لها لم يعط منها شيئا إلا أراد أكثر ومن طلب الآخرة على المحبة
لها لم يعط منها شيئا إلا أراد أكثر وليس لهذا غاية وقال رجل لأبي حازم
أشكو إليك حب الدنيا وليست لي بدار فقال انظر ما آتاكه الله عز وجل منها
فلا تأخذه إلا من حلة ولا تضعه إلا في حقه ولا يضرك حب الدنيا
وإنما قال هذا لأنه لو آخذ نفسه بذلك لألعبه حتى يتبرم بالدنيا ويطلب
الخروج منها وقال يحيى بن معاذ الدنيا حانوت الشيطان فلا تسرق من حانوته
شيئا فيجيء في طلبه فيأخذك وقال الفضيل لو كانت الدنيا من ذهب يفنى والآخرة
من خزف يبقى لكان ينبغي لنا أن نختار خزفا يبقى على ذهب يفنى فكيف وقد
اخترنا خزفا يفني على ذهب يبقى وقال أبو حازم إياكم والدنيا فإنه بلغني أنه
يوقف العبد يوم القيامة إذا كان معظما الدنيا فيقال هذا عظم ما حقره الله
وقال ابن مسعود ما أصبح أحد من الناس إلا وهو ضيف وماله عارية فالضيف مرتحل
والعارية مردودة وفي ذلك قيل
وما المال والأهلون إلا ودائع ... ولا بد يوما أن ترد الودائع
وزار رابعة أصحابها فذكروا الدنيا فأقبلوا على ذمها  فقالت اسكتوا عن
ذكرها فلولا موقعها من قلوبكم ما أكثرتم من ذكرها ألا من أحب شيئا أكثر من
ذكره وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم كيف أنت فقال
نرقع دنيانا بتمزيق ديننا ... فلا ديننا يبقى ولا ما نرقع
فطوبى لعبد آثر الله ربه ... وجاد بدنياه لما يتوقع
وقيل أيضا في ذلك
أرى طالب الدنيا وإن طال عمره ... ونال من الدنيا سرورا وأنعما
PageV03P207
كبان بنى بنيانه فأقامه ... فلما استوى ما قد بناه تهدما
وقيل أيضا في ذلك
هب الدنيا تساق إليك عفوا ... أليس مصير ذاك إلى انتقال
وما دنياك إلا مثل فيء ... أظلك ثم آذن بالزوال
وقال لقمان لابنه يا بني بع دنياك بآخرتك تربحهما جميعا ولا تبع آخرتك
بدنياك تخسرهما جميعا وقال مطرف ابن الشخير لا تنظر إلى خفض عيش الملوك
ولين رياشهم ولكن انظر إلى سرعة ظعنهم وسوء منقلبهم وقال ابن عباس إن الله
تعالى جعل الدنيا ثلاثة أجزاء جزء للمؤمن وجزء للمنافق وجزء للكافر فالمؤمن
يتزود والمنافق يتزين والكافر يتمتع وقال بعضهم الدنيا جيفة فمن أراد منها
شيئا فليصبر على معاشرة الكلاب وفي ذلك قيل يا خاطب الدنيا إلى نفسها ...
تنح عن خطبتها تسلم
إن التي تخطب غدارة ... قريبة العرس من المأتم
وقال أبو الدرداء من هوان الدنيا على الله أنه لا يعصى إلا فيها ولا ينال
ما عنده إلا بتركها
وفي ذلك قيل
إذا امتحن الدنيا لبيب تكشفت ... له عن عدو في ثياب صديق
وقيل أيضا
يا راقد الليل مسرورا بأوله ... إن الحوادث قد يطرقن أسحارا
أفنى القرون التي كانت منعمة ... كر الجديدين إقبالا وإدبارا
كم قد أبادت صروف الدهر من ملك ... قد كان في الدهر نفاعا وضرارا
يا من يعانق دنيا لا بقاء لها ... يمسي ويصبح في دنياه سفارا
هلا تركت من الدنيا معانقة ... حتى تعانق في الفردوس أبكارا
إن كنت تبغي جنان الخلد تسكنها ... فينبغي لك أن لا تأمن النارا
وقال أبو أمامة الباهلي رضي الله عنه لما بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
أتت إبليس جنوده  فقالوا قد بعث نبي وأخرجت أمة قال يحبون الدنيا قالوا نعم
قال لئن كانوا يحبون الدنيا ما أبالي أن لا يعبدوا الأوثان وإنما أغدو
عليهم وأروح بثلاث أخذ المال من غير حقه وإنفاقه في غير حقه وإمساكه عن حقه
والشر كان من هذا نبع وقال رجل لعلي كرم الله وجهه يا أمير المؤمنين صف لنا
الدنيا قال وما أصف لك من دار صح فيها سقم ومن أمن فيها ندم ومن افتقر فيها
حزن ومن استغنى فيها افتتن في حلالها الحساب وفي حرامها العقاب ومتشابهها
العتاب وقيل له ذلك مرة أخرى فقال أطول أم أقصر فقيل قصر فقال حلالها حساب
وحرامها عذاب وقال مالك بن دينار اتقوا السحارة فإنها تسحر قلوب العلماء
يعني الدنيا
وقال أبو سليمان الداراني إذا كانت الآخرة في القلب جاءت الدنيا تزاحمها
فإذا كانت الدنيا في القلب لم تزاحمها الآخرة لأن الآخرة كريمة والدنيا
لئيمة وهذا تشديد عظيم ونرجو أن يكون ما ذكره سيار بن الحكم أصح إذ قال
الدنيا والآخرة يجتمعان في القلب فأيهما غلب كان الآخر تبعا له وقال مالك
بن دينار بقدر ما تحزن للدنيا يخرج هم الآخرة من قلبك وبقدر ما تحزن للآخرة
يخرج هم الدنيا من قلبك وهذا اقتباس مما قاله علي كرم الله وجهه حيث قال
الدنيا
PageV03P208
والآخرة ضرتان فبقدر ما ترضى إحداهما تسخط الأخرى وقال الحسن والله لقد
أدركت أقواما كانت الدنيا أهون عليهم من التراب الذي تمشون عليه ما يبالون
أشرقت الدنيا أم غربت ذهبت إلى ذا أو ذهبت إلى ذا وقال رجل للحسن ما تقول
في رجل آتاه الله مالا فهو يتصدق منه ويصل منه أيحسن له أن يتعيش فيه يعني
يتنعم فقال لا لو كانت له الدنيا كلها ما كان له منها إلا الكفاف ويقدم ذلك
ليوم فقره وقال الفضيل لو أن الدنيا بحذافيرها عرضت على حلالا لا أحاسب
عليها في الآخرة لكنت أتقذرها كما يتقذر أحدكم الجيفة إذا مر بها أن تصيب
ثوبه وقيل لما قدم  عمر رضي الله عنه الشام فاستقبله أبو عبيدة بن الجراح
على الناقة مخطومة بحبل فسلم وسأله ثم أتى منزله فلم ير فيه إلا سيفه وترسه
ورحله فقال له عمر رضي الله عنه لو اتخذت متاعا فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إن
هذا يبلغنا المقيل
وقال سفيان خذ من الدنيا لبدنك وخذ من الآخرة لقلبك
وقال الحسن والله لقد عبدت بنو إسرائيل الأصنام بعد عبادتهم الرحمن بحبهم
الدنيا
وقال وهب قرأت في بعض الكتب الدنيا غنيمة الأكياس وغفلة الجهال لم
يعرفوها حتى خرجوا منها فسألوا الرجعة فلم يرجعوا وقال لقمان لابنه يا بني
إنك استدبرت الدنيا من يوم نزلتها واستقبلت الآخرة فأنت إلى دار تقرب منها
أقرب من دار تباعد عنها وقال سعيد بن مسعود إذا رأيت العبد تزداد دنياه
وتنقص آخرته وهو به راض فذلك المغون الذي يلعب بوجهه وهو لا يشعر وقال عمرو
بن العاص على المنبر والله ما رأيت قوما قط أرغب فيما كان رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم يزهد فيه منكم والله ما مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ثلاث إلا والذي عليه أكثر من الذي له (1)
وقال الحسن بعد أن تلا قوله تعالى {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} من قال ذا
قاله من خلقها ومن هو أعلم بها إياكم وما شغل من الدنيا فإن الدنيا كثيرة
الأشغال لا يفتح رجل على نفسه باب شغل إلا أوشك ذلك الباب أن يفتح عليه
عشرة أبواب وقال أيضا مسكين ابن أدم رضي بدار حلالها حساب وحرامها عذاب إن
أخذه من حله حوسب به وإن أخذه من حرام عذب به ابن آدم يستقل ماله ولا يستقل
عمله يفرح بمصيبته في دينه ويجزع من مصيبته في دنياه وكتب الحسن إلى عمر بن
عبد العزيز سلام عليك أما بعد فكأنك بآخر من كتب عليه الموت قد مات فأجابه
عمر سلام عليك كأنك بالدنيا ولم تكن وكأنك بالآخرة لم تزل وقال الفضيل بن
عياض الدخول في الدنيا هين ولكن الخروج منها شديد وقال  بعضهم عجبا لمن يعرف
أن الموت حق كيف يفرح وعجبا لمن يعرف أن النار حق كيف يضحك وعجبا لمن رأى
تقلب الدنيا بأهلها كيف يطمئن إليها وعجبا لمن يعلم أن القدر حق كيف ينصب
وقدم على معاوية رضي الله عنه رجل من نجران عمره مائتا سنة فسأله عن الدنيا
كيف وجدها فقال سنيات بلاء وسنيات رخاء يوم فيوم وليلة فليلة يولد ولد
ويهلك هالك فلولا المولود لباد الخلق ولولا الهالك ضاقت الدنيا بمن فيها
فقال له سل ما شئت قال عمر مضى فترده أو أجل حضر فتدفعه قال لا أملك ذلك
قال لا حاجة لي إليك وقال داود الطائي رحمه الله يا ابن آدم فرحت ببلوغ
أملك وإنما بلغته بانقضاه أجلك ثم سوفت بعملك كان منفعته لغيرك وقال بشر من
سأل الله الدنيا فإنما يسأله طول الوقوف بين يديه وقال أبو حازم ما في
الدنيا شيء يسرك إلا وقد ألصق الله إليه شيئا يسوءك وقال الحسن لا تخرج نفس
ابن آدم من الدنيا إلا بحسرات ثلاث أنه لم يشبع مما جمع ولم يدرك ما أمل
ولم يحسن الزاد لما يقدم عليه وقيل لبعض العباد قد نلت الغنى فقال إنما نال
الغنى من عتق من رق الدنيا وقال أبو سليمان لا يصبر PageV03P209
عن شهوات الدنيا إلا من كان في قلبه ما يشغله بالآخرة وقال مالك بن دينار
اصطلحنا على حب الدنيا فلا يأمر بعضنا بعضا ولا ينهى بعضنا بعضا ولا يدعنا
الله على هذا فليت شعري أي عذاب الله ينزل علينا وقال أبو حازم يسير الدنيا
يشغل عن كثير الآخرة وقال الحسن أهينوا الدنيا فو الله ما هي لأحد بأهنأ
منها لمن أهانها
وقال أيضا إذا أراد الله بعبد خيرا أعطاه من الدنيا عطية ثم يمسك فإذا
نفذ أعاد عليه وإذا هان عليه عبد بسط له الدنيا بسطا وكان بعضهم يقول في
دعائه يا ممسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنك أمسك الدنيا عني وقال
محمد بن المنكدر أرأيت لو  أن رجلا صام الدهر لا يفطر وقام الليل لا ينام
وتصدق بماله وجاهد في سبيل الله واجتنب محارم الله غير أنه يؤتى به يوم
القيامة فيقال إن هذا عظم في عينه ما صغره الله وصغر في عينه ما عظمه الله
كيف ترى يكون حاله فمن منا ليس هكذا الدنيا عظيمة عنده مع ما اقترفنا من
الذنوب والخطايا وقال أبو حازم اشتدت مؤنة الدنيا والآخرة فأما مؤنة الآخرة
فإنك لا تجد عليها أعوانا وأما مؤنة الدنيا فإنك لا تضرب بيدك إلى شيء منها
إلا وجدت فاجرا قد سبقك إليه وقال أبو هريرة الدنيا موقوفة بين السماء
والأرض كالشن البالي تنادي ربها منذ خلقها إلى يوم يفنيها يا رب يا رب لم
تبغضني فيقول لها اسكتي يا لا شيء وقال عبد الله بن المبارك حب الدنيا
والذنوب في القلب قد احتوشته فمتى يصل الخير إليه وقال وهب بن منبه من فرح
قلبه بشيء من الدنيا فقد أخطأ الحكمة ومن جعل شهوته تحت قدميه فرق الشيطان
من ظله ومن غلب علمه هواه فهو الغالب وقيل لبشر مات فلان فقال جمع الدنيا
وذهب إلى الآخرة ضيع نفسه قيل له إنه كان يفعل ويفعل وذكروا أبوابا من البر
فقال وما ينفع هذا وهو يجمع الدنيا وقال بعضهم الدنيا تبغض إلينا نفسها
ونحن نحبها فكيف لو تحببت إلينا وقيل لحكيم الدنيا لمن هي قال لمن تركها
فقيل الآخرة لمن هي قال لمن طلبها وقال حكيم الدنيا دار خراب وأخرب منها
قلب من يعمرها والجنة دار عمران وأعمر منها قلب من يطلبها وقال الجنيد كان
الشافعي رحمه الله من المريدين الناطقين بلسان الحق في الدنيا وعظ أخا له
في الله وخوفه بالله فقال يا أخي إن الدنيا دحض مزلة ودار مذلة عمرانها إلى
الخراب صائر وساكنها إلى القبور زائر شملها على الفرقة موقوف وغناها إلى
الفقر مصروف الإكثار فيها إعسار والإعسار فيها يسار فافزع إلى الله وارض
برزق الله لا تتسلف من دار بقائك إلى دار فنائك  فإن عيشتك فيء زائل وجدار
مائل أكثر من عملك وأقصر من أملك وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم لرجل أدرهم في
المنام أحب إليك أم دينار في اليقظة فقال دينار في اليقظة فقال كذبت لأن
الذي تحبه في الدنيا كأنك تحبه في المنام والذي لا تحبه في الآخرة كأنك لا
تحبه في اليقظة وعن إسماعيل بن عياش قال كان أصحابنا يسمون الدنيا خنزيرة
فيقولون إليك عنا يا خنزيرة فلو وجدوا لها أسماء أقبح من هذا لسموها به
وقال كعب لتحببن إليكم الدنيا حتى تعبدوها وأهلها وقال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
رحمه الله العقلاء ثلاثة من ترك الدنيا قبل أن تتركه وبنى قبره قبل أن
يدخله وأرضى خالقه قبل أن يلقاه وقال أيضا الدنيا بلغ شؤمها أن تمنيك لما
يلهيك عن طاعة الله فكيف الوقوع فيها وقال بكر بن عبد الله من أراد أن
يستغني عن الدنيا بالدنيا كان كمطفيء النار بالتبن وقال بندار إذا رأيت
أبناء الدنيا يتكلمون في الزهد فاعلم أنهم في سخرة الشيطان وقال أيضا من
أقبل على الدنيا أحرقته نيرانها يعني الحرص حتى يصير رمادا ومن أقبل على
الآخرة صفته بنيرانها فصار سبيكة ذهب ينتفع به ومن أقبل على الله عز وجل
أحرقته نيران التوحيد فصار جوهرا لا حد لقيمته وقال علي كرم الله وجهه إنما
الدنيا ستة أشياء مطعوم ومشروب وملبوس ومركوب
PageV03P210
ومنكوح ومشموم فأشرف المطعومات العسل وهو مذقة ذباب وأشرف المشروبات
الماء ويستوي فيه البر والفاجر وأشرف الملبوسات الحرير وهو نسج دودة وأشرف
المركوبات الفرس وعليه يقتل الرجال وأشرف المنكوحات المرأة وهي مبال في
مبال وإن المرأة لتزين أحسن شيء منها ويراد أقبح شيء منها وأشرف المشمومات
المسك وهو دم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ م م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is blame, censure, and dispraise — the opposite of praise (madḥ). It denotes the act of attributing deficiency or reprehensibility to something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, dhamm is the divine and prophetic declaration of a thing's lowliness in the scale of sacred value, particularly the dunyā as that which distracts from the Hereafter (ākhirah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) when describing actual censure; metaphorically (majāz) when the dunyā itself is personified as a speaking, blameworthy entity in the hadiths.
- Root: د ن و (d-n-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is proximity, lowness, and that which is near or inferior. The dunyā is the "lower" or "nearer" abode, contrasted with the ākhirah (the "last" or "utmost").
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The dunyā is the present life of trial, defined by its temporality and its role as a testing ground; its blameworthiness lies in its capacity to veil the soul from God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally denotes the nearer world; rhetorically, it becomes a symbol of all that is transient, deceptive, and opposed to the enduring abode.
- Root: ز ه د (z-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is renunciation, abstention, and turning away from something with deliberate disregard.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Zuhd is the virtuous disposition of the heart that esteems the dunyā as insignificant, not merely outward poverty but inward detachment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal renunciation of objects; metaphorical renunciation of the heart's attachment to them, which is the true zuhd praised by the prophets.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Emphasis and Restriction (Qaṣr bi-al-Ḥaṣr) — In phrases like "the world is the prison of the believer," the predicate is restricted to the subject, establishing an exclusive equation that demands the listener's full acceptance of the metaphorical equivalence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The verses censuring this world and their examples are many, and most of the Qur'an is comprised of blaming the world, turning creation away from it, and summoning them to the Hereafter. Indeed, that is the very purpose of the prophets, upon them be prayers and peace — they were not sent except for that. Thus there is no need to cite Qur'anic verses as evidence, for their clarity is manifest. We shall only mention some of the reports (akhbār) transmitted concerning this.

It has been related that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a dead sheep and said: "Do you see this sheep as insignificant to its owners?" They said: "Due to its insignificance, they cast it away." He said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, the world is more insignificant to God than this sheep is to its owners. And if the world had weighed before God the wing of a gnat, He would not have given an unbeliever a single drink of water from it."

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the unbeliever."

And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The world is accursed, accursed is all that is in it, except what is of it (i.e., for God's sake)."

And Abu Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever loves his world harms his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter harms his world. So prefer that which remains over that which perishes."

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Love of the world is the head of every sin."

And Zayd ibn Arqam said: We were with Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may God be pleased with him, and he called for a drink. Water and honey were brought to him. When he brought it near his mouth, he wept until he made his companions weep. They fell silent, but he did not. Then he returned and wept until they thought they would not be able to question him. He said: Then he wiped his eyes, and they said: "O Caliph of the Messenger of God, what has made you weep?" He said: "I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I saw him pushing something away from himself, though I saw no one with him. I said: 'O Messenger of God, what is it that you are pushing away from yourself?' He said: 'This world was presented to me. I said to it: "Away from me!" Then it returned and said: "If you escape from me, those after you will not escape from me."'"

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "O wonder, all wonder, for one who believes in the abode of everlastingness yet strives for the abode of delusion."

And it is related that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood by a rubbish heap and said: "Come to the world!" Then he took a tattered rag that had rotted on that heap, and bones that had decayed, and said: "This is the world."

This is an indication that the adornment of the world will become worn like those rags, and that the bodies seen therein will become decayed bones.

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed the world is sweet and green, and God has made you vicegerents over it, so He is watching how you act. When the Children of Israel were given abundance in the world and it was spread out for them, they went astray in ornament, women, perfume, and garments."

And Jesus, upon him be peace, said: "Do not take the world as a lord, lest it take you as slaves. Store your treasure with One Who will not lose it. For the owner of the world's treasure fears affliction upon it, but the owner of God's treasure fears no affliction." And he, upon him be the most excellent prayers and peace, said: "O company of disciples, I have overturned the world before you on its face, so do not raise it up after me. For part of the world's vileness is that God is disobeyed within it, and part of the world's vileness is that the Hereafter is not attained except by abandoning it. Verily, cross through the world and do not build it up. Know that the root of every sin is love of the world. How many an hour of lust has bequeathed its people a long sorrow."

And he also said: "I have spread the world out for you, and you have sat upon its back. So let not the kings and women contend with you over it. As for the kings, do not contend with them over the world, for they will not oppose you as long as you leave them and their world alone. As for the women, guard against them through fasting and prayer." And he also said: "The world is both a seeker and a sought. The seeker of the Hereafter is sought by the world until his provision in it is completed. The seeker of the world is sought by the Hereafter until death comes and seizes him by the neck."

And Mūsā ibn Yasār said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, created no creature more hateful to Him than the world, and since He created it, He has never looked upon it."

And it is related that Solomon son of David, upon them both be peace, passed in his procession, with the birds shading him and the jinn and humans to his right and left. He passed by a worshipper from the Children of Israel who said: "By God, O son of David, God has indeed given you a mighty kingdom." Solomon heard him and said: "A single glorification (tasbīḥah) in the scroll of a believer is better than what has been given to the son of David. For what the son of David has been given will pass away, while the tasbīḥah remains."

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "{«أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ»} (Mutual rivalry in increase diverts you) — the son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth!' But is there anything of your wealth for you except what you ate and consumed, or wore and wore out, or gave in charity and thus preserved?"

The hadith "The world is the abode of one who has no abode" — Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, restricting it to this wording and to his saying: "And for it gathers one who has no intellect," without the rest. Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab added from his chain: "And wealth for one who has no wealth." Its chain is good.

The hadith "Whoever wakes up with the world as his greatest concern is not of God in anything, and God affixes to his heart four traits" — al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in al-Awsaṭ from the hadith of Abū Dharr without his saying "and God affixes to his heart." Likewise Ibn Abī al-Dunyā narrated it from the hadith of Anas with a weak chain, and al-Ḥākim from the hadith of Ḥudhayfah. The owner of al-Firdaws narrated this addition alone from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, and both are weak.

The hadith of Abū Hurayrah: "Shall I show you the entire world with all that is in it?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." So he took my hand and brought me to a valley of the valleys of Medina, and behold, there was a rubbish heap — I have found no basis for it.

And it is related that when God, Mighty and Majestic, brought Adam down to the earth, He said to him: "A son for ruin, born for annihilation."

And Dāwūd ibn Hilāl said: It is written in the scrolls of Abraham, upon him be peace: "O world, how insignificant you are to the righteous! You adorn and beautify yourself for them, yet I have cast into their hearts hatred of you and turning away from you. I created no creature more insignificant to Me than you. All your affair is small, and to annihilation it returns. I decreed upon you on the day I created you that you would not endure for anyone, nor would anyone endure for you. Even if your companion is miserly with you and stingy toward you, blessed are the righteous who have shown Me from their hearts contentment, and from their consciences truthfulness and uprightness. Blessed are they! What reward they have with Me when they arrive from their graves — only light running before them, and angels surrounding them, until I deliver them to what they hope of My mercy."

And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The world has been suspended between heaven and earth since God created it; He has never looked upon it. And on the Day of Resurrection it will say: 'O Lord, make me the portion of the least of Your friends today.' He will say: 'Be silent, O nothing! I was not pleased with you for them in the world, that I should be pleased with you for them today.'"

And it is related in the accounts of Adam, upon him be peace, that when he ate from the tree, his stomach moved to expel the burden — and this had not been placed in any of the foods of Paradise except that tree; therefore they were forbidden from eating it. He said: So he began to wander in Paradise, and God commanded an angel to address him. He said: "Say to him: 'What do you want?'" Adam said: "I want to put down the harm in my belly." So it was said to the angel: "Say to him: 'In what place do you want to put it — upon the couches, or upon the thrones, or upon the rivers, or beneath the shades of the trees? Do you see here any place suitable for that? Descend to the world.'"

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "There will surely come peoples on the Day of Resurrection whose deeds are like the mountains of Tihāmah, yet they will be commanded to the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of God, were they praying?" He said: "Yes, they used to pray and fast and take a portion of the night. But when something of the world was presented to them, they leapt upon it."

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in one of his sermons: "The believer is between two fears: between a term that has passed, of which he does not know what God has done with it, and a term that remains, of which he does not know what God will decree in it. So let the servant take provision from himself for himself, from his world for his Hereafter, from his life for his death, from his youth for his old age. For the world was created for you, and you were created for the Hereafter. By Him in Whose hand is my soul, after death there is no opportunity for appeasement, and after the world there is no abode but Paradise or the Fire."

And Jesus, upon him be peace, said: "Love of the world and the Hereafter cannot be straight in a believer, just as water and fire cannot be straight in a single vessel."

And it is related that Gabriel, upon him be peace, said to Noah, upon him be peace: "O longest-lived of the prophets, how did you find the world?" He said: "Like a house with two doors — I entered through one and exited through the other."

It was said to Jesus, upon him be peace: "If only you took a house to shelter you." He said: "Two days suffice us — those of those who came before us."

And our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Beware of the world, for it is more sorcerous than Hārūt and Mārūt."

And from al-Ḥasan: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out one day to his companions and said: "Is there any among you who wishes that God remove his blindness and make him seeing? Verily, whoever desires the world and lengthens his hope in it, God blinds his heart to the measure of that. And whoever renounces the world and shortens his hope in it, God gives him knowledge without learning and guidance without being guided. Verily, after you there will come a people for whom kingship will not be straight except through killing and tyranny, nor wealth except through pride and miserliness, nor love except through following caprice. Whoever of you reaches that time and endures poverty while able to have wealth, endures hatred while able to have love, endures humiliation while able to have honor — seeking thereby only the Face of God — God will give him the reward of fifty truthful ones."

The hadith of al-Ḥasan, "Is there any among you who wishes that God remove his blindness" — Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab narrated it from his chain in this manner, as a mursal (interrupted chain). In it is Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ashʿath, about whom Abū Ḥātim spoke critically.

And it is related that Jesus, upon him be peace, was hard pressed one day by rain, thunder, and lightning, and he began seeking something to take refuge in. His eye fell upon a tent from afar, so he came to it — and behold, there was a woman in it. He turned away from her. Then he came upon a cave in a mountain, and entered it — and behold, there was a lion in it. He placed his hand upon it and said: "My God, You have made for everything a refuge, but You have made no refuge for me." So God, Exalted, revealed to him: "Your refuge is in the resting place of My mercy. I will marry you on the Day of Resurrection to a hundred houris whom I created with My own hand. I will feed you at your wedding for four thousand years, each day of which is like the age of the world. And I will command a crier to cry: 'Where are the renouncers of the world? Come visit the wedding of the renouncer of the world, Jesus son of Mary.'"

And Jesus son of Mary, upon him be peace, said: "Woe to the owner of the world — how will he die and leave it and all that is in it, while it deceives him and he trusts it and relies upon it, and it abandons him? And woe to the deluded — how will they be shown what they hate, and parted from what they love, and visited by what they were promised? And woe to the one whose concern is the world and whose work is sins — how will he be disgraced tomorrow by his sin?"

And it is said: God, Exalted, revealed to Moses, upon him be peace: "O Moses, what have you to do with the abode of the wrongdoers? It is not for you an abode. Remove your concern from it and part from it with your intellect. Wretched is that abode, except for a worker who works in it — then excellent is that abode. O Moses, I am lying in wait for the wrongdoer until I take from him for the wronged."

And it is related that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, and he brought wealth from Bahrain. The Anṣār heard of Abū ʿUbaydah's arrival, so they attended the dawn prayer with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished the prayer, he turned away, and they intercepted him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled when he saw them, then said: "I think you have heard that Abū ʿUbaydah has brought something." They said: "Indeed, O Messenger of God." He said: "Then rejoice and hope for what pleases you. By God, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear for you that the world will be spread out for you as it was spread out for those before you, and you will vie for it as they vied for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them."

And Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The thing I most fear for you is what God brings forth for you of the blessings of the earth." It was said: "What are the blessings of the earth?" He said: "The bloom of the world."

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Do not occupy your hearts with the remembrance of the world." Thus he forbade even mentioning it, let alone attaining its substance.

And ʿAmmār ibn Saʿīd said: Jesus, upon him be peace, passed by a village and found its people dead in the courtyards and roads. He said: "O company of disciples, these died in wrath. Had they died otherwise, they would have buried one another." They said: "O Spirit of God, we wish we knew their story." So he asked God, Exalted, and He revealed to him: "When it is night, call out to them, and they will answer you." When night came, he ascended a high place and called: "O people of the village!" A responder answered: "At your service, O Spirit of God." He said: "What is your state and your story?" He said: "We spent the night in well-being and woke in the abyss." He said: "How is that?" He said: "By our love of the world and our obedience to the people of sin." He said: "And how was your love of the world?" He said: "Like a child's love for its mother — when she came, we rejoiced at her; when she departed, we grieved and wept over her." He said: "What of your companions — why did they not answer me?" He said: "Because they are muzzled with muzzles of fire in the hands of harsh, severe angels." He said: "Then how did you answer me, among them?" He said: "Because I was among them but not of them. When the punishment descended upon them, it struck me with them, and I am now suspended on the brink of Hell — I do not know whether I will be saved from it or hurled into it." So the Messiah said to the disciples: "Eating barley bread with coarse salt, wearing sackcloth, and sleeping on rubbish heaps is much, alongside the well-being of the world and the Hereafter."

And Anas said: The she-camel of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, al-ʿAḍbāʾ, was never outrun. Then a Bedouin came with his she-camel and outran her. That grieved the Muslims. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "It is a right upon God that He raises nothing of the world except that He lowers it."

And Jesus, upon him be peace, said: "Who builds a house upon the waves of the sea? That is the world. So do not take it as a dwelling."

And it was said to Jesus, upon him be peace: "Teach us a single knowledge by which God will love us." He said: "Hate the world, and God will love you."

And Abū al-Dardāʾ said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, the world would become insignificant to you, and you would prefer the Hereafter."

Then Abū al-Dardāʾ said of his own accord: "If you knew what I know, you would go out to the high places, crying aloud and weeping over yourselves, and you would leave your wealth with no guardian and no one to return to it — except what you cannot do without. But the remembrance of the Hereafter is veiled from your hearts, and hope has attended it, so the world has become more master of your deeds, and you have become like those who do not know. Some of you are worse than beasts that do not abandon their caprice for fear of its consequences. What is the matter with you — you do not love one another, nor counsel one another sincerely, though you are brothers in the religion of God? Nothing divides your caprices except the vileness of your inner consciences. If you gathered upon righteousness, you would love one another. What is the matter with you — you counsel sincerely in the matter of the world but not in the matter of the Hereafter? None of you possesses sincere counsel for the one he loves, to aid him in his affair of the Hereafter. This is nothing but the paucity of faith in your hearts. If you were certain of the good of the Hereafter and its evil, as you are certain of the world, you would prefer seeking the Hereafter, for it is more master of your affairs. If you say: 'Love of the immediate is dominant' — then we see you abandoning the immediate of the world for its deferred, exhausting yourselves with hardship and toil in seeking something you may never attain. Wretched are you as a people! You have not realized your faith by that by which mature faith is known. If you are in doubt about what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, then come to us that we may clarify for you and show you of the light that will settle your hearts. By God, you are not deficient in intellects, so we excuse you not — you discern sound judgment in your worldly affairs and take precaution in your matters. What is the matter with you — you rejoice at the little of the world you attain, and grieve at the little of it that escapes you, until that shows in your faces and appears on your tongues, and you call them 'calamities' and hold mourning assemblies for them. Yet the common folk among you have abandoned much of their religion, and that does not show in your faces, nor does your state change. I see that God has disowned you — you meet one another with joy, and each of you hates to face his companion with what he dislikes, for fear that his companion will face him with the like. So you have consorted upon rancor, your pastures have grown upon dung, and you have made peace upon the rejection of the term. I wish that God would give me rest from you and join me with those I love to see — even if he were alive, he would not endure you. If there is good in you, I have made you hear. And if you seek what is with God, you will find it easy. And by God, I seek help against myself and against you."

And Jesus, upon him be peace, said: "O company of disciples, be content with the lowly of the world alongside the soundness of religion, just as the people of the world are content with the lowly of religion alongside the soundness of the world."

And in its meaning it was said:
"I see men content with the least of religion... and I do not see them content with the lowly in life.
So be rich through religion over the wealth of kings, just as kings are rich through their world over religion."

And Jesus, upon him be peace, said: "O seeker of the world to be purified — your abandoning the world is more pure."

And our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "After me, a world will surely come to you that will devour your faith as fire devours firewood."

And God, Exalted, revealed to Moses, upon him be peace: "O Moses, do not lean toward love of the world, for no great sin will come to Me from you more stubborn than it."

And Moses, upon him be peace, passed by a man who was weeping, and returned while he was still weeping. Moses said: "O Lord, Your servant weeps from fear of You." He said: "O son of ʿImrān, even if his brain flowed with the tears of his eyes, and he raised his hands until they fell off, I would not forgive him while he loves the world."

THE SAYINGS (Āthār):
ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "Whoever gathers six traits in himself has left no request for Paradise unattained and no escape from the Fire: first, that he knows God and obeys Him; knows Satan and disobeys him; knows the truth and follows it; knows falsehood and guards against it; knows the world and rejects it; and knows the Hereafter and seeks it."

And al-Ḥasan said: "May God have mercy on peoples for whom the world was a trust — they returned it to the One Who entrusted them with it, then departed light." And he also said, may God have mercy on him: "Whoever vies with you in your religion, vie with him; and whoever vies with you in your world, throw it at his throat."

And Luqmān, upon him be peace, said to his son: "O my son, the world is a deep sea in which many people have drowned. Let your ship in it be the fear of God, Mighty and Majestic; its stuffing, faith in God, Exalted; its sail, trust in God, Mighty and Majestic. Perhaps you will be saved — but I do not see you as saved."

And al-Fuḍayl said: "My reflection was long upon this verse: {«إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا وَإِنَّا لَجَاعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا»} (Indeed We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it, to test them which of them is best in deed. And indeed We will make what is upon it a barren plain)."

And some of the wise said: "You will not wake in anything of the world except that it had owners before you and will have owners after you. You have nothing of the world but the supper of a night and the breakfast of a day — so do not perish in eating it. Fast from the world and break your fast upon the Hereafter. The capital of the world is caprice, and its profit is the Fire."

And it was said to one of the monks: "How do you see time?" He said: "It wears out bodies, renews hopes, brings death near, and distances wishes." It was said: "Then what is the state of its people?" He said: "Whoever seizes it is weary, and whoever misses it is exhausted." And in that it was said:
"And whoever praises the world for an easy life... soon, by my life, will blame it after a little.
When it turns away, it is regret upon a man... and when it turns toward, its cares are many."

And some of the wise said: "The world was, and I was not in it; and the world will go, and I will not be in it. So I do not settle in it, for its life is wretched, its clarity is turbid, and its people are in dread of it — either a passing blessing, or a descending affliction, or a decisive death."

And some of them said: "Part of the world's defect is that it gives no one what he deserves — rather, it either increases or decreases."

And Sufyān said: "Do you not see blessings as though they are objects of wrath, placed among those who are not their people?"

And Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "Whoever seeks the world out of love for it is not given anything of it except that he wants more. And whoever seeks the Hereafter out of love for it is not given anything of it except that he wants more — and this has no end."

And a man said to Abū Ḥāzim: "I complain to you of love of the world, and it is not my abode." He said: "Look at what God, Mighty and Majestic, has given you of it — take it only from its lawful place, and place it only in its right. And love of the world will not harm you." He only said this because if he had constrained himself to that, it would have wearied him until he became disgusted with the world and sought to exit from it.

And Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "The world is Satan's shop. Do not steal anything from his shop, lest he come seeking it and seize you."

And al-Fuḍayl said: "If the world were gold that perishes and the Hereafter were pottery that remains, it would behoove us to choose pottery that remains over gold that perishes. How then, when we have chosen pottery that perishes over gold that remains?"

And Abū Ḥāzim said: "Beware of the world, for it has reached me that the servant who magnifies the world will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: 'This is one who magnified what God has made insignificant.'"

And Ibn Masʿūd said: "No one wakes among people except that he is a guest, and his wealth is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned." And in that it was said:
"And wealth and family are but trusts... and inevitably one day the trusts are returned."

And Rābiʿah was visited by her companions, and they mentioned the world and began to blame it. She said: "Be silent about mentioning it. Were it not for its place in your hearts, you would not multiply its mention. Verily, whoever loves a thing multiplies its mention."

And it was said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham: "How are you?" He said:
"We patch our world by tearing our religion... so neither our religion remains, nor what we patch.
Blessed is a servant who prefers God his Lord... and gives generously of his world for what he anticipates."

And it was also said in that:
"I see the seeker of the world, though his life be long... and he attains of the world joy and comforts,
Like a builder who builds his structure and raises it... then when what he built is complete, it collapses."

And it was also said in that:
"Grant that the world is driven to you freely... is not its end to departure?
And your world is but like a shade... that covers you, then announces its passing."

And Luqmān said to his son: "O my son, sell your world for your Hereafter, and you will profit both. Do not sell your Hereafter for your world, for you will lose both."

And Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: "Do not look at the ease of kings' living and the softness of their garments, but look at the swiftness of their departure and the evil of their final return."

And Ibn ʿAbbās said: "God, Exalted, has made the world three parts: a part for the believer, a part for the hypocrite, and a part for the unbeliever. The believer takes provision, the hypocrite adorns himself, and the unbeliever enjoys himself."

And some of them said: "The world is a carcass. Whoever wants something of it, let him endure the company of dogs." And in that it was said:
"O suitor of the world to itself... withdraw from courting it, and you will be safe.
The one you court is treacherous... its wedding is near to the mourning."

And Abū al-Dardāʾ said: "Part of the world's insignificance before God is that He is not disobeyed except in it, and what is with Him is not attained except by abandoning it." And in that it was said:
"When a wise man tests the world, it unveils to him... an enemy in the clothes of a friend."

And it was also said:
"O sleeper of the night, joyful in its beginning... verily calamities may strike at dawns.
It has annihilated the generations that lived in comfort... by the turning of the two new days, coming and going.
How many a king has the vicissitudes of time destroyed... who was in time both beneficial and harmful.
O you who embraces a world with no endurance... you spend evening and morning in your world as a traveler.
Why do you not leave off embracing the world... until you embrace in Paradise the virgins?
If you seek the gardens of eternity to dwell in... then it behooves you not to feel safe from the Fire."

And Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, may God be pleased with him, said: When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, Satan's troops came to him and said: "A prophet has been sent, and a community has been brought forth." He said: "Do they love the world?" They said: "Yes." He said: "If they love the world, I care not whether they worship idols. I will only come at them morning and evening with three things: taking wealth from other than its right, spending it in other than its right, and withholding it from its right. And evil springs from this."

And a man said to ʿAlī, may God honor his face: "O Commander of the Faithful, describe the world to us." He said: "What shall I describe to you of an abode in which health is followed by sickness, security by regret, poverty by grief, and wealth by temptation? In its lawful is reckoning, in its unlawful is punishment, and in its ambiguous is reproach." And it was said to him another time: "Long or short?" It was said: "Short." He said: "Its lawful is reckoning, and its unlawful is torment."

And Mālik ibn Dīnār said: "Beware of the sorceress,

chapters.title_en: Exposition of Admonitions Concerning the Blame of This World and Its Description
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| بيان المواعظ في ذم الدنيا وصفتها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ م م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of blame, censure, or dispraise — the opposite of praise (ḥamd); denotes the act of attributing deficiency or reprehensibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, dhamm of al-dunyā refers to the Quranic and prophetic censure of the worldly life as a veil from the Hereafter — not the physical creation itself, but the attachment (ʿalāqah) to it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) blame is directed at a person or act; here it is metaphorical (majāz) — the world is blamed insofar as it is a station of trial (dār al-ibtilāʾ), not as an essence.
- Root: و ع ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Admonition, exhortation, or reminder that softens the heart and incites to righteousness; combines warning (takhwīf) with counsel (naṣīḥah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Waʿẓ is a Quranic mode of guidance (e.g. {فَاعْتَبِرُوا يَا أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ}) that addresses the soul’s heedlessness (ghaflah) through remembrance (tadhkīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its genuine sense — a structured discourse aimed at moral reform, not mere information.
- Root: ص و ف (ṣ-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Description, attribute, or quality; also the root of ṣifah (adjective/attribute) and taṣwīf (mystical path) — indicating the act of delineating characteristics.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, ṣifah denotes an essential or accidental attribute; here it refers to the moral and existential characteristics of al-dunyā as a transient abode.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of observable traits; no metaphorical extension intended — the world’s blameworthy features are enumerated plainly.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "في ذم الدنيا وصفتها" joins two genitive objects (dhamm and ṣifah) under a single preposition (fī), where the second term (ṣifah) is not redundant but adds a distinct dimension: the blame (dhamm) is the judgment, while the description (ṣifah) is the evidential basis for that judgment.
chapters.translation: I say: This section comprises an exposition of admonitions (waʿāẓ) concerning the blame (dhamm) of this world (al-dunyā) and its description (ṣifah) — that the servant may come to know its true nature, and thereby detach his heart from its allurements, and turn his aspiration wholly toward the Abode of Permanence (dār al-qarār). For the world is but a passage (maʿbar) and a bridge, not a dwelling; and whoever takes it as a home has erred in his judgment, and whoever trusts in it has been deceived by a mirage. Its description is that it is a vanishing shadow, a fleeting pleasure, a borrowed ornament — its sweetness is mixed with bitterness, its joy with sorrow, its youth with decrepitude, and its life with death. Blessed is he who regards it with the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah), and takes from it only as a provision (zād) for the journey to his Lord, and does not let its vanities (zakhārif) divert him from the remembrance of his meeting with Him. And in what follows, I shall unfold its blameworthy traits and its deceptive qualities, in accordance with the Book and the Sunnah, and with the sayings of the sages (ḥukamāʾ) and the verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn) — that the seeker may be awakened from his slumber, and the heedless may return to his senses.

chapters.title_en: On the Blameworthiness of This World and the Description of Its Deception
chapters.arabic_text:
قال بعضهم يا أيها الناس اعملوا على مهل وكونوا من الله على وجل ولا
تغتروا بالأمل ونسيان الأجل ولا تركنوا إلى الدنيا فإنها غدارة خداعة قد
تزخرف لكم بغرورها وفتنتكم بأمانيها وتزينت لخطابها فأصبحت كالعروس المجلية
العيون إليها ناظرة والقلوب عليها  عاكفة والنفوس لها عاشقة فكم من عاشق لها
قتلت ومطمئن إليها خذلت فانظروا إليها بعين الحقيقة فإنها دار كثير بوائقها
وذمها خالقها جديدها يبلى وملكها يفنى وعزيزها يذل وكثيرها يقل ودها يموت
وخيرها يفوت فاستيقظوا رحمكم الله من غفلتكم وانتبهوا من رقدتكم قبل أن
يقال فلان عليل أو مدنف ثقيل فهو على الدواء من دليل وهل إلى الطبيب من
سبيل فتدعى له الأطباء ولا يرجى له الشفاء ثم يقال فلان أوصى ولماله أحصى
ثم يقال قد ثقل لسانه فما يكلم إخوانه ولا يعرف جيرانه وعرق عند ذلك جبينك
وتتابع أنينك وثبت يقينك وطمحت جفونك وصدقت ظنونك وتلجلج لسانك وبكى إخوانك
وقيل لك هذا ابنك فلان وهذا أخوك فلان ومنعت من الكلام فلا تنطق وختم على
لسانك فلا ينطلق ثم حل بك القضاء وانتزعت نفسك من الأعضاء ثم عرج بها إلى
السماء فاجتمع عند ذلك إخوانك وأحضرت أكفانك فغسلوك وكفنوك فانقطع عوادك
واستراح حسادك وانصرف أهلك إلى مالك وبقيت مرتهنا بأعمالك وقال بعضهم لبعض
الملوك إن أحق الناس بذم الدنيا وقلاها من بسط له فيها وأعطى حاجته منها
لأنه يتوقع آفة تعدو على ماله فتجتاحه أو على جمعه فتفرقه أو تأتي سلطانه
فتهدمه من القواعد أو تدب إلى جسمه فتسقمه أو تفجعه بشيء هو ضنين به بين
أحبابه فالدنيا أحق بالذم هي الآخذة ما تعطي الراجعة فيما تهب بينا هي تضحك
صاحبها إذا أضحكت منه غيره وبينا تبكي له إذ أبكت عليه وبينا هي تبسط كفها
بالإعطاء إذ بسطتها بالاسترداد فتعقد التاج على رأس صاحبها اليوم وتعفره
بالتراب غدا سواء عليها ذهاب ما ذهب وبقاء ما بقي تجد في الباقي من الذاهب
خلفا وترضى بكل من كل بدلا وكتب الحسن البصري إلى عمر بن عبد العزيز أما
بعد فإن الدنيا دار ظعن ليست بدار إقامة وإنما أنزل آدم عليه السلام من
الجنة إلى عقوبة فاحذرها يا أمير المؤمنين فإن الزاد منها تركها والغني
منها فقرها لها في كل حين قتيل تذل  من أعزها وتفقر من جمعها هي كالسم يأكله
من لا يعرفه وفيه حتفه فكن فيها كالمداوي جراحه يحتمي قليلا مخافة ما يكره
طويلا ويصبر على شدة الدواء مخافة طول الداء فاحذر هذه الدار الغدارة
الختالة الخداعة التي قد تزينت بخدعها وفتنت بغرورها حلت بآمالها وسوفت
بخطابها فأصبحت كالعروس المجلية العيون إليها ناظرة والقلوب عليها والهة
والنفوس لها عاشقة وهي لأزواجها كلهم قالية فلا الباقي بالماضي معتبر ولا
الآخر بالأول مزدجر ولا العارف بالله عز وجل حين أخبره عنها مدكر فعاشق لها
قد ظفر منها بحاجته فاغتر وطغى ونسي المعاد فشغل فيها لبه حتى زلت به قدمه
فعظمت ندامته وكثرت حسرته واجتمعت عليه سكرات الموت وتألمه وحسرات الفوت
بغصته وراغب فيها لم يدرك منها ما طلب ولم يروح نفسه من التعب فخرج بغير
زاد وقدم
PageV03P211
على غير مهاد فاحذرها يا أمير المؤمنين وكن أسر ما تكون فيها أحذر ما
تكون لها فإن صاحب الدنيا كلما اطمأن منها إلى سرور أشخصته إلى مكروه السار
في أهلها غار والنافع فيها غدار ضار وقد وصل الرخاء منها بالبلاء وجعل
البقاء فيها إلى فناء فسروها مشوب بالأحزان لا يرجع منها ما ولى وأدبر ولا
يدري ما هو آت فينتظر أمانيها كاذبة وآمالها باطلة وصفوها كدر وعيشها نكد
وابن آدم فيها على خطر إن عقل ونظر فهو من النعماء على خطر ومن البلاء على
الحذر فلو كان الخالق لم يخبر عنها خبرا ولم يضرب لها مثلا لكانت الدنيا قد
أيقظت النائم ونبهت الغافل فكيف وقد جاء من الله عز وجل عنها زاجرا وفيها
واعظ فما لها عند الله جل ثناؤه قدر وما نظر إليها منذ خلقها ولقد عرضت على
نبيك صلى الله عليه وسلم بمفاتيحها وخزائنها لا ينقصه ذلك عند الله جناح
بعوضة فأبى أن يقبلها (1) إذ كره أن يخالف على الله أمره أو يحب ما أبغضه
خالقه أو يرفع ما وضع مليكه فزواها عن الصالحين اختبارا وبسطها لأعدائه
اغترارا فيظن المغرور بها المقتدر عليها أنه  أكرم بها ونسي ما صنع الله عز
وجل بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حين شد الحجر على بطنه (2)
ولقد جاءت الرواية عنه عن ربه عز وجل أنه قال لموسى عليه السلام إذا رأيت
الغني مقبلا فقل ذنب عجلت عقوبته وإذا رأيت الفقر مقبلا فقل مرحبا بشعار
الصالحين وإن شئت اقتديت بصاحب الروح والكلمة عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام
فإنه كان يقول إدامي الجوع وشعاري الخوف ولباسي الصوف وصلائي في الشتاء في
مشارق الشمس وسراجي القمر ودابتي رجلاي وطعامي وفاكهتي ما أنبتت الأرض أبيت
وليس لي شيء وأصبح وليس لي شيء وليس على الأرض أحد أغنى مني وقال وهب بن
منبه لما بعث الله عز وجل موسى وهارون عليهما السلام إلى فرعون قال لا يرو
عنكما لباسه الذي لبس من الدنيا فإن ناصيته بيدي ليس ينطق ولا يطرف ولا
يتنفس إلا بإذني ولا يعجبنكما ما تمتع به منها فإنما هي زهرة الحياة الدنيا
وزينة المترفين فلو شئت أن أزينكما بزينة من الدنيا يعرف فرعون حين يراها
أن قدرته تعجز عما أوتيتما لفعلت ولكني أرغب بكما عن ذلك فأزوي ذلك عنكما
وكذلك أفعل بأوليائي إني لأذودهم عن نعيمها كما يذود الراعي الشفيق غنمه عن
مراتع الهلكة وإني لأجنبهم ملاذها كما يجنب الراعي الشفيق إبله عن منازل
الغرة وما ذاك لهوانهم علي ولكن ليستكملوا نصيبهم من كرامتي سالما موفرا
إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف والخضوع والتقوى تنبت في قلوبهم وتظهر
على أجسادهم فهي ثيابهم التي يلبسون ودثارهم الذي يظهرون وضميرهم الذي
يستشعرون ونجاتهم التي بها يفوزون ورجاؤهم الذي إياه يأملون ومجدهم الذي به
يفخرون وسيماهم التي بها يعرفون فإذا لقيتهم فاخفض لهم جناحك وذلل لهم قلبك
ولسانك واعلم أنه من أخاف لي وليا فقد بارزني بالمحاربة ثم أنا الثائر له
يوم القيامة
وخطب علي كرم الله وجهه يوما خطبة فقال فيها اعلموا أنكم ميتون ومبعوثون
من بعد الموت وموقوفون على أعمالكم ومجزيون بها فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا
فإنها بالبلاء محفوفة وبالفناء معروفة  وبالغدر موصوفة وكل ما فيها إلى زوال
وهي بين أهلها دول وسجال لا تدوم أحوالها ولا يسلم من شرها نزالها بينا
أهلها منها في رخاء PageV03P212
وسرور إذا هم منها في بلاء وغرور أحوال مختلفة وتارات منصرفة العيش فيها
مذموم والرخاء فيها لا يدوم وإنما أهلها فيها أغراض مستهدفة ترميهم بسهامها
وتقصيهم بحمامها وكل حتفه فيها مقدور وحظه فيها موفور واعلموا عباد الله
أنكم وما أنتم فيه من هذه الدنيا على سبيل من قد مضى ممن كان أطول منكم
أعمارا وأشد منكم بطشا وأعمر ديارا وأبعد آثارا فأصبحت أصواتهم هامدة خامدة
من بعد طول تقلبها وأجسادهم بالية وديارهم على عروشها خاوية وآثارهم عافية
واستبدلوا بالقصور المشيدة والسرر والنمارق الممهدة الصخور والأحجار
المسندة في القبور اللاطئة الملحدة فمحلها مقترب وساكنها مغترب بين أهل
عمارة موحشين وأهل محلة متشاغلين لا يستأنسون بالعمران ولا يتواصلون تواصل
الجيران والإخوان على ما بينهم من قرب المكان والجوار ودنو الدار وكيف يكون
بينهم تواصل وقد طحنهم بكلكله البلا وأكلتهم الجنادل والثرى وأصبحوا بعد
الحياة أمواتا وبعد نضارة العيش رفاتا فجع بهم الأحباب وسكنوا تحت التراب
ظعنوا فليس لهم إياب هيهات هيهات {كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ
إلى يوم يبعثون} فكأن قد صرتم إلى ما صاروا إليه من البلاء والوحدة في دار
المثوى وارتهنتم في ذلك المضجع وضمكم ذلك المستودع فكيف بكم لو عاينتم
الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك
الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار
وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل
يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى
{ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم
عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه
حميد مجيد
وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم بسهامه
ويخترمك بلياليه وأيامه حتى يستغرق  جميع أجزائك فكيف بقاء سلامتك مع وقوع
الأيام بك وسرعة الليالي في بدنك لو كشف لك عما أحدثت الأيام فيك من النقص
لاستوحشت من كل يوم يأتي عليك واستثقلت ممر الساعة بك ولكن تدبير الله فوق
تدبير الاعتبار وبالسلو عن غوائل الدنيا وجد طعم لذاتها وإنها لأمر من
العلقم إذا عجنها الحكيم وقد أعيت الواصف لعيوبها بظاهر أفعالها وما تأتي
به من العجائب أكثر مما يحيط به الواعظ اللهم أرشدنا إلى الصواب وقال بعض
الحكماء وقد استوصف الدنيا وقدر بقائها فقال الدنيا وقتك الذي يرجع إليك
فيه طرفك لأن ما مضى عنك فقد فاتك إدراكه وما لم يأت فلا علم لك به والدهر
يوم مقبل تنعاه ليلته وتطويه ساعاته وأحداثه تتوالى على الإنسان بالتغيير
والنقصان والدهر موكل بتشتيت الجماعات وانخرام الشمل وتنقل الدول والأمل
طويل والعمر قصير وإلى الله تصير الأمور
وخطب عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله عليه فقال يا أيها الناس إنكم خلقتم
لأمر إن كنتم تصدقون به فإنكم حمقى وإن كنتم تكذبون به فإنكم هلكى إنما
خلقتم للأبد ولكنكم من دار إلى دار تنقلون عباد الله إنكم في دار لكم فيها
من طعامكم غصص ومن شرابكم شرق لا تصفو لكم نعمة تسرون بها إلا بفراق أخرى
تكرهون فراقها فاعملوا لما أنتم صائرون إليه وخالدون فيه ثم غلبه البكاء
ونزل
قال علي كرم الله وجهه في خطبته أوصيكم بتقوى الله والترك للدنيا التاركة
لكم وإن كنتم لا تحبون تركها المبلية أجسامكم وأنتم تريدون تجديدها فإنما
مثلكم ومثلها كمثل قوم في سفر سلكوا طريقا وكأنهم قطعوه وأفضوا إلى علم
فكأنهم بلغوه وكم عسى أن يجري المجرى حتى ينتهي إلى الغاية وكم عسى أن يبقى
من له يوم في
PageV03P213
الدنيا وطالب حثيث يطلبه حتى يفارقها فلا تجزعوا لبؤسها وضرائها فإنه إلى
انقطاع ولا تفرحوا بمتاعها ونعمائها فإنه إلى زوال عجبت لطالب الدنيا
والموت يطلبه وغافل وليس بمغفول عنه
وقال محمد بن الحسين لما علم أهل الفضل والعلم والمعرفة والأدب إن  الله
عز وجل قد أهان الدنيا وأنه لم يرضها لأوليائه وأنها عنده حقيرة قليلة وأن
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زهد فيها وحذر أصحابه من فتنتها أكلوا منها
قصدا وقدموا فضلا وأخذوا منها ما يكفي وتركوا ما يلهي لبسوا من الثياب ما
ستر العورة وأكلوا من الطعام أدناه مما سد الجوعة ونظروا إلى الدنيا بعين
أنها فانية وإلى الآخرة أنها باقية فتزودوا من الدنيا كزاد الراكب فخربوا
الدنيا وعمروا بها الآخرة ونظروا إلى الآخرة بقلوبهم فعلموا أنهم سينظرون
إليها بأعينهم فارتحلوا إليها بقلوبهم لما علموا أنهم سيرتحلون إليها
بأبدانهم تعبوا قليلا وتنعموا طويلا كل ذلك بتوفيق مولاهم الكريم أحب ما
أحب لهم وكرهوا ما كره لهم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ م م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, censure, dispraise — the opposite of praise (ḥamd); carries the sense of a quality deserving reproach.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, dhamm denotes the intrinsic disvalue of the world (dhamm al-dunyā) as a station of trial, not creation per se — the blame attaches to heedless attachment, not to existence as such.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) blame of an agent for a culpable act; here metaphorical (majāz) — the world is blamed as a locus, since it is not a moral agent but an instrument of divine testing.
- Root: غ ر ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, delusion, heedlessness; the state of being beguiled by appearances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ghurūr is the soul's being lulled by false hopes (āmal) and the postponement of death (nasīān al-ajal); it is the psychological mechanism of worldly attachment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a mirage or glittering surface; metaphorical: the world's adornment (tazakhruf) that veils its true nature as a passing abode.
- Root: ز خ ر ف (z-kh-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ornamentation, gilding, embellishment — originally of gold-leaf decoration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quranic usage (e.g. {زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ}) denotes deceptive beautification of speech or things that seduce the heart away from truth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical adornment; metaphorical: the world's deceptive allure that conceals its inherent transience (fanāʾ).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clauses with فاء (al-Fāʾ li-taʿqīb al-sharṭ) — The repeated pattern "فَإِذَا... فَـ" (e.g., "فإذا حل بك القضاء فانتزعت نفسك") marks immediate succession of events in the eschatological narrative, requiring the apodosis to follow with the particle fa- to indicate the inevitable sequence of death's stages.
chapters.translation:
One of them said: "O people, act with deliberation, and be in a state of awe before God, and do not be deluded by hope and the forgetfulness of the appointed term. Do not incline toward this world, for it is treacherous, deceitful. It has adorned itself for you with its delusion, and tempted you with its false promises, and beautified itself for its suitors — so it has become like a bride displayed, with eyes gazing upon her, hearts devoted to her, and souls enamored of her. How many a lover of hers has she slain, and how many a one at ease with her has she abandoned! So look upon her with the eye of truth, for she is an abode whose calamities are many, and whose Creator has dispraised her. Her newness decays, her dominion perishes, her mighty are humbled, her abundant become few, her affection dies, and her good passes away. Awaken, may God have mercy on you, from your heedlessness, and rouse yourselves from your slumber, before it is said: 'So-and-so is ill, or gravely burdened, heavy — he is guided to the medicine, but is there any way to the physician?' Then physicians are summoned for him, yet no recovery is hoped for him. Then it is said: 'So-and-so has made his will, and his wealth has been counted.' Then it is said: 'His tongue has grown heavy, so he cannot speak to his brothers, nor recognize his neighbors.' At that moment your brow sweats, your groaning follows in succession, your certainty is confirmed, your eyelids droop, your suspicions are verified, your tongue stammers, your brothers weep, and it is said to you: 'This is your son, so-and-so, and this is your brother, so-and-so.' You are prevented from speech and cannot utter a word, and a seal is set upon your tongue so it cannot move. Then the decree descends upon you, and your soul is torn from your limbs, then it ascends with it to the heaven. At that point your brothers gather, your shrouds are brought, they wash you and wrap you in the shroud — your visitors cease, your enviers find rest, your family turns to your wealth, and you remain pledged for your deeds."

And one of them said to the kings: "The people most deserving of blaming this world and despising it are those to whom it has been spread wide and who have been given their need from it — because they anticipate a calamity that attacks their wealth and sweeps it away, or their gatherings and scatters them, or comes upon their authority and demolishes it from its foundations, or creeps into their bodies and makes them ill, or afflicts them with the loss of something they hold dear among their loved ones. So the world is more deserving of blame — it is the taker of what it gives, the returner of what it bestows. While it makes its companion laugh, it makes others laugh at him; while it weeps for him, it weeps over him; while it spreads its hand in giving, it spreads it in taking back. Today it sets the crown upon its companion's head, and tomorrow it drags him in the dust. It is indifferent whether what has gone has gone, or what remains remains — it finds in what remains a substitute for what has passed, and is content with every exchange for everything."

And al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: "To proceed: Verily this world is an abode of departure, not an abode of residence. Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down from Paradise to a punishment. So beware of it, O Commander of the Faithful, for the provision from it is its abandonment, and the riches from it is its poverty. In every moment it has a slain one — it humiliates whoever honors it, and impoverishes whoever amasses it. It is like poison that one who does not know it eats, and in it is his destruction. So be in it like one who treats his wounds — he abstains for a little while, fearing what he dislikes for a long time, and endures the severity of the medicine, fearing the length of the disease. So beware of this treacherous, deceitful, deluding abode, which has adorned itself with its tricks, tempted with its delusion, settled with its hopes, and procrastinated with its promises — so it has become like a bride displayed, with eyes gazing upon her, hearts enamored of her, and souls in love with her. Yet she is hateful to all her spouses — neither does the remaining one take heed from the departed, nor is the latter deterred by the former, nor does the knower of God, mighty and majestic is He, remember when He has informed him of her. A lover of hers has attained his need from her, so he was deluded and transgressed, and forgot the final return — his intellect was occupied with her until his foot slipped, his regret became immense, his remorse multiplied, and the agonies of death and the sorrows of loss gathered upon him with its choking grief. And one desiring her has not attained what he sought, nor given his soul rest from toil — he departed without provision and arrived upon no resting place. So beware of her, O Commander of the Faithful, and be, when you are most at ease in her, most wary of her. For the companion of this world, whenever he is reassured by a joy in her, is roused to a disliked thing. The one who gladdens among her people is a deceiver, and the one who benefits in her is treacherous and harmful. Her ease has been joined with affliction, and her continuance has been made to end in annihilation. Her joys are mixed with sorrows; what has passed and turned away from her does not return, and one does not know what is coming to be awaited. Her hopes are false, her aspirations vain, her clarity is turbid, her life is wretched. And the son of Adam in her is in danger — if he reflects and looks, he is in danger from blessings, and on guard against affliction. If the Creator had not informed us of her, nor struck a parable for her, this world would still have awakened the sleeping and roused the heedless. How then, when there has come from God, mighty and majestic is He, a deterrent concerning her and a warner within her? What value does she have with God, exalted is His praise? He has not looked upon her since He created her. Indeed, her keys and treasures were offered to your Prophet, peace be upon him, without that diminishing him before God by the wing of a gnat — yet he refused to accept them, disliking to oppose God's command, or to love what his Creator abhors, or to raise what his King has lowered. So He withheld her from the righteous as a test, and spread her wide for His enemies as a delusion. The deluded one who has power over her thinks he is honored by her, and forgets what God, mighty and majestic is He, did with Muḥammad, peace be upon him, when he bound the stone upon his belly."

And the narration has come from him, from his Lord, mighty and majestic is He, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'"

And if you wish, you may follow the companion of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I have nothing, and I wake and I have nothing — and there is none on earth richer than I."

And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "When God, mighty and majestic is He, sent Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, to Pharaoh, He said: 'Let not the garment he has worn of this world deceive you, for his forelock is in My hand — he does not speak, nor blink, nor breathe except by My permission. And let not what he has enjoyed of her please you, for it is but the flower of the life of this world and the adornment of the luxurious. If I wished to adorn you with an adornment of this world such that Pharaoh would know, when he saw it, that his power falls short of what you have been given, I would have done so. But I desire for you to be above that, so I have withheld it from you. And thus do I do with My friends — I drive them away from her delights as the compassionate shepherd drives his flock from the pastures of destruction, and I keep them from her pleasures as the compassionate shepherd keeps his camels from the abodes of delusion. And that is not because they are lowly in My sight, but that they may complete their portion of My honor, safe and abundant. My friends adorn themselves for Me with humility, fear, submission, and piety — which grows in their hearts and appears on their bodies. They are their garments which they wear, their covering with which they appear, their conscience which they harbor, their salvation by which they triumph, their hope which they await, their glory by which they boast, and their mark by which they are known. So when you meet them, lower your wing to them, and humble your heart and tongue before them. And know that whoever frightens a friend of Mine has challenged Me to war — then I am the avenger for him on the Day of Resurrection.'"

And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, delivered a sermon one day and said in it: "Know that you will die, and be raised after death, and be stopped before your deeds, and recompensed for them. So let not the life of this world delude you — for it is surrounded by affliction, known for annihilation, described by treachery. Everything in it is passing, and it is among its people a rotation and an alternation — its states do not endure, nor is its dweller safe from its evil. While its people are in ease and joy, behold they are in affliction and delusion — states differing, and turns departing. Life in it is blameworthy, and ease in it does not last. Its people in it are but targets aimed at — it shoots them with its arrows and cuts them off with its death. Every death in it is decreed, and every portion in it is apportioned. Know, O servants of God, that you and what you are in of this world are upon the path of those who have passed — those who were longer in years than you, stronger in might, more flourishing in abodes, and more far-reaching in traces. Then their voices became still and silent after long reverberation, their bodies decayed, their dwellings fell upon their roofs in ruin, their traces were effaced. They exchanged the lofty palaces, the couches, and the cushioned seats for rocks and stones propped in the low, hollowed graves. Their abode is near, their dweller is a stranger among the people of a habitation made desolate, and the people of a settlement preoccupied — they do not find companionship in the buildings, nor do they connect as neighbors and brothers connect, despite the closeness of place and proximity of abode. How could there be connection among them, when affliction has ground them with its breast, and the stones and dust have consumed them? They became, after life, dead; and after the freshness of living, dust. Their loved ones were bereaved of them, and they settled beneath the soil. They departed, and there is no return for them. Alas! Alas! {«كَلَّا إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَائِلُهَا وَمِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ»} — 'Nay, but it is a word he speaks, and behind them is a barrier until the day they are raised.' As if you have already become what they have become — of affliction and solitude in the abode of settlement, pledged in that resting place, enclosed in that repository. How will it be with you when you behold the matters, and the graves are overturned, and what is in the breasts is brought out, and you are stopped for the reckoning before the Majestic King? Then hearts fly from their fear of past sins, the veils and curtains are torn from you, and your faults and secrets appear. There, every soul shall be recompensed for what it has earned — for God, mighty and majestic is He, says: {لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَى} — 'That He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best.' And He, exalted is He, says: {وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ} — 'And the Book is placed, and you see the criminals fearful of what is in it.' May God make us and you among those who act according to His Book and follow His friends, until He settles us and you in the abode of permanence by His bounty — verily He is Praiseworthy, Glorious."

And one of the sages said: "The days are arrows, and people are targets. Time shoots you every day with its arrows, and cuts you off with its nights and days, until it exhausts all your parts. So how can the survival of your safety be, with the days falling upon you and the swiftness of the nights upon your body? If what the days have wrought in you of diminishment were unveiled to you, you would be horrified by every day that comes upon you, and would find heavy the passing of the hour over you. But God's governance is above the governance of reflection — and it is by forgetfulness of the calamities of this world that the taste of its pleasures is found. Yet it is more bitter than colocynth when the wise one mixes it. The describer of its faults is exhausted by its outward acts, and what it brings of wonders is more than the preacher can encompass. O God, guide us to the right course."

And one of the sages said, when asked to describe this world and its duration was reckoned: "This world is your time, to which your glance returns — for what has passed from you, its attainment has escaped you, and what has not come, you have no knowledge of it. Time is a day approaching — its night announces its passing, and its hours fold it up. Its events follow upon man with change and diminishment. Time is entrusted with scattering the gatherings, breaking the union, and transferring the states. Hope is long, and life is short — and to God all matters return."

And ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may God have mercy on him, delivered a sermon and said: "O people, you have been created for a matter — if you believe it, then you are foolish; and if you deny it, then you are destroyed. You have been created for eternity, but you are transferred from one abode to another. O servants of God, you are in an abode in which your food brings choking and your drink brings strangling. No blessing delights you but through the parting of another whose parting you dislike. So work for that to which you are proceeding and in which you will abide forever." Then weeping overcame him, and he descended.

ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said in his sermon: "I counsel you to fear God, and to abandon this world that is abandoning you — even if you do not love abandoning it, which wears out your bodies while you desire their renewal. For your likeness and its likeness is like a people on a journey — they traveled a road as if they had crossed it, and arrived at a sign as if they had reached it. How much can a runner run until he reaches the goal? And how much can one remain who has a day in this world, with an urgent pursuer pursuing him until he leaves it? So do not be distressed by its hardship and harm, for it is toward cessation; and do not rejoice in its goods and blessings, for it is toward passing away. I marvel at the seeker of this world while death seeks him, and at the heedless one while he is not unheeded."

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn said: "When the people of virtue, knowledge, gnosis, and refinement knew that God, mighty and majestic is He, has humiliated this world, and that He has not approved it for His friends, and that it is contemptible and little in His sight, and that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was ascetic in it and warned his companions of its trial — they ate from it with moderation and gave precedence to the surplus, took from it what sufficed, and left what distracted. They wore of garments what covered the nakedness, and ate of food the humblest that filled the hunger. They looked at this world with the eye that it is passing, and at the Hereafter that it is enduring. So they provisioned themselves from this world as the provision of a rider — they ruined this world and built with it the Hereafter. They looked at the Hereafter with their hearts, knowing they would look at it with their eyes, so they journeyed to it with their hearts, knowing they would journey to it with their bodies. They toiled a little and enjoyed for a long time — all of that by the success of their Generous Master, loving what He loved for them, and disliking what He disliked for them."

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Attributes of the World through Parables
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| بيان صفة الدنيا بالأمثلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ن-ي (d-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "nearness" (qurb) and "lowness" (dunūw); the world (al-dunyā) is that which is immediate and proximate, contrasted with the hereafter (al-ākhirah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-dunyā signifies the present abode of trial and impermanence, whose attributes are deceptive and transient, as opposed to the enduring abode of recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "the nearer" (al-dunyā) as a feminine adjective for "the nearer life" (al-ḥayāt al-dunyā); metaphorically, it denotes all worldly pursuits that veil one from the divine, not merely physical existence.
- Root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "likeness" or "similitude" (shabah); also "to stand before" (mathala) as in representation.
