chapters.arabic_text:
عن محمد بن المنكدر عن أم درة وكانت تخدم عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت إن
معاوية بعث إليها بمال في غرارتين ثمانين ومائة ألف درهم فدعت بطبق فجعلت
تقسمه بين الناس فلما أمست قالت يا جارية هلم فطوري فجاءتها بخبز وزيت
فقالت لها أم درة ما استطعت فيما قسمت اليوم أن تشتري لنا بدرهم لحما نفطر
عليه فقالت لو كنت ذكرتيني لفعلت
وعن أبان بن عثمان قال أراد رجل أن يضار عبيد الله بن عباس فأتى وجوه
قريش فقال يقول لكم عبيد الله تغدوا عندي اليوم فأتوه حتى ملؤا عليه الدار
فقال ما هذا فأخبر الخبر فأمر عبيد الله بشراء فاكهة وأمر قوما فطبخوا
وخبزوا وقدمت الفاكهة إليهم فلم يفرغوا منها حتى وضعت الموائد فأكلوا حتى
صدروا فقال عبيد الله لوكلائه أو موجود لنا هذا كل يوم قالوا نعم قال
فليتغد عندنا هؤلاء في كل يوم
وقال مصعب بن الزبير  حج معاوية فلما انصرف مر بالمدينة فقال الحسين بن
علي لأخيه الحسن لا تلقه ولا تسلم عليه فلما خرج معاوية قال الحسن إن علينا
دينا فلا بد لنا من إتيانه فركب في أثره ولحقه فسلم عليه وأخبره بدينه
فمروا عليه ببختي عليه ثمانون ألف دينار وقد أعيا وتخلف عن الإبل وقوم
يسوقونه فقال معاوية ما هذا فذكر له فقال اصرفوه بما عليه إلى أبي محمد
وعن واقد بن محمد الواقدي قال حدثني أبي أنه رفع رقعة إلى المأمون يذكر
فيها كثرة الدين وقلة صبره عليه فوقع المأمون على ظهر رقعته إنك رجل اجتمع
فيك خصلتان السخاء والحياء فأما السخاء فهو الذي أطلق
PageV03P247
ما في يديك وأما الحياء فهو الذي يمنعك عن تبليغنا ما أنت عليه وقد أمرت
لك بمائة ألف درهم فإن كنت قد أصبت فازدد في بسط يدك وإن لم أكن قد أصبت
فجنايتك على نفسك وأنت حدثتني وكنت على قضاء الرشيد عن محمد بن إسحق عن
الزهري عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للزبير بن العوام يا زبير
اعلم أن مفاتيح أرزاق العباد بإزاء العرش يبعث الله عز وجل إلى كل عبد بقدر
نفقته فمن كثر كثر له ومن قلل قلل له وأنت أعلم (1)
قال الواقدي فوالله لمذاكرة المأمون إياي بالحديث أحب إلى من الجائزة وهي
مائة ألف درهم
وسأل رجل الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما حاجة فقال له يا هذا حق سؤالك إياي
يعظم لدي ومعرفتي بما يجب لك تكبر علي ويدي تعجز عن نيلك بما أنت أهله
والكثير في ذات الله تعالى قليل وما في ملكي وفاه لشكرك فإن قبلت الميسور
ورفعت عني مؤنة الاحتمال والاهتمام لما أتكلفه من واجب حقك فعلت فقال يا
ابن رسول الله أقبل وأشكر العطية وأعذر علي المنع فدعا الحسن بوكيله وجعل
يحاسبه على نفقاته حتى استقصاها فقال هات الفضل من الثلثمائة ألف درهم
فأحضر خمسين ألف قال فما فعلت بالخمسمائة دينار قال هي عندي قال أحضرها
فأحضرها فدفع الدنانير والدراهم إلى الرجل وقال هات من يحملها لك فأتاه
بحمالين فدفع إليه الحسن رداءه لكراء الحمالين فقال له مواليه والله ما
عندنا درهم فقال أرجو أن يكون لي عند الله أجر عظيم
واجتمع قراء البصرة إلى ابن عباس وهو عامل بالبصرة فقالوا لنا جار صوام
قوام يتمنى كل واحد منا أن يكون مثله وقد زوج بنته من ابن أخيه وهو فقير
وليس عنده ما يجهزها به فقام عبد الله بن عباس فأخذ بأيديهم وأدخلها داره
وفتح صندوقا فأخرج منه ست بدر فقال احملوا فحملوا فقال ابن عباس ما أنصفناه
أعطيناه ما يشغله عن قيامه وصيامه ارجعوا بنا نكن أعوانه على تجهيزها فليس
للدنيا من القدر ما يشغل مؤمنا عن عبادة ربه وما بنا من الكبر ما لا نخدم
أولياء الله تعالى ففعل وفعلوا
وحكي أنه لما أجدب الناس بمصر وعبد الحميد بن سعد أميرهم فقال والله
لأعلمن الشيطان أني عدوه فعال محاويجهم إلى أن رخصت الأسعار ثم عزل عنهم
فرحل وللتجار عليه ألف ألف درهم فرهنهم بها حلي نسائه وقيمتها خمسمائة ألف
ألف فلما تعذر عليه ارتجاعها كتب إليهم ببيعها ودفع الفاضل منها عن حقوقهم
إلى من لم تنله صلاته
وكان أبو طاهر بن كثير شيعيا فقال له رجل بحق علي بن أبي طالب لما وهبت
لي نخلتك بموضع كذا وكذا فقال قد فعلت وحقه لأعطينك ما يليها وكان ذلك
أضعاف ما طلب الرجل
وكان أبو مرثد أحد الكرماء فمدحه بعض الشعراء فقال للشاعر والله ما عندي
ما أعطيك ولكن قدمني إلى القاضي وادع علي بعشرة آلاف درهم حتى أقر لك بها
ثم احبسني فإنأهلي لا يتركوني محبوسا ففعل ذلك فلم يمس حتى دفع إليه عشرة
آلاف درهم وأخرج أبو مرثد من الحبس
وكان معن بن زائدة عاملا على العراقين بالبصرة فحضر بابه شاعر فأقام مدة
وأراد الدخول على معن فلم يتهيأ له فقال يوما لبعض خدام معن إذا دخل الأمير
البستان فعرفني فلما دخل الأمير البستان  أعلمه فكتب الشاعر بيتا على خشبة
وألقاها في الماء الذي يدخل البستان وكان معن على رأس الماء فلما بصر
بالخشبة أخذها وقرأها فإذا مكتوب عليها PageV03P248
أيا جود معن ناج معنا بحاجتي ... فما لي إلى معن سواك شفيع
فقال من صاحب هذه فدعي بالرجل فقال له كيف قلت فقال له فأمر له بعشر بدر
فأخذهاووضع الأمير الخشبة تحت بسطاه فلما كان اليوم الثاني أخرجها من تحت
البساط وقرأها ودعا بالرجل فدفع إليه مائة ألف درهم فلما أخذها الرجل تفكر
وخاف أن يأخذ منه ما أعطاه فخرج فلما كان في اليوم الثالث قرأ ما فيها ودعا
بالرجل فطلب فلم يوجد فقال معن حق علي أن أعطيه حتى لا يبقى في بيت مالي
ولا دينار
وقال أبو الحسن المدائني خرج الحسن والحسين وعبد الله بن جعفر حجاجا
ففاتهم أثقالهم فجاعوا وعطشوا فمروا بعجوز في خباء لها فقالوا هل من شراب
فقالت نعم فأناخوا إليها وليس لها إلا شويهة في كسر الخيمة فقالت احلبوها
وامتذقوا لبنها ففعلوا ذلك ثم قالوا لها هل من طعام قالت لا إلا هذه الشاة
فليذبحها أحدكم حتى أهيء لكم ما تأكلون فقام إليها أحدهم وذبحها وكشطها ثم
هيأت لهم طعاما فأكلوا وأقاموا حتى أبردوا فلما ارتحلوا قالوا لها نحن نفر
من قريش نريد هذا الوجه فإذا رجعنا سالمين فألمي بنا فإنا صانعون بك خيرا
ثم ارتحلوا وأقبل زوجها فأخبرته بخبر القوم والشاة فغضب الرجل وقال ويلك
تذبحين شاتي لقوم لا تعرفيهم ثم تقولين نفر من قريش قال ثم بعد مدة
ألجأتهما الحاجة إلى دخول المدينة فدخلاها وجعلا ينقلان البعر إليها
ويبيعانه ويتعيشان بثمنه فمرت العجوز ببعض سكك المدينة فإذا الحسن بن علي
جالس على باب داره فعرف العجوز وهي له منكرة فبعث غلامه فدعا بالعجوز وقال
لها يا أمة الله أتعرفيني قالت لا قال أنا ضيفك يوم كذا ويوم كذا فقالت
العجوز بأبي أنت وأمي أنت هو قال نعم ثم أمر الحسن فاشتروا لها من شياه
الصدقة ألف شاة  وأمر لها معها بألف دينار وبعث بها مع غلامه إلى الحسين
فقال لها الحسين بكم وصلك أخي قالت بألف شاة وألف دينار فأمر لها الحسين
أيضا بمثل ذلك ثم بعث بها مع غلامه إلى عبد الله بن جعفر فقال لها بكم وصلك
الحسن والحسين قالت بألفي شاة وألفي دينار فأمر لها عبد الله بألفي شاة
وألفي دينار وقال لها لو بدأت بي لأتعبتهما فرجعت العجوز إلى زوجها بأربعة
آلاف شاة وأربعة آلاف دينار
وخرج عبد الله بن عامر بن كريز من المسجد يريد منزله وهو وحده فقام إليه
غلام من ثقيف فمشى إلى جانبه فقال له عبد الله ألك حاجة يا غلام قال صلاحك
وفلاحك رأيتك تمشي وحدك فقلت أقيك بنفسي وأعوذ بالله إن طار بجانبك مكروه
فأخذ عبد الله بيده ومشى معه إلى منزله ثم دعا بألف دينار فدفعها إلى
الغلام وقال استنفق هذه فنعم ما أدبك أهلك
وحكي أن قوما من العرب جاءوا إلى قبر بعض أسخيائهم للزيارة فنزلوا عند
قبره وباتوا عنده وقد كانوا جاءوا من سفر بعيد فرأى رجل منهم في النوم صاحب
القبر وهو يقول له هل لك أن تبادل بعيرك بنجيبي وكان السخي الميت قد خلف
نجيبا معروفا به ولهذا الرجل بعير سمين فقال له في النوم نعم فباعه في
النوم بعيره بنجيبه فلما وقع بينهما العقد عمد هذا الرجل إلى بعيره فنحره
في النوم فانتبه الرجل من نومه فإذا الدم يثج من نحر بعيره فقام الرجل
فنحره وقسم لحمه فطبخوه وقضوا حاجتهم منه ثم رحلوا وساروا فلما كان اليوم
الثاني وهم في الطريق استقبلهم ركب فقال رجل منهم من فلان بن فلان منكم
باسم ذلك الرجل فقال أنا فقال له هل بعت من فلان بن فلان شيئا وذكر الميت
صاحب القبر قال نعم بعت بعيري بنجيبه في
PageV03P249
النوم فقال خذ هذا نجيبه ثم قال هو أبي وقد رأيته في النوم وهو يقول إن
كنت ابني فادفع نجيبي إلى فلان بن فلان وسماه
وقدم  رجل من قريش من السفر فمر برجل من الأعراب على قارعة الطريق قد
أقعده الدهر وأضر به المرض فقال يا هذا أعنا على الدهر فقال الرجل لغلامه
ما بقي معك من النفقة فادفعه إليه فصب الغلام في حجر الأعرابي أربعة آلاف
درهم فذهب لينهض فلم يقدر من الضعف فبكى فقال له الرجل ما يبكيك لعلك
استقللت ما أعطيناك قال لا ولكن ذكرت ما تأكل الأرض من كرمك فأبكاني
واشترى عبد الله بن عامر من خالد بن عقبة بن أبي معيط داره التي في السوق
بتسعين ألف درهم فلما كان الليل سمع بكاء أهل خالد فقال لأهله ما لهؤلاء
قالوا يبكون لدارهم فقال يا غلام ائتهم فأعلمهم أن المال والدار لهم جميعا
وقيل بعث هارون الرشيد إلى مالك بن أنس رحمه الله بخمسمائة دينار فبلغ
ذلك الليث به سعد فأنفذ إليه ألف دينار فغضب هارون وقال أعطيته خمسمائة
وتعطيه ألفا وأنت من رعيتي فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إن لي من غلتي كل يوم ألف
دينار فاستحييت أن أعطي مثله أقل من دخل يوم وحكي أنه لم تجب عليه الزكاة
مع أن دخله كل يوم ألف دينار وحكي أن امرأة سألت الليث بن سعد رحمة الله
عليه شيئا من عسل فأمر لها بزق من عسل فقيل له إنها كانت تقنع بدون هذا
فقال إنها سألت على قدر حاجتها ونحن نعطيها على قدر النعمة علينا وكان
الليث ابن سعد لا يتكلم كل يوم حتى يتصدق على ثلثمائة وستين مسكينا
وقال الأعمش اشتكت شاة عندي فكان خيثمة بن عبد الرحمن يعودها بالغداة
والعشي ويسألني هل استوفت علفها وكيف صبر الصبيان منذ فقدوا لبنها وكان
تحتي لبد أجلس عليه فإذا خرج قال خذ ما تحت اللبد حتى وصل إلي في علة الشاة
أكثر من ثلثمائة دينار من بره حتى تمنيت أن الشاة لم تبرأ
وقال عبد الملك بن مروان لأسماء بن خارجة بلغني عنك خصال فحدثني بها فقال
هي من غيري أحسن منها مني فقال  عزمت عليك إلا حدثتني بها فقال يا أمير
المؤمنين ما مددت رجلي بين يدي جليس لي قط ولا صنعت طعاما قط فدعوت عليه
قوما إلا كانوا أمن علي مني عليهم ولا نصب لي رجل وجهه قط يسألني شيئا
فاستكثرت شيئا أعطيته إياه
ودخل سعيد بن خالد على سليمان بن عبد الملك وكان سعيد رجلا جوادا فإذا لم
يجد شيئا كتب لمن سأله صكا على نفسه حتى يخرج عطاؤه فلما نظر إليه سليمان
تمثل بهذا البيت فقال
إني سمعت مع الصباح مناديا ... يا من يعين على الفتى المعوان
ثم قال ما حاجتك قال ديني قال وكم هو قال ثلاثون ألف دينار قال لك دينك
ومثله
وقيل مرض قيس بن سعد بن عبادة فاستبطأ إخوانه فقيل له إنهم يستحيون مما
لك عليهم من الدين فقال أخزى الله مالا يمنع الإخوان من الزيارة ثم أمر
مناديا فنادى من كان عليه لقيس بن سعد حق فهو منه بريء قال فانكسرت درجته
بالعشي لكثرة من زاره وعاده
عن أبي إسحاق قال صليت العصر في مسجد الأشعث بالكوفة أطلب غريما لي فلما
صليت وضع بين يدي حلة ونعلان فقلت لست من أهل هذا المسجد فقالوا إن الأشعث
بن قيس الكندي قدم البارحة من مكة فأمر لكل من صلى في المسجد بحلة ونعلين
PageV03P250
وقال الشيخ أبو سعد الحركوشي النيسابوري رحمه الله سمعت محمد بن محمد
الحافظ يقول سمعت الشافعي المجاور بمكة يقول كان بمصر رجل عرف بأن يجمع
للفقراء شيئا فولد لبعضهم مولود قال فجئت إليه وقلت له ولد لي مولود وليس
معي شيء فقام معي ودخل على جماعة فلم يفتح بشيء فجاء إلى قبر رجل وجلس عنده
وقال رحمك الله كنت تفعل وتصنع وإني درت اليوم على جماعة فكلفتهم دفع شيء
لمولود فلم يتفق لي شيء قال ثم قام وأخرج دينارا وقسمه نصفين وناولني نصفه
وقال هذا دين عليك إلى أن يفتح الله عليك بشيء قال فأخذته وانصرفت فأصلحت
ما اتفق لي به قال فرأى ذلك  المحتسب تلك الليلة ذلك الشخص في منامه فقال
سمعت جميع ما قلت وليس لنا إذن في الجواب ولكن أحضر منزلي وقل لأولادي
يحفروا مكان الكانون ويخرجوا قرابة فيها خمسمائة دينار فاحملها إلى هذا
الرجل فلما كان من الغد تقدم إلى منزل الميت وقص عليهم القصة فقالوا له
اجلس وحفروا الموضع وأخرجوا الدنانير وجاءوا بها فوضعوها بين يديه فقال هذا
مالكم وليس لرؤياي حكم فقالوا هو يتسخى ميتا ولا نتسخى نحن أحياء فلما
ألحوا عليه حمل الدنانير إلى الرجل صاحب المولود وذكر له القصة قال فأخذ
منها دينارا فكسره نصفين فأعطاه النصف الذي أقرضه وحمل النصف الآخر وقال
يكفيني هذا وتصدق به على الفقراء فقال أبو سعيد فلا أدري أي هؤلاء أسخى
وروي أن الشافعي رحمه الله لما مرض مرض موته بمصر قال مروا فلانا يغسلني
فلما توفي بلغه خبر وفاته فحضر وقال ائتوني بتذكرته فأتي بها فنظر فيها
فإذا على الشافعي سبعون ألف درهم دين فكتبها على نفسه وقضاها عنه وقال هذا
غسلي إياه أي أراد به هذا وقال أبو سعيد الواعظ الحركوشي لما قدمت مصر طلبت
منزل ذلك الرجل فدلوني عليه فرأيت جماعة من أحفاده وزرتهم فرأيت فيهم سيما
الخير وآثار الفضل فقلت بلغ أثره في الخير إليهم وظهرت بركته فيهم مستدلا
بقوله تعالى وكان أبوهما صالحا وقال الشافعي رحمه الله لا أزال أحب حماد بن
أبي سليمان لشيء بلغني عنه أنه كان ذات يوم راكبا حماره فحركه فانقطع زره
فمر على الخياط فأراد أن ينزل إليه ليسوي زره فقال الخياط والله لا نزلت
فقام الخياط إليه فسوى زره فأخرج إليه صرة فيها عشرة دنانير فسلمها إلى
الخياط واعتذر إليه من قلتها وأنشد الشافعي رحمه الله لنفسه
يا لهف قلبي على مال أجود به ... على المقلين من أهل المروءات
إن اعتذاري إلى من جاء يسألني ... ما ليس عندي لمن إحدى المصيبات
وعن الربيع بن سليمان قال أخذ رجل بركاب الشافعي رحمه الله فقال يا ربيع
أعطه أربعة دنانير واعتذر  إليه عني وقال الربيع سمعت الحميدي يقول قدم
الشافعي من صنعاء إلى مكة بعشرة آلاف دينار فضرب خباءه في موضع خارج عن مكة
ونثرها على ثوب ثم أقبل على كل من دخل عليه يقبض له قبضة ويعطيه حتى صلى
الظهر ونفض الثوب وليس عليه شيء
وعن أبي ثور قال أراد الشافعي الخروج إلى مكة ومعه مال وكان قلما يمسك
شيئا من سماحته فقلت له ينبغي أن تشتري بهذا المال ضيعة تكون لك ولولدك قال
فخرج ثم قدم علينا فسألته عن ذلك المال فقال ما وجدت بمكة ضيعة يمكنني أن
أشتريها لمعرفتي بأصلها وقد وقف أكثرها ولكني بنيت بمنى مضربا يكون
لأصحابنا إذا حجوا أن ينزلوا فيه وأنشد الشافعي رحمه الله لنفسه يقول
أرى نفسي تتوق إلى أمور ... يقصر دون مبلغهن مالي
فنفسي لا تطاوعني ببخل ... ومالي لا يبلغني فعالي
PageV03P251
وقال محمد بن عباد المهلبي دخل أبي على المأمون فوصله بمائة ألف درهم
فلما قام من عنده تصدق بها فأخبر بذلك المأمون فلما عاد إليه عاتبه المأمون
في ذلك فقال يا أمير المؤمنين منع الموجود سوء ظن بالمعبود فوصله بمائة ألف
أخرى
وقام رجل إلى سعيد بن العاص فسأله فأمر له بمائة ألف درهم فبكى فقال له
سعيد ما يبكيك قال أبكي على الأرض أن تأكل مثلك فأمر له بمائة ألف أخرى
ودخل أبو تمام على إبراهيم بن شكلة بأبيات امتدحه بها فوجده عليلا فقبل
منه المدحة وأمر حاجبه بنيله ما يصلحه وقال
عسى أن أقوم من مرضي فأكافئه فأقام شهرين فوحشه طول المقام فكتب إليه
يقول
إن حراما قبول مدحتنا ... وترك ما نرتجي من الصفد
كما الدراهم والدنانير في البيعحرام إلا يدا بيد
فلما وصل البيتان إلى إبراهيم قال لحاجبه كم أقام بالباب قال شهرين قال
أعطه ثلاثون ألف وجئني بدواة فكتب إليه
أعجلتنا فأتاك عاجل برنا ... قلا ولو أمهلتنا لم نقلل
فخذ القليل وكن كأنك لم تقل ... ونقول نحن كأننا لم نفعل
وروي أنه كان لعثمان على طلحة رضي  الله عنهما خمسون ألف درهم فخرج عثمان
يوما إلى المسجد فقال له طلحة قد تهيأ مالك فاقبضه فقال هو لك يا أبا محمد
معونة لك على مروءتك وقالت سعدى بنت عوف دخلت على طلحة فرأيت منه ثقلا فقلت
له مالك فقال اجتمع عندي مال وقد غمني فقلت وما يغمك ادع قومك فقال يا غلام
علي بقومي فقسمه فيهم فسألت الخادم كم كان قال أربعمائة ألف
وجاء أعرابي إلى طلحة فسأله وتقرب إليه برحم فقال إن هذه الرحم ما سألني
بها أحد قبلك إن لي أرضا قد أعطاني بها عثمان ثلثمائة ألف فإن شئت فاقبضها
وإن شئت بعتها من عثمان ودفعت إليك الثمن فقال الثمن فباعها من عثمان ودفع
إليه الثمن
وقيل بكى علي كرم الله وجهه يوما فقيل ما يبكيك فقال لم يأتني ضيف منذ
سبعة أيام أخاف أن يكون الله قد أهانني
وأتى رجل صديقا له فدق عليه الباب فقال ما جاء بك قال علي أربعمائة درهم
دين فوزن أربعمائة درهم وأخرجها إليها وعاد يبكي فقالت امرأته لم أعطيته إذ
شق عليك فقال إنما أبكي لأني لم أتفقد حاله حتى احتاج إلى مفاتحتي فرحم
الله من هذه صفاتهم وغفر لهم أجمعين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-د (j-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of excellence, quality, and beneficence; al-jūd is the pouring forth of goodness without constraint.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Generosity (jūd) as a praiseworthy moral virtue (faḍīlah) that expends wealth in obedience to God, distinct from prodigality (isrāf).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of flowing water; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the soul's abundant giving.
- Root: س-خ-و (s-kh-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, ease, and liberality; sakhaʾ denotes the natural disposition of open-handedness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sakhaʾ as the middle path between miserliness (bukhl) and waste (tabdhīr), a virtue of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal softness of ground; metaphorical for the heart's gentleness in giving.
- Root: ك-ر-م (k-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Nobility, honor, and generosity; karīm is one who is noble by nature and generous in action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Karam as the comprehensive virtue encompassing all praiseworthy traits, ultimately attributed to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal preciousness of a thing; metaphorical for moral excellence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The use of apposition to clarify and emphasize the subject's attributes, as seen in the chains of narrators and the parallel structures of generosity narratives.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the reports concerning the generosity (sakhaʾ) of the early Muslims (al-salaf) are abundant and well-attested. I shall transmit a selection of them to you, so that your soul may be moved to emulate their noble traits and to adorn itself with their praiseworthy qualities.

Among the reports is that of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umm Darrā, who served ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her. She said: Muʿāwiyah sent to her a sum of money in two saddle-bags — one hundred and eighty thousand dirhams. She called for a large tray and began to distribute it among the people. When evening came, she said, "O maidservant, bring my supper." The maid brought her bread and oil. Umm Darrā said to her, "Could you not, from what you distributed today, have bought us meat for a dirham to break our fast with?" She replied, "Had you reminded me, I would have done so."

It is also related from Abān ibn ʿUthmān that a man wished to cause hardship to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās. He went to the notables of Quraysh and said, "ʿUbayd Allāh says to you: Dine with me today." They came to him until they filled his house. He said, "What is this?" They informed him of the matter. So ʿUbayd Allāh ordered fruit to be purchased, and commanded a group to cook and bake bread. The fruit was presented to them, and before they had finished with it, the tables were laid. They ate until they were satisfied. Then ʿUbayd Allāh said to his agents, "Do we have the means for this every day?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Then let these people dine with us every day."

And Musʿab ibn al-Zubayr said: Muʿāwiyah performed the pilgrimage, and when he departed, he passed through Medina. Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī said to his brother al-Ḥasan, "Do not meet him, and do not greet him." When Muʿāwiyah left, al-Ḥasan said, "We have a debt upon us, and we must go to him." So he rode after him and caught up with him. He greeted him and informed him of his debt. They passed by a Bactrian camel carrying eighty thousand dīnārs, which had grown weary and lagged behind the other camels, with men driving it. Muʿāwiyah said, "What is this?" He was told of it. He said, "Divert it, with all that is upon it, to Abū Muḥammad."

And from Wāqid ibn Muḥammad al-Wāqidī, he said: My father told me that he submitted a petition to al-Maʾmūn mentioning the abundance of his debt and his lack of patience under it. Al-Maʾmūn wrote on the back of his petition: "You are a man in whom two qualities have gathered: generosity (sakhāʾ) and modesty (ḥayāʾ). As for generosity, it is that which has released what is in your hands; and as for modesty, it is that which prevents you from conveying to us your condition. I have ordered that you be given one hundred thousand dirhams. If I have been correct, then increase in the spreading of your hand; and if I have not been correct, then your transgression is upon yourself." And he narrated to me the ḥadīth of al-Rashīd, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām: "O Zubayr, know that the keys to the provisions of the servants are opposite the Throne. God, Mighty and Majestic, sends to every servant according to the measure of his expenditure. Whoever increases, He increases for him; and whoever decreases, He decreases for him. And you know best."

Al-Wāqidī said: By God, al-Maʾmūn's discussing the ḥadīth with me was dearer to me than the gift, which was one hundred thousand dirhams.

And a man asked al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may God be pleased with them both, for a need. He said to him: "O man, the right of your asking of me is great in my sight, and my knowledge of what is obligatory upon me toward you is weighty upon me, and my hand falls short of attaining for you what you deserve. And the abundant in the cause of God, Exalted, is little, and what is in my possession is insufficient for thanking you. If you accept what is easy, and lift from me the burden of bearing and concern for what I undertake of your due right, I shall do so." The man said, "O son of the Messenger of God, I accept, and I thank the gift, and I excuse the refusal." So al-Ḥasan called for his agent and began to reckon with him over his expenditures until he had exhausted them. He said, "Bring the surplus from the three hundred thousand dirhams." He brought fifty thousand. He said, "And what did you do with the five hundred dīnārs?" He said, "They are with me." He said, "Bring them." He brought them. Then he gave the dīnārs and the dirhams to the man, and said, "Bring someone to carry them for you." He brought two porters. Al-Ḥasan gave him his cloak for the hire of the porters. His clients said, "By God, we have not a dirham with us." He said, "I hope that I shall have with God a great reward."

And the Qurrāʾ (readers) of Basra gathered to Ibn ʿAbbās, who was governor of Basra, and said: "We have a neighbor who fasts and prays, and each of us wishes to be like him. He has married his daughter to his brother's son, who is poor, and he has nothing with which to equip her." So ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās arose, took them by their hands, and brought them into his house. He opened a chest and brought out from it six bags (of money). He said, "Carry them." So they carried them. Then Ibn ʿAbbās said, "We have not treated him fairly. We have given him what would occupy him from his prayer and fasting. Let us return and be his helpers in equipping her. For this world has not such worth that it should occupy a believer from the worship of his Lord, and we have not such pride that we should not serve the friends of God." So he did, and they did.

And it is related that when the people of Egypt suffered drought, and ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Saʿd was their governor, he said: "By God, I shall teach Satan that I am his enemy." He occupied himself with the needs of the people until prices fell. Then he was removed from them, and he departed. The merchants had a million dirhams owed to them by him. He pawned to them the jewelry of his wives, whose value was five hundred thousand (dirhams). When it became difficult for him to redeem it, he wrote to them to sell it and to pay the surplus above their claims to those whom his gifts had not reached.

And Abū Ṭāhir ibn Kathīr was a Shīʿī. A man said to him, "By the right of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, give me your palm-tree in such-and-such a place." He said, "I have given it to you, and by his right, I shall give you what adjoins it." And that was many times what the man had asked.

And Abū Murshid was one of the generous. A poet praised him. He said to the poet: "By God, I have nothing to give you. But bring me before the judge and claim against me ten thousand dirhams, so that I may acknowledge them for you. Then imprison me, for my family will not leave me imprisoned." He did that, and before evening, ten thousand dirhams were paid to him, and Abū Murshid was released from prison.

And Maʿn ibn Zāʾidah was governor of the two Iraqs in Basra. A poet presented himself at his door and stayed for a time, wishing to enter upon Maʿn but not being able. One day he said to one of Maʿn's servants, "When the amīr enters the garden, inform me." When the amīr entered the garden, he informed him. The poet wrote a verse on a piece of wood and cast it into the water that flowed into the garden. Maʿn was at the head of the water. When he saw the wood, he took it and read it. Written upon it was:

"O generosity of Maʿn, intercede with him for my need, for I have no intercessor to Maʿn other than you."

He said, "Who is the owner of this?" The man was summoned. He said to him, "How did you say it?" He recited it to him. He ordered that he be given ten bags (of money). He took them. The amīr placed the wood under his carpet. On the second day, he brought it out from under the carpet, read it, and summoned the man, and gave him one hundred thousand dirhams. When the man took it, he reflected and feared that he would take back what he had given him, so he left. On the third day, he read what was in it and summoned the man. He was sought but not found. Maʿn said: "It is incumbent upon me to give him until there remains not a single dīnār in my treasury."

And Abū al-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī said: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar set out as pilgrims. Their baggage lagged behind them, and they became hungry and thirsty. They passed by an old woman in her tent. They said, "Is there any drink?" She said, "Yes." They halted their mounts by her. She had only a small sheep in the corner of the tent. She said, "Milk it and mix the milk with water." They did so. Then they said to her, "Is there any food?" She said, "No, except this sheep. Let one of you slaughter it, so that I may prepare for you what you may eat." One of them arose, slaughtered it, and skinned it. Then she prepared food for them, and they ate and remained until they had cooled down. When they departed, they said to her, "We are men of Quraysh heading for this destination. When we return safely, come to us, for we shall do good to you." Then they departed. Her husband came and she told him of the people and the sheep. The man became angry and said, "Woe to you! You slaughter my sheep for people you do not know, then you say, 'Men of Quraysh'?" He said: Then after a time, need compelled them to enter Medina. They entered it and began to carry dung to it, selling it, and living on its price. The old woman passed through one of the streets of Medina, and there was al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī sitting at the door of his house. He recognized the old woman, though she did not recognize him. He sent his servant to summon her. He said to her, "O handmaid of God, do you recognize me?" She said, "No." He said, "I am your guest on such-and-such a day." The old woman said, "May my father and mother be your ransom, you are he!" He said, "Yes." Then al-Ḥasan ordered that a thousand sheep from the charity (ṣadaqah) sheep be bought for her, and ordered that she be given a thousand dīnārs with them, and sent her with his servant to al-Ḥusayn. Al-Ḥusayn said to her, "With how much did my brother reach you?" She said, "With a thousand sheep and a thousand dīnārs." Al-Ḥusayn ordered that she be given the like of that. Then he sent her with his servant to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. He said to her, "With how much did al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn reach you?" She said, "With two thousand sheep and two thousand dīnārs." ʿAbd Allāh ordered that she be given two thousand sheep and two thousand dīnārs, and said to her, "Had you begun with me, I would have wearied them." The old woman returned to her husband with four thousand sheep and four thousand dīnārs.

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz left the mosque intending his home, alone. A young man of Thaqīf stood before him and walked by his side. ʿAbd Allāh said to him, "Do you have a need, O young man?" He said, "Your well-being and your success. I saw you walking alone, so I said: I shall protect you with myself, and I seek refuge with God if any harm should fly by your side." ʿAbd Allāh took his hand and walked with him to his home. Then he called for a thousand dīnārs and gave them to the young man, saying, "Spend these. How excellent is what your family has taught you!"

And it is related that a group of Arabs came to the grave of one of their generous men to visit it. They alighted at his grave and spent the night there, having come from a distant journey. One of them saw in a dream the owner of the grave saying to him, "Would you like to exchange your camel for my swift she-camel?" The deceased generous man had left a swift she-camel known for him, and this man had a fat camel. He said to him in the dream, "Yes." So he sold him in the dream his camel for his swift she-camel. When the contract was concluded between them, this man took his camel and slaughtered it in the dream. The man awoke from his sleep, and behold, blood was gushing from the neck of his camel. The man arose and slaughtered it, divided its meat, cooked it, and satisfied their need from it. Then they departed and traveled on. On the second day, while they were on the road, a rider met them. One of them said, "Is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, among you?" naming that man. He said, "I am he." He said to him, "Did you sell to so-and-so something?" mentioning the deceased, the owner of the grave. He said, "Yes, I sold my camel for his swift she-camel in a dream." He said, "Take this, his swift she-camel." Then he said, "He is my father. I saw him in a dream saying: If you are my son, then give my swift she-camel to so-and-so, son of so-and-so," and he named him.

And a man of Quraysh arrived from a journey and passed by a Bedouin on the open road whom time had prostrated and illness had harmed. He said, "O man, help us against time." The man said to his servant, "What remains with you of the provisions? Give it to him." The servant poured out four thousand dirhams into the lap of the Bedouin. He went to rise but could not, from weakness. He wept. The man said to him, "What makes you weep? Perhaps you deemed little what we gave you." He said, "No, but I remembered what the earth will eat of your generosity, and that made me weep."

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir bought from Khālid ibn ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ his house in the market for ninety thousand dirhams. When night came, he heard the weeping of Khālid's family. He said to his own family, "What is the matter with these?" They said, "They weep for their house." He said, "O servant, go to them and inform them that the money and the house are both theirs."

And it is said that Hārūn al-Rashīd sent to Mālik ibn Anas, may God have mercy on him, five hundred dīnārs. That reached al-Layth ibn Saʿd, and he sent him a thousand dīnārs. Hārūn became angry and said, "I gave him five hundred, and you give him a thousand, and you are one of my subjects?" He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I have from my estate every day a thousand dīnārs. I was ashamed to give him less than the income of a single day." And it is related that zakāh was not obligatory upon him, despite his income being a thousand dīnārs a day. And it is related that a woman asked al-Layth ibn Saʿd, may God have mercy on him, for some honey. He ordered that she be given a full waterskin of honey. It was said to him, "She would have been content with less than this." He said, "She asked according to her need, and we give according to the grace upon us." And al-Layth ibn Saʿd would not speak each day until he had given charity to three hundred and sixty poor persons.

And al-Aʿmash said: A sheep of mine fell ill, and Khaythamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān used to visit it morning and evening, asking me whether it had taken its full fodder and how the children were enduring since they lost its milk. I had a felt mat upon which I sat. When he left, he would say, "Take what is under the felt." Until there reached me, on account of the sheep's illness, more than three hundred dīnārs of his kindness, until I wished that the sheep had not recovered.

And ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān said to Asmāʾ ibn Khārijah: "It has reached me that you possess certain qualities. Tell me of them." He said, "They are more beautiful from others than from me." He said, "I adjure you to tell me of them." He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I have never stretched my leg between the hands of a sitting companion, nor have I ever prepared food and invited people to it but that they were more secure from me than I was from them, nor has any man ever set his face toward me asking me for something, and I deemed much anything I gave him."

And Saʿīd ibn Khālid entered upon Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. Saʿīd was a generous man; when he found nothing, he would write for the one who asked him a promissory note upon himself until his stipend came out. When Sulaymān looked at him, he recited this verse:

"I heard at dawn a caller: O you who aids the helping man!"

Then he said, "What is your need?" He said, "My debt." He said, "And how much is it?" He said, "Thirty thousand dīnārs." He said, "You have your debt, and the like of it."

And it is said that Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah fell ill, and his brothers were slow to visit him. It was said to him, "They are ashamed because of the debt they owe you." He said, "May God disgrace wealth that prevents brothers from visiting!" Then he ordered a crier to proclaim: "Whoever has a claim upon Qays ibn Saʿd is released from it." He said: His doorstep broke in the evening from the multitude of those who visited him and paid him the sick-visit.

From Abū Isḥāq, he said: I prayed the afternoon prayer in the mosque of al-Ashʿath in Kufa, seeking a debtor of mine. When I prayed, a robe and a pair of sandals were placed before me. I said, "I am not of the people of this mosque." They said, "Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays al-Kindī arrived last night from Mecca and ordered that every person who prays in the mosque be given a robe and a pair of sandals."

And Shaykh Abū Saʿd al-Ḥarkūshī al-Naysābūrī, may God have mercy on him, said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥāfiẓ say: I heard al-Shāfiʿī, the neighbor of Mecca, say: There was in Egypt a man known for collecting things for the poor. A child was born to one of them. He said: I came to him and said to him, "A child has been born to me, and I have nothing with me." He arose with me and entered upon a group, but nothing was opened. Then he came to the grave of a man and sat by it, and said, "May God have mercy on you. You used to do and make. Today I went around to a group and asked them to give something for a newborn, but nothing was arranged for me." He said: Then he arose, brought out a dīnār, divided it in two halves, and handed me one half, saying, "This is a debt upon me to you until God opens something for you." He said: I took it and left, and I set right what I could with it. He said: That inspector (muḥtasib) saw that person that night in a dream. He said: I heard all that you said, and we have no permission to answer. But come to my house and say to my children: Let them dig in the place of the brazier (kānūn) and bring out a purse containing five hundred dīnārs, and carry it to this man. When morning came, he went to the house of the deceased and told them the story. They said to him, "Sit." They dug the place, brought out the dīnārs, and came with them, placing them before him. He said, "This is your wealth, and my dream has no authority." They said, "He was generous in death, and we shall not be stingy in life." When they pressed him, he carried the dīnārs to the man, the father of the newborn, and told him the story. He said: He took from them a dīnār, broke it in two halves, gave him the half he had lent him, and carried the other half, saying, "This suffices me," and gave it in charity to the poor. Abū Saʿd said: I do not know which of them was more generous.

And it is related that al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, when he fell ill with his final illness in Egypt, said: "Order so-and-so to wash me." When he died, the news of his death reached him, and he attended. He said, "Bring me his account book." It was brought, and he looked in it. There was upon al-Shāfiʿī a debt of seventy thousand dirhams. He wrote it upon himself and paid it on his behalf. He said, "This is my washing of him" — meaning he intended thereby this. And Abū Saʿd al-Wāʿiẓ al-Ḥarkūshī said: When I came to Egypt, I sought the house of that man, and they directed me to it. I saw a group of his descendants and visited them. I saw in them the mark of goodness and the traces of virtue. I said, "His effect in goodness has reached them, and his blessing has appeared in them," adducing the saying of God, Exalted: {«وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَالِحًا»} ("And their father was righteous") [Al-Kahf 18:82]. And al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, said: I continue to love Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān for something that reached me about him: that one day he was riding his donkey and spurred it, and his button broke. He passed by a tailor and wanted to dismount to fix his button. The tailor said, "By God, you shall not dismount." The tailor arose to him and fixed his button. He brought out to him a purse containing ten dīnārs and handed it to the tailor, apologizing to him for its smallness. And al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, recited for himself:

"Alas, my heart grieves for wealth I might bestow upon the destitute among men of honor. My apology to one who comes asking me for what I do not possess is one of the calamities."

And from al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān, he said: A man took hold of the stirrup of al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him. He said, "O Rabīʿ, give him four dīnārs and apologize to him on my behalf." And al-Rabīʿ said: I heard al-Ḥumaydī say: Al-Shāfiʿī came from Ṣanʿāʾ to Mecca with ten thousand dīnārs. He pitched his tent in a place outside Mecca, spread them upon a cloth, and then turned to everyone who entered upon him, taking a handful and giving it to him, until he prayed the noon prayer. Then he shook the cloth, and nothing was upon it.

And from Abū Thawr, he said: Al-Shāfiʿī wanted to leave for Mecca, and he had wealth with him. He rarely kept anything, due to his generosity. I said to him, "You should buy with this wealth an estate that would be for you and your children." He said: He left, then returned to us. I asked him about that wealth. He said, "I found no estate in Mecca that I could buy, knowing its origin, and most of it is endowed (waqf). But I built in Minā a tent (miḍrab) for our companions to lodge in when they perform the pilgrimage." And al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, recited for himself:

"I see my soul yearning for things my wealth falls short of reaching. My soul does not obey me in miserliness, and my wealth does not reach my deeds."

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād al-Muhallabī said: My father entered upon al-Maʾmūn, and he gifted him one hundred thousand dirhams. When he arose from his presence, he gave it all in charity. That was reported to al-Maʾmūn. When he returned to him, al-Maʾmūn reproached him for that. He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, withholding what is available is an ill opinion of the Worshipped One." So he gifted him another one hundred thousand.

And a man stood before Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ and asked him. He ordered that he be given one hundred thousand dirhams. The man wept. Saʿīd said to him, "What makes you weep?" He said, "I weep for the earth that it should eat the like of you." He ordered that he be given another one hundred thousand.

And Abū Tammām entered upon Ibrāhīm ibn Shaklah with verses praising him. He found him ill. He accepted the praise and ordered his chamberlain to give him what would set him right. He said:

"Perhaps I shall rise from my illness and recompense him."

He remained (ill) for two months. The length of the stay wearied him, so he wrote to him:

"Verily, it is forbidden to accept our praise while leaving what we hope for of the gift. Just as dirhams and dīnārs in a sale are forbidden except hand to hand."

When the two verses reached Ibrāhīm, he said to his chamberlain, "How long did he remain at the door?" He said, "Two months." He said, "Give him thirty thousand." And he called for an inkwell and wrote to him:

"You hastened us, so our swift kindness came to you. No, had you given us respite, we would not have diminished. Take the little, and be as though you had not spoken, and we say as though we had not done."

And it is related that ʿUthmān had upon Ṭalḥah, may God be pleased with them both, fifty thousand dirhams. One day ʿUthmān went out to the mosque. Ṭalḥah said to him, "Your wealth is ready, so take it." He said, "It is yours, O Abū Muḥammad, as assistance for your munificence." And Saʿdā bint ʿAwf said: I entered upon Ṭalḥah and saw in him a heaviness. I said to him, "What is the matter with you?" He said, "Wealth has gathered with me, and it has grieved me." I said, "And what grieves you? Call your people." He said, "O servant, bring my people." He divided it among them. I asked the servant how much it was. He said, "Four hundred thousand."

And a Bedouin came to Ṭalḥah, asked him, and sought closeness to him through kinship. He said, "This kinship — no one has asked me by it before you. I have land for which ʿUthmān gave me three hundred thousand. If you wish, take it; and if you wish, I shall sell it to ʿUthmān and give you the price." He said, "The price." So he sold it to ʿUthmān and gave him the price.

And it is said that ʿAlī, may God honor his face, wept one day. It was said, "What makes you weep?" He said, "No guest has come to me for seven days. I fear that God has humiliated me."

And a man came to a friend of his and knocked on his door. He said, "What has brought you?" He said, "I owe four hundred dirhams of debt." So he weighed out four hundred dirhams and brought them out to him. Then he returned weeping. His wife said, "Why did you give him, since it pained you?" He said, "I weep only because I did not inquire into his condition until he needed to ask me." May God have mercy on those whose qualities these are, and may He forgive them all.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-خ-ل (b-kh-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is withholding, stinginess, or refusal to give what is due; also denotes a constriction of the soul (ḍīq al-nafs) in parting with wealth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, bukhl is the vice opposed to generosity (jūd) and is linked to a corrupt disposition (sūʾ al-khuluq) that impedes the fulfillment of religious obligations (farāʾiḍ) and commendable acts (mandūbāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to withholding material goods; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to withholding knowledge, praise, or due rights—thus a comprehensive moral failing.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with implicit predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — the title functions as a genitive construction (iḍāfah) where "bayān" (exposition) governs "dhamm" (blame), indicating a structured, didactic discourse.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us set forth the exposition of the blameworthiness of miserliness (bukhl), that the seeker of the Hereafter may be warned against it and may recognize its roots and branches, for it is a vice that corrupts the heart and severs the bonds of brotherhood, and it is contrary to the way of the Prophets, peace be upon them, and to the path of the righteous.

chapters.title_en: The Blameworthiness of Miserliness and the Excellence of Generosity — Section 485
chapters.arabic_text:
قال الله تعالى ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون وقال تعالى ولا يحسبن
الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خير لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما
بخلوا به يوم القيامة وقال تعالى الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل
ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إياكم والشح فإنه
أهلك من كان قبلكم حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم (1)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إياكم والشح PageV03P252
فإنه دعا من كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم
فقطعوا أرحامهم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا
خائن ولا سيء الملكة (2)
وفي رواية ولا جبار وفي رواية ولا منان وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم  ثلاث
مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه (3) حديث أن الله يبغض ثلاثا
الشيخ الزاني والبخيل المنان والفقير المختال أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي من
حديث أبي ذر دون قوله البخيل المنان وقال فيه الغني الظلوم وقد تقدم
وللطبراني في الأوسط من حديث علي إن الله ليبغض الغني الظلوم والشيخ الجهول
والعائل المختال وسنده ضعيف (4) حديث مثل المنفق والبخيل كمثل رجلين عليهما
جبة من حديد الحديث متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة (5) حديث خصلتان لا
تجتمعان في مؤمن البخل وسوء الخلق أخرجه الترمذي من حديث أبي سعيد وقال
غريب (6) حديث اللهم إني أعوذ بك من البخل وأعوذ بك من الجبن الحديث أخرجه
البخاري من حديث سعد وتقدم في الأذكار (7) حديث إياكم والظلم فإن الظلم
ظلمات يوم القيامة الحديث أخرجه الحاكم من حديث عبد الله بن عمرو دون قوله
أمرهم بالكذب فكذبوا وأمرهم بالظلم فظلموا قال عوضا عنهما وبالبخل فبخلوا
وبالفجور ففجروا وكذا رواه أبو داود على ذكر الشح وقد تقدم قبله بسبعة
أحاديث ولمسلم من حديث جابر اتقوا الظلم فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة
واتقوا الشح فذكره بلفظ آخر ولم يذكر الفحش (8) حديث شر ما في الرجل شح
هالع وجبن خالع أخرجه أبو داود من حديث جابر بسند جيد (9) حديث وما يدريك
أنه شهيد فلعله كان يتكلم فيما لا يعنيه أو يبخل بما لا ينقصه أخرجه أبو
يعلى من حديث أبي هريرة بسند ضعيف وللبيهقي في الشعب من حديث أنس أن أمه
قالت ليهنك الشهادة وهو عند الترمذي إلا أن رجلا قال له أبشر بالجنة (10)
حديث جبير بن مطعم بينما نحن نسير مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعه
الناس مقفلة من حنين علقت الأعراب به الحديث أخرجه البخاري وتقدم في أخلاق
النبوة //
وقال عمر رضي الله عنه قسم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسما فقلت غير
هؤلاء كان أحق به PageV03P253
{منهم فقال} إنهم يخيروني بين أن يسألوني بالفحش أو يبخلوني ولست بباخل
(1)
وقال أبو سعيد الخدري دخل رجلان  على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألاه
ثمن بعير فأعطاهما دينارين فخرجا من عنده فلقيهما عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله
عنه فأثنيا وقالا معروفا وشكرا ما صنع بهما فدخل عمر على رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم فأخبره بما قالا فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لكن فلان أعطيته
ما بين عشرة إلى مائة ولم يقل ذلك إن أحدكم ليسألني فينطلق في مسألته
متأبطها وهي نار فقال عمر فلم تعطهم ما هو نار فقال يأبون إلا أن يسألوني
ويأبى الله لي البخل (2)
وعن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الجود من جود الله
تعالى فجودوا يجد الله لكم ألا إن الله عز وجل خلق الجود فجعله في صورة رجل
وجعل رأسه راسخا في أصل شجرة طوبى وشد أغصانها بأغصان سدرة المنتهى ودلى
بعض أغصانها إلى الدنيا فمن تعلق بغصن منها أدخله الجنة ألا إن السخاء من
الإيمان والإيمان في الجنة وخلق البخل من مقته وجعل رأسه راسخا في أصل شجرة
الزقوم ودلى بعض أغصانها إلى الدنيا فمن تعلق بغصن منها أدخله النار ألا إن
البخل من الكفر والكفر في النار (3)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم السخاء شجرة تنبت في الجنة فلا يلج الجنة إلا
سخي والبخل شجرة تنبت في النار فلا يلج النار إلا بخيل (4)
وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لوفد بني لحيان من
سيدكم يا بني لحيان قالوا سيدنا جد بن قيس إلا أنه رجل فيه بخل فقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم وأي داء أدوأ من البخل ولكن سيدكم عمرو بن الجموح (5)
وفي رواية أنهم قالوا سيدنا جد بن قيس فقال بم تسودونه قالوا إنه أكثر
مالا وأنا على ذلك لنرى منه البخل فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم وأي داء أدوأ من
البخل ليس ذلك سيدكم قالوا فمن سيدنا يا رسول الله قالوا سيدكم بشر بن
البراء وقال علي رضي الله عنه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن  الله
يبغض البخيل في حياته السخي عنه موته (6)
وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم السخي الجهول أحب إلى
الله من العابد البخيل (7)
وقال أيضا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الشح والإيمان لا يجتمعان في قلب عبد
(8)
وقال أيضا خصلتان لا يجتمعان في مؤمن البخل وسوء الخلق (9)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينبغي لمؤمن أن يكون بخيلا ولا جبانا (10)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول قائلكم الشحيح PageV03P254
أعذر من الظالم وأي ظلم أظلم عند الله من الشح حلف الله تعالى بعزته
وعظمته وجلاله لا يدخل الجنة شحيح ولا بخيل (1) حديث كان يطوف بالبيت فإذا
رجل متعلق بأستار الكعبة وهو يقول بحرمة هذا البيت إلا غفرت لي الحديث في
ذم البخل وفيه قال إليك عني لا تحرقني بنارك الحديث بطوله وهو باطل لا أصل
له
الآثار قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لما خلق الله جنة عدن قال لها تزيني
فتزينت ثم قال لها أظهري أنهارك فأظهرت عين السلسبيل وعين الكافور وعين
التسنيم فتفجر منها في الجنان أنهار الخمر وأنهار العسل واللبن ثم قال لها
أظهري سررك وحجالك وكراسيك وحليك وحللك وحور عينك فأظهرت فنظر إليها فقال
تكلمى فقالت طوبى لمن دخلني فقال الله تعالى وعزتي لا أسكنك بخيلا
وقالت أم البنين أخت عمر بن عبد العزيز أف للبخيل لو كان البخل قميصا ما
لبسته ولو كان طريقا ما سلكته
وقال طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه إنا لنجد بأموالنا ما يجد البخلاء
لكننا نتصبر
وقال محمد بن المنكدر كان يقال إذا أراد الله بقوم شرا أمر الله عليهم
شرارهم وجعل أرزاقهم بأيدي بخلائهم
وقال علي كرم الله وجهه في خطبته إنه سيأتي على الناس زمان عضوض يعض
الموسر على ما في يده ولم يؤمر بذلك قال الله تعالى ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم
وقال عبد اللهبن عمرو الشح أشد من البخل لأن الشحيح هو الذي يشح على ما في
يد غيره حتى يأخذه ويشح بما في  يده فيحبسه والبخيل هو الذي يبخل بما في يده
وقال الشعبي لا أدري أيهما أبعد غورا في نار جهنم البخل أو الكذب وقيل
ورد على أنوشروان حكيم الهند وفيلسوف الروم فقال للهندي تكلم فقال خير
الناس من ألفى سخيا وعند الغضب وقورا وفي القول متأنيا وفي الرفعة متواضعا
وعلى كل ذي رحم مشفقا
وقام الرومي فقال من كان بخيلا ورث عدوه ماله ومن قل شكره لم ينل النجح
وأهل الكذب مذمومون وأهل النميمة يموتون فقراء ومن لم يرحم سلط عليه من لا
يرحمه
وقال الضحاك في قوله تعالى إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا قال البخل أمسك
الله تعالى أيديهم عن النفقة في سبيل الله فهم لا يبصرون الهدى
وقال كعب ما من صباح إلا وقد وكل به ملكان يناديان اللهم عجل لممسك تلفا
PageV03P255
وعجل لمنفق خلفا
وقال الأصمعي سمعت أعرابيا وقد وصف رجلا فقال لقد صغر فلان في عيني لعظم
الدنيا في عينه وكأنما يرى السائل ملك الموت إذا أتاه
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا أرى أن أعدل بخيلا لأن البخل يحمله على
الاستقصاء فيأخذ فوق حقه خيفة من أن يغبن فمن كان هكذا لا يكون مأمون
الأمانة
وقال علي كرم الله وجهه والله ما استقصى كريم قط حقه
قال الله تعلى عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض وقال الجاحظ ما بقي من اللذات إلا
ثلاث دم البخلاء وأكل القديد وحك الجرب
وقال بشر بن الحارث البخيل لا غيبة له قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك
إذا لبخيل ومدحت امرأة عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا صوامة
قوامة إلا أن فيها بخلا قال فما خيرها إذن // حديث مدحت امرأة عند النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا صوامة قوامة إلا أن فيها بخلا الحديث تقدم في
آفات اللسان
وقال بشر النظر إلى البخيل يقسي القلب ولقاء البخلاء كرب على قلوب
المؤمنين
وقال يحيى بن معاذ ما في القلب للأسخياء إلا حب ولو كانوا فجارا وللبخلاء
إلا بغض ولو  كانوا أبرارا
وقال ابن المعتز أبخل الناس بماله أجودهم بعرضه
ولقي يحيى بن زكريا عليهما السلام
إبليس في صورته فقال له يا إبليس أخبرني بأحب الناس إليك وأبغض الناس
إليك قال أحب الناس إلي المؤمن البخيل وأبغض الناس إلي الفاسق السخي قال له
لم قال لأن البخيل قد كفاني بخله والفاسق السخي الخوف أن يطلع الله عليه في
سخائه فيقبله ثم ولى وهو يقول لولا أنك يحيى لما أخبرتك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ح-ح (sh-ḥ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is constriction, tightness, and intense niggardliness; al-shuḥḥ denotes an avaricious craving that impels one to withhold what one possesses and covet what others possess.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, shuḥḥ is a vice of the soul (radhīlah nafsāniyyah) opposed to the virtue of generosity (sakhāʾ); it is the inward disposition that breeds miserliness (bukhl) as its outward act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, shuḥḥ is the "itch" of avarice in the heart; metaphorically (majāz), it is applied to the moral disease that consumes one's religion, as the Prophet's warning "Beware of shuḥḥ" employs the imperative of caution (īyāka) to signal an imminent destructive threat.
- Root: ب-خ-ل (b-kh-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is withholding and refraining from giving what is due; al-bukhl is the act of stinginess, distinguished from shuḥḥ as its outward manifestation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Bukhl is the withholding of what one is obligated to give, whether wealth, knowledge, or aid; it is a branch of kufr in the moral order, as the prophetic tradition links it to the fire.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The rhetorical contrast between shuḥḥ (inner avarice) and bukhl (outer stinginess) is drawn explicitly in the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr cited herein, where shuḥḥ is deemed more severe — a distinction of degree, not kind.
- Root: س-خ-و (s-kh-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is ease, liberality, and softness; al-sakhāʾ is the natural disposition of giving freely without reluctance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sakhāʾ is the virtue (faḍīlah) by which one expends wealth in obedience to God, and it is paired with īmān in the prophetic traditions, being its fruit and sign.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The tree imagery — "generosity is a tree that grows in Paradise" — is a metaphorical (majāz) personification of moral qualities as botanical entities, a rhetorical device (tashkhīṣ) common in prophetic speech.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional and Exhortative Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-tahdhīr) — The repeated "īyākum wa-l-shuḥḥ" (Beware of miserliness) is an instance of taḥdhīr (warning) with the accusative of the warned-against object, governed by an implied verb (uḥadhdhirukum), a construction Sībawayh treats under bāb al-taḥdhīr, where the warned object is placed in naṣb by virtue of the omitted verb of caution.
chapters.translation:
I say — God Most High said: {«And whoever is saved from the avarice of his own soul — those are the successful»} (Q. 59:9). And He said Most High: {«And let not those who are miserly with what God has given them of His bounty suppose that it is good for them — rather, it is evil for them. They will be collared with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection»} (Q. 3:180). And He said Most High: {«Those who are miserly and command people to miserliness and conceal what God has given them of His bounty»} (Q. 4:37). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Beware of miserliness (al-shuḥḥ), for it destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to deem lawful their forbidden things." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Beware of miserliness, for it summoned those before you, and they shed their blood; it summoned them, and they deemed lawful their forbidden things; it summoned them, and they cut their kinship ties." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No miser (bakhīl), no deceiver (khubb), no traitor (khāʾin), and no evil-tempered master (sīʾ al-malkah) shall enter Paradise." In another narration: "nor any tyrant (jabbār)"; in another narration: "nor any one who reminds others of his favors (mannān)." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Three things are destructive: miserliness obeyed, passion followed, and a man's self-admiration."

The hadith — "God hates three: the elderly fornicator, the miserly one who reminds others of his gifts, and the poor man who is conceited" — was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī from the hadith of Abū Dharr, without the phrase "the miserly one who reminds others of his gifts," and in it he said instead: "the wealthy wrongdoer (al-ghanī al-ẓalūm)," and it has preceded. Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ, from the hadith of ʿAlī: "God indeed hates the wealthy wrongdoer, the elderly ignoramus, and the poor conceited man" — its chain is weak.

The hadith — "The likeness of the spender and the miser is like two men wearing cloaks of iron" — is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh) from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.

The hadith — "Two traits never combine in a believer: miserliness and bad character" — was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī from the hadith of Abū Saʿīd, and he said it is gharīb (unusual).

The hadith — "O God, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice" — was transmitted by al-Bukhārī from the hadith of Saʿd, and it has preceded in the section on invocations (al-adhkār).

The hadith — "Beware of wrongdoing, for wrongdoing is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection" — was transmitted by al-Ḥākim from the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, without his saying: "He commanded them to lie, and they lied; He commanded them to do wrong, and they wronged" — instead he said in place of these two: "and with miserliness, and they were miserly; and with lewdness, and they were lewd." Likewise Abū Dāwūd narrated it with the mention of miserliness (al-shuḥḥ), and it has preceded before it by seven hadiths. Muslim, from the hadith of Jābir: "Fear wrongdoing, for wrongdoing is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection, and fear miserliness" — and he mentioned it with another wording, and did not mention lewdness.

The hadith — "The worst thing in a man is consuming miserliness (shuḥḥ hāliʿ) and paralyzing cowardice (jubn khāliʿ)" — was transmitted by Abū Dāwūd from the hadith of Jābir with a sound chain.

The hadith — "And what makes you know that he is a martyr? Perhaps he used to speak about what did not concern him, or was miserly with what would not diminish him" — was transmitted by Abū Yaʿlā from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah with a weak chain. Al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from the hadith of Anas, that his mother said to him: "May martyrdom be blessed for you" — and it is with al-Tirmidhī, except that a man said to him: "Rejoice with Paradise."

The hadith of Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim — "While we were traveling with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and the people were with him, returning from Ḥunayn, the Bedouins clung to him" — was transmitted by al-Bukhārī, and it has preceded in the section on the character of prophethood.

And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, distributed a distribution, and I said: 'Others than these were more deserving of it.' He said: {«They give me the choice between asking me with importunity or making me miserly, and I am not miserly»}."

And Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: "Two men entered upon the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and asked him for the price of a camel. He gave them two dinars. They left his presence, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, met them. They praised him and spoke well and thanked him for what he had done for them. So ʿUmar entered upon the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him of what they had said. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'But so-and-so — I gave him between ten and a hundred, and he did not say that. Indeed, one of you asks me, and he departs with his request tucked under his arm, and it is a fire.' ʿUmar said: 'Then why do you give them what is fire?' He said: 'They refuse but to ask me, and God refuses for me miserliness.'"

And from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Generosity (al-jūd) is from the generosity of God Most High, so be generous, and God will be generous to you. Indeed, God Almighty created generosity and made it in the form of a man, and made its head firmly rooted in the trunk of the Tree of Ṭūbā, and bound its branches to the branches of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntahā), and lowered some of its branches to the world. Whoever clings to a branch of it, it admits him to Paradise. Indeed, liberality (al-sakhāʾ) is from faith, and faith is in Paradise. And He created miserliness from His wrath, and made its head firmly rooted in the trunk of the Tree of Zaqqūm, and lowered some of its branches to the world. Whoever clings to a branch of it, it admits him to the Fire. Indeed, miserliness is from unbelief, and unbelief is in the Fire.'"

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Generosity is a tree that grows in Paradise, and none enters Paradise but a generous man; and miserliness is a tree that grows in the Fire, and none enters the Fire but a miserly man."

And Abū Hurayrah said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to the delegation of Banū Liḥyān: 'Who is your master, O Banū Liḥyān?' They said: 'Our master is Jadd ibn Qays, except that he is a man in whom there is miserliness.' He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'And what disease is more virulent than miserliness? But your master is ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ.'" In another narration, they said: "Our master is Jadd ibn Qays." He said: "By what do you make him your master?" They said: "He has the most wealth." And despite that, we see in him miserliness. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "And what disease is more virulent than miserliness? That one is not your master." They said: "Then who is our master, O Messenger of God?" They said: "Your master is Bashīr ibn al-Barāʾ."

And ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'God indeed hates the miser in his life, and the generous man at his death.'"

And Abū Hurayrah said: "The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The generous ignoramus is more beloved to God than the miserly worshiper.'"

And he also said: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Miserliness (al-shuḥḥ) and faith do not combine in the heart of a servant.'"

And he also said: "Two traits never combine in a believer: miserliness and bad character."

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is not fitting for a believer to be miserly nor cowardly."

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "One of you says: 'The miserly man is more excusable than the wrongdoer.' But what wrongdoing is more wrongful before God than miserliness? God Almighty has sworn by His might, His majesty, and His glory that no miserly man (shaḥīḥ) and no stingy man (bakhīl) shall enter Paradise."

The hadith — "He was circumambulating the House, and there was a man clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah, saying: 'By the sanctity of this House, forgive me' — the hadith in condemnation of miserliness, in which he said: 'Away from me, do not burn me with your fire' — the hadith in its entirety is false (bāṭil), having no basis.

THE SAYINGS OF THE COMPANIONS AND EARLY SCHOLARS (Āthār):
Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: "When God created the Garden of Eden, He said to it: 'Adorn yourself,' and it adorned itself. Then He said to it: 'Show your rivers,' and it showed the spring of Salsabīl, the spring of Kāfūr, and the spring of Tasnīm, and from them gushed forth in the gardens the rivers of wine, the rivers of honey, and of milk. Then He said to it: 'Show your chambers, your pavilions, your thrones, your ornaments, your garments, and your wide-eyed maidens,' and it showed them. Then He looked at it and said: 'Speak.' It said: 'Blessed is he who enters me.' Then God Most High said: 'By My might, I shall not house a miser in you.'"

And Umm al-Banīn, the sister of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, said: "Fie on the miser! Were miserliness a shirt, I would not wear it; were it a road, I would not tread it."

And Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, may God be pleased with him, said: "We indeed find in our wealth what the misers find, but we endure it patiently."

And Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir said: "It used to be said: 'When God desires evil for a people, He sets their wicked ones over them, and places their provisions in the hands of their misers.'"

And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said in his sermon: "There will come upon the people a biting time (zamān ʿaḍūḍ) in which the wealthy man will bite tightly upon what is in his hand, though he was not commanded to do so. God Most High said: {«And do not forget bounty among yourselves»} (Q. 2:237)."

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: "Miserliness (al-shuḥḥ) is more severe than stinginess (al-bukhl), for the shāḥiḥ (miserly man) is he who is avaricious over what is in another's hand until he takes it, and avaricious over what is in his own hand, so he withholds it; while the bakhīl (stingy man) is he who withholds what is in his own hand."

And al-Shaʿbī said: "I do not know which of the two goes deeper into the fire of Hell: miserliness or lying."

And it was said: "There were presented to Anūshirwān the sage of India and the philosopher of Rome. He said to the Indian: 'Speak.' He said: 'The best of people is he who is found generous, dignified at anger, deliberate in speech, humble in elevation, and compassionate toward every kinsman.' Then the Roman stood and said: 'He who is miserly bequeaths his wealth to his enemy; he whose gratitude is little attains no success; the people of lying are blameworthy; the people of slander die poor; and he who does not show mercy is given dominion over one who will not show him mercy.'"

And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said concerning His saying Most High: {«Indeed, We have placed on their necks fetters»} (Q. 36:8): "It means miserliness — God Most High has restrained their hands from spending in the path of God, so they do not see guidance."

And Kaʿb said: "There is no morning but that two angels are appointed over it, calling out: 'O God, hasten destruction for the withholder, and hasten replacement for the spender.'"

And al-Aṣmaʿī said: "I heard a Bedouin describing a man, and he said: 'So-and-so has become small in my eyes for the greatness of this world in his eye, as though he sees the beggar as the Angel of Death when he comes to him.'"

And Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: "I do not consider a miser to be trustworthy, for miserliness drives him to exacting scrutiny, so he takes more than his due out of fear of being cheated. Whoever is like this cannot be trusted with a trust."

And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: "By God, no noble man has ever exacted his full due." God Most High said: {«He has known some of it and turned away from some»} (Q. 73:20).

And al-Jāḥiẓ said: "Nothing remains of pleasures but three: the blood of misers, eating dried meat, and scratching scabies."

And Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith said: "The miser has no backbiting (i.e., it is not a sin to speak ill of him)." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, you are then miserly." And when a woman was praised before the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, they said: "She fasts and prays, except that there is in her some miserliness." He said: "Then what good is she?" — The hadith of praising a woman before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and their saying "She fasts and prays, except that there is in her some miserliness" has preceded in the section on the afflictions of the tongue.

And Bishr said: "Looking at a miser hardens the heart, and meeting misers is distress upon the hearts of the believers."

And Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "There is nothing in the heart for the generous but love, even were they sinners; and for the misers nothing but hatred, even were they righteous."

And Ibn al-Muʿtazz said: "The most miserly of people with his wealth is the most generous of them with his honor."

And Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, peace be upon them both, met Iblīs in his form and said to him: "O Iblīs, tell me of the most beloved of people to you and the most hateful of people to you." He said: "The most beloved of people to me is the believing miser, and the most hateful of people to me is the sinful generous man." He said to him: "Why?" He said: "Because the miser has sufficed me with his miserliness, while the sinful generous man — I fear that God might look upon him in his generosity and accept him." Then he turned away, saying: "Were you not Yaḥyā, I would not have told you."

### |||| حكايات البخلاء

قيل كان بالبصرة رجل موسر بخيل فدعاه بعض جيرانه وقدم إليه طباهجة ببيض
فأكل منه فأكثر وجعل يشرب الماء فانتفخ بطنه ونزل به الكرب والموت فجعل
يتلوى فلما جهده الأمر وصف حاله للطبيب فقال لا بأس عليك تقيأ ما أكلت فقال
هاه أتقيأ طباهجة ببيض الموت ولا ذلك
وقيل أقبل أعرابي يطلب رجلا وبين يديه تين فغطى التين بكسائه فجلس
الأعرابي فقال له الرجل هل تحسن من القرآن شيئا قال نعم فقرأ والزيتون وطور
سينين فقال وأين التين قال هو تحت كسائك
ودعا بعضهم أخا له ولم يطعمه شيئا فحبسه إلى العصر حتى اشتد جوعه وأخذه
مثل الجنون فأخذ صاحب البيت العود وقال له بحياتي أي صوت تشتهي أن أسمعك
قال صوت المقلى
ويحكى أن محمد بن يحيى بن خالد بن برمك كان بخيلا قبيح البخل فسئل نسيب
له كان يعرفه عنه فقال له قائل صف لي مائدته فقال هي فتر في فتر وصحافه
منقورة من حب الخشخاش قيل فمن يحضرها قال الكرام الكاتبون قال فما يأكل معه
أحد قال بلى الذباب فقال سوأتك بدت وأنت خاص به وثوبك مخرق قال أنا والله
ما أقدر على إبرة أخيطه بها ولو ملك محمد بيتا من بغداد إلى النوبة مملوءا
إبرا ثم جاءه جبريل وميكائيل ومعهما يعقوب النبي عليه السلام يطلبون منه
إبرة ويسألونه إعارتهم إياها ليخيط بها قميص يوسف الذي قد من دبر ما فعل
ويقال كان مروان بن أبي حفصة لا يأكل اللحم بخلا حتى يقرم إليه فإذا قرم
إليه أرسل غلامه فاشترى له رأسا فأكله فقيل له
نراك لا تأكل إلا الرءوس في الصيف والشتاء فلم تختار ذلك قال نعم الرأس
أعرف سعره فآمن خيانة الغلام ولا يستطيع أن يغبنني فيه وليس بلحم يطبخه
الغلام فيقدر أن يأكل منه إن مس عينا أو أذنا أو خدا وقفت على ذلك وآكل منه
ألوانا عينه لونا وأذنه لونا ولسانه لونا وغلصمته لونا ودماغه لونا وأكفي
مؤونة
PageV03P256
طبخه فقد اجتمعت لي فيه مرافق
وخرج يوما يريد الخليفة المهدي فقالت له امرأة من أهله مالي عليك إن رجعت
بالجائزة فقال إن أعطيت مائة ألف أعطيتك درهما فأعطي ستين ألف فأعطاها
أربعة دوانق
واشترى مرة لحما بدرهم فدعاه صديق له فرد اللحم إلى القصاب بنقصان دانق
وقال أكره الإسراف
وكان للأعمش جار وكان لا يزال يعرض عليه المنزل ويقول لو دخلت فأكلت كسرة
وملحا فيأبى عليه الأعمش فعرض عليه ذات يوم فوافق جوع الأعمش فقال سر بنا
فدخل منزله فقرب إليه كسرة وملحا فجاء سائل فقال له رب المنزل بورك فيك
فأعاد عليه المسألة فقال له بورك فيك فلما سأل الثالثة قال له اذهب والله
وإلا خرجت إليك بالعصا قال فناداه الأعمش وقال اذهب ويحك فلا والله ما رأيت
أحدا أصدق مواعيد منه هو منذ مدة يدعوني على كسرة وملح فوالله ما زادني
عليهما

### ||| بيان الإيثار وفضله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-خ-ل (b-kh-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "niggardliness" or "withholding" — the refusal to part with what one possesses, whether wealth, food, or favor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, bukhl is the vice opposing sakhavāʾ (generosity); it is a moral disease of the soul that withholds what is due to God and His creatures, often linked to distrust of divine providence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for avarice in material dealings; metaphorically, it can denote spiritual withholding (e.g., withholding knowledge or praise), but in these narratives it remains in the literal domain of food and money.
- Root: ق-ر-م (q-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To crave" or "to long intensely" for something, especially meat; the root carries a sense of acute desire that overcomes restraint.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ethical discourse, qaram denotes the natural appetite that, when unchecked, leads to excess; here it highlights the miser's struggle between avarice and bodily need.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal craving for flesh; the narrative uses it to expose the hypocrisy of the miser who abstains only until appetite overpowers him.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In sentences like "طباهجة ببيض" (a dish of eggs), the prepositional phrase functions as a qualifier, and the syntax of reported speech (ḥikāyah) requires careful tracking of direct vs. indirect quotation, as seen in the repeated "قال" (he said) chains.
chapters.translation:
I say: Among the tales of the miserly, it is related that there was in Basra a wealthy but miserly man. One of his neighbors invited him and served him a dish of eggs (ṭabāhijah bi-bayḍ). He ate of it excessively and kept drinking water until his belly swelled, and distress and the pangs of death descended upon him, so he began to writhe in agony. When the matter became unbearable for him, he described his condition to a physician, who said: "Nothing is wrong with you — vomit what you have eaten." He replied: "What! Shall I vomit up a dish of eggs — the death of me? Never, not even for that!"

And it is related that a Bedouin came seeking a man, and before the man were figs, so he covered the figs with his cloak. The Bedouin sat down, and the man said to him: "Do you know anything of the Quran?" He said: "Yes." So he recited: {«وَالتِّينِ وَالزَّيْتُونِ وَطُورِ سِينِينَ»} ("By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai"). The man said: "And where is the fig?" He replied: "It is under your cloak."

And another miser invited his brother but fed him nothing, detaining him until late afternoon until his hunger became severe and he was seized with something like madness. So the host took up a lute and said to him: "By my life, what melody do you desire that I should play for you?" He said: "The sound of the frying pan."

And it is related that Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Khālid ibn Barmak was miserly, ugly in his avarice. A kinsman of his who knew him well was asked about him, and a questioner said: "Describe his table to me." He said: "It is a mat upon a mat, with plates hollowed out to the size of poppy seeds." It was said: "Then who attends it?" He said: "The noble recording angels (al-kirām al-kātibūn)." It was said: "Then does no one eat with him?" He said: "Yes — the flies." Then he said: "Your evil has become manifest, and you are singled out for it, and your garment is torn." He replied: "By God, I cannot afford a needle to sew it with. Even if Muḥammad owned a house from Baghdad to Nubia filled with needles, and then Gabriel and Michael came, along with the Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him), seeking from him a single needle and asking him to lend it to them to sew the shirt of Joseph which was torn from behind — he would not do it."

And it is said that Marwān ibn Abī Ḥafṣah would not eat meat out of avarice until he craved it intensely. When he craved it, he would send his servant to buy him a sheep's head and eat it. So it was said to him: "We see that you eat nothing but heads, in summer and winter alike — why have you chosen this?" He said: "Yes — the head, I know its price, so I am safe from the servant's treachery, and he cannot cheat me on it. Nor is it meat that the servant cooks, so he cannot eat some of it. If he touches an eye, an ear, or a cheek, I notice it. And I eat from it various kinds: its eye is one flavor, its ear another, its tongue another, its gullet another, its brain another — and I am spared the expense of cooking it. So all conveniences are gathered for me in it."

And one day he went out intending to visit the Caliph al-Mahdī, and a woman of his household said to him: "What do I get from you if you return with a gift?" He said: "If I am given a hundred thousand, I will give you a dirham." He was given sixty thousand, and he gave her four dānaqs (a fraction of a dirham).

And once he bought meat for a dirham, and a friend invited him, so he returned the meat to the butcher at a loss of one dānaq, saying: "I dislike extravagance."

And al-Aʿmash had a neighbor who would continually offer him his house, saying: "If only you would enter and eat a morsel of bread with salt." But al-Aʿmash would refuse him. One day he offered him this, and it coincided with al-Aʿmash's hunger, so he said: "Lead the way." He entered his house, and the host brought him a morsel of bread and salt. Then a beggar came, and the host said to him: "God bless you" (i.e., go away). The beggar repeated his request, and he said again: "God bless you." When he asked a third time, he said: "Go, by God — or else I will come out at you with a stick!" So al-Aʿmash called out to him and said: "Go, woe to you! By God, I have never seen anyone more truthful in his promises than him. For a long time he has been inviting me to a morsel of bread and salt — and by God, he has given me nothing more than those two things."

chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن السخاء والبخل كل منهما ينقسم إلى درجات
فأرفع درجة السخاء الإيثار وهو أن يجود بالمال مع الحاجة
وإنما السخاء عبارة عن بذل ما لا يحتاج إليه لمحتاج أو لغير محتاج والبذل
مع الحاجة أشد
وكما أن السخاوة قد تنتهي إلى أن يسخو الإنسان على غيره مع الحاجة فالبخل
قد ينتهي إلى أن يبخل على نفسه مع الحاجة فكم من بخيل يمسك المال ويمرض فلا
يتداوى ويشتهي الشهوة فلا يمنعه منها إلا البخل بالثمن ولو وجدها مجانا
لأكلها
فهذا بخيل على نفسه مع الحاجة وذلك يؤثر على نفسه غيره مع أنه محتاج إليه
فانظر ما  بين الرجلين فإن الأخلاق عطايا يضعها الله حيث يشاء وليس بعد
الإيثار درجة في السخاء
وقد أثنى الله على الصحابة رضي الله عنهم به فقال ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو
كان بهم خصاصة وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أيما امرئ اشتهى شهوة فرد
شهوته وآثر على نفسه غفر له (1) حديث عائشة ما شبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم ثلاثة أيام متواليات ولو شئنا لشبعنا ولكنا كنا نؤثر على أنفسنا أخرجه
البيهقي في الشعب بلفظ ولكنه كان يؤثر على نفسه وأول الحديث عند مسلم بلفظ
ما شبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أيام تباعا من خبز بر حتى مضى
لسبيله وللشيخين ما شبع آل محمد منذ قدم المدينة ثلاثة ليال تباعا حتى قبض
زاد مسلم من طعام
ونزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف فلم يجد عند أهله شيئا فدخل عليه
رجل من الأنصار فذهب بالضيف إلى أهله ثم وضع بين يديه الطعام وأمر امرأته
بإطفاء السراج وجعل يمد يده إلى الطعام كأنه يأكل ولا يأكل حتى أكل الضيف
فلما أصبح قال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقد عجب الله من صنيعكم
الليلة إلى ضيفكم ونزلت ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة // حديث نزل
به ضيف فلم يجد عند أهله شيئا فدخل عليه رجل من الأنصار فذهب به إلى أهله
الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة متفق عليه
من حديث أبي هريرة
فالسخاء خلق من أخلاق الله تعالى والإيثار أعلى درجات السخاء
وكان ذلك من أدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى سماه الله تعالى عظيما
فقال تعالى وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم وقال سهل بن عبد الله التستري قال موسى عليه
السلام يا رب أرني بعض درجات محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته فقال يا موسى
إنك لن تطيق ذلك ولكن أريك منزلة من منازله جليلة عظيمة فضلته بها عليك
وعلى جميع خلقي قال فكشف له عن  ملكوت السموات فنظر إلى منزلة كادت تتلف
نفسه من أنوارها وقربها PageV03P257
من الله تعالى فقال يارب بماذا بلغت به إلى هذه الكرامة قال بخلق اختصصته
به من بينهم وهو الإيثار يا موسى لا يأتيني أحد منهم قد عمل به وقتا من
عمره إلا استحييت من محاسبته وبوأته من جنتي حيث يشاء وقيل خرج عبد الله بن
جعفر إلى ضيعة له فنزل على نخيل قوم وفيه غلام أسود يعمل فيه إذ أتى الغلام
بقوته فدخل الحائط كلب ودنا من الغلام فرمى إليه الغلام بقرص فأكله ثم رمى
إليه الثاني والثالث فأكله وعبد الله ينظر إليه فقال يا غلام كم قوتك كل
يوم قال ما رأيت قال فلم آثرت به هذا الكلب قال ما هي بأرض كلاب إنه جاء من
مسافة بعيدة جائعا فكرهت أن أشبع وهو جائع قال فما أنت صانع اليوم قال أطوي
يومي هذا فقال عبد الله بن جعفر ألام على السخاء إن هذا الغلام لأسخى مني
فاشترى الحائط والغلام وما فيه من الآلات فأعتق الغلام ووهبه منه
وقال عمر رضي الله عنه أهدي إلى رجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم رأس شاة فقال إن أخي كان أحوج مني إليه فبعث به إليه فلم يزل واحد
يبعث به إلى آخر حتى تداوله سبعة أبيات ورجع إلى الأول

بينه وبين نبيي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فبات على فراشه يفديه بنفسه ويؤثره
