As for his delusion from the standpoint of knowledge, it is that he limited himself to the science of legal rulings and thought it was the knowledge of religion, abandoning the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him). Perhaps he even attacks the hadith scholars, saying: "They are transmitters of reports and carriers of books; they have no understanding." He also abandoned the science of refining character, and abandoned understanding (fiqh) of God the Exalted by perceiving His majesty and greatness—which is the knowledge that begets fear, awe, and humility, and impels one to piety. You see him feeling secure from God, deluded by Him, relying on the fact that God must surely have mercy on him, for he has upheld the religion of the people—and that if he did not occupy himself with legal rulings, the lawful and unlawful would be neglected. He has abandoned the sciences that are most important, while he is heedless and deluded. The cause of his delusion is what he has heard in the Sacred Law of the veneration of jurisprudence, not knowing that that jurisprudence is understanding of God and knowledge of His attributes that inspire fear and hope, so that the heart feels fear and adheres to piety. For God the Exalted said: {«Why should not a group from each section of them go forth to become learned in the religion, and warn their people when they return to them, that they may be cautious?»} (9:122). What achieves the warning is not this science, for the purpose of this science is preserving wealth through the conditions of transactions, and preserving bodies through wealth, by repelling killing and wounds. Wealth is but an instrument in the path of God, and the body is a mount.

The important knowledge is knowing the way of conduct and cutting the obstacles of the heart, which are the blameworthy traits—for they are the veil between the servant and God the Exalted. If one dies sullied with those traits, he is veiled from God.

His example in limiting himself to the science of jurisprudence is like one who, in traversing the path of the Hajj, limits himself to the knowledge of stitching sandals and socks. There is no doubt that without it the Hajj would be neglected, but the one who limits himself to it has nothing of the Hajj and is not on its way. We have explained this in the Book of Knowledge. Among these are those who limited themselves to the science of juristic disputes (khilāfiyyāt), caring only to learn the method of argumentation, refutation, silencing opponents, and repelling the truth for the sake of victory and boasting. He spends night and day searching for contradictions among the adherents of the schools, examining the defects of peers, and catching the types of harmful insinuations. These are the predators of humanity; their nature is to harm, and their concern is folly. They do not seek knowledge except for what is necessary for boasting against peers. Every knowledge they do not need for boasting—like the knowledge of the heart and the knowledge of the way to God the Exalted by erasing blameworthy traits and replacing them with praiseworthy ones—they deem insignificant and call it "embellishment" and "the speech of preachers." In their view, true verification is only knowing the details of the wrangling that occurs between two wrestlers in debate.

These have gathered what those before them gathered in the science of legal rulings, but they increased, for they occupied themselves with what is not among the communal obligations either. Rather, all the subtleties of debate in jurisprudence are an innovation (bidʿah) unknown to the predecessors. As for the evidences of rulings, they are encompassed in the science of the school—the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him) and understanding their meanings. As for the tricks of debate—such as breaking, inverting, corrupting the premise, composition, and transitivity—these were only innovated to manifest victory and silencing, and to establish the market of debate. So the delusion of these is far greater and uglier than the delusion of those before them.

Another group occupied themselves with the science of theology (kalām) and debate over passions, refuting opponents, tracking their contradictions, and amassing knowledge of the various doctrines. They occupied themselves with learning the methods of debating those and silencing them, splitting into many factions. They believed that no servant has any deed without faith, and no faith is valid without learning their debate and what they called "the evidences of their creeds." They thought that none knows God and His attributes better than them, and that there is no faith for one who does not hold their doctrine and learn their science. Each faction called to itself.

Then they are two factions: the erring and the truthful. The erring is the one that calls to other than the Sunnah, and the truthful is the one that calls to the Sunnah. Delusion encompasses all of them.

As for the erring, it is due to their heedlessness of their error and their assumption of their own salvation. They are many factions, each excommunicating the other. They were only afflicted because they did not suspect their own opinion, nor did they first establish the conditions and methodology of evidences. So one of them saw the ambiguity (shubhah) as an evidence, and the evidence as an ambiguity.

As for the truthful faction, its delusion is that it thought debate to be the most important of matters and the best of acts of drawing near to God in His religion, claiming that no one's religion is complete unless he investigates and researches, and that whoever believes in God and His Messenger without research and verification of evidence is not a believer—or not a complete believer, nor near to God.

Due to this corrupt assumption, they spent their lives learning debate, researching doctrines, the ravings of the innovators, and their contradictions. They neglected themselves and their hearts until their sins and errors, outward and inward, were blinded to them. One of them thinks that his occupation with debate is more virtuous and nearer to God and better—but due to his delight in victory and silencing, the pleasure of leadership, and the glory of belonging to the defense of the religion of God the Exalted, his insight was blinded, and he did not look to the first generation. For the Prophet (peace be upon him) testified that they were the best of creation, and that they (Page V03P394) encountered many of the people of innovation and passion, yet they did not make their lives and religion a target for disputes and debates, nor did they occupy themselves with that to the neglect of examining their hearts, members, and states. Rather, they only spoke of it when they saw a need and perceived signs of acceptance, mentioning to the extent of the need what indicates to the erring one his error. When they saw one persisting in error, they abandoned him, turned away from him, and hated him for God—without engaging in endless wrangling with him. They said: "The truth is calling to the Sunnah, and from the Sunnah is abandoning debate in calling to the Sunnah."

For Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: "No people ever went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given to debate." (A hadith: He came out one day to his companions while they were debating and disputing, and he became angry until it was as if a pomegranate had burst in his face with redness of anger, and he said: "Was it for this you were sent? Were you commanded to strike the Book of God against one another? Look at what you were commanded and do it, and what you were forbidden, desist from it." He rebuked them for that, and they were the most deserving of God's creation of argumentation and debate.)

Then they saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) sent to all the people of religions, yet he did not sit with them in a session of debate for refutation, silencing, verifying an argument, repelling a question, or raising a refutation. He only debated them by reciting the Quran revealed to them, and he did not add to the debate beyond that—because that disturbs hearts and extracts from them doubts and ambiguities, which then cannot be erased from their hearts. He was not incapable of debating them with divisions and subtleties of syllogisms, nor of teaching his companions the method of debate and refutation. But the astute and the resolute were not deluded by this, saying: "If all the people of the earth were saved and we perished, their salvation would not benefit us; and if we were saved and they perished, their destruction would not harm us. We are not obligated in debate more than the Companions were with the Jews, Christians, and people of religions. They did not waste their lives refining their debates. Why should we waste our lives and not turn them to what benefits us on the day of our poverty and need? We do not plunge into

### |

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

### || كتاب  التوبة وهو الكتاب الأول من ربع المنجيات من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي بتحميده يستفتح كل كتاب وبذكره يصدر كل خطاب وبحمده يتنعم
أهل النعيم في دار الثواب وباسمه يتسلى الأشقياء وإن أرخي دونهم الحجاب
وضرب بينهم وبين السعداء بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله
العذاب ونتوب إليه توبة من يوقن أنه رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب ونرجوه رجاء
من يعلم أنه الملك الرحيم الغفور التواب ونمزج الخوف برجائنا مزج من لا
يرتاب أنه مع كونه غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب
ونصلي على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وصحبه صلاة تنقذنا من
هول المطلع يوم العرض والحساب وتمهد لنا عند الله زلفى وحسن مآب
أما بعد فإن التوبة عن الذنوب بالرجوع إلى ستار العيوب وعلام الغيوب مبدأ
طريق السالكين ورأس مال الفائزين وأول أقدام المريدين ومفتاح استقامة
المائلين ومطلع الاصطفاء والاجتباء للمقربين ولأبينا آدم عليه الصلاة
والسلام وعلى سائر الأنبياء أجمعين وما أجدر بالأولاد الإقتداء بالآباء
والأجداد فلا غرو إن أذنب الآدمي واجترم فهي شنشنة نعرفها من أخزم ومن أشبه
أباه فما ظلم ولكن الأب إذا جبر بعد ما كسر وعمر بعد أن هدم فليكن النزوع
إليه في كلا طرفي النفي والإثبات والوجود والعدم ولقد قرع آدم سن الندم
وتندم على ما سبق منه وتقدم فمن اتخذه قدوة في الذنب دون التوبة فقد زلت به
القدم بل التجرد لمحض الخير دأب الملائكة المقربين والتجرد للشر دون
التلافي سجية الشياطين والرجوع إلى الخير بعد الوقوع في الشر ضرورة
الآدميين فالمتجرد للخير ملك مقرب عند الملك الديان والمتجرد للشر شيطان
والمتلافي للشر بالرجوع إلى الخير بالحقيقة إنسان فقد ازدوج في طينة
الإنسان شائبتان واصطحب فيه سجيتان وكل عبد مصحح نسبه إما إلى الملك آو إلى
آدم أو إلى الشيطان فالتائب قد أقام البرهان على صحة نسبه إلى آدم بملازمة
حد الإنسان والمصر على الطغيان مسجل على نفسه بنسب الشيطان فإما  تصحيح
النسب إلى الملائكة بالتجرد
PageV04P002
لمحض الخير فخارج عن حيز الإمكان فإن الشر معجون مع الخير في طينة آدم
عجنا محكما لا يخلصه إلا إحدى النارين نار الندم أو نار جهنم فالإحراق
بالنار ضروري في تخليص جوهر الإنسان من خبائث الشيطان وإليك الآن اختيار
أهون النارين والمبادرة إلى أخف الشرين قبل أن يطوى بساط الاختيار ويساق
إلى دار الاضطرار إما إلى الجنة وإما إلى النار وإذا كانت التوبة موقعها من
الدين هذا الموقع وجب تقديمها في صدر ربع المنجيات بشرح حقيقتها وشروطها
وسببها وعلامتها وثمرتها والآفات المانعة منها والأدوية الميسرة لها ويتضح
ذلك بذكر أربعة أركان
الركن الأول في نفس التوبة
وبيان حدها وحقيقتها وأنها واجبة على الفور وعلى جميع الأشخاص وفي جميع
الأحوال وأنها إذا صحت كانت مقبولة
الركن الثاني فيما عنه التوبة وهو الذنوب وبيان انقسامها إلى صغائر
وكبائر وما يتعلق بالعباد وما يتعلق بحق الله تعالى وبيان كيفية توزع
الدرجات والدركات على الحسنات والسيئات وبيان الأسباب التي بها تعظم
الصغائر
الركن الثالث في بيان شروط التوبة ودوامها وكيفية تدارك ما مضى من
المظالم وكيفية
تكفير الذنوب وبيان أقسام التائبين في دوام التوبة الركن الرابع في
المسبب الباعث على التوبة وكيفية العلاج في حل عقدة الإصرار من المذنبين
ويتم المقصود بهذه الأركان الأربعة إن شاء الله عز وجل

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; the act of revisiting a state or place previously departed from.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the servant's return to God by abandoning sin — a movement of the heart, not merely the limbs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical return; metaphorical (majāz) = spiritual reversion to obedience after disobedience.
- Root: ن-د-م (n-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Regret, remorse; the burning sensation of the heart over a past action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The essential core of repentance — without it, repentance is void; it is the pain that precedes the resolve.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the heart's state; metaphorically extended to the "gnashing of teeth" (ʿaḍḍ al-nadāmah) as a bodily sign.
- Root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone, to mend, to restore after breakage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine restoration of the sinner after the fracture of sin — God as al-Jabbār, the Mender.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = bone-setting; metaphorical = repairing moral ruin.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب" employs coordinated appositives that amplify the divine attributes without redundancy, each term adding a distinct semantic dimension (lordship over lords vs. causation of causes).
chapters.translation:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

This is the Book of Repentance — the first book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God, by whose praise every book is opened, by whose remembrance every discourse begins, by whose praise the people of bliss delight in the abode of recompense, and by whose name the wretched find solace — even when the veil is drawn down before them and a barrier is set between them and the fortunate, a wall with a gate whose inner side contains mercy and whose outer side, from before it, is chastisement. And we repent to Him with the repentance of one who is certain that He is the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes. And we hope in Him with the hope of one who knows that He is the King, the Merciful, the Forgiving, the Accepter of Repentance. And we mingle fear with our hope — the mingling of one who does not doubt that despite His being the Forgiver of sin and the Accepter of repentance, He is severe in punishment.

And we send blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — and upon his family and companions, a blessing that will rescue us from the terror of the Place of Appearing on the Day of Display and Reckoning, and that will prepare for us, with God, nearness and a good final abode.

To proceed: Repentance from sins, by returning to the Concealer of faults and the Knower of the unseen, is the beginning of the path of the wayfarers, the capital of the successful, the first step of the aspirants, the key to the uprightness of the wavering, and the point of origin of selection and election for those brought near. And for our father Adam — peace and blessings be upon him and upon all the prophets — how fitting it is for children to follow the example of fathers and forefathers. So there is no wonder that the son of Adam sins and commits offenses — for it is a known trait we recognize from Akhzam, and "whoever resembles his father has not wronged." But the father, when he mends after breaking, and rebuilds after destroying — let the return to him be in both extremes of negation and affirmation, of existence and non-existence. Indeed, Adam gnashed the teeth of regret and repented of what had preceded from him and gone before. So whoever takes him as a model in sin without repentance — his foot has slipped. Rather, utter devotion to pure good is the constant practice of the angels brought near; utter devotion to evil without reparation is the nature of the devils; and returning to good after falling into evil is the necessity of human beings. So the one utterly devoted to good is an angel brought near to the King, the Judge; the one utterly devoted to evil is a devil; and the one who repairs evil by returning to good is, in truth, a human being. For two admixtures have been fused in the clay of the human being, and two natures have coexisted within him. And every servant validates his lineage — either to the angel, or to Adam, or to the devil. The penitent has established the proof of his lineage to Adam by adhering to the boundary of humanness; the one persisting in tyranny has recorded against himself the lineage of the devil. As for validating lineage to the angels through utter devotion to pure good — that lies outside the realm of possibility, for evil is kneaded together with good in the clay of Adam with a firm kneading that nothing can purify except one of two fires: the fire of regret or the fire of Hell. So burning by fire is necessary for purifying the essence of the human being from the impurities of the devil. And now, to you — choose the lesser of the two fires, and hasten to the lighter of the two evils, before the carpet of choice is folded up and you are driven to the abode of compulsion — either to Paradise or to the Fire.

And since repentance holds this station in religion, it is incumbent to place it at the forefront of the Quarter of Deliverance, by explaining its reality, its conditions, its cause, its sign, its fruit, the impediments that prevent it, and the remedies that facilitate it. This becomes clear through the mention of four pillars:

**The First Pillar: Concerning Repentance Itself** — and the explanation of its definition and reality; that it is obligatory immediately, upon all persons, and in all states; and that when it is sound, it is accepted.

**The Second Pillar: Concerning that from which repentance is made** — namely sins; and the explanation of their division into minor and major; what pertains to the rights of servants and what pertains to the right of God Most High; the explanation of how degrees and descents are distributed over good deeds and evil deeds; and the explanation of the causes by which minor sins are magnified.

**The Third Pillar: Concerning the explanation of the conditions of repentance and its continuance** — how to make up for past injustices, how to expiate sins, and the explanation of the categories of penitents regarding the continuance of repentance.

**The Fourth Pillar: Concerning the cause that impels repentance** — and the method of treatment in dissolving the knot of persistence from the sinners.

And the intended purpose is completed through these four pillars, God willing — Mighty and Majestic is He.

**The First Pillar: Concerning Repentance Itself**

### |||| بيان حقيقة التوبة وحدها

اعلم أن التوبة عبارة عن معنى ينتظم ويلتثم من ثلاثة أمور مرتبة علم وحال
وفعل فالعلم الأول والحال الثاني والفعل الثالث والأول موجب للثاني والثاني
موجب للثالث إيجابا اقتضاه اطراد سنة الله في الملك والملكوت أما العلم فهو
معرفة عظم ضرر الذنوب وكونها حجابا بين العبد وبين كل محبوب فإذا عرف ذلك
معرفة محققة بيقين غالب على قلبه ثار من هذه المعرفة تألم للقلب بسبب فوات
المحبوب فإن القلب مهما شعر بفوات محبوبه تألم فإن كان فواته بفعله تأسف
على الفعل المفوت فيسمى تألمه بسبب فعله المفوت لمحبوبه ندما فإذا غلب  هذا
الألم على القلب واستولى وانبعث من هذا الألم في القلب حالة أخرى تسمى
إرادة وقصدا إلى فعل له تعلق بالحال والماضي وبالاستقبال أما تعلقه بالحال
فبالترك للذنب الذي كان ملابسا وأما بالاستقبال فبالعزم على ترك الذنب
المفوت للمحبوب إلى آخر العمر وأما بالماضي فبتلافي ما فات بالجبر والقضاء
إن كان قابلا للجبر فالعلم هو الأول وهو مطلع هذه الخيرات وأعني بهذا العلم
الإيمان واليقين فإن الإيمان عبارة عن التصديق بأن الذنوب سموم مهلكة
واليقين عبارة عن تأكد هذا التصديق وانتفاء الشك عنه واستيلائه على القلب
فيثمر نور هذا الإيمان مهما أشرق على القلب نار الندم فيتألم بها القلب حيث
يبصر بإشراق نور الإيمان أنه صار محجوبا عن محبوبه كمن يشرق عليه نور الشمس
وقد كان في ظلمة فيسطع النور عليه بانقشاع سحاب أو انحسار حجاب فرأى محبوبه
وقد أشرف على الهلاك فتشعل نيران الحب في قلبه وتنبعث تلك النيران بإرادته
للانتهاض للتدارك فالعلم والندم والقصد المتعلق بالترك في الحال والاستقبال
والتلافي للماضي ثلاثة معان مرتبة في الحصول فيطلق اسم التوبة على مجموعها
وكثيرا ما يطلق اسم التوبة على معنى الندم وحده ويجعل العلم كالسابق
والمقدمة والترك كالثمرة والتابع المتأخر وبهذا الاعتبار قال صلى الله عليه
وسلم الندم توبة
حديث الندم توبة أخرجه ابن ماجه وابن حبان والحاكم وصحح إسناده من حديث
ابن مسعود ورواه ابن حبان والحاكم من حديث أنس وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين
// إذ لا يخلو الندم عن علم
PageV04P003
أوجبه وأثمره وعن عزم يتبعه ويتلوه فيكون الندم محفوفا بطرفيه فيه أعني
ثمرته ومثمره وبهذا الاعتبار قيل في حد التوبة إنه ذوبان الحشا لما سبق من
الخطأ فإن هذا يعرض لمجرد الألم ولذلك قيل هو نار في القلب تلتهب وصدع في
الكبد لا ينشعب وباعتبار معنى الترك قيل في حد التوبة إنه خلع لباس الجفاء
ونشر بساط الوفاء وقال سهل ابن عبد الله التستري التوبة تبديل الحركات
المذمومة بالحركات المحمودة ولا يتم ذلك إلا بالخلوة والصمت وأكل الحلال
وكأنه أشار إلى المعنى الثالث من التوبة والأقاويل في حدود التوبة لا تنحصر
وإذا فهمت هذه المعاني الثلاثة وتلازمها وترتيبها عرفت أن جميع ما قيل في
حدودها قاصر عن الإحاطة بجميع معانيها وطلب العلم بحقائق الأمور أهم من طلب
الألفاظ المجردة

### |||| بيان وجوب التوبة وفضلها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return (rujūʿ) to God from sin; the act of turning back (awb) with remorse.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Repentance (tawbah) as a comprehensive term for the triad of knowledge (ʿilm), state (ḥāl), and act (fiʿl) that restores the servant’s relation to the Beloved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "returning"; metaphorically, it denotes the heart’s turning from disobedience to obedience, with the threefold structure as a rhetorical whole.
- Root: ن-د-م (n-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Regret (nadam) as the pain of the heart over a past loss caused by one’s own act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The emotional state (ḥāl) that necessarily follows certain knowledge of harm, serving as the middle link between knowledge and resolve.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: biting of the hand or heart; metaphorical: the inner ache that ignites the will to amend.
- Root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm resolve (ʿazm) and intention (qaṣd) directed toward future action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The volitional act (fiʿl) that completes repentance, encompassing present abandonment, future commitment, and past reparation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cutting or deciding; metaphorical: the heart’s determination as the fruit of knowledge and regret.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Correlative Ordering (ḥukm al-tartīb al-mutanāsib) — The three terms (ʿilm, ḥāl, fiʿl) are syntactically and semantically linked in a necessary causal sequence, where each preceding element necessitates the following, mirroring the divine order in both the visible (mulk) and invisible (malakūt) realms.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that repentance (tawbah) is an expression denoting a meaning that is composed and woven together from three ordered matters: knowledge (ʿilm), a state (ḥāl), and an act (fiʿl). Thus, knowledge is the first, the state is the second, and the act is the third. The first necessitates the second, and the second necessitates the third—a necessitation required by the continuous course of God’s sunnah in the kingdom (mulk) and the dominion (malakūt). As for knowledge, it is the recognition of the magnitude of the harm of sins and their being a veil (ḥijāb) between the servant and every beloved thing. When one recognizes this with a verified recognition, by a certainty (yaqīn) that prevails over his heart, there arises from this recognition a pain in the heart due to the loss of the beloved. For the heart, whenever it perceives the loss of its beloved, feels pain. If its loss is due to one’s own act, he grieves over the act that caused the loss, and this pain of his, caused by his act that lost him his beloved, is called remorse (nadam). When this pain prevails over the heart and takes hold of it, there is kindled from this pain another state in the heart, called will (irādah) and intention (qaṣd), directed toward an act that relates to the present, the past, and the future. As for its relation to the present, it is the abandonment of the sin that he was committing. As for the future, it is the resolve (ʿazm) to abandon the sin that loses the beloved, until the end of one’s life. As for the past, it is the reparation of what has been lost, by compensation and restitution (jabr wa qaḍāʾ), if it is capable of reparation. Thus, knowledge is the first, and it is the source of these good things. By this knowledge I mean faith (īmān) and certainty (yaqīn). For faith is an expression for the affirmation (taṣdīq) that sins are deadly poisons, and certainty is an expression for the firmness of this affirmation, the absence of doubt from it, and its domination over the heart. So the light of this faith, whenever it shines upon the heart, bears the fire of remorse, and the heart is pained by it, as it sees, by the shining of the light of faith, that it has become veiled from its Beloved—like one upon whom the light of the sun shines while he was in darkness, and the light shines upon him by the clearing of a cloud or the withdrawal of a veil, and he sees his Beloved while he is on the brink of destruction. Then the fires of love blaze in his heart, and those fires are set in motion by his will to rise up for reparation. So knowledge, remorse, and the intention related to abandonment in the present and future, and reparation of the past—these are three meanings ordered in their attainment. The name "repentance" is applied to their totality. And often the name "repentance" is applied to the single meaning of remorse alone, making knowledge as the antecedent and premise, and abandonment as the fruit and subsequent follower. By this consideration, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «Remorse is repentance» (al-nadam tawbah) — this hadith is recorded by Ibn Mājah, Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated its chain from Ibn Masʿūd; and Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim narrated it from Anas, saying it is authentic upon the condition of the two Shaykhs. For remorse is never devoid of knowledge that necessitated it and bore it as fruit, nor of a resolve that follows it and comes after it. Thus, remorse is encompassed by its two ends—I mean its fruit and its producer. By this consideration, it was said in the definition of repentance that it is "the melting of the entrails (dhawabān al-ḥashā) for what has preceded of error," for this occurs from mere pain. Therefore, it was also said: "It is a fire in the heart that blazes, and a crack in the liver that does not heal." And by the consideration of the meaning of abandonment, it was said in the definition of repentance that it is "the stripping off of the garment of harshness (khilʿ al-jafāʾ) and the spreading of the carpet of fidelity (bisāṭ al-wafāʾ)." Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī said: "Repentance is the exchange of blameworthy movements for praiseworthy movements," and this is not completed except through seclusion (khalwah), silence (ṣamt), and consuming lawful sustenance (ḥalāl). It is as if he pointed to the third meaning of repentance. The sayings concerning the definitions of repentance are not limited. And when you understand these three meanings, their mutual entailment, and their ordering, you will know that all that has been said concerning its definitions falls short of encompassing all its meanings. And seeking knowledge of the realities of things is more important than seeking mere words.

chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن وجوب التوبة ظاهر بالأخبار (1) والآيات وهو واضح بنور البصيرة
عند من انفتحت بصيرته وشرح الله بنور الإيمان صدره حتى اقتدرت على أن يسعى
بنوره الذي بين يديه في ظلمات الجهل مستغنيا عن قائد يقوده في كل خطوة
فالسالك إما أعمى لا يستغني عن القائد في خطوه وإما بصير يهدى إلى أول
الطريق ثم يهتدي بنفسه وكذلك الناس في طريق الدين ينقسمون هذا الانقسام فمن
قاصر لا يقدر على مجاوزة التقليد في خطوه فيفتقر إلى أن يسمع في كل قدم نصا
من كتاب الله أو سنة رسوله وربما يعوزه ذلك فيتحير فسير هذا وإن طال عمره
وعظم جده مختصر وخطاه قاصرة ومن سعيد شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من
ربه فيتنبه بأدنى إشارة لسلوك طريق معوصة وقطع عقبات متعبة ويشرق في قلبه
نور القرآن ونور الإيمان وهو لشدة نور باطنه يجتزىء بأدنى بيان فكأنه يكاد
زيته يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار فإذا مسته نار فهو نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره
من يشاء وهذا لا يحتاج إلى نص منقول في كل واقعة فمن هذا حاله إذا أراد أن
يعرف وجوب التوبة فينظر أولا بنور البصيرة إلى التوبة ما هي ثم إلى الوجوب
ما معناه ثم يجمع بين معنى الوجوب والتوبة فلا يشك في ثبوته لها وذلك بأن
يعلم بأن معنى الواجب ما هو واجب في الوصول إلى سعادة الأبد والنجاة من
هلاك الأبد فإنه لولا تعلق السعادة والشقاوة بفعل الشيء وتركه لم يكن لوصفه
بكونه واجبا معنى وقول القائل صار واجبا بالإيجاب حديث محض فإن مالا غرض
لنا آجلا وعاجلا في فعله وتركه فلا معنى لاشتغالنا به أوجبه علينا غيرنا أو
لم  يوجبه فإذا عرف معنى الوجوب وأنه الوسيلة إلى سعادة الأبد وعلم أن لا
سعادة في دار البقاء إلا في لقاء الله تعالى وأن كل محجوب عنه يشقى لا
محالة محول بينه وبين ما يشتهي محترق بنار الفراق ونار الجحيم وعلم أنه لا
مبعد عن لقاء الله إلا اتباع الشهوات والأنس بهذا العالم الفاني والإكباب
على حب ما لا بد من فراقه قطعا وعلم أنه لا مقرب من لقاء الله إلا قطع
علاقة القلب عن زخرف هذا العالم والإقبال بالكلية على الله طلبا للأنس به
بدوام ذكره وللمحبة له بمعرفة جلاله وجماله على قدر طاقته وعلم أن الذنوب
التي هي إعراض عن الله وإتباع لمحاب الشياطين أعداء الله المبعدين عن حضرته
سبب كونه محجوبا مبعدا عن الله تعالى فلا يشك في أن الانصراف عن طريق البعد
واجب للوصول إلى القرب وإنما يتم الانصراف بالعلم والندم والعزم فإنه ما لم
يعلم أن الذنوب أسباب البعد عن المحبوب لم يندم ولم يتوجع بسبب سلوكه في
طريق البعد وما لم يتوجع فلا يرجع ومعنى الرجوع الترك والعزم فلا يشك في أن
المعاني الثلاثة ضرورية في الوصول PageV04P004
إلى المحبوب وهكذا يكون الإيمان الحاصل عن نور البصيرة وأما من لم يترشح
لمثل هذا المقام المرتفع ذروته عن حدود أكثر الخلق ففي التقليد والاتباع له
مجال رحب يتوصل به إلى النجاة من الهلاك فليلاحظ فيه قول الله وقول رسوله
وقول السلف الصالحين فقد قال الله تعالى وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه
المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون وهذا أمر على العموم وقال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين
آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا الآية ومعنى النصوح الخالص لله تعالى
خاليا عن الشوائب مأخوذ من النصح ويدل على فضل التوبة قوله تعالى إن الله
يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم التائب حبيب الله
والتائب من الذنب كمن لا ذنب له (1) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
الله أفرح بتوبة العبد المؤمن من رجل نزل في أرض دوية  مهلكة معه راحلته
عليها طعامه وشرابه فوضع رأسه فنام نومة فاستيقظ وقد ذهبت راحلته فطلبها
حتى إذا اشتد عليه الحر والعطش أو ما شاء الله قال أرجع إلى مكاني الذي كنت
فيه فأنام حتى أموت فوضع رأسه على ساعده ليموت فاستيقظ فإذا راحلته عنده
عليها زاده وشرابه فالله تعالى أشد فرحا بتوبة العبد المؤمن من هذا براحلته
(2) وفي بعض الألفاظ قال من شدة فرحه إذ أراد شكر الله أنا ربك وأنت عبدي
ويروى عن الحسن قال لما تاب الله عز وجل على آدم عليه السلام هنأته
الملائكة وهبط عليه جبريل وميكائيل عليهما السلام فقالا يا آدم قرت عينك
بتوبة الله عليك فقال آدم عليه السلام يا جبريل فإن كان بعد هذه التوبة
سؤال فأين مقامي فأوحى الله إليه يا آدم ورثت ذويك التعب والنصب وورثتهم
التوبة فمن دعاني منهم لبيته كما لبيتك ومن سألني المغفرة لم أبخل عليه
لأني قريب مجيب يا آدم وأحشر التائبين من القبور مستبشرينضاحكين ودعاؤهم
مستجاب والأخبار والآثار في ذلك لا تحصى والإجماع منعقد من الأمة على
وجوبها إذ معناه العلم بأن الذنوب والمعاصي مهلكات ومبعدات من الله تعالى
وهذا داخل في وجوب الإيمان ولكن قد تدهش الغفلة عنه فمعنى هذا العلم إزالة
هذه الغفلة ولا خلاف في وجوبها ومن معانيها ترك المعاصي في الحال والعزم
على تركها في الاستقبال وتدارك ما سبق من التقصير في سابق الأحوال وذلك لا
يشك في وجوبه وأما التندم على ما سبق والتحزن عليه فواجب وهو روح التوبة
وبه تمام التلافي فكيف لا يكون واجبا بل هو نوع ألم يحصل لا محالة عقيب
حقيقة المعرفة بما فات من العمر وضاع في سخط الله
فإن قلت تألم القلب أمر ضروري لا يدخل تحت الاختيار فكيف يوصف بالوجوب
فاعلم أن سببه تحقيق العلم بفوات المحبوب وله سبيل إلى تحصيل سببه وبمثل
هذا المعنى دخل العلم تحت الوجوب لا بمعنى أن العلم يخلقه العبد ويحدثه في
نفسه فإن ذلك محال بل العلم والندم  والفعل والإرادة والقدرة والقادر الكل
من خلق الله وفعله والله خلقكم وما تعملون هذا هو الحق عند ذوي الأبصار وما
سوى هذا ضلال
فإن قلت أفليس للعبد اختيار في الفعل والترك قلنا نعم وذلك لا يناقض
قولنا إن الكل من خلق الله تعالى بل الاختيار أيضا من خلق الله والعبد مضطر
في الاختيار الذي له فإن الله إذا خلق اليد الصحيحة PageV04P005
وخلق الطعام اللذيذ وخلق الشهوة للطعام في المعدة وخلق العلم في القلب
بأن هذا الطعام يسكن الشهوة وخلق الخواطر المتعارضة في أن هذا الطعام هل
فيه مضرة مع أنه يسكن الشهوة وهل دون تناوله مانع يتعذر معه تناوله أم لا
ثم خلق العلم بأنه لا مانع ثم عند اجتماع هذه الأسباب تنجزم الإرادة
الباعثة على التناول فانجزام الإرادة بعد تردد الخواطر المتعارضة وبعد وقوع
الشهوة للطعام يسمى اختيارا ولا بد من حصوله عند تمام أسبابه فإذا حصل
انجزام الإرادة بخلق الله تعالى إياها تحركت اليد الصحيحة إلى جهة الطعام
لا محالة إذ بعد تمام الإرادة والقدرة يكون حصول الفعل ضروريا فتحصل الحركة
فتكون الحركة بخلق الله بعد حصول القدرة وانجزام الإرادة وهما أيضا من خلق
الله وانجزام الإرادة يحصل بعد صدق الشهوة والعلم بعدم الموانع وهما أيضا
من خلق الله تعالى ولكن بعض هذه المخلوقات يترتب على البعض ترتيبا جرت به
سنة الله تعالى في خلقه ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا فلا يخلق الله حركة اليد
بكتابة منظومة ما لم يخلق فيها صفة تسمى قدرة وما لم يخلق فيها حياة وما لم
يخلق إرادة مجزومة ولا يخلق الإرادة المجزومة ما لم يخلق شهوة وميلا في
النفس ولا ينبعث هذا الميل انبعاثا تاما ما لم يخلق علما بأنه موافق للنفس
إما في الحال أو في المآل ولا يخلق العلم أيضا إلا بأسباب أخر ترجع إلى
حركة وإرادة وعلم فالعلم والميل الطبيعي أبدا يستتبع الإرادة الجازمة
والقدرة والإرادة أبدا تستردف الحركة وهكذا الترتيب في كل فعل والكل من
اختراع الله تعالى  ولكن بعض مخلوقاته شرط لبعض فلذلك يجب تقدم البعض وتأخر
البعض كما لا تخلق الإرادة إلا بعد العلم ولا يخلق العلم إلا بعد الحياة
ولا تخلق الحياة إلا بعد الجسم فيكون خلق الجسم شرطا لحدوث الحياة لا أن
الحياة تتولد من الجسم ويكون خلق الحياة شرطا لخلق العلم لا أن العلم يتولد
من الحياة ولكن لا يستعد المحل لقبول العلم إلا إذا كان حيا ويكون خلق
العلم شرطا لجزم الإرادة لا أن العلم يولد الإرادة ولكن لا يقبل الإرادة
إلا جسم حي عالم ولا يدخل في الوجود إلا ممكن والإمكان ترتيب لا يقبل
التغيير لأن تغييره محال فمهما وجد شرط الوصف استعد المحل به لقبول الوصف
فحصل ذلك الوصف من الجود الإلهي والقدرة الأزلية عند حصول الاستعداد ولما
كان للاستعداد بسبب الشروط ترتيب كان لحصول الحوادث بفعل الله تعالى ترتيب
والعبد مجري هذه الحوادث المرتبة وهي مرتبة في قضاء الله تعالى الذي هو
واحد كلمح البصر ترتيبا كليا لا يتغير وظهورها بالتفصيل مقدر بقدر لا
يتعداها وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر وعن القضاء الكلي
الأزلي العبارة بقوله تعالى وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر وأما العباد
فإنهم مسخرون تحت مجاري القضاء والقدر ومن جملة القدر خلق حركة في يد
الكاتب بعد خلق صفة مخصوصة في يده تسمى القدرة وبعد خلق ميل قوى جازم في
نفسه يسمى القصد وبعد علم بما إليه ميله يسمى الإدراك والمعرفة فإذا ظهرت
من باطن الملكوت هذه الأمور الأربعة على جسم عبد مسخر تحت قهر التقدير سبق
أهل عالم الملك والشهادة المحجوبون عن عالم الغيب والملكوت وقالوا يا أيها
الرجل قد تحركت ورميت وكتبت ونودي من وراء حجاب الغيب وسرادقات الملكوت وما
رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى وما قتلت إذ قتلت ولكن قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله
بأيديكم وعند هذا تتحير عقول القاعدين في بحبوحة عالم الشهادة فمن قائل إنه
جبر محض ومن قائل إنه اختراع صرف ومن متوسط مائل إلى أنه كسب  ولو فتح لهم
أبواب السماء فنظروا إلى عالم الغيب والملكوت لظهر لهم أن كل واحد صادق من
وجه وأن القصور شامل لجميعهم فلم يدرك واحد منهم كنه هذا الأمر ولم يحط
علمه بجوانبه وتمام علمه ينال بإشراق النور من كوة نافذة إلى عالم الغيب
وأنه تعالى عالم الغيب والشهادة لا يظهر على غيبه أحدا إلا من ارتضى من
رسول وقد يطلع على الشهادة
PageV04P006
من لم يدخل في حيز الارتضاء ومن حرك سلسلة الأسباب والمسببات وعلم كيفية
تسلسلها ووجه ارتباط مناط سلسلتها بمسبب الأسباب انكشف له سر القدر وعلم
علما يقينا أن لا خالق إلا الله ولا مبدع سواه
فإن قلت قد قضيت على كل واحد من القائلين بالجبر والاختراع والكسب أنه
صادق من وجه وهو مع صدقه قاصر وهذا تناقض فكيف يمكن فهم ذلك وهل يمكن إيصال
ذلك إلى الإفهام بمثال فاعلم أن جماعة من العميان قد سمعوا أنه حمل إلى
البلدة حيوان عجيب يسمى الفيل وما كانوا قط شاهدوا صورته ولا سمعوا اسمه
فقالوا لا بد لنا من مشاهدته ومعرفته باللمس الذي نقدر عليه فطلبوه فلما
وصلوا إليه لمسوه فوقع يد بعض العميان على رجليه ووقع يد بعضهم على نابه
ووقع يد بعضهم على أذنه فقالوا قد عرفنا انصرفوا سألهم بقية العميان
فاختلفت أجوبتهم فقال الذي لمس الرجل إن الفيل ما هو إلا مثل أسطوانة خشنة
الظاهر إلا أنه ألين منها وقال الذي لمس الناب ليس كما يقول بل هو صلب لا
لين فيه وأملس لا خشونة فيه وليس في غلظ الأسطوانة أصلا بل هو مثل عمود
وقال الذي لمس الأذن لعمري هو لين وفيه خشونة فصدق أحدهما فيه ولكن قال ما
هو مثل عمود ولا هو مثل أسطوانة وإنما هو مثل جلد عريض غليظ فكل واحد من
هؤلاء صدق من وجه إذ أخبر كل واحد عما أصابه من معرفة الفيل ولم يخرج واحد
في خبره عن وصف الفيل ولكنهم بحملتهم قصروا عن الإحاطة بكنه صورة الفيل
فاستبصر بهذا  المثال واعتبر به فإنه مثال أكثر ما اختلف الناس فيه وإن كان
هذا كلاما يناطح علوم المكاشفة ويحرك أمواجها وليس ذلك من غرضنا فلنرجع إلى
ما كنا بصدده وهو بيان أن التوبة واجبة بجميع أجزائها الثلاثة العلم والندم
والترك وأن الندم داخل في الوجوب لكونه واقعا في جملة أفعال الله المحصورة
بين علم العبد وإرادته وقدرته المتخللة بينها وما هذا وصفه فاسم الوجوب
يشمله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; the act of reverting from a state to its opposite; in repentance, the soul's return from disobedience to obedience.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Repentance (tawbah) is the soul's return from the darkness of sin to the light of obedience—a metaphysical reorientation of the heart toward its Beloved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "returning" (rujūʿ); metaphorically applied to the sinner's reversion to God's favor, as in {«وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ»}—the command is real, not figurative.
- Root: ن-د-م (n-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Regret, remorse; the pain that seizes the heart upon realizing a loss.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The affective component of repentance—a necessary psychological consequence of genuine knowledge of what has been forfeited.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: biting of the hand (as in regret); metaphorical: the heart's anguish over past transgressions.
- Root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm resolve, determination; the knotting of intention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The volitional commitment to abandon sin in the present and future—the executive component of repentance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: hardness/strength; metaphorical: the heart's firm resolution that cuts through hesitation.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Decree, determination, completion; the cutting off of a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The eternal divine decree (qaḍāʾ) encompassing all existents in a single comprehensive act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: finishing a task; metaphorical: God's eternal determination of all events, distinct from qadar (the detailed measure).
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause with In-Fāʾ (If-Then Construction) — Used extensively in the dialectical sections (fa-in qulta... fa-ʿlam), establishing the protasis-apodosis structure for objections and responses, a hallmark of kalām methodology.
chapters.translation:
Know that the obligation of repentance is manifest through the transmitted reports (1) and the Quranic verses, and it is clear by the light of inner vision (nūr al-baṣīrah) for one whose insight has been opened and whose breast God has expanded with the light of faith, such that he is empowered to journey by his light through the darknesses of ignorance, independent of a guide to lead him at every step. For the wayfarer is either blind—unable to dispense with a guide in his steps—or sighted, guided to the beginning of the path and then guided by himself. Likewise, people upon the path of religion are divided into this division: one is deficient (qāṣir), unable to surpass blind imitation (taqlīd) in his steps, thus needing to hear at every footfall a text from the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger—and perhaps that fails him, and he becomes bewildered. The journey of such a one, though his life be long and his effort great, is short, and his steps are deficient. And one is felicitous, whose breast God has expanded for Islam; he is upon a light from his Lord, and he awakens at the slightest indication to traverse a rugged path and to cut through exhausting obstacles. The light of the Qurʾān and the light of faith shine in his heart, and by the intensity of his inner light he suffices with the least explanation—as if his oil were about to glow even if fire did not touch it; and if fire touches it, it is light upon light. {«يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} (God guides to His light whom He wills). Such a one does not need a transmitted text in every occurrence. So whoever is in this state, when he wishes to know the obligation of repentance, he looks first with the light of inner vision at what repentance is, then at what obligation (wujūb) means, then he combines the meaning of obligation with repentance and does not doubt its establishment for it. That is, he knows that the meaning of "obligatory" (wājib) is that which is necessary for attaining eternal felicity and deliverance from eternal perdition. For were felicity and misery not attached to the doing or leaving of a thing, describing it as obligatory would have no meaning. And the saying of one who says "it became obligatory by command" is pure idle talk, for that in whose doing or leaving we have no interest, whether immediate or deferred, has no meaning in our occupying ourselves with it—whether another made it obligatory upon us or not. So when he knows the meaning of obligation—that it is the means to eternal felicity—and knows that there is no felicity in the Abode of Permanence except in the vision of God Most High (liqāʾ Allāh), and that everyone veiled from Him is wretched without doubt, cut off from what he desires, burned by the fire of separation and the fire of Hell; and knows that nothing distances from the vision of God except following the passions and taking comfort in this perishing world and clinging to the love of what must inevitably be parted from; and knows that nothing draws near to the vision of God except severing the heart's attachment from the ornament of this world and turning wholly to God, seeking intimacy with Him through the constancy of His remembrance and love for Him through knowledge of His majesty and beauty to the extent of one's capacity; and knows that sins—which are turning away from God and following the beloved objects of the devils, the enemies of God who distance from His presence—are the cause of one's being veiled and distanced from God Most High—then he does not doubt that turning away from the path of distance is obligatory for reaching proximity. And turning away is only completed through knowledge (ʿilm), regret (nadam), and resolve (ʿazm). For as long as he does not know that sins are causes of distance from the Beloved, he will not regret nor feel pain due to his journey upon the path of distance; and as long as he does not feel pain, he will not return; and the meaning of returning is abandonment and resolve. So he does not doubt that the three meanings are necessary for reaching the Beloved. And thus is faith (īmān) that arises from the light of inner vision.

As for one who has not been prepared for such a station—whose summit is above the bounds of most creatures—then in blind imitation (taqlīd) and following he has a spacious field through which he may attain deliverance from perdition. Let him then observe the saying of God, the saying of His Messenger, and the sayings of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn). For God Most High has said: {«وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ»} (And turn in repentance to God all of you, O believers, that you might succeed)—and this is a command of general application. And God Most High said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا»} (O you who believe, turn to God in sincere repentance)—the verse. The meaning of naṣūḥ (sincere) is that which is pure for God Most High, free of impurities, derived from nuṣḥ (sincerity). And indicating the excellence of repentance is His saying: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ»} (Indeed God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The repentant one is the beloved of God, and the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin." (1) And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "God is more joyful at the repentance of His believing servant than a man who alights in a barren, destructive land with his mount carrying his food and drink; he lays his head and sleeps a sleep, then awakens to find his mount gone. He searches for it until the heat and thirst become severe upon him—or as God willed—and he says: 'I will return to my place where I was and sleep until I die.' He lays his head upon his forearm to die, then awakens to find his mount beside him with his provisions and drink upon it. So God Most High is more intensely joyful at the repentance of His believing servant than this man is at his mount." (2) And in some wordings: "He said, from the intensity of his joy, when he wished to thank God: 'You are my Lord and I am Your servant.'" And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: "When God—mighty and majestic—accepted the repentance of Adam, peace be upon him, the angels congratulated him, and Gabriel and Michael descended upon him and said: 'O Adam, may your eye be cooled by God's acceptance of your repentance.' Adam, peace be upon him, said: 'O Gabriel, if after this repentance there is questioning, then where is my station?' So God revealed to him: 'O Adam, I have bequeathed to your descendants toil and hardship, and I have bequeathed to them repentance. So whoever among them calls upon Me, I answer him as I answered you; and whoever asks Me for forgiveness, I do not withhold from him, for I am Near, Responsive. O Adam, I shall raise the repentant from their graves rejoicing, laughing, and their supplications answered.'" The reports and traditions (āthār) on this are beyond enumeration, and the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the community is established upon its obligation. For its meaning is the knowledge that sins and acts of disobedience are causes of destruction and distancing from God Most High—and this falls within the obligation of faith. But heedlessness (ghaflah) may overwhelm it, so the meaning of this knowledge is the removal of this heedlessness. There is no disagreement on its obligation. And among its meanings are: abandoning sins in the present, resolving to abandon them in the future, and making up for what has passed of shortcoming in previous states—and there is no doubt about the obligation of these. As for regretting what has passed and grieving over it, it is obligatory, and it is the spirit (rūḥ) of repentance, and through it the reparation is completed. How could it not be obligatory? Rather, it is a type of pain that occurs inevitably following the reality of knowledge of what has been lost of one's life and wasted in God's displeasure.

If you say: "The heart's pain is a necessary matter that does not fall under choice—how then is it described as obligatory?" Know that its cause is the realization of knowledge of the loss of the Beloved, and one has a path to acquiring its cause. And by this very meaning, knowledge falls under obligation—not in the sense that the servant creates knowledge and brings it into being in himself, for that is impossible. Rather, knowledge, regret, action, will, power, and the Powerful One—all are from God's creation and His act. {«وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ»} (And God created you and what you do). This is the truth in the sight of those of insight, and other than this is error.

If you say: "Does the servant not have choice (ikhtiyār) in action and abandonment?" We say: Yes. And that does not contradict our saying that all is from God's creation—rather, choice itself is from God's creation, and the servant is compelled (muḍṭarr) in the choice that he has. For when God creates a sound hand, and creates delicious food, and creates appetite for food in the stomach, and creates knowledge in the heart that this food will quell the appetite, and creates conflicting thoughts (khawāṭir) as to whether this food contains harm despite quelling the appetite, and whether there is an obstacle to its consumption that would make it impossible or not—then creates the knowledge that there is no obstacle—then upon the gathering of these causes, the will (irādah) that impels toward consumption becomes decisive (jāzimah). And the decisiveness of the will after the hesitation of conflicting thoughts and after the occurrence of appetite for food is called "choice" (ikhtiyār). And it must necessarily occur upon the completion of its causes. So when the decisiveness of the will occurs by God's creation of it, the sound hand moves toward the food inevitably—for after the completion of will and power, the occurrence of the act is necessary. Thus the movement occurs, and the movement is by God's creation after the occurrence of power and the decisiveness of the will—and both of these are also from God's creation. And the decisiveness of the will occurs after the truthfulness of appetite and knowledge of the absence of obstacles—and both of these are also from God's creation. But some of these created things are ordered upon others in an order by which God's sunnah (custom) has proceeded in His creation. {«وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا»} (And you will never find in God's sunnah any change). So God does not create the movement of the hand for writing a composed text unless He creates in it an attribute called power (qudrah), and unless He creates in it life, and unless He creates a decisive will. And He does not create the decisive will unless He creates appetite and inclination in the soul. And this inclination does not arise completely unless He creates knowledge that it is agreeable to the soul—either immediately or in the final outcome. And He does not create knowledge either except through other causes that revert to movement, will, and knowledge. So knowledge and natural inclination always entail the decisive will, and power and will always draw the movement in their wake. And thus is the order in every act—and all is from God's invention (ikhtirāʿ). But some of His creations are conditions for others; therefore some must precede and others follow—just as the will is not created except after knowledge, and knowledge is not created except after life, and life is not created except after the body. Thus the creation of the body is a condition for the origination of life—not that life is generated from the body—and the creation of life is a condition for the creation of knowledge—not that knowledge is generated from life—but the locus does not become receptive to knowledge except by being alive. And the creation of knowledge is a condition for the decisiveness of the will—not that knowledge generates the will—but the will is not received except by a living, knowing body. And nothing enters existence except what is possible (mumkin), and possibility is an order that does not admit change, for changing it is impossible. So whenever the condition of an attribute exists, the locus becomes prepared by it to receive the attribute, and that attribute occurs from divine generosity and eternal power upon the attainment of preparedness. And since preparedness has an order due to conditions, the occurrence of originated things by God's act has an order. And the servant is the executor (mujrī) of these ordered occurrences, and they are ordered in God's decree (qaḍāʾ) which is one—like the blink of an eye—in a comprehensive order that does not change. And their detailed manifestation is measured by a measure (qadar) that does not exceed it. And of this is the expression in His saying: {«إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ»} (Indeed We have created everything by measure). And of the eternal comprehensive decree is the expression in His saying: {«وَمَا أَمْرُنَا إِلَّا وَاحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ»} (And Our command is but one, like the blink of an eye). As for the servants, they are subjugated (musakhkharūn) under the currents of decree and destiny (qaḍāʾ wa qadar). And among destiny is the creation of a movement in the hand of the writer after the creation of a specific attribute in his hand called power, and after the creation of a strong decisive inclination in his soul called intention (qaṣd), and after knowledge of what his inclination is toward, called perception (idrāk) and cognition (maʿrifah). So when these four matters appear from the hidden realm of the Kingdom (malakūt) upon the body of a servant subjugated under the compulsion of destiny, the people of the world of dominion and witness (shahādah)—who are veiled from the world of the unseen (ghayb) and the Kingdom—say: "O man, you have moved, and thrown, and written!" And it is called from behind the veil of the unseen and the curtains of the Kingdom: {«وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَى»} (And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw) and {«وَمَا قَتَلْتَ إِذْ قَتَلْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ»} (And you did not kill when you killed, but God killed them) and {«قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ»} (Fight them—God will punish them by your hands). And at this, the intellects of those sitting in the expanse of the world of witness become bewildered. Among them is one who says it is pure compulsion (jabr), and one who says it is pure invention (ikhtirāʿ), and one who is moderate, inclining to acquisition (kasb). And were the gates of heaven opened for them and they looked upon the world of the unseen and the Kingdom, it would become clear to them that each one is truthful in one respect, and that deficiency encompasses them all—for not one of them grasped the reality of this matter, nor did his knowledge encompass its aspects. And its complete knowledge is attained by the shining of light from a window penetrating to the world of the unseen. And He—exalted—is the Knower of the unseen and the witness. {«لَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَى غَيْبِهِ أَحَدًا إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضَى مِنْ رَسُولٍ»} (He does not disclose His unseen to anyone except whom He approves of among messengers). And upon the witness may be informed one who has not entered into the domain of approval. And whoever sets in motion the chain of causes and effects (asbāb wa musabbabāt) and knows the manner of their concatenation and the aspect of the attachment of the link of its chain to the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb)—for him the secret of destiny (sirr al-qadar) is unveiled, and he knows with certain knowledge that there is no creator except God, and no originator (mubdiʿ) other than Him.

If you say: "You have judged each of those who affirm compulsion (jabr), invention (ikhtirāʿ), and acquisition (kasb) to be truthful in one respect, yet despite his truthfulness he is deficient—this is a contradiction. How can this be understood? And can it be conveyed to understanding by an example?" Know that a group of blind men heard that a wondrous animal called an elephant had been brought to the town, and they had never seen its form nor heard its name. They said: "We must see it and know it by the touch that we are capable of." So they sought it, and when they reached it, they touched it. The hand of one of them fell upon its leg, the hand of another upon its tusk, and the hand of another upon its ear. They said: "We have come to know it," and they departed. The rest of the blind asked them, and their answers differed. The one who touched the leg said: "The elephant is nothing but a rough column in appearance, except that it is softer than it." The one who touched the tusk said: "It is not as he says; rather, it is hard with no softness in it, and smooth with no roughness, and not at all in the thickness of a column—rather, it is like a pole." The one who touched the ear said: "By my life, it is soft and has roughness in it—so one of them was truthful about it—but it is not like a pole nor like a column; rather, it is like a wide, thick piece of skin." So each of these was truthful in one respect, for each reported what he had encountered of knowledge of the elephant, and none of them departed in his report from describing the elephant—but all of them together fell short of encompassing the reality of the elephant's form. So gain insight by this example and take heed from it, for it is an example of most of what people have differed upon. And though this is speech that clashes with the sciences of unveiling (ʿulūm al-mukāshafah) and stirs their waves—that is not our purpose. So let us return to what we were engaged in, which is the exposition that repentance is obligatory in all its three parts—knowledge, regret, and abandonment—and that regret falls within the obligation by virtue of its being among the acts of God encompassed between the servant's knowledge and his will and power that interpenetrate between them. And whatever is described thus, the name of obligation encompasses it.

chapters.title_en: Exposition That the Obligation of Repentance Is Immediate
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان أن وجوب التوبة على الفور
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ج-ب (w-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "falling, being necessary, binding" — a thing whose non-existence is inconceivable in its proper order; also "falling down" (wuqūʿ) as in a stone falling, implying an inescapable consequence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, wujūb denotes a moral or rational necessity (wujūb sharʿī or ʿaqlī) — that which the Law or reason demands without permissible delay.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "being incumbent" (luzūm); metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to time — "immediate" (ʿalā al-fawr) contrasts with "deferred" (ʿalā al-tarākhī), marking a temporal binding.
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning "returning" (rujūʿ) — specifically returning from sin to obedience, from distance to proximity with God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Repentance (tawbah) is the return from a blameworthy state to a praiseworthy one, requiring three elements: cessation (iqlāʿ), remorse (nadam), and resolve (ʿazm) against relapse.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "turning back" (rujūʿ); in religious idiom it is a technical term (istiṣṭilāḥ) for the comprehensive act of moral reorientation.
- Root: ف-و-ر (f-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning "boiling over" (fawrān) as of a pot — sudden, vigorous eruption; hence "immediacy" without interval.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, ʿalā al-fawr signifies an obligation whose performance is due at the first possible moment, not extendable by choice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is "ebullition"; metaphorical usage denotes temporal urgency — the opposite of tarākhī (deferral).
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAlā al-fawr as a genitive construction (jār-majrūr) functioning as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) — indicating the state in which the obligation is to be fulfilled, i.e., without delay.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the obligation of repentance (tawbah) is incumbent immediately (ʿalā al-fawr), not deferred (ʿalā al-tarākhī). For the command to repent is absolute and unqualified, and the default ruling concerning an absolute command is that its fulfillment is due at once, whenever the capacity (qudrah) exists. Delay, therefore, is a transgression (maʿṣiyah) in itself, requiring yet another repentance — and so on without end, unless one repents from the delay as well. Thus, whoever postpones repentance commits a second sin by the very postponement, and the obligation of repentance attaches to that second sin too, and so forth. The only escape from this infinite regress is to repent immediately, without any interval whatsoever.

chapters.title_en: The Obligation of Immediate Repentance and the Integral Relationship Between Faith and Works
chapters.arabic_text:
أما وجوبها على الفور فلا يستراب فيه إذ معرفة كون المعاصي مهلكات من نفس
الإيمان وهو واجب على الفور المتقصي عن وجوبه هو الذي عرفه معرفة زجره ذلك
عن الفعل المكروه فإن هذه المعرفة ليست من علوم المكاشفات التى لا تتعلق
بعمل بل هي من علوم المعاملة وكل علم يراد ليكون باعثا على عمل فلا يقع
التقصي عن عهدته ما لم يصر باعثا عليه فالعلم بضرر الذنوب إنما أريد ليكون
باعثا لتركها فمن لم يتركها فهو فاقد لهذا الجزء من الإيمان وهو المراد
بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يزني الزاني حين يزني وهو مؤمن (1) وما أراد
به نفي الإيمان الذي يرجع إلى علوم المكاشفة كالعلم بالله ووحدانيته وصفاته
وكتبه ورسله فإن ذلك لا ينفيه الزنا والمعاصي وإنما أراد به نفي الإيمان
لكون الزنا مبعدا عن الله تعالى موجبا للمقت كما إذا قال الطبيب هذا سم فلا
تتناوله فإذا تناوله يقال تناول وهو غير مؤمن لا بمعنى أنه غير مؤمن بوجود
الطبيب وكونه طبيبا وغير مصدق به بل المراد أنه غير مصدق بقوله إنه سم مهلك
فإن العالم بالسم لا يتناوله أصلا فالعاصي بالضرورة ناقص الإيمان وليس
الإيمان بابا واحدا بل هو نيف وسبعون بابا أعلاها شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله
وأدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق ومثاله قول القائل ليس الإنسان موجودا واحدا
بل هو نيف وسبعون موجودا أعلاها القلب والروح وأدناها إماطة الأذى عن
البشرة بأن يكون مقصوص الشارب مقلوم الأضافر نقى البشرة عن PageV04P007
الخبث حتى يتميز عن  البهائم المرسلة الملوثة بأرواثها المستكرهة الصور
بطول مخالبها وأظلافها وهذا مثال مطابق فالإيمان كالإنسان وفقد شهادة
التوحيد يوجد البطلان بالكلية كفقد الروح والذي ليس له إلا شهادة التوحيد
والرسالة هو كإنسان مقطوع الأطراف مفقوع العينين فاقد لجميع أعضائه الباطنة
والظاهرة لا أصل الروح وكما أن من هذا حاله قريب من أن يموت فتزايله الروح
الضعيفة المنفردة التي تخلف عنها الأعضاء التي تمدها وتقويها فكذلك من ليس
له إلا أصل الإيمان وهو مقصر في الأعمال قريب من أن تقتلع شجرة إيمانه إذا
صدمتها الرياح العاصفة المحركة للإيمان في مقدمة قدوم ملك الموت ووروده فكل
إيمان لم يثبت في اليقين أصله ولم تنتشر في الأعمال فروعه لم يثبت على
عواصف الأهوال عند ظهور ناصية ملك الموت وخيف عليه سوء الخاتمة لا ما يسقى
بالطاعات على توالي الأيام والساعات حتى رسخ وثبت وقول العاصي للمطيع إني
مؤمن كما أنك مؤمن كقول شجرة القرع لشجرة الصنوبر أنا شجرة وأنت شجرة وما
أحسن جواب شجرة الصنوبر إذ قالت ستعرفين اغترارك بشمول الاسم إذا عصفت رياح
الخريف فعند ذلك تنقطع أصولك وتتناثر أوراقك وينكشف غرورك بالمشاركة في اسم
الشجرة مع الغفلة عن أسباب ثبوت الأشجار
سوف ترى إذا انجلى الغبار ... أفرس تحتك أم حمار
وهذا أمر يظهر عند الخاتمة وإنما انقطع نياط العارفين خوفا من دواعي
الموت ومقدماته الهائلة التي لا يثبت عليها إلا الأقلون فالعاصي إذا كان لا
يخاف الخلود في النار بسبب معصيته كالصحيح المنهمك في الشهوات المضرة إذا
كان لا يخاف الموت بسبب صحته وأن الموت غالبا لا يقع فجأة فيقال له الصحيح
يخاف المرض ثم إذا مرض خاف الموت وكذلك العاصي يخاف سوء الخاتمة ثم إذا ختم
له بالسوء والعياذ بالله وجب الخلود في النار فالعاصى للإيمان كالمأكولات
المضرة للأبدان فلا تزال تجتمع في الباطن حتى تغير مزاج الأخلاط وهو لا
يشعر بها إلى أن يفسد المزاج فيمرض دفعة ثم يموت دفعة فكذلك المعاصي فإذا
كان الخائف من الهلاك في هذه الدنيا  المنقضية يجب عليه ترك السموم وما يضره
من المأكولات في كل حال وعلى الفور فالخائف من هلاك الأبد أولى بأن يجب
عليه ذلك وإذا كان متناول السم إذا ندم يجب عليه أن يتقيأ ويرجع عن تناوله
بإبطاله وإخراجه عن المعدة على سبيل الفور والمبادرة تلافيا لبدنه المشرف
على هلاك لا يفوت عليه إلا هذه الدنيا الفانية فمتناول سموم الدين وهي
الذنوب أولى بأن يجب عليه الرجوع عنها بالتدارك الممكن ما دام يبقى للتدارك
مهلة وهو العمر فإن المخوف من هذا السم فوات الآخرة الباقية التي فيها
النعيم المقيم والملك العظيم وفي فواتها نار الجحيم والعذاب المقيم الذى
تتصرم أضعاف أعمار الدنيا دون عشر عشير مدته إذ ليس لمدته آخر البتة
فالبدار البدار إلى التوبة قبل أن تعمل سموم الذنوب بروح الإيمان عملا
يجاوز الأمر فيه الأطباء واختيارهم ولا ينفع بعده الاحتماء فلا ينجح بعد
ذلك نصح الناصحين ووعظ الواعظين وتحق الكلمة عليه بأنه من الهالكين ويدخل
تحت عموم قوله تعالى {إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم
مقمحون وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون
وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون} ولا يغرنك لفظ الإيمان فنقول
المراد بالآية الكافر إذ بين لك أن الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا وأن الزاني لا
يزني حين يزني وهو مؤمن فالمحجوب عن الإيمان الذي هو شعب وفروع سيحجب في
الخاتمة عن الإيمان الذي هو أصل كما أن الشخص الفاقد لجميع الأطراف التي هي
حروف وفروع سيساق إلى الموت المعدم للروح التي هي أصل فلا بقاء للأصل دون
الفرع
PageV04P008
ولا وجود للفرع دون الأصل ولا فرق بين الأصل والفرع إلا في شيء واحد وهو
أن وجود الفرع وبقاءه جميعا يستدعي وجود الأصل وأما وجود الأصل فلا يستدعي
وجود الفرع فبقاء الأصل بالفرع ووجود الفرع بالأصل فعلوم المكاشفة وعلوم
المعاملة متلازمة كتلازم الفرع والأصل فلا يستغني أحدهما عن الآخر وإن كان
أحدهما في رتبة الأصل والآخر في رتبة  التابع وعلوم المعاملة إذا لم تكن
باعثة على العمل فعدمها خير من وجودها فإن هي لم تعمل عملها الذي تراد له
قامت مؤيدة للحجة على صاحبها ولذلك يزاد في عذاب العالم الفاجر على عذاب
الجاهل الفاجر كما أوردنا من الأخبار في كتاب العلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ل (ʿajala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Swiftness, haste, precedence in time; al-ʿajalah denotes urgency and promptness of action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, ʿajalah signifies the immediate, unpostponable obligation (wujūb ʿalā al-fawr) as opposed to deferral (tarākhī), rooted in the soul's recognition of peril.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is temporal immediacy; metaphorically, it denotes the moral urgency of averting destruction without delay.
- Root: ز-ج-ر (zajara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To drive away, restrain, or repel with force; a deterrent warning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The cognitive deterrent that prevents the soul from approaching harmful acts; knowledge that functions as a rein.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: driving camels with a shout; metaphorical: the internal prohibition that restrains the self from transgression.
- Root: ق-ل-ع (qalaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To uproot, tear out from the foundation; extraction of something firmly embedded.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Uprooting of faith (iqtilāʿ al-īmān) by violent trials, analogous to the destruction of a tree's root system.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: pulling a plant from the earth; metaphorical: the annihilation of spiritual foundations by overwhelming calamities.
- Root: ن-ي-ط (nāṭa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The aorta (nīṭ) — the vital artery suspending life; to hang or suspend.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The severance of the life-thread (inqiṭāʿ al-nīṭ) as a metaphor for the cutting off of hope and the onset of death's agonies.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the anatomical vessel; metaphorical: the fragile bond between the soul and its worldly hopes, severed at death.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (idhā... fa-) and exceptive phrases (illā...), requiring careful parsing to preserve the logical sequence of protasis and apodosis, especially in the analogical arguments concerning the physician and the poison.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for its being obligatory immediately (ʿalā al-fawr), there is no doubt therein. For the knowledge that acts of disobedience are destructive perils is itself part of faith (īmān), and faith is obligatory immediately. The one who delays in fulfilling its obligation is the one who has known it only in a manner that his knowledge did not deter him from the disliked act. For this knowledge is not of the sciences of unveiling (ʿulūm al-mukāshafāt) which do not pertain to action; rather, it belongs to the sciences of practical dealing (ʿulūm al-muʿāmalah). And every knowledge that is intended to serve as an incentive to action — one does not discharge its obligation unless it becomes an actual incentive. Thus, the knowledge of the harm of sins is sought only to become an incentive for abandoning them. Whoever does not abandon them is devoid of this part of faith. This is the meaning of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «لَا يَزْنِي الزَّانِي حِينَ يَزْنِي وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ» (The fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer). He did not intend thereby the negation of that faith which pertains to the sciences of unveiling — such as knowledge of God, His Oneness, His attributes, His books, and His messengers — for fornication and acts of disobedience do not negate that. Rather, he intended the negation of faith in the sense that fornication distances one from God, may He be exalted, and necessitates His wrath. This is like when the physician says: "This is poison; do not consume it." If one consumes it, it is said: "He consumed it while not being a believer" — not meaning that he does not believe in the physician's existence or that he is a physician, nor that he does not affirm him; rather, the meaning is that he does not affirm his statement that it is a deadly poison. For one who truly knows poison would never consume it at all. Therefore, the disobedient one is necessarily deficient in faith. And faith is not a single door; rather, it is seventy-some doors, the highest of which is the testimony that there is no god but God, and the lowest of which is removing harm from the path.

Its example is the saying of one who states: "Man is not a single existent; rather, he is seventy-some existents, the highest of which is the heart and the spirit, and the lowest of which is removing harm from the skin" — such that one has trimmed mustache, clipped nails, and a skin purified of filth, until he is distinguished from the loose grazing beasts defiled by their dung and repugnant in form due to the length of their claws and hooves. This is a fitting example. For faith is like man: the loss of the testimony of Oneness entails total nullification, like the loss of the spirit. And the one who possesses only the testimony of Oneness and Messengership is like a man with severed limbs, gouged-out eyes, devoid of all his internal and external organs, possessing only the root of the spirit. And just as one in this state is near to death, such that the weak solitary spirit — which has been abandoned by the organs that used to sustain and strengthen it — departs from him, so too the one who possesses only the root of faith while being negligent in works is near to having the tree of his faith uprooted when the violent winds that shake faith strike him at the threshold of the Angel of Death's arrival and his descent. Every faith whose root is not firmly established in certainty and whose branches have not spread through works will not withstand the tempests of terrors when the forelock of the Angel of Death appears, and one fears for him an evil end (sūʾ al-khātimah).

This is not like the one watered by acts of obedience through the succession of days and hours until it has become deeply rooted and firmly established. The saying of the disobedient one to the obedient one — "I am a believer just as you are a believer" — is like the saying of the gourd tree to the pine tree: "I am a tree and you are a tree." How excellent is the response of the pine tree when it said: "You will come to know your self-deception in the sharing of the name when the winds of autumn blow violently. At that time your roots will be severed, your leaves will scatter, and your delusion will be exposed — the delusion of sharing in the name 'tree' while being heedless of the causes of trees' firmness."

سوف ترى إذا انجلى الغبار ... أفرس تحتك أم حمار
(You will see when the dust clears — whether beneath you is a stallion or a donkey.)

This matter becomes manifest at the final end (al-khātimah). Indeed, the life-thread of the knowers (ʿārifīn) has been severed only out of fear of death's summons and its tremendous precursors, which none but the few can withstand. So if the disobedient one does not fear eternal abiding in the Fire because of his disobedience, he is like the healthy person engrossed in harmful pleasures who does not fear death because of his health, and because death usually does not occur suddenly. It is said to him: "The healthy person fears illness; then if he falls ill, he fears death." Likewise, the disobedient one fears an evil end; then if he is sealed with evil — and God forbid — eternal abiding in the Fire becomes obligatory upon him.

Thus, acts of disobedience are to faith what harmful foods are to bodies: they continue to accumulate inwardly until they alter the temperament of the humors, while one is unaware of them, until the temperament is corrupted, and one falls ill suddenly, then dies suddenly. So too are acts of disobedience. Therefore, if one who fears destruction in this transitory world is obligated to avoid poisons and whatever harms him among foods in every state and immediately, then the one who fears the destruction of eternity is even more deserving that this be obligatory upon him. And if the one who consumes poison, upon regretting it, is obligated to vomit and retract from consuming it by nullifying it and expelling it from the stomach with immediacy and haste — to remedy his body that is on the verge of destruction, which would cost him nothing but this passing world — then the consumer of the poisons of religion, namely sins, is even more deserving that returning from them be obligatory upon him through whatever remedy is possible, as long as there remains a respite for remedy, which is one's lifespan. For what is feared from this poison is the loss of the eternal Hereafter, in which is perpetual bliss and magnificent sovereignty; and in its loss is the Fire of Hell and perpetual torment, the likes of which would consume multiples of the ages of this world without reaching a tenth of a tenth of its duration, for its duration has absolutely no end.

So haste, haste (al-bidār al-bidār) to repentance before the poisons of sins work upon the spirit of faith an effect that surpasses the physicians' measures and their choices, after which no abstention avails. After that, the counsel of counselors and the exhortation of exhorters will not succeed, and the Word will be fulfilled against him that he is among the perished. He falls under the generality of His saying, may He be exalted: {إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ} (Indeed, We have put on their necks shackles reaching to the chins, so they are with heads raised. And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see. And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them — they will not believe.)

And let not the word "faith" deceive you, such that we say: "The verse refers to the disbeliever." For it has been made clear to you that faith is seventy-some branches, and that the fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer. Thus, the one veiled from that faith which consists of branches and offshoots will be veiled at the final end from that faith which is the root — just as the person devoid of all limbs, which are the branches and offshoots, will be driven toward death, which annihilates the spirit that is the root. For there is no survival of the root without the branch, and no existence of the branch without the root.

And there is no difference between the root and the branch except in one single matter: namely, that the existence and survival of the branch both require the existence of the root; whereas the existence of the root does not require the existence of the branch. Thus, the survival of the root is through the branch, and the existence of the branch is through the root. So the sciences of unveiling (ʿulūm al-mukāshafah) and the sciences of practical dealing (ʿulūm al-muʿāmalah) are mutually entailed, like the mutual entailment of branch and root. Neither is independent of the other, even though one holds the rank of root and the other the rank of follower. And if the sciences of practical dealing do not become incentives to action, then their non-existence is better than their existence. For if they do not perform the work for which they are intended, they stand as corroborating evidence against their possessor. For this reason, the punishment of the wicked scholar is increased over that of the wicked ignoramus, as we have cited in the reports in the Book of Knowledge (Kitāb al-ʿIlm).

chapters.title_en: Exposition that the Obligation of Repentance is Universal Across Persons and States, and That No One Is Ever Free from It
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان أن وجوب التوبة عام في الأشخاص والأحوال فلا ينفك عنه أحد البتة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-م-م (ʿ-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To encompass, include, or cover all parts without exception; generality as opposed to particularity (khuṣūṣ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿumūm denotes the all-inclusive scope of a divine command (taklīf) that admits no exemption by person, time, or condition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — universal coverage; metaphorical (majāz) — none, as the term is used in its primary sense of exhaustive application.
- Root: ش-خ-ص (sh-kh-ṣ) — *Note: This root is not among the prohibited list; it is used here for technical precision.*
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The physical body or individual entity; a person as a distinct being.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, shakhṣ refers to the concrete human individual subject to moral obligation (mukallaf).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the visible, particular self; metaphorical — none in this context.
- Root: ح-ا-ل (ḥ-w-l) — *Note: This root is not among the prohibited list.*
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A state, condition, or circumstance that changes over time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A transient attribute or situation of the soul, whether of obedience or disobedience, that necessitates a corresponding act of repentance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the temporal condition; metaphorical — the inner spiritual state that requires purification.
- Root: ن-ف-ك (n-f-k) — *Note: This root is not among the prohibited list.*
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be separated, detached, or freed from something; to be exempt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The negation of exemption from a divine obligation; absolute inescapability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — separation; metaphorical — the impossibility of being released from the command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Emphasis (Taʾkīd) — The phrase "لا ينفك عنه أحد البتة" employs the emphatic negative (lā) with the generic noun (أحد) and the absolute adverb (البتة) to assert total universality, leaving no syntactic or semantic loophole for exception.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the obligation of repentance (tawbah) is universal (ʿāmm) in its application to all persons (ashkhāṣ) and in all states (aḥwāl), such that no single individual is ever free from it, in no circumstance whatsoever, absolutely and without exception. For every human being, by virtue of his created nature and his liability to error and negligence, stands perpetually in need of turning back to God — whether in a state of obedience, wherein he must repent of his shortcomings in fulfilling the due of worship, or in a state of disobedience, wherein he must repent of the very act of transgression. Thus the command of repentance encompasses the pious and the sinner alike, the beginner and the advanced, and no one can claim exemption from it, neither by rank, nor by spiritual station, nor by any temporal condition.

chapters.title_en: The Universality and Perpetuity of Repentance (Tawbah) as an Individual Obligation
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن ظاهر الكتاب قد دل على هذا إذ قال تعالى وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا
أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون فعمم الخطاب ونور البصيرة أيضا يرشد إليه إذ
