He asked about the most learned person on earth and was directed to a monk. He came to him and said: 'I have killed ninety-nine souls; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'No.' So he killed him, completing a hundred. Then he asked about the most learned person on earth and was directed to a learned man. He said to him: 'I have killed a hundred souls; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'Yes. Who stands between you and repentance? Go to such-and-such a land, for there are people who worship God (mighty and majestic). Worship God with them, and do not return to your land, for it is an evil land.' He set out, and when he reached the halfway point, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. The angels of mercy said: 'He came repentant, turning his heart to God.' The angels of punishment said: 'He never did any good.' An angel came to them in the form of a human and they made him an arbiter between them. He said: 'Measure the distance between the two lands; whichever he is closer to, he belongs to it.' They measured and found him closer to the land he intended, so the angels of mercy took him." In another narration: "He was closer to the righteous village by a span, so he was made of its people." In another: "God revealed to this one to move away and to this one to draw near, and said: 'Measure between them.' They found him closer to this one by a span, and he was forgiven." By this you know that there is no deliverance except by the preponderance of the scale of good deeds, even by the weight of an atom. Thus, the penitent must multiply good deeds. This is the ruling of the resolve related to the past.

As for the resolve bound to the future: it is that he make with God a firm covenant and pledge a solemn oath that he will not return to those sins nor to their likes—like one who knows in his illness that fruit harms him, for example, and resolves with absolute determination not to consume fruit until his illness ends. This resolve is strengthened at the moment, even if it is conceivable that desire might overcome him in the next moment. But he is not a penitent unless his resolve is firm at the present moment. It is not conceivable that this be achieved for the penitent at the outset of his affair except through seclusion (ʿuzlah), silence (ṣamt), reducing food and sleep, and securing lawful sustenance. If he has inherited lawful wealth or has a craft by which he earns sufficiency, let him be content with it—for the head of sins is consuming the unlawful. How can one be a penitent while persisting in it? Nor is it sufficient to be content with the lawful and abandon ambiguities (shubuhāt) for one who cannot abandon desires in foods and garments. Some have said: "Whoever is truthful in abandoning a desire and strives against his soul for God seven times will not be afflicted by it." Another said: "Whoever repents from a sin and remains steadfast for seven years will never return to it."

Among the important matters for the penitent, if he is not learned, is to learn what is obligatory upon him in the future and what is forbidden to him, so that he can maintain steadfastness. If he does not choose seclusion, absolute steadfastness is not achieved for him—unless he repents from some sins specifically, like one who repents from drinking, fornication, and usurpation, for example. But this is not an absolute repentance.

Some people have said that such repentance is not sound, while others said it is sound. The word "soundness" (ṣiḥḥah) in this context is ambiguous. We say to the one who says it is not sound: if you mean that abandoning some sins is utterly useless, as if non-existence were equal to existence, then how great is your error! For we know that the multiplicity of sins is a cause of the multiplicity of punishment, and their paucity is a cause of its paucity. And we say to the one who says it is sound: if you mean that repentance from some sins necessitates an acceptance that leads to deliverance or triumph, this too is an error—for deliverance and triumph come only by abandoning all. This is the ruling of the outward, and we do not speak of the hidden secrets of God's pardon.

If the one who holds it is not sound says: "I meant that repentance is an expression for regret, and one only regrets theft, for example, because it is a sin, not because it is theft. It is impossible to regret it without regretting fornication, if his pain is due to sin—for the cause encompasses both. One who grieves over the killing of his son by a sword also grieves over his killing by a knife, because his grief is over the loss of his beloved, whether by sword or knife. Likewise, the servant's grief is over the loss of his Beloved, which occurs through sin, whether he sinned by theft or fornication. So how can he grieve over some and not others? Regret is a state necessitated by knowledge that sin, qua sin, causes the loss of the Beloved. It is inconceivable that it be for some sins and not others. If this were permissible, it would be permissible to repent from drinking wine from one jar but not another. Since that is impossible—because the sin in both jars is one, the jars being mere containers—likewise, the specific sins are instruments of sin, and sin, insofar as it is opposition to the command, is one. Thus, the meaning of 'not sound' is that God has promised the penitent a station, and that station is attained only through regret, and regret over some similar things is inconceivable. It is like ownership (milk) conditioned upon offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl): when offer and acceptance are not completed, we say the contract is not sound—i.e., its fruit, which is ownership, does not follow. The verification of this is that the fruit of mere abandonment is the cessation of punishment for what was abandoned, while the fruit of regret is the expiation of what preceded. Abandoning theft does not expiate theft; rather, regret over it does. And regret is inconceivable except because it is a sin, which encompasses all sins."

This is intelligible and sound speech that compels the fair-minded to a detailed exposition by which the veil is lifted. So we say: repentance from some sins is either from major sins (kabāʾir) without minor ones, or from minor sins without major ones, or from one major sin without another.

As for repentance from major sins without minor ones, this is possible, for one knows that major sins are greater before God and more conducive to His wrath and abhorrence, while minor sins are closer to the possibility of pardon reaching them. Thus, it is not impossible to repent from the greater and regret it—like one who offends against a king's family and his honor, and also offends against his beast, fearing the offense against the family while deeming the offense against the beast trivial. Regret is proportionate to one's magnification of the sin and belief that it distances one from God. This is possible in the Sacred Law, for many penitents have existed in past ages, and none of them was infallible. Repentance does not require infallibility. A physician may warn a patient against honey with severe warning and against sugar with a lighter warning, in a manner suggesting that sugar's harm might not appear at all. The patient then repents by his word from honey but not from sugar. This is not impossible in existence—and if he eats both by his desire, he regrets eating the honey but not the sugar.

Second: that he repents from some major sins but not others. This too is possible, due to his belief that some major sins are more severe and weightier before God—like one who repents from killing, plundering, injustice, and claims of creatures, knowing that the register of creatures is not left aside, while what is between him and God is more readily reached by pardon. This is also possible, just as there is variation between major and minor sins—for major sins also vary in themselves and in the belief of their perpetrator. Thus, one may repent from some major sins that do not involve creatures, as one repents from drinking wine but not from fornication, for example—when it becomes clear to him that wine is the key to evils, and that when his intellect departs he commits all sins without knowing. Proportionate to the preponderance of drinking wine in his estimation, a fear arises in him that necessitates abandonment in the future and regret over the past.

Third: that he repents from a minor sin or minor sins while persisting in a major sin he knows to be major—like one who repents from backbiting, or from looking at what is unlawful, or the like, while persisting in drinking wine. This too is possible. The manner of its possibility is that there is no believer who is not fearful of his sins and regretful of his deed—whether weakly or strongly—but the pleasure of his soul in that sin is stronger than the pain of his heart in the fear of it, due to causes that weaken fear (ignorance and heedlessness) and causes that strengthen desire. Thus, regret exists but is not sufficient to move the resolve nor strong upon it. If he is spared a desire stronger than it—i.e., only what is weaker opposes it—fear overcomes desire and prevails, necessitating the abandonment of the sin. A wicked man may have a fierce craving for wine such that he cannot bear to abstain from it, while his craving for backbiting, slandering people, and looking at the unlawful is weaker. His fear of God may have reached a level that suppresses this weak desire but not the strong one, so the army of fear necessitates the emergence of resolve to abandon. Indeed, this wicked man says to himself: "If Satan has overcome me through the predominance of desire in some sins, I should not throw off the reins entirely and let go of the bridle altogether. Rather, I will strive against him in some sins; perhaps I will overcome him, and my overcoming him in some will be an expiation for some of my sins." Were this not conceivable, it would be inconceivable for a wicked man to pray and fast. It would be said to him: "If your prayer is not for God, it is not sound; and if it is for God, then abandon wickedness for God—for God's command is one. It is inconceivable that you intend by your prayer to draw near to God while you do not draw near by abandoning wickedness." This is impossible. Rather, he says: "I have two commands from God, and upon me are two punishments for opposing them. I am able in one to overcome Satan, and in the other I am incapable. So I overcome him in what I can, and I hope that my striving in it will expiate for me some of what I was incapable of due to the excess of my desire." How can this not be conceivable, when it is the state of every Muslim? For there is no Muslim who does not combine obedience to God and disobedience to Him, and there is no cause for this except this one.

When this is understood, it is understood that the predominance of fear over desire in some sins is possible in existence. Fear, when it arises from a past act, begets regret, and regret begets resolve. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Regret is repentance"—without conditioning regret over every sin. And he said: "The one who repents from a sin is like one who has no sin"—without saying "the one who repents from all sins." By these meanings, the saying of the one who claims that repentance from some sins is impossible—because they are similar in respect of desire and in respect of exposure to God's wrath—is refuted. Indeed, it is permissible to repent from drinking wine but not from nabīdh (date-wine), due to their difference in occasioning wrath; and to repent from much but not little, because the multiplicity of sins has an effect on the multiplicity of punishment. Thus, he indulges his desire to the extent he cannot resist, and abandons some of his desire for God—like the patient whom the physician warned against fruit: he may eat a little of it but does not eat much of it.

From this it is established that one cannot repent from something without repenting from its like. Rather, what he repents from must differ from what remains upon him—either in the severity of the sin or in the predominance of desire. When this difference exists in the penitent's belief, the difference in his state of fear and regret becomes conceivable, and thus the difference in his state of abandonment becomes conceivable. His regret over that sin and his fidelity to his resolve to abandon it joins him to one who has not sinned, even if he has not obeyed God in all commands and prohibitions.

If you say: "Is the repentance of an impotent man (ʿannīn)—one incapable of intercourse—sound for the fornication he committed before impotence struck?" I say: No, because repentance is an expression for a regret that impels resolve to abandon what one is able to do. What one is not able to do has ceased by itself, not by his abandonment of it. But I say: if after impotence there arises for him a disclosure and knowledge by which he realizes the harm of the fornication he committed, and there rises from him burning, grief, and regret—such that

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Categories of Servants Regarding the Continuance of Repentance
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان أقسام العباد في دوام التوبة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, clarity, and distinction between things; making evident what was obscure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, bayān denotes the divine act of clarifying truth from falsehood, often tied to prophetic disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical separation; here metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and moral differentiation of ranks.
- Root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To serve, worship, humble oneself; also denotes a slave or bondsman in absolute obedience.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIbādah is ultimate humility and submission before God, rooted in recognition of His lordship (rubūbiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal servitude; metaphorically extended to all acts of voluntary obedience and self-abasement before the Divine.
- Root: د-و-م (d-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Permanence, continuity, unceasing duration; that which does not cease or interrupt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dawām in spiritual context signifies the perpetual state of the heart’s orientation toward God, not merely episodic acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal temporal continuity; metaphorically used for moral steadfastness and unbroken resolve in repentance.
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; the act of reverting from error to right guidance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawbah is the soul’s return from disobedience to obedience, entailing regret, cessation, and resolve.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical return; here metaphorical for spiritual reversion to divine favor.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase "أقسام العباد" (categories of servants) uses annexation to specify the scope of division, while "في دوام التوبة" (regarding the continuance of repentance) functions as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) delimiting the subject matter.
chapters.translation: I say: Now I shall set forth the categories of the servants of God—may He be exalted—with respect to the continuance of repentance (tawbah), so that the seeker may discern his own station and not be deceived by the mere utterance of seeking forgiveness. Know that repentance, in its true reality, is not a single act that terminates at a moment, but rather a perpetual state that must endure until the end of one’s life. For the servant is never free from the risk of slipping, nor from the whisperings of the soul, nor from the lapses of the heart. Thus, the people are divided, in the permanence of this repentance, into distinct ranks and varying degrees. Among them is one whose repentance is sound at its root, yet he slackens in its continuation; and among them is one who persists in it with vigilance, guarding its conditions and renewing its resolve at every breath. And among them is one who imagines that repentance is accomplished by a single utterance, and thus he neglects the inward reality, falling into the trap of self-delusion. So let the intelligent servant examine himself, and let him know that the continuance of repentance is more difficult than its initiation, for the beginning is a spark, but the enduring is a blazing fire that consumes the veils of heedlessness.

chapters.title_en: The Four Ranks of the Penitent in the Reality of Tawbah
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن التائبين في التوبة على أربع طبقات الطبقة الأولى أن يتوب العاصي
ويستقيم على التوبة إلى آخر عمره فيتدارك ما فرط من أمره ولا يحدث نفسه
بالعود إلى ذنوبه إلا الزلات التي لا ينفك البشر عنها في العادات مهما لم
يكن في رتبة النبوة فهذا هو الاستقامة على التوبة وصاحبه هو السابق
بالخيرات المستبدل بالسيئات حسنات واسم هذه التوبة التوبة النصوح واسم هذه
النفس الساكنة النفس المطمئنة التي ترجع إلى ربها راضية مرضية وهؤلاء هم
الذين إليهم الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم سبق المفردون المستهترون
بذكر الله تعالى وضع الذكر عنهم أوزارهم فوردوا القيامة خفافا (3) فإن فيه
إشارة إلى أنهم كانوا تحت أوزار وضعها الذكر عنهم وأهل هذه الطبقة على رتب
من حيث النزوع إلى الشهوات فمن تائب سكنت شهواته تحت قهر المعرفة ففتر
نزاعها ولم يشغله عن السلوك صرعها وإلى من لا ينفك عن منازعة النفس ولكنه
ملي بمجاهدتها وردها ثم تتفاوت درجات النزاع أيضا بالكثرة والقلة وباختلاف
المدة وباختلاف الأنواع وكذلك يختلفون من حيث طول العمر فمن مختطف يموت
قريبا من توبته يغبط على ذلك لسلامته وموته قبل الفترة ومن ممهل طال جهاده
وصبره وتمادت استقامته وكثرت حسناته وحال هذا أعلى وأفضل إذ كل سيئة فإنما
تمحوها حسنة حتى قال بعض العلماء إنما يكفر الذنب الذي ارتكبه العاصي أن
يتمكن منه عشر مرات مع صدق الشهوة ثم يصبر عنه ويكسر شهوته خوفا من الله
تعالى واشتراط هذا بعيد وإن كان لا ينكر عظم أثره لو فرض ولكن لا ينبغي
للمريد الضعيف أن يسلك هذا الطريق فتهيج الشهوة وتحضر الأسباب حتى يتمكن ثم
يطمع في الانكفاف فإنه لا يؤمن خروج عنان الشهوة عن PageV04P043
اختياره فيقدم على المعصية وينقض توبته بل طريقها الفرار من ابتداء
أسبابه الميسرة له حتى يسد طرقها على نفسه ويسعى مع ذلك في كسر شهوته بما
يقدر  عليه فبه تسلم توبته في الابتداء
الطبقة الثانية تائب سلك طريق الاستقامة في أمهات الطاعات وترك كبائر
الفواحش كلها إلا أنه ليس ينفك عن ذنوب تعتريه لا عن عمد وتجريد قصد ولكن
يبتلى بها في مجاري أحواله من غير أن يقدم عزما على الإقدام عليها ولكنه
كلما أقدم عليها لام نفسه وندم وتأسف وجدد عزمه على أن يتشمر للاحتراز من
أسبابها التي تعرضه لها وهذه النفس جديرة بأن تكون هي النفس اللوامة إذ
تلوم صاحبها على ما تستهدف له من الأحوال الذميمة لا عن تصميم عزم وتخمين
رأي وقصد وهذه أيضا رتبة عالية وإن كانت نازلة عن الطبقة الأولى وهي أغلب
أحوال التائبين لأن الشر معجون بطينة الآدمي قلما ينفك عنه وإنما غاية سعيه
أن يغلب خيره شره حتى يثقل ميزانه فترجح كفة الحسنات فأما أن تخلو بالكلية
كفة السيئات فذلك في غاية البعد وهؤلاء لهم حسن الوعد من الله تعالى إذ قال
تعالى الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم إن ربك واسع المغفرة
فكل إلمام يقع بصغيرة لا عن توطين نفسه عليه فهو جدير بأن يكون من اللمم
المعفو عنه قال تعالى والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله
فاستغفروا لذنوبهم فأثنى عليهم مع ظلمهم لأنفسهم لتندمهم ولومهم أنفسهم
عليه وإلى مثل هذه الرتبة الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما رواه عنه
علي كرم الله وجهه خياركم كل مفتن تواب (1) وفي خبر آخر المؤمن كالسنبلة
يفيء أحيانا ويميل أحيانا (2) وفي الخبر لا بد للمؤمن من ذنب يأتيه الفينة
بعد الفينة (3) أي الحين بعد الحين فكل ذلك أدلة قاطعة على أن هذا القدر لا
ينفض التوبة ولا يلحق صاحبها بدرجة المصرين ومن يؤيس مثل هذا عن درجة
التائبين كالطبيب الذي يؤيس الصحيح عن دوام الصحة بما يتناوله من الفواكه
والأطعمة الحارة مرة بعد أخرى من غير مداومة واستمرار وكالفقيه الذي يؤيس
المتفقه عن نيل درجة الفقهاء بفتوره عن التكرار والتعليق في أوقات نادرة
غير متطاولة ولا  كثيرة وذلك يدل على نقصان الطبيب والفقيه بل الفقيه في
الدين هو الذي لا يؤيس الخلق عن درجات السعادات بما يتفق لهم من الفترات
ومقارفة السيئات المختطفات قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كل بنى آدم خطاءون
وخير الخطائين التوابون المستغفرون (4) وقال تعالى أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين
بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة فما وصفهم بعدم السيئة أصلا
الطبقة الثالثة أن يتوب ويستمر على الاستقامة مدة ثم تغلبه الشهوات فى
بعضالذنوب فيقدم عليها عن صدق وقصد شهوة لعجزه عن قهر الشهوة إلا أنه مع
ذلك مواظب على الطاعات وتارك جملة من الذنوب مع القدرة والشهوة وإنما قهرته
هذه الشهوة الواحدة أو الشهوتان وهو يود لو أقدره الله تعالى على قمعها
وكفاه شرها هذا أمنيته في حال قضاء الشهوة عند الفراغ يتندم ويقول ليتني لم
أفعله وسأتوب عنه وأجاهد نفسى PageV04P044
في قهرها لكنه تسول نفسه ويسوف توبته مرة بعد أخرى ويوما بعد يوم فهذه
النفس هي التي تسمى النفس المسولة وصاحبها من الذين قال الله تعالى فيهم
وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا فأمره من حيث مواظبته
على الطاعات وكراهته لما تعاطاه مرجو فعسى الله أن يتوب عليه وعاقبته مخطرة
من حيث تسويفه وتأخيره فربما بختطف قبل التوبة ويقع أمره في المشيئة فإن
تداركه الله بفضله وجبر كسره وامتن عليه بالتوبة التحق بالسابقين وإن غلبته
شقوته وقهرته شهوته فيخشى أن يحق عليه في الخاتمة ما سبق عليه من القول في
الأزل لأنه مهما تعذر على المتفقه مثلا الاحتراز عن شواغل التعلم دل تعذره
على أنه سبق له في الأزل أن يكون من الجاهلين فيضعف الرجاء في حقه وإذا
يسرت له أسباب المواظبة على التحصيل دل على أنه سبق له في الأزل أن يكون من
جملة العالمين فكذلك ارتباط سعادات الآخرة ودركاتها بالحسنات والسيئات بحكم
تقدير مسبب الأسباب كارتباط المرض والصحة بتناول الأغذية والأدوية وارتباط
حصول فقه النفس الذي به تستحق المناصب العلية في الدنيا بترك الكسل
والمواظبة على تفقيه النفس  فكما لا يصلح لمنصب الرياسة والقضاء والتقدم
بالعلم إلا نفس صارت فقيهة بطول التفقيه فلا يصلح لملك الآخرة ونعيمها ولا
القرب من رب العالمين إلا قلب سليم صار طاهرا بطول التزكية والتطهير هكذا
سبق في الأزل بتدبير رب الأرباب ولذلك قال تعالى ونفس وما سواها فألهمها
فجورها وتقواها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها فمهما وقع العبد في ذنب
فصار الذنب نقدا والتوبة نسيئة كان هذا من علامات الخذلان قال صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن العبد ليعمل بعمل أهل الجنة سبعين سنة حتى يقول الناس إنه من
أهلها ولا يبقى بينه وبين الجنة إلا شبر فيسبق عليه الكتاب فيعمل بعمل أهل
النار فيدخلها (1) فإذن الخوف من الخاتمة قبل التوبة وكل نفس فهو خاتمة ما
قبله إذ يمكن أن يكون الموت متصلا به فليراقب الأنفاس وإلا وقع في المحذور
ودامت الحسرات حين لا ينفع التحسر
الطبقة الرابعة أن يتوب ويجري مدة على الاستقامة ثم يعود إلى مقارفة
الذنب أو الذنوب من غير أن يحدث نفسه بالتوبة ومن غير أن يتأسف على فعله بل
ينهمك انهماك الغافل في اتباع شهواته فهذا من جملة المصرين وهذه النفس هي
النفس الأمارة بالسوء الفرارة من الخير ويخاف على هذا سوء الخاتمة وأمره في
مشيئة الله فإن ختم له بالسوء شقي شقاوة لا آخر لها وإن ختم له بالحسنى حتى
مات على التوحيد فينتظر له الخلاص من النار ولو بعد حين ولا يستحيل أن
يشمله عموم العفو بسبب خفي لا تطلع عليه كما لا يستحل أن يدخل الإنسان
خرابا ليجد كنزا فيتفق أن يجده وأن يجلس في البيت ليجعله الله عالما
بالعلوم من غير تعلم كما كان الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم فطلب المغفرة
بالطاعات كطلب العلم بالجهد والتكرار وطلب المال بالتجارة وركوب البحار
وطلبها بمجرد الرجاء مع خراب الأعمال كطلب الكنور في المواضع الخربة وطلب
العلوم من تعليم الملائكة وليت من اجتهد تعلم وليت من اتجر استغنى وليت من
صام وصلى غفر له فالناس  كلهم محرومون إلا العالمون والعالمون كلهم محرومون
إلا العاملون والعاملون كلهم محرومون إلا المخلصون والمخلصون على خطر عظيم
وكما أن من خرب بيته وضيع ماله وترك نفسه وعياله جياعا يزعم أنه ينتظر فضل
الله بأن يرزقه كنزا يجده تحت الأرض في بيته الخرب يعد عنه ذوي البصائر من
الحمقى والمغرورين وإن كان ما ينتظره غير مستحيل في قدرة الله تعالى وفضله
فكذلك من ينتظر PageV04P045
المغفرة من فضل الله تعالى وهو مقصر عن الطاعة مصر على الذنوب غير سالك
سبيل المغفرة يعد عند أرباب القلوب من المعتوهين والعجب من عقل هذا المعتوه
وترويجه حماقته في صيغة حسنة إذ يقول إن الله كريم وجنته ليست تضيق على
مثلي ومعصيتي ليست تضره ثم تراه يركب البحار ويقتحم الأوعار في طلب الدينار
وإذا قيل له إن الله كريم ودنانير خزائنه ليست تقصر على فقرك وكسلك بترك
التجارة ليس يضرك فاجلس في بيتك فعساه يرزقك من حيث لا تحتسب فيستحمق قائل
هذا الكلام ويستهزىء به ويقول ما هذا الهوس السماء لا تمطر ذهبا ولا فضة
وإنما ينال ذلك بالكسب وهكذا قدره مسبب الأسباب وأجرى به سنته ولا تبديل
لسنة الله ولا يعلم المغرور أن رب الآخرة ورب الدنيا واحد وأن سنته لا
تبديل لها فيهما جميعا وأنه قد أخبر إذ قال وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
فكيف يعتقد أنه كريم في الآخرة وليس بكريم في الدنيا وكيف يقول ليس مقتضى
الكرم الفتور عن كسب المال ومقتضاه الفتور عن العمل للملك لذلك المقيم
والنعيم الدائم وأن ذلك بحكم الكرم يعطيه من غير جهد في الآخرة وهذا يمنعه
مع شدة الاجتهاد في غالب الأمر في الدنيا وينسى قوله تعالى وفي السماء
رزقكم وما توعدون فنعوذ بالله من العمى والضلال فما هذا إلا انتكاس على أم
الرأس وانغماس في ظلمات الجهل وصاحب هذا جدير بأن يكون داخلا تحت قوله
تعالى ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا
فأرجعنا نعمل صالحا أي أبصرنا أنك  صدقت إذ قلت وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
فأرجعنا نسعى وعند ذلك لا يمكن من الانقلاب ويحق عليه العذاب فنعوذ بالله
من دواعي الجهل والشك والارتياب السائق بالضرور إلى سوء المنقلب والمآب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; the act of reverting from sin to obedience; repentance as a decisive turning of the heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawbah is the divinely-facilitated return of the servant to God through abandoning sin, accompanied by resolve and remorse; its perfection is nusūḥ (sincere, unblemished repentance).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "returning" (rujūʿ); metaphorically, it denotes the soul's reorientation from disobedience to obedience, as if the sinner "returns" to his primordial covenant with God.
- Root: ل-و-م (l-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, reproach; the act of censuring oneself for a misdeed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The lawwāmah (self-reproaching soul) is that which censures its owner after a lapse, without prior deliberate intent—distinct from the ammārah (commanding soul) which embraces evil.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to blame; metaphorical: the soul's internal dialogue of regret, as if it stands as a prosecutor against its own inclinations.
- Root: س-و-ل (s-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To embellish, make something appear fair; to entice or seduce.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The musawwilah (procrastinating soul) is that which beautifies sin and postpones repentance, deceiving its owner with false hopes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: adorning; metaphorical: the soul's deceptive presentation of sin as attractive, delaying tawbah until it becomes a mere promise (nisīʾah).
- Root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Command, affair; the soul that commands.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ammārah bi-l-sūʾ (soul commanding evil) is that which persistently urges toward sin, unrepentant and heedless.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: commanding; metaphorical: the soul's tyrannical dominance over the will, driving it to disobedience without remorse.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥāl and Taʿlīq (Circumstantial Clause and Suspension) — In complex periodic sentences, circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) and suspended predicates (taʿlīq) govern the logical flow, as seen in the conditional structures (law, idhā) and the layered descriptions of each rank, ensuring the reader grasps the temporal and causal sequencing of the penitent's states.
chapters.translation:
Know that the penitent, in the matter of repentance (tawbah), fall into four ranks.

**The First Rank:** That a disobedient sinner repents and remains steadfast upon his repentance until the end of his life, thereby making up for what he has neglected of his affairs, and does not prompt himself to return to his sins—except for the slips (zallāt) from which human beings are not free in their habitual conduct, so long as one is not at the rank of prophethood. This is the steadfastness upon repentance, and its possessor is the one who races to good deeds (sābiq bi-l-khayrāt), exchanging his evil deeds for good ones. The name of this repentance is the sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasūḥ), and the name of this soul is the tranquil soul (al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinnah) which returns to its Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. These are the ones to whom the Prophet (peace be upon him) alluded in his saying: «The solitary ones (al-mufarridūn) have preceded—those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God, the Exalted; remembrance has lifted their burdens from them, so they arrive at the Resurrection light (of burden)» (ḥadīth). For in this there is an indication that they were beneath burdens which remembrance lifted from them. The people of this rank are themselves of varying degrees with respect to the pull toward appetites (shahawāt). Among them is a penitent whose appetites have been stilled under the domination of knowledge (maʿrifah), so their pull has weakened and their struggle does not distract him from his path. And among them is one who is not free from the soul's resistance, but he is occupied with struggling against it (mujāhadah) and repelling it. Then the degrees of resistance also vary in abundance and scarcity, in the duration of time, and in the kinds [of appetites]. Likewise, they differ with respect to the length of life: among them is one who is snatched away (mukhtataf), dying soon after his repentance—he is envied for that, due to his safety and his death before any lapse (fatrah)—and among them is one who is given respite, whose struggle and patience are prolonged, whose steadfastness endures, and whose good deeds multiply. The state of this latter is higher and more excellent, for every evil deed is only erased by a good deed. Indeed, some scholars have said: "An offense which a disobedient sinner commits is only expiated when he is able to commit it ten times with sincere appetite, then he abstains from it and breaks his appetite out of fear of God, the Exalted." But stipulating this is far-fetched, even if its great effect is not denied were it to be assumed. However, it behooves not the weak aspirant (murīd) to tread this path, lest the appetite be stirred and the causes present themselves until he is able [to sin], then he hopes to hold back—for it is not safe that the reins of appetite slip from his control, and he advances upon disobedience and breaks his repentance. Rather, his way is to flee from the very beginnings of its facilitated causes, so that he blocks its paths against himself, while striving with all his might to break his appetite. By this, his repentance is rendered safe at its inception.

**The Second Rank:** A penitent who treads the path of steadfastness in the major acts of obedience and abandons all the grave sins (kabāʾir al-fawāḥish), yet he is not free from sins that befall him—not by deliberate intent or pure resolve, but he is afflicted by them in the flow of his circumstances, without having firmly resolved to commit them. However, whenever he does commit them, he blames himself, feels remorse, grieves, and renews his resolve to gird himself against the causes that expose him to them. This soul is worthy of being the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwāmah), for it reproaches its owner for the blameworthy states it falls into—not out of firm resolve or deliberate opinion and intent. This too is a lofty rank, even if it is lower than the first rank. It is the most prevalent state of the penitent, for evil is kneaded into the clay of the human being (ṭīnah al-ādamī) and he is rarely free from it. His utmost striving is only that his good may overcome his evil, until his scale is heavy and the pan of good deeds outweighs. As for the pan of evil deeds being entirely empty—that is extremely remote. These have a good promise from God, the Exalted, for He said: «Those who avoid the grave sins and indecencies, except minor lapses (al-lamam)—indeed your Lord is vast in forgiveness» (Q. 53:32). So every lapse that occurs as a minor sin, not from settling one's soul upon it, is worthy of being among the pardoned lapses. He, the Exalted, said: «And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins» (Q. 3:135)—and He praised them despite their wronging themselves, because of their remorse and their blaming of themselves for it. To this rank is the allusion in his saying (peace be upon him), as related by ʿAlī (may God honor his face): «The best of you are every oft-tried, oft-repentant one» (ḥadīth). And in another report: «The believer is like the ear of grain—it bends sometimes and inclines sometimes» (ḥadīth). And in the report: «There must be for the believer a sin which he commits from time to time» (ḥadīth)—that is, from one period to another. All of these are decisive proofs that this measure does not nullify repentance, nor does it attach its possessor to the rank of the obstinate (muṣirrīn). Whoever despairs of such a one attaining the rank of the penitent is like a physician who despairs of a healthy man maintaining his health because he partakes of fruits and hot foods from time to time, without persistence and continuity—and like a jurist who despairs of a student of jurisprudence attaining the rank of jurists because of his lapses from repetition and study at rare, non-prolonged, and non-frequent times. That indicates the deficiency of the physician and the jurist. Rather, the true jurist in religion is he who does not despair of creation attaining the ranks of felicities because of the lapses (fatrāt) and the fleeting sins that befall them. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «Every son of Adam is an errer, and the best of errers are the oft-repentant, the oft-seeking-forgiveness» (ḥadīth). And He, the Exalted, said: «Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good» (Q. 28:54)—so He did not describe them as being entirely free of evil.

**The Third Rank:** That one repents and continues upon steadfastness for a period, then appetites overcome him in some sins, and he commits them with sincere intent and deliberate appetite, due to his inability to subdue the appetite. Yet, despite that, he is constant upon acts of obedience and abandons a number of sins despite having the ability and the appetite. Only this one appetite, or two appetites, have overcome him. He wishes that God, the Exalted, would empower him to suppress them and spare him their evil—this is his aspiration at the moment of fulfilling the appetite. Upon finishing, he feels remorse and says: "Would that I had not done it; I will repent of it and struggle against my soul to subdue it." But his soul embellishes (tasawwala) for him and he procrastinates his repentance (yasawwifu) time after time, day after day. This soul is the one called the embellishing-procrastinating soul (al-nafs al-musawwilah). Its possessor is among those of whom God, the Exalted, said: «And others who acknowledged their sins—they mixed a righteous deed with another evil one» (Q. 9:102). His affair, in respect of his constancy upon acts of obedience and his abhorrence of what he has perpetrated, is hopeful—perhaps God will turn to him in mercy. But his end is perilous, in respect of his procrastination and delay, for perhaps he will be snatched away before repentance, and his affair falls under the [divine] will (mashīʾah). If God overtakes him with His grace, mends his fracture, and bestows upon him repentance, he joins the forerunners. But if his wretchedness overcomes him and his appetite conquers him, it is feared that what was decreed for him in eternity past (al-azal) will be realized against him at the end. For whenever a student of jurisprudence, for example, finds it impossible to guard against the distractions of learning, the impossibility indicates that it was decreed for him in eternity past that he would be among the ignorant—so hope weakens in his case. And when the causes of constancy upon acquisition are facilitated for him, that indicates that it was decreed for him in eternity past that he would be among the learned. Likewise is the connection of the felicities of the Hereafter and its degrees of misery to good deeds and evil deeds, by the decree of the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb)—just as illness and health are connected to the intake of foods and medicines, and just as the attainment of the jurisprudence of the soul, by which one deserves high positions in this world, is connected to abandoning laziness and being constant upon educating the soul. For just as none is fit for the position of leadership, judgeship, and precedence in knowledge except a soul that has become jurisprudent through prolonged study, so none is fit for the kingdom of the Hereafter and its bliss, nor for nearness to the Lord of the Worlds, except a sound heart (qalb salīm) that has become pure through prolonged purification and cleansing. Thus it was decreed in eternity past by the governance of the Lord of Lords. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: «And by the soul and Him who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness—he has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it» (Q. 91:7-10). So whenever a servant falls into a sin, and the sin becomes ready cash (naqd) while repentance becomes credit (nasīʾah), this is among the signs of abandonment (khidhlān). He (peace be upon him) said: «Indeed, a servant may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise for seventy years, until people say he is among its people, and there remains between him and Paradise but a span—then the decree overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire, and enters it» (ḥadīth). Therefore, fear of the end (khātīmah) must precede repentance, and every breath is the end of what precedes it, for it is possible that death may be connected to it. So let him watch over his breaths—otherwise he will fall into the perilous, and regrets will persist when regret is of no avail.

**The Fourth Rank:** That one repents and runs for a period upon steadfastness, then returns to committing the sin or sins—without prompting himself to repent, without grieving over his deed, but rather plunging headlong, like the heedless, into following his appetites. This one is among the obstinate (muṣirrīn). This soul is the soul commanding evil (al-nafs al-ammārah bi-l-sūʾ), fleeing from good. It is feared for this one that his end will be evil, and his affair is under the will of God. If he is sealed with evil, he is wretched with a wretchedness that has no end. And if he is sealed with the good end, dying upon monotheism (tawḥīd), then deliverance from the Fire is awaited for him, even if after a time. Nor is it impossible that the general pardon (al-ʿafw al-ʿāmm) should encompass him due to a hidden cause upon which one does not gaze—just as it is not impossible that a man should enter a ruin to find a treasure and happen to find it, or that he should sit in his house and God should make him learned in the sciences without study, as was the case with the prophets (peace be upon them). For seeking forgiveness through acts of obedience is like seeking knowledge through effort and repetition, and seeking wealth through trade and crossing the seas. Seeking it through mere hope, with ruined deeds, is like seeking treasures in ruined places, and seeking knowledge from the teaching of angels. Would that whoever strove learned! Would that whoever traded grew rich! Would that whoever fasted and prayed was forgiven! For all people are deprived except the learned; and all the learned are deprived except the doers; and all the doers are deprived except the sincere (mukhliṣūn); and the sincere are upon a great peril. And just as one who ruins his house, wastes his wealth, and leaves himself and his family hungry, claiming that he awaits God's grace by being provided a treasure he finds beneath the earth in his ruined house—such a one is counted by the people of insight among the foolish and deluded, even if what he awaits is not impossible in God's power and grace—so likewise, one who awaits forgiveness from God's grace while being negligent in obedience, obstinate upon sins, and not treading the path of forgiveness, is counted by the people of hearts among the feebleminded. And the wonder is at the intellect of this feebleminded one, and his dressing up of his folly in a fair form, for he says: "God is Generous (Karīm), and His Paradise is not too narrow for the likes of me, and my disobedience does not harm Him." Then you see him crossing the seas and plunging into rugged terrains in pursuit of a dinar. And when it is said to him: "God is Generous, and the dinars of His treasuries are not insufficient for your poverty, and your laziness in abandoning trade does not harm Him—so sit in your house; perhaps He will provide for you from whence you do not expect"—he deems the speaker of this foolish and mocks him, saying: "What is this madness? The sky does not rain gold or silver; that is only attained through earning." Thus is the decree of the Causer of causes, and He has run His sunnah (custom) accordingly—«and you will find no change in the sunnah of God» (Q. 33:62). The deluded one does not know that the Lord of the Hereafter and the Lord of this world are One, and that His sunnah admits no change in both of them, and that He has informed [us] when He said: «And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for» (Q. 53:39). How can he believe that He is Generous in the Hereafter but not Generous in this world? And how can he say that the requirement of generosity is not indolence from earning wealth, while its requirement is indolence from working for that abiding kingdom and perpetual bliss—and that by the decree of generosity He will give it without effort in the Hereafter, while He withholds it, despite intense striving, in most cases in this world? And he forgets His saying, the Exalted: «And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised» (Q. 51:22). So we seek refuge in God from blindness and misguidance! For this is nothing but a turning upside-down upon the crown of the head, and a plunging into the darknesses of ignorance. Its possessor is worthy of being included under His saying, the Exalted: «And if you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard—so return us, and we will work righteousness"» (Q. 32:12)—that is, "We have seen that You spoke truly when You said: 'And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for,' so return us that we may strive." But at that point, turning back will not be permitted, and the chastisement will be realized against him. So we seek refuge in God from the incitements of ignorance, doubt, and suspicion, which drive one inevitably to an evil end and a bad return.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of What the Penitent Must Hasten to Do If a Sin Befalls Him — Whether by Deliberate Intent and Overpowering Desire, or by a Fleeting Lapse Occurring by Way of Chance
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان ما ينبغي أن يبادر إليه التائب إن جرى عليه ذنب إما عن قصد وشهوة غالبة أو عن إلمام بحكم الاتفاق
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-د-ر (b-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to hasten, to rush forward, to be foremost" — derived from the early morning rush (bukūr) toward a goal; implies urgency and precedence in action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes the moral imperative of immediate response to divine command or repentance (tawbah), without delay or procrastination — aligning with the Quranic call to "race toward forgiveness" (sābiqū ilā maghfirah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical haste; metaphorical (majāz) sense is spiritual urgency — the soul's swift turning away from sin and toward obedience, as if fleeing a fire.
- Root: ل-م-م (l-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to touch lightly, to graze, to approach briefly" — also denotes a minor or inadvertent occurrence; from this comes il'mām (a fleeting visit or passing touch).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic ethics, refers to "lesser sins" or inadvertent lapses (lamam) that are not persistent or deliberate — distinguished from major sins (kabā'ir) by their transient nature and lack of full volition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical touching; metaphorical sense is the soul's momentary brush with sin — a passing inclination that does not settle into habit, akin to a traveler's brief stop.
- Root: ا-ت-ف-ق (t-f-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to coincide, to agree, to happen by chance" — from ittifāq (agreement, coincidence); implies an event not premeditated but arising from external circumstances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes the concurrence of causes beyond human intention — yet within divine decree (qadar), so that even "chance" is subsumed under God's ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is mutual agreement; metaphorical sense is the occurrence of an event without prior design — used here to contrast with deliberate sin, highlighting the spectrum of human culpability.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Adverbial Clause Structure (Jumla Sharṭiyya wa Ḥāliyya) — The phrase "إن جرى عليه ذنب" introduces a conditional clause (idhā) governing the entire exposition, while "إما... أو" (either...or) presents a disjunctive enumeration of two distinct causes, each requiring its own penitential response. The preposition "على" (upon him) marks the sin as befalling the subject passively, indicating the event's occurrence rather than the agent's primary act.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that when a sin befalls the penitent — whether it arises from deliberate intent and an overpowering desire that conquers his resolve, or from a fleeting lapse (il'mām) that touches him by way of chance and coincidence, without prior design — he must hasten (yubādira) to certain obligatory measures. For the path of repentance (tawbah) is not complete merely by verbal confession or by a passing pang of regret; rather, it demands immediate and decisive action suited to the nature of the sin that has occurred. If the sin was committed by deliberate choice and a desire that overwhelmed his restraint, then his haste must be greater, for the wound is deeper and the stain more firmly fixed. But if it was but a fleeting touch — a momentary lapse that befell him not by settled intention but by the concurrence of circumstances — his haste is still required, though the remedy may be lighter, for the blemish is less entrenched. In both cases, let him not delay, nor let him say, "I will repent tomorrow," for delay is a snare of the soul and a deception of the accursed one. Rather, let him hasten to sever the cause, to repair what can be repaired, to renew his resolve, and to turn wholly to God — for the moment of sin is a moment of danger, and the swiftness of return is the mark of the sincere.

chapters.title_en: On the Obligation of Repentance and the Expiation of Sins through Countervailing Good Deeds
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن الواجب عليه التوبة والندم والاشتغال بالتكفير بحسنة تضاده كما
ذكرنا طريقه فإن لم تساعده النفس على العزم على الترك لغلبة الشهوة فقد عجز
عن أحد الواجبين فلا ينبغي أن يترك الواجب الثاني وهو أن يدرأ بالحسنة
السيئة ليمحوها فيكون ممن خلط عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا فالحسنات المكفرة
للسيئات إما بالقلب وإما باللسان وإما بالجوارح ولتكن الحسنة في محل السيئة
وفيما يتعلق بأسبابها
فأما بالقلب فليكفره بالتضرع إلى الله تعالى في سؤال المغفرة والعفو
ويتذلل تذلل العبد الآبق ويكون ذله بحيث يظهر لسائر العباد وذلك بنقصان
كبره فيما بينهم فما للعبد الآبق المذنب وجه للتكبر على سائر العباد وكذلك
يضمر بقلبه الخيرات للمسلمين والعزم على الطاعات
وأما باللسان فبالاعتراف بالظلم والاستغفار فيقول رب ظلمت نفسي وعملت
سوءا فاغفر لي ذنوبي وكذلك يكثر من ضروب الاستغفار كما أوردناه في كتاب
الدعوات والأذكار
وأما بالجوارح فبالطاعات والصدقات وأنواع العبادات وفي الآثار ما يدل على
أن الذنب إذا اتبع بثمانية أعمال كان العفو عنه مرجوا أربعة من أعمال
القلوب وهي التوبة أو العزم على التوبة وحب الإقلاع عن الذنب وتخوف العقاب
عليه ورجاء المغفرة له وأربعة من أعمال الجوارح وهي أن تصلي عقيب الذنب
ركعتين ثم تستغفر الله تعالى بعدهم سبعين مرة وتقول سبحان الله العظيم
وبحمده مائة مرة ثم تتصدق بصدقة ثم تصوم
PageV04P046
يوما وفي بعض الآثار تسبغ الوضوء وتدخل المسجد وتصلى ركعتين (1) وفى بعض
الأخبار تصلي أربع ركعات (2) وفى الخبر إذا عملت سيئة فأتبعها حسنة تكفرها
السر بالسر والعلانية بالعلانية (3) ولذلك قيل صدقة السر تكفر ذنوب الليل
وصدقة الجهر تكفر ذنوب النهار وفي الخبر الصحيح أن  رجلا قال لرسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم إني عالجت امرأة فأصبت منها كل شىء إلا المسيس فاقض علي
بحكم الله تعالى فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أو ما صليت معنا صلاة الغداة قال
بلى فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات (4) وهذا يدل على أن
ما دون الزنا من معالجة النساء صغيرة إذ جعل الصلاة كفارة له بمقتضى قوله
صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلوات الخمس كفارات لما بينهن إلا الكبائر فعلى
الأحوال كلها ينبغي أن يحاسب نفسه كل يوم ويجمع سيئاته ويجتهد في دفعها
بالحسنات
فإن قلت فكيف يكون الاستغفار نافعا من غير حل عقدة الإصرار وفي الخبر
المستغفر من الذنب وهومصر عليه كالمستهزىء بآيات الله (5) وكان بعضهم يقول
استغفر الله من قولي أستغفر الله وقيل الاستغفار باللسان توبة الكذابين
وقالت رابعة العدوية استغفارنا يحتاج إلى استغفار كثير فاعلم أنه قد ورد في
فضل الاستغفار أخبار خارجة عن الحصر ذكرناها في كتاب الأذكار والدعوات حتى
قرن الله الاستغفار ببقاء الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال تعالى وما كان
الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون فكان بعض الصحابة
يقول كان لنا أمانان ذهب أحدهما وهو كون الرسول فينا وبقي الاستغفار معنا
فإن ذهب هلكنا (6) فنقول الاستغفار الذي هو توبة الكذابين هو الاستغفار
بمجرد اللسان من غير أن يكون للقلب فيه شركة كما يقول الإنسان بحكم العادة
وعن رأس الغفلة أستغفر الله وكما يقول إذا سمع صفة النار نعوذ بالله منها
من غير أن يتأثر به قلبه وهذا يرجع إلى مجرد حركة اللسان ولا جدوى له فأما
إذا انضاف إليه تضرع القلب إلى الله تعالى وابتهاله في سؤال المغفرة عن صدق
إرادة وخلوص نية ورغبة فهذه حسنة في نفسها فتصلح لأن تدفع بها السيئة وعلى
هذا تحمل الأخبار الواردة في فضل الاستغفار حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما
أصر من استغفر ولو عاد في اليوم سبعين مرة (7) PageV04P047
وهو عبارة عن الاستغفار بالقلب وللتوبة والاستغفار  درجات وأوائلها لا
تخلو عن الفائدة وإن لم تنته إلى أواخرها ولذلك قال سهل لا بد للعبد في كل
حال من مولاه فأحسن أحواله أن يرجع إليه في كل شيء فإن عصى قال يا رب استر
علي فإذا فرغ من المعصية قال يا رب تب علي فإذا تاب قال يا رب ارزقني
العصمة وإذا عمل قال يا رب تقبل مني وسئل أيضا عن الاستغفار الذي يكفر
الذنوب فقال أول الاستغفار الاستجابة ثم الإنابة ثم التوبة فالاستجابة
أعمال الجوارح والإنابة أعمال القلوب والتوبة إقباله على مولاه بأن يترك
الخلق ثم يستغفر الله من تقصيره الذي هو فيه ومن الجهل بالنعمة وترك الشكر
فعند ذلك يغفر له ويكون عنده مأواه ثم التنقل إلى الانفراد ثم الثبات ثم
البيان ثم الفكر ثم المعرفة ثم المناجاة ثم المصافاة ثم الموالاة ثم محادثة
السر وهو الخلة ولا يستقر هذا في قلب عبد حتى يكون العلم غذاءه والذكر
قوامه والرضا زاده والتوكل صاحبه ثم ينظر الله إليه فيرفعه إلى العرش فيكون
مقامه مقام حملة العرش وسئل أيضا عن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم التائب حبيب
الله فقال إنما يكون حبيبا إذا كان فيه جميع ما ذكر في قوله تعالى
{التائبون العابدون} الآية وقال الحبيب هو الذي لا يدخل فيما يكرهه حبيبه
والمقصود إن للتوبة ثمرتين {إحداهما} تكفير السيئات حتى يصير كمن لا ذنب
له والثانية نيل الدرجات حتى يصير حبيبا وللتكفير أيضا درجات فبعضه محو
لأصل الذنب بالكلية وبعضه تخفيف له ويتفاوت ذلك بتفاوت درجات التوبة
فالاستغفار بالقلب والتدارك بالحسنات وإن خلا عن حل عقدة الإصرار من أوائل
الدرجات فليس يخلو عن الفائدة أصلا فلا ينبغي أن تظن أن وجودها كعدمها بل
عرف أهل المشاهدة وأرباب القلوب معرفة لا ريب فيها أن قول الله تعالى {فمن
يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره} صدق وأنه لا تخلو ذرة من الخير عن أثر كما لا
تخلو شعيرة تطرح في الميزان عن أثر ولو خلت الشعيرة الأولى عن أثر لكانت
الثانية مثلها ولكان لا يرجح الميزان بأحمال الذرات وذلك بالضرورة محال بل
ميزان الحسنات يرجح بذرات الخير إلى أن يثقل فترفع كفة السيئات فإياك أن
تستصغر ذرات الطاعات فلا تأتيها وذرات المعاصي فلا تنفيها كالمرأة الخرقاء
تكسل عن الغزل تعللا بأنها لا تقدر في كل ساعة إلا على خيط واحد وتقول أي
غني يحصل بخيط وما وقع ذلك في الثياب ولا تدري المعتوهة أن ثياب الدنيا
اجتمعت خيطا خيطا وأن أجسام العالم مع اتساع أقطاره اجتمعت ذرة فإذن التضرع
والاستغفار بالقلب حسنة لا تضيع عند الله أصلا بل أقول الاستغفار باللسان
أيضا حسنة إذ حركة اللسان بها عن غفلة خير من حركة اللسان في تلك الساعة
بغيبة مسلم أو فضول كلام بل هو خير من السكوت عنه فيظهر فضله بالإضافة إلى
السكوت عنه وإنما يكون نقصانا بالإضافة إلى عمل القلب ولذلك قال بعضهم
لشيخه أبي عثمان المغربي إن لساني في بعض الأحوال يجري بالذكر والقرآن
وقلبي غافل فقال اشكر الله إذ استعمل جارحة من جوارحك في الخير وعوده الذكر
ولم يستعمله في الشر ولم يعوده الفضول وما ذكره حق فإن تعود الجوارح للخير
حتى يصير لها ذلك كالطبع يدفع جملة من المعاصي فمن تعود لسانه الاستغفار
إذا سمع من غيره كذبا سبق لسانه إلى ما تعود فقال أستغفر الله ومن تعود
الفضول سبق لسانه إلى قول ما أحمقك وما أقبح كذبك ومن تعود الاستعاذة إذا
حدث بظهور مبادىء الشر من شرير قال بحكم سبق اللسان نعوذ بالله وإذا تعود
الفضول قال لعنه الله فيعصي في إحدى الكلمتين ويسلم في الأخرى وسلامته أثر
اعتياد لسانه الخير وهو من جملة معاني قوله تعالى {إن الله لا يضيع أجر
المحسنين} ومعاني قوله تعالى {وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه}
PageV04P048
{أجرا عظيما} فانظر كيف ضاعفها إذ جعل الاستغفار في الغفلة عادة اللسان
حتى دفع بتلك العادة شر العصيان بالغيبة واللعن والفضول هذا تضعيف في
الدنيا لأدنى الطاعات وتضعيف الآخرة {أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون}  فإياك وأن تلمح
في الطاعات مجرد الآفات فتفتر رغبتك عن العبادات فإن هذه مكيدة روجها
الشيطان بلعنته على المغرورين وخيل إليهم أنهم أرباب البصائر وأهل التفطن
للخفايا والسرائر فأي خير في ذكرنا باللسان مع غفلة القلب فانقسم الخلق في
هذه المكيدة إلى ثلاثة أقسام ظالم لنفسه ومقتصد وسابق بالخيرات أما السابق
فقال صدقت يا ملعون ولكن هي كلمة حق أردت بها باطلا فلا جرم أعذبك مرتين
وأرغم أنفك من وجهين فأضيف إلى حركة اللسان حركة القلب فكان كالذي داوى جرح
الشيطان بنثر الملح عليه وأما الظالم المغرور فاستشعر في نفسه خيلاء الفطنة
لهذه الدقيقة ثم عجز عن الإخلاص بالقلب فترك مع ذلك تعويد اللسان بالذكر
فأسعف الشيطان وتدلى بحبل غروره فتمت بينهما المشاركة والموافقة كما قيل
وافق شن طبقه وافقه فاعتنقه وأما المقتصد فلم يقدر على إرغامه بإشراك القلب
في العمل وتفطن لنقصان حركة اللسان بالإضافة إلى القلب ولكن اهتدى إلى
كماله بالإضافة إلى السكوت والفضول فاستمر عليه وسأل الله تعالى أن يشرك
القلب مع اللسان في اعتياد الخير فكان السابق كالحائك الذي ذمت حياكته
فتركها وأصبح كاتبا والظالم المتخلف كالذي ترك الحياكة أصلا وأصبح كناسا
والمقتصد كالذي عجز عن الكتابة فقال لا أنكر مقدمة الحياكة ولكن الحائك
مذموم بالإضافة إلى الكاتب لا بالإضافة إلى الكناس فإذا عجزت عن الكتابة
فلا أترك الحياكة ولذلك قالت رابعة العدوية استغفارنا يحتاج إلى استغفار
كثير فلا تظن أنها تذم حركة اللسان من حيث أنه ذكر الله بل تذم غفلة القلب
فهو محتاج إلى الاستغفار من غفلة قلبه لا من حركة لسانه فإن سكت عن
الاستغفار باللسان أيضا احتاج إلى استغفارين لا إلى استغفار واحد فهكذا
ينبغي أن تفهم ذم ما يذم وحمد ما يحمد وإلا جهلت معنى ما قال القائل الصادق
حسنات الأبرار سيئات المقربين فإن هذه أمور تثبت بالإضافة فلا ينبغي أن
تؤخذ من غير إضافة بل ينبغي أن لا تستحقر ذرات الطاعات والمعاصي ولذلك قال
جعفر الصادق إن الله تعالى خبأ  ثلاثا في ثلاث رضاه في طاعته فلا تحقروا
منها شيئا فلعل رضاه فيه وغضبه في معاصيه فلا تحقروا منها شيئا فلعل غضبه
فيه وخبأ ولايته في عباده فلا تحقروا منهم أحدا فلعله ولي الله تعالى وزاد
وخبأ إجابته في دعائه فلا تتركوا الدعاء فربما كانت الإجابة فيه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal, or expiate; the act of blotting out or atoning for an offense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological expiation (takfīr) — the removal of sin's effect through a countervailing act of obedience, distinct from mere verbal remission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "covering"; metaphorically, the good deed "covers" the sin as a veil, erasing its trace.
- Root: د-ر-أ (d-r-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repel, push away, or ward off; to drive back an attacker.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic imperative to "repel evil with good" (idraʾ bi-l-ḥasanah al-sayyiʾah) — a dynamic counteraction of moral harm.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension of physical repulsion to the moral realm; the good deed acts as a shield against the sin's consequence.
- Root: أ-ب-ق (ʾ-b-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The flight of a slave from his master; a runaway (ābiq).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The paradigmatic state of the sinner before God — a fugitive slave who has abandoned his Lord's service and must return in abject humility.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a fleeing bondsman; metaphorically, the soul's estrangement from God through disobedience.
- Root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To penetrate, interpenetrate; a close friend (khalīl) whose love has permeated the heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The highest station of intimacy with God — the "secret conversation" (muḥādathat al-sirr) and the state of being God's beloved (ḥabīb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for something piercing through; metaphorically, the love that pierces the soul's depths, leaving no room for disobedience.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause with In-Fāʾ (الشّرط بالفاء) — When the protasis (e.g., "if the soul does not assist you") is followed by a nominal or negated apodosis, the particle fa- is mandatory, marking the result as contingent upon the condition's fulfillment.
chapters.translation:
Know that what is incumbent upon him is repentance, remorse, and engagement in expiation through a good deed that countervails the sin, as we have already mentioned its method. If the soul does not assist him in resolving to abandon the sin due to the dominance of lust, then he has failed in one of the two obligations — so he must not abandon the second obligation, which is to repel the evil deed with a good deed in order to blot it out, thereby becoming one of those who "mixed a righteous work with another evil one" {«آخَرَ سَيِّئًا»}. The good deeds that expiate evil deeds are either by the heart, or by the tongue, or by the limbs — and let the good deed be in the very locus of the evil deed and in what pertains to its causes.

As for the heart: let him expiate it by supplicating humbly to God Most High in asking for forgiveness and pardon, and let him abase himself with the abasement of a runaway slave. Let his lowliness be such that it becomes apparent to the rest of creation — and that is through the diminishment of his pride among them. For what face does the runaway, sinning slave have to be arrogant toward the rest of creation? Likewise, let him harbor in his heart good intentions toward the Muslims and resolve upon acts of obedience.

As for the tongue: through confession of wrongdoing and seeking forgiveness, saying: "My Lord, I have wronged myself and done evil, so forgive me my sins." Likewise, let him multiply the various forms of seeking forgiveness (istighfār), as we have set forth in the Book of Supplications and Remembrances.

As for the limbs: through acts of obedience, alms-giving, and the various kinds of worship. In the transmitted reports (āthār) there is indication that when a sin is followed by eight works, forgiveness for it is hoped for: four are works of the hearts — namely, repentance, or resolve upon repentance, love of desisting from the sin, fear of its punishment, and hope of forgiveness for it; and four are works of the limbs — namely, that he pray two rakʿahs after the sin, then seek God's forgiveness seventy times after them, and say "Glory be to God the Magnificent and by His praise" one hundred times, then give alms, then fast. And in some reports: "perfect the ablution, enter the mosque, and pray two rakʿahs." And in some reports: "pray four rakʿahs." And in the report: "When you commit an evil deed, follow it with a good deed that expiates it — the secret with the secret, and the open with the open." For this reason it was said: "The secret alms expiates the sins of the night, and the open alms expiates the sins of the day." And in the sound report (al-ḥadīth al-ṣaḥīḥ), a man said to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: "I have dallied with a woman and obtained from her everything except intercourse — so pronounce judgment upon me with God's judgment." He said: "Did you not pray the dawn prayer with us?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds" {«إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ»}. This indicates that what is less than adultery — namely, dalliance with women — is a minor sin, since he made the prayer an expiation for it, in accordance with his saying, peace be upon him: "The five prayers are expiations for what is between them, except for the major sins." So in all circumstances, one ought to reckon with himself every day, gather his evil deeds, and strive to repel them with good deeds.

If you say: "How can seeking forgiveness be beneficial without the dissolution of the knot of persistence (al-iṣrār)? And in the report: 'The one who seeks forgiveness for a sin while persisting in it is like one who mocks the verses of God.' And some of them used to say: 'I seek God's forgiveness from my saying "I seek God's forgiveness."' And it was said: 'Seeking forgiveness with the tongue is the repentance of liars.' And Rābiʿah al-ʿAdawiyyah said: 'Our seeking forgiveness itself needs much seeking of forgiveness.'"

Know that there have come down concerning the virtue of seeking forgiveness reports beyond enumeration, which we have mentioned in the Book of Remembrances and Supplications — so much so that God coupled seeking forgiveness with the survival of the Messenger, peace be upon him, saying: {«وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ»} "But God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness." Some of the Companions used to say: "We had two securities; one of them has departed — namely, the Messenger being among us — and seeking forgiveness remains with us. If it departs, we are destroyed."

So we say: The seeking of forgiveness that is "the repentance of liars" is the seeking of forgiveness by the mere tongue, without the heart having any share in it — as a man says, by force of habit and from the head of heedlessness, "I seek God's forgiveness"; and as he says, when he hears a description of the Fire, "We seek refuge in God from it," without his heart being affected by it. This reverts to the mere movement of the tongue, and it has no benefit. But when there is joined to it the heart's supplication to God Most High and its earnest entreaty in asking forgiveness, with truthful intention and pure resolve and desire — then this is a good deed in itself, and it is fit that one repel the evil deed with it. And upon this are carried the reports concerning the virtue of seeking forgiveness, until he said, peace be upon him: "He who seeks forgiveness is not persistent, even if he returns to the sin seventy times in a day." This is an expression for seeking forgiveness with the heart.

For repentance and seeking forgiveness have degrees, and their beginnings are not devoid of benefit even if they do not reach their ends. For this reason Sahl said: "The servant is in need of his Master in every state; the best of his states is that he return to Him in everything. If he disobeys, he says: 'O Lord, veil me.' When he finishes the act of disobedience, he says: 'O Lord, grant me repentance.' When he repents, he says: 'O Lord, grant me protection (ʿiṣmah).' When he acts, he says: 'O Lord, accept from me.'"

He was also asked about the seeking of forgiveness that expiates sins, and he said: "The first of seeking forgiveness is responsiveness (al-istijābah), then turning back (al-inābah), then repentance (al-tawbah). Responsiveness is the works of the limbs; turning back is the works of the hearts; and repentance is his turning toward his Master by abandoning creation — then he seeks God's forgiveness for the shortcoming in which he is, and for ignorance of the blessing and neglect of gratitude. At that point he is forgiven, and his abode is with Him. Then comes the transition to solitude, then steadfastness, then clarity, then reflection, then knowledge, then intimate conversation (al-munājāh), then pure affection (al-muṣāfāh), then loyal friendship (al-muwālāh), then the secret discourse (muḥādathat al-sirr) — and that is intimate love (al-khullah). This does not settle in a servant's heart until knowledge is his nourishment, remembrance his sustenance, contentment his provision, and trust (tawakkul) his companion. Then God looks upon him and raises him to the Throne, and his station becomes the station of the bearers of the Throne."

He was also asked about his saying, peace be upon him: "The repentant one is the beloved of God" {«التَّائِبُ حَبِيبُ اللهِ»}, and he said: "He is only a beloved when he possesses all that is mentioned in His saying: {«التَّائِبُونَ الْعَابِدُونَ»} 'Those who repent, those who worship' — the verse. And the beloved is he who does not enter into what his Beloved dislikes."

The point is that repentance has two fruits: one is the expiation of evil deeds, so that he becomes like one who has no sin; and the second is the attainment of degrees, so that he becomes a beloved. And expiation also has degrees: some of it is the erasure of the sin's very root entirely, and some of it is its lightening — and this varies according to the variation in the degrees of repentance. So seeking forgiveness with the heart and making amends with good deeds, even if it is devoid of dissolving the knot of persistence, is among the beginnings of the degrees — yet it is not devoid of benefit entirely. You must not think that its existence is like its non-existence. Rather, the people of direct witnessing (ahl al-mushāhadah) and the masters of hearts know with a knowledge in which there is no doubt that God's saying {«فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ»} "Whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it" is true, and that no atom of good is devoid of effect, just as no grain thrown into the balance is devoid of effect. For if the first grain were devoid of effect, the second would be like it, and the balance would never be weighed down by loads of atoms — and that is impossible by necessity. Rather, the balance of good deeds is weighed down by atoms of good until it becomes heavy, and the pan of evil deeds is lifted up.

So beware of deeming the atoms of acts of obedience too insignificant to perform, and the atoms of acts of disobedience too insignificant to repel — like the foolish woman who is too lazy to spin, excusing herself that she cannot produce more than a single thread each hour, and says: "What wealth comes from a thread?" — and it never occurred to her, the imbecile, that the garments of this world are assembled thread by thread, and that the bodies of the world, despite the vastness of their dimensions, are assembled atom by atom.

Thus, supplication and seeking forgiveness with the heart is a good deed that is not lost with God at all. Rather, I say: seeking forgiveness with the tongue is also a good deed — for the tongue's movement in it, even from heedlessness, is better than the tongue's movement in that hour in backbiting a Muslim or in superfluous speech. Indeed, it is better than silence about it, so its virtue appears in relation to silence about it. It is only a deficiency in relation to the heart's work. For this reason, someone said to his master Abū ʿUthmān al-Maghribī: "My tongue in some states flows with remembrance and the Quran while my heart is heedless." He said: "Thank God that He has employed one of your limbs in good and accustomed it to remembrance, and did not employ it in evil nor accustom it to superfluity." And what he said is true — for the habituation of the limbs to good, until it becomes like a second nature to them, repels a host of sins. Whoever accustoms his tongue to seeking forgiveness, when he hears from another a lie, his tongue precedes him to what it is accustomed to, and he says: "I seek God's forgiveness." And whoever accustoms it to superfluity, his tongue precedes him to saying: "How foolish you are! How ugly is your lie!" And whoever accustoms it to seeking refuge when the beginnings of evil appear from an evil person, he says, by the precedence of the tongue: "We seek refuge in God." And if he is accustomed to superfluity, he says: "May God curse him" — so he disobeys in one of the two words and is safe in the other. And his safety is the effect of his tongue's habituation to good. This is part of the meanings of His saying: {«إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ»} "Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the doers of good," and of His saying: {«وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا»} "And if it be a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward."

See how He multiplied it — for He made seeking forgiveness in heedlessness a habit of the tongue, until that habit repelled the evil of disobedience through backbiting, cursing, and superfluity. This is a multiplication in this world for the least of acts of obedience, and the multiplication of the Hereafter is {«أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ»} "greater, if they but knew."

So beware of gazing at mere defects in acts of obedience, lest your desire for worship slackens — for this is a stratagem that Satan has promoted with his curse upon the deluded, making them imagine that they are people of insight and masters of perceiving hidden things and secrets: "What good is there in our mentioning God with the tongue while the heart is heedless?" Thus, creation has divided in this stratagem into three categories: the self-wrongdoer (ẓālim li-nafsihi), the moderate (muqtaṣid), and the foremost in good deeds (sābiq bi-l-khayrāt).

As for the foremost: he said: "You have spoken truly, O accursed one — but it is a word of truth by which you intended falsehood. So I will torment you twice and rub your nose in the dust from two directions." So he added to the tongue's movement the heart's movement, and he was like one who treated Satan's wound by sprinkling salt upon it.

As for the deluded self-wrongdoer: he sensed within himself the pride of cleverness for this subtle point, then failed to achieve sincerity with the heart — yet he abandoned, despite that, the habituation of the tongue to remembrance. So he aided Satan and dangled on the rope of his delusion, and complete partnership and agreement was achieved between them, as it was said: "Wāfiq agreed with Shann — he agreed with him, so he embraced him."

As for the moderate: he could not rub Satan's nose in the dust by joining the heart to the work, and he perceived the deficiency of the tongue's movement in relation to the heart — but he was guided to its perfection in relation to silence and superfluity. So he persisted upon it and asked God Most High to join the heart with the tongue in the habituation to good.

The foremost was like the weaver who was blamed for his weaving, so he abandoned it and became a scribe. The self-wrongdoer who lagged behind was like one who abandoned weaving entirely and became a sweeper. The moderate was like one who could not achieve writing, and said: "I do not deny the merit of weaving — but the weaver is blameworthy in relation to the scribe, not in relation to the sweeper. So if I cannot achieve writing, I will not abandon weaving."

For this reason Rābiʿah al-ʿAdawiyyah said: "Our seeking forgiveness needs much seeking of forgiveness." Do not think that she blames the tongue's movement insofar as it is a remembrance of God — rather, she blames the heart's heedlessness. So he is in need of seeking forgiveness for his heart's heedlessness, not for his tongue's movement. For if he is silent about seeking forgiveness with the tongue as well, he needs two seekings of forgiveness, not one. Thus should you understand the blame of what is blameworthy and the praise of what is praiseworthy — otherwise you will be ignorant of the meaning of what the truthful one said: "The good deeds of the righteous are the evil deeds of those brought near (ḥasanāt al-abrār sayyiʾāt al-muqarrabīn)." For these matters are established in relation (bi-l-iḍāfah), so they must not be taken without relation. Rather, you must not deem insignificant the atoms of acts of obedience and acts of disobedience.

For this reason Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: "God Most High has hidden three things in three: He hid His pleasure in His obedience — so do not deem any of it insignificant, for perhaps His pleasure is in it; and He hid His wrath in His acts of disobedience — so do not deem any of it insignificant, for perhaps His wrath is in it; and He hid His friendship (wilāyah) among His servants — so do not deem anyone of them insignificant, for perhaps he is a friend of God Most High." And he added: "And He hid His response in His supplication — so do not abandon supplication, for perhaps the response is in it."

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Pillar: The Remedy of Repentance and the Method of Treatment for Undoing the Knot of Persistence
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| الركن الرابع في دواء التوبة وطريق العلاج لحل عقدة الإصرار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Physical knotting or binding; a firm tie that restricts movement or release.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A contractual or moral binding of the heart to a resolve; here, the stubborn fixation of the soul on sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tying a rope; metaphorical for the heart’s obstinate adherence to disobedience.
- Root: د-و-ا (d-w-ā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Medicine or cure; that which restores health after illness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual remedy for the soul’s ailment, paralleling bodily treatment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for medicinal substance; metaphorical for the corrective discipline of repentance.
- Root: أ-ص-ر (a-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Binding tightly, constraining; also, pressing or squeezing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Persistence in sin as a self-imposed shackle that prevents return to obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical constraint; metaphorical for the soul’s stubborn refusal to abandon transgression.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase «دواء التوبة» (remedy of repentance) uses annexation to specify the type of cure, while «حل عقدة الإصرار» (undoing the knot of persistence) employs a verbal noun (maṣdar) with an object, indicating the action’s targeted effect.
chapters.translation: As for the fourth pillar—concerning the remedy of repentance and the method of treatment for undoing the knot of persistence—know that the heart, when it has become habituated to sin, is like a limb stricken with chronic illness. Its cure lies not in a single dose, but in a sustained regimen that gradually loosens the grip of stubborn resolve. For persistence (al-iṣrār) is a knot tied by the devil’s whisperings and the soul’s caprice; it cannot be severed by mere intention, but only by a repeated act of opposition—turning the will away from the object of desire, and replacing the habit of transgression with the habit of obedience. Thus, the treatment proceeds in stages: first, awakening the heart to the ugliness of the sin; second, instilling fear of the consequences; third, cultivating shame before the All-Seeing; and fourth, steadfastly refusing the first impulse of desire, until the knot loosens and the soul returns to its natural inclination toward truth.

chapters.title_en: The Cure for Persistence in Sin: The Two Pillars of Knowledge and Patience
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن الناس قسمان شاب لا صبوة له نشأ على الخير واجتناب الشر وهو الذي
قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تعجب ربك من شاب ليست له صبوة (1)
وهذا عزيز نادر والقسم الثاني هو الذي لا يخلو عن مقارفة الذنوب ثم هم
ينقسمون إلى مصرين وإلى تائبين وغرضنا أن نبين العلاج في حل عقدة الإصرار
ونذكر الدواة فيه فاعلم أن شفاء التوبة لا يحصل إلا بالدواء ولا يقف على
الدواء من لا يقف على الداء إذ لا معنى للدواء إلا مناقضة أسباب الداء فكل
داء حصل من سبب فدواؤه حل ذلك السبب ورفعه وإبطاله ولا يبطل الشيء لا بضده
ولا سبب للإصرار إلا الغفلة والشهوة ولا يضاد الغفلة إلا العلم ولا يضاد
الشهوة إلا الصبر على قطع PageV04P049
الأسباب المحركة للشهوة والغفلة رأس الخطايا قال الله تعالى {وأولئك هم
الغافلون لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون} فلا دواء إذن للتوبة إلا
معجون يعجن من حلاوة العلم ومرارة الصبر وكما يجمع السكنجبين بين حلاوة
السكر وحموضة الخل ويقصد بكل منهما غرض آخر في العلاج بمجموعهما فيقمع
الأسباب المهيجة للصفراء فهكذا ينبغي أن تفهم علاج القلب مما به من مرض
الإصرار فإن لهذا الدواء أصلان أحدهما العلم والآخر الصبر ولا بد من
بيانهما
فإن قلت أينفع كل علم لحل الإصرار أم لا بد من علم مخصوص فاعلم أن العلوم
بجملتها أدوية لأمراض القلوب ولكن لكل مرض علم يخصه كما أن علم الطب نافع
في علاج الأمراض بالجملة ولكن يخص كل علة علم مخصوص فكذلك دواء الإصرار
فلنذكر خصوص ذلك العلم على موازنة مرض  الأبدان ليكون أقرب إلى الفهم فنقول
يحتاج المريض إلى التصديق بأمور {الأول} أن يصدق على الجملة بأن للمرض
والصحة أسبابا يتوصل إليها بالاختيار على ما رتبه مسبب الأسباب وهذا هو
الإيمان بأصل الطب فإن من لا يؤمن به لا يشتغل بالعلاج ويحق عليه الهلاك
وهذا وزانه مما نحن فيه الإيمان بأصل الشرع وهو أن للسعادة في الآخرة سببا
هو الطاعة وللشقاوة سببا هو المعصية وهذا هو الإيمان بأصل الشرائع وهذا لا
بد من حصوله إما عن تحقيق أو تقليد وكلاهما من جملة الإيمان
الثاني أنه لا بد أن يعتقد المريض في طبيب معين أنه عالم بالطب حاذق فيه
صادق فيما يعبر عنه لا يلبس ولا يكذب فإن إيمانه بأصل الطب لا ينفعه بمجرده
دون هذا الإيمان ووزانه مما نحن فيه العلم بصدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
والإيمان بأن كل ما يقوله حق وصدق لا كذب فيه ولا خلف
الثالث أنه لا بد أن يصغي إلى الطبيب فيما يحذره عنه من تناول الفواكه
والأسباب المضرة على الجملة حتى يغلب عليه الخوف في ترك الاحتماء فتكون شدة
الخوف باعثة له على الاحتماء ووزانه من الدين الإصغاء إلى الآيات والأخبار
المشتملة على الترغيب في التقوى والتحذير من ارتكاب الذنوب واتباع الهوى
والتصديق بجميع ما يلقى إلى سمعه من ذلك من غير شك واسترابة حتى ينبعث به
الخوف المقوي على الصبر الذي هو الركن الآخر في العلاج
الرابع أن يصغي إلى الطبيب فيما يخص مرضه وفيما يلزمه في نفسه الاحتماء
عنه ليعرفه أولا تفصيل ما يضره من أفعاله وأحواله ومأكوله ومشروبه فليس على
كل مريض الاحتماء عن كل شيء ولا ينفعه كل دواء بل لكل علة خاصة علم خاص
وعلاج خاص ووزانه من الدين أن كل عبد فليس يبتلى بكل شهوة وارتكاب ذنب بل
لكل مؤمن ذنب مخصوص أو ذنوب مخصوصة وإنما حاجته في الحال مرهقة إلى العلم
بأنها ذنوب ثم إلى العلم بآفاتها وقدر ضررها ثم العلم بكيفية التوصل إلى
الصبر عنها  ثم إلى العلم بكيفية تكفير ما سبق منها
فهذه علوم يختص بها أطباء الدين وهم العلماء الذين هم ورثة الأنبياء
فالعاصي إن علم عصيانه فعليه طلب العلاج من الطبيب وهو العالم وإن كان لا
يدري أن ما يرتكبه ذنب فعلى العالم أن يعرفه ذلك وذلك بأن يتكفل كل عالم
بإقليم أو بلدة أو محلة أو مسجد أو مشهد فيعلم أهله دينهم ويميز ما يضرهم
عما ينفعهم وما يشقيهم عما يسعدهم ولا ينبغي أن يصبر إلى أن يسئل عنه بل
ينبغي أن يتصدى لدعوة الناس إلى نفسه فإنهم ورثة الأنبياء والأنبياء ما
تركوا الناس على جهلهم بل كانوا ينادونهم في مجامعهم ويدورون على أبواب
دورهم في الابتداء ويطلبون واحدا واحدا فيرشدونهم فإن مرضى القلوب لا
يعرفون مرضهم كما أن الذي ظهر على وجهه برص
PageV04P050
ولا مرآة معه لا يعرف برصه ما لم يعرفه غيره وهذا فرض عين على العلماء
كافة وعلى السلاطين كافة أن يرتبوا في كل قرية وفي كل محلة فقيها متدينا
يعلم الناس دينهم فإن الخلق لا يولدون إلا جهالا فلا بد من تبليغ الدعوة
إليهم في الأصل والفرع والدنيا دار المرضى إذ ليس في بطن الأرض إلا ميت ولا
على ظهرها إلا سقيم ومرض القلوب أكثر من مرض الأبدان والعلماء أطباء
والسلاطين قوام دار المرضى فكل مريض لم يقبل العلاج بمداواة العالم يسلم
إلى السلطان ليكف شره كما يسلم الطبيب المريض الذي لا يحتمي أو الذي غلب
عليه الجنون إلى القيم ليقيده بالسلاسل والأغلال ويكف شره عن نفسه وعن سائر
الناس
وإنما صار مرض القلوب أكثر من مرض الأبدان لثلاث علل إحداها أن المريض به
لا يدري أنه مريض
والثانية أن عاقبته غير مشاهدة في هذا العالم بخلاف مرض البدن فإن عاقبته
موت مشاهد تنفر الطباع منه وما بعد الموت غير مشاهد وعاقبة الذنوب موت
القلب وهو غير مشاهد في هذا العالم فقلت النفرة عن الذنوب وإن علمها
مرتكبها فلذلك تراه يتكل على فضل الله في مرض القلب  ويجتهد في علاج مرض
البدن من غير اتكال
والثالثة وهو الداء العضال فقد الطبيب فإن الأطباء هم العلماء وقد مرضوا
في هذه الأعصار مرضا شديدا عجزوا عن علاجه وصارت لهم سلوة في عموم المرض
حتى لا يظهر نقصانهم فاضطروا إلى إغواء الخلق والإشارة عليهم بما يزيدهم
