And because renunciation in this world was a present kingdom, Satan envied him for it and barred him from it.

And the meaning of renunciation (al-zuhd) is that the servant possesses his lust and his anger, so that they submit to the motive of religion and the indication of faith. This is a kingdom by merit (mulk bi-al-istiḥqāq), for through it its possessor becomes free. And by the domination of lust over him, he becomes a slave to his private parts, his belly, and his other aims—so he becomes subjugated like a beast, owned, dragged by the rein of lust, seized by its halter to wherever it wishes and desires. How great is man's delusion when he supposes that he attains kingdom by becoming owned, and attains lordship by becoming a servant! Would such a one be anything but inverted in this world and overturned in the Hereafter? That is why one of the kings said to one of the ascetics: "Do you have any need?" He said: "How could I ask you for a need, when my kingdom is greater than your kingdom?" He said: "How is that?" He said: "Whoever is your master is my servant." He said: "How is that?" He said: "You are the servant of your lust, your anger, your private parts, and your belly—and I have mastered all of these, so they are my servants." This, then, is the kingdom in this world, and it is what drives one to the kingdom in the Hereafter. So those deluded by Satan's deception have lost this world and the Hereafter together; and those granted success in pressing on the straight path have won this world and the Hereafter together.

Now that you know the meaning of kingdom and lordship, the meaning of subjugation (al-taskhīr) and servitude (al-ʿubūdiyyah), the entry point of error in that, and the manner of Satan's blinding and obfuscation (talbīs), it becomes easy for you to detach from kingdom and status, to turn away from them, and to be patient upon their loss—for by abandoning them you become a king in the present moment, and you hope thereby for a kingdom in the Hereafter.

And whoever has been unveiled to these matters after having become accustomed to status, familiar with it, and entrenched in it through habit by directly engaging in its causes—mere knowledge and unveiling are not sufficient for his treatment. Rather, he must add action to it. And his action lies in three matters. The first is that he flee from the place of status so that he does not witness its causes, for patience becomes difficult for him in the presence of those causes—just as one overcome by lust flees from witnessing stirring forms. And whoever does not do this has disbelieved in Allah's blessing of the earth's vastness, for He, the Exalted, said: «ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها» — "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you might emigrate therein?" (Q 4:97). The second is that he compel himself in his deeds to actions contrary to what he was accustomed to—replacing affectation (al-takalluf) with self-abasement (al-tabadhdhul), and the garb of dignity (zayy al-ḥishmah) with the garb of humility (zayy al-tawāḍuʿ). Likewise, every appearance, state, and deed—in dwelling, clothing, food, standing, and sitting—that he used to observe in fulfillment of the requirements of his status, he should replace with their opposites, until by habit he becomes entrenched in the opposite of what he was previously entrenched in by habit. For there is no meaning to treatment except opposition (al-muḍāddah). The third is that he observe gentleness (al-talaffuf) and gradualism (al-tadrīj) in that, not moving all at once to the furthest extreme of self-abasement. For nature is averse, and it cannot be moved from its traits except gradually. So he leaves some and consoles himself with the rest; then, when his soul is content with that portion, he begins to leave some of that portion, until he is content with the remainder. And thus he does, little by little, until he suppresses those traits entrenched in him. And to this gradualism points his saying, peace be upon him: «إن هذا الدين متين فأوغل فيه برفق ولا تبغض إلى نفسك عبادة الله فإن المنبت لا أرضا قطع ولا ظهرا أبقى» — "Indeed, this religion is firm, so enter into it with gentleness, and do not make the worship of Allah hateful to your soul. For the one who pushes hard (al-munbit) neither covers the distance nor spares the mount." And to it points his saying, peace be upon him: «لا تشادوا هذا الدين فإن من يشاده يغلبه» — "Do not be harsh with this religion, for whoever is harsh with it, it overcomes him."

So, then, what we have mentioned of the treatment of patience regarding whispering, lust, and status—add it to what we have mentioned of the canons of the ways of striving (qawānīn ṭuruq al-mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Take it as your manual (dustūr) by which you may know the treatment of patience in all the divisions we have detailed before. For detailing each individual case would be lengthy. And whoever observes gradualism, patience will elevate him to a state where patience without it becomes difficult for him, just as patience with it was difficult before. So his affairs become inverted: what was beloved to him becomes detested, and what was disliked becomes a pleasant drink he cannot bear to be patient without. This is known only through experience (al-tajribah) and taste (al-dhawq). And it has a parallel in habits: for a boy is compelled to learning at the beginning by force, and it is difficult for him to be patient without play and patient with learning—until, when his insight opens and he becomes familiar with knowledge, the matter inverts, and it becomes difficult for him to be patient without knowledge and patient with play. And to this points what is related of one of the gnostics (al-ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī about patience—which of its kinds is most severe? He said: "Patience in Allah (al-ṣabr fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for Allah (al-ṣabr li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with Allah (al-ṣabr maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from Allah (al-ṣabr ʿan Allāh)." So al-Shiblī cried out a cry that nearly destroyed his soul. And it has been said regarding the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: «اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا» — "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q 3:200): "Be patient in Allah, vie in patience by Allah, and be steadfast with Allah." And it was said: "Patience for Allah is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by Allah is permanence (baqāʾ); patience with Allah is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from Allah is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said regarding its meaning:

"And patience from You is blameworthy in its outcomes... while patience in all other things is praiseworthy."

And it was also said:

"Patience is borne in all situations... except upon You, for it is not becoming."

This is the end of what we intended to explain of the sciences of patience and its secrets.

### ||| الشطر الثاني من الكتاب في الشكر

وله ثلاثة أركان الأول في فضيلة الشكر وحقيقته وأقسامه وأحكامه الثاني في
حقيقة النعمة وأقسامها الخاصة والعامة الثالث في بيان الأفضل من الشكر
والصبر

### |||| الركن الأول في نفس الشكر

### ||||| بيان فضيلة الشكر

اعلم أن الله تعالى قرن الشكر بالذكر في كتابه مع أنه قال ولذكر الله
أكبر فقال تعالى فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون وقال تعالى ما يفعل
الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وقال تعالى وسنجزي الشاكرين وقال عز وجل
إخبارا عن إبليس اللعين لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو
رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال ولا تجد اكثرم شاكرين وقال تعالى
وقليل من عبادي الشكور وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال
تعالى لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم واستثنى في خمسة أشياء في الإغناء والإجابة
والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء
{وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب {وقال}
ويغفر ما دون ذلك  لمن يشاء {وقال} ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من أخلاق
الربوبية إذ قال تعالى والله شكور حليم وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل
الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه وعده {وقال} وآخر دعواهم أن
الحمد لله رب العالمين
PageV04P080
وأما الأخبار فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الطاعم الشاكر بمنزلة
الصائم الصابر (1) حديث عطاء دخلت على عائشة فقلت لها أخبرينا بأعجب ما
رأيت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت واي امره لم يكن عجبا الحديث
في بكائه في صلاة الليل اخرجه ابو الشيخ ابن حبان في كتاب أخلاق رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن طريقة ابن الجوزي في الوفا وفيه ابو جناب واسمه
يحيى بن ابي حبة ضعفه الجمهور ورواه ابن حبان في صحيحه من رواية عبد الملك
ابن ابي سليمان عن عطاء دون قولها واي امره لم يكن عجبا وهو عند مسلم من
رواية عروة عن عائشة مقتصرا على آخر الحديث وهذا يدل على أن البكاء ينبغي
أن لا ينقطع أبدا وإلى هذا السر يشير ما روي أنه مر بعض الأنبياء بحجر صغير
يخرج منه ماء كثير فتعجب منه فأنطقه الله تعالى فقال منذ سمعت قوله تعالى
وقودها الناس والحجارة فأنا أبكي من خوفه فسأله أن يجيره من النار فأجاره
ثم رآه بعد مدة على مثل ذلك فقال لم تبكي الآن فقال ذاك بكاء الخوف وهذا
بكاء الشكر والسرور وقلب العبد كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة ولا تزول قسوته إلا
بالبكاء في حال الخوف والشكر جميعا وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال
ينادى يوم القيامة ليقم الحمادون فتقوم زمرة فينصب لهم لواء فيدخلون الجنة
قيل ومن الحمادون قال الذين يشكرون الله تعالى على كل حال (2) حديث الحمد
رداء الرحمن لم اجد له اصلا وفي الصحيح من حديث ابي هريرة الكبر رداؤه
الحديث وتقدم في العلم وأوحى الله تعالى إلى أيوب عليه السلام إني رضيت
بالشكر مكافأة من أوليائي في  كلام طويل وأوحى الله تعالى إليه أيضا في صفة
الصابرين أن دارهم دار السلام إذا دخلوها ألهمتهم الشكر وهو خير الكلام
وعند الشكر أستزيدهم وبالنظر إلي أزيدهم ولما نزل في الكنوز ما نزل قال عمر
رضي الله عنه أي المال نتخذ فقال عليه السلام ليتخذ أحدكم لسانا ذاكرا او
قلبا شاكرا // حديث عمر ليتخذ أحدكم لسانا ذاكرا وقلبا شاكرا الحديث تقدم
في النكاح فأمر باقتناء القلب الشاكر بدلا عن المال وقال ابن مسعود الشكر

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to acknowledge a benefit and manifest its effect"; the camel is called *shakūr* for showing the effect of its fodder in its hump and vigor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Gratitude is "recognition of beneficence (niʿmah) and its display"; its opposite is *kufr* (covering/concealing). In theological usage, it is the soul's cognizance of the Giver, the tongue's praise, and the limbs' obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the bodily manifestation of a benefit's trace; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to verbal praise and heartfelt acknowledgment. The verse {«لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ»} is literal in its promise of increase.
- Sībawayh Rule: *Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab* (Coordination on a Causal Basis) — In "قرن الشكر بالذكر" the conjunction links gratitude to remembrance as coordinate causes of divine reward, with the particle *maʿa* implying accompaniment rather than sequence.
chapters.translation:
### The Second Part of the Book — On Gratitude (al-Shukr)

It comprises three pillars: the first concerns the virtue of gratitude, its true nature, its divisions, and its rulings; the second concerns the true nature of the divine blessing (niʿmah), its particular and general divisions; the third concerns the clarification of which is more excellent — gratitude or patience (ṣabr).

### The First Pillar — On Gratitude Itself

#### Clarification of the Virtue of Gratitude

Know that God — exalted be He — coupled gratitude with remembrance (dhikr) in His Book, even though He said {«وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ»} ("and the remembrance of God is greater"). For He — exalted be He — said: {«فَاذْكُرُونِي أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِي وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ»} ("So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me"). And He — exalted be He — said: {«مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إِن شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنتُمْ»} ("What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?"). And He — exalted be He — said: {«وَسَنَجْزِي الشَّاكِرِينَ»} ("And We will reward the grateful"). And He — mighty and majestic — said, reporting from Iblīs the accursed: {«لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ»} ("I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path") — and it is said this path is the path of gratitude. And because of the exalted rank of gratitude, the accursed one attacked the creatures, saying: {«وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرِينَ»} ("and You will not find most of them grateful"). And He — exalted be He — said: {«وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ»} ("and few of My servants are the truly grateful").

God — exalted be He — has decisively affirmed increase (al-mazīd) with gratitude, without any exception, saying: {«لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ»} ("If you are grateful, I will surely increase you"). Yet He made exceptions in five matters — in enrichment, response, provision, forgiveness, and repentance — for He said: {«فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ إِن شَاءَ»} ("God will soon enrich you from His bounty, if He wills"); and He said: {«فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِن شَاءَ»} ("He removes that for which you call upon Him, if He wills"); and He said: {«يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»} ("He provides for whom He wills without account"); and He said: {«وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ»} ("and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills"); and He said: {«وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ»} ("and God turns in repentance to whom He wills").

Gratitude is also an attribute of lordship (min akhlāq al-rubūbiyyah), since He — exalted be He — said: {«وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ»} ("and God is Appreciative, Forbearing"). And God has made gratitude the key to the speech of the people of Paradise, for He — exalted be He — said: {«وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ»} ("and they will say: 'Praise be to God who has fulfilled His promise to us'"); and He said: {«وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ»} ("and the last of their call will be: 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds'").

As for the reports (akhbār), the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "The one who eats and is grateful is like the one who fasts and is patient." (Ḥadīth of ʿAṭāʾ: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said to her: "Tell us of the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him." She said: "Which of his affairs was not wondrous?" — the ḥadīth concerning his weeping in the night prayer. It was transmitted by Abū al-Shaykh Ibn Ḥibbān in the book *Akhlāq Rasūl Allāh* — peace be upon him — and via the path of Ibn al-Jawzī in *al-Wafā*. In its chain is Abū Jināb, whose name is Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ḥabbah, whom the majority have declared weak. Ibn Ḥibbān narrated it in his *Ṣaḥīḥ* from the narration of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān from ʿAṭāʾ, without her saying "Which of his affairs was not wondrous?" It is also found in Muslim from the narration of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah, restricted to the end of the ḥadīth.)

This indicates that weeping ought never to cease. And to this secret points what has been related: that one of the prophets passed by a small stone from which abundant water issued forth, and he marveled at it. God caused it to speak, and it said: "Since I heard the saying of God — exalted be He — {«وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ»} ('whose fuel is men and stones'), I weep out of fear of Him." He asked it to intercede for him against the Fire, and it was granted protection. Then he saw it after a time in the same state and said: "Why do you weep now?" It said: "That was the weeping of fear, and this is the weeping of gratitude and joy."

The heart of the servant is like stones, or even harder in hardness, and its hardness does not depart except through weeping in both states — fear and gratitude alike. It is also related from him — peace be upon him — that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection a caller will cry: 'Let the praisers (al-ḥammādūn) arise!' A group will rise, a banner will be erected for them, and they will enter Paradise." It was said: "And who are the praisers?" He said: "Those who thank God in every state." (The ḥadīth "Praise is the cloak of the Merciful" — I have found no basis for it. In the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah: "Pride is His cloak" — the ḥadīth — and it has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.)

And God revealed to Job (Ayyūb) — peace be upon him — in a lengthy discourse: "I have accepted gratitude as recompense from My beloved ones." And God also revealed to him concerning the description of the patient: "Their abode is the Abode of Peace; when they enter it, I inspire them with gratitude, which is the best of speech. And upon gratitude I increase them, and by looking at Me I augment them."

When the verses concerning treasures (al-kunūz) were revealed, ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — said: "Which wealth should we take?" He — peace be upon him — said: "Let each of you take a remembering tongue and a grateful heart." (The ḥadīth of ʿUmar: "Let each of you take a remembering tongue and a grateful heart" — it has preceded in the Book of Marriage.) Thus he commanded the acquisition of a grateful heart in place of wealth.

And Ibn Masʿūd said: "Gratitude is half of faith."

#### Clarification of the Definition (ḥadd) of Gratitude and Its True Nature

chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن الشكر من جملة مقامات السالكين وهو أيضا ينتظم من علم وحال وعمل
فالعلم هو الأصل فيورث الحال والحال يورث العمل فأما العلم فهو معرفة
النعمة من المنعم والحال هو الفرح الحاصل بإنعامه والعمل هو القيام بما هو
مقصود المنعم ومحبوبه ويتعلق ذلك العمل بالقلب وبالجوارح وباللسان ولا بد
من بيان جميع ذلك ليحصل بمجموعه الإحاطة بحقيقة الشكر فإن كل ما قيل في حد
الشكر قاصر عن الإحاطة بكمال معانيه PageV04P081
فالأصل الأول العلم وهو علم بثلاثة أمور بعين النعمة ووجه كونها نعمة في
حقه وبذات المنعم ووجود صفاته التي بها يتم الإنعام ويصدر الإنعام منه عليه
فإنه لا بد من نعمة ومنعم ومنعم عليه تصل إليه النعمة من المنعم بقصد
وإرادة فهذه الأمور لا بد من معرفتها هذا في حق غير الله تعالى فأما في حق
الله تعالى فلا يتم إلا بأن يعرف أن النعم كلها من الله وهو المنعم
والوسائط مسخرون من جهته
وهذه المعرفة وراء التوحيد والتقديس إذ دخل التقديس والتوحيد فيها بل
الرتبة الأولى في معارف الإيمان التقديس ثم إذا عرف ذاتا مقدسة فيعرف أنه
لا مقدس إلا واحد وما عداه غير مقدس وهو التوحيد ثم يعلم أن كل ما في
العالم فهو موجود من ذلك الواحد فقط فالكل نعمة منه فتقع هذه المعرفة في
الرتبة الثالثة إذ ينطوي فيها مع التقديس والتوحيد كمال القدرة والانفراد
بالفعل وعن هذا عبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  حيث قال من قال سبحان
الله فله عشر حسنات ومن قال لا إله إلا الله فله عشرون حسنة ومن قال الحمد
لله فله ثلاثون حسنة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل الذكر لا إله إلا
الله وأفضل الدعاء الحمد لله (2) وقال ليس شيء من الأذكار يضاعف ما يضاعف
الحمد لله (3) ولاتظنن أن هذه الحسنات بإزاء تحريك اللسان بهذه الكلمات من
غير حصول معانيها في القلب فسبحان الله كلمة تدل على التقديس ولا إله إلا
الله كلمة تدل على التوحيد والحمد لله كلمة تدل على النعمة من الواحد الحق
فالحسنات بإزاء هذه المعارف التي هي من أبواب الإيمان واليقين
واعلم أن تمام هذه المعرفة بنفي الشرك في الأفعال فمن أنعم عليه ملك من
الملوك بشيء فإن رأى لوزيره أو وكيله دخلا في تيسير ذلك وإيصاله إليه فهو
إشراك به في النعمة فلا يرى النعمة من الملك من كل وجه بل منه بوجه ومن
غيره بوجه فيتوزع فرحه عليهما فلا يكون موحدا في حق الملك نعم لا يغض من
توحيده في حق الملك وكمال شكره أن يرى النعمة الواصلة إليه بتوقيعه الذي
كتبه بقلمه وبالكاغد الذي كتبه عليه فإنه لا يفرح بالقلم والكاغد ولا
يشكرهما لأنه لا يثبت لهما دخلا من حيث هما موجودان بأنفسهما بل من حيث هما
مسخران تحت قدرة الملك وقد يعلم أن الوكيل الموصل والخازن أيضا مضطران من
جهة الملك في الإيصال وأنه لو رد الأمر إليه ولم يكن من جهة الملك ارهاق
وامر جزم يخاف عاقبته لما سلم إليه شيئا فإذا عرف ذلك كان نظره إلى الخازن
الموصل كنظره إلى القلم والكاغد فلا يورث ذلك شركا في توحيده من اضافة
النعمة اليه إلى الملك
وكذلك من الكاتب وأن الحيوانات التي لها اختيار مسخرات في نفس اختيارها
فإن الله تعالى هو المسلط للدواعي عليها لتفعل شاءت أم أبت كالخازن المضطر
الذي لا يجد سبيلا إلى مخالفة الملك ولو خلي ونفسه لما اعطاك ذروة مما في
يده فكل من  وصل إليك نعمة من الله تعالى على يده فهو مضطر إذ سلط الله عليه
الإرادة وهيج عليه الدواعي وألقى في نفسه أن خيره في الدنيا والآخرة أن
يعطيك ما أعطاك وأن غرضه المقصود عنده في الحال والمآل لا يحصل إلا به وبعد
أن خلق الله له هذا الاعتقاد لا يجد سبيل إلى تركه فهو إذن إنما يعطيك
PageV04P082
لغرض نفسه لا لغرضك ولو لم يكن غرضه في العطاء لما أعطاك ولو لم يعلم أن
منفعته في منفعتك لما نفعك فهو إذن إنما يطلب نفع نفسه بنفعك فليس منعما
عليك بل اتخذك وسبيله إلى نعمة أخرى وهو يرجوها وإنما الذي أنعم عليك هو
الذي سخره لك وألقى في قلبه من الاعتقادات والإرادات ما صار به مضطرا إلى
الإيصال إليك فإن عرفت الأمور كذلك فقد عرفت الله تعالى وعرفت فعله وكنت
موحدا وقدرت على شكره بل كنت بهذه المعرفة بمجردها شاكرا
ولذلك قال موسى عليه السلام في مناجاته إلهي خلقت آدم بيدك وفعلت وفعلت
فكيف شكرك فقال الله عز وجل علم أن كل ذلك مني فكانت معرفته شكرا
فإذن لا تشكر إلا بأن تعرف أن الكل منه فإن خالجك ريب في هذا لم تكن
عارفا لا بالنعمة ولا بالمنعم فلا تفرح بالمنعم وحده بل وبغيره فبنقصان
معرفتك ينقص حالك في الفرح وبنقصان فرحك ينقص عملك فهذا بيان هذا الأصل
الأصل الثاني الحال المستمدة من أصل المعرفة وهو الفرح بالمنعم مع هيئة
الخضوع والتواضعوهو أيضا في نفسه شكر على تجرده كما أن المعرفة شكر ولكن
إنما يكون شكرا إذا كان حاويا شرطه وشرطه أن يكون فرحك بالمنعم لا بالنعمة
ولا بالإنعام ولعل هذا يتعذر عليك فهمه فنضرب لك مثلا فنقول الملك الذي
يريد الخروج الى سفره فأنعم بفرس على انسانيتصور أن يفرح المنعم عليه
بالفرس من ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أن يفرح بالفرس من حيث أنه فرس وإنه مال ينتفع
به ومركوب يوافق غرضه وإنه جواد نفيس وهذ فرح من لاحظ له في الملك بل  غرضه
الفرس فقط ولو وجده في صحراء فأخذه لكان فرحه مثل ذلك الفرح الوجه الثاني
أن يفرح به لا من حيث إنه فرس بل من حيث تستدل به على عناية الملك به
وشفقته عليه واهتمامه بجانبه لو وجد هذا الفرس في صحراء أو أعطاه غير الملك
لكان لا يفرح به أصلا لاستغنائه عن الفرس أصلا أو استحقاره له بالاضافة الى
مطلوبه من نيل المحل في قلب الملك الوجه الثالث أن يفرح به ليركبه ليخرج في
خدمة الملك ويتحمل مشقة السفر لينال بخدمته القرب منه وربما يرتقي إلى درجة
الوزارة من حيث إنه ليس يقنع بأن يكون محله في قلب الملك أن يعطيه فرسا
ويعتني به هذا القدر من العناية بل هو طالب لأن لا ينعم الملك بشيء من ماله
على أحد إلا بواسطته ثم إنه ليس يريد من الوزارة الوزارة بل يريد مشاهدة
الملك والقرب منه حتى لو خير بين القرب منه دون الوزارة وبين الوزارة دون
القرب لاختار القرب فهذه ثلاث درجات فالأولى لا يدخل فيها معنى الشكر أصلا
لأن نظر صاحبها مقصور على الفرس ففرحه بالفرس لا بالمعطى وهذا حال كل من
فرح بنعمة من حيث إنها لذيذة وموافقة لغرضه فهو بعيد عن معنى الشكر
والثانية داخلة في معنى الشكر من حيث إنه فرح بالمنعم ولكن لا من حيث ذاته
بل من حيث معرفة عنايته التي تستحثه على الإنعام في المستقبل وهذا حال
الصالحين الذين يعبدون الله ويشكرونه خوفا من عقابه ورجاء لثوابه وإنما
الشكر التام في الفرح الثالث وهو أن يكون فرح العبد بنعمة الله تعالى من
حيث إنه يقدر بها على التوصل إلى القرب منه تعالى والنزول في جواره والنظر
إلى وجهه على الدوام فهذا هو الرتبة العليا وأمارته ان لايفرح من الدنيا
إلا بما هو مزرعة للآخرة ويعينه عليها ويحزن بكل نعمة تلهيه عن ذكر الله
تعالى وتصده عن سبيله لأنه ليس يريد النعمة لأنها لذيذة كما يريد صاحب
الفرس لانه جواد ومهملج بل من  حيث إنه يحمله في صحبة الملك حتى تدوم
مشاهدته له وقربه منه ولذلك قال الشبلي رحمه الله الشكر رؤية المنعم
PageV04P083
لا رؤية النعمة وقال الخواص رحمه الله شكر العامة على المطعم والملبس
والمشرب وشكر الخاصة على واردات القلوب وهذه رتبة لا يدركها كل من انحصرت
عنده اللذات في البطن والفرج ومدركات الحواس من الألوان والأصوات وخلا عن
لذة القلب فإن القلب لا يلتذ في حال الصحة إلا بذكر الله تعالى ومعرفته
ولقائه وإنما يلتذ بغيره إذا مرض بسوء العادات كما يلتذ بعض الناس بأكل
الطين وكما يستبشع بعض المرضى الأشياء الحلوة ويستحلي الأشياء المرة كما
قيل
ومن يك ذا فم مر مريض ... جد مرا به الماء الزلالا
فإذن هذا شرط الفرح بنعمة الله تعالى فإن لم تكن إبل فمعزى فإن لم يكن
هذا فالدرجة الثانية أما الأولى فخارجة عن كل حساب فكم من فرق بين من يريد

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes acknowledgment of beneficence, the "opening" or "unveiling" of a favor; it carries the sense of a plant flourishing from irrigation — gratitude as the growth of the soul through recognition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Gratitude (shukr) is the perception of the benefaction (niʿmah) and its display; it is the counterpart of praise (ḥamd) — the former tied to the recipient's recognition, the latter to the giver's worthiness. It is a comprehensive term uniting knowledge (maʿrifah), state (ḥāl), and action (ʿamal).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage (ḥaqīqah) applies to verbal acknowledgment with humility; metaphorical usage (majāz) extends to the heart's state and bodily acts, as in "I thank you" meaning "I acknowledge your precedence."
- Root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, ease, and well-being; the state of living in pleasant conditions; also the act of bestowing a favor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Niʿmah is the voluntary bestowal of benefit by another upon oneself, requiring a giver (munʿim), a recipient (munʿam ʿalayh), and the benefaction itself; in the divine context, all existence is niʿmah from Allah alone.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tangible goods; metaphorical for spiritual graces like guidance and knowledge, as in the Quranic {وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً}.
- Root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Joy and delight; the opposite of sorrow; a state of the heart upon attaining what is beloved.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Farah in the praiseworthy sense is joy in Allah and His bounty; blameworthy joy is delight in worldly goods that distract from Him, as censured in {لَا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the heart's expansion; metaphorical for the outward signs of contentment and submission.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When al-Ghazali lists "from knowledge, state, and action" (من علم وحال وعمل), the conjunction binds coordinate nouns in a sequence of causal generation (tawālud), each term clarifying the preceding as its necessary outcome, requiring the translator to preserve the logical progression: knowledge begets state, state begets action.
chapters.translation:
Know that gratitude (shukr) is among the stations (maqāmāt) of the wayfarers [on the path to God], and it is likewise composed of knowledge (ʿilm), a state (ḥāl), and action (ʿamal). Knowledge is the root, and it engenders the state; the state engenders action. As for knowledge, it is the recognition of the benefaction (niʿmah) from the Benefactor (al-Munʿim). The state is the joy (farah) that arises from His bestowal. The action is the performance of what the Benefactor intends and loves. This action pertains to the heart, the bodily members (jawāriḥ), and the tongue. It is necessary to elucidate all of this so that, through its totality, one may attain comprehensive grasp of the reality of gratitude — for everything that has been said in defining gratitude falls short of encompassing the fullness of its meanings.

**The First Root: Knowledge**

Knowledge concerns three matters: the essence of the benefaction, the aspect by which it is a benefaction for the recipient, and the essence of the Benefactor with the attributes through which the bestowal is perfected and from which it issues upon him. For there must necessarily be a benefaction, a benefactor, and a recipient to whom the benefaction reaches from the benefactor by intent (qaṣd) and will (irādah). These matters must be known. This applies in the case of other than Allah — but in the case of Allah, may He be exalted, it is only complete when one knows that all benefactions are from Allah, that He is the Benefactor, and that the intermediaries are subjugated (musakhkharūn) from His direction.

This knowledge lies beyond tawḥīd (divine unity) and tanzīh (transcendence), for transcendence and unity are subsumed within it. Rather, the first rank in the cognitions of faith is tanzīh — declaring God's transcendence. Then, when one knows a transcendent Essence, one knows that nothing is transcendent except the One, and whatever is other than Him is not transcendent — this is tawḥīd. Then one knows that everything in the world exists from that One alone — so all is a benefaction from Him. This knowledge falls in the third rank, for it encompasses, along with transcendence and unity, the perfection of power (kamāl al-qudrah) and His exclusive agency in action (al-infirād bi-l-fiʿl). It is concerning this that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever says 'Subḥān Allāh' (Glory be to God) has ten good deeds; whoever says 'Lā ilāha illā Allāh' (There is no god but God) has twenty good deeds; and whoever says 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh' (Praise be to God) has thirty good deeds." And he said, peace be upon him: "The best remembrance is 'Lā ilāha illā Allāh,' and the best supplication is 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh.'" And he said: "There is no remembrance whose reward is multiplied as is multiplied the reward of 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh.'" Do not suppose that these good deeds are in exchange for merely moving the tongue with these words without the realization of their meanings in the heart. For "Subḥān Allāh" is a word indicating tanzīh; "Lā ilāha illā Allāh" is a word indicating tawḥīd; and "Al-ḥamdu lillāh" is a word indicating the benefaction from the One, the True. The good deeds are in exchange for these cognitions, which are among the gates of faith and certainty (īmān wa yaqīn).

Know that the completion of this knowledge lies in negating association (shirk) in acts [of bestowal]. If a king bestows something upon a man, and that man perceives that the king's vizier or agent had a role in facilitating it and delivering it to him, then this is association with the king in the benefaction. He would then not see the benefaction as from the king in every respect, but from him in one respect and from another in another respect — so his joy would be divided between the two, and he would not be a muwaḥḥid (unifier) with respect to the king. Indeed, this does not diminish his tawḥīd regarding the king. The perfection of his gratitude is that he sees the benefaction reaching him through the king's decree (tawqīʿ) written by his pen and upon the paper on which it was written — for he does not rejoice in the pen and paper, nor thank them, because he does not attribute to them any role in themselves as independently existing things, but rather as subjugated under the king's power. He may also know that the delivering agent and the treasurer are likewise compelled (muḍṭarrān) by the king's authority in delivering, and that if the matter were left to them without the king's command — a decisive command whose consequence they fear — they would not surrender anything to him. When he knows this, his view of the delivering treasurer becomes like his view of the pen and paper — this does not engender any association in his tawḥīd by attributing the benefaction to other than the king.

Likewise is the case with the scribe and with animals that possess choice (ikhtiyār) — they are subjugated in their very choosing. For Allah, may He be exalted, is the One who empowers the motives (dawāʿī) upon them so that they act whether they will or not — like the compelled treasurer who finds no way to oppose the king, and who, if left to himself, would not give you a speck of what is in his hand. So whoever conveys a benefaction to you from Allah, may He be exalted, at his hand is compelled: Allah has empowered the will upon him, stirred the motives within him, and cast into his soul that his good in this world and the next lies in giving you what he gave, and that his intended purpose in the present and the future is not attained except through it. And after Allah has created this conviction in him, he finds no way to abandon it. He therefore gives you only for his own purpose, not for yours. Had he no purpose in giving, he would not give; and had he not known that his benefit lies in your benefit, he would not benefit you. He is thus seeking his own benefit through your benefit — he is not a benefactor to you, but rather has taken you as a means to another benefaction he hopes for. The One who has truly bestowed upon you is the One who subjugated him to you and cast into his heart the convictions and volitions by which he became compelled to deliver to you. If you know matters thus, you have known Allah, may He be exalted, and known His act, and you are a muwaḥḥid, and you are capable of gratitude — nay, by this knowledge alone you are grateful.

For this reason, Moses, peace be upon him, said in his intimate supplication (munājāh): "My God, You created Adam with Your hand, and You did such and such — how then did he thank You?" Allah, may He be exalted, said: "He knew that all of that was from Me — so his knowledge was gratitude."

Therefore, you do not give thanks except by knowing that all is from Him. If any doubt assails you in this, you are not cognizant — neither of the benefaction nor of the Benefactor — so you do not rejoice in the Benefactor alone, but in other than Him as well. By the deficiency of your knowledge, your state of joy diminishes; and by the deficiency of your joy, your action diminishes. This is the elucidation of this root.

**The Second Root: The State**

The state derived from the root of knowledge is joy in the Benefactor, accompanied by the bearing of humility (khushūʿ) and lowliness (tawāḍuʿ). This state is itself gratitude in its bare form, just as knowledge is gratitude. But it is only gratitude when it encompasses its condition — and its condition is that your joy be in the Benefactor, not in the benefaction nor in the bestowal. Perhaps this will be difficult for you to understand, so we shall give you an example. We say: A king who wishes to set out on a journey bestows a horse upon a man. The recipient may rejoice in the horse in three ways. First: he rejoices in the horse insofar as it is a horse — wealth to be used, a mount suited to his purpose, a noble and precious steed. This is the joy of one who has no regard for the king at all; his purpose is the horse alone. Had he found it in a desert and taken it, his joy would have been the same. Second: he rejoices in it not insofar as it is a horse, but insofar as it indicates the king's care for him, his compassion toward him, and his concern for his welfare. Had he found this horse in a desert, or had someone other than the king given it to him, he would not rejoice in it at all — either because he has no need of a horse, or because he deems it insignificant relative to what he seeks, namely attaining a place in the king's heart. Third: he rejoices in it in order to ride it in the king's service, enduring the hardship of travel so that through his service he may attain closeness (qurb) to him — and perhaps rise to the rank of vizier — for he is not content that his place in the king's heart be such that the king gives him a horse and shows this measure of care. Rather, he seeks that the king bestow nothing of his wealth upon anyone except through his mediation. Yet he does not desire the vizierate for its own sake, but desires the vision of the king and closeness to him — so that were he given the choice between closeness without the vizierate and the vizierate without closeness, he would choose closeness.

These are three degrees. The first does not enter into the meaning of gratitude at all, for its possessor's gaze is confined to the horse — his joy is in the horse, not in the giver. This is the state of everyone who rejoices in a benefaction insofar as it is pleasurable and suited to his purpose — he is far from the meaning of gratitude. The second enters into the meaning of gratitude insofar as he rejoices in the Benefactor — but not in His essence, rather in His known care that urges Him to bestow in the future. This is the state of the righteous (ṣāliḥūn) who worship Allah and thank Him out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. Complete gratitude lies only in the third joy: that the servant's joy in Allah's benefaction be insofar as it enables him to attain closeness to Him, may He be exalted, to descend in His vicinity, and to gaze upon His Face perpetually. This is the highest rank. Its sign is that he rejoices in this world only in what is a sowing-field (mazraʿah) for the Hereafter and aids him toward it, and grieves over every benefaction that distracts him from the remembrance of Allah, may He be exalted, and turns him from His path. For he does not desire the benefaction because it is pleasurable — as the horse's owner desires it because it is noble and ambling — but insofar as it carries him in the king's company so that his vision of him and closeness to him may endure. For this reason, al-Shiblī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Gratitude is the vision of the Benefactor, not the vision of the benefaction." And al-Khawwāṣ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The gratitude of the common folk is for food, clothing, and drink; the gratitude of the elite is for what descends upon the hearts." This is a rank not attained by everyone whose pleasures are confined to the belly and the loins and the perceptions of the senses — colors and sounds — and who is devoid of the heart's pleasure. For the heart takes pleasure, in its sound state, only in the remembrance of Allah, may He be exalted, in knowing Him, and in meeting Him. It takes pleasure in other than Him only when it is diseased by evil habits — just as some people enjoy eating clay, and as some sick persons find sweet things bitter and bitter things sweet, as was said:

*"Whoever has a bitter, diseased mouth — even clear water tastes bitter to him."*

So this is the condition of joy in Allah's benefaction. If you have no camels, then sheep will do — if this [highest rank] is not attained, then the second degree [suffices]. As for the first, it is entirely out of account. How great is the difference between one who wants the king for the horse and one who wants the horse for the king! And how great is the difference between one who wants Allah to bestow upon him, and one who wants Allah's bounties in order to reach Him through them!

**The Third Root: Action**

Action is the performance of what the joy arising from knowledge of the Benefactor requires. This action pertains to the heart, the tongue, and the bodily members. As for the heart: intending good and concealing it for all creatures. As for the tongue: manifesting gratitude to Allah, may He be exalted, through the praises (taḥmīdāt) that indicate Him. As for the bodily members: employing Allah's benefactions in His obedience and guarding against using them in His disobedience — so much so that the gratitude of the two eyes is to conceal every fault you see in a Muslim, and the gratitude of the two ears is to conceal every fault you hear about him. This enters into the totality of gratitude for Allah's benefactions through these organs.

Gratitude by the tongue is the manifestation of contentment (riḍā) with Allah, may He be exalted, and it is commanded. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a man: "How have you arisen?" The man said: "In goodness." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, repeated the question until, on the third time, the man said: "In goodness — I praise Allah and thank Him." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "This is what I wanted from you." [Hadith — recorded by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, raised to the Prophet, with a similar wording; in the third instance he said "I praise Allah" — this is muʿḍal (broken chain). It is also recorded in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr without the repetition of the question, with the wording "I praise Allah to You" — and in it is Rāshid ibn Saʿd, whom the majority weakened for poor memory. Mālik recorded it in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ as a saying of ʿUmar (mawqūf) with a sound chain.] The Salaf (early Muslims) used to ask one another [about their states] with the intention of eliciting gratitude to Allah, may He be exalted — so that the one giving thanks would be obedient, and the one eliciting the thanks would also be obedient. Their intention was not ostentation (riyāʾ) by displaying longing. Every servant asked about his state is between thanking and complaining — or remaining silent. For gratitude is obedience, and complaint is a disobedience — ugly from the people of religion. How could complaint not be ugly — from the King of Kings, in Whose hand is everything, to a possessed servant who has no power over anything? It is more fitting for the servant, if he cannot bear affliction and decree well, and weakness drives him to complaint, that his complaint be to Allah — for He is the Afflicter and the One able to remove affliction. The servant's abasement before his Master is glory; complaint to other than Him is abasement; and displaying abasement to a servant who is a fellow servant is ugly abasement. Allah, may He be exalted, says: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقًا فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ} — "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and thank Him." And He says: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ} — "Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like yourselves." So gratitude by the tongue is part of gratitude.

It is related that a delegation came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allah have mercy on him, and a young man stood up to speak. ʿUmar said: "The elder, the elder!" The young man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if the matter were by age, there are among the Muslims those more deserving of silence than you." He said: "Speak." He said: "We are not a delegation of desire (raghbah) nor a delegation of fear (rahbah). As for desire, your virtue has conveyed it to us; as for fear, your justice has made us secure from it. Rather, we are a delegation of gratitude — we have come to thank you with our tongues, and we shall depart." These, then, are the roots of the meanings of gratitude that encompass the totality of its reality.

As for the one who said that gratitude is the acknowledgment of the Benefactor's benefaction in a manner of humility — he looked to the act of the tongue with some states of the heart. The one who said that gratitude is praise of the benefactor by mentioning his beneficence — he looked to the mere act of the tongue. The one who said that gratitude is remaining upon the carpet of witnessing (bisāṭ al-shuhūd) with the perpetual preservation of reverence (ḥurmah) — he gathered most of the meanings of gratitude, omitting only the act of the tongue. The saying of Ḥamdūn al-Qaṣṣār — "The gratitude for a benefaction is that you see yourself in your gratitude as a mere appendage (ṭufaylī)" — is an indication that the meaning of knowledge is among the meanings of gratitude only. The saying of al-Junayd — "Gratitude is that you do not see yourself as worthy of the benefaction" — is an indication of one of the heart's states in particular. These sayings express their [respective] states — therefore their answers differ and do not agree. Moreover, the answer of each one may differ across two states, for they speak only from their prevailing present state, occupied with what concerns them to the exclusion of what does not — or they speak of what they deem fitting to the questioner's state, confining themselves to the measure of what he needs and turning away from what he does not need. So do not suppose that what we have mentioned constitutes an attack upon them, or that were all the meanings we have explained presented to them, they would deny them. No — no rational person would suppose this at all, unless a dispute arises concerning the lexical usage (waḍʿ al-lisān) of the name "gratitude" — whether it encompasses all these meanings or denotes some of them as its primary intent while the rest are its concomitants and necessary consequences. But we do not intend in this book to explain the lexical conventions of languages — that is not part of the science of the path to the Hereafter in any way. And Allah is the Granter of success, by His mercy.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Method of Unveiling the Veil Concerning Gratitude (Shukr) Toward God Most High
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||||| بيان طريق كشف الغطاء عن الشكر في حق الله تعالى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ش-ف (kashafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To remove, uncover, or disclose what is hidden; lifting a covering (kiswah) from a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Unveiling of the unseen realities (ghayb) through divine illumination, often contrasted with mere sensory perception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical removal of a veil; metaphorical (majāz) = intellectual or spiritual disclosure of truth.
- Root: غ-ط-ي (ghaṭā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling, or obscuring; the act of concealing from sight or understanding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The veil of ignorance or heedlessness that obstructs the heart's perception of divine realities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical covering; metaphorical = the veil of worldly attachment or self-conceit.
- Root: ش-ك-ر (shakara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Recognition of beneficence (niʿmah) and its acknowledgment through praise or action; the opposite of kufr (ingratitude).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Gratitude as a tripartite act—of the heart (perception), tongue (praise), and limbs (obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = verbal acknowledgment; metaphorical = the soul's submission and the body's service in response to divine favor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Idāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase "kashf al-ghitāʾ" (unveiling of the veil) employs a genitive annexation where the first term (kashf) is a verbal noun governing the second (ghitāʾ) as its object, indicating the act of removal is directed upon the covering itself.
chapters.translation: I say: Know—may God grant you success—that the unveiling of the veil concerning gratitude (shukr) toward God Most High is a matter of profound subtlety, for the common folk imagine it to be merely the utterance of praise upon the tongue, or the performance of certain bodily acts of worship. Yet the reality of gratitude is far deeper than this, and its true nature is only disclosed to those whose hearts God has illuminated with the light of discernment (baṣīrah). For gratitude is not complete unless it combines three stations: the station of knowledge (maʿrifah), the station of state (ḥāl), and the station of action (ʿamal). The knowledge is that the benefactor is God alone, the state is the joy and love of the heart toward Him, and the action is the obedience of the limbs in service to Him. Thus, whoever perceives the Benefactor with his intellect, loves Him with his heart, and serves Him with his limbs—he is the one who has truly unveiled the covering of gratitude, and has attained its reality in this world and its reward in the Hereafter.

chapters.title_en: The Reality of Gratitude and the Vision of Pure Unity (Tawḥīd)
chapters.arabic_text:
لعل يخطر ببالك أن الشكر إنما يفعل في حق منعم هو صاحب حظ في الشكر فإنا
نشكر الملوك إما بالثناء ليزيد محلهم في القلوب ويظهر كرمهم عند الناس
فيزيد به صيتهم وجاههم أو بالخدمة التي هي إعانة لهم على بعض أغراضهم أو
بالمثول بين أيديهم في صورة الخدم وذلك تكثير لسوادهم وسبب لزيادة جاههم
فلا يكونون شاكرين لهم إلا بشيء من ذلك وهذا محال في حق الله تعالى من
وجهين أحدهما أن الله تعالى منزه عن الحظوظ والأغراض مقدس عن الحاجة إلى
الخدمة والإعانة وعن نشر الجاه والحشمة بالثناء والإطراء وعن تكثير سواد
الخدم بالمثول بين يديه ركعا سجدا فشكرنا إياه بما لا حظ  فيه يضاهي شكرنا
الملك المنعم علينا بأن ننام في بيوتنا أو نسجد أو نركع إذ لا حظ للملك فيه
وهو غائب لا علم له ولا حظ لله تعالى في أفعالنا كلها الوجه الثاني أن كل
ما نتعاطاه باختيارنا فهو نعمة أخرى من نعم الله علينا إذ جوارحنا وقدرتنا
وإرادتنا وداعيتنا وسائر الأمور التي هي أسباب حركتنا ونفس حركتنا من خلق
الله تعالى ونعمته فكيف نشكر نعمة بنعمة ولو أعطانا الملك مركوبا فأخذنا
مركوبا آخر له وركبناه أو أعطانا الملك مركوبا آخر لم يكن الثاني شكر للأول
منا بل كان الثاني يحتاج إلى شكر كما يحتاج الأول ثم لا يمكن شكر الشكر الا
بنعة أخرى فيؤدي إلى أن يكون الشكر محالا في حق الله تعالى من هذين الوجهين
ولسنا نشك في الامرين جميعا والشرع قد ورد به فكيف السبيل إلى الجمع فاعلم
أن هذا الخاطر قد خطر لداود عليه السلام وكذلك لموسى عليه السلام فقال يا
رب كيف أشكرك وأنا لا أستطيع أن أشكرك إلا بنعمة ثانية من نعمك وفي لفظ آخر
وشكري لك نعمة أخرى منك توجب على الشكر لك فأوحى الله تعالى إليه إذا عرفت
هذا فقد شكرتني وفي خبر آخر إذا عرفت أن النعمة مني رضيت منك بذلك شكرا
فإن قلت فقد فهمت السؤال وفهمي قاصر عن إدراك معنى ما أوحى إليهم فإني
أعلم استحالة الشكر لله تعالى فأما كون العلم باستحالة الشكر شكرا فلا
أفهمه فإن هذا العلم أيضا نعمة منه فكيف صار شكرا وكأن الحاصل يرجع إلى أن
من لم يشكر فقد شكر وأن قبول الخلعة الثانية من الملك شكر للخلعة الأولى
والفهم قاصر عن درك السر فيه فإن أمكن تعريف ذلك بمثال فهو مهم في نفسه
فاعلم أن هذا قرع باب من المعارف وهي أعلى
PageV04P085
من علوم المعاملة ولكنا نشير منها إلى ملامح ونقول ههنا نظران نظر بعين
التوحيد المحض وهذا النظر يعرفك قطعا أنه الشاكر وأنه المشكور وأنه المحب
وأنه المحبوب وهذا نظر من  عرف أنه ليس في الوجود غيره وأن كل شيء هالك إلا
وجهه وأن ذلك صدق في كل حال أزلا وأبدا لأن الغير هو الذي يتصور أن يكون له
بنفسه قوام ومثل هذا الغير لا وجود له بل هو محال أن يوجد إذ الموجود
المحقق هو القائم بنفسه وما ليس له بنفسه قوام فليس له بنفسه وجود بل هو
قائم بغيره فهو موجود بغيره فإن اعتبر ذاته ولم يلتفت إلى غيره لم يكن له
وجود البتة وإنما الموجود هو القائم بنفسه والقائم بنفسه هو الذي لو قدر
عدم غيره بقي موجودا فإن كان مع قيامه بنفسه يقوم بوجوده وجود غيره فهو
قيوم ولا قيوم إلا واحد ولا يتصور أن يكون غير ذلك فإذن ليس في الوجود غير
الحي القيوم وهو الواحد الصمد فإذا نظرت من هذا المقام عرفت أن الكل منه
مصدره وإليه مرجعه فهو الشاكر وهو المشكور وهو المحب وهو المحبوب ومن ههنا
نظر حبيب بن أبي حبيب حيث قرأ {إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب} فقال
واعجباه أعطى وأثنى إشارة إلى أنه إذا أثنى على إعطائه فعلى نفسه أثنى فهو
المثني وهو المثني عليه ومن ههنا نظر الشيخ أبو سعيد المهينى حيث قرىء بين
يديه {يحبهم ويحبونه} فقال لعمري يحبهم ودعه يحبهم فبحق يحبهم لأنه إنما
يحب نفسه أشار به إلى أنه المحب وأنه المحبوب وهذه رتبة عالية لا تفهمها
إلا بمثال على حد عقلك فلا يخفى عليك أن المصنف إذا أحب تصنيفه لقد أحب
نفسه والصانع إذا أحب صنعته فقد أحب نفسه والوالد إذا أحب ولده من حيث إنه
ولده فقد أحب نفسه وكل ما في الوجود سوى الله تعالى فهو تصنيف الله تعالى
وصنعته فإن أحبه فما أحب إلا نفسه وإذا لم يحب الانفسه فبحق أحب ما أحب
وهذا ما أحب وهذا كله نظر بعين التوحيد وتعبر الصوفية عن هذه الحالة بفناء
النفس أي فني عن نفسه وعن غير الله فلم ير إلا الله تعالى فمن  لم يفهم هذا
ينكر عليهم ويقول كيف فني وطول ظله أربعة أذرع ولعله يأكل في كل يوم أرطالا
من الخبز فيضحك عليهم الجهال لجهلهم بمعاني كلامهم وضرورة قول العارفين أن
يكونوا ضحكة للجاهلين وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من
الذين آمنوا يضحكون وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا
فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين ثم بين أن
ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا أعظم إذ قال تعالى {فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار
يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون} وكذلك أمة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه
عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال {إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون}
فهذا أحد النظرين النظر الثاني نظر من لم يبلغ إلى مقام الفناء عن نفسه
وهؤلاء قسمان قسم لم يثبتوا إلا وجود أنفسهم وأنكروا أن يكون لهم رب يعبد
وهؤلاء هم العميان المنكوسون وعماهم في كلتا العينين لأنهم نفوا ما هو
الثابت تحقيقا وهو القيوم الذي هو قائم بنفسه وقائم على كل نفس بما كسبت
وكل قائم فقائم به ولم يقتصروا على هذا حتى أثبتوا أنفسهم ولو عرفوا لعلموا
أنهم من حيث هم هم لا ثبات لهم ولا وجود لهم وإنما وجودهم من حيث أوجدوا لا
من حيث وجدوا وفرق بين الموجود وبين الموجد وليس في الوجود إلا موجود واحد
وموجد فالموجود حق والموجد باطل من حيث هو هو والموجود قائم وقيوم والموجد
هالك وفان وإذا كان كل من عليها فان فلا يبقى إلا وجه ربك ذو الجلال
والإكرام الفريق الثاني ليس بهم عمى ولكن بهم عور لأنهم يبصرون بإحدى
العينين وجود الموجود الحق فلا ينكرونه والعين الأخرى إن تم عماها لم يبصر
بها فناء غير الموجود الحق فأثبت موجودا آخر مع الله تعالى وهذا مشرك
تحقيقا كما
PageV04P086
أن الذي قبله جاحد تحقيقا فإن جاوز حد العمى إلى العمش أدرك تفاوتا بين
الموجودين فأثبت عبدا وربا فبهذا القدر من إثبات التفاوت والنقص من الموجود
الآخر  دخل في حد التوحيد ثم إن كحل بصره بما يزيد في أنواره فيقل عمشه
وبقدر ما يزيد في بصره يظهر له نقصان ما أثبته سوى الله تعالى فإن بقي في
سلوكه كذلك فلا يزال يفضي به النقصان إلى المحو فينمحي عن رؤية ما سوى الله
فلا يرى إلا الله ليكون قد بلغ كمال التوحيد وحيث أدرك نقصا في وجود ما سوى
الله تعالى دخل في أوائل التوحيد وبينهما درجات لا تحصى فبهذا تتفاوت درجات
الموحدين وكتب الله المنزلة على ألسنة رسله هي الكحل الذي به يحصل أنوار
الأبصار والأنبياء هم الكحالون وقد جاءوا داعين إلى التوحيد المحض وترجمته
قول لا إله إلا الله ومعناه أن لا يرى إلا الواحد الحق والواصلون إلى كمال
التوحيد هم الأقلون والجاحدون والمشركون أيضا قليلون وهم على الطرف الأقصى
المقابل لطرف التوحيد إذ عبدة الأوثان قالوا {ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى
الله زلفى} فكانوا داخلين في أوائل أبواب التوحيد دخولا ضعيفا والمتوسطون
هم الأكثرون وفيهم من تنفتح بصيرته في بعض الأحوال فتلوح له حقائق التوحيد
ولكن كالبرق الخاطف لا يثبت وفيهم من يلوح له ذلك ويثبت زمانا ولكن لا يدوم
والدوام فيه عزيز
لكل إلى شأو العلا حركات ... ولكن عزيز في الرجال ثبات
ولما أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب القرب فقيل له {واسجد
واقترب} قال في سجوده أعوذ بعفوك من عقابك وأعوذ برضاك من سخطك وأعوذ بك
منك لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (1) حديث إنه ليغان على قلبي
الحديث تقدم في التوبة وقبله في الدعوات فكان ذلك لترقيه إلى سبعين مقاما
بعضها فوق البعض أولها وإن كان مجاوزا أقصى غايات الخلق ولكن كان نقصانا
بالإضافة إلى آخرها فكان استغفاره لذلك ولما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها أليس
قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فما هذا البكاء في السجود وما هذا
الجهد الشديد PageV04P087
{قال} أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا // حديث عائشة لما قالت له غفر  الله لك ما
تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فما هذا البكاء الحديث رواه ابو الشيخ وهو بقية حديث
عطاء عنها المتقدم قبل هذا بتسعة أحاديث وهو عند مسلم من رواية عروة عنها
مختصرا وكذلك هو في الصحيحين مختصرا من حديث المغيرة بن شعبة معناه أفلا
أكون طالبا للمزيد في المقامات فإن الشكر سبب الزيادة حيث قال تعالى {لئن
شكرتم لأزيدنكم}
واذا تغلغنا في بحار المكاشفة فلنقبض العنان ولنرجع إلى ما يليق بعلوم
المعاملة فنقول الأنبياء عليهم السلام بعثوا لدعوة الحق إلى كمال التوحيد
الذي وصفناه ولكن بينهم وبين الوصول إليه مسافة بعيدة وعقبات شديدة وإنما
الشرع كله تعريف طريق سلوك تلك المسافة وقطع تلك العقبات وعند ذلك يكون
النظر عن مشاهدة أخرى ومقام آخر فيظهر في ذلك المقام بإضافة إلى تلك
المشاهدة الشكر والشاكر والمشكور ولا يعرف ذلك إلا بمثال فأقول يمكنك أن
تفهم أن ملكا من الملوك ارسل الى عبد قد بعد منه مركوبا وملبوسا ونقد الاجل
زاده في الطريق حتى يقطع به مسافة البعد ويقرب من حضرة الملك ثم يكون له
حالتان إحداهما أن يكون قصده من وصول العبد إلى حضرته أن يقوم ببعض مهماته
ويكون له عناية في خدمته والثانية أن لا يكون للملك حظ في العبد ولا حاجة
به إليه بل حضوره لا يزيد في ملكه لأنه لا يقوى على القيام بخدمة تغني فيه
غناء وغيبته لا تنقص من ملكه فيكون قصد من الإنعام عليه بالمركوب والزاد أن
يحظى العبد بالقرب منه وينال سعادة حضرته لينتفع هو في نفسه لا لينتفع
الملك به وبانتفاعه فمنزل العباد من الله تعالى في المنزلة الثانية لا في
المنزلة الأولى فإن الأولى محال على الله تعالى والثانية غير محال ثم اعلم
أن العبد لا يكون شاكرا في الحالة الأولى بمجرد الركوب والوصول إلى حضرته
ما لم يقم بخدمته التي أرادها الملك منه وأما في الحالة الثانية فلا يحتاج
إلى الخدمة أصلا ومع ذلك يتصور أن يكون شاكرا وكافرا ويكون شكره  بأن يستعمل
ما أنفذه إليه مولاه فيما أحبه لأجله لا لأجل نفسه وكفره أن لا يستعمل ذلك
فيه بأن يعطله أو يستعمله فيما يزيد في بعده منه فمهما لبس العبد الثوب
وركب الفرس ولم ينفق الزاد إلا في الطريق فقد شكره مولاه إذ استعمل نعمته
في محبته أي فيما أحبه لعبده لا لنفسه وإن ركبه واستدبر حضرته وأخذ يبعد
منه فقد كفر نعمته أي استعملها فيما كرهه مولاه لعبده لا لنفسه وإن جلس ولم
يركب لا في طلب القرب ولا في طلب البعد فقد كفر أيضا نعمته إذا أهملها
وعطلها وإن كان هذا دون ما لو بعد منه فكذلك خلق الله سبحانه الخلق وهم في
ابتداء فطرتهم يحتاجون إلى استعمال الشهوات لتكمل بها أبدانهم فيبعدون بها
عن حضرته وإنما سعادتهم في القرب منه فأعد لهم من النعم ما يقدرون على
استعماله في نيل درجة القرب وعن بعدهم وقربهم عبر الله تعالى إذ قال {لقد
خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا} الآية
فإذن نعم الله تعالى آلات يترقى العبد بها عن أسفل السافلين خلقها الله
تعالى لأجل العبد حتى ينال بها سعادة القرب والله تعالى غني عنه قرب أم بعد
والعبد فيها بين أن يستعملها في الطاعة فيكون قد شكر لموافقة محبة مولاه
وبين أن يستعملها في معصيته فقد كفر لاقتحامه ما يكرهه مولاه ولا يرضاه له
فإن الله لا يرضى لعباده الكفر والمعصية وإن عطلها ولم يستعملها في طاعة
ولا معصية فهو أيضا كفر كفران إن للنعمة بالتضييع وكل ما خلق في الدنيا
إنما خلق آلة للعبد ليتوصل به إلى سعادة الآخرة ونيل القرب من الله تعالى
فكل مطيع فهو بقدر طاعته شاكر نعمة الله في الأسباب التي استعملها في
الطاعة وكل كسلان ترك الاستعمال أو عاص استعملها في طريق البعد فهو كافر
جار في غير محبة الله تعالى فالمعصية والطاعة تشملهما المشيئة ولكن لا
تشملهما المحبة والكراهة بل رب مراد
PageV04P088
محبوب ورب مراد  مكروه ووراء بيان هذه الدقيقة سر القدر الذي منع من
إفشائه وقد انحل بهذا الإشكال الأول وهو أنه إذا لم يكن للمشكور حظ فكيف
يكون الشكر وبهذا أيضا ينحل الثاني فإنا لم نعن بالشكر إلا انصراف نعمة
الله في جهة محبة الله فإذا انصرفت النعمة في جهة المحبة بفعل الله فقد حصل
المراد وفعلك عطاء من الله تعالى ومن حيث أنت محله فقد أثنى عليك وثناؤه
نعمة أخرى منه إليك فهو الذي أعطى وهو الذي أثنى وصار أحد فعليه سببا
لانصراف فعله الثاني إلى جهة محبته فله الشكر على كل حال وأنت موصوف بأنك
شاكر بمعنى أنك محل المعنى الذي الشكر عبارة عنه لا بمعنى أنك موجب له كما
أنك موصوف بأنك عارف وعالم لا بمعنى أنك خالق للعلم وموجده ولكن بمعنى أنك
محل له وقد وجد بالقدرة الأزلية فيك فوصفك بأنك شاكر إثبات شيئية لك وأنت
شيء إذ جعلك خالق الأشياء شيئا وإنما أنت لا شيء إذا كنت أنت ظانا لنفسك
شيئا من ذاتك فأما باعتبار النظر إلى الذي جعل الأشياء شيئا فأنت شيء إذ
جعلك شيئا فإن قطع النظر عن جعله كنت لا شيء تحقيقيا وإلى هذا أشار صلى
الله الله عليه وسلم حيث قال اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له // حديث اعملوا
فكل ميسر لما خلق له من حديث على وعمران بن حصين لما قيل له يا رسول الله
ففيم العمل إذا كانت الأشياء قد فرغ منها من قبل فتبين أن الخلق مجاري قدرة
الله تعالى ومحل أفعاله وإن كانوا هم أيضا من أفعاله ولكن بعض أفعاله محل
للبعض وقوله {اعملوا} وإن كان جاريا على لسان الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه
وآله وسلم فهو فعل من أفعاله وهو سبب لعلم الخلق أن العمل نافع وعلمهم فعل
من أفعال الله تعالى والعلم سبب لانبعاث داعية جازمة إلى الحركة والطاعة
وانبعاث الداعية أيضا من أفعال الله تعالى وهو سبب لحركة الأعضاء وهي أيضا
من أفعال الله تعالى ولكن بعض  أفعاله سبب للبعض أي الأول شرط للثاني كما
كان خلق الجسم سببا لخلق العرض إذ لا يخلق العرض قبله وخلق الحياة شرط لخلق
العلم وخلق العلم شرط لخلق الإرادة والكل من أفعال الله تعالى وبعضها سبب
للبعض أي هو شرط ومعنى كونه شرطا أنه لا يستعد لقبول فعل الحياة إلا جوهر
ولا يستعد لقبول العلم إلا ذو حياة ولا لقبول الارادة الاذو علم فيكون بعض
أفعاله سببا للبعض بهذا المعنى لا بمعنى أن بعض أفعاله موجد لغيره بل ممهد
شرط الحصول لغيره وهذا إذا حقق ارتقى إلى درجة التوحيد الذي ذكرناه
فإن قلت فلم قال الله تعالى اعملوا وإلا فأنتم معاقبون مذمومون على
العصيان وما إلينا شيء فكيف نذم وإنما الكل إلى الله تعالى فاعلم أن هذا
القول من الله تعالى سبب لحصول اعتقاد فينا والاعتقاد سبب لهيجان الخوف
وهيجان الخوف سبب لترك الشهوات والتجافي عن دار الغرور وذلك سبب للوصول إلى
جوار الله والله تعالى مسبب الأسباب ومرتبها فمن سبق له في الأزل السعادة
يسر له هذه الأسباب حتى يقوده بسلسلتها إلى الجنة ويعبر عن مثله بأن كلا
ميسر لما خلق له ومن لم يسبق له من الله الحسنى بعد عن سماع كلام الله
تعالى وكلام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكلام العلماء فإذا لم يسمع لم
يعلم وإذا لم يعلم لم يخف وإذا لم يخف لم يترك الركون إلى الدنيا وإذا لم
يترك الركون إلى الدنيا بقي في حزب الشيطان وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين فإذا
عرفت هذا تعجبت من قوم يقادون إلى الجنة بالسلاسل فما من أحد إلا وهو مقود
الى الجنة بسلاسل الأسباب وهو تسليط العلم والخوف عليه وما من مخذول إلا
وهو مقود إلى النار بالسلاسل وهو تسليط الغفلة والأمن والغرور عليه
فالمتقون يساقون إلى الجنة قهرا والمجرمون يقادون إلى النار قهرا ولا قاهر
إلا الله الواحد القهار

ولا قادر إلا الملك الجبار واذا انكشفت الغطاء عن أعين الغافلين فشاهدوا
الأمر كذلك سمعوا عند ذلك  نداء المنادي {لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد
القهار} ولقد كان الملك لله الواحد القهار كل يوم لا ذلك على الخصوص ولكن
الغافلين لا يسمعون هذا النداء إلا ذلك اليوم فهو نبأ عما يتجدد للغافلين
من كشف الأحوال حيث لا ينفعهم الكشف فنعوذ بالله الحليم الكريم من الجهل
والعمى فإنه أصل أسباب الهلاك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "the appearance of the effect of bounty upon the recipient," whether in speech (praise), action (service), or state (contentment). It is the opposite of ingratitude (kufrān).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Gratitude (shukr) is the recognition of the bestower of favor (al-munʿim) through humble submission (khudūʿ), love (maḥabbah), and the use of His gifts in obedience to Him. It is a comprehensive term for the soul's cognizance, the tongue's praise, and the limbs' service.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, shukr is "to be saturated" (as in a camel becoming fat). Metaphorically (majāz), it is the "saturation" of the soul with the recognition of the Giver, and the "saturation" of the tongue with praise. The impossibility of literal gratitude to God necessitates a metaphorical understanding.
- Root: و-ج-د (w-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To find, to perceive, to attain. From this derives wujūd (existence) and wajd (ecstatic finding of the Divine).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Existence (wujūd) is of two kinds: that which is self-subsistent (qāʾim bi-nafsihi) and that which is derived from another. True existence belongs only to the Necessary Being; all else is "found" through Him.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is "finding a lost object." Metaphorically, the mystic's "finding" (wajd) is the discovery of the Real (al-Ḥaqq) after the annihilation of the self.
- Root: ف-ن-ي (f-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To perish, to cease, to be annihilated. The opposite of baqāʾ (abiding).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Fanāʾ in the theological sense is the passing away of all contingent things; in the spiritual sense, it is the annihilation of the perception of otherness (ghayr) from the heart of the gnostic.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, the perishing of a thing. Metaphorically, the "passing away" of the servant's attributes and will in the contemplation of the Divine acts and will.
- Root: ق-ي-م (q-y-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, to rise, to uphold. Al-Qayyūm is the Self-Subsistent Who upholds all things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-Qayyūm is He Who is not dependent on a place or a supporter, and upon Whom all else depends for their subsistence. It implies both self-subsistence and the upholding of others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, "the standing one." Metaphorically, the One Who stands over every soul for what it has earned, and upon Whom all standing depends.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Predication (al-Isnād) and the Distinction between the Subject and the Predicate (al-Mubtadaʾ wa al-Khabar). The sentence "He is the Thankful and the Thanked" (huwa al-shākir wa huwa al-mashkūr) requires a careful parsing where the predicate is not a simple attribute but a relational identity, demanding a deep understanding of the copula's metaphysical weight. Also, the Rule of Conditionality (al-Sharṭ) in "If you are grateful, I will increase you" (la-in shakartum la-azīdannakum), where the apodosis is a promise contingent upon the protasis, yet the ultimate agency remains with God.
chapters.translation:
I say: Perhaps it may occur to your mind that gratitude (shukr) is only performed towards a benefactor who has a personal interest (ḥaẓẓ) in that gratitude. For we thank kings either with praise (thanāʾ) to elevate their standing in hearts and display their generosity before people, thereby increasing their fame and prestige (jāh); or with service (khidmah) which assists them in some of their aims; or by standing before them in the posture of servants, which augments their retinue and is a cause for the increase of their honor. Thus, people are not considered thankful to them except by some such act. Now, this is impossible with respect to God, may He be exalted, from two aspects.

The first aspect: God, may He be exalted, is transcendent above personal interests and aims, and is sanctified above any need for service or assistance, above the spreading of prestige and awe through praise and flattery, and above the multiplication of the retinue of servants by standing before Him in bowing and prostration. Thus, our thanking Him with something in which He has no interest would be analogous to our thanking a king who has bestowed a favor upon us by sleeping in our houses, or by prostrating or bowing—since the king has no interest in that, and he is absent, having no knowledge of it. And God, may He be exalted, has no interest in all of our acts.

The second aspect: Everything we undertake by our own choice is itself another favor (niʿmah) from God's favors upon us. For our limbs, our power (qudrah), our will (irādah), our impulses (dāʿiyah), and all other things that are the causes of our movement—and the very movement itself—are from God's creation and His bounty. So how can we thank one favor with another favor? If a king gave us a mount, and we took another mount of his and rode it, or if the king gave us a garment and we took another garment of his and wore it, the second would not be gratitude for the first on our part. Rather, the second would itself require gratitude just as the first required it. Then, gratitude for gratitude cannot be accomplished except by yet another favor, which leads to the conclusion that gratitude is impossible with respect to God, may He be exalted, from these two aspects. And we do not doubt both of these matters, and the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) has come with them. So how is the way to reconcile?

Know that this thought occurred to David (Dāwūd), peace be upon him, and likewise to Moses (Mūsā), peace be upon him. He said: "O Lord, how can I thank You, when I am unable to thank You except through a second favor from Your favors?" And in another wording: "And my thanking You is another favor from You that obligates thankfulness to You." So God, may He be exalted, revealed to him: "When you have known this, you have thanked Me." And in another report: "When you know that the favor is from Me, I am satisfied with that from you as gratitude."

If you say: "I have understood the question, but my understanding falls short of grasping the meaning of what was revealed to them. For I know the impossibility of gratitude to God, may He be exalted. But as for the notion that the knowledge of the impossibility of gratitude is itself gratitude, I do not understand it. For this knowledge is also a favor from Him, so how did it become gratitude?" It is as if the conclusion returns to this: that whoever does not thank has thanked, and that the acceptance of the second robe of honor from the king is gratitude for the first robe. And the understanding falls short of grasping the secret therein. If it is possible to define this by an example, it is important in itself.

Know that this is a knocking at the door of the gnostic sciences (maʿārif), and it is the highest of the sciences of practical conduct (ʿulūm al-muʿāmalah). But we shall indicate some of its features and say: Here there are two perspectives (naẓarān).

The first perspective: The vision with the eye of pure unity (tawḥīd al-maḥḍ). This vision definitively informs you that He is the Thankful (al-shākir) and He is the Thanked (al-mashkūr), that He is the Lover (al-muḥibb) and He is the Beloved (al-maḥbūb). This is the vision of one who knows that there is nothing in existence other than Him, and that everything is perishing except His Face {«كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ»}, and that this is true in every state, eternally without beginning and without end. For "other" (al-ghayr) is that which is conceived to have subsistence by itself, and such an "other" has no existence—rather, it is impossible for it to exist. For the verified existent (al-mawjūd al-muḥaqqaq) is the self-subsistent (al-qāʾim bi-nafsihi). And that which has no subsistence by itself has no existence by itself; rather, it subsists by another, so it exists by another. If one considers its essence and does not look to the other, it has no existence at all. The existent is only the self-subsistent, and the self-subsistent is that which, if its other were supposed non-existent, would remain existent. If, along with its self-subsistence, the existence of others subsists through its existence, then it is the Qayyūm (the Self-Subsistent Sustainer). And there is no Qayyūm except the One, and it is inconceivable that it be otherwise. Therefore, there is nothing in existence other than the Living, the Qayyūm, Who is the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Wāḥid al-Ṣamad).

So when you look from this station, you know that everything originates from Him and to Him is the return. He is the Thankful and He is the Thanked, He is the Lover and He is the Beloved. From this perspective, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Ḥabīb looked when he recited {«إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ»} and said: "How wondrous! He gave and He praised!"—indicating that when He praises His own giving, He praises Himself. So He is the Praiser (al-muthnī) and He is the Praised (al-muthnā ʿalayhi). From this perspective, the Shaykh Abū Saʿīd al-Mayhanī looked when it was recited before him {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} and he said: "By my life, He loves them—leave Him to love them! By His right, He loves them, for He only loves Himself." He indicated thereby that He is the Lover and He is the Beloved.

This is a lofty station that you will not understand except through an example proportionate to your intellect's capacity. It should not be hidden from you that if an artisan loves his craft, he has loved himself; if a maker loves his handiwork, he has loved himself; if a father loves his child insofar as it is his child, he has loved himself. And everything in existence other than God, may He be exalted, is God's handiwork and His creation. If He loves it, He loves only Himself. And if He does not love it for His own sake, then by His right He loves what He loves—and this is what He loves. All of this is the vision with the eye of pure unity. The Sufis express this state as the annihilation of the self (fanāʾ al-nafs), meaning that one is annihilated from oneself and from other than God, and sees nothing but God, may He be exalted.

Whoever does not understand this denies them and says: "How can he be annihilated while his shadow is four cubits long, and perhaps he eats pounds of bread every day?" Thus the ignorant mock them due to their ignorance of the meanings of their words. And it is a necessary consequence that the gnostics (al-ʿārifūn) be a laughingstock for the ignorant. To this, His saying, may He be exalted, points: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ وَمَا أُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ»}. Then He explained that the laughter of the gnostics at them tomorrow will be greater, for He said, may He be exalted: {«فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ»}. Likewise, the nation of Noah, peace be upon him, used to laugh at him when he was occupied with building the ark. He said: {«إِنْ تَسْخَرُوا مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنْكُمْ كَمَا تَسْخَرُونَ»}.

This is one of the two perspectives.

The second perspective: The vision of one who has not attained the station of annihilation from oneself. These are of two categories:

A category who affirmed only the existence of themselves and denied that they have a Lord to worship. These are the blind, inverted ones (al-ʿumyān al-mankūsūn), and their blindness is in both eyes. For they denied what is firmly established in reality—namely, the Qayyūm, Who is self-subsistent and stands over every soul for what it has earned, and every standing thing stands by Him. And they did not stop at this, but even affirmed themselves. Had they known, they would have known that they, insofar as they are themselves, have no stability and no existence. Their existence is only insofar as they are brought into existence (ūjidū), not insofar as they exist (wajadū). And there is a difference between the "existent" (al-mawjūd) and the "brought into existence" (al-mūjad). In existence there is only one Existent and one Bringer-into-existence. The Existent is the Real (al-Ḥaqq), and the brought-into-existence is false (bāṭil) insofar as it is itself. The Existent is self-subsistent and Qayyūm; the brought-into-existence is perishing and passing away. And when {«كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ»}, then nothing remains except {«وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ»}.

The second category: They do not have blindness, but they have one-eyedness (ʿawar). For they see with one eye the existence of the Real Existent and do not deny it. But if the other eye becomes blind, they do not see with it the annihilation of other than the Real Existent. So they affirm another existent alongside God, may He be exalted. This one is a veritable polytheist (mushrik), just as the one before was a veritable denier (jāḥid).

If one passes beyond the limit of one-eyedness to dimness of vision (ʿamash), he perceives a disparity (tafāwut) between the two existents, and affirms a servant and a Lord. By this measure of affirming disparity and deficiency in the other existent, he enters into the bounds of tawḥīd. Then, if he applies kohl to his eye with what increases its lights, his dimness decreases. And in proportion to the increase in his vision, the deficiency of what he affirmed other than God becomes manifest to him. If he continues in this way, the deficiency will lead him to effacement (al-maḥw), and he will be effaced from seeing other than God, seeing only God—so that he may attain the perfection of tawḥīd. And wherever he perceives a deficiency in the existence of other than God, he enters into the beginnings of tawḥīd. Between the two there are countless degrees. By this, the degrees of the monotheists (al-muwaḥḥidūn) are differentiated.

The Books sent down upon the tongues of His messengers are the kohl by which the lights of the eyes are obtained, and the prophets are the oculists (al-kuḥḥālūn). They came calling to pure tawḥīd, whose translation is the saying "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and whose meaning is that one should see nothing but the One, the Real. Those who arrive at the perfection of tawḥīd are the fewest, and the deniers and polytheists are also few, being at the extreme end opposite to the end of tawḥīd. For the idol-worshippers said {«مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفَى»}, so they were entering the beginnings of the gates of tawḥīd with a weak entry. The middling ones are the most numerous. Among them are those whose inner sight opens in some states, and the realities of tawḥīd flash upon them—but like a lightning bolt that does not abide. And among them are those for whom it flashes and abides for a time, but does not endure. And permanence therein is rare:

"To every one, toward the summit of highness, there are movements... but rare among men is steadfastness."

When God, may He be exalted, commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to seek nearness, and it was said to him {«وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ»}, he said in his prostration: "I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself." This was due to his ascent through seventy stations, some above others. The first of them, although it surpassed the utmost limits of the creatures, was nevertheless a deficiency relative to the last of them. Thus, his seeking forgiveness was for that. And when ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "Has not God forgiven you your former and latter sins? Then what is this weeping in prostration and this severe exertion?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?" For gratitude is the cause of increase, as He said, may He be exalted: {«لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ»}.

And when we have plunged into the seas of unveiling (al-mukāshafah), let us pull in the reins and return to what befits the sciences of practical conduct. We say: The prophets, peace be upon them, were sent to call creation to the perfection of tawḥīd which we have described. But between them and reaching it there is a distant distance and severe obstacles. The entire Sacred Law is only the definition of the way of traversing that distance and cutting through those obstacles. And at that point, there is a vision of another witnessing (mushāhadah) and another station. In that station, relative to that witnessing, gratitude, the grateful one, and the thanked one appear. And this is not known except through an example.

I say: You can understand that a king from among the kings sent to a servant who was far from him a mount, garments, and money for provisions for the journey, so that he might traverse the distance of remoteness and draw near to the king's presence. Then the servant has two states:

The first state: The king's intention in having the servant reach his presence is that the servant should carry out some of his important tasks, and the king has an interest in his service.

The second state: The king has no interest in the servant and no need of him. Rather, his presence does not increase the king's dominion, for he is not capable of performing a service that would avail the king anything; and his absence does not diminish the king's dominion. So the king's intention in bestowing the mount and provisions is that the servant should attain the happiness of nearness to him and gain the felicity of his presence—so that the servant benefits himself, not so that the king benefits from him or from his benefiting.

Now, the station of the servants with respect to God, may He be exalted, is the second station, not the first. For the first is impossible with respect to God, and the second is not impossible.

Then know that the servant is not grateful in the first state merely by riding and reaching the king's presence, unless he performs the service that the king intended from him. As for the second state, there is no need for service at all. Nevertheless, it is conceivable that he be grateful or ungrateful. His gratitude consists in using what his master sent to him in what the master loves for his sake—not for the master's own sake. And his ingratitude consists in not using it thus—either by neglecting it or by using it in what increases his distance from him.

So whenever the servant wears the garment, rides the horse, and spends the provisions only on the road, he has thanked his master, for he used his favor in what the master loves—that is, in what the master loves for the servant, not for himself. And if he rides it and turns his back on the king's presence, moving away from him, he has been ungrateful for his favor—that is, he used it in what the master dislikes for the servant, not for himself. And if he sits and does not ride—neither seeking nearness nor seeking distance—he has also been ungrateful for the favor by neglecting and suspending it, though this is less than if he had moved away from him.

Likewise, God, glory be to Him, created the creatures, and they, at the beginning of their natural constitution (fiṭrah), need to use the appetites (shahawāt) to complete their bodies thereby, and through them they move away from His presence. Their happiness is only in nearness to Him. So He prepared for them, from His favors, that by which they are able to attain the degree of nearness.
