ذكر الموت كل يوم عشرين مرة لم أقف له على إسناده // وفي لفظ آخر الذي يذكر
ذنوبه فتحزنه ولا شك في أن ذكر الموت على المريض أغلب فلما أن كثرت فوائد
المرض رأى جماعة ترك الحيلة في زوالها إذ رأوا لأنفسهم مزيدا فيها لا من
حيث رأوا التداوي نقصانا وكيف يكون نقصانا وقد فعل ذلك صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-و-ي (d-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To treat, to medicate, to cure; the act of applying a remedy (dawāʾ) to an ailment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The means (sabab) by which health is sought; in the Qurʾānic worldview, it is a permissible secondary cause that does not negate reliance on the Creator of causes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical medication; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to spiritual remedies, e.g., repentance as the "medicine" of the heart.
- Root: ك-ش-ف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Unveiling, disclosure; the removal of a covering (kashf) so that what is hidden becomes apparent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Ṣūfī and Kalām terminology, it denotes the direct, divinely-granted perception of unseen realities (mukāshafah), a higher epistemic mode than discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: lifting a veil; metaphorical: the soul's perception of the divine decree, rendering secondary causes superfluous in the heart's certainty.
- Root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Endurance, forbearance; the restraint of the soul from complaint and agitation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A cardinal virtue (ḥāl) of the believer; patient perseverance (ṣabr) under divine trial (balāʾ) is the very substance of faith's verification.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: steadfastness in hardship; metaphorical: the soul's "binding" (iṣtibār) against the impulse to seek swift relief, thereby prioritizing the afterlife over the present.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional of Generalization (al-sharṭ al-ʿāmm) — In sentences like "إذا دخل عليه الضرر... فلم يلتفت إليه" (If harm enters upon him... and he pays no heed), the protasis (sharṭ) establishes a universal condition whose apodosis (jawāb) reveals the moral character of the actor, requiring the reader to parse the sequence of verbs as simultaneous states rather than temporal succession.
chapters.translation:
Know that those among the Salaf (the pious predecessors) who sought medical treatment are too numerous to be enumerated. However, a group of the eminent ones (al-akābir) also abandoned treatment. Perhaps one might suppose that this constitutes a deficiency, for if it were a perfection, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) would not have abandoned it — since no one else's state of trust in God (tawakkul) could be more complete than his.

It has been related that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) was told, "Shall we summon a physician for you?" He replied, "The Physician has already looked upon me and said: {«إِنِّي فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا أُرِيدُ»} — 'Indeed, I am the Doer of whatsoever I will' (Q. 11:107)."

It was said to Abū al-Dardāʾ during his illness, "What do you complain of?" He said, "My sins." It was said, "What do you desire?" He said, "My Lord's forgiveness." They said, "Shall we not summon a physician for you?" He said, "The Physician is the One who made me ill."

It was said to Abū Dharr when his eyes were inflamed, "Would you not treat them?" He said, "I am too occupied with them [i.e., with God's remembrance] to attend to them." It was said, "Would you not ask God the Exalted to heal you?" He said, "I ask Him for what is more important to me than them."

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was stricken with paralysis (fālij). It was said to him, "Would you not seek treatment?" He said, "I intended to, but then I remembered ʿĀd and Thamūd and the Companions of al-Rass, and many generations between them — and among them were physicians. Yet the healer and the healed perished alike, and no incantation availed them anything."

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal used to say: "I love for the one who has embraced trust in God (tawakkul) and traversed this path to abandon treatment — whether by drinking medicine or otherwise. And if he has ailments, he should not even inform the physician of them when asked."

It was said to Sahl [al-Tustarī]: "When does trust in God become sound for the servant?" He said: "When harm enters upon his body and loss upon his wealth, and he pays no heed to them — being occupied with his [spiritual] state — and he looks to God's sustaining care (qiyām) over him."

Thus, among them are those who left treatment behind them, and among them are those who disapproved of it. The reconciliation between the practice of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and their practices cannot become clear except by enumerating the deterrents (ṣawārif) from treatment. So we say: abandoning treatment has causes.

**The First Cause**: That the patient be among those granted unveiling (al-mukāshifīn), and it has been unveiled to him that his term has ended and that medicine will not benefit him. This becomes known to him sometimes through a true vision (ruʾyā ṣādiqah), sometimes through intuition and conjecture (ḥads wa ẓann), and sometimes through verified unveiling (kashf muḥaqqaq). It is plausible that al-Ṣiddīq's (may God be pleased with him) abandonment of treatment was of this cause, for he was among those granted unveiling. He said to ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) regarding the matter of inheritance: "They are only your two sisters" — though she had only one sister. But his wife was pregnant and gave birth to a female. So it is known that it had been unveiled to him that she was pregnant with a female. Thus it is not far-fetched that it was also unveiled to him that his term had ended. Otherwise, it should not be supposed of him that he denied treatment, for he had witnessed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) seek treatment and command it.

**The Second Cause**: That the patient be occupied with his [spiritual] state, with fear of its consequence, and with God's oversight of him — such that this forgets him the pain of illness, and his heart finds no leisure for treatment, being occupied with his state. This is indicated by the words of Abū Dharr when he said, "I am too occupied with them," and the words of Abū al-Dardāʾ when he said, "I only complain of my sins." For the pain of his heart from fear of his sins was greater than the pain of his body from illness. This one is like a person stricken by the death of a beloved one, or like a fearful man being led to a king to be killed — when it is said to him, "Will you not eat while you are hungry?" he says, "I am too occupied with the pain of hunger [to eat]." This is not a denial that eating benefits against hunger, nor an attack upon those who eat. Close to this is the occupation of Sahl when it was said to him, "What is sustenance (al-qūt)?" He said, "It is the remembrance of the Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-Ḥayy al-Qayyūm)." It was said, "We only asked you about physical sustenance (al-qiwām)." He said, "Physical sustenance is knowledge." It was said, "We asked you about food (al-ghidhāʾ)." He said, "Food is remembrance (al-dhikr)." It was said, "We asked you about the nourishment of the body." He said, "What have you to do with the body? Leave it to the One who takes charge of it — if not at first, then at last. When an ailment enters upon it, return it to its Maker. Do you not see that when a crafted thing is defective, it is returned to its craftsman until he repairs it?"

**The Third Cause**: That the ailment be chronic, and the medicine prescribed for it be of illusory benefit (mawhūm al-nafʿ), running the course of cauterization (al-kayy) and incantation (al-ruqyah). The one who trusts in God abandons it. To this points the saying of al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym when he said, "I remembered ʿĀd and Thamūd, and among them were physicians, yet the healer and the healed perished" — meaning that medicine is not reliable. This may be so in itself, and it may be so in the patient's estimation due to his lack of practice in medicine and lack of experience with it, so that the conviction of its benefit does not dominate his conjecture (ẓann). There is no doubt that the experienced physician has a stronger conviction in medicines than others. Thus trust and conjecture follow conviction, and conviction follows experience. Most of those who abandon treatment among the worshippers and ascetics have this as their basis — for medicine remains in their view something illusory with no foundation. This is correct regarding some medicines in the view of one who knows the art of medicine, but not correct regarding others. However, the non-physician may look at all of it with a single glance and see treatment as an over-indulgence in secondary causes (taʿammuq fī al-asbāb), like cauterization and incantation, and so he abandons it.

**The Fourth Cause**: That the servant, by abandoning treatment, intends to preserve the illness in order to attain the reward of illness through beautiful patience (ḥusn al-ṣabr) upon God's trial, or to test himself in his capacity for patience. For much has been reported regarding the reward of illness. He (peace be upon him) said: "We, the company of prophets, are the most severely tried of people, then the most excellent, then the most excellent. The servant is tried according to the measure of his faith: if his faith is firm, his trial is intensified; and if there is weakness in his faith, his trial is lightened." {«نَحْنُ مَعَاشِرَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ أَشَدُّ النَّاسِ بَلَاءً ثُمَّ الْأَمْثَلُ فَالْأَمْثَلُ يُبْتَلَى الْعَبْدُ عَلَى قَدْرِ إِيمَانِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَ صُلْبَ الْإِيمَانِ شُدِّدَ عَلَيْهِ الْبَلَاءُ وَإِنْ كَانَ فِي إِيمَانِهِ ضَعْفٌ حُفِّفَ عَنْهُ الْبَلَاءُ»} — Among them are those who emerge like pure gold (al-ibrīz) with no dross, and among them are those below that, and among them are those who emerge black and burnt. He (peace be upon him) also said: "Do you love to be like stray wild donkeys, neither falling ill nor being afflicted?" And Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) said: "You find the believer with the soundest heart and the most ailing body, and you find the hypocrite with the soundest body and the most ailing heart."

When praise of illness and trial became great, a people loved illness and seized upon it to attain the reward of patience upon it. Among them was one who had an ailment which he concealed and did not mention to the physician, enduring the ailment and being content with God's decree. He knew that the Truth (al-Ḥaqq) dominated his heart such that illness could not distract him from it — illness only impedes his bodily members. And they knew that their prayer seated, for example, with patience upon God's decree, is better than prayer standing with health and well-being. For in the report: God the Exalted says to His angels: "Write for My righteous servant what he used to do, for he is in My bond. If I release him, I will replace his flesh with better flesh and his blood with better blood; and if I take him in death, I take him to My mercy." {«اكْتُبُوا لِعَبْدِي الصَّالِحِ مَا كَانَ يَعْمَلُ فَإِنَّهُ فِي وَثَاقِي إِنْ أَطْلَقْتُهُ أَبْدَلْتُهُ لَحْمًا خَيْرًا مِنْ لَحْمِهِ وَدَمًا خَيْرًا مِنْ دَمِهِ وَإِنْ تَوَفَّيْتُهُ تَوَفَّيْتُهُ إِلَى رَحْمَتِي»} And he (peace be upon him) said: "The best of deeds are those to which the souls are compelled." And he said: "Fever and continued illness do not cease from the servant until he walks upon the earth like a pure garment (al-burdah) with no sin upon him." And he mentioned the expiation of sins by fever, whereupon Zayd ibn Thābit asked his Lord (mighty and majestic) that he might never cease to be feverish — and fever did not leave him until he died (may God have mercy on him). A group of the Anṣār asked for the same, and fever never ceased to afflict them. And when he (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever God takes away his two precious things [his eyes], He is not satisfied for him with any reward less than Paradise," there were among the Anṣār those who wished for blindness. And ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) said: "He is not a scholar who does not rejoice at the entry of calamities and illnesses upon his body and wealth, for what he hopes in that of the expiation of his sins." And it is related that Mūsā (peace be upon him) looked upon a servant of great affliction and said: "O Lord, have mercy on him." God the Exalted said: "How shall I have mercy on him when by what afflicts him I have mercy on him?" — that is, by it I expiate his sins and increase his ranks.

**The Fifth Cause**: That the servant senses in himself the beginnings of insolence (al-baṭar) and transgression (al-ṭughyān) due to the prolongation of health. So he abandons treatment out of fear that the swift removal of illness would return him to heedlessness, insolence, and transgression — or to the prolongation of hope (ṭūl al-amal) and procrastination (taswīf) in making up for what has been lost and delaying good deeds. For health is an expression of the strength of the faculties; through it desire (al-hawā) is aroused, appetites (al-shahawāt) are stirred, and they call to disobedience. The least of that is that they call to self-indulgence in permissible things — which is the squandering of times and the neglect of the great profit in opposing the soul and adhering to acts of obedience. When God desires good for a servant, He does not leave him without awakening through illnesses and calamities. For this reason it was said: "The believer is never free from an ailment, a lack, or a slip."

It has been related that God the Exalted says: "Poverty is My prison, and illness is My fetter; I confine with them whom I love among My creatures." When one is in illness, he is restrained from transgression and the commission of sins — what good is greater than this? It is not fitting that one who fears this for himself should occupy himself with treating it, for well-being (al-ʿāfiyah) lies in abandoning disobedience. One of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn) said to a man: "How were you after me?" He said, "In well-being." He said: "If you have not disobeyed God (mighty and majestic), then you are in well-being; but if you have disobeyed Him, then what ailment is more malignant (adwā) than disobedience? He who disobeys God has not been granted well-being." And ʿAlī (may God honor his face), when he saw the adornment of the Nabateans in Iraq on a festival day, said: "What is this that they have displayed?" They said: "O Commander of the Believers, this is their festival day." He said: "Every day on which God (mighty and majestic) is not disobeyed is a festival for us." And God the Exalted said: {«مِن بَعْدِ مَا أَرَاكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ»} — "After what He has shown you of what you love" (Q. 9:14) — it was said [this refers to] well-being (al-ʿawāfī). For {«إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ أَن رَّآهُ اسْتَغْنَىٰ»} — "Indeed, man does transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient" (Q. 96:6-7). Likewise, when he is self-sufficient through well-being. Some said: "Pharaoh only said, 'I am your lord most high' (Q. 79:24) because of the prolongation of well-being — for he remained four hundred years without his head aching, his body fevering, or a vein throbbing. So he claimed divinity — may God curse him. Had he been seized by a migraine for a single day, it would have occupied him from trivialities, let alone the claim of divinity." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Multiply the remembrance of the destroyer of pleasures." {«أَكْثِرُوا مِنْ ذِكْرِ هَاذِمِ اللَّذَّاتِ»} And it was said: "Fever is the herald of death (rāʾid al-mawt)" — it reminds one of it and repels procrastination.

And God the Exalted said: {«أَوَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُمْ يُفْتَنُونَ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ مَّرَّةً أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ لَا يَتُوبُونَ وَلَا هُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ»} — "Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice, yet they neither repent nor take heed?" (Q. 9:126). It was said: "They are tried with illnesses by which they are tested." And it is said: "When a servant falls ill twice and then does not repent, the Angel of Death says to him: 'O heedless one, a messenger from me came to you after a messenger, and you did not respond.'"

The Salaf therefore used to feel uneasy when a year passed without their being afflicted with a loss in soul or wealth. They said: "The believer is never free, within every forty days, from being startled by a fright or struck by a calamity." It is even related that ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir married a woman who never fell ill, so he divorced her. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) was offered a woman, and her qualities were described to him until he intended to marry her. Then it was said, "Indeed, she has never been ill." He said: "I have no need of her." For it has come in the report: "Fever is the share of every believer from the Fire." {«الْحُمَّى حَظُّ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنَ النَّارِ»} And in another wording: "The one who remembers his sins and is grieved by them." There is no doubt that the remembrance of death dominates the ill person.

When the benefits of illness became numerous, a group saw the abandonment of seeking its removal — for they saw for themselves an increase in it — not because they viewed treatment as a deficiency. And how could it be a deficiency, when he (peace be upon him) himself practiced it?

chapters.title_en: Refutation of Those Who Claim That Abandoning Medical Treatment Is Absolutely Preferable
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| بيان الرد على من قال: ترك التداوي أفضل بكل حال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر د د (radda)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, repel, refute; in argumentation, to turn back a claim by evidence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Refutation (radd) as the intellectual act of nullifying a false premise through demonstrative proof (dalīl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical repulsion; here used metaphorically (majāz) for logical rebuttal.
- Root: ت ر ك (taraka)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To leave, abandon, forsake; implies deliberate cessation of an action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious discourse, "tark" often denotes renunciation (zuhd) but must be qualified by intention and context.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal abandonment; metaphorical extension to "preferring non-action" as a claimed virtue.
- Root: ع ل ج (ʿalaja)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To treat, remedy, heal; originally refers to binding a wound or setting a bone.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Medical treatment (muʿālajah) as a lawful means (sabab) within the framework of divine providence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical intervention; here contrasted with tawakkul (reliance on God) — a rhetorical tension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional absolute (sharṭ mutlaq) — "bi-kulli ḥāl" (in every case) functions as a universal quantifier, making the claim overbroad; the refutation targets this unqualified universality.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the claim that abandoning medical treatment is absolutely preferable, in every circumstance, is a false and baseless assertion. For the Prophet (peace be upon him) himself resorted to treatment, and he commanded the sick to seek remedies, saying: {«تداووا فإن الله لم يضع داء إلا وضع له دواء»} — "Treat yourselves, for God has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down for it a cure." Thus, the use of lawful means (asbāb) does not contradict reliance upon God (tawakkul); rather, it is a fulfillment of the divine order to act within the causal order that God has established. To abandon treatment absolutely would be an innovation (bidʿah) in religion and a departure from the prophetic example. However, the matter is nuanced: if a person's heart is so firmly attached to God that he fears that preoccupation with treatment would weaken his trust, and he is among those whose reliance is truly sincere, then leaving treatment may be permissible for him — but this is a special case, not a universal rule. The general principle is that treatment is permissible, and in some cases recommended, for the preservation of life and health is a means to obedience. Therefore, the one who claims absolute preference for abandoning treatment errs by overgeneralizing, for the Prophet's practice and his explicit command refute him.

chapters.title_en: The Subtle Distinctions Between Reliance on God and the Use of Earthly Means
chapters.arabic_text:
فلو قال قائل: إنما فعله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليسن لغيره وإلا
فهو حال الضعفاء ودرجة الأقوياء توجب التوكل بترك الدواء فيقال: ينبغي أن
يكون من شروط التوكل ترك الحجامة والفصد عند تبغ الدم
فإن قيل: إن ذلك أيضا شرط فليكن من شرطه أن تلدغه العقرب أو الحية فلا
ينحيها عن نفسه إذ الدم يلدغ الباطن والعقرب تلدغ الظاهر فأي فرق بينهما
فإن قال: وذلك أيضا شرط التوكل فيقال: ينبغي أن لا يزيل لدغ العطش بالماء
ولدغ الجوع بالخبز ولدغ البرد بالجبة وهذا لا قائل به
ولا فرق بين هذه  الدرجات فإن جميع ذلك أسباب رتبها مسبب الأسباب سبحانه
وتعالى وأجرى بها سنته ويدل على أن ذلك ليس من شرط التوكل ما روي عن عمر
رضي الله عنه وعن الصحابة في قصة الطاعون فإنهم لما قصدوا الشام وانتهوا
إلى الجابية بلغهم الخبر أن به موتا عظيما ووباء ذريعا فافترق الناس فرقتين
فقال بعضهم لا ندخل على الوباء فنلقي بأيدينا إلى التهلكة وقالت طائفة
أخرى: بل ندخل ونتوكل ولا نهرب من قدر الله تعالى ولا نفر من الموت فنكون
كمن قال الله تعالى فيهم ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر
الموت فرجعوا إلى عمر فسألوه عن رأيه فقال نرجع ولا ندخل على الوباء فقال
له المخالفون في رأيه أنفر من قدر الله تعالى قال عمر نعم نفر من قدر الله
إلى قدر الله ثم ضرب لهم مثلا فقال أرأيتم لو كان لأحدكم غنم فهبط واديا له
شعبتان: إحداهما مخصبة: والأخرى مجدبة أليس إن رعى المخصبة رعاها بقدر الله
تعالى وإن رعى المجدبة رعاها بقدر الله تعالى فقالوا: نعم ثم طلب عبد
الرحمن بن عوف ليسأله عن رأيه وكان غائبا فلما أصبحوا جاء PageV04P290
عبد الرحمن فسأله عمر عن ذلك فقال: عندي فيه يا أمير المؤمنين شيء سمعته
من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال عمر: الله أكبر فقال عبد الرحمن:
سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {يقول} اذا سمعتم بالوباء في أرض فلا
تقدموا عليه وإذا وقع في أرض وأنتم بها فلا تخرجوا فرارا منه (1) حديث
تشبيه الفرار من الطاعون بالفار من الزحف رواه أحمد من حديث عائشة بإسناد
جيد ومن حديث جابر بإسناد ضعيف وقد تقدم لأن فيه كسرا لقلوب بقية المسلمين
وسعيا في إهلاكهم فهذه أمور دقيقة فمن لا يلاحظها وينظر إلى ظواهر الأخبار
والآثار يتناقض عنده أكثر ما سمعه وغلط العباد والزهاد في مثل هذا كثير
وإنما شرف العلم وفضيلته لأجل ذلك فإن قلت: ففي ترك التداوي فضل كما ذكرت
فلم لم يترك  رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التداوي لينال الفضل فنقول: فيه
فضل بالإضافة إلى من كثرت ذنوبه ليكفرها أو خاف على نفسه طغيان العافية
وغلبة الشهوات أو احتاج إلى ما يذكره الموت لغلبة الغفلة أو احتاج إلى نيل
ثواب الصابرين لقصوره عن مقامات الراضين والمتوكلين أو قصرت بصيرته عن
الإطلاع على ما أودع الله تعالى في الأدوية من لطائف المنافع حتى صار في
حقه موهوما كالرقي أو كان شغله بحاله يمنعه عن التداوي وكان التداوي يشغله
عن حاله لضعفه عن الجمع فإلى هذه المعاني رجعت الصوارف في ترك التداوي وكل
ذلك كمالات بالإضافة إلى بعض الخلق ونقصان بالإضافة إلى درجة رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم بل كان مقامه أعلى من هذه المقامات كلها إذ كان حاله يقتضي
أن تكون (2) حديث تشبيه الفرار من الطاعون بالفار من الزحف رواه أحمد من
حديث عائشة بإسناد جيد ومن حديث جابر باسناد ضعيف وقد تقدم PageV04P291
مشاهدته على وتيرة واحدة عند وجود الأسباب وفقدها فإنه لم يكن له نظر في
الأحوال إلا إلى مسبب الأسباب ومن كان هذا مقامه لم تضره الأسباب كما أن
الرغبة في المال نقص والرغبة عن المال كراهية له وإن كانت كمالا فهي أيضا
نقص بالإضافة إلى من يستوي عنده وجود المال وعدمه فاستواء الحجر والذهب
أكمل من الهرب من الذهب دون الحجر وكان حاله صلى الله عليه وسلم استواء
المدر والذهب عنده وكان لايمسكه لتعليم الخلق مقام الزهد فإنه منتهى قوتهم
لا لخوفه على نفسه من إمساكه فإنه كان أعلى رتبة من أن تغره الدنيا وقد
عرضت عليه خزائن الأرض فأبى أن يقبلها فكذلك يستوي عنده مباشرة الأسباب
وتركها لمثلهذه المشاهدة وإنما لم يترك استعمال الدواء جريا على سنة الله
تعالى وترخيصا لأمته فيما تمس إليه حاجتهم مع أنه لا ضرر فيه بخلاف ادخار
الأموال فإن ذلك يعظم ضرره نعم التداوي لا يضر الامن حيث رؤية الدواء نافعا
دون خالق الدواء وهذا قد نهي عنه ومن حيث إنه يقصد  به الصحة ليستعان بها
على المعاصي وذلك منهي عنه والمؤمن في غالب الأمر لا يقصد ذلك وأحد من
المؤمنين لا يرى الدواء نافعا بنفسه بل من حيث إنه جعله الله تعالى سببا
للنفع كما لا يرى الماء مروريا ولا الخبز مشبعا فحكم التداوي في مقصوده
كحكم الكسب فإنه إن اكتسب للاستعانة على الطاعة أو على المعصية كان له
حكمها وإن اكتسب للتنعم المباح فله حكمه فقد ظهر بالمعاني التي أوردناها أن
ترك التداوي قد يكون أفضل في بعض الأحوال وأن التداوي قد يكون أفضل في بعض
وأن ذلك يختلف باختلاف الأحوال والأشخاص والنيات وأن واحدا من الفعل والترك
ليس شرطا في التوكل إلا ترك الموهومات كالكي والرقي فإن ذلك تعمق في
التدبيرات لا يليق بالمتوكلين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pave a path, to establish a normative practice, to set a precedent that others follow.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Prophetic Sunnah as the divinely sanctioned paradigm for communal conduct, distinct from individual spiritual stations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage here — the Prophet's act is a legislative precedent (ta shrīʿ), not merely a personal habit.
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measure, decree, divine ordainment; the precise apportionment of all affairs by God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological principle of qadar — that all causes and effects are subsumed under God's eternal decree, yet secondary causality remains real.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The distinction between fleeing from one manifestation of qadar to another — a permissible movement within the divine order, not a denial of it.
- Root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A rope, a cord, a means of connection; that which leads to an end.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The causal nexus (asbāb) as the divinely instituted fabric of the world — God is the M usabbib al-Asbāb (Causer of causes), and means are His custom (sunnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — causes are real instruments of divine action; metaphorical — attributing independent efficacy to them is shirk.
- Root: و-ه-م (w-h-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Imagination, false supposition, that which the mind conjures without reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The epistemic weakness that leads one to believe in the intrinsic power of means (e.g., amulets, cautery) rather than God's sole agency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension — "imagined causes" (mawhūmāt) are those whose efficacy is purely psychological, not real.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Responsive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The text repeatedly employs "fa-law qāla qā'il... fa-yuqāl" (if one says... then it is said), a rhetorical dialectic structure where each hypothetical objection is met with a parallel counter-example, demanding precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis to track the logical escalation.
chapters.translation:
I say: If someone were to object: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) only engaged in medical treatment to establish a Sunnah for others; otherwise, it is the way of the weak, whereas the station of the strong necessitates reliance on God (tawakkul) by abandoning medicine" — then it is said to him: By this logic, it would be incumbent upon the conditions of tawakkul to abandon cupping (ḥijāmah) and venesection (faṣd) when the blood becomes agitated.

And if it is said: "That too is a condition" — then let it also be a condition that when a scorpion or a serpent stings him, he should not repel it from himself. For the blood stings the inward, and the scorpion stings the outward — so what difference is there between the two?

And if he says: "That also is a condition of tawakkul" — then it is said to him: It would likewise be incumbent upon him not to quench the sting of thirst with water, nor the sting of hunger with bread, nor the sting of cold with a cloak. Yet no one holds such a position.

And there is no distinction between these degrees, for all of them are causes (asbāb) arranged by the Causer of causes (Musabbib al-Asbāb), Glorified and Exalted is He, and He has run His custom (sunnah) through them. And that which indicates that this is not a condition of tawakkul is what has been narrated from ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) and from the Companions in the story of the plague (ṭāʿūn). For when they set out for Syria and reached al-Jābiyah, news reached them that there was a great mortality there and a devastating epidemic. The people split into two groups. Some said: "We shall not enter the land of the plague, lest we cast ourselves into destruction with our own hands." Another group said: "Rather, we shall enter and rely on God (tawakkul); we shall not flee from the decree of God (qadar Allāh), nor shall we run from death" — thus becoming like those of whom God, Exalted is He, said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ»} (Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes by the thousands, fearing death? — Qur'an 2:243).

So they returned to ʿUmar and asked him for his opinion. He said: "We shall return, and we shall not enter the land of the plague." Those who opposed his opinion said to him: "Do you flee from the decree of God?" ʿUmar replied: "Yes, we flee from the decree of God to the decree of God." Then he struck for them a parable, saying: "Consider — if one of you had sheep and descended into a valley with two slopes, one fertile and one barren — would he not, if he grazed them on the fertile slope, graze them by the decree of God, and if he grazed them on the barren slope, graze them by the decree of God?" They said: "Yes."

Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was sought so that he might be asked his opinion, but he was absent. When morning came, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān arrived, and ʿUmar asked him about the matter. He said: "I have something concerning this, O Commander of the Faithful, which I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)." ʿUmar said: "God is Most Great." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: "I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) {«يقول»} (say): 'If you hear of a plague in a land, do not advance upon it; and if it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not go forth fleeing from it.'" (1) — A hadith likening flight from the plague to flight from the battle-line (al-firār min al-zahf), narrated by Aḥmad from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah with a sound chain, and from the hadith of Jābir with a weak chain; it has already been mentioned, for it contains a breaking of the hearts of the remaining Muslims and an effort toward their destruction.

These are subtle matters. Whoever does not observe them but looks only at the outward appearances of the reports and the traditions will find most of what he hears contradictory. And the error of the worshippers and ascetics in such matters is frequent. Indeed, the honor of knowledge and its excellence is precisely for this reason.

If you say: "Since there is merit in abandoning medical treatment, as you have mentioned, why did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) not abandon it to attain that merit?" — we say: There is merit in it relative to one whose sins are many, so that it may expiate them; or one who fears for himself the tyranny of well-being and the dominance of passions; or one who needs something to remind him of death due to the prevalence of heedlessness; or one who needs to attain the reward of the patient (ṣābirīn) because of his shortcoming from the stations of the contented (rāḍīn) and the reliant (mutawakkilīn); or one whose insight is too weak to perceive the subtle benefits that God, Exalted is He, has deposited in medicines, until they become in his case merely imagined (mawhūm) like incantations (ruqā); or one whose occupation with his spiritual state prevents him from seeking treatment, and treatment would distract him from his state due to his weakness in combining both.

To these meanings are reduced all the deterrents (ṣawārif) regarding the abandonment of treatment. And all of these are perfections relative to some creatures, but deficiencies relative to the station of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Rather, his station was higher than all these stations, for his state required that his witnessing (mushāhadah) remain on a single uniform course both when causes exist and when they are absent. For he had no regard for circumstances except toward the Causer of causes (Musabbib al-Asbāb). And whoever's station is this, causes do not harm him — just as desire for wealth is a deficiency, and aversion to wealth is a form of disdain for it; and even if aversion is a perfection, it is also a deficiency relative to one for whom the existence and non-existence of wealth are equal. For the equality of stone and gold is more perfect than fleeing from gold while not fleeing from stone. And his state (peace and blessings be upon him) was the equality of clay and gold in his sight. He did not refrain from holding wealth merely to teach creation the station of asceticism (zuhd), for that is the limit of their strength — not out of fear for himself from holding it, for he was of a rank too high to be deceived by this world. The treasures of the earth were offered to him, and he refused to accept them. Likewise, the direct engagement with causes and the abandonment of them were equal in his sight, due to this witnessing.

And he did not abandon the use of medicine only in accordance with the custom (sunnah) of God, Exalted is He, and as a concession (tarkhīṣ) for his community in what their need requires — especially since there is no harm in it — unlike the hoarding of wealth, for its harm is great. Indeed, medicine is not harmful except from the perspective of one who sees the medicine as beneficial apart from the Creator of the medicine — and this has been forbidden. And except from the perspective of one who seeks health by it in order to use it for disobedience — and this too is forbidden. But the believer, in most cases, does not intend this. And none of the believers sees medicine as beneficial in itself, but rather insofar as God, Exalted is He, has made it a cause (sabab) for benefit — just as one does not see water as quenching by itself, nor bread as satiating by itself.

Thus the ruling on medicine in its intention is like the ruling on earning (kasb): if one earns to aid obedience or disobedience, it takes the ruling of that purpose; and if one earns for permissible enjoyment, it takes its own ruling. It has thus become clear, through the meanings we have adduced, that the abandonment of treatment may be more virtuous in some circumstances, and that treatment may be more virtuous in others; that this varies according to circumstances, persons, and intentions; and that neither the act nor the abandonment is a condition of tawakkul — except the abandonment of imagined causes (mawhūmāt) such as cautery (kayy) and incantations (ruqā), for that is an overreach in self-management (taʿammuq fī l-tadbīrāt) unbefitting those who rely on God.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the States of the Mutawakkilūn (Those Who Rely on God) Regarding the Manifestation and Concealment of Illness
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| بيان أحوال المتوكلين في إظهار المرض وكتمانه

اعلم أن كتمان المرض وإخفاء الفقر وأنواع البلاء من كنوز البر وهو من
أعلى المقامات: لأن الرضا بحكم الله والصبر على بلائه معاملة بينه وبين
الله عز وجل فكتمانه أسلم عن الآفات
ومع هذا فالإظهار لا بأس به إذا صحت فيه النية والمقصد ومقاصد الإظهار
ثلاثة: الأول: أن يكون غرضه التداوي فيحتاج إلى ذكره للطبيب فيذكره لا في
معرض الشكاية بل في معرض الحكاية لما ظهر عليه من قدرة الله تعالى فقد كان
بشر يصف لعبد الرحمن المطبب أوجاعه وكان أحمد بن حنبل يخبر بأمراض يجدها
ويقول: إنما أصف قدرة الله تعالى في
الثاني: أن يصف لغير الطبيب وكان ممن يقتدى به وكان مكينا في المعرفة
فأراد من ذكره أن يتعلم منه حسن الصبر في المرض بل حسن الشكر بأن يظهر أنه
يرى أن المرض نعمة فيشكر عليها فيتحدث به كما يتحدث بالنعم قال الحسن
البصري: إذا حمد المريض الله تعالى وشكره ثم ذكر أوجاعه لم يكن ذلك شكوى
الثالث: أن يظهر بذلك عجزه وافتقاره إلى الله تعالى وذلك يحسن ممن تليق
به القوة والشجاعة ويستبعد منه العجز كما روي أنه قيل لعلي في مرضه رضي
الله عنه  كيف أنت قال: بشر فنظر بعضهم إلى بعض كأنهم كرهوا ذلك وظنوا أنه
شكاية فقال: أتجلد على الله فأحب أن يظهر عجزه وافتقاره مع ما علم به من
القوة والضراوة وتأدب فيه بأدب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إياه حيث مرض علي
كرم الله وجهه فسمعه // حديث: أنه عرضت عليه خزائن الأرض فأبى ان يقبلها
ولفظه: عرضت عليه مفاتيح خزائن السماء وكنوز الأرض فردها
PageV04P292
عليه السلام وهو يقول: اللهم صبرني على البلاء فقال له صلى الله عليه
وسلم لقد سألت الله تعالى البلاء فسل الله العافية (1) حديث إذا مرض العبد
أوحى الله إلى الملكين انظر ما يقول لعواده الحديث تقدم وإنما كره بعض
العباد العيادة خشية الشكاية خوف الزيادة في الكلام فكان بعضهم إذا مرض
أغلق بابه فلم يدخل عليه أحد حتى يبرأ فيخرج إليهم منهم: فضيل ووهيب وبشر
وكان فضيل يقول: أشتهي أن أمرض بلا عواد وقال: لا أكره العلة إلا لأجل
العواد رضي الله عنه وعنهم أجمعين كمل كتاب التوحيد والتوكل بعون الله وحسن
توفيقه يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى:
كتاب المحبة والشوق والأنس والرضا والله سبحانه وتعالى الموفق
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ت-م (katama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To conceal, veil, or withhold something from perception; the act of keeping a matter hidden from others' awareness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Concealment as a virtuous discipline of the heart, guarding one's inward state from ostentation (riyāʾ) and preserving the sincerity of one's servitude to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes physical hiding; here employed metaphorically (majāz) for the spiritual act of veiling one's trials to protect the purity of one's transaction with God.
- Root: ب-ل-و (balā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trial, affliction, or testing; derived from the sense of refining and proving, as gold is tested by fire.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine tribulation as a means of spiritual purification and a marker of God's attentive care toward the servant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term oscillates between literal calamity and metaphorical testing of faith; in this context, it signifies the servant's reception of divine decree.
- Root: ش-ك-و (shakā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To complain, lament, or voice a grievance regarding a painful condition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Complaint as a verbal act that may undermine patience (ṣabr) and contentment (riḍā), unless redirected toward acknowledging divine power.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes complaint (shakwā) from narration (ḥikāyah)—the former is blameworthy, the latter praiseworthy when framed as testimony to God's omnipotence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if the intention is sound") and exceptive particles to delineate permissible from impermissible manifestations, requiring precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that concealing illness, hiding poverty, and veiling all varieties of affliction are among the treasures of righteousness (birr) and belong to the most elevated stations (maqāmāt). For contentment with God's decree and patience upon His trial constitute a transaction (muʿāmalah) between the servant and God, Mighty and Majestic—and concealing it is safer from the afflictions (āfāt) [of ostentation and complaint].

Nevertheless, manifestation [of illness] is not blameworthy if the intention and purpose therein are sound. The purposes of manifestation are three:

**The First:** That one's aim is to seek treatment (tadāwī), necessitating mention of the ailment to the physician. One mentions it not in the mode of complaint (shakwā) but in the mode of narration (ḥikāyah) of what has appeared upon him of God's power. Thus, Bishr used to describe his pains to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān the physician, and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal would report the illnesses he experienced, saying: "I am only describing the power of God, Exalted is He."

**The Second:** That one describes [the illness] to someone other than a physician, being one who is emulated and firmly grounded in knowledge, intending thereby that others learn from him the excellence of patience in illness—nay, the excellence of gratitude—by showing that he regards illness as a blessing and gives thanks for it, speaking of it just as one speaks of blessings. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "When a sick person praises God and thanks Him, then mentions his pains, that is not complaint."

**The Third:** That one manifests [the illness] to display his incapacity (ʿajz) and his neediness (iftiqār) toward God. This is becoming of one to whom strength and courage are fitting and from whom incapacity would be deemed unlikely. It is related that during his illness, it was said to ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, "How are you?" He replied: "In good spirits." Some of those present exchanged glances, as if they disapproved, supposing this to be complaint. He then said: "Shall I show fortitude against God? I wish to manifest my incapacity and neediness"—despite what was known of his strength and ferocity. In this, he observed the etiquette taught him by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when ʿAlī, may God honor his face, fell ill and the Prophet heard him saying: "O God, grant me patience upon the trial"—and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "You have asked God for trial; rather ask God for well-being." {«عُرِضَتْ عَلَيْهِ مَفَاتِيحُ خَزَائِنِ السَّمَاءِ وَكُنُوزُ الْأَرْضِ فَرَدَّهَا»} (The keys of the treasures of heaven and the hoards of the earth were offered to him, and he refused them.) The hadith, "When a servant falls ill, God reveals to the two angels: 'See what he says to his visitors'"—has already been mentioned.

Some servants of God disapproved of visiting the sick out of fear of complaint and dread of excess in speech. Thus, some of them, when ill, would close their door and admit no one until they recovered, then would go out to them. Among these were Fuḍayl, Wahīb, and Bishr. Fuḍayl used to say: "I wish to fall ill with no visitors," and he said: "I dislike illness only because of the visitors." May God be pleased with him and with them all.

The Book of Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and Reliance (Tawakkul) is completed with the help of God and His gracious facilitation. It shall be followed, God willing, by:

**The Book of Love (Maḥabbah), Longing (Shawq), Intimacy (Uns), and Contentment (Riḍā)** — and God, Glorified and Exalted, is the Granter of success.

### || كتاب المحبة والشوق والأنس والرضا وهو الكتاب السادس من ربع المنجيات من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي نزه أوليائه عن الالتفات إلى زخرف الدنيا ونضرته وصفي
أسراهم من ملاحظة غير حضرته ثم استخلصها للعكوف على بساط عزته ثم تجلى لهم
بأسمائه وصفاته حتى أشرقت بأنوار معرفته ثم (2) حديث إذا مرض العبد أوحى
الله إلى الملكين انظرا ما يقول لعواده الحديث تقدم PageV04P293
كشف لهم عن سبحات وجهه حتى احترقت بنار محبته ثم احتجب عنها بكنه جلاله
حتى تاهت في بيداء كبريائه وعظمته فكلما اهتزت لملاحظة كنه الجلال غشيها من
الدهش ما اغبر في وجه العقل وبصيرته وكلما همت بالانصراف آيسة نوديت من
سرادقات الجمال صبرا أيها الآيس عن نيل الحق بجهله وعجلته فبقيت بين الرد
والقبول والصد والوصول غرقى في بحر معرفته ومحترقة بنار  محبته والصلاة على
محمد خاتم الأنبياء بكمال نبوته وعلى آله وأصحابه سادة الخلق وأئمته وقادة
الحق وأزمته وسلم كثيرا
أما بعد: فإن المحبة لله هي الغاية القصوى من المقامات والذروة العليا من
الدرجات فما بعد إدراك المحبة مقام إلا وهو ثمرة من ثمارها وتابع من
توابعها كالشوق والأنس والرضا وأخواتها ولا قبل المحبة مقام إلا وهو مقدمة
من مقدماتها كالتوبة والصبر والزهد وغيرها وسائر المقامات إن عز وجودها فلم
تخل القلوب عن الإيمان بإمكانها وأما محبة الله تعالى فقد عز الإيمان بها
حتى أنكر بعض العلماء إمكانها وقال: لا معنى لها إلا المواظبة على طاعة
الله تعالى وأما حقيقة المحبة فمحال إلا مع الجنس والمثال ولما أنكروا
المحبة أنكروا الأنس والشوق ولذة المناجاة وسائر لوازم الحب وتوابعه ولا بد
من كشف الغطاء عن هذا الأمر
ونحن نذكر في هذا الكتاب: بيان شواهد الشرع في المحبة ثم بيان حقيقتها
وأسبابها ثم بيان أن لا مستحق للمحبة إلا الله تعالى ثم بيان أن أعظم
اللذات لذة النظر إلى وجه الله تعالى ثم بيان سبب زيادة لذة النظر في
الآخرة على المعرفة في الدنيا ثم بيان الأسباب المقوية لحب الله تعالى ثم
بيان السبب في تفاوت الناس في الحب ثم بيان السبب في قصور الأفهام عن معرفة
الله تعالى ثم بيان معنى الشوق ثم بيان محبة الله تعالى للعبد ثم القول في
علامات محبة العبد لله تعالى ثم بيان معنى الأنس بالله تعالى ثم بيان معنى
الانبساط في الأنس ثم القول في معنى الرضا وبيان فضيلته ثم بيان حقيقته ثم
بيان أن الدعاء وكراهة المعاصي لا تناقضه وكذا الفرار من المعاصي ثم بيان
حكايات وكلمات للمحبين متفرقة فهذه جميع بيانات هذا الكتاب

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of steadfastness and permanence; the beloved is that which remains fixed in the heart, and love (maḥabbah) is the heart's unwavering attachment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, love of God is the soul's inclination toward the Necessary Being (al-wājib) by virtue of His perfection, not by virtue of sensory or imaginative appeal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) love requires genus and likeness (al-jins wa al-mithāl); metaphorical (majāz) love is obedience and devotion. Ghazali here exposes the error of reducing love to mere metaphor.
- Root: ش و ق (sh-w-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The stretching forth of the soul toward an absent beloved; a yearning that impels movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Longing (shawq) is only conceivable toward what is absent or veiled; it is a necessary concomitant of love when the beloved is not yet fully unveiled.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the soul's journeying toward its object; metaphorically for the believer's yearning for the vision of God (ru'yah).
- Root: أ ن س (ʾ-n-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Familiarity and the dispelling of estrangement; the heart's repose in the presence of the beloved.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intimacy (uns) is the heart's tranquility in witnessing the beloved's beauty, contrasted with the awe (haybah) that precedes full unveiling.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for social companionship; metaphorical for the soul's communion with God in private prayer (munājāh).
- Root: ر ض و (r-ḍ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Satisfaction and approval; the cessation of opposition to what the beloved decrees.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Contentment (riḍā) is the heart's acquiescence to divine decree (qaḍāʾ) without resentment, a station subsequent to love.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for agreement with another's will; metaphorical for the servant's total surrender to God's governance.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Inna and Its Sisters (al-ʿamal fī inna wa akhawātihā) — When the author states "فإن المحبة لله هي الغاية القصوى" (for love of God is the utmost goal), the particle inna governs the nominative subject (al-maḥabbah) and the predicate (al-ghāyah al-quṣwā) in the accusative, establishing a definitive, unqualified assertion that frames the entire treatise.
chapters.translation:
In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God, who purified His elect from turning toward the ornament of this world and its splendor, and who cleansed their innermost hearts from beholding anything other than His presence. Then He singled them out for dwelling upon the carpet of His majesty, and then He manifested Himself to them through His names and attributes until they shone with the lights of His knowledge. Then He unveiled to them the radiance of His countenance until they were consumed by the fire of His love. Then He veiled Himself from them by the very essence of His grandeur, until they wandered lost in the desert of His pride and greatness. So whenever they stirred to behold the essence of His majesty, there overwhelmed them a bewilderment that dimmed the face of the intellect and its insight. And whenever they resolved to turn away in despair, they were called from the pavilions of beauty: "Patience, O you who despair of attaining the Truth by your ignorance and haste!" So they remained between rejection and acceptance, between repulsion and arrival, drowned in the sea of His knowledge and consumed by the fire of His love. And may the blessings of God be upon Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, with the perfection of his prophethood, and upon his family and companions, the masters of creation and its leaders, the guides of truth and its reins — and abundant peace.

To proceed: Know that love of God (maḥabbah) is the utmost goal among the stations and the highest summit among the degrees. For after the attainment of love, there is no station except that it is a fruit of its fruits and a follower of its followers — such as longing (shawq), intimacy (uns), contentment (riḍā), and their sisters. And before love, there is no station except that it is a prelude among its preludes — such as repentance, patience, renunciation, and others. As for the rest of the stations, even if their existence is rare, the hearts have never been devoid of faith in their possibility. But as for the love of God — exalted is He — faith in its very possibility has become rare, to the point that some scholars denied its possibility and said: "It has no meaning other than persisting in obedience to God — exalted is He — and as for the reality of love, it is impossible except with genus and likeness." And because they denied love, they denied intimacy, longing, the delight of private communion (ludhdhat al-munājāh), and all the other necessary concomitants and followers of love. It is therefore imperative to lift the veil from this matter.

And we shall mention in this book: the exposition of the evidences of the Sacred Law concerning love; then the exposition of its reality and its causes; then the exposition that none deserves love except God — exalted is He; then the exposition that the greatest of delights is the delight of gazing upon the face of God — exalted is He; then the exposition of the cause of the increase of the delight of gazing in the Hereafter over knowledge in this world; then the exposition of the causes that strengthen the love of God — exalted is He; then the exposition of the cause of the disparity among people in love; then the exposition of the cause of the failure of intellects to comprehend the knowledge of God — exalted is He; then the exposition of the meaning of longing; then the exposition of God's love for His servant; then the discourse on the signs of the servant's love for God — exalted is He; then the exposition of the meaning of intimacy with God — exalted is He; then the exposition of the meaning of expansiveness in intimacy; then the discourse on the meaning of contentment and the exposition of its excellence; then the exposition of its reality; then the exposition that supplication and the aversion to sins do not contradict it, and likewise fleeing from sins; then the exposition of scattered narratives and sayings of the lovers. These, then, are all the expositions of this book.

اعلم أن الأمة مجمعة على أن الحب لله تعالى ولرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
فرض وكيف يفرض مالا وجود له وكيف يفسر الحب بالطاعة والطاعة تبع الحب
وثمرته فلا بد وأن يتقدم الحب  ثم بعد ذلك يطيع من أحب ويدل على إثبات الحب
لله تعالى قوله عز وجل يحبهم ويحبونه وقوله تعالى والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله
وهو دليل على إثبات الحب وإثبات التفاوت فيه وقد جعل رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم الحب لله من شرط الإيمان في أخبار كثيرة إذ قال أبو رزين
العقيلي: يا رسول الله ما الإيمان قال أن يكون الله ورسوله أحب إليك مما
سواهما (1) حديث لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يكون الله ورسوله أحب إليه مما سواهما
متفق عليه من حديث أنس بلفظ لا يجد أحد حلاوة الإيمان حتى أكون أحب إليه من
أهلاه وماله وذكر بزيادة (2) حديث لا يؤمن العبد حتى أكون أحب إليه من أهله
وماله ونفسه والناس أجمعين وفي رواية ومن نفسه متفق عليه من حديث أنس
واللفظ لمسلم دون قوله ومن نفسه وقال البخاري من والده وولده وله من حديث
عبد الله بن هشام: قال عمر يا رسول الله لأنت أحب إلي من كل شيء إلا نفسي
فقال لا والذي نفسي بيده حتى أكون أحب إليك من نفسك فقال عمر: فأنت الآن
والله أحب إلي من نفسي فقال: الآن يا عمر PageV04P294
نفسه كيف وقد قال تعالى قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم الآية وإنما
أجرى ذلك في معرض التهديد والإنكار وقد أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
بالمحبة فقال أحبوا الله لما يغذوكم به من نعمه وأحبوني لحب الله إياي (1)
حديث أحبوا الله لما غدوكم به من نعمه الحديث أخرجه الترمذي من حديث ابن
عباس وقال حسن غريب ويروى أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله إني أحبك فقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم استعد للفقر فقال إني أحب الله تعالى فقال استعد للبلاء (2)
حديث أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله إني أحبك فقال استعد للفقر الحديث أخرجه
الترمذي من حديث عبد الله بن منفل بلف فأعد للفقر تجفاف دون أخر الحديث
وقال حسن غريب وعن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: نظر النبي صلى الله  عليه وسلم إلى
مصعب بن عمير مقبلا وعليه إهاب كبش قد تنطق له فقال النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم انظروا إلى هذا الرجل الذي نور الله قلبه لقد رأيته بين أبويه يغذوانه
بأطيب الطعام والشراب فدعاه حب الله ورسوله إلى ما ترون (3) حديث عمر قال
نظر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى مصعب بن عمير مقبلا وعليه إهاب كبش قد
تنطق به الحديث أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية باسناد حسن
وفي الخبر المشهور إن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال لملك الموت إذ جاءه لقبض
روحه: هل رأيت خليلا يميت خليله فأوحى الله تعالى إليه: هل رأيت محبا يكره
لقاء حبيبه فقال يا ملك الموت الآن فاقبض (4) حديث ان ابراهيم قال لملك
الموت اذا جاءه ليقبض روحه هل رأبت خلالا يقبض خليله الحديث لم أجد له أصلا
(5) حديث قال أعرابي يا رسول الله متى الساعة قال ما أعددت لها الحديث متفق
عليه من حديث أنس ومن حديث أبي موسى وابن مسعود بنحوه وجاء أعرابي إلى
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله متى الساعة قال ما أعددت
لها فقال: ما أعددت لها كثير صلاة ولا صيام إلا أني أحب الله ورسوله فقال
له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المرء مع من أحب قال أنس: فما رأيت
المسلمين فرحوا بشيء بعد الإسلام فرحهم بذلك وقال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله
عنه من ذاق من خالص محبة الله تعالى شغله ذلك عن طلب الدنيا وأوحشه عن جميع
البشر وقال الحسن: من عرف ربه أحبه ومن عرف الدنيا زهد فيها والمؤمن لا
يلهو حتى يغفل فإذا تفكر حزن وقال أبو سليمان الداراني: إن من خلق الله
خلقا ما يشغلهم الجنان وما فيها من النعيم عنه فكيف يشتغلون عنه بالدنيا
ويروى أن عيسى عليه السلام مر بثلاثة نفر قد نحلت أبدانهم وتغيرت ألوانهم
فقال لهم: ما الذي بلغ بكم ما أرى فقالوا الخوف من النار فقال: حق على الله
أن يؤمن الخائف  ثم جاوزهم إلى ثلاثة آخرين فإذا هم أشد نحولا وتغيرا فقال:
ما الذي بلغ بكم ما أرى قالوا: الشوق إلى الجنة فقال حق على الله أن يعطيكم
ما ترجون ثم جاوزهم إلى ثلاثة آخرين فإذا هم أشد نحولا وتغيرا كأن وجوههم
المرائي من النور فقال: ما الذي بلغ بكم ما أرى قالوا: نحب الله عز وجل
فقال أنتم المقربون أنتم المقربون وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد: مررت برجل قائم
في الثلج فقلت أما تجد البرد فقال من شغله حب الله لم يجد البرد
وعن سري السقطي: تدعى الأمم يوم القيامة بأنبيائها عليهم السلام فيقال يا
أمة موسى ويا أمة عيسى ويا أمة محمد غير المحبين لله تعالى فإنهم ينادون يا
أولياء الله هلموا إلى الله سبحانه فتكاد قلوبهم تنخلع فرحا PageV04P295
وقال هرم بن حيان: المؤمن إذا عرف ربه عز وجل أحبه وإذا أحبه أقبل إليه
وإذا وجد حلاوة الإقبال إليه لم ينظر إلى الدنيا بعين الشهوة ولم ينظر إلى
الآخرة بعين الفترة وهي تحسره في الدنيا وتروحه في الآخرة وقال يحي ابن
معاذ عفوه يستغرق الذنوب فكيف رضوانه ورضوانه يستغرق الآمال فكيف حبه وحبه
يدهش العقول فكيف وده ووده ينسى ما دونه فكيف لطفه وفي بعض الكتب عبدي أنا
وحقك لك محب فبحقي عليك كن لي محبا وقال يحي بن معاذ: مثقال خردلة من الحب
أحب إلي من عبادة سبعين سنة بلا حب وقال يحي بن معاذ إلهي إني مقيم بفنائك
مشغول بثنائك صغيرا أخذتني إليك وسربلتني بمعرفتك وأمكنتني من لطفك ونقلتني
في الأحوال وقلبتني في الأعمال سترا وتوبة وزهدا وشوقا ورضا وحبا تسقيني من
حياضك وتهملني في رياضك ملازما لأمرك ومشغوفا بقولك ولما طر شاربي ولاح
طائري فكيف أنصرف اليوم عنك كبيرا وقد اعتدت هذا منك صغيرا فلي ما بقيت
حولك دندنة وبالضراعة إليك همهمة لأني محب وكل محب بحبيبه مشغوف وعن غير
حبيبه مصروف وقد ورد في حب الله تعالى من الأخبار والآثار مالا يدخل في حصر
حاصر  وذلك أمر ظاهر وإنما الغموض في تحقيق معناه فلنشتغل به
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to love," denoting a profound inclination of the heart toward that which is agreeable; al-ʿAyn adds the nuance of steadfastness and constancy in affection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, love (maḥabbah) for God is the soul's yearning for union with the Divine, rooted in knowledge (maʿrifah) of His perfections; it is the highest station of the servant's journey.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally (ḥaqīqah), love is an emotional state; metaphorically (majāz), it is expressed through obedience, yet the literal sense must precede the metaphorical, as obedience is but the fruit of love.
- Root: ط و ع (ṭ-w-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Denotes voluntary submission and compliance; the root implies an act performed willingly, not under compulsion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Obedience (ṭāʿah) is the outward manifestation of inner devotion, yet it cannot exist without the prior reality of love, which is its source.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for acts of compliance; here, it is a consequence (tabʿ) of love, not its definition.
- Root: و ج د (w-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To find, to experience, or to attain; also denotes a state of emotional intensity or ecstasy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, wujūd is the experiential realization of divine truths, often linked to the sweetness (ḥalāwah) of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "finding"; metaphorically, it signifies the heart's discovery of love's reality, as in the ḥadīth on tasting the sweetness of faith.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa Taʾkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — In the sentence "كيف يفرض مالا وجود له" (How can that be obligatory which has no existence?), the interrogative "كيف" is fronted for rhetorical emphasis, and the relative clause "مالا وجود له" is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) functioning as ṣilah, establishing a logical priority: existence precedes obligation.
chapters.translation:
Know that the Muslim community (ummah) is in consensus that love for God—mighty and majestic is He—and for His Messenger—peace be upon him—is an obligation (farḍ). Yet how could something be obligated that has no existence? And how could love be interpreted as obedience, when obedience is but a follower of love and its fruit? Thus, love must necessarily precede, and thereafter the one who loves obeys. Evidence for affirming love for God—mighty and majestic is He—is His saying—glorified and exalted is He: {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} (He loves them, and they love Him) (Q 5:54), and His saying—exalted is He: {«وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ»} (And those who believe are more intense in love for God) (Q 2:165). This is proof of affirming love and affirming its degrees of variance. The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—made love for God a condition of faith in numerous reports. For Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī said: "O Messenger of God, what is faith?" He said: "That God and His Messenger be more beloved to you than all else besides them." (1) The ḥadīth: "None of you believes until God and His Messenger are more beloved to him than all else besides them" is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), from the report of Anas, with the wording: "None finds the sweetness of faith until I am more beloved to him than his family and his wealth," with an addition mentioned. (2) The ḥadīth: "No servant believes until I am more beloved to him than his family, his wealth, his own self, and all people," and in one narration, "and than his own self," is agreed upon from the report of Anas; the wording is Muslim's, without his saying "and than his own self." Al-Bukhārī said: "from his father and his child." He has it from the report of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hishām: ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of God, you are more beloved to me than everything, except my own self." He said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until I am more beloved to you than your own self." ʿUmar said: "Then now, by God, you are more beloved to me than my own self." He said: "Now, O ʿUmar." PageV04P294

His own self—how [could that be] when He—exalted is He—has said: {«قُلْ إِنْ كَانَ آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوَانُكُمْ»} (Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers...) (Q 9:24), and He only brought this in the context of threat and disapproval. The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—commanded love, saying: "Love God for what He feeds you with of His blessings, and love me for God's love of me." (1) The ḥadīth: "Love God for what He feeds you with of His blessings..." is transmitted by al-Tirmidhī from the report of Ibn ʿAbbās, who deemed it ḥasan gharīb. It is narrated that a man said: "O Messenger of God, I love you." He—peace be upon him—said: "Prepare for poverty." He said: "I love God—exalted is He." He said: "Prepare for tribulation." (2) The ḥadīth that a man said: "O Messenger of God, I love you," and he said: "Prepare for poverty," is transmitted by al-Tirmidhī from the report of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Munfal, with the wording: "So prepare for poverty, a shield without an edge," and he deemed it ḥasan gharīb. And from ʿUmar—may God be pleased with him—he said: The Prophet—peace be upon him—looked at Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr approaching, wearing a sheepskin that he had wrapped around himself. The Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "Look at this man whose heart God has illuminated. I saw him between his parents, who fed him with the finest food and drink, yet love of God and His Messenger called him to what you see." (3) The ḥadīth of ʿUmar: "The Prophet looked at Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr approaching, wearing a sheepskin wrapped around him," is transmitted by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah with a good chain.

In the well-known report, Abraham—peace be upon him—said to the Angel of Death when he came to seize his soul: "Have you seen a beloved (khalīl) who kills his beloved?" So God—exalted is He—revealed to him: "Have you seen a lover who detests meeting his beloved?" He said: "O Angel of Death, now seize." (4) The ḥadīth that Abraham said to the Angel of Death when he came to seize his soul: "Have you seen a beloved who seizes his beloved?"—I have found no basis for it. (5) The ḥadīth: A Bedouin said: "O Messenger of God, when is the Hour?" He said: "What have you prepared for it?" is agreed upon from the report of Anas, and from the reports of Abū Mūsā and Ibn Masʿūd with similar wording. A Bedouin came to the Prophet—peace be upon him—and said: "O Messenger of God, when is the Hour?" He said: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "I have not prepared much prayer or fasting, except that I love God and His Messenger." The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—said to him: "A man is with the one he loves." Anas said: "I never saw the Muslims rejoice at anything after Islam as they rejoiced at that." Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq—may God be pleased with him—said: "Whoever tastes of the pure love of God—exalted is He—is distracted by it from seeking this world and is estranged from all of humanity." Al-Ḥasan said: "Whoever knows his Lord loves Him, and whoever knows this world abstains from it. The believer does not play until he becomes heedless; when he reflects, he grieves." Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "Among God's creation are those whom the Gardens and what they contain do not distract from Him—so how could they be distracted from Him by this world?" It is narrated that Jesus—peace be upon him—passed by three men whose bodies had withered and whose colors had changed. He said to them: "What has brought you to what I see?" They said: "Fear of the Fire." He said: "It is incumbent upon God to grant security to the fearful." Then he passed them to three others, and behold, they were more withered and changed. He said: "What has brought you to what I see?" They said: "Longing for the Garden." He said: "It is incumbent upon God to give you what you hope for." Then he passed them to three others, and behold, they were more withered and changed, as if their faces were mirrors of light. He said: "What has brought you to what I see?" They said: "We love God—mighty and majestic is He." He said: "You are the ones brought near; you are the ones brought near." ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd said: "I passed by a man standing in the snow and said: 'Do you not feel the cold?' He said: 'Whoever is occupied by love of God does not feel the cold.'"

And from Sarī al-Saqaṭī: The nations will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection by their prophets—peace be upon them—and it will be said: "O community of Moses, O community of Jesus, O community of Muhammad"—except the lovers of God—exalted is He—for they will be called: "O friends of God, come to God—glorified is He." Their hearts almost burst asunder with joy. PageV04P295

Haram ibn Ḥayyān said: "The believer, when he knows his Lord—mighty and majestic is He—loves Him; when he loves Him, he turns to Him; and when he finds the sweetness of turning to Him, he does not look at this world with the eye of desire, nor at the Hereafter with the eye of negligence—it grieves him in this world and comforts him in the Hereafter." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "His pardon encompasses sins—so how [great is] His good pleasure? And His good pleasure encompasses hopes—so how [great is] His love? And His love bewilders intellects—so how [great is] His affection? And His affection makes one forget all else—so how [great is] His gentleness?" In some scriptures: "My servant, I, by your right, am a lover of you—so by My right upon you, be a lover of Me." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "A mustard-seed's weight of love is more beloved to me than seventy years of worship without love." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "My God, I am dwelling in Your courtyard, occupied with Your praise. As a child, You took me to Yourself, clothed me with knowledge of You, granted me access to Your gentleness, and moved me through states and turned me through deeds—concealment, repentance, asceticism, longing, contentment, and love—watering me from Your pools and letting me roam in Your meadows, clinging to Your command and enraptured by Your speech. When my mustache grew and my bird took flight, how could I turn away from You today as an elder, having been accustomed to this from You as a child? So as long as I remain, around You is my humming, and with supplication to You is my murmur—for I am a lover, and every lover is enraptured with his beloved and turned away from all else." Reports and traditions concerning love for God—exalted is He—have come down that cannot be encompassed by any enumerator. That is a manifest matter; the obscurity lies only in realizing its true meaning—so let us occupy ourselves with that.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Love, Its Causes, and the True Meaning of the Servant’s Love for God Most High
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| بيان حقيقة المحبة وأسبابها وتحقيق معنى محبة العبد لله تعالى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core root denotes steadfastness, firmness, and the state of being established; from it derives the sense of love as a fixed, abiding inclination of the heart, not a fleeting emotion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, love (maḥabbah) is the soul’s inclination toward what is perceived as good and agreeable; for the servant toward God, it is the will’s total orientation to His commands and the heart’s delight in His remembrance, not a bodily passion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is the heart’s clinging to an object of desire; metaphorical (majāz) sense applies to God’s love for the servant as His gracious acceptance and favor, devoid of any change or need in the Divine essence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with inchoative (mubtadaʾ) and predicate (khabar) — the phrase «بيان حقيقة المحبة» functions as a definite inchoative, with the predicate implied in the section’s exposition, establishing a formal definitional framework.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us set forth the exposition of the reality of love, its causes, and the verification of the meaning of the servant’s love for God Most High. Know that love (maḥabbah) is a term whose reality must be investigated, for its true nature is often obscured by confusion. The heart’s inclination toward a thing is of two kinds: one is the inclination of desire (shawq) toward what brings pleasure or benefit, and this is shared by all sentient beings; the other is the inclination of affirmation (taṣdīq) and reverence (taʿẓīm) toward what is perceived as perfect and majestic, and this is peculiar to those who know. The love of the servant for God is not of the first kind, for God is not an object of sensory pleasure nor of bodily benefit; rather, it is of the second kind, arising from the soul’s recognition of His absolute perfection, His boundless majesty, and His all-encompassing beneficence. Thus, the reality of this love is the heart’s serene repose (sukūn) in the contemplation of the Beloved, the will’s utter compliance with His decree, and the aversion of the soul from all that opposes His command. Its causes are three: the perception of beauty (jamāl), the experience of beneficence (iḥsān), and the witness of perfection (kamāl) — and all three converge in God alone, for He is the Beautiful, the Beneficent, the Perfect, without any deficiency or peer. Therefore, whoever knows Him truly cannot but love Him necessarily, and the measure of love is the measure of knowledge (maʿrifah); where knowledge is weak, love is weak, and where knowledge is strong, love overwhelms the heart and governs all its movements.

chapters.title_en: The Reality of Love, Its Conditions, Causes, and Its True Meaning with Respect to God
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن المطلب من هذا الفصل لا ينكشف إلا بمعرفة حقيقة المحبة في نفسها
ثم معرفة شروطها وأسبابها ثم النظر بعد ذلك في تحقيق معناها في حق الله
تعالى: فأول ما ينبغي أن يتحقق أنه لا يتصور محبة إلا بعد معرفة وإدراك إذ
لا يحب الإنسان إلا ما يعرفه ولذلك لم يتصور أن يتصف بالحب جماد بل هو من
خاصية الحي المدرك ثم المدركات في انقسامها تنقسم إلى ما يوافق طبع المدرك
ويلائمه ويلذه وإلى ما ينافيه وينافره ويؤلمه وإلى ما لا يؤثر فيه بإيلام
وإلذاذ فكل ما في إدراكه لذة وراحة فهو محبوب عند المدرك وما في إدراكه ألم
فهو مبغوض عند المدرك وما يخلو عن استعقاب ألم ولذة لا يوصف بكونه محبوبا
ولا مكروها فإذن كل لذيذ محبوب عند الملتذ به ومعنى كونه محبوبا أن في
الطبع ميلا إليه ومعنى كونه مبغوضا أن في الطبع نفرة عنه فالحب عبارة عن
ميل الطبع إلى الشيء الملذ فإن تأكد ذلك الميل وقوي سمي عشقا والبغض عبارة
عن نفرة الطبع عن المؤلم المتعب فإذا قوي سمي مقتا فهذا أصل في حقيقة معنى
الحب لا بد من معرفته
الأصل الثاني أن الحب لما كان تابعا للإدراك والمعرفة انقسم لا محالة
بحسب انقسام المدركات والحواس فلكل حاسة إدراك لنوع من المدركات ولكل واحد
منها لذة في بعض المدركات وللطبع بسبب تلك اللذة ميل إليها فكانت محبوبات
عند الطبع السليم فلذة العين في الإبصار وإدراك المبصرات الجميلة والصور
المليحة الحسنة المستلذة ولذة الأذن في النغمات الطيبة الموزونة ولذة الشم
في الروائح الطيبة ولذة الذوق في الطعوم ولذة اللمس في اللين والنعومة
ولما كانت هذه المدركات بالحواس ملذة كانت محبوبة أي كان للطبع السليم
ميل إليها حتى قال رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم حبب إلي من دنياكم ثلاث: الطيب
والنساء وجعل قرة عيني في الصلاة  فسمى الطيب محبوبا ومعلوم انه لا حظ للعين
والسمع فيه بل للشم فقط وسمى النساء محبوبات ولاحظ فبهن إلا للبصر واللمس
دون // حديث حبب إلي من دنياكم ثلاث: الطيب والنساء أخرجه النسائي من حديث
أنس دون قوله ثلاث وقد تقدم
PageV04P296
الشم والذوق والسمع وسمى الصلاة قرة عين وجعلها أبلغ المحبوبات ومعلوم
أنه ليس تحظى بها الحواس الخمس بل حس سادس مظنته القلب لا يدركه ألا من كان
له قلب ولذات الحواس الخمس تشارك فيها البهائم الإنسان فإن كان الحب مقصورا
على مدركات الحواس الخمس حتى يقال إن الله تعالى لا يدرك بالحواس ولا يتمثل
في الخيال فلا يحب فإذن قد بطلت خاصية الإنسان وما تميز به من الحس السادس
الذي يعبر عنه إما بالعقل أو بالنور أو بالقلب أو بما شئت من العبارات فلا
مشاحة فيه وهيهات فالبصيرة الباطنة أقوى من البصر الظاهر والقلب أشد إدراكا
من العين وجمال المعاني المدركة بالعقل أعظم من جمال الصور الظاهرة للأبصار
فتكون لا محالة لذة القلب بما يدركه من الأمور الشريفة الإلهية التي تجل عن
أن تدركها الحواس أتم وأبلغ فيكون ميل الطبع السليم والعقل الصحيح إليه
أقوى ولا معنى للحب إلا الميل إلى ما في إدراكه لذة كما سيأتي تفصيله فلا
ينكر إذن حب الله تعالى إلا من قعد به القصور في درجة البهائم فلم يجاوز
إدراك الحواس أصلا
الأصل الثالث أن الإنسان لا يخفى أنه يحب نفسه ولا يخفى أنه قد يحب غيره
لأجل نفسه وهل يتصور أن يحب غيره لذاته لا لأجل نفسه هذا مما قد يشكل على
الضعفاء حتى يظنون أنه لا يتصور أن يحب الإنسان غيره لذاته ما لم يرجع منه
حظ إلى المحب سوى إدراك ذاته والحق أن ذلك متصور وموجود فلنبين أسباب
المحبة وأقسامها وبيانه أن المحبوب الأول عند كل حي نفسه وذاته ومعنى حبه
لنفسه أن في طبعه ميلا إلى دوام وجوده ونفرة عن عدمه وهلاكه لأن المحبوب
بالطبع هو الملائم للمحب وأي شيء أتم  ملاءمة من نفسه ودوام وجوده وأي شيء
أعظم مضادة ومنافرة له من عدمه وهلاكه فلذلك يحب الإنسان دوام الوجود ويكره
الموت والقتل لا لمجرد ما يخافه بعد الموت ولا لمجرد الحذر من سكرات الموت
بل لو اختطف من غير ألم وأميت من غير ثواب ولا عقاب لم يرض به وكان كارها
لذلك ولا يحب الموت والعدم المحض إلا لمقاساة ألم في الحياة ومهما كان
مبتلى ببلاء فمحبوبه زوال البلاء فإن أحب العدم لم يحبه لأته عدم بل لأن
فيه زوال البلاء فالهلاك والعدم ممقوت ودوام الوجود محبوب وكما أن دوام
الوجود محبوب فكمال الوجود أيضا محبوب لان الناقص فاقد للكمال والنقص عدم
بالإضافة إلى القدر المفقود وهو هلاك بالنسبة إليه والهلاك والعدم ممقوت في
الصفات وكمال الوجود كما أنه ممقوت في أصل الذات ووجود صفات الكمال محبوب
كما أن دوام أصل الوجود محبوب وهذه غريزة في الطباع بحكم سنة الله تعالى
ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا
فإذن المحبوب الأول للإنسان ذاته ثم سلامة أعضاءه ثم ماله وولده وعشيرته
وأصدقائه فالأعضاء محبوبة وسلامتها مطلوبة لأن كمال الوجود ودوام الوجود
موقوف عليها والمال محبوب لأنه أيضا آلة في دوام الوجود وكماله وكذا سائر
الأسباب فالإنسان يحب هذه الأشياء لا لأعيانها بل لارتباط حظه في دوام
الوجود وكماله بها حتى إنه ليحب ولده وإن كان لا يناله منه حظ بل يتحمل
المشاق لأجله لأنه يخلفه في الوجود بعد عدمه فيكون في بقاء نسله نوع بقاء
له فلفرط حبه في بقاء نفسه يحب بقاء من هو قائم مقامه وكأنه جزء منه لما
عجز عن الطمع في بقاء نفسه أبدا نعم لو خير بين قتله وقتل ولده وكان طبعه
باقيا على اعتداله آثر بقاء نفسه على بقاء ولده لأن بقاء ولده يشبه بقاءه
من وجه وليس هو بقاء المحقق وكذلك حبه لأقاربه وعشيرته يرجع إلى حبه لكمال
نفسه فإنه يرى نفسه كثيرا بهم قويا بسببهم متجملا بكمالهم فإن العشيرة
والمال والأسباب الخارجة كالجناح المكمل للإنسان  وكمال الوجود ودوامه محبوب
بالطبع لا محالة فإذن المحبوب الأول عند كل حي ذاته وكمال ذاته ودوام
PageV04P297
ذلك كله والمكروه عنده ضد ذلك فهذا هو أول الأسباب
السبب الثاني: الإحسان فإن الإنسان عبد الإحسان وقد جبلت القلوب على حب
من أحسن إليها وبغض من أساء إليها وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم
لا تجعل لفاجر علي يدا فيحبه قلبي (1) حديث: كان يعجبه الخضرة والماء
الجاري أخرجه أبو نعيم في الطب النبوي من حديث ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم كان يحب أن ينظر إلى الخضرة وإلى الماء الجاري وإسناده ضعيف (2)
حديث إن الله جميل يحب الجمال رواه مسلم في أثناء حديث لابن مسعود
الأصل الرابع في بيان معنى الحسن والجمال اعلم أن المحبوس في مضيق
الخيالات والمحسوسات ربما يظن أنه لا معنى للحسن والجمال إلا تناسب الخلقة
والشكل وحسن اللون وكون البياض مشربا بالحمرة وامتداد القامة إلى غير ذلك
مما يوصف من جمال شخص الإنسان فإن الحسن الأغلب على الخلق حسن الإبصار
وأكثر التفاتهم PageV04P298
إلى صور الأشخاص فيظن أن ما ليس مبصرا ولا متخيلا ولا متشكلا ولا ملونا
مقدر فلا يتصور حسنه وإذا لم يتصور حسنه لم يكن في إدراكه لذة فلم يكن
محبوبا وهذا خطأ ظاهر فإن الحسن ليس مقصورا على مدركات البصر ولا على تناسب
الخلقة وامتزاج البياض بالحمرة فإنا نقول هذا خط حسن وهذا صوت حسن وهذا فرس
حسن بل نقول هذا ثوب حسن وهذا إناء حسن فأي معنى لحسن الصوت والخط وسائر
الأشياء إن لم يكن الحسن إلا في الصورة ومعلوم أن العين تستلذ بالنظر إلى
الخط الحسن والأذن تستلذ استماع النغمات الحسنة الطيبة وما من شيء من
المدركات إلا وهو منقسم إلى حسن وقبيح فما معنى الحسن الذي تشترك فيه هذه
الأشياءفلا بد من البحث عنه وهذا البحث يطول ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة
الإطناب فيه فنصرح بالحق ونقول: كل شيء فجماله وحسنه في أن يحضر كماله
اللائق به الممكن له فإذا  كان جميع كمالاته الممكنة حاضرة فهو في غاية
الجمال وإن كان الحاضر بعضها فله من الحسن والجمال بقدر ما حضر فالفرس
الحسن هو الذي جمع كل ما يليق بالفرس من هيئة وشكل ولون وحسن عدو وتيسر كر
وفر عليه والخط الحسن كل ما جمع كل ما يليق بالخط من تناسب الحروف وتوازيها
واستقامة ترتيبها وحسن انتظامها ولكل شيء كمال يليق به وقد يليق بغير ضد
فحسن كل شيء في كماله الذي يليق به فلا يحسن الإنسان بما يحسن به الفرس ولا
يحسن الخط بما يحسن به الصوت ولا تحسن الأواني بما تحسن به الثياب وكذلك
سائر الأشياء
فإن قلت: فهذه الأشياء وإن لم تدرك جميعها بحس البصر مثل الأصوات والطعوم
فإنها لا تنفك عن إدراك الحواس لها فهي محسوسات وليس ينكر الحسن والجمال
للمحسوسات ولا ينكر حصول اللذة بإدراك حسنها وإنما ينكر ذلك في غير المدرك
بالحواس فاعلم أن الحسن والجمال موجود في غير المحسوسات إذ يقال: هذا خلق
حسن وهذا علم حسن وهذه سيرة حسنة وهذه أخلاق جميلة وإنما الأخلاق الجميلة
يراد بها العلم والعقل والعفة والشجاعة والتقوى والكرم والمروءة وسائر خلال
الخير وشيء من هذه الصفات لا يدرك بالحواس الخمس بل يدرك بنور البصيرة
الباطنة وكل هذه الخلال الجميلة محبوبة والموصوف بها محبوب بالطبع عند من
عرف صفاته وآية ذلك وأن الأمر كذلك أن الطباع مجبولة على حب الأنبياء صلوات
الله عليهم وعلى حب الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم مع أنهم لم يشاهدوا بل حب
أرباب المذاهب مثل الشافعي وأبي حنيفة ومالك وغيرهم حتى أن الرجل قد يجاوز
به حبه لصاحب مذهبه حد العشق فيحمله ذلك على أن تنفق جميع ماله في نصرة
مذهبه والذب عنه ويخاطر بروحه في قتال من يطعن في إمامه ومتبوعه فكم من دم
أريق في نصرة أرباب المذاهب وليت شعري من يحب الشافعي مثلا فلم يحبه ولم
يشاهد قط صورته ولو شاهده ربما لم يستحسن صورته فاستحسانه الذي حمله على
إفراط الحب هو  لصورته الباطنة لا لصورته الظاهرة فإن صورته الظاهرة قد
انقلبت ترابا مع التراب وإنما يحبه لصفاته الباطنة من الدين والتقوى وغزارة
العلم والإحاطة بمدارك الدين وانتهاضه لإفادة علم الشرع ولنشره هذه الخيرات
في العالم وهذه أمور جميلة لا يدرك جمالها إلا بنور البصيرة فأما الحواس
فقاصرة عنها وكذلك من يحب أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه ويفضله على غيره أو
يحب عليا رضي الله عنه ويفضله ويتعصب له فلا يحبهم إلا لاستحسان صورهم
الباطنة من العلم والدين والتقوى والشجاعة والكرم وغيره فمعلوم أن من يحب
الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه مثلا ليس يحب عظمه ولحمه وجلده وأطرافه وشكله إذ
كل ذلك زال وتبدل وانعدم ولكن بقي ما كان الصديق به صديقا وهي الصفات
المحمودة التي هي مصادر السير الجميلة فكان
PageV04P299
الحب باقيا ببقاء تلك الصفات مع زوال جميع الصور وتلك الصفات ترجع جملتها
إلى العلم والقدرة إذا علم حقائق الأمور وقدر على حمل نفسه عليها بقهر
شهواته فجميع خلال الخير يتشعب على هذين الوصفين وهما غير مدركين بالحس
ومحلهما من جملة البدن جزء لا يتجزأ فهو المحبوب بالحقيقة وليس للجزء الذي
لا يتجزأ صورة وشكل ولون يظهر للبصر حتى يكون محبوبا لأجله فإذن الجمال
موجود في السير ولو صدرت السيرة الجميلة من غير علم وبصيرة لم يوجب ذلك حبا
فالمحبوب مصدر السير الجميلة وهي الأخلاق الحميدة والفضائل الشريفة وترجع
جملتها إلى كمال العلم والقدرة وهو محبوب بالطبع وغير مدرك بالحواس حتى إن
الصبي المخلى وطبعه إذ أردنا أن نحبب إليه غائبا أو حاضرا حيا أو ميتا لم
يكن لنا سبيل إلا بالإطناب في وصفه بالشجاعة والكرم والعلم وسائر الحضال
الحميدة فمهما اعتقد ذلك لم يتمالك في نفسه ولم يقدر أن لا يحبه فهل فل غلب
الصحابة به رضي الله تعالى عنهم وبغض ابي جهل وبعض إبليس لعنه الله إلا
بالإطناب في وصف المحاسن والمقابح التي لا تدرك بالحواس بل لما وصف الناس
حاتما بالسخاء ووصفوا خالدا بالشجاعة أحبتهم القلوب حبا  ضروريا وليس ذلك عن
نظر إلى صورة محسوسة ولا عن حظ يناله المحب منهم بل إذا حكي من سيرة بعض
الملوك في بعض أقطار الأرض العدل والإحسان وإفاضة الخير غلب حبه على القلوب
مع اليأس من انتشار إحسانه إلى المحبين لبعد المزار ونأي الديار فإذن ليس
حب الإنسان مقصورا على من أحسن إليه بل المحسن في نفسه محبوب وإن كان لا
ينتهي قط إحسانه إلى المحب لأن كل جمال وحسن فهو محبوب والصورة ظاهرة
وباطنة والحسن والجمال يشملهما وتدرك الصور الظاهرة بالبصر الظاهر والصور
الباطنة بالبصيرة الباطنة فمن حرم البصيرة الباطنة لا يدركها ولا يلتذ بها
ولا يحبها ولا يميل إليها ومن كانت الباطنة أغلب عليه من الحواس الظاهرة
كان حبه للمعاني الباطنة أكثر من حبه للمعاني الظاهرة فشتان بين من يحب
نقشا مصورا على الحائط لجمال صورته الظاهرة وبين من يحب نبيا من الأنبياء
لجمال صورته الباطنة
السبب الخامس: المناسبة الخفية بين المحب والمحبوب إذ رب شخصين تتأكد
المحبة بينهما لا بسبب جمال أو حظ ولكن بمجرد تناسب الأرواح كمال قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم فما تعارف منها ائتلف وما تناكر منها اختلف (1) حديث فما
تعارف منها ائتلف أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابي هريرة وقد تقدم في آداب الصحبة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b)
