قال أبو تراب النخشبى في  علامات المحبة أبياتا
لا تخدعن فللحبيب دلائل ... ولديه من تحف الحبيب وسائل
منها تنعمه بمر بلائه ... وسروره في كل ما هو فاعل
فالمنع منه عطية مقبولة ... والفقر إكرام وبر عاجل
ومن الدلائل أي ترى من عزمه ... طوع الحبيب وإن ألح العاذل
ومن الدلائل أن يرى متبسما ... والقلب فيه من الحبيب بلابل
ومن الدلائل أن يرى متفهما ... لكلام من يحظى لديه السائل
ومن الدلائل أن يرى متقشفا ... متحفظا من كل ما هو قائل
وقال يحيى بن معاذ
ومن الدلائل أن تراه مشمرا ... في خرقتين على شطوط الساحل
ومن الدلائل حزنه ونحيبه ... جوف الظلام فما له من عاذل
ومن الدلائل أن تراه مسافرا ... نحو الجهاد وكل فعل فاضل
ومن الدلائل زهده فيما يرى ... من دار ذل والنعيم الزائل
ومن الدلائل أن تراه باكيا ... أن قد رآه على قبيح فعائل
ومن االدلائل أن تراه مسلما ... كل الأمور إلى المليك العادل
ومن الدلائل أن تراه راضيا ... بمليكه في كل حكم نازل
ومن الدلائل ضحكه بين الورى ... والقلب محزون كقلب الثاكل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "love" (al-wudd) — the heart's inclination toward what pleases it; al-ʿAyn adds the nuance of "purity" (ṣafāʾ) and "whiteness" (bayāḍ), suggesting love as the heart's unblemished devotion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, maḥabbah is the soul's yearning for the Beloved (Allah) — a station (maqām) of the ṣiddīqūn, distinct from mere desire (shawq) or hope (rajāʾ), rooted in knowledge (maʿrifah) of the Divine attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) love is the heart's inclination; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends it to actions and states that "testify" to love, e.g., "love of meeting" (ḥubb liqāʾ) as a sign, not the essence.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Certain knowledge (yaqīn) that distinguishes truth from falsehood; al-ʿAyn notes ʿilm as the "trace" (athar) left by knowing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm is the soul's apprehension of reality as it is — the foundation of maʿrifah, which in turn generates love; ignorance (jahl) is its opposite and breeds false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal knowledge vs. metaphorical "knowledge" as tested conviction — the text uses ʿilm to demand proof (burhān) for love's claim.
- Root: م-و-ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Death as cessation of life; al-ʿAyn adds the nuance of "stillness" (sukūn) — the body's final repose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, death is the soul's separation from the body — a transition (intiqāl) to the abode of recompense; love of death signals love of meeting (liqāʾ) the Beloved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal death vs. metaphorical "death" as annihilation of the ego's desires — the text uses it literally as the gate to vision (mushāhadah).
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remembrance, mention; al-ʿAyn notes dhikr as the tongue's utterance and the heart's presence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dhikr is the heart's vigilance against forgetfulness (ghaflah) — the sign of love, as the lover constantly remembers the Beloved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal remembrance (tongue) vs. metaphorical (heart's constant awareness) — the text treats both as inseparable signs of love.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab (Coordination on the Cause) — In the sentence "حب لقاء الحبيب بطريق الكشف والمشاهدة" (love of meeting the Beloved through unveiling and vision), the prepositional phrase is coordinated to the cause, showing that love's object is the vision itself, not mere meeting. Also, Al-Istiṭrād (Digression) — The text digresses from signs to examples (e.g., Abū Ḥudhayfah's marriage) to illustrate the principle of graded love, a rhetorical device Sībawayh notes for emphasis.
chapters.translation:
Know that everyone claims love (maḥabbah) — and how easy is the claim, and how rare is the reality! A person must not be deceived by the devil's dissimulation (talbīs) and the soul's delusion whenever it claims love for Allah the Exalted, unless he tests it by the signs and demands from it proofs and evidences.

Love is a goodly tree whose root is firm and whose branch is in the sky; its fruits appear in the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. Those effects overflowing from it indicate, upon the heart and the limbs, love — just as smoke indicates fire, and fruits indicate trees. And they are many.

Among them is the love of meeting the Beloved by way of unveiling (kashf) and vision (mushāhadah) in the Abode of Peace. For it is inconceivable that the heart loves a beloved without loving to see him and meet him. And when one knows that there is no arrival except by departing from this world and leaving it through death, then he ought to be a lover of death, not fleeing from it. For the lover does not find burdensome the journey from his homeland to the resting-place of his beloved, so as to delight in beholding him. And death is the key to meeting and the door of entry into vision.

The Prophet ﷺ said: «من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه» (Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him). And Ḥudhayfah said at death: "A beloved has come upon destitution; he who regrets has not succeeded."

Some of the Salaf said: "There is no trait more beloved to Allah to be in the servant, after love of meeting Allah, than abundance of prostration." So he placed love of meeting Allah above prostration.

Allah the Glorified has made killing in the path of Allah a condition for the truth of sincerity in love, where they said, "We love Allah" — so He made killing in His path and seeking martyrdom its sign. He said the Exalted: {إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا} (Indeed Allah loves those who fight in His path in ranks), and He said the Mighty and Majestic: {يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون} (They fight in the path of Allah, so they kill and are killed).

And in the testament of Abū Bakr to ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both): "The truth is heavy, and despite its heaviness it is wholesome; falsehood is light, and despite its lightness it is putrid. If you preserve my testament, then no absent thing will be more beloved to you than death — and it will overtake you. And if you waste my testament, then no absent thing will be more hateful to you than death — and you will not escape it."

It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who said: My father told me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh said to him on the day of Uḥud: "Shall we not call upon Allah?" So they withdrew to a corner, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh supplicated, saying: "O Lord, I swear to You that if I meet the enemy tomorrow, let me meet a man of severe might and severe anger, so that I fight him for Your sake and he fights me, then he takes me and cuts off my nose and ears and rips open my belly. Then when I meet You tomorrow, You say: 'O ʿAbd Allāh, who cut off your nose and ears?' So I say: 'For Your sake, O Lord, and for Your Messenger.' Then You say: 'You have spoken truthfully.'" Saʿd said: "I saw him at the end of the day, and his nose and ears were hanging on a string." Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "I hope that Allah will fulfill his last oath as He fulfilled his first."

Al-Thawrī and Bishr al-Ḥāfī used to say: "None hates death except one with a tainted heart (murīb), for the beloved, in every case, does not hate meeting his beloved."

Al-Buwayṭī said to some ascetics: "Do you love death?" And he seemed to hesitate. He said: "If you were truthful, you would love it," and he recited the saying of the Exalted: {فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين} (So wish for death if you are truthful). The man said: "But the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Let none of you wish for death.'" He replied: "He only said that due to a harm that befell him, because contentment with Allah's decree is better than seeking escape from it."

If you say: "One who does not love death — is it conceivable that he loves Allah?" I say: Dislike of death may be due to love of this world and regret over parting from family, wealth, and children. This contradicts the perfection of love for Allah the Exalted, because perfect love is that which engulfs the entire heart. But it is not far that one, along with love of family and children, has a weak admixture of love for Allah the Exalted. For people differ in love. And evidence of this difference is what is narrated: When Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams married his sister Fāṭimah to Sālim, his freed slave, Quraysh reproached him for that, saying: "You have married a noblewoman of the noblewomen of Quraysh to a freed slave?" He said: "By Allah, I have married her to him, and I know he is better than her." His saying this was harder on them than his deed. They said: "How so, when she is your sister and he is your freed slave?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever wishes to look at a man who loves Allah with all his heart, let him look at Sālim.'" This indicates that among people are those who do not love Allah with all their heart — rather, they love Him and also love others. Hence, his bliss in meeting Allah upon arrival to Him is according to his love, and his torment in parting from this world at death is according to his love for it.

As for the second cause of dislike: it is that the servant be at the beginning of the station of love, and he does not dislike death itself, but rather dislikes its hastiness before he has prepared for meeting Allah. This does not indicate weakness of love. It is like the lover to whom news comes of his beloved's arrival, and he wishes his arrival to be delayed an hour so he may prepare his house for him and arrange his means, then meet him as he desires, with the heart empty of distractions and the back light of obstacles. Dislike for this reason does not contradict the perfection of love at all. Its sign is persistence in action and the engrossment of concern in preparation.

Among them is that he prefer what Allah the Exalted loves over what he loves, in his outward and inward. So he endures the hardships of action, avoids following caprice (hawā), turns away from the ease of laziness, and remains constant in obedience to Allah, drawing near to Him through supererogatory acts (nawāfil), seeking with Him the excellences of degrees — just as the lover seeks increased closeness in the heart of his beloved. Allah the Exalted has described the lovers with preference (īthār), saying: {يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة} (They love those who migrated to them, and find in their breasts no need for what they were given, and prefer others over themselves even if they are in poverty). And whoever remains settled upon following caprice — his beloved is what he desires. Rather, the lover abandons his own desire, as was said:

"I desire his union, and he desires my separation — so I abandon what I desire for what he desires."

Indeed, when love prevails, it suppresses caprice, leaving no delight for it except in the Beloved. As it is narrated that when Zulaykhā believed and Yūsuf (peace be upon him) married her, she withdrew from him and devoted herself to worship, cutting herself off to Allah the Exalted. He would call her to his bed by day, and she would defer him to night; when he called her by night, she put him off to day, saying: "O Yūsuf, I loved you before I knew Him; but now that I have known Him, His love has left no love for other than Him, and I desire no substitute for Him." Until he said to her: "Allah the Glorified has commanded me to this, and informed me that He will bring forth from you two sons and make them prophets." She said: "Since Allah the Exalted has commanded you to this and made me a path to Him, then it is obedience to the command of Allah the Exalted." At that she settled with him. So whoever loves Allah does not disobey Him. Hence Ibn al-Mubārak said concerning this:

"You disobey God while you profess His love — this, by my life, is a strange deed!
If your love were true, you would obey Him — indeed, the lover is obedient to his beloved."

In this meaning it was also said:

"And I abandon what I desire for what He has desired — so I am content with what You are content with, even if my soul is displeased."

Sahl (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The sign of love is preferring Him over yourself. And not everyone who acts in obedience to Allah the Mighty and Majestic becomes a lover; rather, the lover is one who avoids the prohibitions." And it is as he said, because his love for Allah the Exalted is the cause of Allah's love for him, as He said the Exalted: {يحبهم ويحبونه} (He loves them and they love Him). And when Allah loves him, He takes charge of him and grants him victory over his enemies. His enemy is only his own soul and his lusts, so Allah does not abandon him nor entrust him to his caprice and lusts. Hence He said the Exalted: {والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا} (And Allah knows best your enemies; sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper).

If you say: "Does disobedience contradict the root of love?" I say: It contradicts its perfection, not its root. How many a person loves himself while sick, and loves health, yet eats what harms him despite knowing it harms him — and that does not indicate absence of self-love. Rather, knowledge may weaken and lust may prevail, so he becomes unable to fulfill the due of love. Evidence for this is what is narrated: Nuʿaymān was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ frequently, and he would have him flogged for a sin he committed, until one day he was brought and he flogged him. A man cursed him, saying: "How often is Nuʿaymān brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" The Prophet ﷺ said: «لا تلعنه فإنه يحب الله ورسوله» (Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger). So disobedience did not remove him from love — rather, disobedience removes him from the perfection of love. Some of the knowers (ʿārifūn) said: "When faith is in the outer part of the heart, one loves Allah with a moderate love; when it enters the core of the heart (suwaydāʾ), he loves Him with a complete love and abandons sins." In sum, in the claim of love there is danger. Hence al-Fuḍayl said: "When it is said to you, 'Do you love Allah the Exalted?' — be silent. For if you say 'No,' you disbelieve; and if you say 'Yes,' your description is not the description of the lovers. So beware of being hated (maqt)." Some scholars said: "There is no bliss in Paradise higher than the bliss of the people of knowledge (maʿrifah) and love, and no torment in Hell severer than the torment of one who claimed knowledge and love without realizing any of that."

Among them is that he be engrossed in the remembrance (dhikr) of Allah the Exalted — his tongue not ceasing from it, and his heart never empty of it. For whoever loves something inevitably mentions it much, and mentions what pertains to it. So the sign of love for Allah is love of His remembrance, love of the Qurʾān which is His speech, love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and love of everyone attributed to him. For whoever loves a person loves his dog and his neighborhood. When love strengthens, it extends from the beloved to everything that surrounds him, encompasses him, and pertains to his causes. This is not partnership in love — for whoever loves the beloved's messenger because he is his messenger, and his speech because it is his speech, has not extended his love to another; rather, it is evidence of the perfection of his love. And whoever's love for Allah prevails over his heart loves all of Allah's creation, because they are His creation. How then would he not love the Qurʾān, the Messenger, and Allah's righteous servants? We have already mentioned the verification of this in the Book of Brotherhood and Companionship. Hence He said the Exalted: {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله} (Say: If you love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you). And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «أحبوا الله لما يغذوكم به من نعمه وأحبوني لله تعالى» (Love Allah for what He feeds you of His blessings, and love me for Allah the Exalted). Sufyān said — regarding the ḥadīth "Love Allah": "Whoever loves one who loves Allah the Exalted has loved Allah; and whoever honors one who honors Allah the Exalted has honored Allah."

It is narrated from one of the aspirants (murīdūn): "I had found the sweetness of intimate converse (munājāt) at the age of aspiration, so I persisted in reciting the Qurʾān night and day. Then a period of languor (fatrah) overtook me, and I ceased recitation." He said: "I heard a caller say in a dream: 'If you claim to love Me, why have you been harsh to My Book? Have you not pondered what is in it of My subtle reproach?'" He said: "I awoke, and love of the Qurʾān had been imbued into my heart, so I returned to my state."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "None of you should ask about himself except through the Qurʾān. If he loves the Qurʾān, he loves Allah the Mighty and Majestic; and if he does not love the Qurʾān, he does not love Allah."

Sahl (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The sign of love for Allah is love of the Qurʾān; the sign of love for Allah and love of the Qurʾān is love of the Prophet ﷺ; the sign of love for the Prophet ﷺ is love of the Sunnah; the sign of love of the Sunnah is love of the Hereafter; the sign of love of the Hereafter is hatred of this world; and the sign of hatred of this world is taking from it only provision and sufficiency for the Hereafter."

Among them is that his intimacy (uns) be in solitude (khalwah) and intimate converse with Allah the Exalted and recitation of His Book. So he persists in night prayer (tahajjud), seizing the stillness of the night and the purity of the time by the removal of obstacles. The least degree of love is delighting in solitude with the Beloved and savoring intimate converse with Him. Whoever finds sleep and engagement in conversation more delightful and pleasant than intimate converse with Allah — how can his love be sound? It was said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham when he descended from the mountain: "From where have you come?" He said: "From intimacy with Allah." And in the reports of Dāwūd (peace be upon him): "Do not seek intimacy with any of My creation, for I have only cut off from Me two men: a man who deemed My reward slow, so he was cut off; and a man who forgot Me and was content with his state." The sign of that is his being left to himself and left in this world bewildered. And whenever he is intimate with other than Allah, to the extent of his intimacy with other than Allah he is estranged from Allah the Exalted and fallen from the degree of His love.

In the story of Barkh — the black servant through whom Mūsā (peace be upon him) sought rain — Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (peace be upon him): "Barkh is an excellent servant of Mine, except that he has a flaw." He said: "O Lord, what is his flaw?" He said: "He delights in the breeze of the dawns and inclines to it. And whoever loves Me does not incline to anything." It is narrated that a worshipper worshipped Allah the Exalted in a thicket for a long time. He looked at a bird that had nested in a tree, taking refuge in it and chirping near it. He said: "If only I moved my mosque to that tree, so I could find intimacy with the sound of this bird." He said: "So he did. Then Allah the Exalted revealed to the prophet of that time: 'Say to that worshipper: You sought intimacy with a creature — I will surely lower your degree to a level you will never attain with any of your deeds.'"

So the sign of love is the perfection of intimacy in intimate converse with the Beloved, the perfection of delight in solitude with Him, and the perfection of estrangement from everything that spoils solitude and hinders the pleasure of intimate converse. The sign of intimacy is that the intellect and understanding become entirely engrossed in the pleasure of intimate converse — like one who addresses his beloved and converses intimately with him. This pleasure reached some to the point that, while in prayer, a fire broke out in his house and he did not notice; and the leg of another was cut off due to an illness that afflicted him while he was in prayer, and he did not feel it. Whenever love and intimacy prevail, solitude and intimate converse become the delight of his eye, by which he repels all worries. Indeed, intimacy and love engross his heart so that he does not comprehend worldly matters unless they are repeated to his ears many times — like the infatuated lover who speaks to people with his tongue while his inner intimacy is with the remembrance of his beloved. So the lover is one who finds no rest except with his beloved.

Qatādah said concerning the saying of the Exalted: {الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب} (Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah — verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest): "They yearned to Him and sought intimacy with Him." And al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Whoever tastes of the pure love of Allah, that occupies him from seeking this world and estranges him from all of humanity."

Muṭarrif ibn Abī Bakr said: "Love does not tire of the discourse of its beloved." And Allah the Exalted revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him): "He who claims to love Me has lied if, when night falls, he sleeps away from Me. Does not every lover love the meeting of his beloved? Here I am, present for whoever seeks Me." And Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, where are You, that I may seek You?" He said: "When you seek, you have arrived." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "Whoever loves Allah hates his own soul." He also said: "Whoever lacks three traits is not a lover: preferring the speech of Allah the Exalted over the speech of creatures, the meeting of Allah the Exalted over the meeting of creatures, and worship over serving creatures."

Among them is that he not regret what he misses of other than Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that his regret be great over every hour that passes without the remembrance of Allah the Exalted and His obedience. So he frequently returns, during moments of heedlessness, with supplication for compassion, reproach, and repentance. Some of the knowers said: "Allah has servants who loved Him and found rest in Him, so regret over what is past departed from them; they are not occupied with their own share, since the dominion of their King is complete — whatever He wills is. What is for them reaches them, and what misses them is by His good governance of them."

The due of the lover, when he returns from his heedlessness in that very moment, is to turn to his Beloved, occupy himself with reproach, and ask Him, saying: "O Lord, for what sin have You cut off Your kindness from me, distanced me from Your presence, and occupied me with myself and with following the devil?" This extracts from him a purity of remembrance and a tenderness of heart that expiates the past heedlessness, and his slip becomes a cause for renewed remembrance and purity of heart. And whenever the lover sees only the Beloved, and sees nothing except from Him, he does not regret nor complain, but receives everything with contentment, knowing that the Beloved has decreed for him only what is good for him — recalling His saying: {وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم} (And perhaps you dislike a thing while it is good for you).

Among them is that he delight in obedience and not find it burdensome, and its fatigue falls away from him. As one of them said: "I struggled against the night for twenty years, then I delighted in it for twenty years."

Al-Junayd said: "The sign of the lover is constant vigor and persistence with desire — his body tires but his heart does not." Some of them said: "Work upon love admits no languor." Some scholars said: "By Allah, a lover of Allah never satiates from His obedience, even if he attains the greatest of means."

All of this and its like exists in observable reality — for the lover does not find burdensome the striving in the desire of his beloved, and delights in serving him with his heart, even if it is arduous on his body. And whenever his body fails, the most beloved of things to him is that ability return to him and incapacity depart, so that he may occupy himself with it. Such is love for Allah the Exalted — for every love that prevails inevitably conquers what is beneath it. Whoever's beloved is more beloved to him than laziness abandons laziness in serving him; and if it is more beloved to him than wealth, he spends wealth in his love.

It was said to one of the lovers — who had expended his soul and wealth until nothing remained to him: "What was the cause of your state in love?" He said: "One day I heard a lover alone with his beloved saying: 'By Allah, I love you with all my heart, while you turn away from me with all your face.' The beloved said to him: 'If you love me, what do you spend on me?' He said: 'O my master, I give you possession of what I own, then I spend my soul on you until it perishes.' So I said: 'This is a creature for a creature, and a servant for a servant — how then with servants for the Worshipped?' All of this is for His sake."

Among them is that he be compassionate toward all of Allah's servants, merciful to them, and severe against all of Allah's enemies and against everyone who commits something He dislikes — as Allah the Exalted said: {أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم} (Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves). No blame of a blamer overtakes him, and nothing turns him from anger for Allah. With this Allah described His friends, saying: "Those who are enamored with Me as a child is enamored with a thing, and take refuge in My remembrance as the eagle takes refuge in its nest, and grow angry for His sanctities as the leopard grows angry when enraged — for he cares not whether people are few or many." Consider this example: the child, when enamored with a thing, never parts from it; if taken from him, his only occupation is weeping and crying until it is returned. If he sleeps, he takes it with him in his clothes; when he wakes, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he parts from it, he weeps; whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever contends with him for it, he hates; whoever gives it to him, he loves. As for the leopard, he does not master himself in anger, until from the severity of his anger he destroys himself.

These are the signs of love. Whoever completes these signs in himself — his love is complete and his affection is pure, so in the Hereafter his drink is clear and his draught is sweet. And whoever's love is mixed with love of other than Allah delights in the Hereafter according to his love — for his drink is mixed with a measure of the drink of the near ones (muqarrabūn). As He said the Exalted concerning the righteous (abrār): {إن الأبرار لفي نعيم} (Indeed the righteous are in bliss), then said: {يسقون من رحيق مختوم ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون ومزاجه من تسنيم عينا يشرب بها المقربون} (They are given to drink of sealed nectar, whose seal is musk — and for that let the competitors compete — and its mixture is from Tasnīm, a spring from which the near ones drink). So the drink of the righteous is sweetened by the admixture of the pure drink that is for the near ones.

The "drink" is an expression for the totality of the bliss of the gardens, just as the Book used it as an expression for all deeds, saying: {إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين} (Indeed the book of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyīn), then said: {يشهده المقربون} (The near ones witness it). So the indication of the loftiness of their book is that it rises to where the near ones witness it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and knowledge by their proximity to the near ones and their witnessing of them, so too is their state in the Hereafter — {ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده} (Your creation and your resurrection are but as one soul; as We began the first creation, We will repeat it). And as He said the Exalted: {جزاء وفاقا} (A recompense fully matching) — that is, the recompense matches their deeds. So the pure is met with the pure drink, and the mixed with the mixed.

The admixture of every drink is according to the prior admixture in his love and deeds. {فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره} (So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it). {وإن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم} (And Allah does not change a people's state until they change what is in themselves). {إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين} (Indeed Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it be a good deed, He multiplies it; and if it be a grain of mustard seed, We bring it — and sufficient are We as Reckoners).

So whoever's love in this world was his hope for the bliss of Paradise, the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn), and the palaces — he is granted Paradise to settle therein wherever he wishes, playing with the youths and enjoying the women. There his pleasure in the Hereafter ends, because each person is given in love what his soul desires and his eye delights in.

And whoever's aim is the Lord of the House and the Owner of the Kingdom, and nothing prevails over him except His love with sincerity and truth — he is settled in {مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر} (a seat of truth near an Omnipotent King). The righteous (abrār) graze in the gardens and delight in the paradises with the wide-eyed maidens and the youths, while the near ones (muqarrabūn) are constant at the Presence, their eyes fixed upon it, deeming the bliss of Paradise insignificant compared to a particle of it. So some are occupied with satisfying the lust of belly and loins, and others with sitting in company. Hence the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «أكثر أهل الجنة البله وعليون لذوى الألباب» (Most of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded, and ʿIlliyyīn is for the people of intellect).

The ḥadīth "Sheybaṭanī Hūd" (Hūd has made me gray) was narrated by al-Tirmidhī and has been mentioned repeatedly. The ḥadīth "Whoever's two days are equal is cheated, and whoever's day is worse than his yesterday is cursed" — I know this only from a dream of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Rawwād, who said: "I saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said that" — with an addition at its end, narrated by al-Bayhaqī in al-Zuhd. The ḥadīth «إنه ليغان على قلبي» (Indeed my heart is veiled) is agreed upon from the ḥadīth of al-Agharr and has been mentioned previously.

His seeking forgiveness was only from the first station (qadam), for it was distance relative to the second station. And this is a punishment for them for languor in the path and turning to other than the Beloved. As it is narrated that Allah the Exalted says: "The least I do to the scholar, when he prefers the lusts of this world over My obedience, is that I strip him of the delight of My intimate converse." So the stripping of increase due to lusts is a punishment for the general. As for the elect (khuṣūṣ), they are veiled from increase by mere claim, self-admiration (ʿujb), and reliance on what appeared of the beginnings of gentleness — and that is the hidden deception (makr khafī) from which none can guard except those of firm footing.

Then the fear of losing what is not attained after its loss: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham heard a caller saying while he was on a journey, on the mountain:

"Everything from You is forgiven — except turning away from us.
We have granted you what has passed — so grant us what has passed from us."

He was agitated and fell unconscious, not reviving for a day and a night, and states came over him. Then he said: "I heard the call from the mountain: 'O Ibrāhīm, be a servant.' So I became a servant, and I found rest."

Then the fear of being forgotten by Him (sulūw): for the lover is accompanied by yearning (shawq) and urgent seeking — he does not slacken in seeking increase, nor is he consoled except by a new gentleness. If he is consoled by that, it is a cause of his stopping or a cause of his regression.

Forgetting enters upon him from where he does not perceive, just as love may enter upon him from where he does not perceive. For these fluctuations have hidden heavenly causes that human power cannot fathom. When Allah wishes to deceive him and lead him on gradually (istidrāj), He conceals from him what has come upon him of forgetting, so he stops with hope and is deluded by good opinion, or by the prevalence of heedlessness, caprice, or forgetfulness. All of these are among the soldiers of the devil that overcome the soldiers of the angels — knowledge, intellect

chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| بيان معنى الأنس بالله تعالى

قد ذكرنا أن الأنس والخوف والشوق من آثار المحبة إلا أن هذه آثار تختلف
على المحب بحسب نظره وما يغلب عليه في وقته فإذا غلب عليه التطلع من وراء
حجب الغيب إلا منتهى الجمال واستشعر قصوره عن الإطلاع على كنه الجلال انبعث
القلب إلى الطلب وانزعج له وهاج إليه وتسمى هذه الحالة في الانزعاج شوقا
وهو بالإضافة إلى أمر غائب وإذا غلب عليه الفرح بالقرب ومشاهدة الحضور بما
هو حاصل من الكشف وكان نظره مقصورا على مطالعة الجمال الحاضر المكشوف غير
ملتفت إلى ما لم يدركه بعد استبشر القلب بما يلاحظه فيسمى استبشاره أنسا
وإن كان نظره إلى صفات العز والاستغناء وعدم المبالاة وخطر إمكان الزوال
والبعد تألم القلب بهذا الاستشعار فيسمى تألمه خوفا
وهذه الأحوال تابعة لهذه الملاحظات والملاحظات تابعة لأسباب تقتضيها لا
يمكن حصرها فالأنس معناه استبشار القلب فرحه بمطالعة الجمال حتى إنه إذا
غلب وتجرد عن  ملاحظة ما غاب عنه وما يتطرق إليه من خطر الزوال عظم نعيمه
ولذته ومن هنا نظر بعضهم حيث قيل له أنت مشتاق فقال لا إنما الشوق إلى غائب
فإذا كان الغائب حاضرا فإلى من يشتاق وهذا كلام مستغرق بالفرح بما ناله غير
ملتفت إلى ما بقي في الإمكان من مزايا الألطاف
ومن غلب عليه حال الأنس لم تكن شهوته إلا في الانفراد والخلوة كما حكي أن
إبراهيم بن أدهم نزل من الجبل فقيل له من أين أقبلت فقال من الأنس بالله
وذلك لأن الأنس بالله يلازمه التوحش من غير الله بل كل
PageV04P339
ما يعوق عن الخلوة فيكون من أثقل الأشياء على القلب كما روي أن موسى عليه
السلام لما كلمه ربه مكث دهرا لا يسمع كلام أحد من الناس إلا أخذه الغثيان
لأن الحب يوجب عذوبة كلام المحبوب وعذوبة ذكره فيخرج من القلب عذوبة ما
سواه
ولذلك قال بعض الحكماء في دعائه يا من آنسني بذكره وأوحشني من خلقه وقال
الله عز وجل لداود عليه السلام كن لي مشتاقا وبي متأنسا ومن سواي مستوحشا
وقيل لرابعة بم نلت هذه المنزلة قالت بتركي ما لا يعنيني وأنسي بمن لم يزل
وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد مررت براهب فقلت له يا راهب لقد أعجبتك الوحدة
فقال يا هذا لو ذقت حلاوة الوحدة لاستوحشت إليها من نفسك الوحدة رأس
العبادة فقلت يا راهب ما أقل ما تجده في الوحدة قال الراحة من مداراة الناس
والسلامة من شرهم قلت يا راهب متى يذوق العبد حلاوة الأنس بالله تعالى قال
إذا صفا الود وخلصت المعاملة قلت ومتى يصفو الود قال إذا اجتمع الهم فصار
هما واحد في الطاعة وقال بعض الحكماء عجبا للخلائق كيف أرادوا بك بدلا عجبا
للقلوب كيف استأنست بسواك عنك
فإن قلت فما علامة الأنس فاعلم أن علامته الخاصة ضيق الصدر من معاشرة
الخلق والتبرم بهم واستهتاره بعذوبة الذكر فإن خالط فهو كمنفرد في جماعة
ومجتمع في خلوة وغريب في حضر وحاضر  في سفر وشاهد في غيبة وغائب في حضور
مخالط بالبدن منفرد بالقلب مستغرق بعذوبة الذكر كما قال علي كرم الله وجهه
في وصفهم هم قوم هجم بهم العلم على حقيقة الأمر فباشروا روح اليقين
واستلانوا ما استوعر المترفون وأنسوا بما استوحش منه الجاهلون صحبوا الدنيا
بأبدان أرواحها معلقة بالمحل الأعلى أولئك خلفاء الله في أرضه والدعاة إلى
دينه
فهذا معنى الأنس بالله وهذه علامته وهذه شواهده
وقد ذهب بعض المتكلمين إلى إنكار الأنس والشوق والحب لظنه أن ذلك يدل على
التشبيه وجهله بأن جمال المدركات بالبصائر أكمل من جمال المبصرات ولذة
معرفتها أغلب على ذوي القلوب ومنهم أحمد بن غالب يعرف بغلام الخليل أنكر
على الجنيد وعلى أبي الحسن النوري والجماعة حديث الحب والشوق والعشق حتى
أنكر بعضهم مقام الرضا وقال ليس إلا الصبر فأما الرضا فغير متصور
وهذا كله كلام ناقص قاصر لم يطلع من مقامات الدين إلا على القشور فظن أنه
لا وجود إلا للقشر فإن المحسوسات وكل ما يدخل في الخيال من طريق الدين قشر
مجرد ووراءه اللب المطلوب فمن لم يصل من الجوز إلا إلى قشره يظن أن الجوز
خشب كله ويستحيل عنده خروج الدهن منه لا محالة وهو معذور ولكن عذره غير
مقبول وقد قيل
الأنس بالله لا يحويه بطال ... وليس يدركه بالحول محتال
والآنسون رجال كلهم نجب ... وكلهم صفوة لله عمال

### |||| بيان معنى الانبساط والإدلال الذي تثمره غلبة الأنس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ ن س (ʾ-n-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core sense of sociability, familiarity, and the absence of estrangement; the heart's repose in what is known and near.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the soul's tranquil delight in the presence of the Beloved, contrasted with the terror of majesty (haybah) and the ache of longing (shawq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes human companionship; here employed as a transferred metaphor (majāz) for the heart's jubilation at unveiled beauty.
- Root: ب س ط (b-s-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Spreading, expansion, and extension.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's expansive ease and boldness (inbisāṭ) before God, born of secure intimacy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical spreading; metaphorical for the heart's dilation in joyful confidence.
- Root: د ل ل (d-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Boldness, forwardness, and confident familiarity, often of a beloved toward the lover.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The saint's audacious reliance on God's mercy, free from servile fear.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal impertinence; metaphorical for the lover's assured approach to the Beloved.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The sequence "الأنس والخوف والشوق" employs coordinated nouns governed by a single predicate, each defined by its distinct cause, requiring precise differentiation of grammatical subjects.
chapters.translation:
### |||| Elucidation of the Meaning of Intimacy (Uns) with God Most High

We have already mentioned that intimacy (uns), fear (khawf), and longing (shawq) are among the effects of love (maḥabbah). Yet these effects vary upon the lover according to his contemplation and what predominates over him at any given moment. For when the gaze beyond the veils of the unseen toward the utmost beauty prevails upon him, and he perceives his own incapacity to attain the inmost reality of majesty (jalāl), the heart is roused to seeking, is agitated thereby, and is stirred toward it. This state of agitation is termed "longing" (shawq), and it is relative to something absent. But when joy in proximity and the witnessing of presence prevails, by virtue of what has been disclosed to him, and his gaze is confined to contemplating the present, unveiled beauty—not turning toward what he has not yet grasped—then the heart rejoices at what it beholds, and its rejoicing is termed "intimacy" (uns). And if his gaze is upon the attributes of might, self-sufficiency, indifference, and the peril of possible cessation and distance, the heart is pained by this perception, and its pain is termed "fear" (khawf).

These states are consequent upon these contemplations, and the contemplations are consequent upon causes that necessitate them, which cannot be enumerated. Thus the meaning of intimacy (uns) is the heart's rejoicing and delight in contemplating beauty—so much so that when it prevails and is stripped of any regard for what is absent from him or any peril of cessation that might intrude upon it, his bliss and pleasure become immense. From this vantage, one of them—when asked, "Are you longing?"—replied: "No. Longing is only toward the absent. When the absent is present, toward whom would one long?" This is speech wholly absorbed in joy at what has been attained, not turning toward what remains possible of the excellences of divine graces.

When the state of intimacy (uns) prevails over a man, his desire is only for seclusion and solitude. Thus it is related that Ibrāhīm ibn Adham descended from the mountain, and it was said to him: "From where have you come?" He replied: "From intimacy with God." For intimacy with God entails estrangement from all besides God—nay, everything that impedes solitude becomes among the heaviest of things upon the heart. As it is related that Moses (peace be upon him), when his Lord spoke to him, remained for a long period unable to hear the speech of any human without being seized by nausea—because love necessitates the sweetness of the Beloved's speech and the sweetness of His remembrance, so that the sweetness of all else departs from the heart.

For this reason, one of the sages said in his supplication: "O He who has made me intimate (ānasani) with His remembrance and estranged me from His creatures." And God Almighty said to David (peace be upon him): "Be to Me longing, with Me intimate, and from all besides Me estranged." It was said to Rābiʿah: "By what did you attain this station?" She said: "By my abandoning what does not concern me, and my intimacy with Him who never ceases." And ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd said: "I passed by a monk and said to him: 'O monk, solitude has impressed you.' He replied: 'O man, had you tasted the sweetness of solitude, you would have fled to it from your very self. Solitude is the head of worship.' I said: 'O monk, how little do you find in solitude!' He said: 'Rest from managing people and safety from their evil.' I said: 'O monk, when does the servant taste the sweetness of intimacy with God Most High?' He said: 'When affection is purified and dealings are sincere.' I said: 'And when does affection become pure?' He said: 'When concerns gather into a single concern—obedience.'" And one of the sages said: "Amazement at creatures—how they sought a substitute for You! Amazement at hearts—how they grew intimate with other than You, apart from You!"

If you say: "What then is the sign of intimacy (uns)?" Know that its specific sign is constriction of the breast from associating with creatures, vexation with them, and being enraptured by the sweetness of remembrance. If he mingles, he is like one alone in a crowd, and one gathered in solitude, and a stranger in a homeland, and one present on a journey, and a witness in absence, and one absent in presence—mingling with the body, alone with the heart, absorbed in the sweetness of remembrance. As ʿAlī (may God honor his face) said in describing them: "They are a people whom knowledge has led to the reality of the matter, so they have touched the spirit of certainty, and found soft what the luxurious found harsh, and grown intimate with what the ignorant find estranged. They accompanied the world with bodies whose souls are suspended from the highest station. Those are God's vicegerents on His earth and the summoners to His religion."

This, then, is the meaning of intimacy (uns) with God, and these are its signs and its evidences.

Some theologians (mutakallimūn) have gone so far as to deny intimacy (uns), longing (shawq), and love (maḥabbah), supposing that this implies anthropomorphism (tashbīh)—ignorant that the beauty of things perceived by inner insights is more complete than the beauty of visible things, and that the pleasure of knowing them prevails over those possessed of hearts. Among them was Aḥmad ibn Ghālib, known as Ghulām al-Khalīl, who denounced al-Junayd, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Nūrī, and their company regarding the discourse of love, longing, and passionate affection (ʿishq)—so much so that some of them denied the station of contentment (riḍā), saying: "There is only patience (ṣabr); as for contentment, it is inconceivable."

All of this is deficient and defective speech. They have not beheld of the stations of religion save the husks, and supposed that nothing exists but the husk. For the sensible things and all that enters the imagination from the path of religion is mere husk, and behind it lies the sought kernel (lubb). Whoever has not reached from the walnut save its shell supposes the walnut to be all wood, and the extraction of its oil seems impossible to him—necessarily. He is excused, but his excuse is not accepted. And it has been said:

"Intimacy with God no idle man attains, / Nor any schemer by his cunning gains.
The intimate ones are men all noble-born, / Each a chosen worker for God's cause."

### |||| Elucidation of the Meaning of Expansiveness (Inbisāṭ) and Bold Familiarity (Idlāl) Produced by the Predominance of Intimacy

chapters.title_en: On Familiarity (Uns) and Its Fruits: The Propriety of Expansive Speech (Inbisāṭ) and Bold Claim (Iidlāl) Before God
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن الأنس إذا دام وغلب واستحكم ولم يشوشه قلق الشوق ولم ينغصه خوف
التغير والحجاب فإنه يثمر نوعا من الانبساط في الأقوال والأفعال والمناجاة
مع الله تعالى وقد يكون منكر الصورة لما فيه من الجراءة وقلة الهيبة ولكنه
محتمل ممن أقيم في مقام الأنس ومن لم يقم في ذلك المقام ويتشبه بهم في
الفعل والكلام هلك به وأشرف على الكفر
ومثاله مناجاة برخ الأسود الذي أمر الله تعالى كليمه موسى عليه السلام أن
يسأله ليستسقي لبني إسرائيل
PageV04P340
بعد أن قحطوا سبع سنين وخرج موسى  عليه السلام ليستسقي لهم في سبعين ألفا
فأوحى الله عز وجل إليه كيف أستجيب لهم وقد أظلمت عليهم ذنوبهم سرائرهم
خبيثة يدعونني على غير يقين ويأمنون مكري ارجع إلى عبد من عبادي يقال له
برخ فقل له يخرج حتى أستجيب له فسأل عنه موسى عليه السلام فلم يعرف فبينما
موسى ذات يوم يمشي في طريق إذا بعبد أسود قد استقبله بين عينيه تراب من أثر
السجود في شملة قد عقدها على عنقه فعرفه موسى عليه السلام بنور الله عز وجل
فسلم عليه وقال له ما اسمك فقال اسمي برخ قال فأنت طلبتنا منذ حين أخرج
فاستسق لنا
فخرج فقال في كلامه ما هذا من فعالك ولا هذا من حلمك وما الذى بدالك
أنقصت عليك عيونك أم عاندت الرياح عن طاعتك أم نفد ما عندك أم اشتد غضبك
على المذنبين ألست كنت غفارا قبل خلق الخطائين خلقت الرحمة وأمرت بالعطف أم
ترينا أنك ممتنع أم تخشى الفوت فتجعل بالعقوبة قال فما برح حتى اخضلت بنو
إسرائيل بالقطر وأنبت الله تعالى العشب في نصف يوم حتى بلغ الركب قال فرجع
برخ فاستقبله موسى عليه السلام فقال كيف رأيت حين خاصمت ربى كيف أنصفني فهم
موسى عليه السلام به فأوحى الله تعالى إليه إن برخا يضحكني كل يوم ثلاث
مرات
وعن الحسن قال احترقت أخصاص بالبصرة فبقي في وسطها خص لم يحترق وأبو موسى
يومئذ أمير البصرة فأخبر بذلك فبعث إلى صاحب الخص قال فأتي بشيخ فقال يا
شيخ ما بال خصك لم يحترق قال إني أقسمت على ربي عز وجل أن لا يحرقه فقال
أبو موسى رضي الله عنه إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يكون في
أمتي قوم شعثة رءوسهم دنسة ثيابهم لو أقسموا على الله لأبرهم (1) قال ووقع
حريق بالبصرة فجاء أبو عبيدة الخواص فجعل يتخطى النار فقال له أمير البصرة
انظر لا تحترق بالنار فقال إني أقسمت على ربي عز وجل أن لا يحرقني بالنار
قال  فاعزم على النار أن تطفأ قال فعزم عليها فطفئت
وكان أبو حفص يمشي ذات يوم فاستقبله رستاقي مدهوش فقال له أبو حفص ما
أصابك فقال ضل حماري ولا أملك غيره قال فوقف أبو حفص وقال وعزتك لا أخطو
خطوة ما لم ترد عليه حماره قال فظهر حماره في الوقت ومر أبو حفص رحمه الله
فهذا وأمثاله يجري لذوي الأنس وليس لغيرهم أن يتشبه بهم
قال الجنيد رحمه الله أهل الأنس يقولون في كلامهم ومناجاتهم في خلواتهم
أشياء هي كفر عند العامة
وقال مرة لو سمعها العموم لكفروهم وهم يجدون المزيد في أحوالهم بذلك
وذلك يحتمل منهم ويليق بهم وإليه أشار القائل
قوم تخالجهم زهو بسيدهم ... والعبد يزهو على مقدار مولاه
تاهوا برؤيته عما سواه له ... يا حسن رؤيتهم في عز ما تاهوا
ولا تستبعدون رضاه عن العبد بما يغضب به على غيره مهما اختلف مقامهما ففي
القرآن تنبيهات على هذه المعاني لو فطنت وفهمت فجميع قصص القرآن تنبيهات
لأولي البصائر والأبصار حتى ينظروا إليها بعين الاعتبار فإنما هي عند ذوي
الاعتبار من الأسماء
فأول القصص قصة آدم عليه السلام وإبليس أما تراهما كيف اشتركا في اسم
المعصية والمخالفة ثم تباينا في الاجتباء والعصمة
أما إبليس فأبلس عن رحمته وقيل إنه من المبعدين
وأما آدم عليه السلام فقيل فيه وعصى آدم ربه فغوى ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب
عليه وهدى PageV04P341
وقد عاتب الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الإعراض عن عبد والإقبال على
عبد وهما في العبودية سيان ولكن في الحال مختلفان فقال وأما من جاءك يسعى
وهو يخشى فأنت عنه تلهى وقال فى الآخرة أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى وكذلك
أمره بالقعود مع طائفة فقال عز وجل وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل
سلام عليكم وأمره بالإعراض عن غيرهم فقال وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا
فأعرض عنهم حتى قال فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمبن وقال تعالى
واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي
فكذلك الانبساط  والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض فمن انبساط الأنس
قول موسى عليه السلام إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء وقوله
في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له اذهب إلى فرعون {فقال} ولهم على ذنب وقوله
إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني وقوله إننا نخاف أن يفرط
علينا أو أن يطغى وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذي أقيم
مقام الأنس يلاطف ويحتمل ولم يحتمل ليونس عليه السلام ما دون هذا لما أقيم
مقام القبض والهيبة فعوقب بالسجن في بطن الحوت في ظلمات ثلاث ونودي عليه
إلى يوم القيامة لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء وهو مذموم قال
الحسن العراء هو القيامة ونهى نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقتدى به
وقيل له فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم
وهذه الاختلافات بعضها لاختلاف الأحوال والمقامات وبعضها لما سبق في
الأزل من التفاضل والتفاوت في القسمة بين العباد وقد قال تعالى ولقد فضلنا
بعض النبين على بعض وقد قال منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات فكان عيسى
عليه السلام من المفضلين ولإدلاله سلم على نفسه فقال والسلام علي يوم ولدت
ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا وهذا انبساط منه لما شاهد من اللطف في مقام الأنس
وأما يحيى بن زكريا عليه السلام فإنه أقيم مقام الهيبة والحياء فلم ينطق
حتى أثنى عليه خالقه فقال وسلام عليه
وانظر كيف احتمل لأخوة يوسف ما فعلوه بيوسف وقد قال بعض العلماء قد عددت
من أول قوله تعالى إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا إلى رأس العشرين
من إخباره تعالى عن زهدهم فيه نيفا وأربعين خطيئة بعضها أكبر من بعض وقد
يجتمع في الكلمة الواحدة الثلاث والأربع فغفر لهم وعفا عنهم ولم يحتمل
العزير في مسألة واحدة سأل عنها في القدر حتى قيل محي من ديوان النبوة
وكذلك كان بلعام بن باعوراء من أكابر العلماء  فأكل الدنيا بالدين فلم يحتمل
له ذلك
وكان آصف من المسرفين وكانت معصيته في الجوارح فعفا عنه
فقد روي أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى سليمان عليه السلام يا رأس العابدين ويا
ابن محجة الزاهدين إلى كم يعصيني ابن خالتك آصف وأنا أحلم عليه مرة بعد مرة
فوعزتى وجلالي لئن أخذته عصفة من عصفاتي عليه لأتركنه مثلة لمن معه ونكالا
لمن بعده فلما دخل آصف على سليمان عليه السلام أخبره بما أوحى الله تعالى
إليه فخرج حتى علا كثيبا من رمل ثم رفع رأسه ويديه نحو السماء وقال إلهي
وسيدي أنت أنت وأنا وأنا فكيف أتوب إن لم تتب علي وكيف أستعصم إن لم تعصمني
لأعودن فأوحى الله تعالى إليه صدقت يا آصف أنت أنت وأنا وأنا أستقبل التوبة
وقد تبت عليك وأنا التواب الرحيم وهذا كلام مدل به عليه وهارب منه إليه
وناظر به إليه
PageV04P342
وفي الخبر إن الله تعالى أوحى إلى عبد تداركه بعد أن كان أشفى على الهلكة
كم من ذنب واجهتني به غفرته لك قد أهلكت في دونه أمة من الأمم
فهذه سنة الله تعالى في عباده بالتفضيل والتقديم والتأخير على ما سبقت به
المشيئة الأزلية
وهذه القصص وردت في القرآن لتعرف بها سنة الله في عباده الذين خلوا من
قبل فما في القرآن شيء إلا وهو هدى ونور وتعرف من الله تعالى إلى خلقه
فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم
يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول الملك
القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر وتارة يتعرف إليهم في
أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول ألم
تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل
ولايعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله
وتقديسه أو معرفة صفاته وأسمائه أو معرفة أفعاله وسنته مع عباده
ولما اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على  أحد هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهو التقديس
وازنها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بثلث القرآن فقال من قرأ سورة الإخلاص
فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن (1) حديث دعائه لابن عباس اللهم فقهه في الدين وعلمه
التأويل متفق عليه دون قوله وعلمه التأويل ورواه أحمد بهذه الزيادة وتقدم
في العلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ن-س (alif-nūn-sīn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core sense of sociability, companionship, and the absence of estrangement (waḥshah); the heart's repose in the presence of the beloved.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's tranquil intimacy with God, contrasted with the awe (haybah) of majesty; a station (maqām) of the elect where fear of separation is quelled.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes human companionship; metaphorical (majāz) usage here elevates it to the servant's confidential communion (munājāh) with the Divine, where formal reserve yields to loving boldness.
- Root: ب-س-ط (bā-sīn-ṭā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Spreading, extending, widening; the opposite of constriction (qabḍ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, the expansion of the breast (sharḥ al-ṣadr) permitting unguarded speech and action before God, born of confirmed intimacy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical extension of a thing. Metaphorical: the soul's liberation from the shackles of reverential fear, manifesting as audacity (jarāʾah) in supplication.
- Root: د-ل-ل (dāl-lām-lām)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To point, indicate, guide; also to presume upon a beloved's affection, to act with familiar boldness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The servant's confident reliance on God's prior kindness, permitting a tone of loving reproach—a privilege of those established in the station of proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: indication (dalālah). Metaphorical: the beloved's audacious claim upon the lover, rooted in certainty of acceptance, not in disrespect.

chapters.translation:
Know that when intimacy (uns) endures, prevails, and becomes firmly established—unperturbed by the restlessness of longing and unspoiled by the fear of change or veiling—it yields a kind of expansiveness (inbisāṭ) in words, deeds, and confidential prayer (munājāh) with God, exalted be He. This may assume a form deemed objectionable, owing to the audacity (jarāʾah) and diminished awe (haybah) it contains. Yet it is tolerated from one who is established in the station of intimacy. As for one who is not established in that station yet imitates them in deed and speech, he is destroyed by it and verges upon unbelief.

An example of this is the confidential prayer of Barakh the Black, whom God, exalted be He, commanded His interlocutor Moses (peace be upon him) to ask to come forth, so that he might pray for rain for the Children of Israel—after they had suffered drought for seven years. Moses (peace be upon him) went out to pray for rain for them amidst seventy thousand. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed to him: "How shall I respond to them, when their sins have darkened them, their inner selves are foul, they call upon Me without certainty, and they feel secure from My stratagem? Return to a servant of My servants named Barakh, and say to him: 'Come forth, so that I may respond to him.'" Moses (peace be upon him) inquired about him but found no one who knew him. Then, one day, as Moses was walking upon a road, a black servant met him, with dust between his eyes from the trace of prostration, wrapped in a single garment (shamlah) knotted about his neck. Moses recognized him by the light of God, exalted be He, greeted him, and asked: "What is your name?" He replied: "My name is Barakh." Moses said: "You are the one we have been seeking. Come forth and pray for rain for us."

So he went out and said in his speech: "This is not of Your doing, nor this of Your forbearance. What has changed You? Have Your eyes been diminished, or have the winds rebelled against Your obedience, or has what You possess been exhausted, or has Your wrath against the sinners intensified? Were You not ever-Forgiving before the creation of the sinners? You created mercy and commanded compassion. Or do You show us that You are unattainable, or do You fear escape, and thus resort to punishment?" He said: He had hardly finished before the Children of Israel were drenched with rain, and God, exalted be He, caused vegetation to sprout within half a day, until it reached the knees. He said: Then Barakh returned, and Moses (peace be upon him) met him and said: "How did you see it when I argued with my Lord—how He granted me justice?" Moses (peace be upon him) intended to rebuke him, but God, exalted be He, revealed to him: "Verily, Barakh makes Me laugh three times every day."

It is related from al-Ḥasan that he said: Huts (aṣkhiṣ) caught fire in Basra, and in their midst one hut remained unburned. Abū Mūsā was at that time the governor of Basra. When informed of this, he sent for the owner of the hut. He said: An old man was brought, and he said: "O elder, why was your hut not burned?" He replied: "I made an oath upon my Lord, mighty and majestic, that He would not burn it." Abū Mūsā (may God be pleased with him) said: "I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) say: 'There will be in my community a people with disheveled heads and soiled garments; if they were to swear an oath upon God, He would fulfill it for them.'" He said: A fire also broke out in Basra, and Abū ʿUbaydah al-Khawwāṣ came and began stepping across the fire. The governor of Basra said to him: "Take care not to be burned by the fire." He replied: "I have made an oath upon my Lord, mighty and majestic, that He will not burn me with fire." He said: "Then command the fire to be extinguished." He said: So he commanded it, and it was extinguished.

Abū Ḥafṣ (may God have mercy on him) was walking one day when a distraught villager met him. Abū Ḥafṣ asked: "What has befallen you?" He said: "My donkey is lost, and I own no other." Abū Ḥafṣ then stood still and said: "By Your might, I shall not take a single step until You return his donkey to him." He said: His donkey appeared at once, and Abū Ḥafṣ (may God have mercy on him) passed on.

This and the like occurs for the people of intimacy, and it is not for others to imitate them in it. Al-Junayd (may God have mercy on him) said: "The people of intimacy utter in their speech and their confidential prayers in their seclusions things that are unbelief in the eyes of the common folk." And he said once: "If the masses heard them, they would declare them unbelievers—while they find increase in their states thereby." That is tolerated from them and befits them. To this the poet alluded:

"A people whom pride in their Master pervades—and the servant takes pride according to the measure of his Lord.
They are lost in beholding Him, apart from all else—how fair their beholding, in the might of their being lost!"

Do not deem it far-fetched that He is pleased with the servant for what would anger Him from another, whenever their stations differ. In the Qurʾān there are intimations of these meanings, if you would but discern and understand. For all the stories of the Qurʾān are intimations for the possessors of insight and sight, that they might regard them with the eye of consideration. For they are, to those who reflect, but names (asmāʾ) [of deeper realities].

The first of the stories is the story of Adam (peace be upon him) and Iblīs. Do you not see how they shared in the name of disobedience and opposition, yet diverged in being chosen and protected? As for Iblīs, he was cut off (ublisa) from mercy, and it is said he was among the expelled. As for Adam (peace be upon him), it was said of him: {«And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray. Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him»} (20:121-122).

God also reproached His Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) for turning away from one servant and turning toward another, while both were equal in servitude but differed in state. He said: {«But as for him who came to you striving, while he fears—from him you turn away. And as for him who is self-sufficient, to him you attend»} (80:8-10). Likewise, He commanded him to sit with a group, saying, exalted be He: {«And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you»} (6:54), and commanded him to turn away from others, saying: {«And when you see those who plunge into Our signs, turn away from them»} (6:68), until He said: {«Then do not sit with the wrongdoing people after the reminder»} (6:68). And He said, exalted be He: {«And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening»} (18:28).

Thus, expansiveness (inbisāṭ) and bold claim (idlāl) are tolerated from some servants and not from others. From the expansiveness of intimacy is the saying of Moses (peace be upon him): {«It is but Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will»} (7:155), and his words of explanation and excuse when it was said to him, "Go to Pharaoh": {«And they have a sin against me, so I fear they will kill me»} (26:14), and his saying: {«Indeed, I fear they will deny me, and my breast will be straitened, and my tongue will not be loosed»} (26:12-13), and his saying: {«Indeed, we fear that he may hasten against us or that he may transgress»} (20:45). This, from anyone other than Moses (peace be upon him), would be ill manners—because one established in the station of intimacy is treated with gentleness and tolerated. Yet less than this was not tolerated from Jonah (peace be upon him), because he was established in the station of contraction (qabḍ) and awe (haybah); thus he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale, in threefold darkness, and it was proclaimed against him until the Day of Resurrection: {«Had not a grace from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the barren shore while he was blameworthy»} (68:49). Al-Ḥasan said: "The barren shore (al-ʿarāʾ) is the Day of Resurrection." And our Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) was forbidden to follow his example, being told: {«So be patient with the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was anguished»} (68:48).

These differences are partly due to the difference of states and stations, and partly due to what was decreed in eternity of precedence and disparity in the apportionment among servants. God, exalted be He, has said: {«And We have favored some of the prophets over others»} (17:55), and He said: {«Of them are those to whom God spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees»} (2:253). Jesus (peace be upon him) was among the favored, and due to his bold claim (idlāl) he greeted himself, saying: {«And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive»} (19:33). This was an expansiveness from him, owing to what he witnessed of gentleness in the station of intimacy. As for John son of Zachariah (peace be upon him), he was established in the station of awe and modesty, and did not speak until his Creator praised him, saying: {«And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive»} (19:15).

Observe how He tolerated from Joseph's brothers what they did to Joseph. Some scholars have said: I have counted, from the beginning of His saying, exalted be He: {«When they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we»} (12:8), to the end of the twentieth [verse] of God's informing us of their disdain for him, over forty sins, some greater than others—and in a single word three or four may combine—yet He forgave them and pardoned them. But He did not tolerate from ʿUzayr a single question he asked concerning the decree (qadar), until it was said he was erased from the register of prophethood. Likewise, Balaam son of Beor was among the greatest scholars, yet he sold the Hereafter for the world, and that was not tolerated from him. Asaph was among the prodigal, and his sin was in the limbs, so he was pardoned.

It has been related that God, exalted be He, revealed to Solomon (peace be upon him): "O head of the worshippers, O son of the path of the ascetics! How long shall Asaph, your cousin, disobey Me, while I forbear with him time after time? By My might and My majesty, if I seize him with one of My seizures, I shall leave him as a warning to those with him and a chastisement for those after him." When Asaph entered upon Solomon (peace be upon him), he informed him of what God, exalted be He, had revealed. So he went out until he climbed a mound of sand, then raised his head and hands toward heaven and said: "My God and my Master! You are You, and I am I. How shall I repent if You do not turn to me, and how shall I be preserved if You do not preserve me? I shall surely return." Then God, exalted be He, revealed to him: "You have spoken truly, O Asaph. You are you, and I am I. I embrace repentance, and I have turned to you in forgiveness, and I am the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful." This is the speech of one who makes bold claim upon Him (mudill ʿalayhi), fleeing from Him to Him, and looking through Him to Him.

In the report: God, exalted be He, revealed to a servant whom He had rescued after he had verged upon destruction: "How many sins did you confront Me with, which I forgave you—though in less than them I destroyed a nation among the nations?"

This is the way (sunnah) of God, exalted be He, with His servants—in favoring, advancing, and deferring—according to what the eternal will (mashīʾah azaliyyah) has preceded.

These stories are related in the Qurʾān so that you may know thereby God's way with His servants who passed away before. There is nothing in the Qurʾān but that it is guidance and light, and a self-disclosure (taʿarruf) from God, exalted be He, to His creation. Sometimes He discloses Himself to them through sanctification (taqdīs), saying: {«Say: He is God, the One. God, the Eternal Refuge. He begets not, nor is He begotten, and there is none equal to Him»} (112:1-4). Sometimes He discloses Himself to them through the attributes of His majesty, saying: {«The Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Protector, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Proud»} (59:23). And sometimes He discloses Himself to them through His fearful and hopeful acts, reciting to them His way with His enemies and with His prophets, saying: {«Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd—Iram of the pillars?»} (89:6-7), and {«Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?»} (105:1).

The Qurʾān does not exceed these three divisions: guidance to knowledge of God's essence and His sanctification, or knowledge of His attributes and names, or knowledge of His acts and His way with His servants. Since Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ comprises one of these three divisions—namely, sanctification—the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) weighed it against a third of the Qurʾān, saying: "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ has recited a third of the Qurʾān." This is the ḥadīth of his supplication for Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)"—agreed upon [by al-Bukhārī and Muslim] without the phrase "and teach him the interpretation"; Aḥmad narrated it with this addition, and it has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.

chapters.title_en: On the Meaning of Contentment with God’s Decree, Its Reality, and What Has Been Reported Concerning Its Virtue
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| القول في معنى الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى وحقيقته وما ورد في فضيلته

اعلم أن الرضا ثمرة من ثمار المحبة وهو من أعلى مقامات المقربين وحقيقته
غامضة على الأكثرين وما يدخل عليه من التشابه والإبهام غير منكشف إلا لمن
علمه الله تعالى التأويل وفهمه وفقهه في الدين فقد أنكر منكرون تصور الرضا
بما يخالف الهوى ثم قالوا إن أمكن الرضا بكل شيء لأنه فعل الله فينبغى أن
يرضى بالكفر والمعاصى وانخدع بذلك قوم فرأوا الرضا بالفجور والفسوق وترك
الاعتراض والإنكار من باب التسليم لقضاء الله تعالى
ولو انكشفت هذه الأسرار لمن اقتصر على سماع ظواهر الشرع لما دعا رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لابن عباس حيث قال اللهم فقهه في الدين وعلمه
التأويل
فلنبدأ ببيان فضيلة الرضا
ثم بحكايات أحوال الراضين PageV04P343
ثم نذكر حقيقة الرضا وكيفية تصوره فيما يخالف الهوى ثم نذكر ما يظن أنه
من تمام الرضا وليس منه كترك الدعاء والسكوت على المعاصي

### |||| بيان فضيلة الرضا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ض-و (raḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is satisfaction and approval; the opposite of displeasure (sakhaṭ). It denotes a state where the heart finds rest in what has been apportioned.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, raḍā is the soul’s acquiescence to the divine decree (qaḍāʾ), rooted in the recognition that all that occurs is from God’s wisdom and justice—not mere passive resignation but an active affirmation of God’s perfect governance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally (ḥaqīqah), it is the heart’s inclination toward what is agreeable; metaphorically (majāz), it is applied to the servant’s surrender to God’s will, where the metaphor transfers from sensory pleasure to spiritual assent.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To decree, determine, or settle; carries the sense of finality and execution of a command.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, qaḍāʾ is God’s eternal decree encompassing all existents—His pre-eternal knowledge and will that brings things into being according to His wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is judicial settlement; metaphorical usage extends to divine ordainment, where the decree is likened to a judge’s binding verdict.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional phrasing (“if contentment with everything were possible…”) and exceptive clauses (“nothing is unveiled except…”) requiring precise parsing to distinguish hypothetical objections from categorical affirmations.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that contentment (raḍā) is a fruit among the fruits of love (maḥabbah), and it is among the highest stations of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn). Its reality is obscure to the majority, and what enters upon it of ambiguity and obscurity is not unveiled except to one whom God—exalted is He—has taught the interpretation (taʾwīl), granted understanding of it, and given deep comprehension in religion (fiqh al-dīn). For certain deniers have rejected the very conceivability of contentment with that which opposes caprice (hawā), then said: “If contentment with everything is possible—since it is God’s act—then one ought to be content with unbelief (kufr) and acts of disobedience (maʿāṣī).” And a group was deluded by this, deeming contentment with immorality (fujūr) and transgression (fusūq), and abandoning objection and denunciation, to be part of submission (taslīm) to God’s decree.

Had these secrets been unveiled to one who confines himself to hearing the outward aspects of the Law (ẓawāhir al-sharʿ), the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—would not have supplicated for Ibn ʿAbbās when he said: {«اللهم فقهه في الدين وعلمه التأويل»} (“O God, grant him deep comprehension in religion and teach him the interpretation”).

Let us begin by expounding the virtue of contentment (faḍīlat al-raḍā).
Then, with narratives of the states of those who are content (aḥwāl al-rāḍīn).
Then, we shall mention the reality of contentment and how it is conceivable with respect to that which opposes caprice.
Then, we shall mention what is imagined to be part of complete contentment but is not of it—such as abandoning supplication (duʿāʾ) and remaining silent over acts of disobedience.

### |||| Exposition of the Virtue of Contentment

chapters.title_en: On Divine Good Pleasure (Riḍā) and the Servant's Contentment with the Decree
chapters.arabic_text:
أما من الآيات فقوله تعالى {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه} وقد قال تعالى {هل
جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان} ومنتهى الإحسان رضا الله عن عبده وهو ثواب رضا
العبد عن الله تعالى
وقال تعالى {ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر} فقد رفع الله
الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره فوق الصلاة حيث قال {إن الصلاة تنهي عن
الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر} فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر
من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان
وفي الحديث إن الله تعالى يتجلى للمؤمنين فيقول سلوني فيقولون رضاك (1)
فسؤالهم الرضا بعد النظر نهاية التفضيل
وأما رضا  العبد فسنذكر حقيقته وأما رضوان الله تعالى عن العبد فهو بمعنى
آخر يقرب مما ذكرناه في حب الله للعبد ولا يجوز أن يكشف عن حقيقته إذ تقصر
أفهام الخلق عن دركه ومن يقوى عليه فيستقل بإدراكه من نفسه
وعلى الجملة فلا رتبة فوق النظر إليه فإنما سألوه الرضا لأنه سبب دوام
النظر فكأنهم رأوه غاية الغايات وأقصى الأماني لما ظفروا بنعيم النظر فلما
أمروا بالسؤال لم يسألوا إلا دوامه وعلموا أن الرضا هو سبب دوام رفع الحجاب
وقال الله تعالى {ولدينا مزيد} قال بعض المفسرين يأتي أهل الجنة في وقت
المزيد ثلاث تحف من عند رب العالمين أحداها هدية من عند الله تعالى ليس
عندهم في الجنان مثلها فذلك قوله تعالى فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة
عين والثانية السلام عليهم من ربهم فيزيد ذلك على الهدية فضلا وهو قوله
تعالى {سلام قولا من رب رحيم} والثالثة يقول الله تعالى إني عنكم راض فيكون
ذلك أفضل من الهدية والتسليم فذلك قوله تعالى {ورضوان من الله أكبر} أي من
النعيم الذي هم فيه فهذا فضل رضا الله تعالى وهو ثمرة رضا العبد
وأما من الأخبار فقد روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل طائفة من
أصحابه ما أنتم فقالوا مؤمنون فقال ما علامة إيمانكم فقالوا نصبر على
البلاء ونشكر عند الرخاء ونرضى بمواقع القضاء فقال مؤمنون ورب الكعبة (2)
وفي خبر آخر أنه قال حكماء علماء كادوا من فقههم أن يكونوا أنبياء (3) وفي
الخبر طوبى لمن هدي للإسلام وكان رزقه كفافا ورضي به (4) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم من رضي من الله تعالى بالقليل من الرزق رضي الله تعالى منه
بالقليل من العمل (5) وقال أيضا إذا أحب الله تعالى عبدا ابتلاه فإن صبر
اجتباه فإن رضي اصطفاه وقال أيضا إذا كان يوم القيامة أنبت الله تعالى
لطائفة من أمتي أجنحة فيطيرون من قبورهم إلى PageV04P344
الجنان يسرحون فيها ويتنعمون فيها كيف شاءوا فتقول لهم الملائكة هل رأيتم
الحساب فيقولون ما  رأينا حسابا فتقول لهم هل جزتم الصراط فيقولون ما رأينا
صراطا فتقول لهم هل رأيتم جهنم فيقولون ما رأينا شيئا فتقول الملائكة من
أمة من أنتم فيقولون من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فتقول ناشدناكم الله
حدثونا ما كانت أعمالكم في الدنيا فيقولون خصلتان كانتا فينا فبلغنا هذه
المنزلة بفضل رحمة الله فيقولون وماهما فيقولون كنا إذا خلونا نستحي أن
نعصيه ونرضى باليسير مما قسم لنا فتقول الملائكة يحق لكم هذا (1) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم يا معشر الفقراء أعطوا الله الرضا من قلوبكم تظفروا بثواب
فقركم وإلا فلا (2)
وفي أخبار موسى عليه السلام إن بني إسرائيل قالوا له سل لنا ربك أمرا إذا
نحن فعلناه يرضى به عنا فقال موسى عليه السلام
إلهي قد سمعت ما قالوا فقال يا موسى قل لهم يرضون عنى حتى أرضى عنهم
ويشهد لهذا ما روي عن نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من أحب أن يعلم
ماله عند الله عز وجل فلينظر ما لله عز وجل عنده فإن الله تبارك وتعالى
ينزل العبد منه حيث أنزله العبد من نفسه (3) حديث قال الله أنا الله لا إله
إلا أنا من لم يصبر على بلائي الحديث أخرجه الطبرانى في الكبير وابن حبان
في الضعفاء من حديث أبى هند الدارى مقتصرا على قوله من لم يرض بقضائى ويصبر
على بلائى فليلتمس ربا سواى وإسناده ضعيف (4) وفي الخبر المشهور يقول الله
تعالى خلقت الخير والشر فطوبى لمن خلقته للخير وأجريت الخير على يديه وويل
لمن خلقته للشر وأجريت الشر على يديه وويل ثم ويل لمن قال لم وكيف (5)
وفي الأخبار السالفة أن نبيا من الأنبياء شكا إلى الله عز وجل الجوع
والفقر والقمل عشر سنين فما أجيب إلى ما أراد ثم أوحى الله تعالى إليه كم
تشكو هكذا كان بدؤك عندي في أم الكتاب قبل أن أخلق السموات PageV04P345
والأرض وهكذا سبق لك مني وهكذا قضيت عليك قبل أن أخلق الدنيا أفتريد أن
أعيد خلق الدنيا  من أجلك أم تريد أن أبدل ما قدرته عليك فيكون ما تحب فوق
ما أحب ويكون ما تريد فوق ما أريد وعزتي وجلالي لئن تلجلج هذا في صدرك مرة
أخرى لأمحونك من ديوان النبوة
وروي أن آدم عليه السلام كان بعض أولاده الصغار يصعدون على بدنه وينزلون
يجعل أحدهم رجله على أضلاعه كهيئة الدرج فيصعد إلى رأسه من ينزل على أضلاعه
كذلك وهو مطرق إلى الأرض لا ينطق ولا يرفع رأسه فقال له بعض ولده يا أبت
أما ترى ما يصنع هذا بك لو نهيته عن هذا فقال يا بني إني رأيت ما لم تروا
وعلمت ما لم تعلموا إني تحركت حركة واحدة فأهبطت من دار الكرامة إلى دار
الهوان ومن دار النعيم إلى دار الشقاء
فأخاف أن أتحرك أخرى فيصيبنى مالا أعلم
وقال أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر
سنين فما قال لي لشيء فعلته لم فعلته ولا لشيء لم أفعله لم لا فعلته ولا
قال في شيء كان ليته لم يكن ولا في شيء لم يكن ليته كان وكان إذا خاصمني
مخاصم من أهله يقول دعوه لو قضي شيء لكان (1)
ويروى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود إنك تريد وأريد
وإنما يكون ما أريد فإن سلمت لما أريد كفيتك ما تريد وإن لم تسلم لما أريد
أتعبتك فيما تريد ثم لا يكون إلا ما أريد
وأما الآثار فقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
أول من يدعى إلى الجنة يوم القيامة الذين يحمدون الله تعالى على كل حال
وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز ما بقي لي سرور إلا في مواقع القدر وقيل له ما
تشتهي فقال ما يقضي الله
وقال ميمون بن مهران من لم يرض بالقضاء فليس لحمقه دواء
وقال الفضيل إن لم تصبر على تقدير الله لم تصبر على تقدير نفسك وقال عبد
العزيز بن أبي رواد ليس الشأن في أكل خبز الشعير والخل  ولا في لبس الصوف
والشعر ولكن الشأن في الرضا عن الله عز وجل وقال عبد الله بن مسعود لأن
الحس جمرة أحرقت ما أحرقت وأبقت ما أبقت أحب إلي من أن أقول لشئ كان ليته
لم يكن أو لشيء لم يكن ليته كان
ونظر رجل إلى قرحة في رجل محمد بن واسع فقال إني لأرحمك من هذه القرحة
فقال إني لأشكرها منذ خرجت إذ لم تخرج في عيني
وروي في الإسرائيليات أن عابدا عبد الله دهرا طويلا فأري في المنام فلانة
الراعية رفيقتك في الجنة فسأل عنها إلى أن وجدها فاستضافها ثلاثا لينظر إلى
عملها فكان يبيت قائما وتبيت نائمة ويظل صائما وتظل مفطرة
فقال أما لك عمل غير ما رأيت فقالت ماهو والله إلا ما رأيت لا أعرف غيره
فلم يزل يقول تذكري حتى قالت خصيلة واحدة هي في إن كنت في شدة لم أتمن أن
أكون في رخاء وإن كنت في مرض لم أتمن أن أكون في صحة وإن كنت في الشمس لم
أتمن أن أكون في الظل فوضع العابد يده على رأسه وقال أهذه خصيلة هذه والله
خصلة عظيمة يعجز عنها العباد
وعن بعض السلف أن الله تعالى إذا قضى في السماء قضاء أحب من أهل الأرض أن
يرضوا بقضائه
وقال أبو الدرداء ذروة الإيمان الصبر للحكم والرضا بالقدر وقال عمر رضي
الله عنه
ما أبالي على أي حال أصبحت وأمسيت من شدة أو رخاء
وقال الثوري يوما عند رابعة اللهم ارض عني فقالت أما تستحي من الله أن
تسأله الرضا وأنت عنه غير راض فقال أستغفر الله فقال جعفر بن سليمان الضبعي
فمتى يكون العبد راضيا عن الله PageV04P346
تعالى قالت إذا كان سروره بالمصيبة مثل سروره بالنعمة
وكان الفضيل يقول إذا استوى عنده المنع والعطاء فقد رضي عن الله تعالى
وقال أحمد بن أبي الحواري قال أبو سليمان الداراني إن الله عز وجل من كرمه
قد رضي من عبيده بما رضي العبيد من مواليهم قلت وكيف  ذاك قال أليس مراد
العبد من الخلق أن يرضى عنه مولاه قلت نعم قال فإن محبة الله من عبيده أن
يرضوا عنه
وقال سهل حظ العبيد من اليقين على قدر حظهم من الرضا وحظهم من الرضا على
قدر عيشهم مع الله عز وجل وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله عز وجل
بحكمته وجلاله جعل الروح والفرح في الرضا واليقين وجعل الغم والحزن في الشك
والسخط (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is the absence of displeasure and the soul's inclination toward what is agreeable; riḍā denotes a state of satisfaction where the heart finds repose in the decree.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, riḍā of God toward the servant is His volitional approval and beneficence, while riḍā of the servant toward God is the cessation of complaint and full acquiescence to divine providence (qaḍāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes mutual satisfaction between two parties; metaphorical (majāz) usage elevates it to the highest station of the lovers of God, surpassing even the delights of Paradise.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To decree, determine, and execute a matter with finality; qaḍāʾ is the divine ordainment that precedes all things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine decree encompasses both good and evil as created realities; contentment with it is the mark of true submission (islām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to judicial verdicts; metaphorical usage extends to the totality of God's eternal determination of all events.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The frequent use of conditional particles (in, law) and exceptive clauses (illā) in the prophetic reports structures the logical priority of riḍā as both condition and cause of divine reward.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the verses [indicating this station], there is His saying, the Exalted: {«رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه»} [Allah is well pleased with them and they are well pleased with Him] (Q. 5:119, 9:100, 58:22). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان»} [Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?] (Q. 55:60). The ultimate limit of goodness (iḥsān) is God's good pleasure with His servant, and that is the reward for the servant's good pleasure with God, the Exalted.

And He, the Exalted, said: {«ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر»} [And pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden, and good pleasure from Allah is greater] (Q. 9:72).
