chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The self, soul, breath; that which animates and is the locus of command and inclination
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul as the battleground between the commanding (ammārah), blaming (lawwāmah), and tranquil (muṭmaʾinnah) states
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal self-reproach (muʿātabah) as direct address; metaphorical "war" against the soul as jihād akbar
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with repeated vocative (yā nafs) for rhetorical emphasis (iltifāt)
chapters.translation:
Know that your most hostile enemy is your own soul which resides between your sides. It was created commanding toward evil (ammārah bi-l-sūʾ), inclining toward wickedness, fleeing from goodness. You have been commanded to purify it, to straighten it, and to lead it with the chains of compulsion toward the worship of its Lord and Creator, to restrain it from its appetites, and to wean it from its pleasures. For if you neglect it, it will bolt and run wild, and you will never lay hold of it thereafter. But if you persist with it through reproach, rebuke, censure, and blame, then your soul becomes the blaming soul (al-nafs al-lawwāmah) by which God swore, and you may hope that it becomes the tranquil soul (al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinnah), summoned to enter among the ranks of God's servants, pleased and well-pleasing.

He said: Do not neglect for a single hour its remembrance and its reproach, and do not occupy yourself with preaching others while you have not first preached to your own soul. God Most High revealed to Jesus (upon him peace): "O son of Mary, preach to your own soul; if it heeds, then preach to the people; otherwise, be ashamed before Me." And He Most High said: {«وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرَىٰ تَنفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ»} ("And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers").

Your way is to turn toward it and to establish before it its ignorance and its stupidity — that it forever boasts of its cleverness and guidance, while its pride and haughtiness intensify when it is attributed with foolishness. So say to it: "O soul, how immense is your ignorance! You claim wisdom, intelligence, and acumen, while you are the most stupid and foolish of people. Do you not know what lies before you — the Garden and the Fire — and that you are destined for one of them imminently? Why then do you rejoice and laugh and occupy yourself with frivolity while you are sought for this tremendous matter? Perhaps today you will be snatched away, or tomorrow. I see you regarding death as distant, while God sees it as near. Do you not know that everything coming is near, and that which is distant is only what has not yet arrived? Do you not know that death comes suddenly, without a messenger sent ahead, without appointment or prior agreement — that it comes in no thing rather than another, in no winter rather than summer, in no summer rather than winter, in no day rather than night, in no night rather than day, in no youth rather than old age, nor in old age rather than youth? Rather, every single breath may be the moment of sudden death. And if death does not come suddenly, then illness comes suddenly, and then leads to death. Why do you not prepare for death, which is nearer to you than anything near?

Do you not ponder His saying: {«اقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ * مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ * لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ»} ("The reckoning for the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness, turning away. No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while they play — their hearts distracted").

Woe to you, O soul! If your audacity toward disobeying God stems from your belief that God does not see you, then how immense is your disbelief! And if it is despite your knowledge of His awareness of you, then how severe is your shamelessness and how little your modesty!

Woe to you, O soul! If a servant of your servants — nay, a brother among your brethren — were to confront you with what you detest, how would your anger and hatred toward him be? With what audacity do you expose yourself to God's hatred, His wrath, and His severe punishment? Do you suppose you can endure His chastisement? Far from it, far from it! Test yourself: if heedless pride diverts you from His painful punishment, then restrain yourself for an hour in the sun, or in the bathhouse, or bring your finger near fire, so that your capacity becomes evident to you.

Are you deluded by God's generosity and bounty, and His independence from your obedience and worship? Why then do you not rely upon God's generosity in the important matters of your worldly life? When an enemy approaches you, why do you devise stratagems to repel him rather than entrusting the matter to God's generosity? And when a need for some worldly appetite presses upon you — one that cannot be fulfilled except through dinar and dirham — why do you exhaust yourself in seeking and acquiring it through every means of stratagem, without relying upon God's generosity until He causes you to stumble upon a treasure or subjugates one of His servants to carry your need to you without any effort or seeking on your part? Do you suppose that God is generous in the Hereafter but not in this world, when you know that God's way (sunnah) admits no change, that the Lord of the Hereafter and this world is One, and that {«وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ»} ("man has nothing but what he strives for")?

Woe to you, O soul! How astonishing is your hypocrisy and your vain pretensions! You claim faith with your tongue while the traces of hypocrisy are manifest upon you. Has not your Master and Lord said to you: {«وَمَا مِن دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا»} ("There is no creature on earth but that its provision is upon God")? And He said concerning the matter of the Hereafter: {«وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ»} ("man has nothing but what he strives for"). Thus He has undertaken for you the matter of this world specifically, and diverted you from striving in it — yet you have belied Him with your deeds, and you have become clamorous in seeking it like the frantic scramble of one demented and reckless. And He has entrusted the matter of the Hereafter to your striving — yet you have turned away from it with the turning of one deluded and contemptuous. What are these the signs of faith? If faith were merely by the tongue, then why were the hypocrites placed in the lowest depth of the Fire?

Woe to you, O soul! It is as though you do not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and you suppose that when you die you will slip away and be released. Far from it! Do you suppose you were created in vain? Were you not a drop of emitted semen, then a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned you? Is not He who did this able to bring the dead to life? If this is what you harbor within yourself, then how immense is your disbelief and your ignorance!

Do you not reflect: from what did He create you? From a drop He created you and determined you; then He made the path easy for you; then He caused you to die and buried you. Do you then belie Him in His saying: {«ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنشَرَهُ»} ("Then when He wills, He raises him")? If you are not a denier, then why do you not take your precautions?

If a Jew were to inform you that the most delicious food you eat would harm you in your illness, you would abstain from it and abandon it, struggling against your soul in that matter. Is the word of the prophets, supported by miracles, and the word of God Most High in His revealed books, of less effect upon you than the word of a Jew speaking from conjecture, guesswork, and opinion, with deficient intellect and limited knowledge?

And astonishingly, if a child were to tell you there is a scorpion in your garment, you would cast off your garment immediately, without demanding from him proof or evidence. Is the word of the prophets, the scholars, the sages, and all the saints of lesser account to you than the word of a child among the foolish? Or has the heat of Hell, its chains, its fetters, its zaqqūm, its iron clubs, its pus, its scorching wind, its vipers, and its scorpions become more contemptible to you than a scorpion whose pain you would not feel except for a day or less? What are these the deeds of the intelligent? Nay, if the beasts were to perceive your state, they would laugh at you and mock your intellect.

If you, O soul, have known all this and believed in it, then why do you procrastinate in action while death lies in ambush for you — perhaps it will snatch you without respite? By what have you been assured against the hastening of the term? Even if you were promised respite for a hundred years, do you suppose that one who feeds his mount at the foot of the mountain pass will succeed in crossing the pass with it? If you suppose that, then how immense is your ignorance!

Consider: if a man traveled abroad to acquire religious knowledge, and remained there for years, idle and unoccupied, promising himself that he would study in the final year upon his return home — would you not laugh at his intellect and his supposition that the acquisition of knowledge is something to be hoped for within a short period, or his assumption that the stations of the jurists are attained without jurisprudence, relying upon the generosity of God (glorified and exalted be He)?

Then even if you grant that effort at the end of life is beneficial and that it leads to the highest stations — perhaps today is the last day of your life. Why then do you occupy yourself with other than that? If you have been inspired with respite, what prevents you from hastening? And what impels you to procrastinate? Is there any cause for it except your incapacity to oppose your appetites, due to the toil and hardship involved? Do you await a day that will come in which opposing appetites is not difficult? That is a day God has never created and never will create. The Garden will never be anything but surrounded by hardships (makārih), and hardships will never be light upon souls — this is an impossibility in existence.

Do you not reflect: how long have you been promising yourself, saying "tomorrow, tomorrow"? Tomorrow has come and become today — how did you find it? Do you not know that the tomorrow which came and became today had the same ruling as yesterday? Nay — what you are incapable of today, you will be even more incapable of tomorrow, for appetite is like a deeply-rooted tree which the servant labors to uproot. When the servant is too weak to uproot it and postpones it, he is like one who, being young and strong, is unable to uproot a tree and postpones it for another year, knowing full well that the length of time only increases the tree's strength and rootedness, and increases the uprooter's weakness and frailty. What cannot be done in youth can never be done in old age. Rather, disciplining the aged is torment, and refining the hardened is punishment. The fresh green branch accepts bending; but when it dries and time passes over it, it no longer accepts it.

If you, O soul, do not comprehend these clear matters and cling to procrastination, then why do you claim wisdom? What foolishness exceeds this foolishness?

Perhaps you will say: "Nothing prevents me from uprightness except my craving for the pleasure of appetites and my lack of patience for pains and hardships." How immense is your stupidity and how ugly your excuse! If you are truthful in that, then seek the enjoyment of pleasures that are pure of turbidity, enduring forever and ever — and there is no hope of that except in the Garden. If you are looking to your appetite, then looking to it lies in opposing it: one meal withheld prevents many meals.

What do you say of the intellect of a sick man whose physician advised him to abstain from cold water for three days so that he might be cured and enjoy a single drink for the rest of his life, informing him that if he drinks it he will fall into chronic illness and be deprived of it for the rest of his life? What does the intellect require in fulfilling the claim of appetite — does he endure three days to enjoy a lifetime, or does he satisfy his appetite immediately, fearing the pain of opposition for three days, until he incurs the pain of opposition for three hundred days and three thousand days? All of your life, compared to eternity — which is the duration of the bliss of the people of the Garden and the torment of the people of the Fire — is less than three days compared to an entire lifetime, however long it may be.

Would that I knew: is the pain of abstaining from appetites more severe and longer in duration, or the pain of the Fire in the depths of Hell? One who cannot endure the pain of striving — how can he endure the pain of God's chastisement?

I see you are negligent in looking to yourself only because of hidden disbelief or manifest foolishness. As for hidden disbelief, it is the weakness of your faith in the Day of Reckoning and your scant knowledge of the immense magnitude of reward and punishment. As for manifest foolishness, it is your reliance upon God's generosity and pardon without regard to His cunning (makr), His gradual enticement (istidrāj), and His independence from your worship — while you do not rely upon His generosity even for a morsel of bread, a single grain of wealth, or a single word you hear from people. Rather, you attain your purpose in that through every stratagem. And by this ignorance you deserve the title of foolishness from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), who said: "The intelligent one is he who subdues his soul and works for what comes after death; the foolish one is he who follows his soul's whims and harbors vain hopes upon God."

Woe to you, O soul! It befits you not that the life of this world should delude you, nor that the Deceiver should delude you concerning God. {«لَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ»} ("Let not the Deceiver delude you concerning God"). Look to yourself, for you have not been commanded with anything important for others. Do not waste your hours, for breaths are numbered. When a breath passes from you, a part of you has gone. Seize health before sickness, leisure before occupation, wealth before poverty, youth before old age, and life before death. And prepare for the Hereafter according to the measure of your remaining in it.

O soul! Do you not prepare for winter according to the length of its duration, gathering for it provisions, clothing, firewood, and all means — not relying in that upon God's bounty and generosity to ward off the cold from you without a cloak, felt, firewood, or other things, though He is capable of that? Do you suppose, O soul, that the piercing cold (zamharīr) of Hell is lighter in coldness and shorter in duration than the cold of winter? Or do you suppose it is less than this? Never! It is not so, nor is there any proportion between them in severity and coldness. Do you suppose that the servant is saved from it without effort? Far from it! Just as the cold of winter is not repelled except by the cloak, the fire, and other means, so the heat and cold of the Fire are not repelled except by the fortress of tawḥīd and the trench of acts of obedience. God's generosity lies in that He taught you the way of fortification and facilitated its means for you — not in that the punishment is repelled from you without your fortifying yourself. Just as God's generosity in repelling the cold of winter lies in His creating fire and guiding you to the way of extracting it from between iron and stone, so that you repel the cold of winter with it — and just as the purchase of firewood and the cloak is something your Creator and Master is independent of, and you only purchase them for yourself since He created them as a means to your comfort — so likewise your acts of obedience and your strivings are things He is independent of; they are only your path to your salvation. {«مَنْ أَحْسَنَ فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فَعَلَيْهَا وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ»} ("Whoever does good, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And God is independent of the worlds").

Woe to you, O soul! Withdraw from your ignorance and measure your Hereafter by your worldly life. {«مَّا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ»} ("Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul"). {«وَكَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُ»} ("As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it"). {«وَكَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ»} ("As He originated you, so shall you return"). And you will find no change in God's way (sunnah), nor any alteration.

Woe to you, O soul! I see you have become accustomed to this world and at ease with it, so that parting from it has become difficult for you — while you are advancing toward it and confirming in yourself affection for it. It is as though you are heedless of God's punishment and reward, and of the terrors of the Resurrection and its states. You are not truly believing in death, which separates you from all you love. Do you consider that one who enters the abode of a king to exit from the other side, and casts his gaze upon a beautiful face knowing it will engross his heart, and then is compelled inevitably to part from it — is he counted among the intelligent or the foolish?

Do you not know that this world is the abode of the King of Kings, and that in it there is nothing but passage (majāz)? Everything in it does not accompany those who pass through it after death. For this reason the Master of mankind (peace be upon him) said: "The Holy Spirit breathed into my heart: Love whom you will, for you shall part from him; work what you will, for you shall be recompensed for it; live as you will, for you shall die."

Woe to you, O soul! Do you not know that everyone who turns to the pleasures of this world and finds comfort in them, while death lies behind him, only accumulates regret at the moment of parting, and only provisions himself with deadly poison without knowing it? Do you not look at those who have passed — how they built and rose high, then went and left empty? How God bequeathed their lands and their homes to their enemies? Do you not see how they gathered what they did not eat, built what they did not inhabit, and hoped for what they did not attain? Each one builds a palace raised toward the sky, while his resting place is a grave dug beneath the earth. Is there in this world any foolishness and perversity greater than this — that one builds his worldly life while he is certainly departing from it, and ruins his Hereafter while he is certainly proceeding to it?

Are you not ashamed, O soul, of assisting these fools in their foolishness? Suppose that you are not one possessed of insight to be guided to these matters, but merely incline by nature to imitation and emulation. Then measure the intellect of the prophets, the scholars, and the sages against the intellect of these who are bent upon this world, and emulate from the two groups the one who is more intelligent in your estimation — if you believe yourself to possess intellect and acumen.

O soul! How astonishing is your affair, how severe your ignorance, and how manifest your transgression! Astonishing indeed that you are blind to these clear and sublime matters! Perhaps, O soul, the love of status (jāh) has intoxicated you and stupefied you from understanding them. Do you not reflect that status has no meaning except the inclination of hearts of some people toward you? Suppose that everyone on the face of the earth prostrated to you and obeyed you — do you not know that after fifty years neither you nor anyone on the face of the earth who worshipped you and prostrated to you will remain? And a time will come when neither your mention nor the mention of those who mentioned you will remain, just as it came upon the kings who were before you. Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them even a whisper? {«فَهَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًا»} ("Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them even a whisper?")

How then, O soul, do you sell what endures forever and ever for what does not endure more than fifty years — if even that endures? Even if you were a king of the kings of the earth, with the east and west surrendered to you, necks subdued to you, and all means arranged for you — how, when your decline and misery refuse to surrender to you even the matter of your own quarter, nay, the matter of your own house, let alone your quarter?

If you, O soul, do not abandon this world out of desire for the Hereafter, due to your ignorance and the blindness of your insight — then why do you not abandon it out of elevation above the baseness of its partners, out of purity from the abundance of its toil, and out of caution against the swiftness of its passing? Or why do you not abstain from its little, when much of it has abstained from you? Why do you rejoice in a world which, even if it aids you, your own land is not free of a company of Jews and Magians who surpass you in it and exceed you in its comfort and adornment? Fie upon a world in which these base ones surpass you! How immense is your ignorance, how base your aspiration, and how low your opinion — when you have preferred not to be among the ranks of those brought near — the prophets and the truthful — in the vicinity of the Lord of the Worlds forever and ever, but rather to be in the row of sandals among the foolish and ignorant for a few brief days!

O regret upon you if you lose both this world and the religion! Hasten, woe to you, O soul — you have come to the brink of destruction, death has drawn near, and the warner has come. Who will pray on your behalf after death? Who will fast on your behalf after death? Who will seek your Lord's pleasure on your behalf after death?

Woe to you, O soul! You have nothing but numbered days — they are your merchandise. If you were to trade in them, you have already wasted most of them. If you were to weep for the rest of your life over what you have wasted of it, you would still be falling short of your soul's due. How then, when you waste the remainder and persist in your habit?

Do you not know, O soul, that death is your appointment, the grave your home, the dust your bed, the worms your companions, and the Great Terror before you? Do you not know, O soul, that the army of the dead is at your city's gate awaiting you? They have sworn upon themselves with solemn oaths that they will not leave their place until they take you with them. Do you not know, O soul, that they long to return to this world for a single day to occupy themselves with making up what they neglected — while you are in their very wish? A single day of your life, if it were sold to them for the whole world in its entirety, they would buy it if they could — while you waste your days in heedlessness and idleness!

Woe to you, O soul! Are you not ashamed to adorn your exterior for people while you confront God in secret with enormities? Are you ashamed before people but not before the Creator? Woe to you — is He the least significant of those who observe you? You command people to good while you are sullied with vices; you call to God while fleeing from Him; you remind others of God while forgetful of Him. Do you not know, O soul, that the sinner is more foul than filth, and that filth does not purify other than itself? Why do you hope to purify others while you yourself are not pure?

Woe to you, O soul! If you knew yourself with true knowledge, you would suppose that people are afflicted with no trial except through your ill-omen. Woe to you, O soul! You have made yourself a donkey for Iblīs, which he leads wherever he wills and mocks you — and despite this, you marvel at your own deeds, which contain such afflictions that if you were to escape them head-for-head, the profit would be in your hands. How can you marvel at your deeds with the abundance of your sins and slips? God cursed Iblīs for a single sin after he had worshipped Him for two hundred thousand years, and expelled Adam from the Garden for a single sin despite his being His prophet and chosen one.

Woe to you, O soul! How treacherous you are! Woe to you, O soul! How shameless you are! Woe to you, O soul! How ignorant you are, and how audacious toward sins! Woe to you — how often you tie knots and then undo them! Woe to you — how often you make covenants and then betray them!

Woe to you, O soul! Do you occupy yourself, amid these sins, with building your worldly life as though you were not departing from it? Do you not look at the people of the graves — how they gathered much, built lofty structures, and hoped far-reaching hopes? Then their gathering became ruin, their buildings became graves, and their hopes became delusion. Woe to you, O soul! Have you no lesson in them? Have you no glance toward them? Do you suppose that they were called to the Hereafter while you are among those who abide forever? Far from it, far from it! Evil is what you imagine! You are only in the demolition of your life-span since you fell from your mother's womb. Build your palace on the face of the earth, then — for its belly will soon be your grave.

Do you not fear, when the soul reaches your collarbone {«بَلَغَتِ الْقَلْبَ»} — that the messengers of your Lord will descend upon you with blackened colors and grim faces, bearing tidings of punishment? Will regret benefit you then? Will sorrow be accepted from you? Will weeping bring you mercy?

The wonder — all the wonder — is from you, O soul, that despite all this you claim insight and acumen. And from your acumen is that you rejoice every day at the increase of your wealth, yet do not grieve at the decrease of your life-span. What benefit is wealth that increases while life decreases?

Woe to you, O soul! You turn away from the Hereafter while it advances toward you, and you advance toward this world while it turns away from you. How many are those who face a day they do not complete! How many are those who hope for a tomorrow they do not reach! You witness this in your brethren, your relatives, and your neighbors — you see their regret at death, yet you do not return from your ignorance.

Beware, O wretched soul, of a day in which God has sworn upon Himself that He will not leave a servant whom He commanded in this world and forbade, until He asks him about his deeds — their small and their great, their secret and their open. Look then, O soul: with what body will you stand before God, and with what tongue will you answer? Prepare for the question an answer, and for the answer correctness. Work the remainder of your life — in short days for long days, in an abode of passing for an abode of permanence, in an abode of grief and toil for an abode of bliss and eternity. Work before you cannot work. Depart from this world voluntarily, with the departure of the free, before you are driven out of it by compulsion. Do not rejoice in what aids you of the blossoms of this world — for many a rejoicing one is deceived, and many a deceived one does not perceive. Woe to him who has woe, then does not perceive — laughing, rejoicing, playing, exulting, eating, drinking, while it is established for him in the Book of God that he is among the fuel of the Fire.

Let your gaze, O soul, upon this world be one of reflection (iʿtibār), your striving in it one of necessity (iḍṭirār), your renunciation of it one of choice (ikhtiyār), and your seeking of the Hereafter one of haste (ibtidār). Do not be among those who are incapable of gratitude for what they have been given, who seek increase in what remains, who forbid people while not forbidding themselves.

Know, O soul, that there is no substitute for religion, no exchange for faith, no replacement for the body. One whose mount is night and day is carried along even if he does not move.

So heed this admonition, O soul, and accept this counsel. For whoever turns away from admonition has accepted the Fire — and I do not see you as accepting it, nor as heedful of this admonition. If hardness of heart prevents you from accepting admonition, then seek help against it through persistence in night prayer (tahajjud) and standing in worship. If it does not cease, then through constancy in fasting. If it does not cease, then through reducing social mixing and speech. If it does not cease, then through maintaining family ties and kindness to orphans. If it does not cease, then know that God has sealed your heart and locked it, and that the darkness of sins has accumulated upon its exterior and interior. Then prepare yourself for the Fire — for God created the Garden and created for it its people, and created the Fire and created for it its people; each is facilitated for what he was created for.

If there remains in you no room for admonition, then despair of yourself — yet despair (qunūṭ) is itself one of the grave sins. We seek refuge in God from that! You have no path to despair, nor any path to hope while the ways of good are blocked against you — for that would be delusion, not hope.

Look now: does grief seize you over this calamity with which you have been afflicted? Does your eye permit a tear of mercy upon yourself? If it does, then the source of tears is from the sea of mercy — there remains in you a place for hope. Then persist in lamentation and weeping, seek help from the Most Merciful of the merciful, complain to the Most Generous of the generous, persist in seeking succor, and do not weary of lengthy complaint. Perhaps He will have mercy upon your weakness and succor you. For your calamity has become great, your trial has become severe, your persistence has become long, the stratagems have been cut off from you, and the excuses have departed from you. There is no escape, no object of seeking, no succor, no refuge, no shelter, no deliverance — except to your Master. So flee to Him with supplication, and humble yourself in your supplication according to the measure of your immense ignorance and the abundance of your sins. For He has mercy upon the supplicant who is abased, succors the seeker who is anguished, and answers the call of the distressed. {«أَمَّن يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ»} ("Or who answers the distressed when he calls upon Him?")

Today you have become distressed toward Him, and in need of His mercy. The paths have become narrow for you, the roads have been blocked against you, the stratagems have been cut off from you, admonitions have not succeeded with you, and reproach has not broken you. Yet the One sought from is Generous, the One asked is Munificent, the One from whom succor is sought is Righteous and Compassionate. Mercy is vast, generosity overflowing, pardon all-encompassing.

Say: "O Most Merciful of the merciful! O Compassionate, O Merciful! O Forbearing, O Mighty, O Generous! I am the sinner who persists! I am the audacious one who does not desist! I am the one who continues on who does not feel shame! This is the station of the distressed supplicant, the wretched poor one, the weak and contemptible one, the perishing and drowning one! So hasten my succor and my relief, show me the traces of Your mercy, make me taste the coolness of Your pardon and forgiveness, and grant me strength through Your might — O Most Merciful of the merciful!"

Following the example of your father Adam (upon him peace). Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When God caused Adam to descend from the Garden to the earth, he remained with his tears never drying. God (mighty and majestic) looked upon him on the seventh day while he was sorrowful, dejected, oppressed, with head bowed. God Most High revealed to him: "O Adam, what is this exertion I see in you?" He said: "My Lord, my calamity has become great, my sin has encompassed me, and I have been expelled from the dominion of my Lord. I have come to an abode of humiliation after honor, an abode of misery after happiness, an abode of toil after rest, an abode of trial after well-being, an abode of passing after permanence, and an abode of death and annihilation after eternity and endurance. How should I not weep over my sin?" God Most High revealed to him: "O Adam, did I not choose you for Myself, settle you in My abode, single you out with My honor, and warn you of My wrath? Did I not create you with My hand, breathe into you of My spirit, and cause My angels to prostrate to you? Yet you disobeyed My command, forgot My covenant, and exposed yourself to My wrath. By My might and My majesty, if you filled the earth with men all like you, worshipping Me and glorifying Me, then they disobeyed Me — I would cast them down to the stations of the disobedient." At that, Adam (upon him peace) wept for three hundred years.

ʿUbayd Allāh al-Bajalī was given to much weeping. He would say in his weeping throughout his night: "My God, I am the one whose sins increase as his life grows longer. I am the one who, whenever I resolve to abandon a sin, another appetite presents itself to me. O my grief — a sin that has not withered while its possessor seeks another! O my grief — if the Fire is to be your resting place and abode! O my grief — if the iron clubs are prepared for your head! O my grief — You have fulfilled the needs of the seekers; perhaps Your need will not be fulfilled!"

Mansūr ibn ʿAmmār said: I heard in one of the nights in Kūfah a worshipper communing with his Lord, saying: "O Lord, by Your might, I did not intend by disobeying You to oppose You. I did not disobey You while ignorant of Your station, nor seeking Your punishment, nor making light of Your gaze. But my soul enticed me, my misery aided me in that, and Your veil lowered over me deluded me. So I disobeyed You in my ignorance and opposed You by my deed. chapters.arabic_text:
### || كتاب التفكر وهو الكتاب التاسع من ربع المنجيات من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي لم يقدر لانتهاء عزته نحوا ولا قطرا ولم يجعل لمراقى
أقدام الأوهام ومرمى سهام الأفهام إلى حمى عظمته مجرى بل ترك قلوب الطالبين
في بيداء كبريائه والهة حيرى كلما اهتزت لنيل مطلوبها ردتها سبحات الجلال
قسرا وإذا همت بالانصراف آيسة نوديت من سرادقات الجمال صبرا صبرا ثم قيل
لها أجيلى فى ذل العبودية منك فكرا لأنك لو تفكرت في جلال الربوبية لم
تقدرى له قدرا وإن طلبت وراء الفكر في صفاتك أمرا فانظرى في نعم الله تعالى
وأياديه كيف توالت عليك تترى وجددى لكل نعمة منها ذكرا وشكرا وتأملى في
بحار المقادير كيف فاضت على العالمين خيرا وشرا ونفعا وضرا وعسرا ويسرا
وفوزا وخسرا وجبرا وكسرا وطيا ونشرا وإيمانا وكفرا وعرفانا ونكرا فإن جاوزت
النظر في الأفعال إلى النظر  في الذات فقد حاولت أمرا إمرا وخاطرت بنفسك
مجاوزة حد طاقة البشر ظلما وجورا فقد انبهرت العقول دون مبادى
إشراقهوانتكصت على أعقابها اضطرارا وقهرا والصلاة على محمد سيد ولد آدم وإن
كان لم يعد سيادته فخرا صلاة تبقى لنا في عرصات القيامة عدة وذخرا وعلى آله
وأصحابه الذين أصبح كل واحد منهم في سماء الدين بدرا ولطوائف المسلمين صدرا
وسلم تسليما كثيرا
أما بعد فقد وردت السنة بأن تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سنة (1) وكثر الحث في
كتاب الله تعالى على التدبر والاعتبار والنظر والافتكار ولا يخفى أن الفكر
هو مفتاح الأنوار ومبدأ الاستبصار وهو شبكة العلوم ومصيدة المعارف والفهوم
وأكثر الناس قد عرفوا فضله ورتبته لكن جهلوا حقيقته وثمرته ومصدره ومورده
ومجراه ومسرحه وطريقه وكيفيته ولم يعلم أنه كيف يتفكر وفيماذا يتفكر ولماذا
يتفكر وما الذى يطلب به أهو مراد لعينه أم لثمرة تستفاد منه فإن كان لثمرة
فما تلك الثمرة أهى من العلوم أو من الأحوال أو منهما جميعا وكشف جميع ذلك
مهم ونحن نذكر أولا فضيلة التفكر
ثم حقيقة التفكر وثمرته
ثم مجارى الفكر ومسارحه إن شاء الله تعالى

### ||| فضيلة التفكر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ك-ر (f-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deliberation, turning over an affair in the mind; the heart's movement toward discernment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intellectual reflection (tafakkur) as the soul's journey from sensory particulars to intelligible universals — the bridge between knowledge (ʿilm) and action (ʿamal).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — mental traversal of meanings; metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's "grazing" (marʿā) in fields of contemplation.
- Root: ت-د-ب-ر (t-d-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Considering the end/consequence (dubur) of a matter; looking to what follows.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quranic term for pondering the outcomes of divine acts — the opposite of superficial glance (naẓar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — turning to the rear; metaphorical — tracing effects back to their causes.
- Root: ع-ب-ر (ʿ-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Crossing over from one state to another; extracting a lesson (ʿibrah) from a witnessed event.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of passing from the seen (shāhid) to the unseen (ghāʾib) — the epistemological basis of analogical reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — traversing a valley; metaphorical — the mind's crossing from creation to Creator.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Inversion and Parenthetical Insertion (al-taqdīm wa al-taʾkhīr maʿa al-iʿtirāḍ) — In the opening doxology, the relative clause "الذي لم يقدر..." is fronted as a sustained epithet of Allah, with multiple parallel negated verbs (لم يقدر، لم يجعل) creating a rhythmic cascade; the parenthetical "وإن كان لم يعد سيادته فخرا" interrupts the eulogy of the Prophet to preempt any charge of boastfulness, requiring the translator to preserve this concessive aside.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to Allah, who did not ordain for the extremity of His might any direction or pole, and who made no passage for the climbing-steps of fancies or the flight-path of intellects' arrows toward the sanctuary of His grandeur. Rather, He left the hearts of the seekers in the wasteland of His majesty — bewildered, distracted. Whenever they stirred to attain their sought object, the splendors of His glory repelled them by force; and when they resolved to turn away in despair, a voice called to them from the pavilions of His beauty: "Patience, patience!" Then it was said to them: "Roam within the lowliness of servitude, reflecting — for if you reflected upon the majesty of Lordship, you could never measure His due. And if you seek something beyond reflection upon your own attributes, then look upon the blessings of Allah and His favors — how they have poured upon you in succession. Renew for every blessing a remembrance and a thanksgiving. And contemplate the seas of decrees — how they have overflowed upon the worlds with good and evil, benefit and harm, hardship and ease, triumph and loss, mending and breaking, folding and unfolding, faith and disbelief, knowledge and denial. For if you pass beyond the consideration of acts to the consideration of the Essence, you have attempted a monstrous matter and risked yourself in transgressing the limit of human capacity — wrongfully and tyrannically. For intellects are overwhelmed before the thresholds of His dawning light, and they recoil upon their heels — compelled and subdued."

And the prayer of blessing upon Muhammad, the master of the children of Adam — though he did not count his mastery as a boast — a prayer that remains for us in the plains of the Resurrection as a provision and a store. And upon his family and his companions, each of whom became in the heaven of religion a full moon, and for the factions of the Muslims a foremost breast. And abundant peace.

To proceed: The Sunnah has conveyed that "reflection for an hour is better than a year of worship" {«تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سنة»}. And the exhortation in the Book of Allah is abundant concerning pondering (al-tadabbur), taking heed (al-iʿtibār), considering (al-naẓar), and reflecting (al-iftikār). It is no secret that reflection (al-fikr) is the key to lights, the beginning of insight, the net of sciences, and the snare of understandings and comprehensions. Most people have known its virtue and rank, but they have been ignorant of its reality, its fruit, its source, its destination, its course, its pasture, its path, and its modality. They have not known: How does one reflect? Upon what does one reflect? Why does one reflect? And what is sought by it — is it desired for its own sake, or for a fruit derived from it? For if it is for a fruit, then what is that fruit — is it among the sciences, or among the states (al-aḥwāl), or from both together? The unveiling of all of this is important. We shall mention first the virtue of reflection (faḍīlat al-tafakkur), then the reality of reflection and its fruit, then the courses of reflection and its pastures — if Allah Most High wills.

### ||| The Virtue of Reflection
