When God's command descended upon him, his mother bent over him and began saying: "My son, I used to warn you of this your fall, and I said you have a day." He said: "O mother, I have a Lord of abundant kindness, and I hope that He will not deprive me today of some of His kindness." Thābit said: So God had mercy on him for his good opinion of his Lord.

Jābir ibn Wadāʿah said: There was a young man with waywardness (rahq). When he was in his death-throes, his mother said: "My son, do you leave any instruction?" He said: "Yes—my ring, do not strip it from me, for it bears the remembrance of God; perhaps God will have mercy on me." When he was buried, he was seen in a dream and said: "Tell my mother that the word has benefited me, and that God has forgiven me."

A Bedouin fell ill, and it was said to him: "You are dying." He said: "Where am I being taken?" They said: "To God." He said: "Then why should I dislike going to One from whom no good is seen but from Him?"

Abū al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān said: My father said, when death approached him: "O Muʿtamir, narrate to me the concessions (rukhaṣ), so that perhaps I may meet God Almighty while holding a good opinion of Him." And they used to deem it commendable to mention to a servant the good deeds of his works at his death, so that he might hold a good opinion of his Lord.

### ||||| Exposition of the Regret at the Encounter with the Angel of Death, Through Narratives Whose State of Affairs the Tongue of the Situation Expresses

chapters.title_en: The Angel of Death and the Taking of Souls: Accounts of the Righteous and the Tyrants
chapters.arabic_text:
قال أشعث بن أسلم سأل إبراهيم عليه السلام ملك الموت وأسمه عزرائيل وله
عينان عين في وجهه وعين في قفاه فقال يا ملك الموت ما تصنع
إذا كان نفس بالمشرق ونفس بالمغرب ووقع الوباء بأرض والتقى الزحفان كيف
تصنع قال أدعوا الأرواح بإذن الله فتكون بين اصبعي هاتين وقال قد دحيت له
الأرض فتركت مثل الطشت بين يديه يتناول منها ما يشاء قال وهو يبشره بأنه
خليل الله عز وجل
وقال سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام لملك الموت عليه السلام مالى لا أراك
تعدل بين الناس تأخذ هذا وتدع هذا قال ما أنا بذلك بأعلم منك إنما هي صحف
أو كتب تلقى إلي فيها أسماء وقال وهب بن منبه كان ملك من الملوك أراد أن
يركب إلى أرض فدعا بثياب ليلبسها فلم تعجبه فطلب غيرها حتى لبس ما أعجبه
بعد مرات وكذلك طلب دابة فأتى بها فلم تعجبه حتى أتى بدواب فركب أحسنها
فجاء إبليس فنفخ في منخره نفخة فملأه كبرا
ثم سار وسارت معه الخيول وهو لا ينظر إلى الناس كبرا فجاءه رجل رث الهيئة
فسلم فلم يرد عليه السلام فأخذ بلجام دابته فقال أرسل اللجام فقد تعاطيت
أمر عظيما قال إن لي إليك حاجة قال اصبر حتى أنزل قال لا الآن فقهره على
لجام دابته فقال أذكرها قال هو سر فأدنى له رأسه فساره وقال أنا ملك الموت
فتغير لون الملك واضطرب لسانه ثم قال دعني حتى أرجع إلى أهلي وأقضي حاجتي
وأودعهم قال لا والله لا ترى أهلك وثقلك أبدا فقبض روحه فخر كأنه خشبة ثم
مضى فلقي عبدا مؤمنا في تلك الحال فسلم عليه فرد السلام فقال إن لي إليك
حاجة أذكرها في أذنك فقال هات فساره وقال أنا ملك الموت فقال أهلا ومرحبا
بمن طالت غيبته على فوالله ما كان في الأرض غائب أحب إلى أن ألقاه منك فقال
ملك الموت اقض حاجتك التي خرجت لها فقال مالي حاجة أكبر عندي ولا أحب من
لقاء الله تعالى قال فاختر على أي حال شئت أن أقبض روحك فقال تقدر على ذلك
قال نعم إني أمرت بذلك قال فدعني حتى اتوضأ وأصلي ثم اقبض روحي وأنا ساجد
فقبض روحه وهو ساجد وقال أبو بكر بن عبد الله المزني جمع رجل من بني
إسرائيل مالا فلما أشرف على الموت قال لبنيه أروني أصناف أموالي فأتى بشيء
كثير من الخيل والإبل والرقيق وغيره فلما نظر إليه بكي تحسرا عليه فرآه ملك
الموت وهو يبكى فقال له ما يبكيك فوالذي خولك ما أنا بخارج من منزلك حتى
أفرق بين روحك وبدنك قال فالمهلة حتى أفرقه قال هيهات انقطعت عنك المهلة
فهلا كان ذلك قبل حضور أجلك فقبض روحه
وروى أن رجلا جمع مالا فأوعى ولم يدع صنفا من المال إلا اتخذه وابتنى
قصرا وجعل عليه بابين وثيقين وجمع عليه حرسا من غلمانه ثم جمع أهله وصنع
لهم طعاما وقعد على سريره ورفع إحدى رجليه على الأخرى وهم يأكلون فلما
فرغوا قال يا نفس أنعمي لسنين فقد جمعت لك ما يكفيك فلم يفرغ من كلامه حتى
أقبل إليه ملك الموت في هيئة رجل عليه خلقان من الثياب وفي عنقه مخلاة
يتشبه بالمساكين فقرع الباب بشدة عظيمة قرعا أفزعه وهو على فراشه فوثب إليه
الغلمان وقالوا ما شأنك فقال أدعوا إلى مولاكم فقالوا وإلى مثلك يخرج
مولانا قال نعم فأخبروه بذلك فقال هلا فعلتم به وفعلتم فقرع الباب قرعة أشد
من الأولى فوثب إليه الحرس فقال أخبروه أني ملك الموت فلما سمعوه ألقى
عليهم الرعب ووقع على مولاهم الذل والتخشع فقال قولوا له قولا لينا وقولوا
هل تأخذ به أحدا فدخل عليه وقال اصنع في مالك ما أنت صانع فإني لست بخارج
منها حتى أخرج روحك فأمر بماله حتى وضع بين يديه فقال حين رآه لعنك الله من
مال أنت شغلتني عن عبادة ربي ومنعتني أن  أتخلى لربي فأنطق
PageV04P467
الله المال فقال لم تسبني وقد كنت تدخل على السلاطين بي ويرد المتقي عن
بابهم وكنت تنكح المتنعمات بي وتجلس مجالس الملوك بي وتنفقني في سبيل الشر
فلا امتنع منك ولو أنفقتني في سبيل الخير نفعتك خلقت يا بن آدم من تراب
فمنطلق ببر ومنطلق بإثم ثم قبض ملك الموت روحه فسقط
وقال وهب بن منبه قبض ملك الموت روح جبار من الجبابرة ما في الأرض مثله
ثم عرج إلى السماء فقالت الملائكة لمن كنت أشد رحمة ممن قبضت روحه قال أمرت
بقبض نفس امرأة في فلاة من الأرض فأتيتها وقد ولدت مولودا فرحمتها لغربتها
ورحمت ولدها لصغره وكونه في فلاة لا متعهد له بها
فقالت الملائكة الجبار الذي قبضت الآن روحه هو ذلك المولود الذي رحمته
فقال ملك الموت سبحان اللطيف لما يشاء قال عطاء بن يسار إذا كانت ليلة
النصف من شعبان دفع إلى ملك الموت صحيفة فيقال اقبض في هذه السنة من في هذه
الصحيفة قال فإن العبد ليغرس الغراس وينكح الأزواج ويبني البنيان وإن اسمه
في تلك الصحيفة وهو لا يدري
وقال الحسن ما من يوم إلا وملك اليوم يتصفح كل بيت ثلاث مرات فمن وجده
منهم قد استوفى رزقه وانقضى أجله قبض روحه فإذا قبض روحه أقبل أهله برنة
وبكاء فيأخذ ملك الموت بعضادتي الباب فيقول والله ما أكلت له رزقا ولا
أفنيت له عمرا ولا انتقصت له أجلا وإن لي فيكم لعودة بعد عودة حتى لا ابقي
منكم أحدا
قال الحسن فوالله لو يرون مقامه ويسمعون كلامه لذهلوا عن ميتهم ولبكوا
على أنفسهم وقال يزيد الرقاشى بينما جبار من الجبابرة من بني إسرائيل جالس
في منزله قد خلا ببعض أهله إذ نظر إلى شخص قد دخل من باب بيته فثار إليه
فزعا مغضبا فقال له من أنت ومن أدخلك على داري فقال أما الذي أدخلني الدار
فربها وأما أنا فالذي لا يمنع من الحجاب ولا استأذن على الملوك ولا أخاف
صولة  المتسلطين ولا يمتنع مني كل جبار عنيد ولا شيطان مريد قال فسقط في يد
الجبار وارتعد حتى سقط منكبا على وجهه ثم رفع رأسه إليه مستجديا متذللا له
فقال له أنت إذن ملك الموت قال أنا هو قال فهل أنت ممهل حتى أحدث عهدا قال
هيهات انقطعت مدتك وانقضت أنفاسك ونفدت ساعاتك فليس إلى تأخيرك سبيل قال
فإلى أين تذهب بي قال إلى عملك الذي قدمته وإلى بيتك الذي مهدته قال فإني
لم اقدم عملا صالحا ولم أمهد بيتا حسنا قال فإلى لظى نزاعة للشوى ثم قبض
روحه فسقط ميتا بين أهله فمن بين صارخ وباك
قال يزيد الرقاشى لو يعلمون سوء المنقلب كان العويل على ذلك اكثر
وعن الأعمش عن خيثمة قال دخل ملك الموت على سليمان بن داود عليه السلام
فجعل ينظر إلى رجل من جلسائه يديم النظر إليه فلما خرج قال الرجل من هذا
قال هذا ملك الموت قال لقد رايته ينظر إلى كأنه يريدني قال فماذا تريد قال
أريد أن تخلصني منه فتأمر الريح حتى تحملني إلى أقصى الهند ففعلت الريح ذلك
ثم قال سليمان لملك الموت بعد أن أتاه ثانيا رأيتك تديم النظر إلى واحد من
جلسائي قال نعم كنت أتعجب منه لأني كنت أمرت أن أقبضه بأقصى الهند في ساعة
قريبة وكان عندك فعجبت من ذلك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ض (q-b-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seize, grasp, take hold of firmly; to contract or draw together; used for taking possession of something entirely.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, qabḍ al-rūḥ is the divine act of seizing the soul at death—an execution of God's decree, not a mere physical action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical grasping; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's extraction from the body, implying divine authority.
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; one who holds authority over a realm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Malak (angel) as a spiritual agent executing God's command; malik al-mawt as the appointed executor of death's decree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for human kingship; metaphorical for angelic authority, emphasizing subordination to God's will.
- Root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Mercy, compassion, tenderness; from raḥim (womb), implying protective care.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine mercy (raḥmah) as an attribute of God, and human mercy as a virtue reflecting divine compassion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for emotional compassion; metaphorical for God's overarching mercy in decreeing death's timing.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — The use of circumstantial accusatives (e.g., "وهو يبشره" — "while he was giving him glad tidings") to depict simultaneous actions, enhancing narrative vividness and temporal layering.
chapters.translation:
I say: Ashʿath ibn Aslam said: Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, questioned the Angel of Death, whose name is ʿAzrāʾīl, and he has two eyes—one in his face and one in the back of his head. He said: "O Angel of Death, what do you do when a soul is in the East and a soul in the West, and a plague strikes a land, and two armies clash—how do you manage?" He replied: "I summon the spirits by God's permission, and they come between these two fingers." And he said: "The earth has been spread out for me, and it is left like a basin before me; I take from it whatever I wish." He was giving him glad tidings that he was the Khalīl (intimate friend) of God, Mighty and Majestic.

And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, peace be upon them both, said to the Angel of Death, peace be upon him: "Why do I not see you being equitable among people—taking this one and leaving that one?" He said: "I am not more knowledgeable of that than you. It is merely scrolls or books cast upon me containing the names." And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: There was a king among the kings who wished to ride to a certain land. He called for garments to wear, but they did not please him, so he sought others until he wore what pleased him after several attempts. Likewise, he sought a mount, and one was brought, but it did not please him, until several mounts were brought, and he rode the finest of them. Then Iblīs came and blew a breath into his nostril, filling him with pride.

Then he set out, and the horses rode with him, and he did not look at the people out of arrogance. A man of shabby appearance came to him and greeted him, but he did not return the greeting. The man seized the reins of his mount and said: "Release the reins, for you have undertaken a grave matter." He said: "I have a need of you." The king said: "Wait until I dismount." He said: "No, now." So he overpowered him over the reins of his mount and said: "Remember it." He said: "It is a secret." So he lowered his head to him, and he whispered to him, saying: "I am the Angel of Death." The king's color changed, and his tongue faltered. Then he said: "Let me return to my family, settle my affairs, and bid them farewell." He said: "No, by God, you shall never see your family or your wealth again." So he seized his soul, and he fell like a piece of wood. Then he departed and met a believing servant in that same state, and he greeted him, and he returned the greeting. He said: "I have a need of you; I will mention it in your ear." He said: "Come forth." So he whispered to him and said: "I am the Angel of Death." He said: "Welcome and greetings to one whose absence has been long! By God, there was no absent one on earth more beloved to me to meet than you." The Angel of Death said: "Fulfill the need for which you set out." He said: "I have no need greater to me, nor more beloved, than meeting God, the Exalted." He said: "Choose in whatever state you wish that I seize your soul." He said: "Can you do that?" He said: "Yes, I have been commanded to do so." He said: "Then let me perform ablution and pray, then seize my soul while I am prostrating." So he seized his soul while he was prostrating.

And Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī said: A man from the Children of Israel amassed wealth. When death approached him, he said to his sons: "Show me my various kinds of wealth." So a great quantity of horses, camels, slaves, and other things was brought. When he looked upon it, he wept in regret over it. The Angel of Death saw him weeping and said to him: "What makes you weep? By Him who granted you this, I will not leave your house until I separate your soul from your body." He said: "Then grant me respite until I divide it." He said: "Alas! Respite has been cut off from you. Why was this not done before the arrival of your term?" So he seized his soul.

And it is narrated that a man amassed wealth and stored it, leaving no kind of wealth except that he acquired it. He built a palace and placed upon it two strong gates, and gathered guards from his servants. Then he gathered his family and prepared food for them, and sat upon his couch, raising one leg over the other, while they were eating. When they finished, he said: "O soul, enjoy yourself for years, for I have gathered for you what suffices you." He had not finished his speech when the Angel of Death approached him in the form of a man wearing two worn garments, with a sack around his neck, resembling the poor. He knocked at the door with a tremendous knock that frightened him while he was on his bed. The servants rushed to him and said: "What is your matter?" He said: "Summon your master to me." They said: "Should our master go out to one like you?" He said: "Yes." So they informed him of that, and he said: "Why did you not do such-and-such to him?" Then he knocked at the door with a knock more severe than the first. The guards rushed to him, and he said: "Inform him that I am the Angel of Death." When they heard that, terror was cast upon them, and humiliation and abasement fell upon their master. He said: "Say to him a gentle word, and ask: 'Will you take anyone in his place?'" So he entered upon him and said: "Do with your wealth what you will, for I will not leave this place until I extract your soul." So he ordered his wealth to be placed before him. When he saw it, he said: "May God curse you, O wealth! You have occupied me from the worship of my Lord and prevented me from devoting myself to my Lord." Then God caused the wealth to speak, saying: "Do not revile me. I used to enter with you upon the sultans, and the God-fearing were turned away from their doors. You married the pleasure-seeking women with me, and you sat in the assemblies of kings with me, and you spent me in the path of evil, and I did not withhold from you. Had you spent me in the path of good, I would have benefited you. You were created, O son of Adam, from dust, and you depart with virtue or depart with sin." Then the Angel of Death seized his soul, and he fell.

And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The Angel of Death seized the soul of a tyrant among the tyrants, the like of whom was not on earth. Then he ascended to heaven, and the angels said: "To whom were you more merciful than the one whose soul you have just seized?" He said: "I was commanded to seize the soul of a woman in a desolate land. I came to her, and she had just given birth to a child. I had mercy on her for her estrangement, and I had mercy on her child for his smallness and his being in a desolate land with no one to care for him." The angels said: "The tyrant whose soul you have just seized—he is that very child whom you had mercy upon." So the Angel of Death said: "Glory be to the Subtle One, who does as He wills."

And ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār said: When it is the night of the middle of Shaʿbān, a scroll is delivered to the Angel of Death, and it is said: "Take in this year whoever is in this scroll." He said: "For the servant may plant saplings, marry spouses, and build buildings, while his name is in that scroll, and he does not know."

And al-Ḥasan said: There is no day except that the Angel of Death surveys every house three times. Whoever he finds among them has completed his provision and fulfilled his term, he seizes his soul. When he seizes his soul, his family turns to wailing and weeping. So the Angel of Death takes hold of the doorposts and says: "By God, I have not eaten his provision, nor have I exhausted his lifespan, nor have I diminished his term. And I have a return to you after this return, until I leave none of you remaining." Al-Ḥasan said: "By God, if they saw his station and heard his words, they would be distracted from their dead and would weep for themselves."

And Yazīd al-Raqqāshī said: While a tyrant among the tyrants of the Children of Israel was sitting in his house, having secluded himself with one of his family, he saw a figure entering through the door of his house. He rose to him in fright and anger, saying: "Who are you, and who brought you into my abode?" He said: "As for the one who brought me into the house, it is its Lord. As for me, I am the one who is not prevented by veils, nor do I seek permission from kings, nor do I fear the assault of tyrants, nor does any obstinate tyrant or rebellious devil resist me." The tyrant's hands fell in despair, and he trembled until he fell on his side upon his face. Then he raised his head to him, begging and humbling himself, and said: "You are then the Angel of Death." He said: "I am he." He said: "Will you grant me respite until I make a new covenant?" He said: "Alas! Your term is cut off, your breaths are exhausted, and your hours are spent. There is no way to delay you." He said: "Then where will you take me?" He said: "To your deeds which you have sent ahead, and to your house which you have prepared." He said: "But I have not sent ahead righteous deeds, nor have I prepared a good house." He said: "Then to the blazing fire, which strips away the skin." Then he seized his soul, and he fell dead among his family—some screaming, some weeping. Yazīd al-Raqqāshī said: "If they knew the evil of the final destination, the wailing would be greater than that."

And from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, he said: The Angel of Death entered upon Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and began looking intently at a man among his companions, fixing his gaze upon him. When he departed, the man said: "Who was that?" He said: "That was the Angel of Death." He said: "I saw him looking at me as though he intended me." He said: "Then what do you want?" He said: "I want you to save me from him, so command the wind to carry me to the farthest reaches of India." So the wind did that. Then Sulaymān said to the Angel of Death, after he came to him a second time: "I saw you fixing your gaze upon one of my companions." He said: "Yes, I was marveling at him, because I was commanded to seize his soul in the farthest reaches of India at a near hour, and he was with you. So I marveled at that."

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Chapter on the Death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the Rightly-Guided Caliphs After Him — The Death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| الباب الرابع في وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والخلفاء الراشدين من بعده

### ||||| وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-و-ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core linguistic root meaning — cessation of vital functions; death as the departure of the soul from the body; also used for the "death" of inanimate things (e.g., land becoming barren).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — in the Quranic and theological context, death (mawt) is not annihilation but a transition (intiqāl) from one abode to another; for the Prophet ﷺ, it is the supreme mark of his human nature (bashariyyah) and the completion of his prophetic mission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical death; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual death (e.g., ignorance) or the "death" of a community's honor. Here, it is literal, but with a reverential nuance of "passing" (wafāh), which elevates the register.
- Root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core linguistic root meaning — right guidance, maturity of judgment, uprightness in conduct; the opposite of error (ghayy).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "Rightly-Guided" (rāshidūn) as a technical title for the four caliphs, signifying their infallible adherence to the prophetic sunnah in governance and jurisprudence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal for those who follow the straight path; metaphorical for those whose rule embodies divine guidance (hidāyah) as a collective blessing.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "الخلفاء الراشدين" is an appositive to "رسول الله" in the genitive construction, clarifying the scope of the chapter's subject; the wa (and) here functions as a coordinating conjunction linking two distinct but sequential historical events, requiring the reader to parse the temporal succession (tartīb) implied by "من بعده" (after him).
chapters.translation: I say: Now we come to the fourth chapter, concerning the death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the rightly-guided caliphs (al-khulafāʾ al-rāshidūn) who succeeded him. And the first matter to be treated herein is the passing (wafāh) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).

chapters.title_en: The Death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as an Admonition and Exemplar
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسوة حسنة حيا وميتا وفعلا
وقولا وجميع أحواله عبرة للناظرين
PageV04P468
وتبصرة للمستبصرين إذ لم يكن أحد أكرم على الله منه إذ كان خليل الله
وحبيبه ونجيه وكان صفيه ورسوله ونبيه فأنظر هل أمهله ساعة عند انقضاء مدته
وهل أخره لحظة بعد حضور منيته لا بل أرسل إليه الملائكة الكرام الموكلين
بقبض أرواح الأنام فجدوا بروحه الزكية الكريمة لينقلوها وعالجوها ليرحلوها
عن جسده الطاهر إلى رحمة ورضوان وخيرات حسان  بل إلى مقعد صدق في جوار
الرحمن فاشتد مع ذلك في النزع كربه وظهر أنينه وترادف قلقه وارتفع حنينه
وتغير لونه وعرق جبينه واضطربت في الإنقباض والإنبساط شماله ويمينه حتى بكى
لمصرعه من حضره وانتحب لشدة حاله من شهد منظره فهل رأيت منصب النبوة دافعا
عنه مقدورا وهل راقب الملك فيه أهلا وعشيرا وهل سامحه إذ كان للحق نصيرا
وللخلق بشيرا ونذيرا هيهات بل امتثل ما كان به مأمورا واتبع ما وجده في
اللوح مسطورا فهذا كان حاله وهو عند الله ذو المقام المحمود والحوض المورود
وهو أول من تنشق عنه الأرض وهو صاحب الشفاعة يوم العرض فالعجب أنا لا نعتبر
به ولسنا على ثقة فيما نلقاه بل نحن أسراء الشهوات وقرناء المعاصي والسيئات
فما بالنا لا نتعظ بمصرع محمد سيد المرسلين وإمام المتقين وحبيب رب
العالمين لعلنا نظن أننا مخلدون أو نتوهم أنا مع سوء أفعالنا عند الله
مكرمون هيهات هيهات بل نتيقن أنا جميعا على النار واردون ثم لا ينجو منها
إلا المتقون فنحن للورود مستيقنون وللصدور عنها متوهمون لا بل ظلمنا أنفسنا
إن كنا كذلك لغالب الظن منتظرين فما نحن والله من المتقين وقد قال الله رب
العالمين {وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا
ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا} فلينظر كل عبد إلى نفسه أنه إلى الظالمين أقرب أم
إلى المتقين فانظر إلى نفسك بعد أن تنظر إلى سيرة السلف الصالحين فلقد
كانوا مع ما وفقوا له من الخائفين
ثم انظر إلى سيد المرسلين فإنه كان من أمره على يقين إذ كان سيد النبيين
وقائد المتقين واعتبر كيف كان كربه عند فراق الدنيا وكيف اشتد أمره عند
الانقلاب إلى جنة المأوى قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه دخلنا على رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيت أمنا عائشة رضي الله عنها حين دنا الفراق فنظر
إلينا فدمعت عيناه صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قال مرحبا بكم حياكم الله آواكم
الله  نصركم الله وأوصيكم بتقوى الله وأوصى بكم الله إني لكم منه نذير مبين
ألا تعلوا على الله في بلاده وعباده وقد دنا الأجل والمنقلب إلى الله وإلى
سدرة المنتهى وإلى جنة المأوى وإلى الكأس الأوفى فاقرءوا على أنفسكم وعلى
من دخل في دينكم بعدى مني السلام ورحمة الله حديث ابن مسعود دخلنا على رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيت أمنا عائشة حين دنا الفراق الحديث رواه
البزار وقال هذا الكلام قد روى عن مرة عن عبد الله من غير وجه وأسانيدها
متقاربة قال وعبد الرحمن الأصبهاني لم يسمع هذا من مرة وإنما هو عمن أخبره
عن مرة قال ولا أعلم أحد رواه عن عبد الله غير مرة قلت وقد روى من غير وجه
رواه ابن سعد في الطبقات من رواية ابن عوف عن ابن مسعود وروينا في مشيخة
القاضي أبي بكر الأنصاري من رواية الحسن العربي عن ابن مسعود ولكنهما
منقطعان وضعيفان والحسن العربي إنما يرويه عن مرة كما رواه ابن أبي الدنيا
والطبراني في الأوسط (1) حديث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لجبريل عند موته
من لأمتي بعدي فأوحى الله تعالى إلى جبريل أن بشر حبيبي ان لا أخذله في
أمته الحديث أخرجه الطبراني من حديث جابر وابن عباس في حديث طويل فيه من
لأمتي المصطفاة من بعدي قال أبشر ياحبيب الله فإن الله عز وجل يقول قد حرمت
الجنة على جميع الأنبياء والأمم حتى تدخلها أنت وأمتك قال الآن طابت نفسي
وإسناده ضعيف وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها أمرنا PageV04P469
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نغسله بسبع قرب من سبعة آبار ففعلنا ذلك
فوجد راحة فخرج فصلى بالناس واستغفر لأهل أحد ودعا لهم وأوصى بالأنصار فقال
أما بعد يا معشر المهاجرين فإنكم تزيدون وأصبحت الأنصار لا تزيد على التى
هي عليها اليوم وإن الأنصار عيبتي التي أويت إليها فأكرموا كريمهم يعنى
محسنهم وتجاوزوا عن مسيئهم ثم قال إن عبدا خير بين الدنيا وبين ما عند  الله
فاختار ما عند الله فبكى أبو بكر رضي الله عنه وظن أنه يريد نفسه فقال
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على رسلك يا أبا بكر سدوا هذه الأبواب الشوارع في
المسجد إلا باب أبي بكر فإني لا أعلم أمرا أفضل عندي في الصحبة من أبي بكر
(1) قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها فقبض صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيتي وفي يومي
وبين سحري ونحري وجمع الله بين ريقي وريقه عند الموت فدخل على أخي عبد
الرحمن وبيده سواك فجعل ينظر إليه فعرفت انه يعجبه ذلك فقلت له آخذه لك
فأومأ برأسه أن نعم فناولته إياه فأدخله في فيه فاشتد عليه فقلت إلينه لك
فأومأ برأسه أن نعم فلينته وكان بين يديه ركوة ماء فجعل يدخل فيها يده
ويقول لا إله إلا الله إن للموت لسكرات ثم نصب يده يقول الرفيق الأعلى
الرفيق الأعلى فقلت إذن والله لا يختارنا (2) وروى سعيد بن عبد الله عن
أبيه قال لما رأت الأنصار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يزداد ثقلا أطافوا
بالمسجد فدخل العباس رضي الله عنه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأعلمه
بمكانهم وإشفاقهم ثم دخل عليه الفضل فأعلمه بمثل ذلك ثم دخل عليه علي رضي
الله عنه فأعلمه بمثله فمد يده وقال ها فتناولوه فقال {ما تقولون} قالوا
نقول نخشى أن تموت وتصايح نساؤهم لاجتماع رجالهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم فثار رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فخرج متوكئا على علي والفضل
والعباس أمامه ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوب الرأس يخط برجليه حتى
جلس على أسفل مرقاة من المنبر وثاب الناس إليه فحمد الله وأثنى عليه وقال
أيها الناس إنه بلغني أنكم تخافون على الموت كأنه استنكار منكم للموت وما
تنكرون من موت نبيكم ألم أنع إليكم وتنعى إليكم أنفسكم هل خلد نبي قبلي
فيمن بعث فأخلد فيكم ألا إني لاحق بربي وإنكم لاحقون به وإني أوصيكم
بالمهاجرين الأولين خيرا وأوصي المهاجرين فيما بينهم فإن الله  عز وجل قال
والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا إلى آخرها وإن الأمور تجري بإذن
الله فلا يحملنكم استبطاء أمر على استعجاله فإن الله عز وجل لا يعجل لعجلة
أحد ومن غالب الله غلبه ومن خادع الله خدعه فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا
في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم وأوصيكم بالأنصار خيرا فإنهم الذين تبوءوا الدار
والإيمان من قبلكم أن تحسنوا إليهم ألم يشاطروكم الثمار ألم يوسعوا عليكم
في الديار ألم يؤثروكم على أنفسهم وبهم الخصاصة ألا فمن ولي أن يحكم بين
رجلين فليقبل من محسنهم وليتجاوز عن مسيئهم ألا ولا تستأثروا عليهم ألا
وإني فرط لكم وأنتم لاحقون بي ألا وإن موعدكم الحوض حوضي أعرض مما بين بصرى
الشام وصنعاء اليمن يصب فيه ميزاب الكوثر ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وألين من
الزبد وأحلى من الشهد من شرب منه لم يظمأ أبدا حصباؤه اللؤلؤ وبطحاؤه المسك
من حرمه في الموقف غدا حرم الخير كله ألا فمن أحب أن يرده علي غدا فليكفف
لسانه ويده إلا مما ينبغي فقال العباس يا نبي الله أوص بقريش فقال إنما
أوصي بهذا الأمر قريشا والناس تبع لقريش برهم لبرهم وفاجرهم لفاجرهم
فاستوصوا آل قريش بالناس خيرا يا أيها الناس إن الذنوب تغير النعم وتبدل
القسم فإذا بر الناس برهم أئمتهم وإذا فجر الناس عقولهم قال الله تعالى
وكذلك نولى PageV04P470
بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون (1) حديث ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى
الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بكر سل يا أبا بكر فقال يا رسول الله دنا الأجل
فقال قد دنا الأجل الحديث في سؤالهم له من يلي غسلك وفيم نكفنك وكيفية
الصلاة عليه رواه ابن سعد في الطبقات عن محمد بن عمر وهو الواقدي باسناد
ضعيف إلى ابن عوف عن ابن مسعود وهو مرسل ضعيف كما تقدم (2) فقام عمر فلما
كبر وكان رجلا صيتا سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صوته بالتكبير فقال
أين أبو بكر يأبى الله ذلك والمسلمون قالها  ثلاث مرات مروا أبا بكر فليصل
بالناس فقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها يا رسول الله إن أبا بكر رجل رقيق القلب
إذا قام في مقامك غلبه البكاء فقال إنكن صويحبات يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل
بالناس قال فصلى أبو بكر بعد الصلاة التي صلى عمر فكان عمر يقول لعبد الله
بن زمعة بعد ذلك ويحك ماذا صنعت بي والله لولا أني ظننت أن رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم أمرك ما فعلت
فيقول عبد الله إني لم أر أحدا أولى بذلك منك قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
وما قلت ذاك ولا صرفته عن أبي بكر إلا رغبة به عن الدنيا ولما في الولاية
من المخاطرة والهلكة إلا من سلم الله وخشيت أيضا أن لا يكون الناس يحبون
رجلا صلى في مقام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو حي أبدا إلا أن يشاء الله
فيحسدونه ويبغون عليه ويتشاءمون به فإذن الأمر أمر الله والقضاء قضاؤه
وعصمه الله من كل ما تخوفت عليه من أمر الدنيا والدين (3) وقالت عائشة رضي
الله عنها فلما PageV04P471
كان اليوم الذي مات فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأوا منه خفة في
أول النهار فتفرق عنه الرجال إلى منازلهم وحوائجهم مستبشرين وأخلوا رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنساء فبينا نحن على ذلك لم نكن على مثل حالنا
في الرجاء والفرح قبل ذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اخرجن عني هذا
الملك يستأذن علي فخرج من في البيت غيري ورأسه في حجري فجلس وتنحيت في جانب
البيت فناجى الملك طويلا ثم إنه دعاني فأعاد رأسه في حجري وقال للنسوة
ادخلن فقلت ما هذا بحس جبريل عليه السلام فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم أجل يا عائشة هذا ملك الموت جاءني فقال إن الله عز وجل أرسلني وأمرني
أن لا أدخل عليك إلا بإذن فإن لم تأذن لي أرجع وإن أذنت لي دخلت وأمرني أن
لا أقبضك حتى تأمرني فماذا أمرك فقلت أكفف عني  حتى يأتيني جبريل عليه
السلام فهذه ساعة جبريل فقالت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها فاستقبلنا بأمر لم
يكن له عندنا جواب ولا رأى فوجمنا وكأنما ضربنا بصاخة ما نحير إليه شيئا
وما يتكلم أحد من أهل البيت إعظاما لذلك الأمر وهيبة ملأت أجوافنا قالت
وجاء جبريل في ساعته فسلم فعرفت حسه وخرج أهل البيت فدخل فقال إن الله عز
وجل يقرأ عليك السلام ويقول كيف تجدك وهو أعلم بالذي تجد منك ولكن أراد أن
يزيدك كرامة وشرفا وأن يتم كرامتك وشرفك على الخلق وأن تكون سنة في أمتك
فقال أجدني وجعا فقال أبشر فإن الله تعالى أراد أن يبلغك ما أعد لك فقال يا
جبريل إن ملك الموت استأذن علي وأخبره الخبر فقال جبريل يا محمد إن ربك
إليك مشتاق ألم يعلمك الذي يريد بك لا والله تعالى ما استأذن ملك الموت على
أحد قط ولا يستأذن عليه أبدا إلا أن ربك متم شرفك وهو إليك مشتاق قال فلا
تبرح إذن حتى يجىء وأذن للنساء فقال يا فاطمة ادنى فأكبت عليه فناجاها
فرفعت رأسها وعيناها تدمع وما تطيق الكلام ثم قال أدني مني رأسك فأكبت عليه
فناجاها فرفعت رأسها وهي تضحك وما تطيق الكلام فكان الذي رأينا منها عجبا
فسألتها بعد ذلك فقالت أخبرني وقال إني ميت اليوم فبكيت ثم قال إني دعوت
الله أن يلحقك بي في أول أهلي وأن يجعلك معي فضحكت وأدنت ابنيها منه فشمهما
قالت وجاء ملك الموت واستأذن فأذن له فقال الملك
ما تأمرنا يا محمد قال الحقني بربي الآن فقال بلى من يومك هذا أما إن ربك
إليك مشتاق ولم يتردد عن أحد تردده عنك ولم ينهنى عن الدخول على أحد إلا
بإذن غيرك ولكن ساعتك أمامك وخرج قالت وجاء جبريل فقال السلام عليك يا رسول
الله هذا آخر ما أنزل فيه إلى الأرض أبدا طوى الوحي وطويت الدنيا وما كان
لي في الأرض حاجة غيرك ومالي فيها حاجة إلا حضورك ثم لزوم موقفي  لا والذي
بعث محمدا بالحق ما في البيت أحد يستطيع أن يحير إليه في ذلك كلمة ولا يبعث
إلى أحد من رجاله لعظم ما يسمع من حديثه ووجدنا وإشفاقنا قالت فقمت إلى
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أضع رأسه بين ثديي وأمسكت بصدره وجعل يغمى
عليه حتى يغلب وجبهته ترشح رشحا ما رأيته من إنسان قط فجعلت أسلت ذلك العرق
وما وجدت رائحة شيء أطيب منه فكنت أقول له إذا أفاق بأبي أنت وأمي ونفسي
وأهلي ما تلقى جبهتك من الرشح فقال يا عائشة إن نفس المؤمن تخرج بالرشح
ونفس الكافر تخرج من شدقيه كنفس الحمار فعند ذلك ارتعنا وبعثنا إلى أهلنا
فكان أول رجل جاءنا ولم يشهده أخي بعثه إلى أبي فمات رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم قبل أن يجيء أحد وإنما صدهم الله عنه لأنه ولاه جبريل وميكائيل
وجعل إذا أغمى عليه قال بل الرفيق الأعلى كأن الخيرة تعاد عليه فإذا أطاق
الكلام قال الصلاة الصلاة إنكم لا تزالون متماسكين ما صليتم جميعا الصلاة
الصلاة كان يوصي بها حتى مات وهو
PageV04P472
يقول الصلاة الصلاة (1) قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها مات رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم بين ارتفاع الضحى وانتصاف النهار يوم الاثنين (2) قالت فاطمة رضي
الله عنها ما لقيت من يوم الاثنين والله لا تزال الأمة تصاب فيه بعظيمة
وقالت أم كلثوم يوم أصيب علي كرم الله وجهه بالكوفة مثلها ما لقيت من يوم
الاثنين مات فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيه قتل علي كرم وفيه قتل
أبي فما لقيت من يوم الاثنين وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لما مات رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم اقتحم الناس حين ارتفعت الرنة وسجى رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم الملائكة بثوبة فاختلفوا فكذب بعضهم بموته وأخرس بعضهم فما تكلم
إلا بعد البعد وخلط آخرون فلاثوا الكلام بغير بيان وبقي آخرون معهم عقولهم
وأقعد آخرون فكان عمر بن الخطاب فيمن كذب بموته وعلي فيمن أقعد  وعثمان فيمن
أخرس
فخرج عمر على الناس وقال أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يمت
وليرجعنه الله عز وجل وليقطعن أيدي وأرجل رجال من المنافقين يتمنون لرسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الموت إنما واعده الله عز وجل كما واعد موسى وهو
آتيكم (3) وفي رواية أنه قال يا أيها الناس كفوا ألسنتكم عن رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم فإنه لم يمت والله لا أسمع أحدا يذكر أن رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم قد مات إلا علوته بسيفي هذا
وأما علي فإنه أقعد فلا يبرح البيت
وأما عثمان فجعل لا يكلم أحدا يؤخذ بيده فيجاء به ويذهب به ولم يكن أحد
من المسلمين في مثل حال أبي بكر والعباس فإن الله عز وجل أيدهما بالتوفيق
والسداد وإن كان الناس لم يرعووا إلا بقول أبي بكر حتى جاء العباس فقال
والله الذي لا إله إلا هو لقد ذاق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الموت ولقد
قال وهو بين أظهركم {إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم
تختصمون}
وبلغ أبا بكر الخبر وهو في بني الحرث بن الخزرج فجاء ودخل على رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم فنظر إليه PageV04P473
ثم أكب عليه فقبله ثم قال بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله ما كان الله تعالى
ليذيقك الموت مرتين فقد والله توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم خرج
إلى الناس فقال أيها الناس من كان يعبد محمدا فإن محمدا قد مات ومن كان
يعبد رب محمد فإنه حى لا يموت قال الله تعالى وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من
قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل أنقلبتم على أعقابكم الآية (1) فكأن الناس لم
يسمعوا هذه الآية إلا يومئذ وفي رواية أن أبا بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه لما
بلغه الخبر دخل بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي على النبي صلى
الله عليه وسلم وعيناه تهملان وغصصه ترتفع كقصع الجرة وهو في  ذلك جلد الفعل
والمقال فأكب عليه فكشف عن وجهه وقبل جبينه وخديه ومسح وجهه وجعل يبكي
ويقول بأبي أنت وأمي ونفسي وأهلي طبت حيا وميتا انقطع لموتك ما لم ينقطع
لموت أحد من الأنبياء والنبوة فعظمت عن الصفة وجللت عن البكاء وخصصت حتى
صرت مسلاة وعممت حتى صرنا فيك سواء ولولا أن موتك كان اختيارا منك لجدنا
لحزنك بالنفوس ولولا أنك نهيت عن البكاء لأنفذنا عليك ماء العيون فأما مالا
نستطيع نفيه عنا فكمد وأدكار محالفان لا يبرحان اللهم فأبلغه عنا اذكرنا يا
محمد صلى الله عليك عند ربك ولنكن من بالك فلولا ما خلفت من السكينة لم يقم
أحد لما خلفت من الوحشة اللهم أبلغ نبيك عنا وأحفظه فينا (2)
وعن ابن عمر أنه لما دخل أبو بكر البيت وصلى وأثنى عج أهل البيت عجيجا
سمعه أهل المصلى كلما ذكر شيئا ازدادوا فما سكن عجيجهم إلا تسليم رجل على
الباب صيت جلد قال السلام عليكم يا أهل البيت {كل نفس ذائقة الموت} الآية
إن في الله خلفا من كل أحد ودركا لكل رغبة ونجاة من كل مخافة فالله تعالى
فارجوا وبه فثقوا
فاستمعوا له وأنكروه وقطعوا البكاء فلما انقطع البكاء فقد صوته فاطلع
أحدهم فلم ير أحدا ثم عادوا فبكوا فناداهم مناد آخر لا يعرفون صوته يا اهل
البيت اذكروا الله تعالى واحمدوه على كل حال تكونوا من المخلصين إن في الله
عزاء من كل مصيبة وعوضا من كل رغيبة فالله فأطيعوا وبأمره فاعملوا
فقال أبو بكر هذا الخضر واليسع عليهما السلام حضرا النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم (3) واستوفى القعقاع بن عمرو حكاية خطبة أبي بكر رضي الله عنه فقال
قام أبو بكر في الناس PageV04P474
خطيبا حيث قضى الناس عبراتهم بخطبة جلها الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم فحمد الله وأثنى عليه على كل حال وقال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده
صدق وعده ونصر عبده وغلب الأحزاب وحده فلله الحمد وحده وأشهد أن محمدا عبده
ورسوله وخاتم  أنبيائه وأشهد أن الكتاب كما شرع وأن الدين كما شرع وأن
الحديث كما حدث وأن القول كما قال وأن الله هو الحق المبين اللهم فصل على
محمد عبدك ورسولك ونبيك وحبيبك وأمينك وخيرتك وصفوتك بأفضل ما صليت به على
أحد من خلقك اللهم واجعل صلواتك ومعافاتك ورحمتك على سيد المرسلين وخاتم
النبيين وإمام المتقين محمد قائد الخير وإمام الخير ورسول الرحمة اللهم قرب
زلفته وعظم برهانه وكرم مقامه وابعثه مقاما محمودا يغبطه به الأولون
وألاخرون وانفعنا بمقامه المحمود يوم القيامة واخلفه فينا في الدنيا
والآخرة وبلغه الدرجة والوسيلة في الجنة اللهم صلي على محمد وعلى آل محمد
وبارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت وباركت على إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد
أيها الناس إنه من كان يعبد محمدا فإن محمدا قد مات ومن كان يعبد الله فإن
الله حي لم يمت وإن الله قد قدم إليكم في أمره فلا تدعوه جزعا فإن الله عز
وجل قد اختار لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ما عنده على ما عندكم وقبضه إلى
ثوابه وخلف فيكم كتابه وسنة نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن أخذ بهما عرف ومن
فرق بينهما أنكر {يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط} ولا يشغلنكم
الشيطان بموت نبيكم ولا يفتننكم عن دينكم وعالجوا الشيطان بالخير تعجزوه
ولا تستنظروه فيلحق بكم ويفتنكم
وقال ابن عباس لما فرغ أبو بكر من خطبته قال يا عمر أنت الذي بلغني انك
تقول ما مات نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما ترى أن نبي الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم قال يوم كذا كذا وكذا ويوم كذا كذا وكذا وقال تعالى في كتابه
{إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون} فقال والله لكأني لم أسمع بها في كتاب الله قبل الآن
لما نزل بنا أشهد أن الكتاب كما أنزل وأن الحديث كما حدث وأن الله حي لا
يموت {إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون} وصلوات الله على رسوله وعند الله نحتسب
رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم جلس  إلى أبي بكر
وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لما اجتمعوا لغسله قالوا والله ما ندري كيف
نغسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنجرده عن ثيابه كما نصنع بموتانا أو
نغسله في ثيابه قالت فأرسل الله عليهم النوم حتى ما بقي منهم رجل إلا واضع
لحيته على صدره نائما ثم قال قائل لا يدري من هو غسلوا رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم في ثيابه فانتبهوا ففعلوا ذلك فغسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
في قميصه حتى إذا فرغوا من غسله كفن
وقال علي كرم الله وجهه أردنا خلع قميصه فنودينا لا تخلعوا عن رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم ثيابه
فأقررناه فغسلناه في قميصه كما نغسل موتانا مستلقيا ما نشاء أن يقلب لنا
منه عضو لم يبالغ فيه إلا قلب لنا حتى نفرغ منه وإن معنا لحفيفا في البيت
كالريح الرخاء ويصوت بنا ارفقوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنكم
ستكفون فهكذا كانت وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يترك
PageV04P475
سبدا ولا لبدا إلا دفن معه
قال أبو جعفر فرش لحده بمفرشه وقطيفته وفرشت ثيابه عليها التي كان يلبس
يقظان على القطيفة والمفرش ثم وضع عليها في أكفانه فلم يترك بعد وفاته مالا
ولا نبي في حياته لبنة على لبنة ولا وضع قصبة على قصبة (1) ففي وفاته عبرة
تامة وللمسلمين به أسوة حسنة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ب-ر (ʿ-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cross over, to traverse from one state to another; the essential meaning of passing through and extracting a lesson from what is witnessed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIbrah (admonition) is the state of the soul that moves one from heedlessness to reflection upon the divine decree, particularly regarding mortality and the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its ḥaqīqah (literal) sense of "crossing over" from life to death, and metaphorically (majāz) as the "lesson" that transports the heart from worldly attachment to otherworldly concern.
- Root: أ-س-و (a-s-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To heal, to mend; the core sense of restoring what is broken.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Us'wah (exemplar) — a model whose conduct, when followed, heals the spiritual malady of the soul and restores its sound disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is employed in its literal sense of "pattern to be imitated," yet carries the rhetorical weight of a physician's remedy for the sickness of worldly attachment.
- Root: ن-ز-ع (n-z-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pull out violently, to extract forcibly; the violent drawing forth of something from its place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Nazʿ (the agony of death) — the forcible separation of the soul from the body, a theological reality that afflicts even the most honored of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for the physical extraction of the soul by the angel of death; metaphorically extended to the spiritual struggle of detachment from worldly existence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension of Governing) — The construction "اعلم أن..." (Know that...) governs a nominal sentence in the accusative, establishing a definitive epistemic frame for the entire discourse that follows, marking the author's authoritative pedagogical voice.
chapters.translation:
Know that in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there is a beautiful exemplar (us'wah ḥasanah) — in his life and in his death, in his deeds and in his words. All of his states are an admonition (ʿibrah) for those who look, and an insight for those who seek discernment. For there was none more honored before Allah than he, for he was the Intimate Friend of Allah (khalīl Allāh), His Beloved (ḥabībuhu), and His Confidant (najiyyuhu). He was His Chosen One (ṣafiyyuhu), His Messenger (rasūluhu), and His Prophet (nabiyyuhu).

Consider then: Did Allah grant him respite for even an hour when his term concluded? Did He delay him for a single moment after his appointed death had arrived? No indeed! Rather, He sent to him the noble angels entrusted with seizing the souls of all creation. They hastened to his pure and generous spirit to transport it, and they labored over it to remove it from his sacred body — unto mercy, good pleasure, and beautiful bounties. Nay, unto a seat of truth in the proximity of the All-Merciful.

Yet despite all this, his distress at the throes of death intensified, his groaning became manifest, his restlessness followed in succession, his yearning rose high, his color changed, his brow perspired, and his right and left sides trembled in contraction and expansion — until those present wept at his fall, and those who witnessed his state sobbed at the severity of his condition.

Do you see the station of prophethood repelling what was decreed from him? Did the angel observe in him family or kin? Did he show him leniency because he was a supporter of the Truth and a bearer of glad tidings and a warner to creation? Far from it! Rather, he fulfilled what he was commanded, and followed what he found inscribed upon the Preserved Tablet.

Such was his state — while he holds before Allah the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) and the Presented Basin (al-ḥawḍ al-mawrūd). He is the first from whom the earth will split open, and he is the master of intercession on the Day of Presentation.

The wonder is that we do not take admonition from him, nor are we certain of what we shall encounter. Rather, we are captives of lusts and companions of sins and misdeeds. What is the matter with us that we do not take heed from the death of Muhammad, the Master of the Messengers, the Imam of the God-fearing, and the Beloved of the Lord of the Worlds? Do we suppose that we shall be immortalized? Or do we imagine that we, despite our evil deeds, are honored before Allah? Far from it! Far from it! Rather, we are certain that we shall all enter the Fire — {«وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا كَانَ عَلَى رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَقْضِيًّا ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it [Hell]; this is with your Lord a decree which must be accomplished. Then We shall save those who used to fear Allah and were dutiful to Him. And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.) [Maryam 19:71-72]

So let every servant look to himself: is he nearer to the wrongdoers or to the God-fearing? Look to yourself after you have looked to the conduct of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn) — for they, despite what they were granted of success, were among the fearful.

Then look to the Master of the Messengers — for he was certain of his affair, being the leader of the prophets and the guide of the God-fearing. Consider how severe was his distress at parting from this world, and how intense was his state at his return to the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-maʾwā).

Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: We entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of our mother ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) when the parting drew near. He looked at us and his eyes filled with tears (ﷺ). Then he said: "Welcome to you. May Allah give you life, may Allah shelter you, may Allah grant you victory. I enjoin upon you the fear of Allah, and I entrust you to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner. Do not rise above Allah in His lands and among His servants. The term has drawn near, and the return is to Allah, to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntahā), to the Garden of Refuge, and to the fullest cup. Convey from me peace and the mercy of Allah upon yourselves and upon those who enter your religion after me."

[The narrator notes:] The hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — "We entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of our mother ʿĀʾishah when the parting drew near" — was narrated by al-Bazzār, who said: "This statement has been narrated from Murrah from ʿAbdullāh through multiple chains, and their chains are close [in strength]. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣbahānī did not hear this from Murrah; rather, it is from one who informed him from Murrah. I know of no one who narrated it from ʿAbdullāh other than Murrah." I [al-Ghazālī] say: It has also been narrated through other chains — Ibn Saʿd narrated it in al-Ṭabaqāt from the narration of Ibn ʿAwf from Ibn Masʿūd, and we have narrated it in the Mashyakhah of Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Anṣārī from the narration of al-Ḥasan al-ʿArabī from Ibn Masʿūd — but both are disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) and weak (ḍaʿīf). Al-Ḥasan al-ʿArabī only narrates it from Murrah, as did Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ.

[Another narration:] That he (ﷺ) said to Jibrīl at his death: "Who will be for my community after me?" So Allah (Exalted is He) revealed to Jibrīl: "Give glad tidings to My Beloved that I shall not abandon him regarding his community." [Al-Ṭabarānī narrated it from the hadith of Jābir and Ibn ʿAbbās in a long hadith containing:] "Who will be for my chosen community after me?" He said: "Rejoice, O Beloved of Allah, for Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says: 'I have forbidden Paradise to all the prophets and nations until you and your community enter it.'" He said: "Now my soul is at peace." Its chain is weak.

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to wash him with seven waterskins from seven wells, and we did so. He found relief, then went out and led the people in prayer, sought forgiveness for the people of Uḥud, supplicated for them, and enjoined [good] upon the Anṣār. He said: "To proceed: O company of the Muhājirūn, you will increase, while the Anṣār will not increase beyond what they are today. Indeed, the Anṣār are my inner circle (ʿaybatī) to whom I have resorted. So honor their honorable ones — meaning their doers of good — and overlook their wrongdoers." Then he said: "Indeed, a servant was given the choice between this world and what is with Allah, and he chose what is with Allah." Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) wept, thinking he meant himself. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gently, O Abū Bakr. Block these open doors into the mosque except the door of Abū Bakr, for I do not know anyone better in companionship to me than Abū Bakr."

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: He was taken (qubiḍa) (ﷺ) in my house, on my day, between my chest and my neck. Allah joined my saliva with his saliva at death. My brother ʿAbd al-Raḥmān entered carrying a tooth-stick (siwāk). He [the Prophet] kept looking at it, and I knew he desired it. I said to him: "Shall I take it for you?" He nodded his head — yes. I gave it to him, and he put it in his mouth, but it was hard for him. I said: "Shall I soften it for you?" He nodded — yes. I softened it. Before him was a small vessel of water. He kept dipping his hand into it and saying: "There is no god but Allah. Indeed, death has agonies (sakarāt)." Then he raised his hand saying: "The Most Exalted Companion (al-rafīq al-aʿlā)! The Most Exalted Companion!" I said: "Then, by Allah, he will not choose us."

Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated from his father: When the Anṣār saw that the Prophet (ﷺ) was growing heavier [in illness], they surrounded the mosque. Al-ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of their position and concern. Then al-Faḍl entered and informed him likewise. Then ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) entered and informed him likewise. He extended his hand and said: "Here!" So they took it. He said: "What do you say?" They said: "We say we fear that you may die, and their women have begun to cry out at the gathering of their men to the Prophet (ﷺ)." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose and went out, leaning upon ʿAlī and al-Faḍl, with al-ʿAbbās before him — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his head bandaged, tracing lines with his feet — until he sat on the lowest step of the pulpit (minbar). The people gathered to him. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:

"O people, it has reached me that you fear death for me — as though you find my death objectionable. And what do you find objectionable about the death of your Prophet? Did I not announce to you, and was not your own death announced to you? Was any prophet before me immortalized among those to whom he was sent, such that I would be immortalized among you? Indeed, I am joining my Lord, and you shall join Him. I enjoin upon you goodness toward the early Muhājirūn, and I enjoin the Muhājirūn to [maintain] good relations among themselves. For Allah (Mighty and Majestic) said: {«وَالْعَصْرِ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا»} (By Al-ʿAṣr. Verily, man is in loss, except those who believe...) to the end of the chapter. Indeed, affairs proceed by the permission of Allah. Do not let your deeming a matter slow cause you to hasten it. For Allah (Mighty and Majestic) does not hasten due to anyone's haste. Whoever contends with Allah will be overcome, and whoever deceives Allah will be deceived. {«فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ»} (Would you then, if you were given the authority, do mischief in the land, and sever your ties of kinship?) [Muhammad 47:22]

I enjoin upon you goodness toward the Anṣār, for they are those who {«تَبَوَّءُوا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمَانَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ»} (settled in the home [Madinah] and adopted faith before you) [al-Ḥashr 59:9]. Be good to them. Did they not share their fruits with you? Did they not make room for you in their dwellings? Did they not prefer you over themselves even in poverty? Indeed, whoever is appointed to judge between two men, let him accept from their good-doers and overlook their wrongdoers. Indeed, do not take exclusively for yourselves over them. Indeed, I am your forerunner (faraṭ) and you shall join me. Indeed, your appointment is at the Basin (al-ḥawḍ) — my Basin, whose width is greater than the distance between Busrā of Syria and Ṣanʿāʾ of Yemen. Into it flows the spout of al-Kawthar. Its water is whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again. Its pebbles are pearls and its soil is musk. Whoever is denied it at the Standing tomorrow has been denied all good. Indeed, whoever wishes to return to it tomorrow, let him restrain his tongue and his hand from everything except what is proper."

Al-ʿAbbās said: "O Prophet of Allah, enjoin [good] upon Quraysh." He said: "I only enjoin this matter upon Quraysh. The people are followers of Quraysh — their righteous follow their righteous, and their wicked follow their wicked. I enjoin the family of Quraysh to treat the people well. O people, indeed sins change blessings and alter what is apportioned. When the righteous are righteous, their leaders are righteous; and when the people become wicked, their intellects become wicked." Allah (Exalted is He) said: {«وَكَذَلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضًا بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ»} (And thus We do make the wrongdoers turn to others as friends because of what they used to earn.) [al-Anʿām 6:129]

[The hadith of Ibn Masʿūd:] That the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abū Bakr: "Ask, O Abū Bakr." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the term has drawn near." He said: "The term has drawn near." [This is] the hadith concerning their asking him who would wash him, in what he would be shrouded, and the manner of praying over him. Ibn Saʿd narrated it in al-Ṭabaqāt from Muhammad ibn ʿUmar — who is al-Wāqidī — with a weak chain to Ibn ʿAwf from Ibn Masʿūd, and it is a disconnected (mursal) weak narration, as mentioned previously.

Then ʿUmar stood — and he was a man with a loud voice. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard his voice saying the takbīr and said: "Where is Abū Bakr? Allah refuses that, and the Muslims [refuse it]." He said it three times: "Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer." ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Bakr is a soft-hearted man. When he stands in your place, weeping overcomes him." He said: "Indeed, you are [like] the companions of Yūsuf. Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer." So Abū Bakr led the prayer after the prayer that ʿUmar had led. ʿUmar would thereafter say to ʿAbdullāh ibn Zamʿah: "Woe to you! What have you done to me? By Allah, had I not thought that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded you, I would not have done it." ʿAbdullāh would say: "I did not see anyone more worthy of that than you."

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: I did not say that, nor did I turn him away from Abū Bakr, except out of concern for him regarding this world and what is in leadership of danger and destruction — except for one whom Allah saves. I also feared that the people might not love a man who prayed in the station of the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was alive — ever — unless Allah willed, and they would envy him, seek to harm him, and consider him ill-omened. But the matter is Allah's matter, and the decree is His decree. Allah protected him from everything I feared for him regarding the affairs of this world and the religion.

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: On the day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, they saw some lightness in him at the beginning of the day, so the men dispersed from him to their homes and needs, rejoicing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone with the women. While we were in that state — never had we been in a state like ours of hope and joy before — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave me, for this angel seeks permission to enter upon me." So everyone in the house left except me, and his head was in my lap. He sat up, and I moved to the side of the house. He conversed privately with the angel for a long time. Then he called me, and returned his head to my lap, and said to the women: "Enter." I said: "This is not the sensation of Jibrīl (peace be upon him)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, O ʿĀʾishah, this is the Angel of Death. He came to me and said: 'Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has sent me and commanded me not to enter upon you except with your permission. If you do not permit me, I shall return; and if you permit me, I shall enter. And He commanded me not to seize you until you command me.' So what do you command?" I said: "Withhold from me until Jibrīl (peace be upon him) comes to me — for this is Jibrīl's hour."

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: We were confronted with a matter for which we had no answer, nor any opinion. We were stunned, as though we had been struck by a deafening blow, unable to respond to anything. No one in the household could speak, out of reverence for that matter and an awe that filled our hearts.

She said: Jibrīl came at his hour and greeted, and I recognized his presence. The people of the house left, and he entered. He said: "Allah (Mighty and Majestic) conveys His greeting of peace to you and says: 'How do you find yourself?' — though He knows better than you what you find — but He wishes to increase you in honor and nobility, to complete your honor and nobility over creation, and to make it a sunnah (established practice) in your community." He said: "I find myself ill." He said: "Rejoice, for Allah (Exalted is He) wishes to convey to you what He has prepared for you." He said: "O Jibrīl, the Angel of Death sought permission to enter upon me," and he told him the news. Jibrīl said: "O Muhammad, your Lord yearns for you. Did He not inform you of what He intends for you? No, by Allah — the Angel of Death has never sought permission to enter upon anyone, nor will he ever seek permission upon anyone, except that your Lord is completing your honor, and He yearns for you." He said: "Then do not leave until he comes."

He then gave permission to the women and said: "O Fāṭimah, come near." She leaned over him, and he spoke privately with her. She raised her head, her eyes weeping, unable to speak. Then he said: "Bring your head near to me." She leaned over him, and he spoke privately with her. She raised her head, laughing, unable to speak. What we saw from her was astonishing. I asked her afterward, and she said: "He told me that he would die today, so I wept. Then he said: 'I have asked Allah to join you with me as the first of my family, and to make you with me.' So I laughed." She brought her two sons near to him, and he smelled them.

She said: The Angel of Death came and sought permission, and he permitted him. The angel said: "What do you command us, O Muhammad?" He said: "Join me to my Lord now." He said: "Yes, from this very day of yours. Indeed, your Lord yearns for you. He has not delayed from anyone the way He has delayed from you, nor has He refrained from entering upon anyone except with permission — other than you. But your hour is before you." And he left.

She said: Jibrīl came and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. This is the last time I shall descend to the earth ever. The revelation has been folded up, and this world has been folded up with you. I had no need in the earth other than you, and I have no need in it other than your presence, then my remaining at my station."

She said: By Him who sent Muhammad with the truth, there was no one in the house who could utter a single word in response to that, nor could anyone send for his men, due to the magnitude of what they heard of his speech, and our grief and concern.

She said: I stood up to the Prophet (ﷺ) until I placed his head between my breasts, and I held his chest. He kept losing consciousness until it overwhelmed him, and his forehead poured with sweat — a sweat I had never seen from any human. I kept wiping away that sweat, and I never found any scent more fragrant than it. I would say to him when he regained consciousness: "May my father and mother, my soul and my family be your ransom — what your forehead pours with sweat!" He said: "O ʿĀʾishah, indeed the soul of the believer exits with sweat, and the soul of the disbeliever exits from his jaws like the breath of a donkey."

At that point we were alarmed and sent for our family. The first man to come to us — my brother, whom she had sent to her father — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died before anyone came. Allah only kept them from him because He entrusted him to Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl. When he lost consciousness, he would say: "Rather, the Most Exalted Companion!" — as though the choice were being presented to him again. When he could speak, he would say: "The prayer! The prayer! You will not cease to hold firm as long as you pray together. The prayer! The prayer!" He kept enjoining it until he died, saying: "The prayer! The prayer!"

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died between the rising of the forenoon (ḍuḥā) and midday, on Monday.

Fāṭimah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I have never suffered from a Monday — by Allah, the community will never cease to be afflicted on it with a great calamity." Umm Kulthūm said on the day ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face) was struck in Kūfah something similar: "I have never suffered from a Monday — on it the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, on it ʿAlī was killed, and on it my father was killed. I have never suffered from a Monday."

ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, the people rushed in when the cry rose high. The angels covered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his garment. The people differed — some denied his death, some were struck mute and could not speak except after a long while, others became confused and stammered without clarity, others retained their intellects, and others sat down [stunned]. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was among those who denied his death, ʿAlī was among those who sat down, and ʿUthmān was among those struck mute.

ʿUmar went out to the people and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not died. Allah (Mighty and Majestic) will surely return him, and I will cut off the hands and feet of men among the hypocrites who wish for the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah (Mighty and Majestic) only promised him as He promised Mūsā, and he will come to you." In another narration, he said: "O people, restrain your tongues regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he has not died. By Allah, I will not hear anyone mention that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has died except that I will strike him with this sword of mine."

As for ʿAlī, he sat down and would not leave the house. As for ʿUthmān, he would not speak to anyone — he would be taken by the hand and led about.

No one among the Muslims was in the state of Abū Bakr and al-ʿAbbās, for Allah (Mighty and Majestic) supported them with success (tawfīq) and rightness (sadād). Though the people did not desist except by the words of Abū Bakr — until al-ʿAbbās came and said: "By Allah, there is no god but He — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has indeed tasted death. And he said while he was among you: {«إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَيِّتُونَ»} (Verily, you will die and verily they will die.) [al-Zumar 39:30]"

The news reached Abū Bakr while he was among Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. He came and entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), looked at him, then leaned over him and kissed him. Then he said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah. Allah (Exalted is He) would not make you taste death twice. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has indeed passed away." Then he went out to the people and said: "O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad — then Muhammad has died. And whoever worshipped the Lord of Muhammad — then He is Living and does not die." Allah (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ»} (Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; many were the Messengers that passed away before him. If he died or was killed, would you then turn back on your heels?) [Āl ʿImrān 3:144]

It was as though the people had never heard this verse until that day. In another narration: When the news reached Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), he entered the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was praying over the Prophet (ﷺ), his eyes overflowing and his sobs rising like the gurgling of a jar — yet all the while he was firm in action and speech. He leaned over him, uncovered his face, kissed his forehead and cheeks, wiped his face, and kept weeping, saying: "May my father and mother, my soul and my family be your ransom. You were pure in life and in death. By your death, what has been cut off has not been cut off by the death of any of the prophets — prophethood. It is too great for description, too majestic for weeping. You were singled out until you became a consolation, and you were universal until we became equal in you. Had your death not been your own choice, we would have offered our souls for grief over you. Had you not forbidden weeping, we would have poured out the water of our eyes upon you. As for what we cannot repel from ourselves — it is a grief and a remembrance that are constant companions, never departing. O Allah, convey from us to him. Remember us, O Muhammad, may Allah bless you, before your Lord, and let us be on your mind. Were it not for the tranquility you left behind, no one could have stood before the desolation you left. O Allah, convey to Your Prophet from us, and preserve him among us."

Ibn ʿUmar narrated: When Abū Bakr entered the house, prayed, and praised [Allah], the people of the household raised a wailing that was heard by the people of the prayer area. Every time he mentioned something, they increased [their wailing]. Their wailing did not cease until a man at the door — loud-voiced and firm — greeted: "Peace be upon you, O people of the household. {«كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ»} (Every soul shall taste death.) [Āl ʿImrān 3:185] Indeed, in Allah there is a replacement for everyone, a fulfillment for every desire, and a deliverance from every fear. So place your hope in Allah (Exalted is He), and in Him put your trust."

They listened to him but did not recognize him, and they ceased weeping. When the weeping ceased, his voice was gone. One of them looked out and saw no one. Then they returned to weeping, and another caller whose voice they did not recognize called out: "O people of the household, remember Allah (Exalted is He) and praise Him in every state, and you will be among the sincere. Indeed, in Allah there is consolation from every calamity and compensation for every desire. So obey Allah and act by His command."

Abū Bakr said: "This is al-Khiḍr and al-Yasaʿ (peace be upon them) — they attended the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn ʿAmr completed the account of Abū Bakr's sermon (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: Abū Bakr stood before the people as a speaker, after the people had finished their tears, with a sermon whose greater part was prayer upon the Prophet (ﷺ). He praised Allah and extolled Him in every state, and said:

"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, who fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and alone defeated the confederates. To Allah belongs all praise, alone. I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the Seal of His Prophets. I bear witness that the Book is as He legislated, that the religion is as He legislated, that the hadith is as he narrated, that the statement is as he said, and that Allah is the Clear Truth. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your Messenger, Your Prophet, Your Beloved, Your Trusted One, Your Chosen One, and Your Pure One — with the best blessings You have sent upon any of Your creation. O Allah, place Your blessings, Your pardon, and Your mercy upon the Master of the Messengers, the Seal of the Prophets, the Imam of the God-fearing — Muhammad, the leader of good, the imam of good, the Messenger of Mercy. O Allah, bring near his rank, magnify his proof, honor his station, and raise him to a Praiseworthy Station (maqām maḥmūd) that the first and the last will envy. Benefit us with his Praiseworthy Station on the Day of Resurrection, and be his successor among us in this world and the Hereafter. Convey him to the highest degree and the means (al-wasīlah) in Paradise. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings and blessings upon Ibrāhīm — indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad — then Muhammad has died. And whoever worshipped Allah — then Allah is Living and has not died. Allah has indeed brought you forward in His matter, so do not call upon Him in panic. For Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has chosen for His Prophet (ﷺ) what is with Him over what is with you, and has taken him to His reward. He has left among you His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ). Whoever holds fast to both will know [the truth], and whoever separates between them will deny [it]. {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ»} (O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice...) [al-Māʾidah 5:8] Let not Satan distract you with the death of your Prophet, nor tempt you away from your religion. Combat Satan with good and you will overcome him. Do not wait for him, for he will overtake you and tempt you."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: When Abū Bakr finished his sermon, he said: "O ʿUmar, you are the one who, I have been told, said that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) has not died

chapters.title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him)
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||||| وفاة أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

لما احتضر أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه جاءت عائشة رضي الله عنها فتمثلت
بهذا البيت لعمرك ما يغنى الثراء عن الفتى ... إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها
الصدر
فكشف عن وجهه وقال ليس كذا ولكن قولي {وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت
منه تحيد} انظروا ثوبي هذين فاغسلوهما وكفنوني فيهما فإن الحي إلى الجديد
أحوج من الميت
وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها عند موته
وأبيض يستسقى الغمام بوجهه ... ربيع اليتامى عصمة للأرامل
فقال أبو بكر ذاك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ودخلوا  عليه فقالوا ألا
ندعوا لك طبيبا ينظر إليك قال قد نظر إلى طبيبي وقال إني فعال لما أريد
ودخل عليه سلمان الفارسي رضي الله تعالى عنه يعوده فقال يا أبا بكر أوصنا
فقال إن الله فاتح عليكم الدنيا فلا تأخذن منها إلا بلاغك واعلم أن من صلى
صلاة الصبح فهو في ذمة الله فلا تخفرن الله في ذمته فيكبك في النار على
وجهك
ولما ثقل أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه وأراد الناس منه أن يستخلف فاستخلف
عمر رضي الله عنه فقال الناس له استخلفت علينا فظا غليظا فماذا تقول لربك
فقال أقول استخلفت على خلقك خير خلقك
ثم أرسل إلى عمر رضي الله عنه فجاء فقال إني موصيك بوصية اعلم إن لله حقا
في النهار لا يقبله في الليل وأن لله حقا في الليل لا يقبله في النهار وأنه
لا يقبل النافلة حتى تؤدى الفريضة وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم
القيامة باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا
الحق أن يثقل وإنما خفت موازين من خفت موزاينهم يوم القيامة باتباع الباطل
وخفته عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلاالباطل أن يخف وإن الله ذكر أهل
الجنة بأحسن أعمالهم وتجاوز عن سيئاتهم فيقول القائل أنا دون هؤلاء ولا
أبلغ مبلغ صالح الذي عملوا فيقول القائل أنا أفضل من هؤلاء وإن الله ذكر
آية الرحمة وآية العذاب ليكون المؤمن راغبا راهبا ولا يلقى بيديه إلى
التهلكة ولا يتمنى على الله غير الحق
فإن حفظت وصيتي هذه فلا يكون غائب أحب إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه وإن
ضيعت وصيتي فلا يكون غائب أبغض إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه ولست بمعجزه
وقال سعيد بن المسيب لما احتضر أبو بكر رضي الله عنه أتاه ناس من الصحابة
فقالوا يا خليفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زودنا فإنا نراك لما بك
فقالوا أبو بكر من قال هؤلاء الكلمات ثم مات جعل الله روحه  في الأفق
المبين قالوا وما الأفق المبين قال قاع بين يديالعرش فيه رياض الله وأنهار
وأشجار يغشاه كل يوم مائة PageV04P476
رحمة فمن قال هذا القول جعل الله روحه في هذا المكان اللهم إنك ابتدأت
الخلق من غير حاجة بك إليهم ثم جعلتهم فريقين فريقا للنعيم وفريقا للسعير
فاجعلني للنعيم ولا تجعلني للسعير اللهم إنك خلقت الخلق فرقا وميزتهم قبل
أن تخلقهم فجعلت منهم شقيا وسعيدا وغويا ورشيدا فلا تشقني بمعاصيك
اللهم إنك علمت ما تكسب كل نفس قبل أن تخلقها فلا محيص لها مما علمت
فاجعلني ممن تستعمله بطاعتك اللهم إن أحدا لا يشاء حتى تشاء فاجعل مشيئتك
أن أشاء ما يقربني إليك
اللهم إنك قد قدرت حركات العباد فلا يتحرك شيء إلا بإذنك فاجعل حركاتي في
تقواك اللهم إنك خلقت الخير والشر وجعلت لكل واحد منهما عاملا يعمل به
فاجعلني من خير القسمين اللهم إنك خلقت الجنة والنار وجعلت لكل واحدة منهما
أهلا فاجعلني من سكان جنتك
اللهم إنك أردت بقوم الضلال وضيقت به صدورهم فاشرح صدري للإيمان وزينه في
قلبي اللهم إنك دبرت الأمور وجعلت مصيرها إليك فأحيني بعد الموت حياة طيبة
وقربني إليك زلفى اللهم من أصبح وأمسى ثقته ورجاؤه غيرك فأنت ثقتي ورجائي
ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله قال أبو بكر هذا كله في كتاب الله عز وجل

### ||||| وفاة عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, attendance; the state of being before someone or something; also the onset of death (ḥuḍūr al-mawt).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The moment of death as the "presence" of the final reality before the servant—an unveiling of what was previously unseen.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical attendance; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's confrontation with the angel of death.
- Root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Commandment, bequest, exhortation; to enjoin something upon someone with emphasis.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The covenantal charge (waṣiyyah) that binds the believer to Allah's rights (ḥuqūq) in this life and the next.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a last will; metaphorical for the prophetic legacy of counsel transmitted to the community.
- Root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Heaviness, weight; the burden of a thing upon a scale.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The weighing of deeds (mīzān) on the Day of Judgment—the metaphysical balance where truth (ḥaqq) alone carries weight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical weight; metaphorical for moral and spiritual gravity in the divine reckoning.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna (الشّرط مع إنّ) — The repeated use of "inna" (إنّ) in Abu Bakr's supplications establishes a causal nexus between divine decree (qadar) and human action, parsed as nominal sentences (jumal ismiyyah) that assert permanent, unalterable truths.
chapters.translation:
I say: When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not a youth... when the chest constricts upon him one day at the final gasp." He uncovered his face and said: "Not so—but say: {«And the stupor of death comes with the truth: that is what you were fleeing from»} (Q. 50:19). Look at these two garments of mine—wash them and shroud me in them, for the living has greater need of new clothes than the dead."

And ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said at his death: "A white-faced man by whose countenance rain is sought... a spring for orphans, a refuge for widows." Abu Bakr said: "That is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)." Then they entered upon him and said: "Shall we not call a physician to examine you?" He said: "My Physician has already examined me, and He said: 'I do whatsoever I will.'"

Salman al-Fārisī (may Allah be pleased with him) entered to visit him and said: "O Abu Bakr, give us a counsel (waṣiyyah)." He said: "Verily Allah will open the world upon you—so take from it only what suffices you (balāgh). And know that whoever prays the dawn prayer is under the protection (dhimmah) of Allah—so do not violate Allah's covenant in His protection, lest He cast you into the Fire on your face."

When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) grew heavy [with illness] and the people desired him to appoint a successor, he appointed ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him). The people said to him: "You have appointed over us one harsh and stern—what will you say to your Lord?" He said: "I will say: I appointed over Your creation the best of Your creation."

Then he sent for ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), and he came. He said: "I enjoin upon you a counsel (waṣiyyah). Know that Allah has a right in the day that He does not accept in the night, and a right in the night that He does not accept in the day, and that the supererogatory (nāfilah) is not accepted until the obligatory (farīḍah) is performed. And the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are only made heavy by their following the truth in this world and its weight upon them—and it is fitting that a scale in which nothing but truth is placed should be heavy. And the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection are only made light by their following falsehood and its lightness upon them—and it is fitting that a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed should be light. Verily Allah mentioned the people of Paradise by their best deeds and overlooked their evil deeds, so one says: 'I am lesser than these—I will not reach the station of the righteous in what they did.' And another says: 'I am better than these.' And verily Allah mentioned the verse of mercy and the verse of chastisement, so that the believer might be both desirous (rāghib) and fearful (rāhib), neither casting himself into destruction with his own hands, nor wishing upon Allah other than the truth. If you preserve this counsel of mine, then no absent thing will be more beloved to you than death—and it is inevitable for you. But if you squander this counsel of mine, then no absent thing will be more hateful to you than death—and it is inevitable for you, and you will not escape it."

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, a group of the Companions came to him and said: "O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, provide us with provisions (zawwidnā), for we see that you are about to depart." They said: "O Abu Bakr, whoever utters these words and then dies, Allah will place his soul in the clear horizon (al-ufuq al-mubīn)." They said: "And what is the clear horizon?" He said: "A hollow before the Throne (al-ʿArsh) containing the gardens of Allah, rivers, and trees, over which a hundred mercies pass every day. Whoever utters this saying, Allah will place his soul in this place. O Allah, You began creation without any need of them, then You made them two groups—a group for bliss and a group for the blaze—so make me of the bliss and not of the blaze. O Allah, You created the creatures as factions and distinguished them before creating them, making among them the wretched and the blessed, the misguided and the rightly-guided—so do not make me wretched through Your disobedience. O Allah, You knew what every soul earns before creating it, and there is no escape for it from what You knew—so make me among those whom You employ in Your obedience. O Allah, no one wills until You will—so make Your will be that I will what draws me near to You. O Allah, You have decreed the movements of the servants, and nothing moves except by Your permission—so make my movements in Your piety. O Allah, You created good and evil, and appointed for each of them a worker who works by it—so make me of the better of the two portions. O Allah, You created Paradise and the Fire, and appointed for each of them its people—so make me among the inhabitants of Your Paradise. O Allah, You willed for some people misguidance and constricted their breasts thereby—so expand my breast for faith and adorn it in my heart. O Allah, You have disposed all affairs and made their end return to You—so give me after death a goodly life and bring me near to You in proximity (zulfā). O Allah, whoever wakes and sleeps with his trust and hope in other than You—You are my trust and my hope, and there is no might and no power except in Allah." Abu Bakr said: "All of this is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

### ||||| The Death of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him)

chapters.title_en: The Assassination of ʿUmar and His Final Testament
chapters.arabic_text:
قال عم بن ميمون كنت قائما غداة أصيب عمر ما بيني وبينه إلا عبد الله بن
عباس وكان إذا مر بين الصفين قام بينهما فإذا رأى خللا قال استووا حتى إذا
لم ير فيهم خللا لا تقدم فكبر قال وربما قرأ سورة يوسف أو النحل أو نحو ذلك
في الركعة الأولى حتى يجتمع الناس فما هو إلا أن أكبر فسمعته يقول قتلني أو
أكلني الكلب حين طعنه أبو لؤلؤة وطار العلج بسكين ذات طرفين لا يمر على أحد
يمينا أو شمالا إلا طعنه حتى طعن ثلاثة عشر رجلا فمات  منهم تسعة وفي رواية
سبعة
فلما رأى ذلك رجل من المسلمين طرح عليه برنسا فلما ظن العلج أنه مأخوذ
نحر نفسه
وتناول عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه عبد الرحمن بن عوف فقدمه فأما من كان يلي
عمر فقد رأى ما رأيت وأما نواحي المسجد ما يدرون ما الأمر غير أنهم فقدوا
صوت عمر وهم يقولون سبحان الله سبحان الله فصلى بهم عبد الرحمن صلاة خفيفة
فلما انصرفوا قال يا ابن العباس انظر من قتلني قال فغاب ساعة ثم جاء فقال
غلام المغيرة بن شعبة فقال عمر رضي الله عنه قاتله الله لقد كنت أمرت به
معروفا
ثم قال الحمد لله الذي لم يجعل منيتي بيد رجل مسلم قد كنت أنت وأبوك
تحبان أن يكثر العلوج بالمدينة وكان العباس أكثرهم رقيقا فقال ابن عباس إن
شئت فعلت أي إن شئت قتلناهم قال بعدما تكلموا بلسانكم وصلوا إلى قبلتكم
وحجوا حجكم فاحتمل إلى بيته فانطلقنا معه قال وكأن الناس لم تصبهم مصيبة
قبل يومئذ قال فقائل يقول أخاف عليه وقائل يقول لا بأس
فأتى بنبيذ فشرب منه فخرج من جوفه ثم أتى بلبن فشرب منه فخرج من جوفه
فعرفوا أنه ميت
قال فدخلنا عليه وجاء الناس يثنون عليه وجاء رجل شاب فقال أبشر يا أمير
المؤمنين ببشرى من الله عز وجل قد كان لك صحبة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه
