chapters.arabic_text:
فاستعد يا مسكين لهذا اليوم العظيم شأنه المديد زمانه القاهر سلطانه
القريب أوانه يوم ترى السماء فيه قد انفطرت والكواكب من هوله قد انتثرت
والنجوم الزواهر قد انكدرت والشمس قد كورت والجبال قد PageV04P515
سيرت والعشار قد عطلت والوحوش قد حشرت والبحار قد سجرت والنفوس إلى
الأبدان قد زوجت والجحيم قد سعرت والجنة قد أزلفت والجبال قد نسفت والأرض
قد مدت يوم ترى الأرض قد زلزلت فيه زالزالها وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها يومئذ
يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة
فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة وانشقت السماء فهى يومئذ واهية والملك على أرجائها
ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية يوم
تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت
هباء منبثا يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش
يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى
وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات
وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا
ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم
تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان
يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى
والأقدام يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن
بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت
يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره سيد المرسلين إذ قال له
الصديق رضي الله عنه أراك قد شبت يا رسول الله قال شيبتنى هود وأخواتها (1)
وهى الواقعة والمرسلات وعم يتساءلون وإذا الشمس كورت فيا أيها القارىء
العاجز إنما حظك من قراءتك أن تمجمج القرآن وتحرك به اللسان ولو كنت  متفكرا
فيما تقرؤه لكنت جديرا بأن تنشق مرارتك مما شاب منه شعر سيد المرسلين وإذا
قنعت بحركة اللسان فقد حرمت ثمرة القرآن فالقيامة أحد ما ذكر فيه وقد وصف
الله بعض دواهيها وأكثر من أساميها لنقف بكثرة أساميها على كثرة معانيها
فليس المقصود بكثرة الأسامي تكرير الأسامي والألقاب بل الغرض تنبيه أولي
الألباب فتحت كل اسم من أسماء القيامة سر وفي كل نعت من نعوتها معنى فاحرص
على معرفة معانيها
ونحن الآن نجمع لك أساميها وهى يوم القيامة ويوم الحسرة ويوم الندامة
ويوم المحاسبة ويوم المساءلة ويوم المسابقة ويوم المناقشة ويوم المنافسة
ويوم الزلزلة ويوم الدمدمة ويوم الصاعقة ويوم الواقعة ويوم القارعة ويوم
الراجفة ويوم الرادفة ويوم الغاشية ويوم الداهية ويوم الآزفة ويوم الحاقة
ويوم الطامة ويوم الصاخة ويوم التلاق ويوم الفراق ويوم المساق ويوم القصاص
ويوم التناد ويوم الحساب ويوم المآب ويوم العذاب ويوم الفرار ويوم القرار
ويوم اللقاء ويوم البقاء ويوم القضاء ويوم الجزاء ويوم البلاء ويوم البكاء
ويوم الحشر ويوم الوعيد ويوم العرض ويوم الوزن ويوم الحق ويوم الحكم ويوم
الفصل ويوم الجمع ويوم البعث ويوم الفتح ويوم الخزى ويوم عظيم ويوم عقيم
ويوم عسير ويوم الدين ويوم اليقين ويوم النشور ويوم المصير ويوم النفخة
ويوم الصيحة ويوم الرجفة ويوم الرجة ويوم الزجرة ويوم السكرة ويوم الفزع
ويوم المنتهى ويوم الجزع ويوم المأوى ويوم الميقات ويوم الميعاذ ويوم
المرصاد ويوم القلق ويوم العرق ويوم الافتقار ويوم الانكار ويوم الانتشار
ويوم الانشقاق ويوم الوقوف ويوم الخروج ويوم الخلود ويوم التغابن ويوم عبوس
ويوم معلوم ويوم الساعة ويوم مشهود ويوم لا ريب فيه ويوم تبلى فيه السرائر
ويوم لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ويوم تشخص فيه الأبصار ويوم PageV04P516
لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى
نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار
ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه  وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا
ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم
على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم
ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار
يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار
يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات
وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير
فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت
النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح
الإنسان
فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلقت الأبواب وأرخيت الستور
واستترت عن الخلائق فقارفت الفجور فماذا تفعل وقد شهدت عليك جوارحك فالويل
كل الويل لنا معشر الغافلين يرسل الله لنا سيد المرسلين وينزل عليه الكتاب
المبين ويخبرنا بهذه الصفات من نعوت يوم الدين ثم يعرفنا غفلتنا ويقول
اقترب الناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا
استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ثم يعرفنا قرب القيامة فيقول اقتربت
الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة
تكون قريبا ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر
معانيه ولا ننظر في كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من
دواهيه
فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Inability, weakness, incapacity to accomplish a task; the state of falling short of a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Human impotence before divine power (qudrah); the creature's inherent limitation in grasping the metaphysical realities of the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense denotes physical incapacity; here used metaphorically (majāz) for the intellectual and spiritual failure to contemplate the Quran's meanings.
- Root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neglect, heedlessness, absence of awareness from the heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic state of those who turn away from divine reminders; the opposite of dhikr (remembrance) and tadabbur (reflection).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: inattention; metaphorical: the heart's veiling from the reality of the Hour despite its proximity.
- Root: د-ه-ي (d-h-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calamity, affliction, overwhelming disaster that strikes suddenly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The terrors (dawāhī) of the Day of Judgment as described in revelation; events that confound human comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a sudden misfortune; metaphorical: the cosmic cataclysms of the Hour that defy ordinary causal explanation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension) and Istiṭrād (Digression) — The passage employs extended anaphoric repetition of "yawma" (the day) as a suspended accusative of time (ẓarf), building a cumulative rhetorical crescendo before the main clause resolves, mirroring the Quranic style of apocalyptic enumeration.
chapters.translation:
So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time has drawn near — a Day wherein you shall see the heaven split asunder, the stars scattered in terror, the shining celestial bodies extinguished, the sun wrapped in darkness, the mountains set in motion, the pregnant camels neglected, the wild beasts gathered together, the seas set ablaze, the souls reunited with their bodies, the Hellfire kindled, the Garden brought near, the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out flat. A Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its convulsion, and the earth casts forth its burdens, and mankind proceeds in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. A Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing, then the Imminent Event befalls, the heaven splits open and becomes frail, with the angels at its edges, and eight bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours remains hidden. A Day when the mountains pass away and you see the earth laid bare; a Day when the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumble into scattered dust. A Day when mankind becomes like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool. A Day when every nursing mother forgets what she nursed, and every pregnant female casts her burden, and you see people intoxicated though they are not intoxicated — but the punishment of God is severe. A Day when the earth is changed to a different earth, and the heavens likewise, and they appear before God, the One, the Subduer. A Day when the mountains are blown away utterly, leaving a level plain — you see in it no crookedness nor curve. A Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass like the passing of clouds. A Day when the heaven splits open and becomes rose-red like molten oil. On that Day, no human or jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient is prevented from speech, and no question is asked about their bodies, but they are seized by their forelocks and their feet. A Day when every soul finds what it did of good brought forth, and what it did of evil — wishing that between it and that evil there were a vast distance. A Day when every soul knows what it has presented, and bears witness to what it sent ahead and what it left behind. A Day when tongues fall silent and the bodily members speak. A Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white — when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have aged, O Messenger of God." He replied: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have aged me" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.

O helpless reader! Your only share of your recitation is to mumble the Quran and move your tongue with it. Had you but reflected upon what you recite, your gall bladder would be fit to burst from what turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white. And if you are content with mere tongue movement, then you have been deprived of the fruit of the Quran. For the Resurrection is one of the things mentioned therein, and God has described some of its calamities and multiplied its names — so that by the multiplicity of its names we might grasp the multiplicity of its meanings. The purpose of the many names is not mere repetition of titles and epithets; rather, the aim is to awaken those of understanding. Beneath every name of the Resurrection lies a secret, and in every attribute of it resides a meaning. So strive earnestly to know their meanings.

And now we shall gather for you its names: the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Regret, the Day of Remorse, the Day of Reckoning, the Day of Questioning, the Day of Racing, the Day of Scrutiny, the Day of Emulation, the Day of Convulsion, the Day of Destruction, the Day of the Thunderbolt, the Day of the Imminent Event, the Day of the Clatterer, the Day of the Trembling, the Day of the Following Blast, the Day of the Overwhelming, the Day of the Calamity, the Day of the Approaching, the Day of the Reality, the Day of the Overwhelming Disaster, the Day of the Deafening Cry, the Day of Encounter, the Day of Separation, the Day of Driving, the Day of Retribution, the Day of Mutual Calling, the Day of Account, the Day of Return, the Day of Punishment, the Day of Flight, the Day of Settlement, the Day of Meeting, the Day of Permanence, the Day of Decree, the Day of Recompense, the Day of Trial, the Day of Weeping, the Day of Gathering, the Day of Threat, the Day of Presentation, the Day of Weighing, the Day of Truth, the Day of Judgment, the Day of Decision, the Day of Assembly, the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Opening, the Day of Disgrace, the Day of Greatness, the Day of Barrenness, the Day of Hardship, the Day of Religion, the Day of Certainty, the Day of Rising, the Day of Destination, the Day of the Blast, the Day of the Cry, the Day of the Quake, the Day of the Shake, the Day of the Rebuke, the Day of Intoxication, the Day of Terror, the Day of the Final End, the Day of Anguish, the Day of Refuge, the Day of the Appointed Time, the Day of the Promise, the Day of the Ambush, the Day of Anxiety, the Day of Sweat, the Day of Destitution, the Day of Denial, the Day of Scattering, the Day of Splitting, the Day of Standing, the Day of Emergence, the Day of Eternity, the Day of Mutual Loss, the Day of Frowning, the Day Known, the Day of the Hour, the Day Witnessed, the Day of No Doubt, the Day when secrets are tested, the Day when no soul avails another soul in anything, the Day when eyes are fixed in stare, the Day when no protector avails his protegée in anything, the Day when no soul possesses anything for another soul, the Day when they are summoned to the Fire of Hell with a summons, the Day when they are dragged in the Fire upon their faces, the Day when their faces are turned about in the Fire, the Day when no parent recompenses his child, the Day when a man flees from his brother, his mother, and his father, the Day when they do not speak nor are they permitted to offer excuses, the Day from which there is no reprieve from God, the Day when they are exposed, the Day when they are tried at the Fire, the Day when neither wealth nor children avail, the Day when the excuses of the wrongdoers do not profit them — for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode.

A Day when excuses are returned, secrets are tested, inner thoughts become manifest, and veils are lifted. A Day when eyes are humbled, voices fall silent, glances cease to wander, hidden things emerge, and sins become apparent. A Day when the servants are driven forth accompanied by witnesses, the young grow old, and the old become intoxicated. On that Day the scales are set up, the scrolls are unrolled, Hell is brought forth, the scalding water boils, the Fire bellows, the disbelievers despair, the flames are kindled, colors change, the tongue falls mute, and the limbs of man speak.

So O man! What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord, when you closed the doors, drew down the curtains, and concealed yourself from creation while committing lewd acts? What will you do when your own limbs bear witness against you? Woe, all woe, to us — the company of the heedless! God sent to us the Master of the Messengers, revealed to him the Clear Book, informed us of these descriptions of the Day of Religion, then acquainted us with our heedlessness, saying: {«اقترب الناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم»} (The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they turn away in heedlessness. No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while they play — their hearts distracted). Then He informs us of the nearness of the Hour, saying: {«اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا»} (The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. They see it as distant, but We see it as near. And what makes you know — perhaps the Hour is near). Then the best of our states would be to take the study of this Quran as mere occupation, without pondering its meanings, without examining the multitude of descriptions and names of this Day, and without preparing to escape its calamities.

So we seek refuge in God from this heedlessness — unless God overtakes us with His vast mercy.

chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| صفة المساءلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-’a-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, demand, or inquire; the act of seeking an answer or account. In the context of the afterlife, it denotes the formal interrogation of the soul.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, it refers to the divine questioning (mas’alah) on the Day of Judgment—an inquest into deeds, intentions, and knowledge, distinct from mere informational inquiry.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is a direct request for something; metaphorical (majāz) usage here signifies the eschatological reckoning where the soul is confronted with its acts, as in {«لَتُسْأَلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ»} (Q. 16:93).
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with definite subject (al-mubtada’ wa al-khabar) — “al-mas’alah” is the subject, and “ṣifat” is the predicate, indicating a definitional description, not a narrative event.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the description of the questioning (ṣifat al-mas’alah) is that which the hearts of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn) have pondered, and the tongues of the speakers have differed concerning its reality. For some have affirmed it as a literal event, and others have interpreted it as an unveiling of the inward state. Yet the truth, in my view, is that the questioning is a necessary consequence of the divine wisdom, by which the servant is made to stand before his Lord—not as one ignorant of what he has done, but as one who is caused to witness the record of his deeds, so that the proof is established against him, and the excuse is cut off. For the questioning is not for the sake of information, since God, exalted is He, knows all things; rather, it is for the manifestation of the servant’s own state, and the sealing of his tongue against denial, and the confirmation of the testimony of his limbs. Thus, the description of the questioning is the description of a station (maqām) of unveiling, not of a need for inquiry. And this is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: {«فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الْمُرْسَلِينَ»} (Q. 7:6) — a questioning that is a manifestation of justice, not a seeking of knowledge.

chapters.title_en: The Questioning, the Terror of the Standing, and the Exposure of Deeds Before the Omnipotent
chapters.arabic_text:
ثم تفكر يا مسكين بعد هذه الأحوال فيما يتوجه عليك من السؤال شفاها من
غير ترجمان فتسئل عن القليل والكثير والنقير والقطمير فبينا أنت في كرب
القيامة وعرقها وشدة عظائمها إذ نزلت ملائكة من رجاء السماء بأجسام عظام
وأشخاص ضخام غلاظ شداد أمروا أن يأخذوا بنواصى المجرمين إلى موقف العرض على
الجبار قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله عز وجل ملكا ما بين شفرى
عينيه مسيرة مائة عام (1) فما ظنك بنفسك إذا شاهدت مثلا هؤلاء الملائكة
أرسلوا إليك ليأخذوك إلى مقام العرض وتراهم على عظم أشخاصهم منكسرين لشدة
اليوم مستشعرين مما بدا من غضب الجبار على عباده وعند نزولهم لا يبقى نبى
ولا صديق ولا صالح إلا ويخرون لأذقانهم خوفا من أن يكونوا هم المأخوذين
فهذا حال المقربين فما ظنك بالعصاة المجرمين وعند ذلك يبادر اقوام من شدة
الفزع فيقولون للملائكة أفيكم ربنا وذلك لعظم موكبهم وشدة هيبتهم فتفزع
الملائكة من سؤالهم إجلالا لخالقهم عن أن يكون فيهم فنادوا بأصواتهم منزهين
لمليكهم عما توهمه أهل الأرض وقالوا سبحان ربنا ما هو فينا ولكنه آت من بعد
وعند ذلك تقوم الملائكة صفا محدقين بالخلائق من الجوانب وعلى جميعهم شعار
الذل والخضوع وهيئة الخوف والمهابة لشدة اليوم
وعند ذلك يصدق الله تعالى قوله {فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن
المرسلين فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين} وقوله {فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين
عما كانوا يعملون} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء {يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول}
PageV04P517
{ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب} فيا لشدة يوم تذهل
فيه عقول الأنبياء وتنمحى علومهم من شدة الهيبة إذ يقال لهم ما أجبتم وقد
أرسلتم إلى الخلائق وكانوا قد علموا فتدهش عقولهم فلا يدرون بماذا يجيبون
فيقولون من شدة الهيبة لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب
وهم فى ذلك الوقت صادقون إذ طارت منهم العقول وانمحت العلوم إلى أن
يقويهم الله تعالى فيدعى نوح عليه السلام فيقال له هل بلغت فيقول نعم فيقال
لأمته هل بلغكم فيقولون ما أتانا من نذير
ويؤتى بعيسى عليه السلام فيقول الله تعالى له {أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني
وأمي إلهين من دون الله} فيبقى متشحطا تحت هيبة هذا السؤال سنين فيالعظم
يوم تقام فيه السياسة على الأنبياء بمثل هذا السؤال ثم تقبل الملائكة
فينادون واحدا واحدا يا فلان بن فلانة هلم إلى موقف العرض وعند ذلك ترتعد
الفرائص وتضطرب الجوارح وتبهت العقول ويتمنى أقوام أن يذهب بهم إلى النار
ولا تعرض قبائح أعمالهم على الجبار ولا يكشف سترهم  على ملأ الخلائق
وقبل الابتداء بالسؤال يظهر نور العرش {وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها} وايقن كل
عبد بإقبال الجبار لمساءلة العباد وظن كل واحد أنه ما يراه أحد سواه وأنه
المأخوذ بالأخذ والسؤال دون من عداه فيقول الجبار سبحانه وتعالى عند ذلك يا
جبريل ائتى بالنار فيجىء لها جبريل ويقول يا جهنم أجيبي خالقك ومليكك
فيصادفها جبريل على غيظها وغضبها فلم يلبث بعد ندائها أن ثارت وفارت وزفرت
إلى الخلائق وشهقت وسمع الخلائق تغيظها وزفيرها وانتهضت خزنتها متوثبة إلى
الخلائق غضبا على من عصى الله تعالى وخالف أمره فأخطر ببالك وأحضر فى قلبك
حالة قلوب العباد وقد امتلأت فزعا ورعبا فتساقطوا جثيا على الركب وولوا
مدبرين يوم ترى كل أمة جاثية وسقط بعضهم على الوجوه منكبين وينادى العصاة
والظالمون بالويل والثبور وينادى الصديقون نفسى نفسى فبينما هم كذلك إذ
زفرت الناس زفرتها الثانية فتضاعف خوفهم وتخاذلت قواهم وظنوا أنهم مأخوذون
ثم زفرت الثالثة فتساقط الخلائق على وجوههم وشخصوا بأبصارهم ينظرون من طرف
خفى خاشع وانهضمت عند ذلك قلوب الظالمين فبلغت الحناجر كاظمين وذهلت العقول
من السعداء والأشقياء أجمعين
وبعد ذلك اقبل الله تعالى على الرسل وقال ماذا أجبتم فإذا رأوا ما قد
أقيم من السياسة على الأنبياء اشتد الفزع على العصاة ففر الوالد من ولده
والأخ من أخيه والزوج من زوجته وبقى كل واحد منتظرا لأمره ثم يؤخذ واحد
واحد فيسأله الله تعالى شفاها عن قليل عمله وكثيره وعن سره وعلانيته وعن
جميع جوارحه وأعضائه قال أبو هريرة قالوا يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم
القيامة فقال هل تضارون فى رؤية الشمس فى الظهيرة ليس دونها سحاب قالوا لا
قال فهل تضارون فى رؤية القمر ليلة البدر ليس دونه سحاب قالوا لا قال
فوالذي نفسي بيده لا تضارون فى رؤية ربكم فيلقى العبد فيقول له ألم أكرمك
وأسودك وأزوجك وأسخر لك الخيل والإبل وأذرك ترأس وتربع فيقول العبد بلى
فيقول أظننت أنك ملاقى فيقول لا فيقول فأنا أنساك كما نسيتنى  (1) فتوهم
نفسك يا مسكين وقد أخذت الملائكة بعضديك وأنت واقف بين يدي الله تعالى
يسألك شفاها فيقول لك ألم أنعم عليك بالشباب ففيماذا أبليته ألم أمهل لك فى
العمر ففيماذا أفنيته الم أرزقك المال فمن أين اكتسبته وفيماذا أنفقته ألم
أكرمك بالعلم فماذا عملت فيما علمت فكيف ترى حياءك وخجلتك وهو يعد عليك
إنعامه ومعاصيك وأياديه ومساويك فإن أنكرت شهدت عليك جوارحك قال أنس رضي
الله عنه كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم PageV04P518
فضحك ثم قال أتدرون مم أضحك قلنا الله ورسوله أعلم قال من مخاطبة العبد
ربه يقول يا رب الم تجرنى من الظلم قال يقول بلى قال فيقول فإنى لا أجيز
على نفسى إلا شاهدا منى فيقول كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا وبالكرام
الكاتبين شهودا قال فيختم على فيه ويقال لأركانه انطقى قال فتنطق بأعماله
ثم يخلى بينه وبين الكلام فيقول لأعضائه بعدا لكن وسحقا فعنكن كنت أناضل
(1) فنعوذ بالله من الافتضاح على ملأ الخلق بشهادة الأعضاء إلا أن الله
تعالى وعد المؤمن بأن يستر عليه ولا يطلع عليه غيره
سأل ابن عمر رجل فقال له كيف سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول فى
النجوى فقال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدنو أحدكم من ربه حتى يضع
كنفه عليه فيقول عملت كذا وكذا فيقول نعم فيقول عملت كذا وكذا فيقول نعم ثم
يقول إنى سترتها عليك فى الدنيا وإنى أغفرها لك اليوم (2) وقد قال رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من ستر على مؤمن عورته ستر الله عورته يوم القيامة
(3) فهذا إنما يرجى لعبد مؤمن ستر على الناس عيوبهم واحتمل فى حق نفسه
تقصيرهم ولم يحرك لسانه بذكر مساويهم ولم يذكرهم فى غيبتهم بما يكرهون لو
سمعوه فهذا جدير بأن يجازى بمثله فى القيامة وهب أنه قد ستره عن غيرك أليس
قد قرع سمعك النداء إلى العرض فيكفيك تلك الروعة جزاء عن ذنوبك إذ يؤخذ
بناصيتك فتقاد وفؤادك مضطرب ولبك طائر وفرائصك  مرتعدة وجوارحك مضطربة ولونك
متغير والعالم عليك من شدة الهول مظلم فقدر نفسك وأنت بهذه الصفة تتخطى
الرقاب وتخرق الصفوف وتقاد كما تقاد الفرس المجنوب وقد رفع الخلائق إليك
أبصارهم فتوهم نفسك أنك فى أيدى الموكلين بك على هذه الصفة حتى انتهى بك
إلى عرش الرحمن فرموك من أيديهم وناداك الله سبحانه وتعالى بعظيم كلامه يا
ابن آدم ادن منى فدنوت منه بقلب خافق محزون وجل وطرف خاشع ذليل وفؤاد منكسر
وأعطيت كتابك الذي لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها فكم من فاحشة
نسيتها فتذكرتها وكم من طاعة غفلت عن آفاتها فانكشف لك عن مساويها فكم لك
من خجل وجبن وكم لك من حصر وعجز فليت شعري بأي قدم تقف بين يديه وبأي لسان
تجيب وبأي قلب تعقل ما تقول ثم تفكر فى عظم حياتك إذا ذكرك ذنوبك شفاها إذ
يقول يا عبدى أما استحييت منى فبارزتنى بالقبيح واستحييت من خلقى فأظهرت
لهم الجميل أكنت أهون عليك من سائر عبادي استخففت بنظرى إليك فلم تكترت
واستعظمت نظر غيرى ألم أنعم عليك فماذا غرك بى اظننت أنى لا أراك وأنك لا
تلقانى
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما منكم من أحد إلا ويسأله الله رب
العالمين ليس بينه وبينه حجاب ولا ترجمان (4) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم ليقفن أحدكم بين يدي الله عز وجل ليس بينه وبينه حجاب فيقول له ألم
أنعم عليك ألم أوتك ما لا فيقول بلى فيقول ألم أرسل إليك رسولا فيقول بلى
ثم ينظر عن يمينه فلا يرى إلا النار ثم ينظر عن شماله فلا يرى إلا النار
فليتق أحدكم النار ولو بشق تمرة فإن لم يجد فبكلمة طيبة (5) وقاله ابن
مسعود ما منكم من أحد إلا سيخلو الله عز وجل به كما يخلو أحدكم بالقمر ليلة
البدر ثم يقول يا ابن آدم ما غرك بى يا ابن آدم ما عملت فيما علمت يا ابن
آدم ماذا أجبت المرسلين يا ابن آدم  ألم أكن رقيبا على عينك وأنت تنظر بها
إلى ما لا يحل PageV04P519
لك ألم أكن رقيبا على أذنيك وهكذا حتى عد سائر أعضائه وقال مجاهد لا تزول
قدما عبد يوم القيامة من بين يدي الله عز وجل حتى يسأله عن أربع خصال عن
عمره فيما أفناه وعن علمه ما عمل فيه وعن جسده فيما أبلاه وعن ماله من أين
اكتسبه وفيماذا أنفقه فأعظم يا مسكين بحيائك عند ذلك بخطرك فإنك بين أن
يقال لك سترتها عليك فى الدنيا وأنا أغفرها لك اليوم فعند ذلك يعظم سرورك
وفرحك ويغبطك الأولون والآخرون وإما أن يقال للملائكة خذوا هذا العبد السوء
فغلوه ثم الجحيم صلوه وعند ذلك لو بكت السموات والأرض عليك لكان ذلك جديرا
بعظم مصيبتك وشدة حسرتك على ما فرطت فيه من طاعة الله وعلى ما بعت آخرتك من
دنيا دنيئة لم تبق معك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, to demand an account; the root implies a formal, binding inquiry that necessitates a response.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qurʾān, it denotes the eschatological interrogation (musāʾalah) by which God holds His creatures accountable, a pillar of justice (ʿadl) and recompense (jazāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for verbal questioning; metaphorical (majāz) when attributed to God, signifying His perfect knowledge manifesting as judgment, not ignorance or need for information.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To present, expose, or display; also width/breadth. The verbal noun ʿarḍ implies bringing something before a superior for inspection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the presentation of deeds (ʿarḍ al-aʿmāl) before God on the Day of Resurrection, a scene of universal manifestation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical display; metaphorical for the unveiling of hidden intentions and deeds, as nothing is concealed from the Divine sight.
- Root: ه-ي-ب (h-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Awe, reverence, dread mixed with veneration; the state of one overwhelmed by a majestic presence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The psychological state of the creature before the Creator's majesty (haybah), distinct from fear (khawf) as it includes reverential awe.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the emotion; used rhetorically to describe the overwhelming effect of Divine self-disclosure on prophets and angels alike.
- Root: ف-ض-ح (f-ḍ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To expose, disgrace, or shame publicly; to strip away covering so that faults become manifest.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The eschatological exposure (iftiḍāḥ) of sins before all creation, the ultimate humiliation for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for unveiling; metaphorical for the spiritual ruin resulting from public disclosure of hidden sins.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The text employs intricate conditional structures (e.g., "fa-baynamā... idhā...") where the protasis sets a temporal scene and the apodosis delivers the sudden, dramatic event, mirroring the abruptness of the Hereafter's terrors.
chapters.translation:
Then reflect, O wretched one, after these states upon what will be directed at you of questioning, face to face, without any interpreter. You will be asked about the little and the much, the speck on a date-stone (al-naqīr) and the husk around it (al-qaṭmīr). For while you are in the distress of the Resurrection, its sweat, and the severity of its great horrors, suddenly the angels descend from the horizon of heaven with immense bodies and gigantic forms, stern and severe. They are commanded to seize the forelocks of the criminals and drag them to the standing-place of exposure before the Omnipotent (al-Jabbār). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, has an angel between whose two eyelids is a distance of a hundred years' journey." So what is your opinion of yourself when you behold the likes of these angels sent to you to take you to the station of exposure, and you see them, despite the enormity of their forms, broken down by the severity of that Day, filled with dread at what has appeared of the Omnipotent's wrath upon His servants? When they descend, there remains no prophet, no veracious one (ṣiddīq), no righteous soul, but they fall upon their chins in fear that they themselves might be the ones seized. Such is the state of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) — so what is your opinion of the disobedient criminals?

At that moment, certain groups, from the extremity of their terror, hasten forward and say to the angels: "Is our Lord among you?" — this because of the grandeur of their procession and the intensity of their awe. The angels are alarmed by their question, revering their Creator from being contained among them, and they cry out with their voices, glorifying their King against what the people of the earth had imagined, saying: "Glory be to our Lord! He is not among us, but He is coming after this." Then the angels arrange themselves in ranks, encircling all creatures from every side, and upon all of them is the insignia of abasement and submission, and the appearance of fear and dread, because of the severity of that Day.

At that moment, God, Exalted is He, fulfills His word: {«For We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. Then We will relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent»} (7:6-7), and His word: {«So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do»} (15:92-93). He begins with the prophets: {«On the Day when God gathers the messengers and says, "What answer were you given?" They say, "We have no knowledge; indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen"»} (5:109). Alas for the severity of a Day in which the intellects of the prophets are confounded and their knowledge is erased by the intensity of the awe, when it is said to them: "What answer were you given, when you were sent to the creatures?" — though they had known — yet their minds are stunned, and they know not with what to reply. So they say, from the intensity of the awe: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen." And at that time they are truthful, for their intellects have flown away and their knowledges have been erased, until God, Exalted is He, strengthens them. Then Noah, peace be upon him, is summoned, and it is said to him: "Did you convey the message?" He says: "Yes." Then it is said to his community: "Did he convey to you?" They say: "No warner came to us."

And Jesus, peace be upon him, is brought forth, and God, Exalted is He, says to him: {«Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God"?»} (5:116). He remains convulsed under the awe of this question for years. Alas for the greatness of a Day in which such questioning is established as the procedure (siyāsah) even against the prophets! Then the angels come forward and call out, one by one: "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, come forth to the standing-place of exposure!" At that, the flanks tremble, the limbs quake, the intellects are stupefied, and certain people wish to be taken to the Fire rather than have their ugly deeds displayed before the Omnipotent, or their veil torn open before the assembly of all creatures.

Before the commencement of the questioning, the light of the Throne appears: {«And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord»} (39:69). Every servant becomes certain of the approach of the Omnipotent for the questioning of His servants, and each one thinks that no one sees him but Him alone, and that he is the one seized for the taking and the questioning, to the exclusion of all others. Then the Omnipotent, Glorified and Exalted is He, says: "O Gabriel, bring the Fire!" Gabriel comes to it and says: "O Jahannam, answer your Creator and your King!" He finds it in its fury and rage, and no sooner does he call it than it erupts and boils over, and it sighs (zafīr) toward the creatures and gasps (shahīq). The creatures hear its fury and its sighing. Its keepers rise up, leaping toward the creatures in wrath against those who disobeyed God and opposed His command.

So bring to your mind, and present in your heart, the state of the servants' hearts when they are filled with terror and dread. They fall down on their knees, and turn away fleeing — {«On the Day when you see every nation kneeling»} (45:28). Some fall on their faces, prostrate. The disobedient and the wrongdoers cry out in woe and destruction, and the veracious ones cry out: "Ourselves! Ourselves!" While they are in this state, the Fire gives its second sigh, and their fear is multiplied, their strength fails, and they think they are surely seized. Then it gives its third sigh, and all creatures collapse on their faces, their eyes fixed, gazing from a hidden, humble glance. At that, the hearts of the wrongdoers are crushed, reaching their throats, choked with grief, and the intellects of both the fortunate and the wretched are utterly confounded.

After that, God, Exalted is He, turns to the messengers and says: "What answer were you given?" When the disobedient see what procedure has been established against the prophets, their terror intensifies. The father flees from his son, the brother from his brother, the husband from his wife, and each one remains awaiting his own command. Then they are taken, one by one, and God, Exalted is He, questions him face to face about the little of his deeds and the much, about his secret and his public, and about all his limbs and organs.

Abū Hurayrah said: "They said: 'O Messenger of God, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: 'Do you doubt seeing the sun at noon when there is no cloud before it?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you doubt seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud before it?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not doubt seeing your Lord.' Then a servant is brought forth, and He says to him: 'Did I not honor you, make you a leader, marry you, and subject to you horses and camels, and let you lead and rule?' The servant says: 'Yes.' He says: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He says: 'No.' He says: 'Then I will forget you as you forgot Me.'"

So imagine yourself, O wretched one, when the angels have seized your arms, and you are standing before God, Exalted is He, as He questions you face to face, saying to you: "Did I not bestow upon you youth — in what did you spend it? Did I not grant you respite in life — in what did you consume it? Did I not provide you wealth — from where did you earn it, and in what did you spend it? Did I not honor you with knowledge — what did you do with what you knew?" How do you see your shame and your embarrassment, as He counts upon you His favors and your disobediences, His blessings and your evils? If you deny, your limbs bear witness against you.

Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: "We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he laughed, then said: 'Do you know why I laugh?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Because of the servant's addressing his Lord. He says: "O Lord, did You not protect me from injustice?" He says: "Yes." He says: "Then I will not accept against myself any witness but myself." He says: "Sufficient is your own soul this Day as a reckoner against you, and the noble scribes as witnesses." He said: "Then a seal is placed upon his mouth, and it is said to his limbs: 'Speak.' So they speak of his deeds. Then he is left free to speak, and he says to his limbs: 'Away with you, and destruction! It was for you that I was fighting!'""

So we seek refuge in God from exposure (iftiḍāḥ) before the assembly of creatures through the testimony of the limbs — unless God, Exalted is He, has promised the believer that He will conceal him and not expose him to anyone else.

A man asked Ibn ʿUmar: "How did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, speak about the private consultation (al-najwā)?" He said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'One of you will draw near to his Lord until He places His covering over him, and He says: "You did such-and-such?" He says: "Yes." He says: "You did such-and-such?" He says: "Yes." Then He says: "I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today."'" And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever conceals the fault of a believer, God will conceal his fault on the Day of Resurrection." This hope is only for a believing servant who concealed the faults of people, bore their shortcomings toward himself, did not move his tongue to mention their faults, and did not mention them in their absence with what they would dislike to hear. Such a one is worthy of being recompensed with the like on the Day of Resurrection. But even if you suppose that He conceals you from others — has not the call to the standing of exposure already struck your ears? That very terror suffices as recompense for your sins, when you are seized by your forelock and dragged, your heart trembling, your mind flying, your flanks quaking, your limbs convulsing, your color changed, and the world darkened before you by the intensity of the horror.

So reckon yourself in this condition, stepping over necks, tearing through ranks, dragged as a spurred horse is dragged, while all creatures raise their eyes toward you. Imagine yourself in the hands of those appointed over you in this state, until you are brought to the Throne of the Merciful. They cast you from their hands, and God, Glorified and Exalted is He, calls you with His mighty speech: "O son of Adam, draw near to Me." So you draw near to Him with a heart palpitating, sorrowful, trembling; with a glance humble and abased; with a broken spirit. And your book is given to you — {«which leaves out nothing, small or great, but has counted it»} (18:49). How many an obscenity you had forgotten, and you remember it! How many an act of obedience whose hidden defects you had neglected, and its faults are unveiled to you! How much shame and cowardice you have! How much constraint and incapacity! Would that I knew with what foot you will stand before Him, with what tongue you will answer, with what heart you will comprehend what you say!

Then reflect upon the greatness of your shame when He reminds you of your sins face to face, saying: "O My servant, were you not ashamed of Me, that you confronted Me with the ugly, yet were ashamed of My creatures, so you showed them the beautiful? Was I of less account to you than My other servants? Did you make light of My watching you, so you did not care, yet magnified the gaze of others upon you? Did I not bestow favors upon you — what then deceived you concerning Me? Did you think that I did not see you, and that you would not meet Me?"

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "There is not one of you but God, the Lord of the worlds, will question him with no veil between him and Him, and no interpreter." And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Each of you will surely stand before God, Mighty and Majestic, with no veil between him and Him. He will say: 'Did I not bestow favors upon you? Did I not give you wealth?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'Did I not send to you a messenger?' He says: 'Yes.' Then he looks to his right and sees nothing but the Fire, then looks to his left and sees nothing but the Fire. So let each of you guard against the Fire, even with half a date, and if he finds not, then with a good word."

And Ibn Masʿūd said: "There is not one of you but God, Mighty and Majestic, will be alone with him as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon. Then He says: 'O son of Adam, what deceived you concerning Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, what answer did you give the messengers? O son of Adam, was I not watching over your eye when you looked with it at what was unlawful for you? Was I not watching over your ears?'" — and so on until he counted all his limbs.

And Mujāhid said: "A servant's feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection from before God, Mighty and Majestic, until he is asked about four matters: about his life — in what he consumed it; about his knowledge — what he did with it; about his body — in what he wore it out; and about his wealth — from where he earned it and in what he spent it."

So magnify, O wretched one, your shame at that moment, and your peril! For you are between two outcomes: either it is said to you: "I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today" — and then your joy and happiness become immense, and the first and the last envy you; or it is said to the angels: "Seize this evil servant, shackle him, then roast him in the Blazing Fire!" And at that moment, if the heavens and the earth wept over you, it would be fitting for the greatness of your calamity and the severity of your regret over what you neglected of obedience to God, and over what you sold of your Hereafter for a base world that did not remain with you.

chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| صفة الميزان

ثم لا تغفل عن الفكر في الميزان وتطاير الكتب إلى الأيمان والشمائل فإن
الناس بعد السؤال ثلاث فرق {فرقة} ليس لهم حسنة فيخرج من النار عنق أسود
فيلقطهم لقط الطير الحب وينطوى عليهم ويلقيهم فى النار فتبتلعهم النار
وينادى عليهم شقاوة لا سعادة بعدها وقسم آخر لا سيئة لهم فينادى مناد ليقم
الحمادون لله على كل حال فيقومون ويسرحون إلى الجنة ثم يفعل ذلك بأهل قيام
الليل ثم بمن لم تشغله تجارة الدنيا ولا بيعها عن ذكر الله تعالى
وينادى عليهم سعادة لا شقاوة بعدها ويبقى قسم ثالث وهم الأكثرون خلطوا
عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وقد يخفى عليهم ولا يخفى على الله تعالى أن الغالب
حسناتهم أو سيئاتهم ولكن يأبى الله إلا أن يعرفهم ذلك ليبين فضله عند العفو
وعدله عند العقاب فتتطاير الصحف والكتب منطوية على الحسنات والسيئات وينصب
الميزان وتشخص الأبصار إلى الكتب أتقع فى اليمين أو فى الشمال ثم إلى لسان
الميزان أيميل إلى جانب السيئات أو إلى جانب الحسنات وهذه حالة هائلة تطيش
فيها عقول الخلائق وروى الحسن أن رسول الله  صلى الله عليه وسلم كان رأسه فى
حجر عائشة رضي الله عنها فنعس فذكرت الآخرة فبكت حتى سال دمعها فنقط على خد
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فانتبه فقال ما يبكيك يا عائشة قالت ذكرت
الآخرة هل تذكرون أهليكم يوم القيامة قال والذي نفسي بيده فى ثلاث مواطن
فإن أحدا لا يذكر إلا نفسه إذا وضعت الموازين ووزنت الأعمال حتى ينظر ابن
آدم أيخف ميزانه أم يثقل
وعند الصحف حتى ينظر أبيمينه يأخذ كتابه أو شماله وعند الصراط (1) وعن
أنس يؤتى بابن آدم يوم القيامة حتى يوقف بين كفتى الميزان ويوكل به ملك فإن
ثقل ميزانه نادى الملك بصوت يسمع الخلائق سعد فلان سعادة لا يشقى بعدها
أبدا وإن خف ميزانه نادى بصوت يسمع الخلائق شقى فلان شقاوة لا يسعد بعدها
أبدا
وعند خفه كفة الحسنات تقبل الزبانية وبأيديهم مقامع من حديد عليهم ثياب
من نار فيأخذون نصيب النار إلى النار قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في
يوم القيامة إنه يوم ينادى الله تعالى فيه آدم عليه السلام فيقول له قم يا
آدم فابعث بعث النار فيقول وكم بعث النار فيقول من كل ألف تسعمائة وتسعة
وتسعون فلما سمع الصحابة ذلك أبلسوا حتى ما أوضحوا بضاحكة فلما رأى رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما عند أصحابه قال اعملوا وأبشروا فوالذى نفس محمد
بيده إن معكم لخليقتين ما كانتا مع أحد قط إلا كثرتاه مع من هلك من بنى آدم
وبنى إبليس قالوا وما هما يا رسول الله قال يأجوج ومأجوج قال فسرى عن القوم
فقال اعملوا وأبشروا فوالذى نفس PageV04P520
محمد بيده ما أنتم فى الناس يوم القيامة إلا كالشامة فى جنب البعير أو
كالرقمة فى ذراع الدابة (1)

### |||| صفة الخصماء ورد المظالم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ز-ن (w-z-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring by balance; al-wazn denotes the act of determining weight, and al-mīzān is the instrument of equitable weighing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the eschatological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice (ʿadl) by which deeds are weighed—not by physical mass but by the metaphysical weight of obedience (ṭāʿah) and disobedience (maʿṣiyah), manifesting God's wisdom in recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage (ḥaqīqah) refers to physical scales; here it is majāz (metaphorical) extended to the weighing of moral acts, yet retained as a real event (ḥaqq) in the unseen realm, not a mere figure of speech.
- Root: ط-ي-ر (ṭ-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fly, to scatter swiftly; taṭāyur al-kutub denotes the rapid dispersal of scrolls.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The flying of the books (ṣuḥuf) to the right and left hands symbolizes the division of destinies—right (yamīn) for felicity, left (shimāl) for misery—rooted in Quranic depiction of the reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal flight of physical scrolls; metaphorically, the instantaneous divine decree assigning each soul its record without delay.
- Root: خ-ل-ط (kh-l-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Mixing, blending; khalatū ʿamalan ṣāliḥan wa ākhara sayyi'an means intermingling good and evil deeds.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Qur'anic usage (e.g., {«خَلَطُوا عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَآخَرَ سَيِّئًا»}), it denotes a state of moral ambiguity where neither category wholly prevails, requiring divine discernment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal mixing of substances; metaphorically, the composite moral state of the majority of humanity, whose final judgment is deferred to the Balance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnā') — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "in thaqula mīzānuhu... in khaffa mīzānuhu") with apodosis marked by the king's proclamation, and exceptive phrasing ("lā yadhkuru illā nafsahu") to emphasize exclusivity, requiring precise parsing of the protasis-apodosis relationship for accurate rendering.
chapters.translation:
### |||| The Description of the Balance

Then do not neglect reflection upon the Balance (al-mīzān) and the flying of the books (ṣuḥuf) to the right hands and the left hands. For the people after the questioning are three groups: a group having no good deeds—a black neck emerges from the Fire, snatching them as a bird snatches seeds, folding over them, and casting them into the Fire, and the Fire swallows them; and it is proclaimed over them: "Wretchedness, with no felicity after it!" Another group has no evil deeds—a herald calls out: "Let those who praised God in every state arise!" So they arise and are sent forth to Paradise. Then this is done for the people of night prayer (qiyām al-layl), then for those whom neither the commerce of the world nor its trade distracted from the remembrance of God the Exalted; and it is proclaimed over them: "Felicity, with no wretchedness after it!" There remains a third group—and they are the majority—who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one. It may be hidden from them, but it is not hidden from God the Exalted whether their good deeds or their evil deeds predominate. Yet God refuses except to make this known to them, to manifest His bounty (faḍl) at the time of pardon and His justice (ʿadl) at the time of punishment. So the scrolls and books fly, folded upon the good deeds and the evil deeds, and the Balance is erected, and the eyes stare fixedly at the books—will they fall to the right or to the left?—then at the tongue of the Balance—does it incline toward the side of evil deeds or toward the side of good deeds? This is a tremendous state (hālahā hā'ilah) in which the intellects of creatures are confounded.

Al-Ḥasan narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had his head in the lap of ʿĀ'ishah (may God be pleased with her), and he dozed. She mentioned the Hereafter and wept until her tears flowed and dripped upon the cheek of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He awoke and said: "What makes you weep, O ʿĀ'ishah?" She said: "I mentioned the Hereafter—will you remember your families on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, in three places no one will remember anyone but himself: when the balances are set up and the deeds are weighed, until the son of Adam sees whether his balance is light or heavy; and at the scrolls, until he sees whether he takes his book in his right hand or his left; and at the Ṣirāṭ (the Bridge)."

And on the authority of Anas: The son of Adam is brought on the Day of Resurrection until he is made to stand between the two pans of the Balance, and an angel is appointed over him. If his balance is heavy, the angel calls out with a voice heard by all creatures: "So-and-so has been felicitous—felicity after which he will never be wretched!" And if his balance is light, he calls out with a voice heard by all creatures: "So-and-so has been wretched—wretchedness after which he will never be felicitous!"

And when the pan of good deeds is light, the Zabāniyah (the stern angels of punishment) advance, holding iron maces, wearing garments of fire, and they seize the portion of the Fire and take it to the Fire. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, it is a day on which God the Exalted calls out to Adam (peace be upon him) and says to him: 'Arise, O Adam, and send forth the contingent of the Fire!' He says: 'And how many is the contingent of the Fire?' He says: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'" When the Companions heard this, they were stricken with despair until they did not show a single smile. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) saw what his Companions were experiencing, he said: "Work and rejoice! For by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, there are with you two creatures who have never been with any people except that they increased them—alongside those who perished from the children of Adam and the children of Iblīs." They said: "And who are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Ya'jūj and Ma'jūj (Gog and Magog)." He said: "Then the distress was lifted from the people, and he said: 'Work and rejoice! For by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you are among the people on the Day of Resurrection only like a mole on the flank of a camel, or like a small mark on the foreleg of a beast.'"
