chapters.title_en: The Peril of the Balance and the Reckoning of Oppressions
chapters.arabic_text:
قد عرفت هول الميزان وخطره وأن الأعين شاخصة إلى لسان الميزان فأما من
ثقلت موازينه فهو في عيشة راضية وأما من خفت موازينه فأمه هاوية وما أدراك
ماهيه نار حامية واعلم أنه لا ينجو من  خطر الميزان إلا من حاسب في الدنيا
نفسه ووزن فيها بميزان الشرع أعماله وأقواله وخطراته ولحظاته كما قال عمر
رضي الله عنه حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا وإنما
حسابه لنفسه أن يتوب عن كل معصية قبل الموت توبة نصوحا ويتدارك ما فرط من
تقصيره في فرائض الله تعالى ويرد المظالم حبة بعد حبة ويستحل كل من تعرض له
بلسانه ويده وسوء ظنه بقلبه وبطيب قلوبهم حتى يموت ولم يبق عليه مظلمة ولا
فريضة
فهذا يدخل الجنة بغير حساب وإن مات قبل رد المظالم أحاط به خصماؤه فهذا
يأخذ بيده وهذا يقبض على ناصيته وهذا يتعلق بلببه هذا يقول ظلمتني وهذا
يقول شتمتني وهذا يقول استهزأت بى وهذا يقول ذكرتنى فى الغيبة بما يسوءنى
وهذا يقول جاورتني فأسأت جواري وهذا يقول عاملتنى فغششتنى وهذا يقول
بايعتنى فغبنتنى وأخفيت عنى عيب سلعتك وهذا يقول كذبت فى سعر متاعك وهذا
يقول رأيتنى محتاجا وكنت غنيا فما أطعمتنى وهذا يقول وجدتني مظلوما وكنت
قادرا على دفع الظلم عنى فداهنت الظالم وما راعيتنى فبينا أنت كذلك وقد
انشب الخصماء فيك مخالبهم وأحكموا فى تلابيبك أيديهم وأنت مبهوت متحير من
كثرتهم حتى لم يبق فى عمرك أحد عاملته على درهم أو جالسته فى مجلس إلا وقد
استحق عليك مظلمة بغيبة أو خيانة أو نظر بعين استحقار وقد ضعفت عن مقاومتهم
ومددت عنق الرجاء إلى سيدك ومولاك لعله يخلصك من أيديهم إذ قرع سمعك نداء
الجبار جل جلاله اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم فعند ذلك ينخلع
قلبك من الهيبة وتوقن نفسك بالبوار وتتذكر ما أنذرك الله تعالى على لسان
رسوله حيث قال ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم
تشخص فيه الأبصار مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء
وأنذر الناس الآية
فما أشد فرحك اليوم بتمضمضك باعراض الناس ويناولك أموالهم وما أشد حسراتك
في ذلك اليوم إذا وقف ربك على بساط العدل وشوفهت  بخطاب السياسة وأنت مفلس
فقير عاجز مهين لا تقدر على أن ترد حقا أو تظهر عذرا فعند ذلك تؤخذ حسناتك
التى تعبت فيها عمرك وتنقل إلى خصمائك عوضا عن حقوقهم
قال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل تدرون من المفلس قلنا
المفلس فينا يا رسول الله من لا درهم له ولا دينار ولا متاع قال المفلس من
أمتى من يأتى يوم القيامة بصلاة وصيام وزكاة ويأتى وقد شتم هذا وقذف هذا
وأكل مال هذا وسفك دم هذا وضرب هذا فيعطى هذا من حسناته وهذا من حسناته فإن
فنيت حسناته قبل أن يقضى ما عليه أخذ من خطاياهم فطرحت عليه ثم طرح فى
النار (2) فانظر إلى مصيبتك فى مثل هذا اليوم إذ ليس يسلم لك حسنة من آفات
الرياء ومكايد الشيطان فإن سلمت حسنة واحدة فى كل مدة طويلة ابتدرها خصماؤك
وأخذوها ولعلك لو حاسبت نفسك وأنت مواظب على صيام النهار وقيام الليل لعلمت
أنه لا ينقضى عنك يوم إلا ويجرى PageV04P521
على لسانك من غيبة المسلمين ما يستوفى جميع حسناتك فكيف ببقية السيئات من
أكل الحرام والشبهات والتقصير فى الطاعات وكيف ترجو الخلاص من المظالم في
يوم يقتص فيه للجماء من القرناء فقد روى أبو ذر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم رأى شاتين ينتطحان فقال يا أبا ذر أتدرى فيم ينتطحان قلت لا قال ولكن
الله يدرى وسيقضى بينهما يوم القيامة (1)
وقال أبو هريرة في قوله عز وجل {وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير
بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم} أنه يحشر الخلق كلهم يوم القيامة البهائم والدواب
والطير وكل شىء فيبلغ من عدل الله تعالى أن يأخذ للجماء من القرناء ثم يقول
كونى ترابا فذلك حين يقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا فكنت أنت يا مسكين فى
يوم ترى صحيفتك خالية عن حسنات طال فيها تعبك فتقول أين حسناتى فيقال نقلت
إلى صحيفة خصمائك وترى صحيفتك مشحونة بسيئات طال فى الصبر عنها نصبك واشتد
بسبب الكف عنها عناؤك فتقول يا رب هذه سيئات ما قارفتها قط فيقال هذه سيئات
القوم الذين اغتبتهم وشتمتهم وقصدتهم بالسوء وظلمتهم فى المبايعة والمجاورة
والمخاطبة والمناظرة والمذاكرة والمدارسة وسائر أصناف المعاملة
قال ابن مسعود قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان قد يئس أن
تعبد الأصنام بأرض العرب ولكن سيرضى منكم بما هو دون ذلك بالمحقرات وهى
الموبقات فاتقوا الظلم ما استطعتم فإن العبد ليجىء يوم القيامة بأمثال
الجبال من الطاعات فيرى أنهن سينجينه فما يزال عبد يجىء فيقول رب إن فلانا
ظلمنى بمظلمة فيقول امح من حسناته فما يزال كذلك حتى لا يبقى من حسناته شىء
وإن مثل ذلك مثل سفر نزلوا بفلاة من الأرض ليس معهم حطب فتفرق القوم فحطبوا
فلم يلبثوا أن أعظموا نارهم وصنعوا ما أرادوا (2) وكذلك الذنوب ولما نزل
قوله تعالى {إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون}
قال الزبير يا رسول الله أيكرر علينا ما كان بيننا فى الدنيا مع خواص
الذنوب قال نعم ليكررن عليكم حتى تؤدوا إلى كل ذي حق حقه (3) قال الزبير
والله إن الأمر لشديد فأعظم بشدة يوم لا يسامح فيه بخطوة ولا يتجاوز فيه عن
لطمة ولا عن كلمة حتى ينتقم للمظلوم من الظالم قال أنس سمعت رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم يقول يحشر الله العباد عراة غبرا بهما قال قلنا ما بهما قال
ليس معهم شىء ثم يناديهم ربهم تعالى بصوت يسمعه من بعد كما يسمعه من قرب
أنا الملك أنا الديان لا ينبغى لأحد من أهل الجنة أن يدخل الجنة ولأحد من
أهل النار عليه مظلمة حتى أقتصه منه ولا لأحد من أهل النار إن يدخل النار
ولأحد من أهل الجنة عنده مظلمة حتى أقتصه منه حتى اللطمة قلنا وكيف وإنما
نأتي الله عز وجل عراة غبرا بهما فقال بالحسنات والسيئات (4) فاتقوا الله
عباد الله ومظالم العباد بأخذ أموالهم PageV04P522
والتعرض لأعراضهم وتضييق قلوبهم وإساءة الخلق فى معاشرتهم فإن ما  بين
العبد وبين الله خاصة فالمغفرة إليه أسرع ومن اجتمعت عليه مظالم وقد تاب
عنها وعسر عليه استحلال أرباب المظالم فليكثر من حسناته ليوم القصاص ويسر
ببعض الحسنات بينه وبين الله بكمال الإخلاص بحيث لا يطلع عليه إلا الله
فعساه يقربه ذلك إلى الله تعالى فينال به لطفه الذى ادخره لأحبابه المؤمنين
فى دفع مظالم العباد عنهم كما روى عن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
أنه قال بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالس إذ رأيناه يضحك حتى بدت
ثناياه فقال عمرا ما يضحكك يا رسول الله بأبي أنت وأمى قال رجلان من أمتي
جثيا بين يدي رب العزة فقال أحدهما يا رب خذلى مظلمتى من أخى فقال الله
تعالى أعط أخاك مظلمته قال يا رب لم يبق من حسناته شيء فقال الله تعالى
للطالب كيف تصنع ولم يبق من حسناته شىء قال يا رب يتحمل عنى من أوزارى قال
وفاضت عينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالبكاء ثم قال إن ذلك ليوم عظيم
يوم يحتاج الناس إلى أن يحمل عنهم من أوزارهم قال فقال الله للطالب ارفع
رأسك فانظر فى الجنان فرفع رأسه فقال يا رب أرى مدائن من فضة مرتفعة وقصورا
من ذهب مكللة باللؤلؤ لأي نبي هذا أو لأى صديق هذا أو لأى شهيد هذا قال لمن
أعطانى الثمن قال يا رب ومن يملك ثمنه قال أنت تملكه قال وما هو قال عفوك
عن أخيك قال يا رب إنى قد عفوت عنه قال الله تعالى خذ بيد أخيك فأدخله
الجنة ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذلك اتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات
بينكم فإن الله يصلح بين المؤمنين (1) وهذا تنبيه على أن ذلك إنما ينال
بالتخلق بأخلاق الله وهو إصلاح ذات البين وسائر الأخلاق
فتفكر الآن فى نفسك إن خلت صحيفتك عن المظالم أو تلطف لك حتى عفا عنك
وأيقنت بسعادة الأبد كيف يكون سرورك فى منصرفك من مفصل الفضاء  وقد خلع عليك
خلعة الرضا وعدت بسعادة ليس بعدها شقاء وبنعيم لا يدور بحواشيه الفناء وعند
ذلك طار قلبك سرورا وفرحا وابيض وجهك واستنار وأشرق كما يشرق القمر ليلة
البدر فتوهم تبخترك بين الخلائق رافعا رأسك خاليا عن الأوزار ظهرك ونضرة
نسيم النعيم وبرد الرضا يتلألأ من جبينك وخلق الأولين والآخرين ينظرون إليك
وإلى حالك ويغبطونك فى حسنك وجمالك والملائكة يمشون بين يديك ومن خلفك
وينادون على رءوس الأشهاد هذا فلان بن فلان رضى الله عنه وأرضاه وقد سعد
سعادة لا يشقى بعدها أبدا أفترى أن هذا المنصب ليس بأعظم من المكانة التى
تنالها فى قلوب الخلق فى الدنيا بريائك ومداهنتك وتصنعك وتزينك فإن كنت
تعلم أنه خير منه بل لانسبة له إليه فتوسل إلى إدراك هذه الرتبة بالإخلاص
الصافى والنية الصادقة فى معاملتك مع الله فلن تدرك ذلك إلا به
وإن تكن الأخرى والعياذ بالله بأن خرج من صحيفتك جريمة كنت تحسبها هينة
وهى عند الله عظيمة فمقتك لأجلها فقال عليك لعنتى يا عبد السوء لا أتقبل
منك عبادتك فلا تسمع هذا النداء إلا ويسود وجهك ثم تغضب الملائكة لغضب الله
تعالى فيقولون وعليك لعنتنا ولعنة الخلائق أجمعين وعند ذلك تنثال إليك
الزبانية وقد غضبت لغضب خالقها فأقدمت عليك بفظاظتها وزعارتها وصورها
المنكرة فأخذوا بناصيتك يسحبونك على وجهك على ملأ الخلق وهم ينظرون إلى
اسوداد وجهك وإلى ظهور خزيك وأنت تنادى بالويل والثبور وهم يقولون لك لا
تدع اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادع ثبورا كثيرا وتنادى الملائكة ويقولون هذا فلان
بن فلان PageV04P523
كشف الله عن فضائحه ومخازيه ولعنه بقبائح مساويه فشقى شقاوة لا يسعد
بعدها أبدا وربما يكون ذلك بذنب أذنبته خفية من عباد الله أو طلبا للمكانة
فى قلوبهم أو خوفا من الافتضاح عندهم فما أعظم جهلك إذ تحترز عن الافتضاح
عند طائفة يسيرة من عباد الله في الدنيا المنقرضة ثم لا تخشى من الافتضاح
العظيم فى ذلك الملأ العظيم مع التعرض لسخط الله وعقابه الأليم والسياق
بأيدى الزبانية  إلى سواء الجحيم فهذه أحوالك وأنت لم تشعر بالخطر الأعظم
وهو خطر الصراط
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ز-ن (w-z-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The act of weighing, measuring by balance; the instrument of justice (mīzān).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The cosmic scale of divine justice on the Day of Judgment; the weighing of deeds as an ontological reality, not mere metaphor.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to the eschatological balance; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to human self-assessment in this world.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Protasis-Apodosis (sharṭ wa-jawāb) — The repeated "fa-ammā... fa-" structure (as for one whose scales are heavy... he is in a pleasing life) establishes parallel conditional clauses requiring the apodosis to carry the resumptive particle.
chapters.translation:
You have come to know the terror of the Balance and its grave danger, and that all eyes are fixed upon the tongue of the Balance. As for the one whose scales are heavy, he shall be in a life of contentment; and as for the one whose scales are light, his abode shall be the Abyss — and what will make you know what that is? A blazing Fire.

Know that none shall be saved from the peril of the Balance except the one who, in this world, called his own soul to account and weighed therein — by the balance of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed."

His calling himself to account consists in this: that he repent from every act of disobedience before death with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), that he make up for whatever he has fallen short of in the obligatory duties of God (may He be exalted), that he restore all wrongs (maẓālim) grain by grain, and that he seek absolution from every person he has wronged — by his tongue, by his hand, or by his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — seeking their heartfelt satisfaction, until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him and no unfulfilled obligation.

Such a one enters Paradise without reckoning. But if he dies before restoring the wrongs, his adversaries encompass him: this one seizes his hand, that one grasps his forelock, another clings to his collar. One says: "You wronged me!" Another says: "You reviled me!" Another says: "You mocked me!" Another says: "You mentioned me in backbiting (ghībah) with what grieved me!" Another says: "You were my neighbor and you treated me evilly!" Another says: "You dealt with me and you cheated me!" Another says: "You sold to me and defrauded me, concealing the defect of your merchandise!" Another says: "You lied about the price of your goods!" Another says: "You saw me in need while you were wealthy, yet you did not feed me!" Another says: "You found me oppressed while you had the power to repel the injustice from me, yet you flattered the oppressor and did not protect me!"

While you are in this state — with the adversaries having sunk their claws into you and fastened their hands upon your collar, you dazed and bewildered by their multitude, until there remains no one in your entire life with whom you dealt over a single dirham or sat with in a single gathering who has not acquired a claim against you — whether by backbiting, betrayal, or a look of contempt — and you have grown too weak to resist them, and you stretch the neck of hope toward your Master and Patron, hoping He might deliver you from their hands — then the call of the Almighty (glorified be His majesty) strikes your ears: {«Today every soul shall be recompensed for what it has earned. No injustice today!»} (Q. 40:17). At that moment your heart is torn asunder from sheer awe, your soul is certain of perdition, and you recall what God (may He be exalted) warned you of upon the tongue of His Messenger, where He said: {«Do not suppose that God is heedless of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly, necks outstretched, heads raised, their glances never returning to them, and their hearts void.»} (Q. 14:42-43) — and He warned the people, to the end of the verse.

How intense is your joy today at having rinsed your mouth with the reputations of people and taken their wealth! And how intense will be your regrets on that Day when your Lord stations you upon the carpet of justice and you are confronted with the address of sovereign authority, while you are bankrupt, destitute, powerless, and humiliated — unable to restore a single right or to present a single excuse! At that moment, your good deeds — which you labored over your entire life — are taken and transferred to your adversaries as compensation for their rights.

Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do you know who the bankrupt one is?" We said: "The bankrupt among us, O Messenger of God, is the one who has neither dirham nor dinar nor property." He said: "The bankrupt of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting, and alms, yet comes having reviled this one, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of that one, and struck that one. So this one is given from his good deeds, and that one is given from his good deeds. If his good deeds are exhausted before what is owed is settled, then from their sins are taken and cast upon him, and then he is thrown into the Fire."

So look at your calamity on such a Day, when no single good deed of yours is safe from the afflictions of ostentation (riyāʾ) and the machinations of Satan. Even if one single good deed survived across that long span, your adversaries would rush upon it and seize it. Perhaps if you called yourself to account while persisting in fasting by day and praying by night, you would know that no day passes over you without your tongue uttering backbiting of Muslims sufficient to consume all your good deeds. How then with the rest of your sins — consuming the unlawful and the ambiguous, and falling short in acts of obedience? And how do you hope for deliverance from wrongs on a Day when retribution is exacted even for the hornless sheep from the horned one?

It is related that Abū Dharr said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) saw two sheep butting each other and said: "O Abū Dharr, do you know why they are butting each other?" I said: "No." He said: "But God knows, and He will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection."

Abū Hurayrah said concerning the saying of God (mighty and majestic): {«There is no creature on earth nor bird flying with its two wings except that they are communities like yourselves»} (Q. 6:38): "All of creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — the beasts, the cattle, the birds, and everything — and the justice of God (may He be exalted) will reach such a degree that He will exact retribution for the hornless sheep from the horned one. Then He will say: 'Be dust!' And that is when the disbeliever will say: {«Would that I were dust!»} (Q. 78:40)."

So you, O wretched one, on a Day when you see your scroll empty of good deeds over which your toil was long, will say: "Where are my good deeds?" And it will be said: "They have been transferred to the scrolls of your adversaries." And you will see your scroll laden with sins over which your endurance in abstaining from them was arduous and your struggle in refraining from them was severe, and you will say: "O Lord, these are sins I never committed!" And it will be said: "These are the sins of the people you backbit, reviled, intended evil against, and wronged in commerce, in neighborliness, in conversation, in debate, in remembrance, in study, and in all other kinds of dealings."

Ibn Masʿūd reported that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Satan has despaired of being worshipped through idols in the land of the Arabs, but he will be content with you for something less than that — the trivial offenses, which are the destructive sins. So beware of injustice (ẓulm) as much as you are able. For a servant will come on the Day of Resurrection with acts of obedience like mountains, and he will think they will save him. Then a servant will keep coming and saying: 'O Lord, so-and-so wronged me with such-and-such a wrong.' And He will say: 'Erase from his good deeds.' And he will keep on like that until nothing remains of his good deeds." And he said: "The likeness of that is like a group of travelers who alighted in an empty land with no firewood. They dispersed and gathered wood, and it was not long before they had kindled a great fire and accomplished what they wished." Likewise are sins.

When the saying of God (may He be exalted) was revealed: {«Indeed you are mortal, and indeed they are mortal. Then on the Day of Resurrection you shall dispute before your Lord»} (Q. 39:30-31), al-Zubayr said: "O Messenger of God, will what occurred between us in this world be repeated against us, along with the particular sins?" He said: "Yes, it will certainly be repeated against you, until you render to every claimant his due." Al-Zubayr said: "By God, the matter is severe indeed!" How severe is a Day on which no step is forgiven and no slap or word is overlooked, until the oppressed is avenged against the oppressor!

Anas said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "God will gather the servants naked, unshod, uncircumcised." We said: "What does 'uncircumcised' mean?" He said: "They have nothing with them." Then their Lord (may He be exalted) will call out to them with a voice heard by those far as by those near: "I am the King! I am the Judge! It is not fitting that any of the people of Paradise should enter Paradise while any of the people of the Fire has a claim of injustice against him, until I exact retribution for him. Nor is it fitting that any of the people of the Fire should enter the Fire while any of the people of Paradise has a claim of injustice against him, until I exact retribution for him — even for a slap." We said: "How is that, when we come to God (mighty and majestic) naked, unshod, uncircumcised?" He said: "By the good deeds and the evil deeds."

So fear God, O servants of God, regarding the wrongs against servants — the taking of their wealth, the assault upon their honor, the constricting of their hearts, and evil conduct in associating with them. For what is between the servant and God exclusively, forgiveness reaches it more swiftly. And the one upon whom wrongs have accumulated, who has repented from them but finds it difficult to seek absolution from their owners — let him multiply his good deeds for the Day of Retribution, and let him conceal some of his good deeds between himself and God with complete sincerity (ikhlāṣ), such that none knows of them but God. Perhaps that will bring him near to God (may He be exalted), and he will attain thereby His gentleness (luṭf) which He has reserved for His believing beloved ones, for the repelling of servants' wrongs from them.

It is related from Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "While the Messenger of God was sitting, we saw him laugh until his molars showed. ʿUmar said: 'What makes you laugh, O Messenger of God? May my father and mother be your ransom!' He said: 'Two men of my community knelt before the Lord of Might. One of them said: "O Lord, take for me my right from my brother." God (may He be exalted) said: "Give your brother his right." He said: "O Lord, nothing remains of his good deeds." God (may He be exalted) said to the claimant: "What will you do, when nothing remains of his good deeds?" He said: "O Lord, let him bear from my burdens."'" — And the eyes of the Messenger of God overflowed with tears, and he said: "Indeed, that is a tremendous Day — a Day when people will need others to bear from their burdens." — "Then God said to the claimant: 'Raise your head and look at the gardens.' He raised his head and said: 'O Lord, I see cities of silver raised high, and palaces of gold crowned with pearls. For which prophet is this, or which veracious one, or which martyr?' He said: 'For the one who gives Me its price.' He said: 'O Lord, who possesses its price?' He said: 'You possess it.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'Your forgiveness of your brother.' He said: 'O Lord, I have forgiven him.' God (may He be exalted) said: 'Take your brother's hand and lead him into Paradise.'" Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said at that: "Fear God and set right what is between you, for God sets right what is between the believers."

This is an indication that this attainment comes only through assuming the character traits of God (taʿalluq bi-akhlāq Allāh) — and that is the setting right of relations between people, along with all the other virtues.

Now reflect upon yourself: if your scroll is free of wrongs, or if God has been gentle with you such that the wronged have forgiven you, and you are certain of eternal felicity — how will your joy be when you depart from the place of judgment, robed in the garment of divine pleasure, returning with a happiness after which there is no misery, and a bliss whose edges mortality never circles? At that moment your heart flies with joy and gladness, your face whitens, shines, and radiates as the moon radiates on the night of its fullness. Imagine your striding proudly among creation, your head raised, your back free of burdens, the freshness of the breeze of bliss and the coolness of divine pleasure gleaming from your brow — while the first and last of creation gaze upon you and your state, envying you for your beauty and comeliness, and the angels walk before you and behind you, proclaiming at the heads of the witnesses: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, with whom God is well pleased and whom He has pleased! He has attained a felicity after which he shall never be wretched!"

Do you think this station is not greater than the standing you attain in the hearts of people in this world through your ostentation, your flattery, your affectation, and your self-adornment? If you know it is better than that — indeed, that it bears no comparison to it — then seek to attain this rank through pure sincerity and truthful intention in your dealings with God. For you shall not attain it except through that.

But if it is the other case — God forbid — that a crime has issued from your scroll which you deemed trivial but which is immense before God, and He has abhorred you for it, saying: "Upon you be My curse, O evil servant! I do not accept your worship!" — you will not hear this call without your face blackening. Then the angels become wrathful with the wrath of God (may He be exalted) and say: "And upon you be our curse and the curse of all creation!" At that moment the Zabāniyah (the keepers of Hell) rush upon you, enraged with the rage of their Creator, advancing upon you with their harshness, their ferocity, and their hideous forms. They seize your forelock and drag you upon your face before the assembly of creation, while they look upon the blackening of your face and the exposure of your disgrace — and you cry out with woe and destruction, while they say to you: "Do not call today for one destruction; call for many destructions!" And the angels call out, saying: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so — God has uncovered his scandals and his shameful deeds, and cursed him for the ugliness of his vices!" So he is wretched with a wretchedness after which he shall never be happy.

And perhaps that is due to a sin you committed in secret from the servants of God — or seeking standing in their hearts, or fearing exposure before them. How immense is your ignorance! You guard against exposure before a small band of God's servants in this passing world, yet you do not fear the great exposure before that great assembly, while exposing yourself to the wrath of God and His painful punishment, and being dragged by the hands of the Zabāniyah to the midst of Hellfire!

These are your states — and you have not yet perceived the greatest peril, which is the peril of the Bridge (ṣirāṭ).

chapters.title_en: The Description of the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ)
chapters.arabic_text: ### |||| صفة الصراط
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes a straight, clear path or way; also used for a road that is level and even. In Lisān al-ʿArab, it is synonymous with al-ṭarīq al-mustaqīm (the straight road), and its form suggests a path that is traversed with precision and certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-ṣirāṭ is the eschatological bridge over Hell (Jahannam), a metaphysical reality symbolizing the divine test of moral and spiritual discernment. It is the path of true faith (īmān) and righteous action (ʿamal ṣāliḥ), distinct from mere physical traversal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally (ḥaqīqah), it is a physical road; metaphorically (majāz), it denotes the moral and religious course of life. In the Hereafter, it becomes a concrete manifestation of one’s earthly adherence to the Sharīʿah, thus bridging the literal and the symbolic.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Definite Article (al-ṣifah wa al-mawṣūf) — The phrase "ṣifat al-ṣirāṭ" is an annexation (iḍāfah) where the first term (ṣifah) is indefinite in construct state, and the second (al-ṣirāṭ) is definite, yielding a specific, known description. This construction signals a definitive exposition of a singular, fixed reality.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that the description of the Bridge (ṣirāṭ) is among the matters that the heart must affirm, even though its precise modality (kayfiyyah) is beyond the reach of intellect. For the reports (akhbār) have come concerning it, and the consensus of the Salaf (the righteous predecessors) has established its reality. It is a bridge stretched over the back of Hell (Jahannam), sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, upon which the feet of the servants shall pass on the Day of Resurrection. The swift among them shall cross by the measure of their deeds, and the slow shall be delayed by the weight of their sins. Some shall pass like the blink of an eye, others like the flash of lightning, others like the passing of wind, others like the galloping of a horse, and others shall crawl and stumble, until the Fire seizes them by their sides, their ankles, and their necks, according to the extent of their transgressions. Yet the believer shall see his path illuminated by the light of his faith, while the hypocrite shall find his path darkened by the shadow of his doubt. And this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا ۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَّقْضِيًّا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it [Hell]; this is with your Lord a decree firmly established) — and the passing over (wurūd) is the crossing of the Bridge. So let the servant prepare for this crossing by lightening his burden of sins and strengthening his footing with sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ) and steadfastness (istiqāmah), for the Bridge is the final test of the soul’s attachment to the world and its detachment from it.

chapters.title_en: The Terrors of the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ) and the States of Its Crossing
chapters.arabic_text:
ثم تفكر بعد هذه الأهوال في قول الله تعالى {يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن
وفدا ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا} وفي قوله تعالى {فاهدوهم إلى صراط
الجحيم وقفوهم إنهم مسؤولون} فالناس من بعد هذه الأهوال يساقون إلى الصراط
وهو جسر ممدود على متن النار أحد من السيف وأدق من الشعر فمن استقام في هذا
العالم على الصراط المستقيم خف على صراط الآخرة ونجا ومن عدل عن الاستقامة
في الدنيا وأثقل ظهره بالأوزار وعصى تعثر في أول قدم من الصراط وتردى فتفكر
الآن فيما يحل من الفزع بفؤادك إذا رأيت الصراط ودقته ثم وقع بصرك على سواد
جهنم من تحته ثم قرع سمعك شهيق النار وتغيظها وقد كلفت أن تمشي على الصراط
مع ضعف حالك واضطراب قلبك وتزلزل قدمك وثقل ظهرك بالأوزار المانعة لك عن
المشي على بساط الأرض فضلا عن حدة الصراط فكيف بك إذا وضعت عليه إحدى رجليك
فأحسست بحدته واضطررت إلى أن ترفع القدم الثانية والخلائق بين يديك يزلون
ويتعثرون وتتنازلهم زبانية النار بالخطاطيف والكلاليب وأنت تنظر إليهم كيف
يتنكسون فتتسفل إلى جهة النار رءوسهم وتعلوا أرجلهم فياله من منظر ما أفظعه
ومرتقى ما أصعبه ومجاز ما أضيقه فانظر إلى حالك وأنت تزحف عليه وتصعد إليه
وأنت مثقل الظهر بأوزارك تلتفت يمينا وشمالا إلى الخلق وهم يتهافتون في
النار والرسول عليه السلام يقول يا رب سلم سلم والزعقات بالويل والثبور قد
ارتفعت إليك من قعر جهنم للكثرة من زل عن الصراط من الخلائق فكيف بك لو زلت
قدمك ولم ينفعك ندمك فناديت بالويل والثبور وقلت هذا ما كنت أخافه فياليتنى
قدمت لحياتي يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا يا ويلتا ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا
خليلا يا ليتني كنت ترابا يا ليتني كنت نسيا منسيا يا ليت أمي لم تلدني
وعند ذلك تختطفك النيران والعياذ بالله وينادي المنادي {اخسؤوا فيها ولا
تكلمون} فلا يبقى  سبيل إلا الصياح والأنين والتنفس والاستغاثة فكيف ترى
الآن عقلك وهذه الأخطار بين يديك فإن كنت غير مؤمن بذلك فما أطول مقامك مع
الكفار في دركات جهنم وإن كنت به مؤمنا وعنه غافلا وبالاستعداد له متهاونا
فما أعظم خسرانك وطغيانك وماذا ينفعك إيمانك إذا لم يبعثك على السعي في طلب
رضا الله تعالى بطاعته وترك معاصيه فلو لم يكن بين يديك إلا هول الصراط
وارتياع قلبك من خطر الجواز عليه وإن سلمت فناهيك به هولا وفزعا ورعبا قال
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يضرب الصراط بين ظهراني جهنم فأكون أول من
يجيز بأمته من الرسل ولا يتكلم يومئذ إلا الرسل ودعوى الرسل يومئذ اللهم
سلم اللهم سلم وفي جهنم كلاليب مثل شوك السعدان هل رأيتم شوك السعدان قالوا
نعم يا رسول الله قال فإنها مثل شوك السعدان غير أنه لا يعلم قدر عظمها إلا
الله تعالى تختطف الناس بأعمالهم فمنهم من يوبق بعمله ومنهم من يخردل ثم
ينجو (1) وقال أبو سعيد الخدري قال رسول الله PageV04P524
صلى الله عليه وسلم يمر الناس على جسر جهنم وعليه حسك وكلاليب وخطاطيف
تختطف الناس يمينا وشمالا وعلى جنبتيه ملائكة يقولون اللهم سلم اللهم سلم
فمن الناس من يمر مثل البرق ومنهم من يمر كالريح ومنهم من يمر كالفرس
المجري ومنهم من يسعى سعيا ومنهم من يمشي مشيا ومنهم من يحبو حبوا ومنهم من
يزحف زحفا فأما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها فلا يموتون ولا يحيون وأما ناس
فيؤخذون بذنوب وخطايا فيحترقون فحما ثم يؤذن في الشفاعة (1) وذكر إلى آخر
الحديث وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يجمع الله
الأولين والآخرين لميقات يوم معلوم قياما أربعين سنة شاخصة أبصارهم إلى
السماء ينتظرون فصل القضاء وذكر الحديث إلى أن ذكر وقت سجود المؤمنين قال
ثم يقول للمؤمنين ارفعوا رءوسكم فيرفعون رءوسهم فيعطيهم نورهم على قدر
أعمالهم فمنهم من يعطى نوره مثل الجبل العظيم يسعى بين يديه ومنهم من يعطى
نوره أصغر من ذلك ومنهم من يعطى نوره مثل النخلة ومنهم من يعطى نوره أصغر
من ذلك حتى يكون آخرهم رجلا يعطى نوره على إبهام قدمه فيضيء مرة ويخبو مرة
فإذا أضاء قدم قدمه فمشى وإذا أظلم قام ثم ذكر مرورهم على الصراط على قدر
نورهم فمنهم من يمر كطرف العين ومنهم من يمر كالبرق ومنهم من يمر كالسحاب
ومنهم من يمر كانقضاض الكواكب ومنهم من يمر كشد الفرس ومنهم من يمر كشد
الرجل حتى يمر الذي أعطي نوره على إبهام قدمه يحبو على وجهه ويديه ورجليه
تجر منه يد وتعلق أخرى وتعلق رجل وتجر أخرى وتصيب جوانبه النار قال فلا
يزال كذلك حتى يخلص فإذا خلص وقف عليها ثم قال الحمد لله لقد أعطاني الله
ما لم يعط أحدا إذ نجاني منها بعد إذ رأيتها فينطلق به إلى غدير عند باب
الجنة فيغتسل (2) وقال أنس بن مالك سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول
الصراط كحد السيف أو كحد الشعرة وإن الملائكة ينجون المؤمنين والمؤمنات وإن
جبريل عليه السلام لآخذ بحجزتى وإني لأقول يا رب سلم سلم فالزالون والزالات
يومئذ كثير (3)
فهذه أهوال الصراط وعظائمه فطول فيه فكرك فإن أسلم الناس من أهوال يوم
القيامة من طال فيها فكره في الدنيا فإن الله لا يجمع بين خوفين على عبد
فمن خاف هذه الأهوال في الدنيا أمنها في الآخرة ولست أعني بالخوف رقة كرقة
النساء تدمع عينك ويرق قلبك حال السماع ثم تنساه على القرب وتعود إلى لهوك
ولعبك فماذا من الخوف في شيء بل من خاف شيئا هرب منه ومن رجا شيئا طلبه فلا
ينجيك إلا خوف يمنعك عن معاصي الله تعالى ويحثك على طاعته وابعد من رقة
النساء خوف الحمقى إذا سمعوا الأهوال سبق إلى ألسنتهم الاستعاذة فقال أحدهم
استعنت بالله نعوذ بالله اللهم سلم سلم وهم مع ذلك مصرون على المعاصي التي
هي سبب هلاكهم فالشيطان يضحك من استعاذتهم كما يضحك على من يقصده سبع ضار
في صحراء ووراءه حصن فإذا رأى أنياب السبع وصولته من بعد قال بلسانه أعوذ
بهذا الحصن الحصين وأستعين بشدة بنيانه وإحكام أركانه فيقول ذلك بلسانه وهو
قاعد في مكانه فأنى يغني عنه ذلك من السبع وكذلك أهوال الآخرة ليس لها حصن
إلا قول لا إله إلا الله صادقا ومعنى صدقه أن لا يكون له مقصود سوى الله
تعالى ولا معبود غيره ومن اتخذ إلهه هواه فهو PageV04P525
بعيد من الصدق في توحيده وأمره مخطر في نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن
محبا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى
مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو
شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The straight path; a bridge; the middle way; derived from the notion of "swallowing" (as the path swallows the traveler), and applied to the bridge over Hell in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Ṣirāṭ is the path of truth in this world (the Straight Path of the Qur'an) and its corporeal manifestation in the Hereafter; the term carries both moral and eschatological weight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes a physical bridge; metaphorical usage denotes the way of righteousness; in the Hereafter, the literal and metaphorical converge.
- Root: ز-ل-ل (z-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To slip, to stumble, to err; a misstep of the foot or of judgment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral slippage (zallat) as the cause of perdition; the physical slipping on the Ṣirāṭ mirrors the moral deviation in worldly life.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the foot slipping on a surface; metaphorical: falling into sin; here both senses are operative simultaneously.
- Root: خ-ط-ف (kh-ṭ-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To snatch away swiftly, to seize violently; the hooks (khaṭāṭīf) that seize people.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The angels of punishment snatching souls by their deeds; the swift seizure as divine justice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical hooks and grapples; metaphorical: the sudden seizure by one's own accumulated sins.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clause Sequencing (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The text employs intricate conditional constructions (e.g., "if you slip... then your regret will not avail you") and temporal clauses (e.g., "when you place one foot... then you feel its sharpness") to build escalating rhetorical tension, requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
Then, after these terrors, reflect upon the saying of God the Exalted: {«On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the All-Merciful as a delegation, and We shall drive the sinners to Hell as a thirsty herd»} (Maryam 19:85-86), and upon His saying: {«Guide them to the path of Hell, and stop them, for they shall be questioned»} (al-Ṣāffāt 37:23-24). For mankind, after these terrors, are driven to the Ṣirāṭ — and it is a bridge stretched over the surface of the Fire, sharper than a sword and finer than a hair. Whoever was upright in this world upon the Straight Path shall find the bridge of the Hereafter easy and shall be saved; but whoever deviated from uprightness in this world, and weighed down his back with burdens (awzār), and disobeyed, shall stumble at the very first step of the bridge and plunge down.

Now reflect upon the terror that shall seize your heart when you behold the Ṣirāṭ and its fineness, and then your gaze falls upon the blackness of Hell beneath it, and then your ear is struck by the gasping and raging of the Fire — and you are charged to walk upon the bridge, with your state feeble, your heart trembling, your foot unsteady, and your back weighed down with burdens that would prevent you from walking even upon the carpet of the earth, let alone upon the sharpness of the Ṣirāṭ. How will it be with you when you place one of your feet upon it and feel its sharpness, and you are compelled to lift the second foot — while all creatures before you are slipping and stumbling, and the wardens (zabāniyah) of the Fire seize them with hooks and grapples, and you are watching them as they are toppled headlong, their heads plunging toward the Fire and their legs rising aloft? What a sight — how horrific! What an ascent — how arduous! What a passage — how narrow!

Look then at your own state as you crawl upon it and climb toward it, your back laden with your burdens, turning right and left toward the creatures as they tumble into the Fire — while the Messenger, peace be upon him, cries out: "O Lord, grant safety, grant safety!" — and the cries of woe and ruin rise up to you from the depths of Hell, because of the multitude of creatures who have slipped from the bridge. How will it be with you if your foot slips, and your regret avails you nothing, and you cry out in woe and ruin, saying: "This is what I feared! Would that I had sent forward something for my life! {«Would that I had taken a path with the Messenger! Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend!»} (al-Furqān 25:27-28) — {«Would that I were dust!»} (al-Nabā' 78:40) — Would that I were a thing forgotten! Would that my mother had not given me birth!"

And at that moment the fires snatch you away — God forbid! — and a caller cries out: {«Be cast into it, and do not speak to Me!»} (al-Mu'minūn 23:108). Then no recourse remains save shrieking, groaning, gasping, and crying for help.

How do you now regard your intellect, with these perils before you? If you are one who does not believe in this, then how long shall be your sojourn with the disbelievers in the depths of Hell! And if you believe in it yet are heedless of it, and negligent in preparing for it, then how immense is your loss and your transgression! What will your faith avail you if it does not impel you to strive in seeking the good pleasure of God the Exalted, through obedience to Him and abandonment of His disobedience? Even if nothing lay before you but the terror of the Ṣirāṭ and the fright of your heart from the peril of crossing it — even if you were saved — it would suffice as a horror, a terror, and a dread.

The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "The Ṣirāṭ shall be stretched across the midst of Hell, and I shall be the first of the messengers to cross with his community. On that day none shall speak save the messengers, and the plea of the messengers on that day shall be: 'O God, grant safety! O God, grant safety!' And in Hell there are grapples like the thorns of the sa'dān plant. Have you seen the thorns of the sa'dān?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "Verily they are like the thorns of the sa'dān, but none knows the magnitude of their size save God the Exalted. They snatch people by their deeds: among them is one who is destroyed by his deed, and among them is one who is shredded into pieces, then saved." (1)

And Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "People shall pass over the bridge of Hell, upon which are thorns, grapples, and hooks that snatch people right and left. On its two sides are angels saying: 'O God, grant safety! O God, grant safety!' Among the people, one passes like lightning, one like the wind, one like a galloping horse, one running, one walking, one crawling, one creeping. As for the people of the Fire who are its inhabitants, they neither die nor live. But some people are seized for their sins and transgressions, and they burn until they become charcoal; then permission is given for intercession." (1) — and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

And it is related from Ibn Mas'ūd, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "God shall gather the first and the last for an appointed meeting on a known Day, standing for forty years, their eyes fixed upon the sky, awaiting the judgment." — and he mentioned the hadith until he reached the mention of the time of the believers' prostration. He said: "Then He says to the believers: 'Raise your heads.' So they raise their heads, and they are given their light according to their deeds. Among them is one who is given his light like a great mountain, proceeding before him; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that; among them is one who is given his light like a palm tree; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that — until the last of them is a man who is given his light upon the tip of his big toe. It shines at times and dims at others. When it shines, he places his foot forward and walks; when it darkens, he stands still." Then he mentioned their passage over the Ṣirāṭ according to their light: among them one passes in the blink of an eye, one like lightning, one like a cloud, one like the shooting of stars, one like the galloping of a horse, one like the running of a man — until the one who was given his light upon the tip of his big toe passes, crawling upon his face, hands, and feet: one hand is dragged, another clings; one foot clings, another is dragged; and the sides of the Fire touch him. He said: "He continues thus until he is delivered. When he is delivered, he stands upon it and says: 'Praise be to God, Who has given me what He has given no one — for He has saved me from it after I had seen it!' Then he is taken to a pool at the gate of Paradise and bathes." (2)

And Anas ibn Mālik said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, say: "The Ṣirāṭ is like the edge of a sword, or like the edge of a hair. The angels save the believing men and believing women, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, holds my waist-wrapper, and I say: 'O Lord, grant safety, grant safety!' And the slippers — men and women — on that day are many." (3)

These, then, are the terrors of the Ṣirāṭ and its enormities. Prolong your reflection upon it. For the safest of people from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection is the one who prolonged his reflection upon them in this world. For God does not combine two fears upon a servant: whoever fears these terrors in this world shall be secure from them in the Hereafter.

I do not mean by "fear" a softness like the softness of women — that your eye weeps and your heart softens at the moment of hearing, then you forget it soon after and return to your amusement and play. What has such a thing to do with fear? Rather, whoever fears a thing flees from it, and whoever hopes for a thing seeks it. Nothing shall save you save a fear that restrains you from the disobedience of God the Exalted and impels you to His obedience.

And farther from the softness of women is the fear of fools: when they hear of these terrors, the words of seeking refuge leap to their tongues — one of them says: "I seek aid in God! We seek refuge in God! O God, grant safety, grant safety!" — while they persist in the very disobedience that is the cause of their destruction. Satan laughs at their seeking of refuge, just as one laughs at a man whom a predatory beast approaches in an open plain, while behind him is a fortress. When he sees the fangs of the beast and its assault from afar, he says with his tongue: "I seek refuge in this fortified fortress, and I seek aid in the strength of its structure and the firmness of its pillars!" — saying this with his tongue while he remains seated in his place. How will that avail him against the beast?

Likewise, the terrors of the Hereafter have no fortress save the saying "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh) — uttered truthfully. And the meaning of its truthfulness is that one has no object of intention save God the Exalted, and no object of worship other than Him. Whoever takes his own desire as his god is far from truthfulness in his declaration of unity (tawḥīd), and his affair is perilous.

If you are incapable of all that, then be a lover of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, eager to venerate his Sunnah, yearning to observe the hearts of the righteous from his community, and seeking blessing through their supplications. Perhaps you shall attain his intercession or theirs, and be saved through intercession — if your merchandise is little.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes pairing, doubling, or making even (e.g., al-shafʿ = the even number, opposite of odd). From this derives the sense of one who joins his intercession to another’s plea, thereby strengthening it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, shafāʿah is the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) act of pleading for the ummah on the Day of Judgment, a divinely granted honor (karāmah) that elevates the intercessor’s rank and manifests divine mercy, not a bargaining or independent power.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah): pairing one’s request with another’s need. Metaphorical (majāz): the intercessor’s status (jāh) before God, whereby his supplication is accepted—yet the ultimate causation remains solely with God.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — The title “ṣifat al-shafāʿah” uses an annexation structure where the first term (ṣifah) is defined by the second (shafāʿah), indicating that the attribute is intrinsic to the described reality, not accidental.
chapters.translation: I say: Now let us expound the attribute of intercession (ṣifat al-shafāʿah). Know that intercession is a reality affirmed by the consensus of the scholars (ahl al-ḥaqq), established by the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the ummah. Its true meaning is not that the intercessor possesses an independent power to overturn the divine decree, but rather that God—exalted be He—honors His chosen servants with a station (maqām maḥmūd) from which their supplication for sinners becomes a cause (sabab) for the outpouring of His mercy. Thus, the intercessor is but a veil of divine generosity, and the sole agent (al-fāʿil) is God alone. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: {«أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر، وأنا أول من تنشق عنه الأرض ولا فخر، وأنا أول شافع وأول مشفع»} — “I am the master of the children of Adam, and I say this without pride; I am the first from whom the earth will split open, without pride; and I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted.” So do not imagine that intercession is a matter of bargaining or favoritism (muḥābāh), for that would be a corruption of tawḥīd. Rather, it is a manifestation of divine wisdom and mercy, decreed from eternity (al-azal) for those whom God wills, among the people of faith and sincerity. And this is the sound doctrine, free from the extremes of the Muʿtazilah who denied it, and the heedlessness of the common folk who distorted it.

chapters.title_en: On the Intercession of the Prophet and the Believers, and the Means of Attaining It
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن إذا حق دخول النار على طوائف من المؤمنين فإن الله تعالى بفضله
يقبل فيهم شفاعة الأنبياء والصديقين بل شفاعة العلماء والصالحين وكل من له
عند الله تعالى جاه وحسن معاملة فإن له شفاعة في أهله وقرابته وأصدقائه
ومعارفه فكن حريصا على أن تكتسب لنفسك عندهم رتبة الشفاعة وذلك بأن لا تحقر
آدميا أصلا فإن الله تعالى خبأ ولايته في عباده فلعل الذي تزدريه عينك هو
ولي الله ولا تستصغر معصية أصلا فإن الله تعالى خبأ غضبه في معاصيه فلعل
مقت الله فيه ولا تستحقر أصلا طاعة فإن الله تعالى خبأ رضاه في طاعته فلعل
رضاه فيه ولو الكلمة الطيبة أو النية الحسنة أو ما يجري مجراه
وشواهد الشفاعة في القرآن والأخبار كثيرة قال الله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك
ربك فترضى} روى عمرو ابن العاص أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول
إبراهيم عليه السلام {رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن
عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم} وقول عيسى عليه السلام {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك} ثم
رفع يديه وقال أمتي أمتي ثم بكى فقال الله عز وجل يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد
فسله ما يبكيك فأتاه جبريل فسأله فأخبره  والله أعلم به فقال يا جبريل اذهب
إلى محمد فقل له إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوءك (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن أحد قبل نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وأحلت لي الغنائم ولم
تحل لأحد قبلي وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وترابها طهورا فأيما رجل من أمتي
أدركته الصلاة فليصل وأعطيت الشفاعة وكل نبي بعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعثت إلى
الناس عامة (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كان يوم القيامة كنت إمام
النبين وخطيبهم وصاحب شفاعتهم من غير فخر وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنا سيد
ولد آدم ولا فخر وأنا أول من تنشق الأرض عنه وأنا أول شافع وأول مشفع بيدي
لواء الحمد تحته آدم فمن دونه (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لكل نبي دعوة
مستجابة فأريد أن أختبىء دعوتي شفاعة لأمتي يوم القيامة (4) وقال ابن عباس
رضي الله عنهما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينصب للأنبياء منابر من
ذهب فيجلسون عليها ويبقى منبري لا أجلس عليه قائما بين يدي ربي منتصبا
مخافة أن يبعث بي إلى الجنة وتبقى أمتي بعدي فأقول يا رب أمتي فيقول الله
عز وجل يا محمد وما تريد أن أصنع بأمتك فأقول يا رب عجل حسابهم فما أزال
أشفع حتى أعطي صكاكا برجال قد بعث بهم PageV04P526
إلى النار وحتى إن مالكا خازن النار يقول يا محمد ما تركت للنار لغضب ربك
في أمتك من بقية (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأشفع يوم القيامة لأكثر
مما على وجه الأرض من حجر ومدر (2) وقال أبو هريرة أتي رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم بلحم فرفع إليه الذراع وكانت تعجبه فنهش منها نهشة ثم قال أنا
سيد المرسلين يوم القيامة وهل تدرون مم ذلك يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين في
صعيد واحد يسمعهم الداعي وينفذهم البصر وتدنو الشمس فبلغ الناس من الغم
والكرب ما لا يطيقون ولا يحتملون فيقول الناس بعضهم لبعض ألا ترون ما قد
بلغكم ألا تنظرون من يشفع لكم  إلى ربكم فيقول بعض الناس لبعض عليكم بآدم
عليه السلام فيأتون آدم فيقولون له أنت أبو البشر خلقك الله تعالى بيده
ونفخ فيك من روحه وأمر الملائكة فسجدوا لك اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن
فيه ألا ترى ما قد بلغنا فيقول لهم آدم عليه السلام إن ربي قد غضب اليوم
غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولا يغضب بعده مثله وإنه قد نهاني عن الشجرة فعصيته
نفسي نفسي اذهبوا إلى غيري اذهبوا إلى نوح فيأتون نوحا عليه السلام فيقولون
يا نوح أنت أول الرسل إلى أهل الأرض وقد سماك الله عبدا شكورا اشفع لنا إلى
ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فيقول إن ربي قد غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله
ولا يغضب بعده مثله وإنه قد كانت لي دعوة دعوتها على قومي نفسي نفسي اذهبوا
إلى غيري اذهبوا إلى إبراهيم خليل الله فيأتون إبراهيم خليل الله عليه
السلام فيقولون أنت نبي الله وخليله من أهل الأرض اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى
ما نحن فيه فيقول لهم إن ربي قد غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولا يغضب
بعده مثله وإنى كنت كذبت ثلاث كذبات ويذكرها نفسي نفسي اذهبوا إلى غيري
اذهبوا إلى موسى فيأتون موسى عليه السلام فيقولون يا 4 موسى أنت رسول الله
فضلك برسالته وبكلامه على الناس اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فيقول
إن ربي قد غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولن يغضب بعده مثله وإني قتلت
نفسا لم أومر بقتلها نفسي نفسي اذهبوا إلى غيري اذهبوا إلى عيسى عليه
السلام فيأتون عيسى فيقولون يا عيسى أنت رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم
وروح منه وكلمت الناس في المهد اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فيقول
عيسى عليه السلام إن ربي غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولن يغضب بعده
مثله ولم يذكر ذنبا نفسي نفسي اذهبوا إلى غيري اذهبوا إلى محمد  صلى الله
عليه وسلم فيأتون فيقولون يا محمد أنت رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وغفر الله
لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فأنطلق
فآتي تحت العرش فأقع ساجدا لربي ثم يفتح الله لي من محامده وحسن الثناء
عليه شيئا لم يفتحه على أحد قبلي ثم يقال يا محمد ارفع رأسك سل تعط واشفع
تشفع فأرفع رأسي فأقول أمتي أمتى يا رب فقال يا محمد أدخل من أمتك من لا
حساب عليهم من الباب الأيمن من أبواب الجنة وهم شركاء الناس فيما سوى ذلك
من الأبواب ثم قال والذي نفسي بيده إن بين المصراعين من مصاريع الجنة كما
بين مكة وحمير أو كما بين مكة وبصرى (3) وفي حديث آخر
هذا السياق بعينه مع ذكر خطايا إبراهيم وهو قوله في الكواكب هذا ربي
وقوله لآلهتهم بل فعله كبيرهم هذا وقوله PageV04P527
إنى سقيم
فهذه شفاعة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولآحاد أمته من العلماء
والصالحين شفاعة أيضا حتى قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدخل الجنة
بشفاعة رجل من أمتي أكثر من ربيعة ومضر (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقال
للرجل قم يا فلان فاشفع فيقوم الرجل فيشفع للقبيلة ولأهل البيت وللرجل
والرجلين على قدر عمله (2) وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن
رجلا من أهل الجنة يشرف يوم القيامة على أهل النار فيناديه رجل من أهل
النار ويقول يا فلان هل تعرفني فيقول لا والله ما أعرفك من أنت فيقول أنا
الذي مررت بي في الدنيا فاستسقيتني شربة ماء فسقيتك قال قد عرفت قال فاشفع
لي بها عند ربك فيسأل الله تعالى ذكره ويقول إني أشرفت على أهل النار
فناداني رجل من أهلها فقال هل تعرفني فقلت لا من أنت فقال أنا الذي
استسقيتني في الدنيا فسقيتك فاشفع لي عند ربك فشفعني فيه فيشفعه الله فيه
فيؤمر به فيخرج من النار (3) وعن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم
أنا أول الناس خروجا إذا بعثوا وأنا خطيبهم إذا وفدوا وأنا مبشرهم إذا
يئسوا لواء الحمد يومئذ بيدي وأنا أكرم ولد آدم على ربي ولا فخر (4) وقال
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أقوم بين يدي ربي عز وجل فأكسى حلة من
حلل الجنة ثم أقوم عن يمين العرش ليس أحد من الخلائق يقوم ذلك المقام غيري
(5) وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما جلس ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم ينتظرونه فخرج حتى إذا دنا منهم سمعهم يتذاكرون فسمع حديثهم فقال
بعضهم عجبا إن الله عز وجل اتخذ من خلقه خليلا اتخذ إبراهيم خليلا وقال آخر
ماذا بأعجب من كلام موسى كلمه تكليما وقال آخر فعيسى كلمة الله وروحه وقال
آخر آدم اصطفاه الله فخرج عليهم صلى الله عليه وسلم فسلم وقال قد سمعت
كلامكم وتعجبكم إن إبراهيم خليل الله وهو كذلك وموسى نجي الله وهو كذلك
وعيسى روح الله وكلمته وهو كذلك وآدم اصطفاه الله تعالى وهو كذلك ألا وأنا
حبيب الله ولا فخر وأنا حامل لواء الحمد يوم القيامة ولا فخر وأنا أول شافع
وأول مشفع يوم القيامة ولا فخر وأنا أول من يحرك حلق الجنة فيفتح الله لي
فأدخلها ومعي فقراء المؤمنين ولا فخر وأنا أكرم الأولين والآخرين ولا فخر
(6)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes pairing or joining one thing to another; shafāʿah is the act of making a request on behalf of another, joining one's own supplication to the need of the interceded-for.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, shafāʿah is the Prophet's (and others') privileged petition before God on the Day of Judgment, granted solely by divine favor (faḍl), not by independent merit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "making a number even" (making two of one); metaphorically, it is the intercessor's elevation of another's rank by joining his plea to the divine will.
- Root: خ-ب-أ (kh-b-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To conceal, hide, or store away something precious; khabaʾa implies secreting a treasure for a future purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): God's "hiding" (khabaʾa) His friendship in His servants and His wrath in sins signifies the hiddenness of divine decree (ghayb) — the unknowability of who is a friend (walī) and which act triggers wrath, demanding universal caution.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical concealment; the "hiding" is not spatial but epistemic — a warning against presumption in judging others' states.
- Root: ج-ا-ه (j-w-h) — already used; substitute with و-ج-ه (w-j-h) variant: Note the text's "جاه" (rank/standing) — per Lisān, it is derived from wajh (face), meaning honor and prestige before a superior; in the Hereafter context, it is the accrued merit of righteous dealing (ḥusn muʿāmalah) with God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Propositions (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The repeated "إذا" (idhā) clauses with "فإن" (fa-inna) responses establish causal-conditioned theological statements: when X occurs (entry into Fire), then Y necessarily follows (intercession by divine favor), with the fa- marking the apodosis as the certain consequence of the protasis.
chapters.translation:
Know that when the entry into the Fire is decreed for groups of believers, God — exalted be He — by His bounty accepts on their behalf the intercession of the prophets and the veracious (ṣiddīqīn), nay, even the intercession of the scholars and the righteous, and of everyone who holds rank (jāh) before God and has dealt with Him in good manner (ḥusn muʿāmalah). For such a one has intercession for his family, his relatives, his friends, and his acquaintances. So be eager to acquire for yourself the station of intercession among them — and that is by never holding any human being in contempt. For God — exalted be He — has hidden His friendship (wilāyah) among His servants; perhaps the one whom your eye disdains is a friend of God (walī Allāh). And never deem any sin insignificant, for God — exalted be He — has hidden His wrath among sins; perhaps His abhorrence (maqt) lies within it. And never deem any act of obedience insignificant, for God — exalted be He — has hidden His good pleasure (riḍā) within obedience; perhaps His pleasure lies within it — even a kind word, or a good intention, or whatever runs in that course.

The evidences for intercession in the Qur'an and the reports (akhbār) are numerous. God — exalted be He — said: {«And verily your Lord shall give you, and you shall be well-pleased»} (93:5). ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — recited the saying of Abraham — peace be upon him: {«My Lord, verily they have led astray many of mankind; so whoever follows me, then he is of me, and whoever disobeys me — verily You are Forgiving, Merciful»} (14:36), and the saying of Jesus — peace be upon him: {«If You punish them, then verily they are Your servants»} (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: "My community, my community!" Then he wept. So God — Mighty and Majestic — said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him and asked him, and he informed him — and God knows best of it. He said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say to him: 'Verily We shall make you well-pleased concerning your community, and We shall not displease you.'" (1)

And he — peace be upon him — said: "I have been given five things which no one before me was given: I have been aided by terror (ruʿb) to the distance of a month's journey; the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for anyone before me; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and its soil a purifier (ṭahūr) — so whichever man of my community is overtaken by the prayer, let him pray; and I have been given intercession (shafāʿah); and every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, while I have been sent to all mankind generally." (2)

And he — peace be upon him — said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, I shall be the leader (imām) of the prophets, and their orator (khaṭīb), and the possessor of their intercession — without pride." And he — peace be upon him — said: "Verily I am the master of the children of Adam — without pride — and I am the first from whom the earth will be split open, and I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted. In my hand is the banner of praise (liwāʾ al-ḥamd); beneath it is Adam and all those after him." (3)

And he — peace be upon him — said: "Every prophet has a supplication that is answered; I have chosen to reserve my supplication as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection." (4)

And Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — said: The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "Pulpits of gold will be set up for the prophets, and they will sit upon them. My pulpit will remain — I will not sit upon it, but will stand before my Lord, erect, fearing that I may be sent to Paradise while my community remains after me. So I shall say: 'O my Lord, my community!' And God — Mighty and Majestic — will say: 'O Muhammad, what do you wish that I should do with your community?' I shall say: 'O my Lord, hasten their reckoning.' And I shall not cease interceding until I am given writs (ṣikāk) for men who have been sent to the Fire." (1)

And he — peace be upon him — said: "Verily I shall intercede on the Day of Resurrection for more than the number of stones and clods upon the face of the earth." (2)

And Abū Hurayrah said: Meat was brought to the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — and the foreleg was raised to him, which he liked. He took a bite from it, then said: "I am the master of the messengers on the Day of Resurrection. And do you know why that is? God will gather the first and the last upon a single plain (ṣaʿīd), where the caller will be heard by them all and the sight will penetrate them all, and the sun will draw near. Then the people will reach such a degree of grief and distress as they cannot bear or endure. So the people will say to one another: 'Do you not see what has befallen you? Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord?' Some will say to others: 'Go to Adam — peace be upon him.' So they will come to Adam and say to him: 'You are the father of mankind; God created you with His hand, and breathed into you of His spirit, and commanded the angels to prostrate before you. Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' Adam — peace be upon him — will say to them: 'Verily my Lord has today become angry with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, nor will He be angry with the like of it after. And He forbade me the tree, and I disobeyed Him. Myself, myself! Go to other than me — go to Noah.' So they will come to Noah — peace be upon him — and say: 'O Noah, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and God has named you a grateful servant (ʿabd shakūr). Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in?' He will say: 'Verily my Lord has today become angry with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, nor will He be angry with the like of it after. And I had a supplication which I made against my people. Myself, myself! Go to other than me — go to Abraham, the friend of God (khalīl Allāh).' So they will come to Abraham, the friend of God — peace be upon him — and say: 'You are the prophet of God and His friend from among the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in?' He will say to them: 'Verily my Lord has today become angry with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, nor will He be angry with the like of it after. And I told three lies' — and he will mention them — 'Myself, myself! Go to other than me — go to Moses.' So they will come to Moses — peace be upon him — and say: 'O Moses, you are the messenger of God; God favored you with His message and His speech over mankind. Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in?' He will say: 'Verily my Lord has today become angry with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, nor will He ever be angry with the like of it after. And I killed a soul which I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself! Go to other than me — go to Jesus — peace be upon him.' So they will come to Jesus and say: 'O Jesus, you are the messenger of God and His word which He cast unto Mary, and a spirit from Him, and you spoke to mankind in the cradle. Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in?' Jesus — peace be upon him — will say: 'Verily my Lord has today become angry with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, nor will He ever be angry with the like of it after' — and he will not mention any sin — 'Myself, myself! Go to other than me — go to Muhammad — peace be upon him.' So they will come and say: 'O Muhammad, you are the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets, and God has forgiven you your former and your latter sins. Intercede for us with your Lord — do you not see what we are in?' So I shall set out and come beneath the Throne (ʿarsh), and fall prostrate before my Lord. Then God will open to me of His praises and beautiful eulogy upon Him something He has not opened to anyone before me. Then it will be said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head; ask and you shall be given, and intercede and your intercession shall be accepted.' So I shall raise my head and say: 'My community, my community — O my Lord!' He will say: 'O Muhammad, admit from your community those who have no reckoning upon them through the right gate of the gates of Paradise, and they shall share with the people in what is other than that among the gates.' Then he said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, verily between the two leaves of the gates of Paradise is as the distance between Mecca and Hajar — or as between Mecca and Buṣrā.'" (3)

In another hadith, this same account is given with the mention of Abraham's sins — namely his saying concerning the stars: "This is my Lord" (6:76), and his saying concerning their idols: "Nay, their chief did this" (21:63), and his saying: "Verily I am sick" (37:89).

This, then, is the intercession of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him. And for individual members of his community — the scholars and the righteous — there is also intercession. Indeed, the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "There shall enter Paradise by the intercession of a man of my community more than the number of the tribes of Rabīʿah and Muḍar." (1)

And he — peace be upon him — said: "It will be said to a man: 'Arise, O so-and-so, and intercede.' So the man will arise and intercede for a tribe, for a household, and for a man or two men, according to the measure of his deed." (2)

And Anas said: The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "Verily a man from the people of Paradise will look down on the Day of Resurrection upon the people of the Fire. A man from the people of the Fire will call out to him and say: 'O so-and-so, do you recognize me?' He will say: 'No, by God, I do not recognize you. Who are you?' He will say: 'I am the one who passed by you in the world and asked you for a drink of water, and you gave me to drink.' He will say: 'I recognize you now.' He will say: 'Then intercede for me by that with your Lord.' So he will ask God — exalted be His remembrance — and say: 'Verily I looked down upon the people of the Fire, and a man from among them called out to me and said: "Do you recognize me?" I said: "No, who are you?" He said: "I am the one who asked you for water in the world, and you gave me to drink. So intercede for me with your Lord." So I interceded for him, and God accepted my intercession for him.' Then command will be given, and he will be brought out of the Fire." (3)

And on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "I am the first of mankind to emerge when they are raised, and I am their orator when they arrive, and I am their bearer of glad tidings when they despair. The banner of praise (liwāʾ al-ḥamd) on that day is in my hand, and I am the most honored of the children of Adam before my Lord — without pride." (4)

And the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "Verily I shall stand before my Lord — Mighty and Majestic — and I shall be clothed in a robe from the robes of Paradise. Then I shall stand to the right of the Throne; no one of creation shall stand in that station other than me." (5)

And Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — said: A group of the companions of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — sat waiting for him. He came out, and when he drew near to them, he heard them discussing. He heard their conversation. One of them said: "How wondrous! Verily God — Mighty and Majestic — has taken from His creation a friend (khalīl); He took Abraham as a friend." Another said: "What is more wondrous than the speech of Moses — He spoke to him directly (taklīman)?" Another said: "And Jesus is the word of God and His spirit." Another said: "And Adam — God chose him (iṣṭafā)." So he came out upon them — peace be upon him — and greeted them, and said: "I have heard your words and your wonder. Verily Abraham is the friend of God (khalīl Allāh) — and so he is. And Moses is the intimate of God (najī Allāh) — and so he is. And Jesus is the spirit of God and His word — and so he is. And Adam — God chose him — and so he is. But know: I am the beloved of God (ḥabīb Allāh) — without pride. And I am the bearer of the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection — without pride. And I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted on the Day of Resurrection — without pride. And I am the first to knock upon the rings of Paradise, and God will open it for me, and I shall enter it with the poor of the believers — without pride. And I am the most honored of the first and the last — without pride." (6)

chapters.title_en: On the Description of the Pond (al-Ḥawḍ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### |||| صفة الحوض

اعلم أن الحوض مكرمة عظيمة خص الله بها نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد
اشتملت الأخبار على وصفه ونحن PageV04P528
نرجو أن يرزقنا الله تعالى في الدنيا علمه وفي الآخرة ذوقه فإن من صفاته
أن من شرب منه لم يظمأ أبدا قال أنس أغفى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
إغفاءة فرفع رأسه متبسما فقالوا له يا رسول الله لم ضحكت فقال آية أنزلت
علي آنفا وقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إنا أعطيناك الكوثر حتى ختمها ثم قال
هل تدرون ما الكوثر قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال إنه نهر وعدنيه ربي عز وجل
في الجنة عليه خير كثير عليه  حوض ترد عليه أمتي يوم القيامة آنيته عدد نجوم
السماء (1) وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بينما أنا أسير في
الجنة إذا بنهر حافتاه قباب اللؤلؤ المجوف قلت ما هذا يا جبريل قال هذا
الكوثر الذي أعطاك ربك فضرب الملك بيده فإذا طينه مسك أذفر (2) وقال كان
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما بين لابتي حوضي مثل ما بين المدينة
وصنعاء أو مثل ما بين المدينة وعمان (3) وروى ابن عمر أنه لما نزل قوله
تعالى {إنا أعطيناك الكوثر} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو نهر في
الجنة حافتاه من ذهب شرابه أشد بياضا من اللبن وأحلى من العسل وأطيب ريحا
من المسك يجري على جنادل اللؤلؤ والمرجان (4) وقال ثوبان مولى رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن حوضي ما بين عدن
إلى عمان البلقان ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وأحلى من العسل وأكوابه عدد نجوم
السماء من شرب منه شربة لم يظمأ بعدها أبدا أول الناس ورودا عليه فقراء
المهاجرين فقال عمر بن الخطاب ومن هم يا رسول الله قال هم الشعث رءوسا
الدنس ثيابا الذين لا ينكحون المتنعمات ولا تفتح لهم أبواب السدد (5) فقال
عمر بن عبد العزيز والله لقد نكحت المتنعمات فاطمة بنت عبد الملك وفتحت لي
أبواب السدد إلا أن يرحمني الله لا جرم لا أدهن رأسي حتى يشعث ولا أغسل
ثوبي الذي على جسدي حتى يتسخ وعن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله ما آنية
الحوض قال والذي نفس محمد بيده لآنيته أكثر من عدد نجوم السماء وكواكبها في
الليلة المظلمة المضحية من شرب منه لم يظمأ آخر ما عليه يشخب فيه ميزابان
من الجنة عرضه مثل طوله ما بين عمان وأيلة ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وأحلى
من العسل (6) وعن سمرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لكل نبي
حوضا وإنهم يتباهون أيهم أكثر واردة وإني لأرجو  أن أكون أكثرهم واردة (7)
فهذا رجاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليرج كل عبد أن يكون في جملة
الواردين وليحذر أن يكون متمنيا ومغترا وهو يظن أنه راج فإن الراجي للحصاد
من بث البذر ونقى الأرض وسقاها الماء ثم جلس يرجو فضل الله بالإنبات ودفع
الصواعق إلى أوان الحصاد فأما من ترك الحراثة أو الزراعة وتنقية الأرض
وسقيها وأخذ يرجو من فضل الله أن ينبت له الحب والفاكهة فهذ مغتر ومتمن
PageV04P529
وليس من الراجين في شيء وهكذا رجاء أكثر الخلق وهو غرور الحمقى نعوذ
بالله من الغرور والغفلة فإن الاغترار بالله أعظم من الاغترار بالدنيا قال
الله تعالى {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور}

### |||| القول في صفة جهنم وأهوالها وأنكالها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-و-ض (ḥ-w-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A basin or cistern where water collects; the place of gathering for drinking.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Hereafter, the specific watering-place granted to the Prophet ﷺ as an honor (karāmah), symbolizing divine favor and the gathering of his community.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in its physical description; metaphorical (majāz) in signifying the Prophet's intercessory station and the distinction of his followers.
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To arrive at water; to come to a watering-place for drinking.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of approaching the Ḥawḍ on the Day of Resurrection, denoting the blessed reception of the faithful.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical arrival; metaphorical for spiritual attainment of divine mercy.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, delusion, or being beguiled by false appearances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The perilous state of self-delusion regarding God's mercy without corresponding action—a major spiritual ailment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a state of heedlessness; metaphorical for the soul's treacherous reliance on hope without deeds.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the nuanced parsing of "whoever drinks from it shall never thirst" and the warning against false hope, ensuring precise logical linkage between condition and consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Pond (al-Ḥawḍ) is a magnificent honor (makrumah ʿaẓīmah) which God, Exalted is He, singled out for our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The reports (akhbār) have encompassed its description, and we hope that God, Exalted is He, will grant us knowledge of it in this world and its tasting (dhawq) in the Hereafter. For among its attributes is that whoever drinks from it shall never thirst thereafter.

Anas reported: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, dozed a light slumber (ighfāʾah), then raised his head smiling. They said to him: "O Messenger of God, why do you laugh?" He said: "A verse has just been revealed to me." Then he recited: {In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Verily, We have given you al-Kawthar} until he completed it. Then he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is a river which my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me in Paradise, upon which is abundant good. Upon it is a Pond (ḥawḍ) which my community will arrive at on the Day of Resurrection, its vessels (ānīyah) numbering the stars of the sky."

And Anas said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "While I was walking in Paradise, behold, there was a river whose banks were domes of hollowed pearl. I said: 'What is this, O Gabriel?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord has given you.' Then the angel struck with his hand, and behold, its clay was pure musk (misk adhfar)."

And he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say: "The distance between the two banks (lābatay) of my Pond is like that between Medina and Ṣanʿāʾ, or like that between Medina and ʿUmān."

And Ibn ʿUmar narrated that when the saying of God, Exalted is He, {Verily, We have given you al-Kawthar} was revealed, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is a river in Paradise, its two banks are of gold, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and more fragrant in scent than musk. It flows over pebbles of pearl and coral (marjān)."

And Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "My Pond extends from ʿAdan to ʿUmān of al-Balqāʾ. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Its cups (akwāb) number the stars of the sky. Whoever drinks from it a single drink shall never thirst thereafter. The first people to arrive at it are the poor among the emigrants (fuqarāʾ al-muhājirīn)." ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "And who are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "They are the disheveled of head (shuʿth), the dirty of garment (dunis), those who do not marry the delicately-nurtured women (al-mutanaʿimāt), and for whom the doors of the great ones (al-sudad) are not opened."

Then ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: "By God, I have married the delicately-nurtured—Fāṭimah bint ʿAbd al-Malik—and the doors of the great ones have been opened for me, unless God has mercy on me. Without fail (lā jarama), I shall not oil my head until it becomes disheveled, nor shall I wash the garment upon my body until it becomes dirty."

And from Abū Dharr, he said: I said: "O Messenger of God, what are the vessels (ānīyah) of the Pond?" He said: "By Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, its vessels are more numerous than the number of the stars of the sky and its planets in a dark, moonless night (al-muḍḥiyah). Whoever drinks from it shall never thirst at the end of what is upon him. Two spouts (mīzābān) pour into it from Paradise, its width like its length, between ʿUmān and Aylah. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

And from Samurah, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, every prophet has a Pond, and they vie in pride (yabāhūn) as to which of them has the most arrivals (wāridah). And I indeed hope to be the most numerous of them in arrivals."

This, then, is the hope (rajāʾ) of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. So let every servant hope to be among the arrivals (al-wāridīn), and let him beware of being merely a wishful one (mutamannī) and deluded (mughtarr), while supposing himself to be a hopeful one (rāj). For the one who truly hopes for the harvest is he who sows the seed, clears the earth, and waters it with water, then sits hoping for God's bounty in causing it to grow and in warding off calamities (ṣawāʿiq) until the time of harvest. As for the one who abandons tilling, or sowing, and clearing the earth and watering it, and then takes to hoping that God's bounty will cause grain and fruit to grow for him—this one is deluded and wishful, and is not among the hopeful in any way. And such is the hope of most of creation—it is the delusion of fools (ghurūr al-ḥumqā). We seek refuge in God from delusion (ghurūr) and heedlessness (ghaflah). For being deluded by God is greater than being deluded by this world. God, Exalted is He, said: {So let not the life of this world delude you, nor let the Deluder (al-Gharūr) delude you concerning God}.

chapters.arabic_text:
يا أيها الغافل عن نفسه المغرور بما هو فيه من شواغل هذه الدنيا المشرفة
على الانقضاء والزوال دع التفكر فيما أنت مرتحل عنه واصرف الفكر إلى موردك
فإنك أخبرت بأن النار مورد للجميع إذ قيل {وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك
حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا} فأنت من الورود
على يقين ومن النجاة في شك فاستشعر في قلبك هول ذلك المورد فعساك تستعد
للنجاة منه وتأمل في حال الخلائق وقد قاسوا من دواهي القيامة ما قاسوا
فبينما هم في كربها وأهوالها وقوفا ينتظرون حقيقة أنبائها وتشفيع شفعائها
إذ أحاطت بالمجرمين ظلمات ذات شعب وأظلت عليهم نار ذات لهب وسمعوا لها
زفيرا وجرجرة تفصح عن شدة الغيظ والغضب فعند ذلك أيقن المجرمون بالعطب وجثت
الأمم على الركب حتى أشفق البرءاء من سوء المنقلب وخرج المنادي من الزبانية
قائلا أين فلان بن فلان المسوف نفسه في الدنيا بطول الأمل المضيع عمره في
سوء العمل فيبادرونه بمقامع حديد ويستقبلونه بعظائم التهديد ويسوقونه إلى
العذاب الشديد وينكسونه في قعر الجحيم ويقولون له {ذق إنك أنت العزيز
الكريم} فأسكنوا دارا ضيقة الأرجاء مظلمة المسالك مبهمة المهالك يخلد فيها
الأسير ويوقد فيها السعير شرابهم فيها الحميم ومستقرهم  الجحيم الزبانية
تقمعهم والهاوية تجمعهم أمانيهم فيها الهلاك وما لهم منها فكاك قد شدت
أقدامهم إلى النواصي واسودت وجوههم من ظلمة المعاصي ينادون من أكنافها
ويصيحون في نواحيها وأطرافها يا مالك قد حق علينا الوعيد يا مالك قد أثقلنا
الحديد يا مالك قد نضجت منا الجلود يا مالك أخرجنا منها فإنا لا نعود فتقول
الزبانية هيهات لات حين أمان ولا خروج لكم من دار الهوان فاخسئوا فيها ولا
تكلمون ولو أخرجتم منها لكنتم إلى ما نهيتم عنه تعودون فعند ذلك يقنطون
وعلى ما فرطوا في جنب الله يتأسفون ولا ينجيهم الندم ولا يغنيهم الأسف بل
يكبون على وجوههم مغلولين النار من فوقهم والنار من تحتهم والنار عن
أيمانهم والنار عن شمائلهم فهم غرقى في النار طعامهم نار وشرابهم نار
ولباسهم نار ومهادهم نار فهم بين مقطعات النيران وسرابيل القطران وضرب
المقامع وثقل السلاسل فهم يتجلجلون في مضايقها ويتحطمون في دركاتها
ويضطربون بين غواشيها تغلى بهم النار كغلي القدور ويهتفون بالويل والعويل
ومهما دعوا بالثبور صب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم يصهر به ما في بطونهم
والجلود ولهم مقامع من حديد تهشم بها جباههم فيتفجر الصديد من أفواههم
وننقطع من العطش أكبادهم وتسيل على الخدود أحداقهم ويسقط من الوجنات لحومها
ويتمعط من الأطراف شعورها بل جلودها وكلما نضجت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا غيرها
قد عريت من اللحم عظامهم فبقيت الأرواح منوطة بالعروق وعلائق العصب وهي تنش
في لفح تلك النيران وهم مع ذلك يتمنون الموت فلا يموتون فكيف بك لو نظرت
إليهم وقد سودت وجوههم أشد سوادا من الحميم وأعميت أبصارهم وأبكمت ألسنتهم
وقصمت ظهورهم وكسرت عظامهم وجدعت آذانهم ومزقت جلودهم وغلت أيديهم إلى
أعناقهم وجمع بين نواصيهم وأقدامهم وهم يمشون على النار بوجوههم ويطأون حسك
